Aa di waabɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na aakekeln aaboln ki di ŋal ubiŋ pu yaan ngbaan mu, ki gbaŋ goln nimɔgben. 16Ni li bi likpakpaln, ki kpab ni nfum mulee, naafɔfɔk li ye lisaŋ ni ligeln, le naapepeen mu li ye lisaŋ ni ligeln. 17Aa di ŋitakpanyaan ŋitaa lur nfum munaa pu, ki tam kikekengeŋ ngbaan pu; aa di litakpanyaan mamaln li bi yin li ke rubi na, ni litakpanyaan li waa chain aan bi yin li ke topas na, ni litakpanyaan mamaln li waa chain, li bi yin li ke ganet na, ki di lur njan aakuul pu; 18ki di litakpanyaan li ye liŋaankal aan bi yin li ke emeral na, ni litakpanyaan li bɔn timm aan bi yin li ke safir na, ni litakpanyaan li moor aan bi yin li ke diamonn na, ki di lur lelee aakuul pu; 19ki di litakpanyaan li ye liŋaankal ki bɔn timm aan bi yin li ke tukois na, ni litakpanyaan li bi yin li ke agate na, ni litakpanyaan li man chaun aan bi yin li ke ametis na, ki di lur taataa aakuul pu; 20ki di litakpanyaan li bi yin li ke beril na, ni litakpanyaan li bi yin li ke kaneliann na, ni litakpanyaan li ye nkonyon, bi yin li ke jaspa na, ki di lur nanaa aakuul pu. Aa di ŋi mɔmɔk tam salmaa pu. 21Ŋitakpanyaan kipiik ni ŋilee ŋee pu, ni ŋmee Jakob aabijabim kipiik ni bilee na aayimbil paan ŋi pu, aan ni mɔk Israel yaab aanibol. 22Aa ŋa salmaa aakululn ti mur ke iŋmin na. 23Aa ŋa salmaa aabɔmbim mulee, aan ki di mbɔmbim ngbaan ŋal dab kibiŋ aakekengeŋ ngbaan aapaacham aamɔju ilee, 24ki di salmaa aakululn tilee ngbaan ki di ŋal dab mbɔmbim mulee ngbaan, 25ki di imɔju ilee ngbaan ki di tam ŋitakpanyaan ŋilee na aah dab libɔgbiln aaŋmin ilee i pu na, 26ki ŋa salmaa aabɔmbim mulee mu, ki di dab kibiŋ aakekengeŋ ngbaan aaponn ni aataab aamɔju ilee i bi libɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na chee. 27Aa ki ŋa salmaa aabɔmbim mulee kpee, aan ki di mu ŋal dab libɔkul ngbaan aabɔgbiln aaŋminju aataab, nimbiin ni wɔb, ki duun baah ŋal dab nin chee na, ligbapapaln na aapaacham. 28Aa di ŋŋmimurkoo mu bɔn timm na, ki di gbin kibiŋ aakekengeŋ na, ni libɔkul na aabɔmbim, aan nima kan, kibiŋ aakekengeŋ ngbaan li baa ligbapapaln na aapaacham ki taa sɔkr.
29“N‑yoonn mu Aaronn ti ban u koo Chain Aapepel ni na, u ga li pee kibiŋ aakekengeŋ ki ni ŋmee Israel yaab aanibol aayimbil ki paan ŋitakpanyaan na pu na, nima kan, min Uwumbɔr ga li teer maanib bɔr. 30Aa di tiwan ni bi yin ni ke Urim ni Tumim na ki di ŋa kibiŋ aakekengeŋ ngbaan aakpalɔŋ ni, aan nima kan, Aaronn ga li joo ni n‑yoonn mu u ti dan nnimbiin ni na. N‑yoonn mumɔk u choo nnimbiin ni na kan, u li pee kibiŋ aakekengeŋ ngbaan, nima kan, u ga ŋmaa bee maageehn ki tuk Israel yaab.
Bitotoorb aawanpeenkaan niken aabɔr
(Nnyam 39.22-31)
31“Kikpalk ki u ga di peen libɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na taab na, ni di ŋitan ŋi bɔn timm na ŋal ki. 32Kikpalk na li kpa uyil aah ga jer nin chee na, ni gbaŋ mann goln uyil yaan ngbaan aan ni taa kar. 33-34Aa di upiih aakur ti man chaun ki bɔn timm, ni nsiin, ni timann, ki buu ti nkokon, ki di ni ni salmaa aabɔluln ki di tuun char tɔb ni, ki mann goln kikpalk ngbaan aataab. 35Aaronn yaa ti ban u toor kitork tii mi kan, u di peen. N‑yoonn mu u ti dan nnimbiin ni Chain Aapepel ni na, bee u yaa chaa nya kan, ŋibɔlun ngbaan ga li weeni aan m ŋun, nima kan, waan kpo.
36“Aa di salmaa ŋmeen ki ŋa tiwanyaan, ki ŋmee ni pu ke ‘Uwumbɔr yoo’, 37ki di litaln li bɔn timm na buu tiwan ngbaan ki di jɔn Aaronn aayikpupuk na, uyigbeer pu. 38Aaronn di kiyikpupuk ngbaan chiŋ aan tiwanyaan na li jɔn uyigbeer pu, nima kan, min Uwumbɔr ga gaa Israel yaab aapiin i Aaronn ga di dan m chee na, hali binib ngbaan yaa galn baah ban bi tii ipiin pu na kan, m ga gaa i.
39“Aa di tikokonn nyaan ki luu Aaronn aabɔkul, ki di ŋitanyaan ŋa kiyikpupuk, ni kikekengeŋ ki bi joo buu kichaŋ ni na, ki gbaŋ mann goln umɔgben.
40“Aa ŋa ŋibɔkul, ni kichaŋ aakekengen, ni tiyikpupur, ki tii Aaronn aabijabim, bi li kpa kipak ni kinyaan. 41Aa di tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan ki di peen aakpel Aaronn ni waabijabim, ki nyan bi siin ki di olif aakpan kpir bi pu, aan bi li ye bitotoorb. 42Aa ŋal ŋitanyaan aatuutagen tii bi, bi li fɔk ki ti saa bitaŋaayil mɔk, nima kan, baan di bibaa mɔk binib. 43Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib yaa ban bi dan nnimbiin ni, bee bi yaa ban bi koo Chain Aapepel ni, bi nan ŋa kitork aatuln kan, bi ga yiin tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan la, aan nima kan, baan li kpa ngalm ki kpo. Aaronn ni uyaabitiib mɔmɔk ga li joo nkaal ngbaan kina, le ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

english_text:
Instructions for Ordaining Priests
(Leviticus 8.1-36)
The Lord said to Moses:
1When you ordain Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests, choose a young bull and two rams that have nothing wrong with them. 2Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil. 3Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
4Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves. 5Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash. 6Put on his turban with its narrow strip of engraved gold 7and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
8Next, dress Aaron's sons in their special shirts, 9caps, and sashes, then ordain them, because they and their descendants will always be priests.
10Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head. 11Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent. 12Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar. 13Then take the fat from the animal's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and send them up as an offering to me in the smoke from the altar. 14But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
15Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 16Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar. 17Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head. 18 Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
19Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 20Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 21Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
22This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 23Take one loaf of each kind of bread from the basket, 24and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me. 25After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
26You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
27-28In the future, when anyone from Israel offers the ribs and a hind leg of a ram either to ordain a priest or to ask for my blessing, the meat belongs to me, but it may be eaten by the priests. This law will never change.
29-30After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
31Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place, 32then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent. 33At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it. 34If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
35Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you. 36Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy. 37Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy.
Daily Sacrifices
(Leviticus 6.8-13; Numbers 28.1-8)
The Lord said:
38Each day you must sacrifice two lambs a year old, 39one in the morning and one in the evening. 40-41With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me. 42-43You and your descendants must always offer this sacrifice on the altar at the entrance to the sacred tent.
People of Israel, I will meet and speak with you there, and my shining glory will make the place holy. 44Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests. 45I will live among you as your God, 46and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_text:
Baah ga di kitork aatuln tii Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib pu na aabɔr
(Liifai Yaab 8.1-36)
1“Saah ga ŋa pu ki di kitork aatuln tii Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aan bi li tun maatuln pu na sɔ. Aa ban unaaja ni ipihja ilee, i taa li kpa iween ibaa. 2Aa di boroboro aayon mu ŋan chain kaa kpa nnyɔk na ŋa boroboro, ki di olif aakpan mu ŋa boroboro ngem, u li bi ke maab na, ki di nkpan gbaa bi. 3Aa di bi ŋa kibɔɔkuuk ni, ki di tii mi n‑yoonn mu ni ban ni di unaaja ni ipihja ilee na toor kitork tii mi na.
4“Aa di Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib dan nnimbiin ni, Maabool aabisamɔb chee, ki nan fu bi nnyun. 5Aa di utotoor aawanpeenkaan ni ye libɔkul, ni kibiŋ aakekengeŋ, ni libɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na, ni kikpalk ki u ga di peen libɔkul ngbaan taab na, ni ligbapapaln na, ki di peen Aaronn. 6Aa di kiyikpupuk na chiŋ u, ki di tiwanyaan ni mɔk ke Uwumbɔr le lee u na buu tam kiyikpupuk na, 7ki di nkpan kpir uyil pu, ki ŋa u utotoor.
8“Aa li joo ni ujapɔtiib mu ki di ŋibɔkul peen bi, 9ki di ŋitan buu bichaŋ ni, ki ki di ŋitan buu biyil. Kina le aa ga kaan Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib bi li tun kitork aatuln. Bi ni biyaabitiib ga li tun kitork aatuln tii mi kina, le ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
10“Aa di unaaja ngbaan dan nnimbiin ni, Maabool aabisamɔb chee, aan ki cha Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib di biŋaal paan uyil pu. 11Kɔr unaaja ngbaan nnimbiin ni, Maabool aabisamɔb chee. 12Aa teŋ waasin ngbaan, ki di aaŋanbik tuu nsin ngbaan, ki di ŋa kitork aabimbiln na aamɔju inaa na pu, ki di mu gur na kpir libimbiln ngbaan taab.
13“Ni paa na, aa nyan u ponn ni aakpan, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na, ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil, ni nkpan mu paa ŋi pu na, ki di see mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln paab, ki tii mi. 14Aa di waanann, ni ngban, ni ponn ni aawan, ki di nya lipaal ki ti see ni mmii. Ipiin i ga cha m cha pinn bitotoorb ngbaan aatunwanbir na le na.
15“Nyan upihja ubaa ki cha Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib di biŋaal paan uyil pu. 16Kɔr u, ki teŋ waasin, ki di mu mee kpir kitork aabimbiln ngbaan aapepel ŋinaa pu, 17ki geei waanann ŋichek ŋichek, ki finn uponn ni aawan mɔmɔk, ni ŋitaa, ki di paan uyil ni tinann na pu, 18ki see upihja ngbaan aanann mɔmɔk libimbiln ngbaan paab, aan ni li ye tijikaar aapiin aatork tii mi. Kitork ngbaan aanunun mɔ m chee.
19“Aa di upihja uken na, u aa ga di toor ki ŋa bitotoorb na, aan ki tuk Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib ke bi di biŋaal paan uyil pu. 20Kɔr u, aan ki di waasin ngem ŋa Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aaŋangii aatafalan ni, ni biŋangii aaŋanbijam pu, ni biŋangii aataŋanbijam pu, ki di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln ngbaan aapepel ŋinaa ngbaan pu. 21Aa ban nsin mu bi libimbiln ngbaan pu na ngem, ni olif aakpan na mu ngem, aan ki yɔk Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aawanpeenkaan pu. Nima kan, uma, ni waabim, ni baawanpeenkaan ga li ye min yaan la.
22“Aa gii nyan upihja ngbaan aakpan, ni ujuul aakpan, ni uponn ni aakpan, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na, ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil, ni ŋaakpan, ni ŋŋangii aataajal; 23ki nyan boroboro u bi kibɔɔkuuk ni, ni di u tii mi na, nyan boroboro kpiln libaabaa: nyan boroboro kpiln li bi di olif aakpan ŋa li na libaa, ni baah kaa di olif aakpan ŋa li na mu libaa, ki nyan maab ubaa mu. 24Aa di tijikaar ngbaan ŋa Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aaŋaal ni, ki tuk bi ke bi di ti ŋa kitorkpaan tii mi, 25aan aa ki gaa ti bi chee, ki di paan kitork ki bi kitork aabimbiln na paab ki see ti mmii, ni li ye tijikaar aatork aapiin tii mi. Kitork ngbaan aapiin aabaan nu mɔ m chee.
26“Chuu nyan upihja ngbaan aabingbaal ki di tii mi, ni li ye kitorkpaan. Libingbaal aanann tee le ga li ye si yaan.
27“N‑yoonn mu ni kaan utotoor u li tun tii mi na, upihja u ni ga ti di toor kitork na, ni di libingbaal ni litaajal tii mi, ni li ye kitorkpaan. Bitotoorb le yeh tinann ngbaan. 28N‑yoonn mu maanib ti toor kimɔbaan aatork tii mi na, bitotoorb le yeh kiwakork ngbaan aabingbaal ni litaajal. Min le siin kina, kaan kpeln maalandak. Binib ngbaan aapiin i bi tii min Uwumbɔr na le na.
29“Aaronn yaa ti kpo buyoonn na kan, ni di waatork aawanpeenkaan di tii waabim, aan bi yaa ti kaan bi bitotoorb kan, bi li joo peeni. 30Aaronn aajapɔɔn u ga kal waajal pu, ki li ye utotoor, ki ga li koo chain aapepel ni, nnimbiin ni na kan, u di utotoor aawanpeenkaan peen ki ti saa iwiin ilole.
31“Aa nyan upihja u ni di toor kitork ki kaan Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib na, ki ŋaan ti lipepel li bi chain na ni. 32Bi kpaan ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan, ni boroboro u gur kibɔɔkuuk ni na, Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb, nnimbiin ni. 33Bi ki ŋmɔ kiwakork ki bi di toor chapinn aatork na aanann. Bitotoorb baanja le ŋeer bi ji tijikaar ngbaan, ba pu? ti ye chain aajikaar la. 34Tinann ni tijikaar ngbaan ngem yaa gur ki woln kitaak kan, ni di ti see mmii, ni taa ki ji ti, ba pu? ti ye chain la.
35“Aa di iwiin ilole toor Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib bitotoorb aatork, ke maah mɔk si pu na mɔmɔk. 36Idaa mɔmɔk kan, aa ti kɔr unaaja ubaa ki toor chapinn aatork. Nima le ga cha kitork aabimbiln ngbaan ŋa chain, le aa nin di olif aakpan meen li, li ŋa min Uwumbɔr yaan. 37Idaa mɔmɔk kan, aa ti ŋa kina ki ti saa iwiin ilole, aan nima kan, libimbiln ngbaan ga ŋa chain kookoo, le unii, bee tiwan, taa meeh li, see u mu ye chain.
Baah ga toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr iwiin mɔmɔk pu na
(Nkahm 28.1-8)
38“N‑yoonn mu choo na, iwiin mɔmɔk, ni li joo libiln libaa aapiih ilee toor kitork, libimbiln paab tii mi. 39Ni di ubaa toor kichakpiik ni, aan ki nan di uken mu toor kijook. 40Ni yaa ban ni di njan aapiih toor kan, ni ban boroboro aayon mu ŋan na kuruwaa ubaa, ki di olif aakpan kpalba ubaa buun mu. Ni bar ŋisubil aadaan kpalba ubaa mu ki di ŋa ipiin ngbaan. 41Kijook kan, ni di upiih uken na toor kitork, aan ki ban boroboro aayon, ni nkpan, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ki ŋa ke naah ba ŋa kichakpiik ni pu na. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ye tijikaar aatork aapiin le ki tii min Uwumbɔr, le naabaan nu mɔ m chee. 42N‑yoonn mu choo na, ni li seer ipiin aatork ngbaan mmii ni ki tii mi, nnimbiin ni, Libool na aabisamɔb chee. Nima chee le m ga pii maanib, ki len aa chee tibɔr. 43Nima chee le m ga pii maanib, Israel yaab, le maawiihn mu moor lak lak na ga ŋa nima chee chain. 44M ga ŋa Libool, ni kitork aabimbiln ngbaan chain. M ga nyan Aaronn ni waabijabim le bi li ye maatotoorb. 45M ga li bi maanib Israel yaab chee, ki li ye Baawumbɔr, 46le bi ga bee ke min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, nima kan, m ga ŋmaa li bi bi chee. Min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.

english_text:
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 37.25-28)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense. 2Make it 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high, and make each of its four corners stick up like the horn of a bull. 3Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 4Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar. 5These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
6Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there. 7-8From now on, when Aaron takes care of the lamps each morning and evening, he must burn sweet-smelling incense to me on the altar. 9Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings. 10 Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me.
The Money for the Sacred Tent
11The Lord said to Moses:
12Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them. 13-15 Each man over 19, whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards. 16This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 38.8)
17The Lord said to Moses:
18-21 Make a large bronze bowl and a bronze stand for it. Then put them between the altar for sacrifice and the sacred tent, so the priests can wash their hands and feet before entering the tent or offering a sacrifice on the altar. Each priest in every generation must wash himself in this way, or else he will die right there.
The Oil for Dedication and Ordination
(Exodus 37.29)
22 The Lord said to Moses:
23-25Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture 26for dedicating the tent and chest, 27the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils, 28the altar for sacrifices, and the large bowl with its stand. 29By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
30When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil, 31and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord. 32So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves. 33If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.”
The Sweet-Smelling Incense
34-35Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy. 36Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy. 37It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves. 38If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_text:
Baah ga li seer tulalee aayon kitork aabimbiln li paab na aabɔr
(Nnyam 37.25-28)
1“Ni di lisiijal aadɔ ki di ŋa tiwan ni pu ni ga li seer tulalee aayon na. 2Ni li bi likpakpaln, naafɔfɔk li ye ŋisaŋ ŋitaa, naawawaan li ye ŋisaŋ ŋitaa, le naafɔfɔk paacham li ye ŋisaŋ ŋiloob. Naamɔchɔn ŋinaa na, ni nima li ye liwanbaal. 3Ni di salmaa aakur donn biin ni paacham, ni ŋimɔgben ŋinaa, ni ŋimɔchɔn ŋinaa, ki ŋa salmaa aakuul mann gonn ni. 4Ni ki ŋa salmaa aabuen ilee, ki di baan ŋimɔgben aataab, nin chee idɔ i ni ga li joo yoor u na, ki di i bɔ mu ni. 5Ni di lisiijal aadɔ ki ŋa idɔ ngbaan, ki donn salmaa aakur ŋmeen biin i pu. 6Ni di tulalee aayon aabimbiln ngbaan ki di siin likekeln li gbin Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa chee na aapuwɔb. M ga dan nima, ni chee. 7Kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni, n‑yoonn mu Aaronn ti dan u nan toor ki gor karyaa tiib na kan, u ti see tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ na nima chee. 8U yaa ki dan u nan see karyaa tiib kijook wɔb kan, u ki ŋa kina. Ni li seer tulalee aayon ngbaan tii mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, nibaa taa kiir nimi. 9Ni taa di tulalee aayon mu maa gee na ki di see nima chee, ki taa toor kiwakork aatork, bee njikaabim aatork li pu, ki taa bar ŋisubil aadaan kpir li pu. 10Libiln ponn ni kan, Aaronn ti di kiwakork ki u di toor titunwanbir aachapinn na aasin, ki di gbaa ŋimɔchɔn ŋinaa pu nfum mbaa aan ki ŋa li chain. Ŋibin mɔmɔk ni kan, u ti ŋa kina nfum mbaa. Tulalee aayon aabimbiln ngbaan li bi chain, ni di li tii min Uwumbɔr.”
Uwumbɔr aah bi Libool li ponn ni na aalampoo aabɔr
11Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, 12“Tɔ, aa yaa ti kahn Israel yaab ki bee baah bi pu na kan, bi mɔmɔk ga ti pa tipar tii mi, baamɔfal pu, nima kan, falaa ubaa aan dan bi pu buyoonn bi bi kahn bi na. 13Baah kahn bimɔk na ga pa ŋimombil ŋeer baah siin pu na. Bi mɔmɔk pa kina aapiin tii mi. 14Baah kahn umɔk aan u fuu ŋibin moninko ki jer na ŋeer u pa kina aamombil tii mi. 15Bi yaa ban bi pa ŋimombil ngbaan baamɔfal pu kan, uwankpadaan taa pa jer, ugiin mu taa pa bar. 16Ni gaa ŋimombil ngbaan Israel yaab chee, ki li joo toor Maabool li m bi li ponn ni na. Lampoo ngbaan aamombil le ye baamɔfal aapar, le m ga li kii bi.”
Tikumann aakur aasambil
17Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, 18“Di tikumann aakur ŋa lisambil aan li li kpa lipɔtaln, ki li ye tikumann aakur ŋmeen, ki di li siin Libool ni kitork aabimbiln aakaasisik ni, ki ban nnyun ŋa li ponn ni. 19Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib ga li joo nnyun ngbaan le finn biŋaal ni bitaa, 20le ki nin koo Libool ngbaan ni, bee bi nin buen ti toor tijikaar aatork. Nima kan, baan kpo. 21Bi li finni biŋaal ni bitaa, ki taa kpo. Bi ni baamaal li joo nkaal ngbaan ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
Nkpan mu bi joo ŋani Uwumbɔr aanib, ni waawan pu na aabɔr
22Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, 23“Di mbaabil ŋi nu mɔ na, ni li ye mir aanyun kuruwaa biloob, ni tiwan ni nu mɔ aan bi yin ni ke sinamonn na kuruwaa bitaa, ni ŋibun aayon kuruwaa bitaa, 24ni nsupuun mu nu mɔ na kuruwaa biloob. Ni di tiwan ni bi joo ŋaŋni tiwan Maabool ponn ni na ŋaŋ ni mɔmɔk, ki di olif aakpan galaŋ ubaa di kpee, 25aan ki ŋa maakpan tii mi. Aa di ni mɔmɔk ŋmal tɔb ni ke tulalee na. 26Aa di mu meen Maabool, ni Maakaal Aadakaa, 27ni teebul, ni waawan mɔmɔk, ni karyaa tiib aah tɔŋni tiwan ni pu na, ni naawan mɔmɔk, ni tulalee aayon aabimbiln, 28ni libimbiln li bi seer kitork li paab na, ni laawan mɔmɔk, ni lisambil li bi joo nnyun ŋani ki finni biŋaal ni bitaa na, ni laapɔtaln ni. 29Ni ŋa tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk kina aan ni ŋa chain, le unii, bee tiwan taa meeh maawan ngbaan nibaa, see u mu ye chain. 30Aa di mu kpir Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aayil pu ki ŋa bi bitotoorb aan bi li tun tii mi. 31Bui Israel aanib ngbaan ke, ‘Maakpan mu bi chain na, ni li joo mu tun lituln kina n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 32Ni taa di nkpan ngbaan ki di kpir unii u kaa ye utotoor na pu, ki taa di tiwan nimɔk ni di ŋa nkpan ngbaan na ki di ŋa nkpan muken. Mu ye chain aakpan la, nima pu na, ni li joo mu chain. 33Unii ubaa yaa ŋa nkpan ngbaan aaboln, bee u yaa di mu ki di meen unii u kaa ye utotoor na kan, waan ki li ye maanii.’”
Tulalee aayon
34Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, “Ban mbaabil ŋi nu mɔ na. Ŋaayimbil sɔ, stakte, ni onika, ni galbanum, ni frankinsense aatulalee, ki cha ni mɔmɔk li ŋak tɔb. 35Aa di tiwan ngbaan kpaan ki ŋmal ni ke tulalee na, ki ban n‑yaan ŋa ni ponn ni, ni li bi chain ki taa bii. 36Aa ban ngem ki san, ni ŋa n‑yon, ki di koo Maabool ponn ni, aan ki ti di ni yɔk Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aanimbiin ni. Aa li joo tulalee aayon ngbaan chain. 37Ni taa di maah mɔk nimi tiwan ni na ŋa tulalee kina aaboln ki li joo nibaa. Ni li joo tulalee aayon ngbaan chain ki di u tii mi baanja. 38Unii ubaa yaa ŋa tulalee kina aaboln ki joo u kan, waan ki li ye maanii.”

english_text:
The Lord Chooses Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 35.30—36.1)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings. 3-5Not only have I filled him with my Spirit, but I have given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 6I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you: 7-11the sacred tent with its furnishings, the sacred chest with its place of mercy, the table with all that is on it, the lamp with its equipment, the incense altar, the altar for sacrifices with its equipment, the bronze bowl with its stand, the beautiful priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons, the oil for dedication and ordination services, and the sweet-smelling incense for the holy place.
Laws for the Sabbath
12-13Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said:
The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own. 14-15 Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
16Every generation of Israelites must respect the Sabbath. 17 This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
18When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_text:
Binib bi ga ŋmaa ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool aawan na
(Nnyam 35.30–36.1)
1Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, 2“M lee Uri aajapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Besalel u ye Hur aayaabil ki nyan ni Juda aanibol ni na, 3le ki gbiin u min Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn. M cha u kpa ŋuntii, ki kpa nlan ki nyi tiwan mɔmɔk aatuln, 4u kpa nlandak ki nyi waah ga di salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni tikumann, 5ki donn ŋa tiwanyaan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ pu na, ki geei ŋitakpanyaan, ki kpii tiwanyaan aabɔŋ mu. 6M ki nyan Ahisamak aajapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Oholiab, ki nyan ni Dann aanibol ni na, ke u ter u. M ki tii binib bi mu nyi tiwan mɔmɔk aatuln na nlan, ke bi ŋmaa ŋa tiwan ni mɔmɔk m tuk bi ke bi ŋa na. 7Bi ga ŋa Maabool, ni Maakaal Aadakaa ni waabiil, ni Libool ngbaan aawan mɔmɔk, 8ni teebul ni waawan mɔmɔk, ni karyaa tiib aah tɔŋni salmaa aawan ni pu na, ni naawan mɔmɔk, ni baah seer tulalee aayon nin chee na, 9ni baah seer kitork nin chee na, ni naawan mɔmɔk, ni nnyun aasambil, ni laapɔtaln, 10ni bitotoorb aawanpeenkaanyaan ki tii Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib, bi li joo tun kitork aatuln, 11ni maakpan, ni tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ, aan bi joo ŋani Chain Aapepel ni na. Bi yaa ban bi ŋa tiwan ngbaan kan, bi ŋa ni mɔmɔk maah mɔk si pu na.”
Likpaakool daal, lifuur aawiin daal
12Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses 13ke u tuk Israel yaab ke, “Ni li joo likpaakool daal, nwiin mundaal ni ga fuur na; ba pu? mu ye limɔkl, le ki mɔk ke tipuur bi m ni nimi aakaasisik ni ki cha n‑yoonn mu choo na, le ki mɔk ke min Uwumbɔr le lee nimi, ni li ye maanib. 14Ni li joo lifuur aawiin ngbaan; ba pu? mu bi chain. Unii umɔk yii, kaa joo mu chain, ki tun lituln nwiin ngbaan daal na kan, ni ku u. 15Ni kpa iwiin iloob, ni li tun nibaa aatuln, le winlole daal ngbaan ye lifuur aawiin le tii min. Umɔk tun lituln liyaadaal ngbaan na kan, ni ku u. 16Israel yaab li joo nwiin mue daal, mu li ye tipuur aamɔkl. 17Ni ga li ye limɔkl le m ni Israel yaab chee; ba pu? Min Uwumbɔr le di iwiin iloob naan paacham ni kitiŋ, le winlole daal m doo lituln, ki kal fuur.”
18N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr len Moses chee tibɔr doo, Sainai Aajool paab na, le u di ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi uma Uwumbɔr ubaa ŋmee waakaal ŋi pu na di tii u.

english_text:
The People Make an Idol To Worship
(Deuteronomy 9.6-29)
1 After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
2Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.” 3Everybody took off their earrings and brought them to Aaron, 4 then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull.
All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
5When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.” 6 The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
7The Lord said to Moses:
Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools. 8They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt. 9Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are, 10and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
11 Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind:
Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them. 12If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
13 Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
14So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
15-16Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
17When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
18But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
19As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain. 20He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it. 21Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
22Aaron answered:
Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil. 23They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.” 24Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
25Moses knew that the people were out of control and that it was Aaron's fault. And now they had made fools of themselves in front of their enemies. 26So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!”
Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses, 27and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
28The men of the Levi tribe followed his orders, and that day they killed about 3,000 men. 29Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
30The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
31Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god. 32 But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
33The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me. 34Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
35So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_text:
Salmaa aanaaja
(Ikaal 9.6-29)
1N‑yoonn mu binib ngbaan nan bee ke Moses yunn lijool ngbaan paab, kaa sunn ni, ki bi nima chee na, le bi kuun ni ki mann goln Aaronn, le ki bui u ke, “Taa nyi tiwan ni ŋa Moses u nan nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na aan waa gir ni na, nima pu na, ŋa liwaal tii timi, ti li dii li.”
2Le Aaronn bui bi ke, “Chuu nyan ni tafajɔn bi nipuutiib, ni nijapɔtiib, ni nibisatiib tuu na, ki li joo ni bi man.” 3Nima pu le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan chuun nyan ni baasalmaa aatafajɔn le ki joo ni Aaronn chee. 4Le u gaa tafajɔn ngbaan le ki donn bi, le ki di kpaar ŋa tiwan ni naahn unaa na ni, le ni kpaln salmaa aanaajabo.
Le binib ngbaan bui ke, “Timi Israel yaab aawaal li nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na le na.”
5Nima chee le Aaronn nan maa kitork aabimbiln, salmaa aanaajabo ngbaan aanimbiin ni, le ki moon ke, “Fen kan, ti ga fe ŋa kitork aajim ki nyuŋ Uwumbɔr.” 6Le ni woln kichakpiik ni, le bi joo ni tiwakor ke bi toor kitork ki di see mmii ni, ki di tiken ŋa tijikaar ki kpaan ji tɔb chee. Le binib ngbaan kal bi ji njim ngbaan, le ni ti kpaln lidanyul ni kidagook aatuln.
7Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, “Gir sunn mala, ba pu? saanib bi aa nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na tun titunwanbir, ki yii mi a. 8Maah mɔk bi ke bi li dii mi pu na, bi di lii a, le ki donn salmaa ŋa unaajabo ki dooni u, ki toor kitork tii u, le ki len ke baawaal sɔ, uma le nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 9M nyi binib ngbaan aasui aah pɔɔ sakpen pu na. 10Nimina ma kan, taa ki gaŋ mi. Liŋuul chuu mi sakpen, le m ga bii bi. M ga tee cha aa ni saamaal ma pɔr ki ŋa linibol sakpeln.”
11Tɔ, Moses nan gaŋ Udindaan Uwumbɔr le ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr, ba ŋa aa cha saaŋuul fii saanib pu sakpen kina, naa ye saapɔɔn sakpiin pu le aa nan di nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni ii? 12Aa ban ke Ijipt yaab len ke aa nyan ni saanib Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ke aa nan ku bi ŋijoo ŋee ni, ki bii bi kookoo la aa? Cha saaŋuul sɔŋ, ki kpeln saalandak, ki taa bii saanib ngbaan kina. 13Teer saanaagbiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob bɔr. Teer tipuur bamɔnn ti aa nan puu, ke aa ga cha bi maa ki pɔr, ki li wiir ke iŋmabi i bi kitaapaak na, ki di kitiŋ ki aa nan puu ke aa ga di tii bi, aan bi li yeh ki n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na bɔr.” 14Nima pu na, Uwumbɔr nan kpeln waalandak, le kaa ki daa bitafal waah nan dak pu na.
15Le Moses gir sunn ni lijool ngbaan aataab, ki joo ni ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi Uwumbɔr ŋmee ikaal ŋi pu na. 16Uwumbɔr ubaa le nan kpii ŋitakpal ngbaan, le ki ŋmee ikaal ngbaan paan ŋi pu.
17Tɔ, Josua nan ŋun binib ngbaan kpa kifuuk, le u bui Moses ke, “M ŋun butɔb aafuuk linampal.”
18Le Moses nan bui u ke, “Kifuuk ngbaan aa ye ke bi kan linyaŋ la, ki mu aa ki ye ke bi san dii bi la, ni ye ilahn le bi gaa ki kpa kifuuk.”
19N‑yoonn mu Moses fuu ni linampal ki kan unaajabo aawaal, aan binib ngbaan bi waa liwaal linimbiin ni na, le liŋuul chuu u. Le u di ŋitakpapapan na di lii lijool ngbaan aataab, le ŋi wii. 20U nan donn unaajabo u bi nan mɔɔ na, le ki san u, u ti kpaln n‑yon, le ki di buun nnyun ni, ki di tii binib ngbaan le bi nyun. 21Le u baa Aaronn ke, “Binib ngbaan ŋa si kinye, aan aa cha bi tun titunwanbir sakpen timina aaboln?”
22Aaronn nan giin bui u ke, “Uninkpel, taa gee liŋuul m pu; aa nyi binib ngbaan aanimbil aah man ke bi tun ni kaa ŋan na pu na. 23Bi bui mi ke, ‘Moses, uma le nan nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, taa nyi tiwan ni ŋa u aan u ti yunn sakpen kina na, nima pu na, ŋa liwaal tii timi.’ 24Le m bui bi ke bi li joo ni salmaa aatafajɔn tiib, le binib bi kpa na joo ni nan tii mi. Le m donn bi mmii ni, ki di ŋa unaajabo ngbaan.”
25Moses nan kan ke Aaronn le cha binib ngbaan gaa bibaa ki ŋa kijɔrk aatuln, baadim aanimbil ni. 26Nima chee le u sil mbisamɔb chee le ki teen ke, “Ŋma si Uwumbɔr aachaŋ ni na? Udaan nyan ni ki dan m chee.” Nima pu na, Liifai aamaal nan buen ti sil gbaŋ u. 27Le u bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr, u ye nimi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui ke, ‘Nimi bi si uchaŋ ni na di nimi aajaak aajum ki bɔ dii binib bi gur na ni, ki ku nina aabim, ni nijɔtiib, ni nido yaab mɔmɔk.’” 28Liifai aamaal ngbaan nan kii, le ki ku binib ŋichur ŋitaa liyaadaal ngbaan. 29Le Moses bui Liifai aamaal ngbaan ke, “Din wee, ni toor nibaa ki mɔk ke ni ye Uwumbɔr aatotoorb, nima le cha ni ku nijapɔtiib ni nina aabim, nima pu na, Uwumbɔr mu ŋa waanyoor ŋa ni pu.”
30Naah woln kitaak na, le Moses bui binib ngbaan ke, “Ni tun titunwanbir pam. Tɔ, m ga ki gir buen lijool ngbaan paab Uwumbɔr chee; nibaakan, ni ga kan chapinn nimi aatunwanbir pu.” 31Moses nan ki gir buen Uwumbɔr chee ki ti bui ke, “Binib ngbaan tun titunwanbir pam. Bi di salmaa le ŋa liwaal le ki dooni li. 32Uwumbɔr, di cha pinn bi baatunwanbir; aa yaa kaan ŋa kina kan, chuu ber maayimbil kigbaŋ ki aa ŋmee saanib aayimbil ki ponn ni na.”
33Le Uwumbɔr giin bui u ke, “Ni ye binib bi tun titunwanbir m chee na aayimbil le m ga ber maagbaŋ ni. 34Tɔ, siir ki li cha, ki ti loln binib ngbaan pu nsan, ki buen nin chee m bui si na. Teer ke maatuun ga loln ni pu nsan; tɔ, n‑yoonn choo le m ga daa binib ngbaan aatafal, baatunwanbir pu.”
35Nima pu na, Uwumbɔr nan daa bitafal ki cha iween i bir na lir bi pu, ba pu? bi nan muk Aaronn le u ti ŋa salmaa aanaajabo aawaal tii bi.

english_text:
The Lord Tells Israel To Leave Mount Sinai
1 The Lord said to Moses:
You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 2-3It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
4-5Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning, 6and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry.
The Lord Is with His People
7Moses used to set up a tent far from camp. He called it the “meeting tent,” and whoever needed some message from the Lord would go there. 8Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter. 9-11Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent.
The Lord Promises To Be with His People
12Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me. 13If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
14The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
15Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place. 16But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
17So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
18Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
19 The Lord answered:
All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name, 20but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die. 21There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it, 22and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by. 23Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah nan bui Israel yaab ke bi fii Sainai Aajool chee ki li cha pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, “Fii do, aa ni binib bi aa nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, ki li cha kitiŋ ki m puu tii Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob, ni biyaabitiib na ni. 2M ga cha maatuun loln ni pu nsan, le m ga jenn nyan Kanaann yaab, ni Amor yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab. 3Ni cha kitiŋ ki kpa nkpan, ni n‑yaan, ki nyuun na ni la. Min mbaa aan dii nimi buen; ba pu? nitafal aah pɔɔ pu na, nibaakan m ga ti kuln nimi nsan ni.”
4N‑yoonn mu binib ngbaan ŋun kina na, le bisui bii, baa ki peeni salmaa aawan kpala, 5ba pu? Uwumbɔr le nan bui Moses ke u tuk binib ngbaan ke, “Nitafal pɔɔ pam. Nibaakan, m yaa ban m dii nimi foor siib kan, m ga kuln nimi kookoo. Tɔ, chuu nyan nimi aasalmaa aaleen, aan m dakl lik maah ga ŋa nimi pu na.” 6Nima pu na, baah nyan Sainai Aajool chee ki cha na, binib ngbaan aa nan ki peeni salmaa aaleen kpala.
Uwumbɔr aah bi Libool li ponn ni na aabɔr
7N‑yoonn mumɔk Israel aanib ngbaan ti kal nin chee na kan, le Moses di Uwumbɔr Aabool li bi chain na ti gaa dandar. U nan yin li ke Uwumbɔr aah bi Libool li ponn ni na, le unii umɔk nan ban u baa Uwumbɔr tibɔr na kan, le u ti buen li chee. 8N‑yoonn mu Moses buen nima na kan, le binib ngbaan nya sil baadir aabisamɔi, le ki lik Moses le u ti koo li ponn ni. 9Moses yaa ti koo li ponn ni kan, le ntaalangbam dan nan sil Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb, le Uwumbɔr len Moses chee tibɔr ntaalangbam ngbaan ponn ni. 10Binib ngbaan yaa ti kan ntaalangbam ngbaan kan, le bi ti gbaan kitiŋ. 11Le Uwumbɔr len Moses chee tibɔr, le ni bi ke unii ni ujɔ le aah bi len tɔb chee na. Le Moses ki gir buen linampal. Le unachipɔɔn u nan ter u, bi yin u ke Josua aan u ye Nunn aajapɔɔn na ma ti bee Libool ngbaan ni.
Uwumbɔr puu ke u ga li bi waanib chee
12Moses nan bui Uwumbɔr ke, “Ni ye mbamɔn ke aa tuk mi ke m loln binib ngbaan pu nsan, ki di bi buen kitiŋ ngbaan ni, tɔ, saa tuk mi u ga cheen mi na. Aa bui ke aa nyi mi, ki gee maabɔr mbamɔm. 13Ni yaa ye kina kan, tuk mi saalandak, nima kan, m ga dii si ki piir aasui n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Teer ke sin le lee linibol ngbaan ke bi li ye saanib.”
14Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “M mamaŋ ga dii si buen, le ki ga tii si lifuur.”
15Moses nan giin bui u ke, “Aa yaa kaan dii timi kan, taa cha ti nya do ki buen. 16Aa yaa kaa dii timi buen kan, ni ga ŋa kinye aan unii bee ke aasui piin m ni saanib pu? Saah bi ti chee pu na le ga cha ti ni biken aabimbin taa li kpaa dulnyaa wee ni.”
17Uwumbɔr nan gar Moses ke, “M ga ŋa saah mee pu na, ba pu? m nyi si, le nsui piin aa pu mbamɔm.”
18Le Moses mee ke, “Uwumbɔr, kina kan, cha m kan si, saawiihn mu moor ki deer ŋinimbil na ni.”
19Le Uwumbɔr ki bui u ke, “M ga cha maajilmaa aawiihn ngbaan jer aanimbiin ni, le m ga yin maayimbil li bi chain na. Min le ye Uwumbɔr, le ki kpa linimbaasaln unii u m lee u na pu. 20Maan cha aa kan nnimbil wɔb, ba pu? unii ubaa aan ŋmaa kan mi ki ki li fu; 21m chee do, mpaan mubaa bi litakpal lee pu aa ga ŋmaa sil. 22N‑yoonn mu maawiihn mu moor ki deer ŋinimbil na yaa nan jer kan, m ga di si siin kitakpaluŋ kee ni, ki di ŋŋaal biin aa pu, aan ki ti jer doo. 23M ga chuu nyan ŋŋaal aa pu, le aa ga kan mpuwɔb ki taa kan nnimbil wɔb.”

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Deuteronomy 10.1-5)
1One day the Lord said to Moses, “Cut two flat stones like the first ones I made, and I will write on them the same commandments that were on the two you broke. 2Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. 3No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.” 4So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
5The Lord God came down in a cloud and stood beside Moses there on the mountain. God spoke his holy name, “the Lord.” 6 Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted. 7I keep my promises to my people forever, but I also punish anyone who sins. When people sin, I punish them and their children, and also their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.”
8Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord. 9He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.”
A Promise and Its Demands
(Exodus 23.14-19; Deuteronomy 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10The Lord said:
I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things. 11I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today. 12Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap. 13 Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah. 14I demand your complete loyalty—you must not worship any other god! 15Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals. 16Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
17 Don't make metal images of gods.
18 Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
19 The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
20 You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son.
Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
21 Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting. 22 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
23Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel. 24As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
25 When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
26 I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
27The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel. 28Moses stayed on the mountain with the Lord for 40 days and nights, without eating or drinking. And he wrote down the Ten Commandments, the most important part of God's agreement with his people.
Moses Comes Down from Mount Sinai
29 Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining. 30When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him. 31Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them. 32Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
33The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil. 34Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say. 35They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah nan ki ŋmee ikaal lelee pu na
(Ikaal 10.1-5)
1Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, “Kpii ŋitakpal ŋilee, ŋi li bi ke njan yee na, aan m ki ŋmee ŋi pu ŋimɔbon ŋi nan bi njan yee, ŋi aa nan di lii wii na. 2Gor aabaa, aan kichakpiik ni kan, aa fe dan Sainai Aajool paab m chee nima. 3Ubaa taa dii ni si; ubaa taa cha m kan u lijool chee nima; kiwakork kibaa taa dan lijool ngbaan taab ki nan ŋmɔ timoor.” 4Le Moses nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah len pu na, ki kpii ŋitakpal ŋilee ngbaan. Naah woln kichakpiik ni na, le u di ŋi jon Sainai Aajool ngbaan paab.
5Le Uwumbɔr sunn ni ntaalangbam ponn ni, ki nan sil u chee nima, le ki yin ubaa ke U‑ye‑na u aayimbil bi chain na. 6Uwumbɔr nan jer unimbiin ni le ki bui u ke, “Min, U‑ye‑na, min le ye Uwumbɔr u kpa linimbaasaln, kaa gee liŋuul yɔl yɔl na, ki gee binib mbamɔm, ki ŋani maah len pu na. 7M joo maah puu tipuur ti na le ti ye ki tii mmaal lichur, le ki cha pinni titunwanbir; mmaal mu aatetiib tun titunwanbir na kan, m ga daa biyaabitiib ni biyaabisɔsɔk aatafal.”
8Moses nan gbaan kitiŋ mala le ki doon u, 9le ki bui ke, “Ndindaan, maabimbin yaa piir aasui kan, m mee si ke aa dii timi buen. Binib ngbaan aasui pɔɔ pam. Cha pinn timi aataani, ni timi aatunwanbir, aan ki cha ti li ye saanib.”
Uwumbɔr aah ki fikr waah puu tipuur ti na
(Nnyam 23.14-19; Ikaal 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, “M ki puu tipuur Israel yaab chee la. M ga ŋa lijinjiir aatuln li kaa kee ŋa dulnyaa wee ni na, binimbil ni. Le binib mɔmɔk ga kan litukpaan li min Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa ŋa na; ba pu? m ga ŋa lijinjiir aawan tii nimi. 11Ni li kpa ŋuntii ki joo cha ikaal i m di mɔk nimi din wee na wɔb. M ga jenn nyan Amor yaab, ni Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab, naah ga li tur koo bi ponn ni pu na. 12Ni taa kpaan binib ngbaan chee ki ŋa kimɔbaan; ba pu? ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga cha ni yenn. 13Ni gbaa wii baawaa aatork aabimbin, ni ŋitakpal ŋi bi dooni na, ki bii baawaapii li bi yin li ke Asera na, ni laawan mɔmɔk.
14“Ni taa doon liwaal libaa; ba pu? Min, Uwumbɔr aan kii ke Israel yaab li dooni tiwan nibaa ki kpee m pu. 15Ni taa kpaan binib ngbaan chee ki ŋa kimɔbaan, ba pu? n‑yoonn mu bi toor baawaa na kan, bi ga chɔi nimi, ni ji kitork aajikaar ngbaan. 16Nibaakan, nijapɔtiib mu ga yoor bibisatiib, le bibisatiib ngbaan ga fenn nijapɔtiib aasui, le bi ga yii mi ki dii binib ngbaan aawaa.
17“Ni taa di tikur ŋa liwaal ki li dooni li.
18“Ni li ji boroboro u kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na aajim. N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, ni li ŋmɔ boroboro u kaa kpa nnyɔk na ki ti saa iwiin ilole, Abib aaŋmal ni, ba pu? uŋmal ngbaan ni, le ni nan nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ni.
19“Israel yaab aah ma njan aabijabim bi na, ni baawakor aajan aabim mɔmɔk ye min yaan la, 20tɔ, see ni ki gir di upihjabo kpeln ibon aajan aabim m chee. Ni yaa kaan kpeln kan, ni nyii koo usil. Nimi aabijabim ma kan, see ni ki gir daa bi m chee.
“Unii umɔk choo nnimbiin ni ke u nan doon mi na kan, u li joo ni ipiin.
21“Ni kpa iwiin iloob le ni di tun nimi aatuln, ni taa tun nibaa winlole daal, ni yaa ye likuul yoonn, bee liwancheel yoonn kan, ni taa tun nibaa liyaadaal ngbaan.
22“Ni li ji Ndipɔndaan Aajim n‑yoonn mu ni piin ki bi chee njikaabim na, ki li ji Tikakar Aajim buyoonn ni ti kuun tijikaar doo na.
23“Libiln ni kan, ni dan ki nan doon min, nimi Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr, u ni dii u na, nfum mutaa. 24Buyoonn m ti jenn nyan ŋinibol ŋimɔk bi ni chee aan ki taln nimi aatiŋ na, ubaa aan ki tak nimi njim mutaa mue aayoonn.
25“N‑yoonn mu ni di kiwakork toor kitork na kan, ni taa di boroboro u kpa nnyɔk na kpaan tii mi. Ni yaa di kiwakork toor Lakr‑jer Aajim aatork kan, ni taa cha tinann ngbaan gur ki woln kitaak.
26“Ni li joo ni njan aajikaar ti pue biir nimi aasar ni na, ki di dan min Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni ki nan tii mi.
“Ni taa di upiih, bee uŋoob aabiin ŋaa waabo.”
27Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, “Ŋmee tibɔr ngbaan bil; ba pu? tibɔr tee pu le m ga puu tipuur tii sin ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk.” 28Le Moses nan bi Uwumbɔr chee nima nwiin pu ni kinyeek ki ti saa iwiin imonko ilee, kaa ji, kaa nyu. Le u ŋmee tipuur aakaal kipiik na, ŋitakpapapan ŋilee na pu.
Moses aah nan sunn ni Sainai Aajool taab pu na
29N‑yoonn mu Moses nan sunn ni Sainai Aajool taab ki joo ni Ikaal kipiik na, le unimbil wɔb moor; ba pu? u nan bi Uwumbɔr chee, le u ni u len tɔb chee tibɔr; Moses ma aa nan nyi kina ubaa. 30Aaronn ni binib ngbaan aah nan lik Moses aanimbil wɔb na, le bi kan ni moor; le baa kaa ke bi buen u chee. 31Le Moses yin bi, le Aaronn ni Israel yaab aaninkpiib buen u chee, le Moses ti len bi chee tibɔr. 32Nee aapuwɔb, le Israel yaab mɔmɔk buen ti sil mann gonn u; le Moses di ikaal imɔk Uwumbɔr di tii u lijool paab na, ki di tuk bi. 33Moses aah len bi chee tibɔr doo na, le u di likekeln biin unimbil pu. 34N‑yoonn mu Moses ti buen Uwumbɔr Aabool ni, u ti len u chee na kan, le u chuu biir likekeln ngbaan unimbil wɔb. U yaa ti nyan ni kan, le u tuk Israel aanib ngbaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na, 35le bi ti kan ke unimbil wɔb moor. Le u ki di likekeln ngbaan biin unimbil pu, see u ti ki gir cha Uwumbɔr chee.

english_text:
Laws for the Sabbath
1Moses called together the people of Israel and told them that the Lord had said:
2 You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death. 3Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath.
Offerings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 25.1-9; 35.10-19)
4Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
5I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze; 6blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 7tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood; 8olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or 9onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
10If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded: 11the sacred tent with its covering and hooks, its framework and crossbars, and its post and stands; 12the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it; 13the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 14the lamp with its equipment and oil; 15the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent; 16the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 17the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance; 18the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard; 19and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
Gifts for the Lord
20Moses finished speaking, and everyone left. 21Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes. 22Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. 23Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather. 24Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
25The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made. 26And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
27The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest. 28They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests. 29Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts.
Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 31.1-11)
30Moses said to the people of Israel:
The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe. 31-33Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 34The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others. 35And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_text:
Likpaakool daal aabɔr
1Moses nan yin Israel yaab mɔmɔk ki kuun ni bi ubaa chee, le ki nan bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr aah bui ke m tuk nimi pu na sɔ: 2ni kpa iwiin iloob, ni li tun nibaa aatuln, winlole daal ma kan, ni li joo mu chain, ni di mu tii mi Uwumbɔr, nwiin ngbaan li ye lifuur daal. Unii umɔk tun lituln nwiin ngbaan daal na kan, ni ku u. 3Uwumbɔr aakpaakool ngbaan daal kan, ubaa taa tuur mmii udo lichiln ni.”
Uwumbɔr Aabool aapiin aabɔr
(Nnyam 25.1-9)
4Moses nan ki bui Israel yaab ngbaan mɔmɔk ke, “Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: 5Tiin Uwumbɔr ipiin man. Unii umɔk ban u ŋa kina na kan, u li joo ni salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni tikumann, 6ni ŋitanyaan, ni ŋitambɔn, ni ŋitaman, ni tiŋɔkor aakeken, 7ni ipihja aagbaman, ni igbanyaan, ni lisiijal aadɔ, 8ni nkpan mu bi joo seer karyaa tiib na, ni tulalee u bi joo ŋmalni Uwumbɔr aakpan ni na, ni tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ na; 9ni ŋitakpanyaan ŋi bi ga di ŋa Utotoorninkpel aabɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na, ni liwapapaln li bi ubiŋ pu na.
Uwumbɔr Aabool aawan
(Nnyam 39.32-43)
10“Bijab bi nyi baatuln mbamɔm na, nimi le ga nyan ni ki ŋa Uwumbɔr aah tuk nimi pu na. 11Waah ban ni ŋa tiwan ni na sɔ: Libool ngbaan, ni baah ga li joo tiwan ni biini li pu na nilee, ni ipigɔrkee, ni tiwon, ni idɔpuinkee, ni idɔja, ni idɔ i dɔ taab na, 12ni Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa, ni waadɔ, ni waabiil, ni likekeln li bi ga di kiir u na, 13ni teebul, ni waadɔ, ni waawan mɔmɔk, ni boroboro u ni ga di tii Uwumbɔr na, 14ni karyaa tiib aah ga li tɔŋni tiwan ni pu na, ni waawan mɔmɔk, ni karyaa tiib ni baakpan, 15ni tulalee aayon aabimbiln, ni laadɔja, ni Uwumbɔr aakpan, ni tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ na, ni mbisamɔb aakekeln, 16ni baah ga li seer ipiin aatork ni pu na aabimbiln, ni tikumann aaŋulk ki tak li na, ki kpee laadɔja ni laawan mɔmɔk, ni lisambil li bi ga li ŋir biŋaal li ponn ni na, ni laapɔtaln, 17ni ŋikeken ŋi bi ga di gob mann Libool ngbaan na, ni idɔja, ni idɔ i dɔ taab na, ni mbisamɔb aakekeln, 18ni ikpaa, ni iŋmin, 19ni ŋibɔkunyaan ŋi bitotoorb ga li joo peeni n‑yoonn mu bi yaa ti ban bi tun lituln, chain aapepel ni na, ŋi ye ŋikekenyaan ŋi Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib bi ye bitotoorb na ga li peeni na.”
Baah nan tii Uwumbɔr baapiin pu na
20Israel aanib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan siir, 21le binib bi mɔmɔk nan gee ke bi tii na nan joo ni baapiin nan tii Uwumbɔr, bi di ŋa Waabool. Bi nan joo ni tiwan nimɔk bi ga li joo dooni Uwumbɔr na, ni baah ga di ni ŋal bitotoorb aawanpeenkaan na. 22Binib bi mɔmɔk nan gee bi tii na, bijab ni bipiib mɔmɔk, nan joo ni ipinbi waatiir i ŋan na, ni tafajɔn tiib, ni mbɔmbim, ni neeni aakuleen, ki kpee salmaa aawan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ, le ki di tii Uwumbɔr. 23Unii umɔk nan kpa ŋitanyaan, ni upiih aakur ti man chaun na, ni nsiin, ni timann, ni tiŋɔkor aakekeln; ni ipihgbaman, ni igbanyaan, bi nan joo ni nimɔk. 24Binib bimɔk nan kpa tikunabr, bee tikumann na, nan joo ni baah ga ŋmaa tii pu na, le ki nan tii Uwumbɔr baapiin, le binib bi nan kpa lisiijal aadɔ bi ga ŋmaa di i ŋa nibaa na, mu nan joo ni. 25Bipiib bi mɔmɔk ŋmaa fik tikokonn na nan joo ni tikokonn ti ŋan na, ni tibɔmbɔnn, ni timamann, ni tikur mamann aakokonn mu. 26Bi nan di tiŋɔkor mu fik tikokonn ki joo ni. 27Le bisalolm joo ni ŋitakpanyaan aabɔŋ, bi di ŋa utotoor aabɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na, ni kibiŋ aakekengeŋ na mu, 28ni mbaabil, ni nkpan mu bi ga li joo ŋani karyaa tiib ponn ni, ni Uwumbɔr aakpan, ni tulalee aayon mu na. 29Le Israel aanib bimɔk nan gee bi tii na nan joo ni baapiin ki nan tii Uwumbɔr, waah nan bui Moses lituln li na pu.
Binib bi ga ŋmaa ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool aawan na
(Nnyam 31.1-11)
30Moses nan ki bui Israel yaab ke, “Uwumbɔr lee Uri aajapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Besalel, aan u ye Hur aayaabil na, ki nyan ni Juda aanibol ni na. 31Uwumbɔr gbiin u mpɔɔn, le ki tii u nnyim, ni nlan, ni mbeem, ke u li nyi tiwanyaan aatuln mɔmɔk, 32le u kpa nlandak ki nyi waah ga di salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni tikumann ki donn ŋa tiwanyaan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ pu na, 33le ki nyi waah ga gii ŋitakpanyaan pu ki ŋeer waah ban pu na; ki ŋmaa kpii tiwan aabɔŋ, ki nyi tiwanyaan aatuln mɔmɔk. 34Uwumbɔr di kina aalan ki di tii u ni Ahisamak aajapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Oholiab aan u nyan ni Dann aanibol ni na, ke bi di baah nyi pu na mɔk biken. 35U cha bi ŋmaa kpii ŋitakpanyaan pu, bee tikunabr pu, ki ŋmee ki naani tiwan aabɔŋ ni pu, ki ŋmaa joo tikokonn luu ŋitanyaan, ni ŋikeken ŋiken aabɔŋ. Bi nyi ki ŋmaa ŋani tiwan aabɔŋ, ki ŋmaa joo ipiih aakur ti man chaun, ni nsiin, ni timann na gbaŋni nyɔla nyɔla mɔmɔk aabɔŋ.

english_text:
1The Lord has given to Bezalel, Oholiab, and others the skills needed for building a place of worship, and they will follow the Lord's instructions.
2Then Moses brought together these workers who were eager to work, 3and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning, 4that finally everyone stopped working 5and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.” 6So Moses sent word for the people to stop giving, and they did. 7But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done.
The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.1-14)
8-9The skilled workers got together to make the sacred tent and its linen curtains that were woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Each of the ten panels was twelve meters long and two meters wide, 10and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each. 11-13Then 50 loops of blue cloth were put along one of the wider sides of each curtain, and the two curtains were fastened together at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
14-15As the material for protecting the tent, goat hair was used to weave eleven sections 13 meters by 2 meters each. 16These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections. 17Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel, 18and the two panels were fastened at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 19Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.15-30)
20Acacia wood was used to build the framework for the walls of the sacred tent. 21Each frame was 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 22-26with two wooden pegs near the bottom. Then two silver stands were placed under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so they could be joined together. Twenty of these frames were used along the south side and 20 more along the north. 27Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side 28-29with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom. 30Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
31-33Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 34The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through.
The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.31-37)
35They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 36They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
37For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 38They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_text:
1“Besalel, ni Oholiab, ni biwanŋab biken bi Uwumbɔr nan di kina aalan ni nnyim tii bi, aan bi nyi tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi ga di ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool ngbaan na, ga ŋa tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr aah tuk bi pu na.”
Baah nan joo ni ipiin sakpen pu na
2Moses nan yin Besalel, ni Oholiab, ni biken bi Uwumbɔr di nnyim aalan tii bi aan bi ban ke bi ter na, ki tuk bi ke bi piin lituln ngbaan. 3Bi nan gaa u chee ipiin i mɔmɔk Israel yaab nan joo ni ke bi nan di ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool ngbaan na. Tɔ, Israel yaab nan beenin joo ni baapiin, ki nan tii Moses kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni. 4Le biwanŋab bi nan bi tun lituln ngbaan na buen 5ti tuk Moses ke, “Binib ngbaan aah joo ni pu na, ni chaar jer Uwumbɔr aah bui ke ti di tiwan ni ŋa Waabool ngbaan na.”
6Le Moses tun binib ngbaan chee, ki bui bi ke ni ŋeer a, ubaa taa ki joo ni nibaa; nima pu na, binib ngbaan aa nan ki di nibaa buen. 7Baah nan joo ni pu na nan wiir ti jer baah ban pu na.
Baah ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool pu na
(Nnyam 26.1-37)
8Biwanŋab ponn ni, binib bi nyi lituln ngbaan sakpen na nan ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool na. Bi nan di ipiih aakur ti man chaun, ni nsiin, ni timann, luu ŋitanyaan aakeken kipiik, le ki gbaŋ ŋi ki naan tiwan ni kpa ifeen na mann gonn ŋi pu, le ki ŋa ŋi. 9Ŋitan ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ŋak tɔb la, ŋaah fɔk pu na nan ye ŋipiikeken ŋilole, le mpepeen nan ye lipiikekeln libaa. 10Bi nan di ŋikeken ŋiŋmu ki kpaan ŋal dab tɔb, le ki di ŋiŋmu ŋi gur na mu ŋal dab tɔb. 11Bi nan di ŋikekengen bɔmbɔn le ki di ŋa iŋminsarkee ki kpaŋ igbaan, lipaal aakeken mɔmɔk pu. 12Bi nan ŋa iŋminsarkee piiŋmu le njan aakekeln pu, le ki ŋa piiŋmu mu ligeln liken na pu, le ŋi ŋak tɔb. 13Bi nan di salmaa ŋa ipigɔrkee piiŋmu, ki di chuu iŋminsarkee ngbaan dab tɔb aan ni ŋa likekeln libaa.
14Bi nan di ŋitan ŋi bi di uŋoob aakur luu na aagen kipiik ni libaa ŋa likekeln biin Libool ngbaan pu. 15Bi nan ŋa ni mɔmɔk ŋak tɔb la, nfɔfɔk nan ye ŋipiikeken ŋilole ni ligeln, le mpepeen ye lipiikekeln libaa. 16Bi nan di ŋitan ŋiŋmu le ŋal dab tɔb, le ki di ŋiloob mu ŋal dab tɔb, le ni ŋa ŋikeken ŋilee. 17Bi nan ŋa iŋminsarkee piiŋmu le ki di kpaŋ libaa, le ki ŋa iŋminsarkee piiŋmu mu kpaŋ liken na. 18Bi nan di tikumann ŋa ipigɔrkee piiŋmu, le ki di ŋipepel ŋilee ngbaan lɔk dab tɔb aan ni ŋa lipepel libaa aawan. 19Bi nan di ipihja aagbaman le ki di ŋa libiil libaa, le ki di ngbanyaan muken ŋa liken, aan ni li bii paab.
20Bi nan di lisiijal aadɔ kpaa Libool ngbaan aawon ki di siin. 21Tiwon ngbaan aafɔfɔk nan ye ŋitaa kipiik ni ŋiŋmu la, le naawawaan mu ye ŋisaŋ ŋinaa ni ligeln. 22Bi nan ŋa ŋimɔchɔn ŋilelee, aan nima kan, tiwon ngbaan aadɔ ga ŋmaa toŋ tɔb pu. Ni mɔmɔk nan bi kina la. 23Bi nan di idɔja moninko le ki di ŋa ŋŋangii wɔb aawon, 24le ki di tikunabr aakudɔ imonko ilee ki di bɔ puin taab, ikudɔ ilee le bi di bɔ puin idɔja ngbaan ibaabaa aataab, ki di kpaa dab tiwon aamɔchɔn ŋilee. 25Bi nan di idɔja moninko le ki di ŋa ŋŋangan wɔb aawon, 26le ki di tikunabr aakudɔ imonko ilee bɔ puin taab, ikudɔ ilee le bi di bɔ puin idɔja ngbaan ibaabaa aataab. 27Bi nan di idɔja iloob le ki ŋa liwilir wɔb, Libool ngbaan aapuwɔb, 28le ki di idɔja ilelee ki ŋa igulɔ mɔmɔk. 29Bi nan di igulɔ aadɔja ngbaan di kpaa dab taab, le i di kina ti dab paacham aadɔ mu. Bi nan ŋa igulɔ ilee ngbaan aawon aadɔja kina la. 30Idɔja ngbaan nan ti kpaan iniin la, ni tikunabr aakudɔ kipiik ni iloob i dɔ taab na, bi nan di ilelee le di kpaa dab taab aadɔja na mɔmɔk.
31Bi nan di lisiijal aadɔ le ŋa idɔpuinkee kipiik ni iŋmu, Libool ngbaan aapepel libaa nan kpa iŋmu la, 32lipepel liken mu iŋmu, le liwilir, lipuwɔb mu iŋmu. 33Kaasisik ni aadɔpuinkoo ma, bi nan di i puin i dan paacham aadɔja na pu, ki piin Libool ngbaan aapepel libaa ki ti saa liken. 34Bi nan di salmaa aakur le donn biin idɔ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu, le ki di salmaa aabɔmbim ŋmaan dab idɔpuinkee ngbaan mɔmɔk, bi nan donn salmaa aakur le ki biin i mu pu.
35Bi nan di ŋitanyaan ŋi bi di ipiih aakobɔnn, ni timann, ni nsiin luu ŋi na, ki di ŋa likekeln, le ki gbaŋ, ki naan tiwan ni kpa ifeen na li pu. 36Bi nan di lisiijal aadɔ le ki ŋa idɔja inaa, ki donn salmaa aakur biin i pu, le ki di salmaa aapigɔrkee di ŋmaan chuu likekeln ngbaan ki yakr Libool ngbaan nfum mulee. Bi nan ŋa tikunabr aadɔ inaa i dɔ taab na ki di chuu idɔja ngbaan. 37Bi nan di ŋitanyaan ŋi bi di ipiih aakobɔnn, ni timann, ni nsiin luu ŋal dab tɔb na, le ki gbaŋ ŋimɔgben, le ki di biin mbisamɔb. 38Bi nan kpii idɔja iŋmu, le ki ŋa ipigɔrkee i pu, le ki di ŋmaan chuu likekeln ngbaan. Bi nan di salmaa aakur le donn biin idɔja ngbaan aapaacham ni taab, le ki di tikumann aakudɔ iŋmu di punn mbisamɔb aadɔja ngbaan aataab.

english_text:
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 25.10-22)
1Bezalel built a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 2He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top. 3He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 4Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold, 5and put them through the rings, so the chest could be carried by the poles.
6The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy. 7-9On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 25.23-30)
10Bezalel built a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11-12He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 13He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs 14near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings 15and were made of acacia wood covered with gold. 16Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 25.31-40)
17Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold, 18with three branches on each of its two sides. 19There were three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 20and four on the stem. 21There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem. 22The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 23-24The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about 35 kilograms of pure gold.
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 30.1-5)
25For burning incense, Bezalel made an altar of acacia wood. It was 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull. 26He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 27Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar. 28These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold.
The Oil for Dedication and the Incense
(Exodus 30.22-38)
29 Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_text:
Baah kpaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa pu na
(Nnyam 25.10-22)
1Besalel nan kpaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa; u nan di lisiijal aadɔ le ki di kpaa u, dakaa ngbaan aah nan fɔk kitiŋ pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋilole ni ligeln, le waah waa pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋinaa ni ligeln. Nfɔfɔk paacham mu nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋinaa ni ligeln la. 2U nan di salmaa aakur ŋmeen le donn biin u ponn ni, ni lipaal mɔmɔk, le ki di salmaa aakur ŋa nkuul mann gonn u paacham aamɔgben. 3U nan di salmaa aakur le mɔɔ ibuen inaa ki di dab ŋipepel ŋinaa ngbaan aataa. 4U nan kpii lisiijal aadabil ŋilee ke bi li joo yoor dakaa ngbaan, le ki di salmaa aakur donn biin ŋi pu, 5le ki di ŋi bɔ ibuen inaa i dab baa dakaa ngbaan aataa na. 6U nan di salmaa aakur ŋmeen le ŋa libiil. Laah nan fɔk pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋilole ni ligeln la, le laah waa pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋinaa ni ligeln. 7U nan di ligagaar gbaa salmaa aakur ki mɔɔ tiwan ni kpa ifeen na nilee, 8nibaa nan si dakaa aagbaan mubaa, le niken mu si ngbaan muken. U nan mɔɔ ni, le tiwan ngbaan ni libiil dab tɔb ki kpaan liwanbaal. 9Tiwan ngbaan si libiil pu le ki tok tɔb, le naafeen bii li pu.
Baah kpaa Uwumbɔr aaboroboro aateebul pu na
(Nnyam 25.23-30)
10U nan di lisiijal aadɔ le kpaa teebul ngbaan, waah nan fɔk kitiŋ pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋiloob, le waah waa pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋitaa, le waah fɔk paacham pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋinaa ni ligeln. 11U nan di salmaa aakur ŋmeen le donn biin u pu, le ki di salmaa aakur ŋa nkuul mann gonn u paacham. 12U nan mɔɔ limɔgbaln aakuul, naah nan pee pu na nan ye lisangeln, le u di kpaŋ umɔgben. 13U nan mɔɔ salmaa aakur aabuen inaa dab teebul ngbaan aamɔgben ŋinaa ngbaan, nin chee ŋitaa ŋinaa baa na. 14Ibuen ngbaan ni, le bi di ŋidabil ŋi bi joo yoor teebul ngbaan na bɔ i ponn ni, teebul ngbaan aamɔgben chee. 15U nan di lisiijal aadɔ le kpii ŋidabil ŋilee ngbaan, le ki di salmaa aakur donn biin ŋi pu. 16U nan di salmaa aakur le mɔɔ teebul ngbaan aawan mɔmɔk, ni nan ye nsambim, ni mbobim, ni ŋisambijal aan bi joo ŋani ŋisubil aadaan aapiin na.
Baah ŋa karyaa aah tɔŋni tiwan ni pu na aabɔr
(Nnyam 25.31-40)
17U nan di salmaa aakur ŋmeen le mɔɔ karyaa tiib aah tɔŋni tiwan ni pu na. U nan di ligagaar gbaa ki ŋa tiwan ni pu karyaa tiib tɔŋni na, ki naan nsupuun dab ni pu, aan ni ŋa tiwanbaan.
18U nan mɔɔ ŋipan ŋitaa ŋŋangii, ŋitaa mu ŋŋangan, le ni kpaan ŋipan ŋiloob. 19U nan naan nsupuun mutataa ki di dab ŋipan ŋiloob ngbaan mɔmɔk pu. 20U nan naan nsupuun munaa ki di dab kaasisik ni aapachachaal na pu. 21U nan naan nsupuun aah laa bi ŋeeni pu na ki di dab ŋipan ŋiloob ngbaan mɔmɔk pu. 22Tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ye baah di ligagaar gbaa salmaa u na ŋmeen la. 23U nan ŋa karyaa bilole ki ŋeer ŋipan ŋilole ngbaan, le ki di salmaa ŋmeen mɔɔ kijubababr, ni ŋipen. 24U nan di salmaa aakur ŋmeen ti aanyunyuun ga pii ndibim kuruwaa piitaa na le mɔɔ tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk.
Baah nan ŋa baah seer tulalee aayon nin chee na pu na
(Nnyam 30.1-5)
25U nan di lisiijal aadɔ le ŋa baah seer tulalee aayon tiwan ni pu na. Ni nan bi likpakpaln, le naah fɔk kitiŋ pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋitaa, le naah waa pu na mu nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋitaa, le naah fɔk paacham mu pu na nan ye ŋisaŋ ŋiloob. Naamɔchɔn ŋinaa, ni nima nan ye liwanbaal la. 26U nan di salmaa aakur ŋmeen le donn biin paacham, ni isikakl mɔmɔk inaa, ni ŋimɔchɔn ŋinaa, le ki di salmaa aakur ŋa nkuul mann gonn ni. 27U nan mɔɔ salmaa aakur aabuen ilee, ki di dab baan ŋimɔgben aataab, nin chee bi ga di idɔ bɔ ki li joo yoor tiwan ngbaan na. 28U nan di lisiijal aadɔ le kpii idɔ ngbaan, ki donn salmaa aakur biin i pu.
29U nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aakpan ni tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ na mu.

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 27.1-8)
1Bezalel built an altar of acacia wood for offering sacrifices. It was 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high 2with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull, and it was completely covered with bronze. 3The equipment for the altar was also made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4About halfway up the altar he built a ledge around it and covered the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. 5Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through. 6He covered two acacia wood poles with bronze and 7put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 30.18-21)
8 Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 27.9-19)
9-17Around the sacred tent Bezalel built a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. He used 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts.
18-19For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was 2.25 meters high, the same height as the one for the rest of the courtyard, and was made of fine linen embroidered and woven with blue, purple, and red wool. He hung the curtain on the four posts, using silver hooks and rods. 20The pegs for the tent and for the curtain around the tent were made of bronze.
The Sacred Tent
21-23Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done.
Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent. 24According to the official weights, the amount of gold given was a ton, 25 and the silver that was collected when the people were counted came to 3.4 tons. 26 Everyone who was counted paid the required amount, and there was a total of 603,550 men who were 20 years old or older.
27Thirty-four kilograms of the silver were used to make each of the 100 stands for the sacred tent and the curtain. 28The remaining 30 kilograms of silver were used for the hooks and rods and for covering the tops of the posts.
29Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given. 30And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar, 31the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_text:
Baah ŋa kitork aabimbiln pu na
(Nnyam 27.1-8)
1U nan di lisiijal aadɔ le ŋa kitork aabimbiln. Li nan ye likpakpaln la, laah fɔk pu na nan ye ŋitaa ŋilole ni ligeln, le laah waa pu na mu ye ŋitaa ŋilole ni ligeln, le laah fɔk paacham pu na ye ŋitaa ŋinaa ni ligeln. 2U nan ŋa ŋimɔchɔn ki baan ŋimɔgben ŋinaa pu, le ni kpaan liwanbaal. U nan di tikumann aakur le donn biin li pu. 3U nan ki ŋa laawan mɔmɔk kpee li pu: ŋisambil ŋi bi ga li joo nfatan ŋani ŋi ponn ni na, ni ŋichakpaa, ni ŋisambil, ni inanmoon. Bi nan di tikumann aakur le ŋa ni mɔmɔk. 4U nan di tikumann aakur le mɔɔ kiŋulk le ki di taŋ libimbiln ngbaan aakaasisik ni. 5U nan mɔɔ ibuen inaa le ki di dab baan ŋimɔgben ŋinaa ngbaan. 6U nan di lisiijal aadɔ le kpii idɔ, le ki donn tikumann aakur biin i pu, 7le ki di i bɔ ibuen inaa na ponn ni. Bi nan di idɔ le ŋa li, le li ponn ni ye kiloŋ.
Baah ŋa tikumann aakur aasambil pu na
(Nnyam 30.18)
