Toor kitork ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr ki nyan binib ngbaan aatunwanbir, ke Uwumbɔr aah mɔk pu na.”
8Le Aaronn buen kitork aabimbiln chee ki ti kɔr unaaja, u ye uma ubaa aatunwanbir aatork aapiin aawakork na. 9Le ujapɔtiib joo ni kaasin u chee, le u di uŋanbik bɔn mu ni, ki di ngem ŋa libimbiln ngbaan aalɔlɔ aamɔju pu, le ki di mu gur na kpir libimbiln aataab, 10le ki see kiwakork ngbaan aakpan, ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na, mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ke Uwumbɔr aah tuk Moses pu na. 11U nan nyan lipaal le ki ti see tinann, ni ngban, mmii ni.
12U nan ki kɔr kiwakork ki ye uma ubaa aatork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin aawakork. Le ujapɔtiib joo ni kaasin u chee, le u di mu mee kpir libimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu. 13Bi nan ki di kiwakork ngbaan aayil, ni tinann tiken, ki di tii u, le u see ti mmii ni, libimbiln paab. 14U nan ki finn ponn ni aawan, ni ŋitaajal, le ki di paan kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na pu, libimbiln paab, ki see mmii.
15Nee aapuwɔb na, u nan di binib ngbaan aatork mu tii Uwumbɔr ipiin. U nan di uŋoob u u ga di toor binib ngbaan aatunwanbir pu na, ki kɔr toor ke waah toor waatunwanbir aatork pu na. 16U nan ki joo ni kiwakork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, le ki di ki mu toor, nkaal aah mɔk pu na. 17U nan toor njikaabim aatork mu, le ki lee n‑yon paan kitork aabimbiln paab, ki see mu mmii. U nan ŋa nimina mɔmɔk ki di kpee nwiin mɔk aatork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na pu. 18U nan kɔr unaaja ni upihja, le ni ye kimɔbaan aatork aapiin, binib ngbaan pu. Le ujapɔtiib joo ni tiwakor ngbaan aasin, le u di mu kpir libimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu. 19Aaronn nan di unaaja ni upihja aakpan aawan mɔmɔk 20ki di paan ŋibingbaa aanann pu, ki di buen kitork aabimbiln chee. U nan see nkpan ngbaan mmii ni, libimbiln paab, 21le ki di ŋibingbaa ni ŋŋangii aataajal tii Uwumbɔr ipiinkpaan, le ki nin giin ni tii bitotoorb, ke Moses aah nan tuk u pu na.
22N‑yoonn mu Aaronn toor kitork mɔmɔk doo na, le u yoor uŋaal paacham ki toŋ binib ngbaan wɔb, ki mee Uwumbɔr, u ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu, le ki nin sunn ni. 23Moses ni Aaronn nan buen Uwumbɔr Aabool ni; baah nyan ni na, le bi mee Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa bi pu, le Uwumbɔr aawiihn mu moor ki deer ŋinimbil na sunn ni bi mɔmɔk pu. 24Libuul ngbaan ni, le Uwumbɔr cha mmii nyan ni paacham ki nan wun kitork ki bi ban bi di see mmii ni na aapiin, ni nkpan, libimbiln paab. N‑yoonn mu binib ngbaan kan kina na, le bi teen mpɔɔn pu, ki tar lir kitiŋ lichichikr.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Nadab ni Abihu aatunwanbir aabɔr
1Nadab ni Abihu bi nan ye Aaronn aajapɔtiib na, nan yoor tiwan ni bi seer tulalee aayon mmii ni ponn ni na, ki ban mmiisakɔl ŋa ni ponn ni, le ki ban tulalee aayon paan ŋi pu ki di tii Uwumbɔr. Tɔ, mmii ngbaan aa nan ye chain aamii, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa nan tii bi nsan ke bi ŋa kina. 2Baah ŋa kina na, libuul ngbaan ni, le Uwumbɔr cha mmii dan le ki nan ku bi, unimbiin ni. 3Moses nan bui Aaronn ke, “Kina pu le Uwumbɔr len ki bui ke, ‘Binib bimɔk tun maatuln na, ni ŋan ke bi li pak maah bi chain pu na; le m ga kpiir mɔk maanib maah nyuun sakpen pu na.’” Le ni gar Aaronn; waa ki ŋmaa len tibɔr tibaa.
4Le Moses yin ni Misael ni Elsafann bi nan ye Aaronn aaweeja Usiel aajapɔtiib na, ki nan bui bi ke, “Dan do man ki nan yoor ninaabitiib nya Uwumbɔr Aabool ni, ki di buen lipaal.” 5Moses aah mɔk bi pu na, le bi dan nan chuu baawanpeenkaan ki di bi nyan lipaal.
6Moses nan ki bui Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib bilee bi gur ki bi, aan bi yin bi ke Eleasar ni Itamar na ke, “Ni toor nimi aayikpir, ki taa kar nimi aawanpeenkaan, ki taa cha nisui bii ninaabitiib ngbaan pu. Ni yaa cha nisui bii bi pu kan, ni mu ga kpo; le Uwumbɔr ga gee liŋuul ŋa Israel yaab mɔmɔk pu. Tɔ, nido yaab Israel yaab bi gur na wii baakpuul, Uwumbɔr aah cha mmii ku ninaabitiib na pu. 7Nima taa nya Libool ngbaan ni, ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga kpo, ba pu? bi di Uwumbɔr aakpan kpir niyil pu ki di nimi tii uma Uwumbɔr a.” Le bi ŋa Moses aah tuk bi pu na.
Bitotoorb aakaal
8Uwumbɔr nan bui Aaronn ke, 9“Aa ni aajapɔtiib yaa nyun ŋisubil aadaan, bee ndaan muken na kan, ni taa koo ni Maabool ponn ni; ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga kpo. Aa ni saamaal li joo nkaal mue kina cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 10Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki li nyi tiwan ni ye min Uwumbɔr aatuln aawan na, ni ni kaa ye maatuln aawan na, ni tiwan ni ye chain na, ni ni kaa ye chain na. 11Maah di ikaal imɔk tii Moses aan u di mɔk si na, aa di i mɔk Israel aanib mɔmɔk.”
12Moses nan ki bui Aaronn, ni ujapɔtiib Eleasar ni Itamar bi gur na ke, “Ni di njikaabim aatork ti gur ki nyan ni tijikaar aatork ponn ni, aan ni di tii Uwumbɔr na, ki ŋa boroboro u kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na, ki ŋmɔ u kitork aabimbiln chee, ba pu? ipiin ngbaan ye i bi chain na la. 13Ni ŋmɔ u chain aapepel ni; tijikaar aapiin ngbaan ye tijikaar ti bi di tii Uwumbɔr aan u mu di tii nimi na la. Uwumbɔr aah tuk mi pu na le na. 14Aa ni saamaal ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ libingbaal ni litaajal aanann ti ye ipiinkpaan ni tootookpaan aan bi di tii Uwumbɔr, aan u mu di tii bitotoorb na. Ni ga ŋmaa ji tijikaar ngbaan ŋipepel ŋi ye chain na ni. Israel yaab aah di kimɔbaan aapiin i tii Uwumbɔr na, le u mu di tii aa ni saamaal mu ipiin. 15N‑yoonn mu bi ti ban bi di nkpan see mmii ni ki tii Uwumbɔr aan ni ye tijikaar aatork na, bi li joo ni litaajal ni libingbaal mu. Uwumbɔr aah mɔk pu na, aa ni saamaal le yeh litaajal ni libingbaal aanann, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
16Tɔ, Moses nan baa bi uŋoob u bi di toor titunwanbir aatork na aabɔr, le ki bee ke bi di u see mmii ni a. Le waaŋuul fii Aaronn aajapɔtiib Eleasar ni Itamar pu, le u baa bi ke, 17“Ba ŋa naa jin titunwanbir aatork ngbaan aajikaar chain aapepel ni? Kitork ngbaan ye chain aatork la, le Uwumbɔr di tii nimi ke ki nyan Israel yaab mɔmɔk baatunwanbir ni. 18Naah kaa di kiwakork ngbaan aasin buen Uwumbɔr Aabool ponn ni na, ni ba ga ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan nima, ke maah tuk nimi pu na.”
19Le Aaronn giin bui Moses ke, “Bi toor titunwanbir aatork, ni kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin din wee, ki tii Uwumbɔr, le tibɔbir tee aaboln dan m pu. M yaa ba ŋman titunwanbir aatork aanann ngbaan kan, ni ba ga li mɔ Uwumbɔr aa?” 20N‑yoonn mu Moses ŋun kina na, le ni piir usui.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_text:
Tijikaar ti kɔ na ni ti kaa kɔ na aabɔr
(Ikaal 14.3-21)
1Uwumbɔr nan len Moses ni Aaronn chee tibɔr timina 2ke bi di tuk Israel yaab, “Tiwakor ni ipeel i ni ga ŋmaa ji i na sɔ: 3Tiwan ni aataabuseen yakr, aan ni ŋmɔ timoor ki biir ki ki ŋmɔ na. 4-6Ni mu taa ŋmɔ laakumii, ni timoor ni aawan ni bi ke sandee na, ni sandee. Ni ŋmɔ timoor la, le nitaabuseen mu aa yakr, ni ye tiwan ni kɔ ni chee na la. 7Ni taa li ŋmɔ igbeer. Ni li kɔ i; yaataabuseen yakr le i ŋmɔ timoor ki mu aa biir ti ki ki ŋmɔ. 8Ni taa ji ipeel ni tiwakor ngbaan, ki taa meeh ti kpo na mu, ni li kɔ ti.
9“Ijan i kpa tigbar ni tipɔkr na, ni ga ŋmaa ji i. 10Tiwan ni bi nnyun ni kaa kpa tigbar ni tikpɔkr na, ni taa ji ni. 11Tiwan ngbaan aaboln kɔ. Ni taa ji ni, ki mu taa meeh ni kpo na. 12Tiwan ni bi nnyun ni kaa kpa tigbar ni tipɔkr na, ni taa ji ni.
13-19“Ni taa ji inyoon imina: Ŋikaagii, ni ifiin, ni kaasaa tiib, ni titakpatoor, ni kaaŋaaŋaa tiib, ni nangba tiib, ni ŋikakaa, ni taataa tiib, ni inyumuil, ni ineepɔɔn, ni inaakpaapiin, ni imɔɔkaa, ni ŋibaa, ni tinanjenn.
20“Tiwayukaan nimɔk kpa ifeen na kɔ, 21see ni yukr kaa fii na le aa kɔ. 22Ni ga ŋmaa ji itoon, ni ipaan, ni inaakan. 23Tɔ, tiwayukaan ni ye niwaatiir ki kpa ifeen ki baar na kɔ.
24-28“Unii umɔk meeh tiwakor ni ipeel nimina aawankpol na aa ki bi chain kina le ki ti saa kijook wɔb: Tiwakor ni ipeel ni kpa ŋitaa ŋinaa ni tinyanyar na, ni tiwakor ni ipeel nimɔk kpa itaabuseen na, see naataabuseen yakr aan ni ŋmɔ timoor ki biir ki ki ŋmɔ na le aa kɔ. Unii umɔk tun tiwakor bee ipeel ni kɔ na aanann na finn waawanpeenkaan; u mu aan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.
29-30“Tiwan ni mu kɔ na le ye ŋinaasɔn, ni ŋisayik, ni ilapol, ni itakpaja. 31Unii umɔk meeh ni, bee naawankpol na, aa ki bi chain kina ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 32Le naawankpol yaa lir tiwan nimɔk pu na kan, naa ki bi chain. Tiwan ngbaan yaa ye idɔ, bee tiwanpeenkaan, bee igban, bee bɔtɔ, bee bi yaa joo tiwan nimina ŋani lituln li na kan, naa ki bi chain, bi di nnyun mu bi chain na ki finn ni, le naan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 33Le naawankpol yaa lir libuul ni kan, tiwan nimɔk bi li ponn ni na aa ki bi chain; ni gbaa wii libuul ngbaan. 34Nnyun mu bi libuul ngbaan ni na yaa kpir ki meeh tijikaar ti ni ga ŋmaa ji ti na kan, taa ki bi chain, le tiwanyukaan ni bi libuul ngbaan ni na mu aa bi chain. 35Tiwan nimɔk pu naawankpol lir ni pu na aa ki bi chain, ni yaa ye tiyakr aafan, bee boroboro aadiik kan, see ni gbaa wii ni. 36Tɔ, ni yaa ye nnyunbun, bee nin chee bi maa ki di nnyun ŋa ni ponn ni na kan, nima aa bii, tiwan niken ma yaa meeh naawankpol ngbaan kan, naa ki bi chain. 37Ni ponn ni nibaa yaa lir njikaabim mu bi ban bi di bu na pu kan, nwanbim ngbaan aa bii. 38Ni mu yaa di nwanbim ngbaan pɔɔn nnyun ni, le ni lir ni ponn ni kan, nwanbim ngbaan aa ki bi chain.
39“Tiwakor ti ni ga ŋmaa ji ti na yaa kpo aan ni meeh ti kan, naan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 40Unii umɔk ŋman tinann ngbaan na, see u finn waawanpeenkaan, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. Unii umɔk tun tinann ngbaan na mu finn waawanpeenkaan, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.
41“Ni taa ji ipeel waatiir i chuun na. 42I yaa baar, bee i yaa chuun ŋitaa ŋinaa pu, bee i yaa kpa ŋitaa ŋi wiir na kan, ni taa ji i. 43Ni taa ji i aan ki bii nibaa man. 44Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, le ni ŋan ke ni li joo nibaa chain, ba pu? m bi chain la. 45Min le ye Uwumbɔr u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni ke m li ye nimi Aawumbɔr na. Ni li bi chain, ba pu? m bi chain la.
46“Nkaal mue le m tii nimi ki joo cha ipeel, ni inyoon, ni tiwan ni bi nnyun ponn ni na, ni tiwan nimɔk chuun na wɔb. 47Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki gann aan ki bee tiwan ni bi chain na, ni ni kaa bi chain na, nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa bee tiwakor ti kɔ na, ni ti kaa kɔ na.”

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Umarpɔɔn aatork
1Uwumbɔr nan ki len Moses chee 2ke u bui Israel yaab tibɔr timina: Upii yaa ma ubijabo ki bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole kan, waa bi chain, le ni bi ke waah fuu mpiikpen le na. 3Winiin daal kan, ni gii ubo ngbaan aachakpaln. 4Nsin aah nyan upii ngbaan ni pu na, see u bi ki ti saa iwiin piitaa ni itaa, le ki nin ŋa chain. N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, u taa meeh tiwan ni bi chain na, ki mu taa koo Uwumbɔr Aabool ponn ni ki ti saa bundaal u ga ŋa chain na.
5Upii yaa ma upiibo ki bi ki ti saa iwiin kipiik ni inaa daal kan, waa bi chain, le ni bi ke waah fuu mpiikpen le na. Nsin aah nyan upii ngbaan ni pu na, see u ki bi ki ti saa iwiin imonko itaa ni iloob kpee, le ki nin ŋa chain.
6Iwiin ngbaan aapuwɔb na, ubo yaa ye ubijabo, bee upiibo kan, upii ngbaan li joo ni libiln libaa aapihbo utotoor chee, Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee, aan ki nan tii Uwumbɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin, ki ki li joo ni libɔrnanjel, bee linanjel, ki nan toor titunwanbir aatork. 7Le utotoor na ga di waapiin ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr, ki toor kitork aan ki nyan u tijɔŋ ni, ki ŋa u chain. Upii yaa ma kan, kina le u ga ŋa.
8Upii yaa kaa kpa upihbo u toor kan, u li joo ni ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee, bee ŋinanjel ŋilee, ki di libaa toor kitork ki di see mmii ni, ki di liken mu toor titunwanbir aatork. Utotoor ga toor ki nyan u tijɔŋ ni, aan u ŋa chain.

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
Tiwon aaween aakaal
1Uwumbɔr nan ki di ikaal imina di tii Moses ni Aaronn. 2Ni ponn ni ubaa yaa kpa mbuun uwon pu, bee lichakpelar, bee nibaa chee yaa puun ki ga ŋa tiwon aaween i bir na kan, ni li joo ni u utotoor Aaronn, bee waamaal ponn ni ubaa chee. 3Le utotoor ga lik iween ngbaan, le nima chee aakor yaa piir aan libuul ngbaan nyoo kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la, le utotoor ga len ke waa bi chain. 4Tɔ, nima chee yaa piir kaa nyoo aan tikor mu aa piir kan, utotoor nyan u ki di u ŋa nibaa chee ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 5Winlole daal kan, utotoor ki ŋaŋ u ki lik, iween ngbaan yaa beenin bi kina, kaa kpee kan, utotoor ki kpee u iwiin ilole. 6Utotoor ki gir lik u winlole daal ngbaan, u yaa kan ke iween ngbaan bi door, kaa kpee kan, u ga len ke u ye chain, ni ye tilalab la, u finn waawanpeenkaan ki ŋa chain. 7Ni yaa ye ke utotoor aah ŋaŋ u doo, ki len ke u bi chain na aapuwɔb le iween ngbaan yaa ki pɔr kpee kan, u ki gir ni utotoor chee. 8Le utotoor ga ki gir lik u, le u yaa kan ke i sil pɔr kpee kan, u ga len ke waa ki bi chain; le ni mɔk ke ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la.
9Ni ponn ni ubaa yaa kpa tiwon aaween i bir na kan, ni li joo ni u utotoor chee, 10le u ga lik u. Uwon nibaa chee yaa duun aan nima chee aakor piir ki kpa tinar kan, 11ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la. Utotoor ga len ke udaan aa bi chain, ni taa ki nyan u, u ti li bi nibaa chee ke ni lik u waahr; ni ye le ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain. 12Ni yaa ye ke iween ngbaan pɔr ki yaa gaa uwon mɔmɔk ki nyan uyil ki ti saa utaa kan, 13utotoor ki gir lik u. U yaa kan ke iween ngbaan yaa gaa uwon mɔmɔk pu kan, u len ke u bi chain. Uwon mɔmɔk yaa kpar piir kan, u bi chain le na. 14N‑yoonn mu mbuun ŋa uwon pu na, waa ki bi chain. 15Utotoor yaa ki gir lik u, ki kan mbuun u pu kan, u len ke waa bi chain. Mbuun ngbaan mɔk ke ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la, le mu cha udaan ngbaan aa ki bi chain. 16Mbuun ngbaan yaa yann ki ki piir kan, u ga ki gir buen utotoor chee, 17aan u ki gir lik u. Le ni yaa ye ke mu yann ki piir kan, u ki ŋa chain le na, le utotoor ga len ke u bi chain.
18Unii yaa kpa lichakpelar aan li foor kan, 19kina aapuwɔb na, ni yaa ki gir duun ki piin, bee ki man kan, udaan ngbaan ki buen utotoor chee. 20Le utotoor ga lik u, u yaa kan ke ni ŋa mbuun ki nyoo, le nima chee aakor yaa piir kan, u len ke waa bi chain. Ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na, le ki pue ŋa ke lichakpelar na. 21Utotoor mu yaa ŋaŋ u aan ki kan ke nima chee aakor aa piir, li mu aa nyoo, kaa man sakpen kan, utotoor nyan u ŋa nibaa chee, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 22Ni yaa moo pɔr kpee kan, utotoor len ke waa bi chain le ki kpa tiwon aaween i bir na. 23Ni yaa kaa moo pɔr kpee le ki yann cha kibuweek kan, utotoor ngbaan len ke u bi chain.
24Tiwantonn le yaa see unii, le mbuun ngbaan yaa piir, bee mu ponn ni man chaun kan, 25utotoor ŋaŋ u. Mbuun ngbaan yaa nyoo, le nima chee aakor yaa piir kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na le koo mu ponn ni, le utotoor ga len ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain. 26Mu yaa kaa nyoo, kaa man sakpen, le nima chee aakor aa piir kan, utotoor nyan u ŋa nibaa chee, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 27Le utotoor ga ki gir lik u winlole daal, mu yaa moo pɔr kpee kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la; utotoor ga len ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain. 28Ni yaa kaa pɔr kpee, aan naah man pu na mu yaa kaa kpee kan, naa ye tiwon aaween i bir na. Utotoor ga len ke u bi chain, ba pu? ni ye tiwantonn aah nan see u pu na aabuweek la.
29Ni ponn ni, uja, bee upii yaa kpa mbuun uyil, bee ulangbachuun pu kan, 30ni cha utotoor lik mu. Mu yaa nyoo aan mu ponn ni aakor yaa bi ke nkonyon na, kaa wiir kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la, le utotoor bui ke waa bi chain. 31Tɔ, n‑yoonn mu utotoor lik u, aan mbuun ngbaan aa nyoo, le nima chee aakor aa ŋan na kan, ni nyan udaan, u li bi nibaa chee ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 32Le winlole daal kan, utotoor ki gir lik mbuun ngbaan, le mu yaa kaa ki pɔr kpee, kaa kpa tikor ti bi ke nkonyon na, ki mu aa ki nyoo kan, 33udaan ngbaan kuu tikor ti mann goln mbuun chee na. Le utotoor ga ki gir cha u li bi waah nan koo nin chee na ki ki saa iwiin ilole. 34Winlole daal kan, utotoor ki gir lik u, mbuun ngbaan yaa kaa pɔr kpee, kaa ki nyoo kan, utotoor len ke u ŋa chain a. Le udaan ga finn waawanpeenkaan aan ki ŋa chain. 35Tɔ, utotoor yaa len ke u bi chain, aan nee aapuwɔb, mbuun ngbaan ki pɔr kan, 36utotoor ki gir lik u. Mu yaa pɔr kan, utotoor taa ki lik ke mu aakor ŋan aan mu aa ŋan; ni ye le ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain. 37Utotoor yaa lik ki dakl ke mbuun ngbaan aa ki pɔr, le tikopɔnn piin ki pa libuul ni kan, mbuun yann le na, utotoor len ke u ŋa chain a.
38Uja bee upii yaa kpa uwon nibaa chee ni piin kan, 39ni cha utotoor lik u. Nima chee yaa kaa piin sakpen kan, ni ye tiwan ni kaa bir na le nyan nima chee, udaan ngbaan bi chain.
40-41Uja aayikpir yaa gui ugbangbataab bee uyigbeer kan, nima aan cha u ŋa tijɔŋdaan. 42Ni yaa ye ke mbuun mu man chaun na bi uyil nin chee gui na kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la. 43Utotoor lik u, aan ki yaa kan ke ni man ki piin ki ye mbuun kan, 44utotoor len ke waa bi chain, ba pu? ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la, le ki bi uyil pu.
45Unii u kpa tiwon aaween i bir na li peeni tikekekpir, ki taa chaa uyikpir, ki di likekeln biin umɔb wɔb, aan ki li tar mpɔɔn pu ke, “Maah bi chain, maah bi chain.” 46Kikɔŋ ngbaan yaa bi u pu ki ti saa buyoonn na kan, waa bi chain, le ni cha u nya linampal biken chee, ki ti li bi ubaa.
Lipɔpɔl aabɔr
47-48Tiwanpeenkaan, bee likekeln aawan ni bi di tiwakor aakor, bee tikokonn luu ni, bee ngban aawanpeenkaan ni bi di ngban ŋa ni na, yaa ŋa lipɔpɔl, 49li yaa ye liŋaankal bee limamaln kan, ni di tiwan ngbaan mɔk utotoor, ba pu? ni ye tiwan ni ga pɔr na la. 50Le utotoor ga lik tiwan ngbaan mbamɔm, ki di ni bil nibaa chee ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 51Winlole daal kan, u ki gir lik ni, le lipɔpɔl ngbaan yaa moo kpee kan, tiwan ngbaan aa bi chain. 52Utotoor di ni see mmii ni, ba pu? lipɔpɔl ngbaan ga pɔr, le ni ŋan ke bi di ni see mmii ni.
53Tɔ, u yaa lik tiwan ngbaan, aan lipɔpɔl aa ŋa ni pu kpee kan, 54utotoor cha bi finn ni, aan u ki di ni bil ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 55U yaa ti ki lik ni, aan lipɔpɔl ngbaan yaa kaa kpeln naabimbin, ki mu aa ŋa kpee kan, tiwan ngbaan aa nin bi chain, ni yaa ye ke lipɔpɔl ngbaan piin kinyaan wɔb bee tibir wɔb kan, ni see ni mmii. 56Tɔ, ni yaa ye ke n‑yoonn mu bi finn ni na, le utotoor ki gir lik ni, aan ni wuur kan, u chuu nin chee lipɔpɔl ngbaan baan na, ki kar nyan ni tiwan ngbaan pu. 57Lipɔpɔl yaa ki gir nyan ni pu kan, ni bi pɔr kpei la, uwandaan see ni mmii ni. 58Tɔ, u yaa finn tiwan ngbaan, aan lipɔpɔl wuur ki nyan doo kan, u ki gir finn ni lelee, le ni ga ki ŋa chain.
59Nima pu na, lipɔpɔl yaa baan tiwanpeenkaan, bee likekeln aawan ni bi di tiwakor aakor, bee tikokonn luu ni na, bee ngban aawan ni bi di ngban ŋa ni na, nkaal mue le ni ga dii ki toor ni.

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
Tiwon aaween i bir na aatork
1Uwumbɔr nan di ikaal imina tii Moses 2ki joo cha tiwon aaween i bir na aah ti doo unii pu kan, baah ga toor pu ki ŋa u chain na. Nwiin mundaal bi ga toor ki ŋa u chain na, ni li joo ni u utotoor chee. 3Le utotoor ga di u nya n‑gbaan ki di u buen nibaa chee ki ti lik u. Le iween ngbaan yaa doo u pu kan, 4utotoor ga cha bi li joo ni ŋinanjel ŋilee ki kpee santina aadɔ, ni ŋŋmin maman, ni nkiisuk pu. 5Le utotoor cha bi kɔr linanjel libaa, tiyakr aasambil li nnyunbun aanyunpɔm bi li ponn ni na aapaacham. 6U ga di linanjel li gur baa kɔr na, ni santina aadɔ, ni ŋŋmin maman, ni nkiisuk, ki di bɔ baah kɔr linanjel li na aasin ni, 7ki di mu yɔk yɔk uweendaan ngbaan pu nfum mulole, ki bui ke u ŋa chain a. Linanjel li gur waa kɔr li na, utotoor di li lii aan li fii buen. 8Le udaan ngbaan finn waawanpeenkaan, ki kuu waakor mɔmɔk aan ki fu nnyun; le kitork ngbaan ga ŋa u chain. U yaa kun linampal kan, u taa koo waadichal ni, u li bi lipaal ki tii saa iwiin ilole. 9Winlole daal kan, u ki gir kuu uyikpir, ni ulangbaln, ni tinimbikee, ni tikor timɔk bi uwon pu na; u ki finn waawanpeenkaan mɔmɔk ki fu nnyun le ki nin ŋa chain.
10Winiin daal kan, u li joo ni ipihjabi ilee, ni upihsal, timɔk li ye libiln libaa aawakor ti ŋan na, ni boroboro aayon mu olif aakpan ŋmal mu ponn ni na kuruwaa bitaa, ni olif aakpan likpalbageln. 11Le utotoor ga di uweendaan ngbaan, ni tiwan nimina mɔmɔk buen Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Waabool aabisamɔb chee. 12Utotoor nyan upihjabo ubaa ki kpee nkpan pu, ki di toor kitork aan ni li ye lipɔln aapam aatork. U di ni toor, ni li ye ipiinkpaan tii Uwumbɔr aan utotoor li yeh tiwan ngbaan. 13U kɔr upiih ngbaan chain aapepel, nin chee bi joo tiwakor toor titunwanbir aatork na, ni kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na wɔb. U ŋa kina, ba pu? lipɔln aatork ye utotoor yaan ki bi chain, ke titunwanbir aatork na. 14Utotoor ban upihbo ngbaan aasin ki di ŋa uweendaan ngbaan aaŋangii aatafalan ni, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu. 15Utotoor ban olif aakpan ngem ŋa uŋangan aaŋaapɔtan ni, 16ki di uŋangii aaŋanbik bɔ mu ni, ki di yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nima chee, nfum mulole. 17U ga ki ban nkpan ngem mu bi uŋaapɔtan ni na, ni upihbo ngbaan aasin, ki di ŋa baah bi toor unii u bi ŋa u chain na aaŋangii aatafalan ni, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu. 18Nkpan mu gur uŋaapɔtan ni na, u di kpir uja ngbaan aayil pu. U yaa ŋa kina kan, u toor ki ŋa udaan ngbaan chain le na.
19Le utotoor ga ki toor titunwanbir aachapinn aatork mu ki ŋa udaan chain. Nee aapuwɔb, le u ga kɔr kiwakork, ki toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, 20ki di tijikaar aatork kpee, ki ŋa ni kitork aabimbiln pu. Kina le utotoor ga toor ki ŋa u chain, le udaan ngbaan ga ŋa chain.
21Unii ngbaan yaa ye ugiin le kaan ŋmaa tii naah ye pu na kan, u li joo ni upihjabo ubaa ki nan toor lipɔln aatork aan bi di toor ki ŋa u chain, i ye ipiinkpaan le ki tii Uwumbɔr, le utotoor le yeh tiwan ngbaan. U ki li joo ni boroboro aayon kuruwaa ubaa, ki di olif aakpan ŋmal mu ni, ki nan di tii tijikaar aapiin aatork, ki kpee olif aakpan likpalbageln. 22U ki li joo ni ŋinanjel ŋilee, bee ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee. U di libaa toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aatork. 23Winiin daal aan bi ga toor ki ŋa u chain na, u li joo ni tiwan ngbaan utotoor chee, Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee. 24Utotoor ga di upihjabo ni olif aakpan, ni ye ipiinkpaan na, ki di tii Uwumbɔr; utotoor yeh tiwan ngbaan. 25U ga kɔr upihjabo ngbaan, le ki di waasin ngem ki ŋa unii ngbaan aaŋangii aatafalan pu, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu. 26Le utotoor ga bar nkpan ngem ki di ŋa uŋangan aaŋaapɔtan ni, 27aan ki di uŋangii aaŋanbik bɔ mu ni, ki di yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nima chee, nfum mulole. 28U ki di nkpan mu ŋa unii ngbaan nin chee u ba di nsin ŋa na, unii ngbaan aaŋangii aatafalan pu, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu. 29Nkpan mu gur uŋaapɔtan ni na, u di kpir unii ngbaan aayil pu, le ki toor chain aatork. 30Le u nin di linanjel libaa, bee libɔrnanjel libaa 31toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ki kpee njikaabim aapiin aatork pu. Kina le utotoor ga ŋa ki toor kitork ki ŋa udaan ngbaan chain. 32Nkaal mu uweendaan u ye ugiin aan iween ngbaan doo u pu, u ban ke u toor ki ŋa ubaa chain na, le na.
Lidichal ni aapɔpɔl aabɔr
33Uwumbɔr nan ki len Moses ni Aaronn chee tibɔr timina: 34Ni yaa ti koo Kanaann aatiŋ ki m ban m di tii nimi ki li ye nimi yaan na kan, lipɔpɔl yaa ŋa unii aadichal ni kan, 35u buen utotoor chee ki ti bui u lipɔpɔl ngbaan aabɔr. 36Le utotoor cha bi nyan tiwan nimɔk bi lidichal ngbaan ni na aan u nin koo ki ti lik lipɔpɔl ngbaan; ni yaa kaa ye kina kan, tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk aan ki li bi chain. Le u ga koo lidichal ngbaan ni 37ki ti lik lipɔpɔl ngbaan. U yaa kan ke lipɔpɔl ngbaan ŋa tiwan ni wuun ki bi ke liŋaankal, bee nimamann na, ki baa ligoln pu kan, 38u nyan lidichal ngbaan ni, ki laŋ li, ki ti saa iwiin ilole. 39Winlole daal kan, u ki gir ti lik. U yaa kan ke lipɔpɔl ngbaan kpee kan, 40u cha bi nyan ŋifakuu ŋi pu lipɔpɔl ngbaan baa na, ki nyan ŋi kitiŋ aagbaan, ki di ŋi mee nin chee aa bi chain na. 41Nee aapuwɔb, u cha bi pɔkr nyan titan mɔmɔk, ponn ni aagon pu, ki di titan ngbaan nya kitiŋ ni, ki di ti mee nin chee aa bi chain na. 42Le bi ki ban ŋifakuu yayan ki di saŋ ŋimana aabuul ni, ki pɔ ponn ni, ni mɔmɔk.
43Bi yaa nyan ŋifakuu ki pɔkr lidichal ngbaan ponn ni kina, ki ki gir pɔn aan lipɔpɔl ngbaan ki gir ŋa kan, 44utotoor ki gir koo li ponn ni ki ti lik; lipɔpɔl yaa ki nyan kan, lidichal ngbaan aa ki bi chain. 45U cha bi gbaa wii lidichal ngbaan, ki faa laafakuu, ni idɔ, ni titan timɔk bi di pɔn na, ki nyan ni mɔmɔk kitiŋ aagbaan, ki di buen ti mee nin chee aa bi chain na. 46N‑yoonn mu bi laŋ lidichal ngbaan aan unii koo li ponn ni na, waa ki bi chain le ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 47Unii umɔk doon, bee u jin tijikaar lidichal ngbaan ni na, u finn waawanpeenkaan mɔmɔk.
48N‑yoonn mu bi pɔkr ponn ni aagoln ngbaan ki gir pɔn na, nee aapuwɔb, utotoor yaa koo u ti lik, ki kan ke lipɔpɔl aa ki gir nyan kan, u len ke lidichal ngbaan ŋa chain a, ba pu? lipɔpɔl ngbaan aa ki bi, baah pɔkr titan na, bi nyan lipɔpɔl doo a. 49U yaa ban u toor ki ŋa lidichal ngbaan chain kan, u ban ŋinanjel ŋilee, ni santina aadɔ, ni ŋŋmiman, ni nkiisuk. 50U ga kɔr linanjel ngbaan libaa, tiyakr aasambil li bi di nnyunbun aanyupɔm ŋa li ponn ni na aapaacham, 51le ki di santina aadɔ, ni nkiisuk, ni ŋŋmiman na, ki kpee linanjel li gur baa kɔr na bɔ waah ba ku linanjel li na aasin, ni nnyunpɔm na ponn ni, aan ki di yɔk yɔk lidichal ngbaan ni, nfum mulole. 52Kina le u ga di linanjel ngbaan aasin, ni nnyunpɔm, ni linanjel li fu na, ni santina aadɔ, ni nkiisuk na, ni ŋŋmiman na, ŋa lidichal ngbaan chain. 53Le u cha linanjel li fu na fii nya kitiŋ ni ki buen timoor ni. U ga ŋa kina le ki toor lidichal ngbaan chain, le li ŋa chain.
54Ikaal i m di tii nimi ki joo cha tiwon aaween i bir na, 55-56ni ibuun, ni ŋichakpelar, ni tiwanduunkaan, ni lipɔpɔl li ŋani ŋikeken bee ŋidichal ni na, le na. 57Ikaal ngbaan le mɔk tiwan ni ye chain, ni ni kaa ye chain na.

english_text:
Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
8If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 9-10Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
translation_text:
Tiwan ni ŋani unii tijɔŋdaan na aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr nan ki di ikaal imina tii Moses ni Aaronn 2ke bi di mɔk Israel yaab. N‑yoonn mu uja aachakpaln ni ti nyan tinar na kan, tinar ngbaan pu na, waa ki bi chain. 3Ni yaa ye ke ti nya tibaa pu, bee ti yaa ŋeeb li kan, tima pu na, waa bi chain. 4U yaa doon tiwandookaan ni pu na, bee u kal ni pu kan, tiwandookaan ngbaan aa ki bi chain. 5Unii umɔk meeh tiwandookaan ngbaan, 6bee u kal tiwan nimɔk pu uja ngbaan kal na kan, u finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 7Sin umɔk meeh uja u tinar nya u ni na kan, finn saawanpeenkaan mɔmɔk, ki fu nnyun, le saan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 8Uja u tinar nya u ni na yaa tii timɔɔtan lɔb sin u bi chain na kan, finn saawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, le saan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 9Uja ngbaan yaa kal tiwankaakaan nimɔk pu na kan, naa ki bi chain. 10Le unii umɔk meeh waah kal tiwan ni pu na kan, udaan aa ki bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. Unii yaa tun waah kal tiwan ni pu na kan, u finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun mu, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 11Uja ngbaan yaa kaa ŋir uŋaal ki meeh unii u na kan, udaan ngbaan finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, le waan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 12Tiyakr aabuul limɔk uja ngbaan meeh na, ni gbaa wii li; le ni yaa ye idɔ aasambil kan, ni ŋir ŋi mɔmɔk.
13Nee aapuwɔb na, waaween ngbaan yaa doo kan, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole daal, aan ki nin finn waawanpeenkaan, ki fu nnyunbun aanyunpɔm, le u ga ŋa chain. 14Winiin daal kan, u ban ŋinanjel ŋilee, bee ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee, ki di buen Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee, ki ti di tii utotoor. 15Utotoor ga di linanjel libaa toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken mu toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na. Kina le u ga toor ki ŋa udaan ngbaan chain.
16N‑yoonn mu uja daŋ tidaŋ ki nyeen tijar gbaa ubaa na, u fu uwon mɔmɔk nnyun, ki mu aan ki li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 17Tijar ngbaan yaa lir likekeln, bee ngban pu kan, ni finn tiwan ngbaan, le naan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 18Uja yaa doon upii chee doo kan, bi mɔmɔk fu nnyun, ki mu aan ki li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.
19N‑yoonn mu upii kan mpiikpen na, waa ki bi chain ki ti saa iwiin ilole. Unii umɔk meeh u na kan, waa ki bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 20Tiwan nimɔk u kal, bee u doon ni pu, ki joo mpiikpen na, tiwan ngbaan aa ki bi chain. 21-23Unii umɔk meeh waawandookaan, bee tiwan nimɔk u kal ni pu na kan, u finn waawanpeenkaan, ki fu nnyun, udaan mu aan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 24Uja yaa doon upii ngbaan chee buyoonn u joo mpiikpen na kan, waah kaa bi chain pu na le cha uja mu ŋa tijɔŋ, le uja ngbaan mu aan li bi chain ki ti saa iwiin ilole, le waah doon tiwandookaan ni pu na mu aa bi chain.
25Upii aapiikpen yaa doo aan nsin beenin nya, ni mu aa ki ye mpiikpen pu, le nsin ngbaan nya kaa door kan, waa bi chain, le ni bi ke waah joo mpiikpen kan, waah kaa bi chain pu na la. 26N‑yoonn mu nsin ngbaan beenin nya na, tiwandookaan nimɔk u doon ni pu na, ni tiwan nimɔk u kal ni pu na, aa ki bi chain. 27Le unii umɔk meeh tiwan ngbaan na mu aa ki bi chain, see u finn waawanpeenkaan, ki fu nnyun, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. 28Nee aapuwɔb, nsin ngbaan yaa gii kaa ki nya kan, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole daal le ki nin ŋa chain. 29Winiin daal kan, upii ngbaan ban ŋinanjel ŋilee, bee ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee, ki di buen Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Waabool aabisamɔb, utotoor chee. 30Le utotoor ga di libaa toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken mu toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aatork. Kina le u ga toor ki ŋa upii ngbaan chain.
31Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke u sur Israel yaab baah kaa bi chain pu na, nima kan, bi li nyi ki taa bii Waabool li u bi li ponn ni, ki si bikaasisik ni na, ke bi yaa bii li kan, u ga ku bi.
32Ikaal imina le ye ki joo cha uja u tinar nya uchakpaln ni, bee u yaa nyeen tijar gbaa ubaa, 33bee upii u bi mpiikpen ni na, bee upii u joo mpiikpen aan uja doon u chee na aabɔr wɔb.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Titunwanbir aatork aawiindaal
1Aaronn aajapɔtiib bilee na aah nan di mmii mu kaa bi chain, ki see tulalee aayon tii Uwumbɔr aan ki kpo na aapuwɔb, 2le Uwumbɔr len Moses chee ke, “Bui aakpel Aaronn ke u taa li koo Chain Chain Aapepel ni, nin chee likekeln gii Libool ngbaan ni na yɔl yɔl, see n‑yoonn mu u ga koo ni ponn ni na ti fuu, ba pu? nima chee le m bi ntaalangbam ni, Maakaal Aadakaa aabiil aapaacham. U yaa yii ki koo kan, u ga kpo. 3N‑yoonn mu u ti joo ni unaajabo u nan toor titunwanbir aatork, ni upihja u u joo ni u nan toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, le u ga ŋmaa koo nima chee.”
4Uwumbɔr nan ki di baah ga li ŋani pu na tuk u. Waahr aan Aaronn koo Chain Chain Aapepel ni na, see u fu nnyun, ki di utotoor aawanpeenkaan peen: nima le ye ŋitanyaan aabɔkul ni lipeetugeln, ni ligbapapaln, ni kiyikpupuk.
5Israel yaab mɔmɔk ga kpaan tii Aaronn iŋoja ilee u di toor titunwanbir aatork, ni upihja u di toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin aatork. 6U di unaaja toor kitork ki nyan ubaa, ni waamaal aatunwanbir. 7Le u ga di iŋoja ilee na buen Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Waabool aabisamɔb chee. 8U ban ŋitakpal ŋilee nima chee ki daan libaa pu ke, “Uwumbɔr yaan,” ki daan liken pu ke, “Titunwanbir aanyam aaŋoob,” ki too inaan. 9Le Aaronn ga di uŋoob u ye Uwumbɔr yoo na, ki di toor titunwanbir aatork ki tii u. 10Uŋoob u ye titunwanbir aanyam aaŋoob na, Aaronn ga di u tii Uwumbɔr, u fuub, aan bi di u buen kipɔɔk ni, ki ti di u lii, u li cha, le u ga di binib ngbaan aatunwanbir buen.
11N‑yoonn mu Aaronn di unaaja na toor titunwanbir aatork ki nyan ubaa, ni waamaal aatunwanbir na, 12u yoor mmii aasambil ki ban kitork aabimbiln pu mmiisakɔl, ki lee tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ na iŋaal ilee, aan ki li joo ni Chain Chain Aapepel ni. 13Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nima chee, u di tulalee aayon ngbaan paan mmii pu, lisambil ni, le iŋmanyuu ga fii biin Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aabiil pu, nima kan, waan kan libiil ngbaan, ki kpo. 14U ga di uŋanbik bɔ unaaja na aasin ni, ki di ngem yɔk yɔk libiil ngbaan aamɔb pu, ki di ngem yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa chee, nfum mulole.
15U yaa ŋa kina doo kan, u kɔr uŋoja ki di toor binib ngbaan aatunwanbir aatork, ki li joo ni waasin Chain Chain Aapepel ni, aan ki nan di mu yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa chee, ni waabiil pu, ke waah di unaaja aasin ŋa pu na. 16Kina le u ga toor ki ŋa Chain Chain Aapepel ni chain, ki nyan Israel yaab aah kaa bi chain pu na, ni baatunwanbir. U ŋa Libool ngbaan kina, ba pu? li si binib ngbaan aah ka pu na aakaasisik ni la, le baa bi chain. 17N‑yoonn mu Aaronn koo Chain Chain Aapepel ni, u ti toor aan ki ŋa ni chain, ki ki nya ni na, unii ubaa taa li bi Libool ngbaan ni. N‑yoonn mu u toor ki ŋa ubaa, ni waamaal, ni binib ngbaan chain na, 18u nyan buen kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aabimbiln chee, ki ti ŋa li chain. U ban unaaja aasin ngem, ni uŋoja aasin ngem, ki di ŋa libimbiln ngbaan aamɔju aalɔlɔ ni. 19U di uŋanbik bɔ nsin ngbaan ni, ki di ngem yɔk yɔk libimbiln ngbaan pu nfum mulole. Kina le u ga ŋa li, ki nyan li Israel yaab aatunwanbir ni, ki ŋa li chain.
Uŋoob u nyani baatunwanbir na aabɔr
20N‑yoonn mu Aaronn toor Chain Chain Aapepel, ni Uwumbɔr Aabool aapepel li gur na, ni kitork aabimbiln doo na, u di uŋoob u nyani baatunwanbir na, ki di siin Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni. 21U di uŋaal ilee paan uŋoob ngbaan aayil pu, ki kpiir Israel yaab aatunwanbir, ni baah yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb pu na mɔmɔk, ŋa uyil pu, ki nyan uja ubaa, u jenn uŋoob ngbaan buen kipɔɔk ni. 22Le uŋoob ngbaan ga di baatunwanbir ti bi u pu na buen nin chee binib aa bi na.
23Nee aapuwɔb le Aaronn ga gir koo Libool na ponn ni, ki ti peer waatotoor aawanpeenkaan ni u ba pee ki di koo Chain Chain Aapepel ni na, ki di leen li ponn ni. 24U ban nnyun ki fu mu, chain aapepel ni, ki ki di ubaa aawanpeenkaan peen. U yaa ŋa kina doo kan, u nya ki ti toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ki nyan ubaa, ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk mu aatunwanbir. 25U di kiwakork ki u di toor titunwanbir aatork na aakpan see mmii, kitork aabimbiln paab. 26Uja u jenn uŋoob u nyan baatunwanbir na buen kipɔɔk ni na, finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun waahr aan ki nin kun linampal biken chee. 27Unaaja ni uŋoob ni bi di toor titunwanbir aatork na aasin mu bi joo ni Chain Chain Aapepel ni ke mu nyan titunwanbir na, bi di i nya lipaal nibaa chee ki ti see i mmii ni. Bi di igban, ni tinann, ni tineer mɔmɔk see mmii ni. 28Udaan u di ni see mmii ni na finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun waahr aan ki nin gir kun linampal biken chee.
Baah ga joo titunwanbir aatork aawiindaal pu na aabɔr
29Ni li dii ikaal imina ki cha n‑yoonn mu choo na mɔmɔk. Ŋmalole aawinpiik daal kan, Israel yaab, ni biwɔwɔm mɔmɔk bi koo bi chee na kpaan ki lul bumɔb, ki taa tun lituln libaa liyaadaal ngbaan. 30Liyaadaal kan, utotoor toor ki nyan binib ngbaan baatunwanbir mɔmɔk ni, ki ŋa bi chain. 31Liyaadaal ngbaan ye chain chain aawiin la. Ni lul bumɔb liyaadaal ngbaan, ki taa tun lituln libaa. Ni li joo ikaal ngbaan ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 32Utotoorninkpel u bi di nkpan kpir uyil pu, ki kaan u mbamɔm, ke u nan gaa ute aajal na le ga toor kitork ki nyani titunwanbir na. U di utotoor aawanpeenkaan peen, 33aan ki toor Chain Chain Aapepel, ni Uwumbɔr Aabool aapepel li gur na, ni kitork aabimbiln, ni bitotoorb, ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk ki ŋa ni mɔmɔk chain. 34Ni li joo ikaal ngbaan ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Libiln ni kan, ni toor kitork ngbaan nfum mubaa, ki nyan Israel yaab mɔmɔk baatunwanbir ni, ki ŋa bi chain.
Kina pu na, Moses nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah tuk u pu na.

english_text:
Where To Offer Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
3-4Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 5And so, when you sacrifice an animal to ask my blessing, it must not be done out in a field, 6but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 7Don't ever turn from me again and offer sacrifices to goat-demons. This law will never change.
8Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere 9except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people.
Do Not Eat Blood
The Lord said:
10 I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you. 11 Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own. 12That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood. 13Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
14The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
15If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening. 16If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
translation_text:
Nsin aabɔr
1Le Uwumbɔr bui Moses 2ke u di ikaal imina di tii Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib, ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk. 3-4Israel aanii umɔk kɔr unaa, bee upiih, bee uŋoob ki di toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr lipaal nibaa chee, kaa di buen Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee unimbiin ni na kan, u bii Uwumbɔr aakaal la. U nyan tiwan ni fu na aamɔfal yɔli; waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa. 5Nkaal ngbaan aatataa le ye ke Israel yaab mɔmɔk li joo ni baawakor ti bi joo toor kitiŋ ponn ni yɔl yɔl na nan toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr. Bi li joo i ki nan di tii utotoor, Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee, aan u di toor kimɔbaan aapiin aatork. 6Le utotoor ga di nsin mee kpir kpir kitork aabimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk, Libool aabisamɔb chee, ki di nkpan see mmii, aan ni nyan nnumɔɔn, ki li nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee. 7Israel aanib taa ki yii Uwumbɔr ki li kɔr baawakor tisar, ni ŋinampal, ki toor kitork tii kinimbɔŋ. Israel aanib mɔmɔk li joo nkaal ngbaan ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
8Israel aanii ubaa, bee biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na ubaa yaa toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, bee u yaa toor kitork kibaa aaboln nibaa chee 9ki tii Uwumbɔr, kaa di buen Waabool aabisamɔb chee kan, waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.
10Israel aanii ubaa, bee biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na ponn ni ubaa yaa ŋman tinann ti nsin beenin bi ti ponn ni na kan, Uwumbɔr ga daa utafal, udaan ngbaan aan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa. 11Tiwanfuurkaan mɔmɔk aamɔfal bi nsin ni la, kina pu le Uwumbɔr siin nkaal ke ni nyan tiwakor aasin mɔmɔk ŋa kitork aabimbiln pu, aan mu nyan binib ngbaan aatunwanbir. Nsin, mu ye limɔfal na, le nyani titunwanbir. 12Nima pu le Uwumbɔr tuk Israel yaab ke bi ni biwɔwɔm bi koo bi chee na ubaa taa ŋmɔ tinann ti nsin beenin bi ti ponn ni na.
13Israel aanii ubaa, bee biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na ubaa yaa buen kikpaŋ ki ku upeel, bee unyoon u ni ga ji u na kan, u kɔr u ki nyan nsin lii kitiŋ, ki di titan biin mu pu. 14Ba pu? tiwanfuurkaan mɔmɔk aamɔfal bi nsin ni la, nima pu le Uwumbɔr bui Israel yaab ke bi taa ji tinann ti nsin bi ti ponn ni na, ke unii umɔk ŋa kina na, waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.
15Israel aanii, bee uwɔwɔnja umɔk jin kiwakork ki kpo kibaa pu, bee upeel yaa chuu kiwakork ki ki ŋman gur na kan, udaan finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, ki li kii kijook wɔb aan ki nin ŋa chain. 16U yaa yii kan, u ga kan ntafadaan.

english_text:
Forbidden Sex
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel:
I am the Lord your God! 3So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you. 4I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings. 5 Obey them and you will live. I am the Lord.
6Don't have sex with any of your close relatives, 7especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father. 8 And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives. 9 Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not. 10Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter 11or half sister 12-13 or a sister of your father or mother. 14Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife. 15 Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law 16 or sister-in-law. 17 And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean. 18As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
19 When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
20 Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
21 Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
22 It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
23 Anyone who has sex with an animal is unclean.
24Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves 25and the land so unclean, that I punished the land because of their sins, and I made it vomit them up. 26-27Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings. 28Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them. 29-30If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
translation_text:
Mbimbin mu kaa ŋan na aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses 2ke u tuk Israel yaab ke, “Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. 3Ni taa dii Ijipt yaab bi ni nan bi bi chee na aah ŋani pu na, bee Kanaann yaab bi aatiŋ pu m joo nimi cha na aah ŋani pu na. 4Ni kii ki li joo maakaal ki ŋa maah bui nimi pu na. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. 5Ni li ŋani ki li dii maakaal i m di mɔk nimi na; ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga li kpa limɔfal. Min le ye Uwumbɔr.”
6Le Uwumbɔr nan di ikaal imina tuk bi. Ni taa doon nimi aamaal ni aapii ubaa chee. 7Taa koo ki ti doon aana chee ki jinn aate inimɔɔn. Taa jinn aana inimɔɔn. 8Taa koo ki ti doon aate aapuutiib ubaa chee ki jinn aate inimɔɔn. 9Taa koo ki ti doon aaninkpan u ye aate aabisal, bee aana aabisal na chee, bi yaa ma u nibaa chee, bee aa ni u yaa kpaan lichiln kan, naa ŋan ke aa doon u chee. 10Taa koo ti doon upii u ye aayaabil na chee; ni ga li ye inimɔɔn le ki tii si. 11Taa koo aatewaa, bee aatekpel aabisal chee, ba pu? u mu ye aaninkpan la. 12-13Taa koo ki ti doon aapuul chee, naa ŋan ke aa doon aate aaninkpan, bee aanakpel, bee aanawaa chee. 14Taa koo ki ti doon aatewaa, bee aatekpel aapuu chee, u mu ye aapuul la. 15Taa koo ki ti doon aabipuu chee, 16bee aakpel, bee aanaal aapuu chee. 17Aa taa koo ki ti doon upii u aa doon u chee na aabisal, bee uyaabil chee, bi ye saamaal ni aanib la, le naa ŋan ke aa ŋa kina. 18Aapuu yaa beenin bi limɔfal ni kan, aa taa ki yoor unaal, bee ukpel, ki di ŋa aapuu.
19Upii yaa joo mpiikpen kan, taa koo ki ti doon u chee, ba pu? waah bi chain. 20Taa koo ki ti doon aaŋeen aatɔ aapuu chee; ni ga cha ni taa ki li bi chain. 21Taa di nimi aabim tii ke bi di toor kitork tii liwaal Molek, ba pu? ni ga joo ni inimɔɔn Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu. 22Uja ubaa taa koo ti doon uja ŋeen aatɔ chee; Uwumbɔr aa gee kina. 23Uja taa doon kiwakork chee, upii mu taa cha kiwakork doon u chee; kininsuŋ ngbaan le ga ŋa nimi tijɔŋ.
24Ni taa cha tiwan nimina mɔmɔk bii nimi ki ŋa nimi tijɔŋ; kina le binib bi kaa dii Uwumbɔr na ŋani le kaa bi chain, binib kina aaboln le bi kitiŋ ki ni chaa koo ki ni na, le Uwumbɔr ga jenn nyan bi, aan ni gaa ki. 25Baah tun pu na le cha kitiŋ ngbaan aa bi chain, le kina pu Uwumbɔr ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan fam, le binib ngbaan aa ŋman bi koo ki ponn ni. 26-27Bi ŋa inimɔɔn aawan ngbaan mɔmɔk kina, le ki cha kitiŋ ngbaan aa bi chain. Nima taa ŋa kina kpala. Ni mɔmɔk, Israel yaab, ni biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na, ni li joo Uwumbɔr aakaal, ni waah len pu na mɔmɔk, 28le kitiŋ ngbaan ga li ŋan tii nimi, kaan yii nimi ke kaah nan yii binib bi nan koo ki ponn ni na. 29Ni nyi ke unii umɔk ŋa inimɔɔn aawan nee na, waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.
30Le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ni kii ki li joo maah di ikaal i tuk nimi na, ki taa dii binib bi koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni na aah ŋani pu na ki cha baabimbin ngbaan bii nimi, ki ŋa nimi tijɔŋ. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Moral and Religious Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2 to say to the community of Israel:
I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too! 3-4 Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
5When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions. 6You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day. 7If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it. 8In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
9 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. 10Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
11 Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
12 Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
13 Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
14 I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
15 Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
16Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
17 Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting. 18 Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
19 Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
20If a man has sex with a slave woman who is promised in marriage to someone else, he must pay a fine, but they are not to be put to death. After all, she was still a slave at the time. 21-22The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the sacred tent and give it to a priest, who will then offer it as a sacrifice to me, so the man's sins will be forgiven.
23After you enter the land, you will plant fruit trees, but you are not to eat any fruit from them for the first three years. 24In the fourth year the fruit must be set apart, as an expression of thanks 25to me, the Lord God. Do this, and in the fifth year, those trees will produce an abundant harvest of fruit for you to eat.
26 Don't eat the blood of any animal.
Don't practice any kind of witchcraft.
27-28 I forbid you to shave any part of your head or beard or to cut and tattoo yourself as a way of worshiping the dead.
29 Don't let your daughters serve as temple prostitutes—this would bring disgrace both to them and the land.
30 I command you to respect the Sabbath and the place where I am worshiped.
31 Don't make yourselves disgusting to me by going to people who claim they can talk to the dead.
32I command you to show respect for older people and to obey me with fear and trembling.
33 Don't mistreat any foreigners who live in your land. 34Instead, treat them as well as you treat your own people and love them as much as you love yourself. Remember, you were once foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
35-36 Use honest scales and don't cheat when you weigh or measure anything.
I am the Lord your God. I rescued you from Egypt, 37and I command you to obey my laws.
translation_text:
Mbimbin chain ni mbamɔn aakaal
1Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses 2ke u tuk Israel yaab ke, “Ni li bi chain, ba pu? min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi chain la. 3Ni mɔmɔk li pak nitetiib ni ninatiib, ki li joo Likpaakool daal ke maah siin pu na. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
4“Ni taa yii mi aan ki li dooni ŋiwaa, ni taa di tikur naan ŋiwaa ki doon ŋi. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
5“N‑yoonn mu ni kɔr kiwakork ki ŋa kimɔbaan aatork na, ni li joo ikaal i m tuk nimi na, le m ga gaa kitork ngbaan. 6Bundaal ni kɔr kitork ngbaan aawakork na kan, ni ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan liyaadaal, ni kitaak ki ga ki woln na. Wintaa daal, tinann ngbaan yaa ki gur kan, ni taa ŋmɔ ti, ni see ti mmii ni, 7ba pu? taa ki bi chain, le umɔk ŋman ti na kan, maan ki gaa waapiin aatork. 8Unii umɔk ŋman ti na aabɔr ga bii, ke waa lik faar tiwan ni bi di tii mi na, waan ki li ye maanib ponn ni ubaa.
9“Ni yaa bi chee tijikaar, nimi aasar ni kan, tijikaar ti bi mmogbaan na, ni taa chee ti, ki taa ki gir buen naah chee nimi aasar ti ni na, ki ti lɔi tijikaar ti gur na. 10Ni taa ki gir buen nimi aasubil aasar ni, ki ti lɔi ŋisubil ŋi gur, ni ŋi lir kitiŋ na; di cha ŋi man, aan bigiim ni biwɔwɔm buen ti lɔi. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
11“Ni taa su kinaayuk, bee ni ji niŋeen aatɔ pem pem, bee ni gii inyamɔn. 12Ni yaa kaan ŋmaa giin tipuur kan, ni taa puu ti maayimbil pu. Mbimbin kina joo ni inimɔɔn le maayimbil pu. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
13“Ni taa ji unii ubaa pem pem, bee ni gaa waawan. Unii yaa tun saatuln kan, pɔɔn aabaa ki pa u, ki taa cha ni woln kitaak. 14Ni li san min ijawaan man, ki taa puun lii utafakpaa pu, ki taa di tiwan bil ujoon aasan ni ke u gbeer ki lir. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
15“Ni yaa bi ji unii tibɔr kan, ni len ibamɔn ki li kpa kipak; ni yaa ji ugiin tibɔr kan, ni taa li kpa imaagann, ki mu taa li san biwankpadam ijawaan. 16Ni taa li geei inyamɔn paani unii ubaa. Bi yaa bi ji unii ubaa aabɔr aan u ban u nyan nkun ni, aan aa nyi ke u kpa mbamɔn kan, ter u ki gaa u lii. Min le ye Uwumbɔr.
17“Aa taa li joo aaŋeen aatɔ liŋuul; pɔɔn aabaa ki toor nimi aabɔr ni man, nima kan, saan tun titunwanbir u pu. 18Aa taa li ban ke aa teen ubaa bakaa, ki li nan udaan ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, tɔ, aa li gee aaŋeen aatɔ ke saah gee aabaa pu na. Min le ye Uwumbɔr.
19“Ni li joo maakaal. Ni taa di linampal aawakor ti kaa kpaa na kpaan tɔb chee ke ti dur. Ni taa di njikaabim mulee aabɔŋ kpaan bu bukpaab bubaa ni, ki taa di tikokonn ni tiwan ni kaa ye tikokonn na ŋmal tɔb ni ki di ŋa tiwanpeenkaan.
20“Uja yaa puu ke u ga di waanaagbiipiibo kooh tii uja ŋeen aatɔ ke u li ye upuu, le uja u ban u daa upiibo na yaa kaa kee pan, le uja uken yaa doon upiibo ngbaan chee kan, ni daa bitafal, ni taa ku bi; ba pu? unaagbiipii ngbaan laa beenin ye udindaan yoo la. 21Uja ngbaan li joo ni upihja Maabool aabisamɔb chee, ki nan pa lipɔln aatork. 22Le utotoor ga toor ki ŋa u chain ki nyan u waatunwanbir ni, le min Uwumbɔr ga di cha pinn u.
23“Ni yaa ti fuu Kanaann aatiŋ ni, ki bun ŋisubil aasui aaboln i na kan, ni taa kee ji yaasubil ngbaan ki ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa, ba pu? ni kɔ. Ŋibin ŋitaa ngbaan ni, ni taa ji ŋi. 24Libiln nanar ni kan, ni di ŋisubil ngbaan mɔmɔk tii mi Uwumbɔr, ni li ye nimi aadoon aatork. 25Libiln ŋmuŋmur ni kan, ni ga ŋmaa ji ŋisubil ngbaan. Ni yaa ŋa maah mɔk nimi pu na kan, nimi aasubil aasui ga lu sakpen. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
26“Ni taa ŋmɔ tinann ti nsin beenin bi ti ni na. Ni taa li ŋani bibɔɔb aatuln ki ji inyɔk. 27Ni taa chee nitapak ni ŋilangban aakor, 28bee ni daan nimi aawon pu nibaa chee, bee ni geei geei niwon utekpiir pu. Min le ye Uwumbɔr.
29“Ni taa di nibisatiib ŋa tiwaadir ni aadagoob ki jinn bi inimɔɔn; ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga fenn dii ŋiwaa, le kitiŋ ngbaan ga gbiin kidagook aatuln ŋmeen. 30Ni li joo Likpaakool aawiin chain, ki li pak nin chee ni dooni mi na. Min le ye Uwumbɔr.
31“Ni taa ban binib bi baa bitekpiib chee tibɔr na aasurm. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga bii nibaa, kaan ki li bi chain. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
32“Min le ye Uwumbɔr, ni li san mi ijawaan, ki li pak binib bi jer nimi na, ki li nyuŋni bi.
33“Ni taa ŋa biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na mbiin. 34Ni li ŋani bi tiŋann ke naah ŋani niŋeen aatɔtiib Israel yaab biken pu na, ki li gee bi ke naah gee nibaa pu na. Ni teer ke ni mu nan ye biwɔwɔm le Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
35“Ni taa ji tɔb pem pem ki joo tiwan ni kaa ye nibamɔnn na ŋaŋni tiwan aafɔfɔk, ni naanyunyuun, ni naawiwiir. 36Ni li joo mbamɔn aawan ŋaŋni tiwan mɔmɔk. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, le ki nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 37Ni li joo maakaal ki ŋa maah len pu na mɔmɔk. Min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Penalties for Disobeying God's Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
Death by stoning is the penalty for any citizens or foreigners in the country who sacrifice their children to the god Molech. 3They have disgraced both the place where I am worshiped and my holy name, and so I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. 4Some of you may let them get away with human sacrifice, 5but not me. If any of you worship Molech, I will turn against you and your entire family, and I will no longer let you belong to my people.
6I will be your enemy if you go to someone who claims to speak with the dead, and I will destroy you from among my people. 7Dedicate yourselves to me and be holy because I am the Lord your God. 8I have chosen you as my people, and I expect you to obey my laws.
