40Arad aabɔr u nan bi Kanaann aatiŋ, ŋŋangii wɔb na, nan ŋun ke Israel yaab choo.
41-49Israel yaab aah nan nyan Hor Aajool chee ke bi ti fuu Moab yaab aateer ni, ki kal kal ntim mu ni na aayimbil le paa na: Salmona, ni Punonn, ni Obof, ni Abarim aalangbenn ti bi Moab aapepel ni na, ni Dibonn Gad, ni Almonn Diblataim, ni Abarim Aajool li bi gbɔk Nebo Aajool chee na, ni Moab yaab aateer mu bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee ki lik Jeriko aatiŋ limɔɔdapuul na, ni bi Bef Jesimof ni Sitim Aafataŋ aakaasisik ni la.
Baah ga ti ŋa pu Jɔɔdann aamɔɔdapuul na aabɔr
50Baah nan bi Moab yaab aateer mu bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee ki lik Jeriko aatiŋ limɔɔdapuul na, le Uwumbɔr nan tuk Moses 51ke u bui Israel yaab tibɔr ti paa na: “N‑yoonn mu ni puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki koo Kanaann aatiŋ ni na, 52ni pɔɔn nibaa ki jenn nyan binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni na. Ni bii baah di ŋitakpal ni tikur ŋa baawaa ŋi na, ni ŋiwaa ngbaan aah si nin chee na mɔmɔk. 53Ni gaa kitiŋ ngbaan ki kal nima, ba pu? m di ki tii nimi la. 54Ni too inaan ki yakr kitiŋ ngbaan ki tii ŋinibol, ni itaŋaal ni yaab mɔmɔk. Bi aataŋaal yaab wiir na kan, ni gii kitiŋ ki li wiir ki tii bi, aan ki gii kitiŋ waatiir tii bi kaa wiir na mu. 55Tɔ, ni yaa yii, kaa jenn nyan binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni na kan, bi gur na ga tii nimi tibɔr pam, ki li bi ke liwanchɔl na le ninimbil ni, ki ki li bi ke ikokon na le ki saar nimi, le ki ga tak nimi. 56Ni yaa kaa jenn nyan bi kan, m ga kuln nimi, ke maah dak ke m ga kuln bi pu na.”

english_text:
Israel's Borders
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel that their land in Canaan would have the following borders:
3The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea. 4It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon. 5It will run along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
6The western border will be the Mediterranean Sea.
7The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor. 8After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land. 9From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
10The eastern border will begin at Hazar-Enan in the north, then run south to Shepham, 11and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee, 12then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea.
The land within those four borders will belong to you.
13 Then Moses told the people, “You will receive the land inside these borders. It will be yours, but the Lord has commanded you to divide it among the nine and a half tribes. 14The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh have already been given their land 15across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.”
The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
16The Lord said to Moses, 17“Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites. 18One leader from each tribe will help them, 19-28and here is the list of their names:
Caleb son of Jephunneh
from Judah,
Shemuel son of Ammihud
from Simeon,
Elidad son of Chislon
from Benjamin,
Bukki son of Jogli
from Dan,
Hanniel son of Ephod
from Manasseh,
Kemuel son of Shiphtan
from Ephraim,
Elizaphan son of Parnach
from Zebulun,
Paltiel son of Azzan
from Issachar,
Ahihud son of Shelomi
from Asher,
and Pedahel son of Ammihud
from Naphtali.”
29These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_text:
Kanaann aatiŋ aanaanmɔk
1Uwumbɔr nan tuk Moses 2ke u di tibɔr timina bui Israel yaab, “Ni yaa koo Kanaann aatiŋ ki m ban m di tii nimi na ni kan, kitiŋ ngbaan aanaanmɔk aah ga li ye pu na sɔ: 3Kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangii wɔb ga dii kina ti nya Sinn aateersakpiin ni, ki dii Edom aatiŋ mɔk. Ki yoor liwipuul wɔb, nimi aatiŋ ga piin N‑yaan Aanyusakpem aadoon mɔk ŋŋangii wɔb la; 4le ki fenn buen ŋŋangii wɔb ki di toŋ Akrabim aasan wɔb, ki puur ti nya Sinn aateersakpiin ni, ki ti nya Kades Banea aaŋangii wɔb; le ki ki fenn kpaa ŋŋangan ni liwilir wɔb ki di buen Hasar Adar, le ki di ti ker Asmonn aatiŋ pu, 5nima chee le ki ga fenn toŋ kifataŋ ki bi Ijipt aanaanmɔk na, ki ti doo Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem chee.
6“Kitiŋ ngbaan aawilir wɔb aanaanmɔk le ga li ye Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk.
7“Kitiŋ ngbaan ŋŋangan wɔb kan, ni lur nkuul ki yoor Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk, ki ti nya Hor Aajool pu, 8ki ki yoor nima ti nya Hamaf aasan chee; le ki di dii kina ti nya Sedad, 9ki ki di kina ti nya Sifronn chee, ki ti doo Hasar Enann.
10“Kitiŋ ngbaan liwipuul aanaanmɔk kan, ni ga lur nkuul ki yoor Hasar Enann chee, ki ti nya Sefam pu; 11le ki ga dii ŋŋangii wɔb ki ti nya Habel pu, Ayinn aawipuul wɔb, le ki dii ŋigongon pu, ki ti nya Galilee Aanyusakpem aagbaan, liwipuul wɔb, 12le ki yoor kina ki dii ŋŋangii wɔb, ki di kpaŋ Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, ki ti nya N‑yaan Aanyusakpem chee.
“Kitiŋ ngbaan aapepel ŋinaa aanaanmɔk le na.”
13Moses nan bui Israel yaab ke, “Naah ga too inaan ki yakr kitiŋ ki na le na. Kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr di tii ŋinibol ŋiwae ni ligeln na le na. 14Rubenn, ni Gad, ni Manase aanibol ligeln bi bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl liwipuul wɔb na, bima puun kan baatiŋ a, bi yakr kitiŋ ngbaan deedee, ki ŋeer baamaal aah ye pu na, 15ki bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb, ki tok Jeriko aatiŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann aawilir wɔb na.”
Biyidam bi aatuln nan ye ke bi yakr kitiŋ ngbaan na
16Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, 17“Eleasar u ye utotoor na, ni Nunn aajapɔɔn Josua le ga yakr kitiŋ ngbaan ki tii Israel aanibol ngbaan. 18Nyan linibol mɔmɔk ni uyidaan, aan bi ter bi.” 19-28Bijab bi Uwumbɔr nan nyan na sɔ:
Linibol Uyidaan
Juda Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb
Simeonn Amihud aajapɔɔn Selumiel
Benjaminn Kislonn aajapɔɔn Elidad
Dann Jogli aajapɔɔn Buki
Manase Efod aajapɔɔn Haniel
Efraim Siftann aajapɔɔn Kemuel
Sebulunn Paanak aajapɔɔn Elisafann
Isakar Asann aajapɔɔn Paltiel
Aser Selomi aajapɔɔn Ahihud
Naftali Amihud aajapɔɔn Pedahel
29Uwumbɔr nan nyan binib bee le ke bi yakr Kanaann aatiŋ tii Israel yaab ngbaan.

english_text:
The Towns for the Levites
1 While the people of Israel were still camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses 2to say to them:
When you receive your tribal lands, you must give towns and pastures to the Levi tribe. 3That way, the Levites will have towns to live in and pastures for their animals. 4-5The pasture around each of these towns must be in the shape of a square, with the town itself in the center. The pasture is to measure 900 meters on each side, with 450 meters of land outside each of the town walls. This will be the Levites' pastureland.
6Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites 42 other towns, 7so they will have a total of 48 towns with their surrounding pastures.
8Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones.
The Safe Towns
(Deuteronomy 19.1-13; Joshua 20.1-9)
9 The Lord then told Moses 10to tell the people of Israel:
After you have crossed the Jordan River and are settled in Canaan, 11choose Safe Towns, where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. 12If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
13There are to be six of these Safe Towns, 14three on each side of the Jordan River. 15They will be places of protection for anyone who lives in Israel and accidentally kills someone.
Laws about Murder and Accidental Killing
The Lord said:
16-18Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death 19by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
20-21Or suppose you get angry and kill someone by pushing or hitting or by throwing something. You are a murderer and must be put to death by one of the victim's relatives.
22-24But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty. 25If they decide that you are innocent, you will be protected from the victim's relative and sent to stay in one of the Safe Towns until the high priest dies. 26But if you ever leave the Safe Town 27and are killed by the victim's relative, he cannot be punished for killing you. 28You must stay inside the town until the high priest dies; only then can you go back home.
29The community of Israel must always obey these laws.
30 Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime. 31You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life! 32And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
33-34I, the Lord, live among you people of Israel, so your land must be kept pure. But when a murder takes place, blood pollutes the land, and it becomes unclean. If that happens, the murderer must be put to death, so the land will be clean again. Keep murder out of Israel!
translation_text:
Baah ga di ntim mu tii Liifai yaab na
1Baah nan bi Moab yaab aateer mu bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee ki lik Jeriko aatiŋ limɔɔdapuul wɔb na, le Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, 2“Bui Israel yaab ke kitiŋ ki bi yakr tii bi na, bi mu ki yakr baatim ngem mu li kpa kimoŋmɔpɔɔk ki mann goln ntim ngbaan na tii Liifai yaab. 3Le Liifai yaab mu ga li kpa baatim ki li bi mu ni. Le bi ga li kpaa baawakor ti mɔmɔk bi kpa na kimoŋmɔpɔɔk aatim ni. 4Kimoŋmɔpɔɔk ga piin ligoln li bi maa gob baatim na, ki taln ŋipepel mɔmɔk ki saa ŋitaa lichur libaa ni ikui iŋmu, 5nima kan, kitiŋ ngbaan aapepel ga li ŋak tɔb ki saa ŋitaa ŋichur ŋitaa, aan kitiŋ ngbaan li bi kaasisik ni. 6Ni di mbɔbɔryaan aatim muloob tii Liifai yaab, nin chee unii yaa peln ku uken kan, u ga san buen nima ki ti ŋmar na. Ni kpee na, ni ki tii bi ntim muken mu saa imonko ilee ni mulee, 7ki cha mu li kpa kimoŋmɔpɔɔk aan mu kpaan saa imonko ilee ni muniin. 8Ntim mu ni ga di tii Liifai yaab na ga nya ŋinibol ngbaan aatim aah wiir pu na la.”
Mbɔbɔryaan aatim
(Ikaal 19.1-13; Josua 20.1-9)
9Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses 10ke u tuk Israel yaab ke, “Ni yaa puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki koo Kanaann aatiŋ ni kan, 11ni nyan mbɔbɔryaan aatim, nima kan, unii yaa kaa nyi le ki peln ku uken kan, u san buen nima chee ki ŋmar. 12U yaa san ti koo nima chee kan, waah ku u na aado aanii aan ki pii u ki ku u mu. Baah galn unii u ke u ku uken na, bi taa ku u see bi jin waabɔr binib aanimbil ni. 13Ni nyan ntim muloob, 14mutaa li bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb, aan mutaa mu li bi Kanaann aatiŋ wɔb. 15Ntim ngbaan le ga li ye mbɔbɔryaan ki tii Israel yaab, ni biwɔwɔm bi koo bi chee na, ni binib bi kaan yunn ki jer kakaan na. Unii ubaa yaa kaa nyi ki ku uken kan, u ga ŋmaa san buen nima ki ŋmar.
16-18“Tɔ, unii yaa di tijawan ni ye tikur, bee litakpal, bee ndɔ ku uken kan, u ye unikur la, le ni ŋeer bi ku u mu. 19Linikpol ngbaan aado aanii kpa nsan ke u ku u teen. U yaa pii u kan, u ku u.
20“Nibaakan, unii yaa nan uken le ki tur u lii, bee u yaa di tiwan le mee u, 21bee u yaa di linyakaakul le faa ku u kan, u ye unikur la, le ni ŋeer bi ku u. Linikpol ngbaan aado aanii kpa nsan ke u ku u teen. U yaa pii u kan, u ku u.
22“Tɔ, unii yaa kaa nyi le ki peln ku uken kaa nan u kan, u yaa tur u lii, bee u yaa mee u tiwan le ki ku u, 23bee u yaa kaa lik uken wɔb le ki mee litakpal ku u, ki mu aa ye ke u ye waadin ki ban u ku u, 24kina yaa ŋa kan, bi gur na ji tibɔr kpee udaan u ku unii na pu, bi taa kpee linikpol aado yaab bi ban bi ku u teen na pu. 25Israel yaab bi gur na gaa unikur ngbaan linikpol na aado yaab chee lii, aan ki giin u buen mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ ki u nan san buen ki ponn ni na. U li koo nima ki ti saa buyoonn Utotoorninkpel u bi nan di Uwumbɔr aakpan kpir uyil pu na aah ga nan kpo na. 26Ni yaa ye ke unikur na yaa ki nyan mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ ki u nan san buen ke u ŋmar na ni 27aan linikpol ngbaan aado aanii yaa pii u ki ku u kan, waa kpa taani. 28Nima pu na, unikur yaa san buen mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ ngbaan ni kan, u taa ki nyan nima ki ti saa buyoonn Utotoorninkpel ga kpo na. Nee aapuwɔb na, unikur ngbaan ga ŋmaa gir kun. 29Israel yaab, ni biyaabitiib yaa bi nin chee mɔmɔk na kan, bi li joo nkaal ngbaan.
30“Binib yaa pii bilee, bee ki jer kina, ki ye seeraadam ki len mbamɔn ke unikur ngbaan tun taani kan, ni ŋeer bi ku u; unibaan le yaa ye seeraadaan kan, naa ŋeer ke bi ku u. 31Unikur mɔmɔk ŋeer nkun la. Waan ŋmaa pa ŋimombil ke u nya ntafadaan ngbaan ni. 32Unikur yaa san buen mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ ni kan, ni taa cha u pa ŋimombil aan ki gir kun waahr aan Utotoorninkpel nin kpo. 33Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga bii kitiŋ ki ni koo ki ponn ni na. Linikul bii kitiŋ la, le unii yaa ku uken kan, see bi ku udaan ngbaan mu, naa ye kina kan, kitork kibaa aa ki bi, ni ga ŋmaa toor ki ŋaŋ baah ku unii kitiŋ ki pu na. 34Nima pu na, ni taa bii kitiŋ ki ni koo ki ponn ni na, ba pu? min le ye Uwumbɔr, ki bi nimi Israel yaab chee.”

english_text:
The Laws about Married Women and Land
1One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel 2 and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received. 3But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, the land they receive will become part of that tribe's inheritance and will no longer belong to us. 4Even when land is returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration, we will not get back Zelophehad's land—it will belong to the tribe into which his daughters married.”
5So Moses told the people that the Lord had said:
These men from the Manasseh tribe are right. 6I will allow Zelophehad's daughters to marry anyone, as long as those men belong to one of the clans of the Manasseh tribe.
7Tribal land must not be given to another tribe—it will remain the property of the tribe that received it. 8-9In the future, any daughter who inherits land must marry someone from her own tribe. Israel's tribal land is never to be passed from one tribe to another.
10-11Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah the daughters of Zelophehad obeyed the Lord and married their uncles' sons 12and remained part of the Manasseh tribe. So their land stayed in their father's clan.
13These are the laws that the Lord gave to Moses and the Israelites while they were camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_text:
Bipiib bi mɔn tichar na aafaal aabɔr
1Gilead u nan ye Makir aajapɔɔn, ki mu ye Josef aajapɔɔn Manase aayaabil na aamaal ni aayidam nan buen Moses ni biyidam biken chee, 2ki ti bui ke, “Uwumbɔr nan tuk si ke aa too inaan aan ki yakr kitiŋ ngbaan tii Israel yaab. U nan ki tuk si ke aa yakr kitiŋ tii Selofehad u ye timi aanii na aabisatiib. 3Tɔ, bijab bi ye ŋinibol ŋiken ni aanib na yaa yoor bipiib ngbaan kan, bipiib ngbaan aafaal ga kun bichatiib yaab aanibol wɔb la, le baah nan yakr kitiŋ ki tii timi na ga bar. 4Ni yaa nan saa libiln li Israel yaab ga giin baah nan daa daa ntim mu na tii bitindam kan, Selofehad aabisatiib aatiŋ ga buen bichatiib aanibol wɔb la, le ki nya ti chee.”
5Nima pu le Moses nan di Uwumbɔr aabɔr timina tuk Israel yaab, ke Manase aanibol aah len pu na, ti ye tibɔbamɔnn la. 6Kina pu le Uwumbɔr nan bui ke Selofehad aabisatiib ga ŋmaa mɔn baah gee bijab bi na, bi mu li ye baanibol ni aajab. 7Israel aanii mɔmɔk aatiŋ ŋan ke ki bee linibol li ponn ni u nyan ni na la. 8Upii umɔk kpa kitiŋ Israel aanibol ni na, ni ŋan ke u mɔn waah nyan ni linibol li ponn ni na la. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, Israel aanii mɔmɔk ga ji uyaaja aatiŋ, 9le kitiŋ kibaa aan nyan linibol libaa ni, ki buen liken wɔb. Le linibol mɔmɔk ga li beenin kpa laatiŋ, ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
10-11Nima pu na, Selofehad aabisatiib bi bi nan yin bi ke Mala, ni Tirsa, ni Hogla, ni Milka, ni Nowa na, nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah nan tuk Moses ke bi ŋa pu na, le ki mɔn bitekpetiib, ni bitewaatiib aajapɔtiib. 12Bi nan mɔn Josef aajapɔɔn Manase aanibol ni la, le baatim mɔmɔk gaar bite aanibol ni.
13Uwumbɔr aah nan di ikaal i mɔk Moses ke u di tii Israel yaab na le na. N‑yoonn ngbaan bi nan bi Moab yaab aateer mu bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee, ki lik Jeriko aatiŋ, limɔɔdapuul wɔb.

english_text:
The Final Speeches of Moses
1-5 This book contains the speeches that Moses made while Israel was in the land of Moab, camped near the town of Suph in the desert east of the Jordan River. The town of Paran was in one direction from their camp, and the towns of Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab were in the opposite direction.
Earlier, Moses had defeated the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. Moses had also defeated King Og of Bashan, who used to live in Ashtaroth for part of the year and in Edrei for the rest of the year.
Although it takes only eleven days to walk from Mount Sinai to Kadesh-Barnea by way of the Mount Seir Road, these speeches were not made until 40 years after Israel left Egypt.
The First Speech: Moses Reviews the Past
The Lord's Command at Mount Sinai
The Lord had given Moses his laws for the people of Israel. And on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses began explaining those laws by saying:
6People of Israel, when we were in our camp at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God told us:
You have stayed here long enough. 7Leave this place and go into the land that belongs to the Amorites and their neighbors the Canaanites. This land includes the Jordan River valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Southern Desert, the Mediterranean seacoast, the Lebanon Mountains, and all the territory as far as the Euphrates River. 8I give you this land, just as I promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Now you must go and take the land.
Leaders Were Appointed
(Exodus 18.13-27)
Moses said:
9Right after the Lord commanded us to leave Mount Sinai, I told you:
Israel, being your leader is too big a job for one person. 10The Lord our God has blessed us, and so now there are as many of us as there are stars in the sky. 11God has even promised to bless us a thousand times more, and I pray that he will. 12But I cannot take care of all your problems and settle all your arguments alone. 13Each tribe must choose some experienced men who are known for their wisdom and understanding, and I will make those men the official leaders of their tribes.
14You answered, “That's a good idea!” 15Then I took these men, who were already wise and respected leaders, and I appointed them as your official leaders. Some of them became military officers in charge of groups of 1,000, or 100, or 50, or 10, 16and others became judges. I gave these judges the following instructions:
When you settle legal cases, your decisions must be fair. It doesn't matter if the case is between two Israelites, or between an Israelite and a foreigner living in your community. 17And it doesn't matter if one is helpless and the other is powerful. Don't be afraid of anyone! No matter who shows up in your court, God will help you make a fair decision.
If any case is too hard for you, bring the people to me, and I will make the decision.
18After I gave these instructions to the judges, I taught you the Lord's commands.
Men Were Sent To Explore the Hill Country
(Numbers 13.1-33)
Moses said to Israel:
19The Lord had commanded us to leave Mount Sinai and go to the hill country that belonged to the Amorites, so we started out into the huge desert. You remember how frightening it was, but soon we were at Kadesh-Barnea, 20-21and I told you, “We have reached the hill country. It belongs to the Amorites now, but the Lord our God is giving it to us. He is the same God our ancestors worshiped, and he has told us to go in and take this land, so don't hesitate and be afraid.”
22Then all of you came to me and said, “Before we go into the land, let's send some men to explore it. When they come back, they can tell us about the towns we will find and what roads we should take to get there.”
23It seemed like a good idea, so I chose twelve men, one from each tribe. 24They explored the hill country as far as Bunch Valley 25and even brought back some of the fruit. They said, “The Lord our God is giving us good land.”
Israel Refused To Obey the Lord
(Numbers 14.1-45)
Moses said to Israel:
26 You did not want to go into the land, and you refused to obey the Lord your God. 27You stayed in your tents and grumbled, “The Lord must hate us—he brought us out of Egypt, just so he could hand us over to the Amorites and get rid of us. 28We are afraid, because the men who explored the land told us that the cities are large, with walls that reach to the sky. The people who live there are taller and stronger than we are, and some of them are Anakim. We have nowhere to go.”
29Then I said, “Don't worry! 30The Lord our God will lead the way. He will fight on our side, just as he did when we saw him do all those things to the Egyptians. 31 And you know that the Lord has taken care of us the whole time we've been in the desert, just as you might carry one of your children.”
32 But you still would not trust the Lord, 33even though he had always been with us in the desert. During the daytime, the Lord was in the cloud, leading us in the right direction and showing us where to camp. And at night, he was there in the fire.
34 You had made the Lord angry, and he said:
35You people of this generation are evil, and I refuse to let you go into the good land that I promised your ancestors. 36Caleb son of Jephunneh is the only one of your generation that I will allow to go in. He obeyed me completely, so I will give him and his descendants the land he explored.
37The Lord was even angry with me because of you people, and he said, “Moses, I won't let you go into the land either. 38Instead, I will let Joshua your assistant lead Israel to conquer the land. So encourage him.”
39Then the Lord spoke to you again:
People of Israel, you said that your innocent young children would be taken prisoner in the battle for the land. But someday I will let them go into the land, and with my help they will conquer it and live there.
40Now, turn around and go back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
41Then you told me, “We disobeyed the Lord our God, but now we want to obey him. We will go into the hill country and fight, just as he told us to do.” So you picked up your weapons, thinking it would be easy to take over the hill country.
42But the Lord said, “Moses, warn them not to go into the hill country. I won't help them fight, and their enemies will defeat them.”
43I told you what the Lord had said, but you paid no attention. You disobeyed him and went into the hill country anyway. You thought you were so great! 44But when the Amorites in the hill country attacked from their towns, you ran from them as you would run from a swarm of bees. The Amorites chased your troops into Seir as far as Hormah, killing them as they went. 45Then you came back to the place of worship at Kadesh-Barnea and wept, but the Lord would not listen to your prayers.
Israel Spent Years in the Desert
Moses said to Israel:
46After we had been in Kadesh for a few months, we obeyed the Lord and headed back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
translation_text:
1Israel yaab aah nan bi nteersakpiin ni, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee, liwipuul wɔb na, le Moses di tibɔr ti bi kigbaŋ kee ponn ni na tuk bi. Bi nan bi Jɔɔdann aafataŋ ni, ki bi gbɔk kitiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Suf na, ki nan bi Parann aatiŋ, ni ntim mu bi nan yin mu ke Tofel, ni Labann, ni Haserof, ni Disahab na aakaasisik ni la. 2Aa yaa nyan ni Sainai Aajool chee ki cha Kades Banea, ki dii ŋigongon aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Edom na ni kan, aa ga di iwiin kipiik ni mbaa le fuu nima chee. 3Baah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni aan ni ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee na, ŋmapiik ni ubaa aajan aawiin daal, le Moses nan di Uwumbɔr aakaal imɔk u nan tuk u na mɔk binib ngbaan. 4Uwumbɔr aah nan nyaŋ Amor yaab aabɔr u bi yin u ke Sihonn, u nan bi Hesbonn aatiŋ ki joo waanib na, ni Basann aapepel aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Og, u nan bi Astarof ni Edrei aatim ki joo waanib na, aapuwɔb le Moses nan di ikaal ngbaan tuk bi. 5Binib ngbaan aah nan bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb, ni bi Moab aapepel ni na, le Moses piin ki kpiir Uwumbɔr aakaal ngbaan aatataa mɔk bi.
6U nan bui ke, “Taah nan bi Sainai Aajool chee buyoonn na, le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan bui timi ke, ‘Ni kal lijool ngbaan chee ni yunn pam. 7Fiin nima chee ki li cha man. Ni li cha Amor yaab aatiŋ ki ye ŋigongon na ni, ni ŋipepel mɔmɔk ŋi fab na ni, ŋi ye Jɔɔdann aafataŋ, ni ŋigongon na, ni ŋigongon aataab, ki ti ker ŋŋangii aapepel wɔb, ki yoor kina ki ti ker Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem aagbaan. Ni li cha Kanaann aatiŋ ni, ki jer koo Lebanonn Aajoo ni, ki yoor kina ki ti fuu Yufrates Aamɔɔl sakpeln mɔk. 8Ntim mumina mɔmɔk le min Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur ke m ga di tii niyaajatiib, Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob, ni biyaabitiib na. Ni li cha ki ti gaa mu man.’”
Moses aah nan lee bijojoob pu na aabɔr
(Nnyam 18.13-27)
9Le Moses bui binib ngbaan ke, “Taah nan laa bi Sainai Aajool chee na, le m nan tuk nimi ke, ‘Maah ga joo nimi m baanja pu na, lituln ngbaan wiir jer mi a. Maan ŋmaa tun li m baanja. 10Nidindaan Uwumbɔr cha ni pɔr ki wiir ke iŋmabi i bi paacham na. 11Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na, le cha ni moo pɔr ŋichur ŋichur ki jer naah bi pu na, aan ki kan tinyoor ke waah nan puu pu na. 12Tɔ, naah wiir sakpen pu na, min baanja ga ŋa kinye ki li toor nimi aabɔr? 13Ni lee ni ponn ni binib bi kpa nlan, ki nyi mbimbin mbamɔn na ngem ubaabaa linibol mɔmɔk ni, aan m cha bi li lik nimi.’ 14Ni nan kii ke ni ŋan kina. 15Nima pu na, m nan di binib bi kpa nlan, ki nyi mbimbin mbamɔm, aan ni nan nyan bi nimi aanibol ni ki di bi tii mi na, ki di nimi kpaan bi. Bibaa nan lik nimi binib lichur, biken mu binib nkub, le biken mu binib piiŋmu, biken mu kipiik. M nan ki nyan biyidam bibaa mu ke bi li lik ŋinibol ngbaan mɔmɔk.
16“N‑yoonn ngbaan m nan tuk bi ke, ‘Kinikpakpak yaa fii binib ngbaan aakaasisik ni kan, ni lik ti ponn ni mbamɔm. Ni li toor kina aabɔr ibamɔn ni; ni li toor nimi aanib, ni biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na mɔmɔk aabɔr kina. 17Ni taa li kpa imaagann nimi aabɔjil ni, ni li dii nsanbaan ki toor ugiin ni uwankpadaan mɔmɔk aabɔr. Taa san ubaa ijawaan, Uwumbɔr le ga tii nimi nlan le ni len ibamɔn. Tibɔr ti jer nimi aapɔɔn na kan, ni li joo ni ti m chee, aan m nan toor ti.’ 18N‑yoonn ngbaan m nan tuk nimi naah ga ŋa pu na mɔmɔk.
Binib aah nan buen bi ti pekr Kanaann aatiŋ pu na aabɔr
(Nkahm 13.1-33)
19“Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan bui ke ti ŋa pu na, ti nan ŋa kina. Ti nan fii Sainai Aajool chee, ki di bɔ dii ijawaan aateersakpiin ngbaan ni, le ki di buen Amor yaab aatiŋ ki ye ŋigongon na ni. N‑yoonn mu ti nan ti fuu Kades Banea aatiŋ ni na, 20-21le m bui nimi ke, ‘Ni fuu ni Amor yaab aatiŋ ki ye ŋigongon na ni a, kitiŋ ki Tidindaan Uwumbɔr u ye tiyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na di tii nimi na. Lik man, kima le ti bi na. Waah nan len pu na, li cha ki ti gaa ki man. Ni ŋa mala man, ki taa san ijawaan.’
22“Le ni nan dan m chee ki nan bui ke, ‘Cha ti tun binib bi ti pekr lik kitiŋ ngbaan aah bi pu na, nima kan, bi ga ŋmaa gir ni ki nan mɔk timi taah ga dii pu na, ni ntim mu aaboln bi nima na.’
23“Naah nan kpokl pu na, ni nan ŋan m chee, le m nan nyan bijab kipiik ni bilee ŋinibol mɔmɔk ni. 24Bi nan buen ŋigongon aatiŋ ngbaan ni, ki di kina ti ker Eskol aafataŋ ni, ki lik nima chee. 25Bi nan joo ni nima chee aasubil, le ki tuk timi ke Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban u di kitiŋ ki tii timi na ŋan pam.
26“Le ni yii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb, kaa kii ke ni koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni. 27Ni nan ŋulni tɔb chee ki len ke: ‘Uwumbɔr aa gee timi. U nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni ke u nan di timi ŋa Amor yaab aaŋaal ni aan bi ku timi. 28Ba pu aan ti ga buen nima? Ti san ijawaan la. Bijab bi ti tun bi na tuk timi ke binib bi koo nima na pɔɔ, ki fɔk jer timi, le ki mu ki bi ŋigon ŋi fɔk ti tuu kitaapaak na aatim ni la. Bi nan ki kan ŋiwɔk mu nima.’
29“M nan bui nimi ke, ‘Ni taa li san binib ngbaan ijawaan. 30Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga loln ni pu nsan, ki jan ni pu, ke waah nan ŋa pu Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ni nteersakpiin ni, aan ni kan na. 31Ni kan waah joo ni nimi laafee ni, ki nan saa do chee na, ke ubo aate aah joo u pu na.’ 32Le maah sur nimi ki len pu na, naa ban ke ni kii tii Uwumbɔr. 33Hali, waah lolni ni pu nsan ki ti ban nkakaayaan tii nimi pu na, naa ban ni ŋun tii u. Waah nan ban u mɔk nimi nsan na, kinyeek kan, u nan bi mmii ni ki wiin, le nwiin pu kan, u nan bi ntaalangbam ni ki loln ni pu nsan.
Uwumbɔr aah nan daa bitafal pu na aabɔr
(Nkahm 14.20-45)
34“Uwumbɔr ŋun naah ŋulni pu na, le liŋuul chuu u, le u puu ki bui ke, 35‘Maah puu ke m ga di kitinyaan ki tii niyaajatiib na, nimi titunwanbir aanib bimina ubaa aan koo ki ponn ni, 36Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb baanja le ga koo ki ni. Uma le si chob ki tii mi naadii; m ga di kitiŋ ki u nan buen ti pekr ki chuun mann ki ponn ni na, tii u ni uyaabitiib.’ 37Hali, nimi aabimbin pu, Uwumbɔr gee m pu liŋuul, ki bui mi ke, ‘Sin Moses aan koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni. 38Tɔ, pɔɔk Nunn aajapɔɔn Josua u ye saateter na aataakpab. Uma le ga loln nimi Israel yaab pu nsan, le ni gaa kitiŋ ngbaan.’
39“Le Uwumbɔr ki bui timi, ke timi aabim, bi laa diin, kaa nyi ni ŋan na, ni ni kaa ŋan na, mbim bi ni nan bui ke nimi aadim ga gaa bi ni chee na, bima le ga koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni. M ga di kitiŋ ngbaan tii bi, le bi gaa ki kookoo. 40Nimi ma kan, fenn man, ki di niyil toŋ nteersakpiin ni, ki li dii nsan mu cha Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem na chee.
41“Le ni giin bui ke, ‘Moses, ti tun titunwanbir Uwumbɔr chee. Tɔ, dandana wee ma kan, ti ga fii ki ti tak timi aadim, Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bui ke ti ŋa pu na.’ Le ni mɔmɔk gor ke ni jan kijaak, ki dak ke ni ga li diin tii nimi aan ni gaa ŋigongon aatiŋ ngbaan.
42“Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, ‘Sur binib ngbaan ke bi taa buen ti tak baadim, ba pu? maan ter bi, le baadim ga nyaŋ bi.’ 43M tuk nimi Uwumbɔr aah len pu na, le naa gar mi. Ni yii waamɔb, le nimi aagaak pu, ni buen ti lir ŋigongon aatiŋ aanib ngbaan pu. 44Le Amor yaab bi ka ŋigongon ngbaan ni na fii lir ni pu ke inangbee na. Bi nan jenn nimi ki ti nyan Homa aatiŋ ni, le ki ti nyaŋ nimi, ŋigongon aatiŋ ki bi Edom aatiŋ ni na. 45Kina pu na, ni nan wii yin Uwumbɔr ke u ter nimi, le u yii ke waan gar nimi, ke utafal aa nan bi ni ni. 46Nima pu na, ti nan bi Kades aatiŋ ni ki yunn.

english_text:
1 We spent many years wandering around outside the hill country of Seir, 2until the Lord said:
Moses, 3Israel has wandered in these hills long enough. Turn and go north. 4 And give the people these orders: “Be very careful, because you will soon go through the land that belongs to your relatives, the descendants of Esau. They are afraid of you, 5but don't start a war with them. I have given them the hill country of Seir, so I won't give any of it to you, not even enough to set a foot on. 6And as you go through their land, you will have to buy food and water from them.”
7The Lord has helped us and taken care of us during the past 40 years that we have been in this huge desert. We've had everything we needed, and the Lord has blessed us and made us successful in whatever we have done.
8We went past the territory that belonged to our relatives, the descendants of Esau. We followed Arabah Road that starts in the south at Elath and Ezion-Geber, then we turned onto the desert road that leads to Moab.
9 The Lord told me, “Don't try to start a war with Moab. Leave them alone, because I gave the land of Ar to them, and I will not let you have any of it.”
Tribes That Lived near Canaan
10Before the Lord gave the Moabites their land, a large and powerful tribe lived there. They were the Emim, and they were as tall as the Anakim. 11The Moabites called them Emim, though others sometimes used the name Rephaim for both the Anakim and the Emim.
12The Horites used to live in Seir, but the Edomites took over that region. They killed many of the Horites and forced the rest of them to leave, just as Israel did to the people in the land that the Lord gave them.
Israel Crossed the Zered Gorge
Moses said to Israel:
13When we came to the Zered Gorge along the southern border of Moab, the Lord told us to cross the gorge into Moab, and we did. 14 This was 38 years after we left Kadesh-Barnea, and by that time all the men who had been in the army at Kadesh-Barnea had died, just as the Lord had said they would. 15-16The Lord kept getting rid of them until finally none of them were left.
17Then the Lord told me, 18“Moses, now go past the town of Ar and cross Moab's northern border 19 into Ammon. But don't start a war with the Ammonites. I gave them their land, and I won't give any of it to Israel.”
More Nations That Lived near Canaan
20Before the Ammonites conquered the land that the Lord had given them, some of the Rephaim used to live there, although the Ammonites called them Zamzummim. 21The Zamzummim were a large and powerful tribe and were as tall as the Anakim. But the Lord helped the Ammonites, and they killed many of the Zamzummim and forced the rest to leave. Then the Ammonites settled there. 22The Lord helped them as he had helped the Edomites, who killed many of the Horites in Seir and forced the rest to leave before settling there themselves.
23A group called the Avvim used to live in villages as far south as Gaza, but the Philistines killed them and settled on their land.
Israel Crossed the Arnon Gorge
Moses said:
24After we went through Ammon, the Lord told us:
Israel, pack up your possessions, take down your tents, and cross the Arnon River gorge. The territory of the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon lies on the other side of the river, but I now give you his land. So attack and take it! 25Today I will start making all other nations afraid of you. They will tremble with fear when anyone mentions you, and they will be terrified when you show up.
The Defeat of King Sihon of Heshbon
(Numbers 21.21-30)
Moses said to Israel:
26After we had crossed the Arnon and had set up camp in the Kedemoth Desert, I sent messengers to King Sihon of Heshbon, telling him that his nation and ours could be at peace. I said:
27Please let Israel go across your country. We will walk straight through, without turning off the road. 28-29You can even sell us food and water, and we will pay with silver. We need to reach the Jordan River and cross it, because the Lord our God is giving us the land on the west side. The Edomites and Moabites have already let us cross their land. Please let us cross your land as well.
30-31But Sihon refused to let us go across his country, because the Lord made him stubborn and eager to fight us. The Lord told me, “I am going to help you defeat Sihon and take his land, so attack him!”
32We met Sihon and his army in battle at Jahaz, 33and the Lord our God helped us defeat them. We killed Sihon, his sons, and everyone else in his army. 34Then we captured and destroyed every town in Sihon's kingdom, killing everyone, 35but keeping the livestock and everything else of value. 36The Lord helped us capture every town from the Arnon River gorge north to the boundary of Gilead, including the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge and the town in the middle of the gorge.
37However, we stayed away from all the Ammonite towns, both in the hill country and near the Jabbok River, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Israel yaab aah nan bi nteersakpiin ni na
1“Nee aapuwɔb le ti nan ki fii nima, le ki koo nteersakpiin ni, ki dii nsan mu cha Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem na, Uwumbɔr aah nan bui timi pu na, le ti nan chuun yiini ŋigongon aatiŋ Edom ni, ki yunn pam.
2“Le Uwumbɔr tuk mi 3ke ti chuun yiini ŋigongon aatiŋ ngbaan ni ki yunn, kina pu na, ti li cha kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangan wɔb. 4U nan tuk mi ke m bui nimi tibɔr tee: ‘Ni ban ni dii ŋigongon aatiŋ Edom, ki ye nimi aamaal ponn ni aanib Esɔ aayaabitiib aatiŋ na ni le jer. Bi ga li san nimi ijawaan; 5ni mu taa tak bi, ba pu? maan di baatiŋ nibaa chee tii nimi. M di Edom aapepel tii Esɔ aayaabitiib la. 6Ni ga ŋmaa daa bi chee tijikaar, ni nnyun.’
7“Ni teer man Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu nimi aatuln mɔmɔk ponn ni pu na. Naah nan chuun yiini nteersakpiin ponn ni pu na, le u kii nimi, ki joo nimi mbamɔm. Ŋibin imonko ilee ŋimina ponn ni, uma le joo nimi, le ni kan tiwan nimɔk ni ban na.
8“Nima na, ti nan fii nima chee, kaa nan dii nsan mu nya Elaf ni Esionn Geber aatim ni ki cha N‑yaan Aanyusakpem chee na. Ti nan fenn toŋ ŋŋangan ni liwipuul aakaasisik ni, Moab aapepel wɔb. 9Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, ‘Taa muk Moab yaab, ki taa tak bi, Lot aayaabitiib le bi na. M di Ar aatiŋ le tii bi, le maan di baatiŋ nibaa chee tii nimi.’”
10Ŋiwɔk aanibol li bi yin li ke Em yaab na le nan koo Ar aatiŋ ni. Bi nan fɔk ke Anak yaab bi mu nan ye ŋiwɔk na la. 11Bi nan yin bi ni Anak yaab mu ke Refa yaab la, le Moab yaab ma nan yin bi ke Em yaab. 12Hor yaab le nan koo Edom aapepel ni, le Esɔ aayaabitiib jenn nyan bi, ki kuln baatimbol, ki kal nima chee bibaa, ke Israel yaab aah jenn nyan baadim kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr di tii bi na ni pu na.
13“Le ti puur Sered Aamɔɔl, Uwumbɔr aah nan bui timi ke ti ŋa pu na. 14Taah nan nyan ni Kades Banea buyoonn na aabin piitaa ni ŋiniin le na. Uwumbɔr aah nan bui ke bijab bi waan cha bi koo tipuur aatiŋ ni na nan kpo doo a. 15Uwumbɔr le nan gann nyan bi, le ki bii bi mɔmɔk, ŋibin piitaa ni ŋiniin ngbaan ponn ni.
16“Bi mɔmɔk aah kpo doo na, 17le Uwumbɔr nan bui timi ke, 18‘Din wee, ni bɔ dii Ar aatiŋ ki bi Moab yaab aapepel ni na. 19Naan li daa Lot aayaabitiib, Amonn yaab aatiŋ. Ni taa muk bi, ki taa tak bi, ba pu? maah di kitiŋ ki tii bi na, maan ki di ki nibaa chee tii ni mu.’”
20Bi ki yin lipepel ngbaan ke Refa yaab aatiŋ, ba pu? binib bi nan bi nima chee na, bi nan yin bi kina la, le Amonn yaab ma yin bi ke Samsum yaab. 21Bi nan fɔk ke Anak yaab na la. Bi nan ye linibol li wiir na la, le ki kpa mpɔɔn sakpen. Le Uwumbɔr nan tee kuln bi, ki di baatiŋ tii Amonn yaab, le bi kal nima chee. 22Kina le Uwumbɔr nan ŋa tii Esɔ aayaabitiib, Edom yaab, bi koo ŋigongon aatiŋ Edom aapepel ni na. U nan kuln Hor yaab, le ki cha Edom yaab gaa baatiŋ ki kal nima chee ki nan saa din. 23Krete aadikl aanib le nan ka kpak Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem aagbaan. Bima le nan kuln Afim yaab. Binib ngbaan le nan pue ka nima chee, le bi kuln bi, ki gaa baatiŋ ki dii ŋŋangii wɔb ki ti nyan Gasa aatiŋ ni.
24“Taah dii Moab aapepel ki jer doo na, le Uwumbɔr bui timi ke, ‘Dandana wee, fenn ki puur Anonn Aamɔɔl man. M ga di Amor yaab aabɔr Sihonn u koo Hesbonn aatiŋ ni na, ni waatiŋ, ŋa niŋaal ni. Tak u man, ki piin ki gaa waatiŋ man. 25Din wee ki joo cha, m ga cha ŋipepel mɔmɔk aanib san nimi ijawaan. Unii umɔk ŋun nimi aayimbil bɔr na kan, ijawaan ga chuu u, le uwon gbaa.’
Israel yaab aah nan nyaŋ ubɔr Sihonn pu na
(Nkahm 21.21-30)
26“Kedemof aateersakpiin ni, le m nan tun ituun Hesbonn aabɔr u bi yin u ke Sihonn na chee, ki di nsuudoon aabɔr tee bui u ke, 27‘Cha ti dii saatiŋ ni ki jer. Ti gaa li dii nsanja le chob, taan paar ki dii nibaa. 28Ti ga pa tijikaar ti ga ji na pu, ni nnyun mu ti ga nyu na pu. Ti ban le ke ti dii saatiŋ ni jer, 29aan ki ti puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, ki koo Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban u di kitiŋ ki tii timi na ni. Esɔ aayaabitiib bi koo Edom aatiŋ ni na, ni Moab yaab bi koo Ar aatiŋ ni na, kii tii timi, le ti dii baapepel ni ki jer.’
30“Le ubɔr Sihonn nan yii, ke ti taa dii waatiŋ ni jer. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan cha usui pɔɔk, le u yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, le Uwumbɔr cha ti nyaŋ u, ki gaa baatiŋ ki ti laa koo ki ponn ni na.
31“Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, ‘Lik, m di ubɔr Sihonn ni waatiŋ ŋa niŋaal ni, le baa ki kpa mpɔɔn, nima pu na, nyaŋ bi, ki gaa kitiŋ ngbaan.’ 32Ubɔr Sihonn ni waajab mɔmɔk nan nyan ni, le ki to timi butɔb, Jahas aatiŋ chee, 33le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan di bi ŋa tiŋaal ni, le ti nyaŋ bi, ki ku ubɔr ngbaan, ni ujapɔtiib, ni waajab mɔmɔk. 34N‑yoonn ngbaan, ti nan ki nyaŋ ki kuln waatim, ni binib bi mɔmɔk nan bi mu ni na, bijab, ni bipiib, ni mbim. Taa nan cha unii ubaa kina ŋmar. 35Ti nan chur baawakor, ki yoor tiwan mɔmɔk baatim ni. 36Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le nan cha ti gaa ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk, ki nyan Aroer aatiŋ ni, ki di dii Anonn aafataŋ aagbaan, ni kitisakpeŋ ki mu bi kifataŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni na, ki di ti ker Gilead aatiŋ. Ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk aagon aa nan pɔɔ nyaŋ timi. 37Tɔ, taa nan buen Amonn yaab aapepel ni, ki mu aa buen Jabok Aamɔɔl aagbaan. Taa nan buen ŋigongon aatim aapepel ni, kaa buen nin chee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan bui ke ti taa buen na.

english_text:
The Defeat of King Og of Bashan
(Numbers 21.31-35)
Moses said to Israel:
1When we turned onto the road that leads to Bashan, King Og of Bashan led out his whole army to fight us at Edrei. 2But the Lord told me, “Moses, don't be afraid of King Og. I am going to help you defeat him and his army and take over his land. Destroy him and his people, just as you did with the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon.”
3-6The Lord our God helped us destroy Og and his army and conquer his entire kingdom of Bashan, including the Argob region. His kingdom had lots of villages and 60 towns with high walls and gates that locked with bars. We completely destroyed them all, killing everyone, 7but keeping the livestock and everything else of value.
8Sihon and Og had ruled Amorite kingdoms east of the Jordan River. Their land stretched from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, and we captured it all. 9Mount Hermon is called Mount Sirion by the people of Sidon, and it is called Mount Senir by the Amorites. 10We captured all the towns in the highlands, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, two of the towns that Og had ruled.
Og's Coffin
11King Og was the last of the Rephaim, and his coffin is in the town of Rabbah in Ammon. It is made of hard black rock and is four meters long and almost two meters wide.
The Land East of the Jordan River Is Divided
(Numbers 32.1-42)
Moses said to Israel:
12-17I gave some of the land and towns we captured to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. Their share started at the Arnon River gorge in the south, took in the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge, and went far enough north to include the southern half of the Gilead region. The northern part of their land went as far east as the upper Jabbok River gorge, which formed their border with the Ammonites. I also gave them the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, from Lake Galilee south to the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
I gave the northern half of Gilead and all of the Bashan region to half the tribe of Manasseh. Bashan had belonged to King Og, and the Argob region in Bashan used to be called the Land of the Rephaim. Jair from the Manasseh tribe conquered the Argob region as far west as the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. The Israelites even started calling Bashan by the name “Villages of Jair,” and that is still its name. I gave the northern half of Gilead to the Machir clan.
18-19 At that time I told the men of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
The Lord our God told me to give you this land with its towns, and that's what I have done. Now your wives and children can stay here with your large flocks of sheep and goats and your large herds of cattle. But all of you men that can serve in our army must cross the Jordan River and help the other tribes, because they are your relatives. 20The Lord will let them defeat the enemy nations on the west side of the Jordan and take their land. Afterwards, you can come back here to the land I gave you.
21-22Then I told Joshua, “You saw how the Lord our God helped us destroy King Sihon and King Og. So don't be afraid! Wherever you go, the Lord will fight on your side and help you destroy your enemies.”
God Refused To Let Moses Enter Canaan
Moses said to Israel:
23 At that time I prayed and begged, 24“Our Lord, it seems that you have just begun to show me your great power. No other god in the sky or on earth is able to do the mighty things that you do. 25The land west of the Jordan is such good land. Please let me cross the Jordan and see the hills and the Lebanon Mountains.”
26But the Lord was angry with me because of you people, and he refused to listen. “That's enough!” he said. “I don't want to hear any more. 27Climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look north, south, east, and west. Take a good look, but you are not going to cross the Jordan River. 28Joshua will lead Israel across the Jordan to take the land, so help him be strong and brave and tell him what he must do.”
29After this we stayed in the valley at Beth-Peor.
translation_text:
Israel yaab aah nan nyaŋ ubɔr Og pu na
(Nkahm 21.31-35)
1“Ni paa na, ti nan di buen ŋŋangan wɔb, Basann aapepel ni, le ubɔr Og ni waajab mɔmɔk nyan ni ke bi nan faa timi butɔb, Edrei aatiŋ chee. 2Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, ‘Ni taa li san u ijawaan. M ban m di u ni waajab, ni waapepel mɔmɔk, tii nimi la. Ni ŋa u ke naah ŋa Amor yaab aabɔr Sihonn u nan koo Hesbonn aatiŋ ni na pu na.’
3“Nima pu na, Uwumbɔr nan di ubɔr Og ni waanib ŋa tiŋaal ni, le ti ku bi mɔmɔk. 4N‑yoonn ngbaan, ti nan ki nyaŋ waatim mɔmɔk. Taa nan cha kitiŋ kibaa kina gur. Ntim mu ti nan nyaŋ, Agob aapepel li Basann aabɔr Og nan joo na, nan ti saa ntim imonko itaa la. 5Ntim mue mɔmɔk nan kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk na, le ki kpa jaaleŋ tiib bi joo laŋ ni ibisamɔi na. Itingbaan pam mu nan bi, kaa kpa ŋigon mann gob ŋi. 6Ti nan bii ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk, ki ku binib bimɔk nan bi mu ni na; ti nan ku bijab, ni bipiib, ni mbim, ke taah nan ŋa Hesbonn aabɔr Sihonn ni waanib pu na. 7Ti nan chur baawakor, ki yoor tiwan mɔmɔk, ntim ngbaan ni.
8“N‑yoonn ngbaan, ti nan gaa Amor yaab aabɔrb bilee ngbaan aatiŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul wɔb, ki yoor Anonn Aamɔɔl chee ki ti ker Hemonn Aajool mɔk na. 9Tɔ, Saidonn yaab yin Hemonn Aajool ngbaan ke Sirionn, le Amor yaab mu yin li ke Senir. 10Ti nan gaa Basann aatiŋ aabɔr Og aapepel mɔmɔk doo; ntim mu nan bi ŋigongon ŋi bi taar na pu, ki kpee Gilead ni Basann aapepel, li di ti nyan Saleka ni Edrei aatim mu bi liwipuul wɔb na.”
11Ubɔr Og le nan gur ye ŋiniwɔk Refa yaab aakookoo aanii, nima chee. Bi nan di ŋitakpal le ŋa waanikpol aadakaa, waawawaan nan ye ŋitaa ŋiloob la, le waafɔfɔk mu ga nan li pii ŋitaa kipiik ni ŋinaa, le ni dii baah nan ŋaŋni tiwan mɔmɔk pu na. Dakaa ngbaan beenin bi Amonn yaab aatiŋ Raba ni, ki nan saa din.
Ŋinibol ŋi nan kal Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl liwipuul wɔb na aabɔr
(Nkahm 32.1-42)
12“Taah nan gaa kitiŋ ngbaan na, m nan di lipepel li bi Aroer aatiŋ ŋŋangan wɔb ki bi gbɔk Anonn Aamɔɔl chee, ni ŋigongon aatiŋ Gilead aapepel nibaa wɔb, ni kaatim, le di tii Rubenn ni Gad aanibol. 13M nan di Gilead aapepel li gur na, ni Basann aatiŋ ki ubɔr Og nan joo aan ki ye Agob aapepel mɔmɔk na, tii Manase aanibol ligeln libaa.”
Tɔ, bi nan yin Basann aatiŋ ke Refa yaab aatiŋ. 14Le Jair, u nan ye Manase aanibol ni aanii na, nan gaa Agob aapepel mɔmɔk. Bi ki yin nima ke Basann, le waanaanmɔk nan di ti ker Gesur ni Maaka aatim mɔk. U nan di waayimbil le yin ntimbim ngbaan, le bi beenin yin mu ke Jair aatim ki nan saa din.
15“M nan di Gilead aatiŋ le tii Makir aataŋaal yaab bi nyan ni Manase aanibol ni na; 16ki yoor Gilead mɔk ki ti ker Anonn Aamɔɔl na, m nan di nima tii Rubenn ni Gad aanibol la. Limɔɔl ngbaan aakaasisik ni le nan ye baatiŋ ngbaan aaŋangii wɔb aanaanmɔk, le ŋŋangan wɔb aanaanmɔk nan ye Jabok Aamɔɔl mɔk, lipepel ngbaan libaa mu nan ye Amonn yaab aanaanmɔk. 17Liwilir wɔb mu, baanaanmɔk nan di kina ti ker Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl mɔk la, ki yoor Galilee Aanyusakpem ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa N‑yaan Aanyusakpem mɔk ŋŋangii wɔb, ki di ti ker Pisga Aajool taab, liwipuul wɔb.
18“N‑yoonn ngbaan, maah nan ki di tibɔr ti tuk bi na sɔ: ‘Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le di Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul aatiŋ kee tii nimi. Dandana wee, cha nimi aajab gor bibaa ki puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, ki loln Israel aanibol ŋi gur na nsan, aan ki ti ter bi mu bi gaa baatiŋ. 19M nyi ke ni kpa tiwakor pam, kina pu na, nipuutiib, ni nimi aabim, ni tiwakor ma ga gaar kitiŋ ki m di tii nimi na pu. 20Ni buen ti ter niŋeen aatɔtiib Israel yaab biken, aan bi mu gaa kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr ga di tii bi, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aadapuul, liwilir wɔb na, ki ti saa buyoonn Uwumbɔr ga tii bi nsuudoon ke waah tii nimi do pu na. Nee aapuwɔb, ni ga ŋmaa gir kun ni kitiŋ ki m di tii nimi na ni.’
21“Le m tuk Josua ke: ‘Aa kan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan ŋa bibɔrb bilee na, Sihonn ni Og pu na, kina le u ga ŋa bibɔrb bimɔk ni ga gaa baatim na. 22Ni taa li san bi ijawaan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga jan tii nimi.’
Moses aah kaa nan ŋmaa koo Kanaann aatiŋ ni pu na
23“N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan mee Uwumbɔr linimaln mbamɔm ke, 24‘Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, m nyi ke aa piin ki mɔk mi saah ga ŋa tiwan sakpenn, ni iwaan aawan ni aa ban ke aa ŋa na. Liwaal libaa aa bi paacham, bee kitiŋ pu, ki ga ŋmaa ŋa tiwan sakpenn nimɔk aa ŋa na. 25Uwumbɔr, cha m puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, aan ki kan kitiŋ ki nyuun na, ki bi nima wɔb, ki ye ŋigongon aatinyanyaan ngbaan na, ni Lebanonn Aajoo.’
26“Le nimi binib bee pu, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii m pu, le waa kii tii mi. Le u giin bui mi ke, ‘Ni ŋeer a. Taa ki kpiir kina lelee. 27Li cha Pisga Aajool aapaacham, ki ti lik ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa ŋŋangii wɔb, ki ki lik liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa liwilir wɔb. Saah waa tiwan nimɔk na, aa lik ni mbamɔm, ba pu? saa kpa nsan ke aa puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl. 28Tuk Josua waah ga ŋa pu na. Pɔɔk utaakpab ki sur u, ba pu? uma le ga loln binib ngbaan pu nsan, aan bi puur ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki aa lik waa ki na.’
29“Nima pu na, ti nan gaar kifataŋ ki dɔ tok Bef Peor aatiŋ na ni.”

english_text:
Israel Must Obey God
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to these laws and teachings! If you obey them, you will live, and you will go in and take the land that the Lord is giving you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, 2 and now he is your God. I am telling you everything he has commanded, so don't add anything or take anything away.
3 You saw how he killed everyone who worshiped the god Baal Peor. 4But all of you that were faithful to the Lord your God are still alive today.
5-8 No other nation has laws that are as fair as the ones the Lord my God told me to give you. If you faithfully obey them when you enter the land, you will show other nations how wise you are. In fact, everyone that hears about your laws will say, “That great nation certainly is wise!” And what makes us greater than other nations? We have a God who is close to us and answers our prayers.
9You must be very careful not to forget the things you have seen God do for you. Keep reminding yourselves, and tell your children and grandchildren as well. 10Do you remember the day you stood in the Lord's presence at Mount Sinai? The Lord said, “Moses, bring the people of Israel here. I want to speak to them so they will obey me as long as they live, and so they will teach their children to obey me too.”
11 Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain, 12and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him. 13 The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
14 That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River.
Don't Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
15When God spoke to you from the fire, he was invisible. So be careful 16 not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women, 17 animals, birds, 18reptiles, or fish. 19And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship. 20 But you are the Lord's people, because he rescued you from Egypt, that fiery furnace.
21 The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you. 22So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
23Always remember the agreement that the Lord your God made with you, and don't make an idol in any shape or form. 24 The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
25-26Soon you will cross the Jordan River and settle down in the land. Then in the years to come, you will have children, and they will give you grandchildren. After many years, you might lose your sense of right and wrong and make idols, even though the Lord your God hates them. So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out. 27 Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations. 28There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
29-30 In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God. 31The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
32-34When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
35-36 The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
37The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt. 38Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
39So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below. 40Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you.
Safe Towns
41-43 Moses said, “People of Israel, you must set aside the following three towns east of the Jordan River as Safe Towns: Bezer in the desert highlands belonging to the Reuben tribe; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to the Gad tribe; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the Manasseh tribe. If you kill a neighbor without meaning to, and if you had not been angry with that person, you can run to one of these towns and find safety.”
The Second Speech: Moses Tells What the Lord Demands
Israel at Beth-Peor
44-46The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him 47and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River 48from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon. 49Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
translation_text:
Moses aah nan sur Israel yaab ke bi li kpa limɔkiir pu na aabɔr
1Moses nan bui Israel yaab ke, “Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii tii ikaal i m bi mɔk nimi na, nima le ga cha ni li bi, ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na, ban u di tii nimi na. 2Ni taa di nibaa kpee ikaal ngbaan ni, ki taa nyan nibaa i ni. Ni kii tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal i m joo tuk nimi na mbamɔm. 3Ninimbigbaŋ kan Uwumbɔr aah nan ŋa pu Peor Aajool chee na. U nan kuln unii umɔk nan dooni liwaal Baal na; 4le nimi bi nan dii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr na ma laa beenin bi limɔfal ni, ki nan saa din.
5“M di ikaal ngbaan mɔmɔk mɔk nimi, ke Ndindaan Uwumbɔr aah bui mi ke m ŋa pu na. Ni yaa ti gaa kitiŋ ngbaan ki koo nima kan, ni li joo ikaal ngbaan mbamɔm. 6Ni li joo i mbamɔm, le ŋinibol ŋiken ga kan naah kpa nlan pu na. Le bi yaa ŋun ikaal ngbaan aabɔr kan, bi ga bui ke, ‘Ba aalanboln, ni nnyim, linibokpaan limina kpa kina.’
7“Linibokpaan liken aa bi ki kpa laawaa li bi bi chee baamukl ni ke Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi ti chee pu na. Ti yaa bi limukl ni ki yin u kan, see u ter timi. 8Linibokpaan liken aa bi ki kpa ikaal i ŋan ke maah di i mɔk nimi din wee na. 9Ni li kii nibaa man. Ni yaa bi limɔfal ni ki ti saa buyoonn na kan, ni taa suln ninimbigbaŋ aah kan tiwan ni Uwumbɔr ŋa na. Ni tuk nimi aabim, ni niyaabitiib, 10tiwan ni nan ŋa, bundaln ni nan sil Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Sainai Aajool taab na. N‑yoonn ngbaan, u nan bui mi ke, ‘Kuun ni maanib ngbaan. M ban bi ŋun maah ga len pu na la, nima kan, bi ga li nyi baah ga kii maamɔb pu, ki ti saa baamɔfal aadoon na. Nima kan, bi ga mɔk baabim, aan bi mu li san mi ijawaan.’
11“Tuk nimi aabim naah nan sil lijool ngbaan aataab aan iŋmanyuu i bɔn sakpen na biin li pu, le mmii gaal ki fii ti pii kitaapaak pu na. 12Ni ki tuk bi Uwumbɔr aah nan len tibɔr mmii ngbaan ponn ni pu na; ni ŋun waah len pu na, ki mu aa waa waah bi pu na. 13U nan tuk nimi naah ga ŋa pu aan ki li joo waah nan puu tipuur ti tii nimi na pu na; ke ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii tii ikaal kipiik i u nan ŋmee paan ŋitakpal ŋilee pu na. 14Uwumbɔr nan tuk mi ke m di ikaal ngbaan mɔmɔk mɔk nimi, aan ni li joo i mbamɔm, kitiŋ ki ni ban ni ti gaa ki koo ki ponn ni na.
Moses nan sur binib ngbaan ŋiwaa aabɔr pu
15“N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan len ni chee tibɔr, mmii ni, Sainai Aajool pu na, naa nan waa u. Ni yaa ban ke ni li ŋan tii nimi kan, ni chuu nibaa 16ki taa tun titunwanbir ke ni di tiwan nibaa ŋa liwaal tii nibaa, aan ni li naahn upii, bee uja, 17bee ki di naŋ tiwakor, bee unyoon, 18bee tiwanbaarkaan, bee ujan. 19Ni taa cha nibaa tɔŋ nimi aan ni li dooni tiwan ni ni waa kitaapaak, ni ye nwiin, ni uŋmal, ni iŋmabi na. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le di tiwan nimina mɔmɔk tii binib bi mɔmɔk bi dulnyaa wee ni na. 20Nimi ma kan, uma le nyan nimi Ijipt yaab aamuk ni. U nyan ni nimi ke u di nimi ŋa waanib, ke naah ye waanib din wee pu na. 21Nimi pu le Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii m pu, le u puu ke waan cha m puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki koo kitinyanyaan ki u ban u di tii nimi na ni. 22Mma kan, m ga kpo kitiŋ kee ni, kaan puur limɔɔl ngbaan daalbaadaal. Le ni ma ban ni puur ki ti gaa kitinyanyaan ngbaan. 23Ni pɔɔn nibaa, ki taa suln tipuur ti Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan puu tii nimi na. Ni kii waamɔb, ki taa naan liwaal libaa tii nibaa. 24Ba pu? Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi ke mmiigaal na la, le kaa ban ke unibɔn ki dii tiwan nibaa ki kpee u pu.
25“Hali ni yaa bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu na, ki ma mbim ni yaabitiib kan, ni taa tun titunwanbir ki naan liwaal, ki di naŋ tiwan nibaa. Kina aatun aa ŋan Uwumbɔr chee, le ki ga cha u gee liŋuul ni pu. 26Ni yaa yii maah tuk nimi pu na kan, paacham ni kitiŋ le ye maaseeraadam din wee, ni ga kpo doo kitiŋ ngbaan pu. Le kina aan cha ni li bi ki yunn, naah ban ni puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki na ni. U ga kuln nimi doo. 27Uwumbɔr ga cha ni yaa buen ŋinibol yayan aatim ni, le nimi siib kina le ga ti gur ki ŋmar. 28Nima chee le ni ga ti li dooni unibɔn aah di uŋaal ŋa idɔ ni ŋitakpal aawaa ŋi na. Ŋiwaa ngbaan aa waa, kaa ŋun, kaa ŋmaa ji, kaa ŋun nnun. 29Nima chee le ni ga lik ki ban Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, le ni yaa di nisui mɔmɔk ban u kan, ni ga kan u. 30N‑yoonn mu ni ti kan limukl, aan tiwanbir ngbaan mɔmɔk pii nimi na, le ni ga fenn ban Uwumbɔr ki kii tii u. 31Uma le ye Uwumbɔr u kpa linimbaasaln na. Waan di nimi lii, ki mu aan kuln nimi doo, waan suln tipuur ti u nan puu tii niyaajatiib na.
32“Ni baa n‑yoonn mu jer na aabɔr, n‑yoonn mu jer aan bi nin ma nimi na, buyoonn Uwumbɔr nan naan unibɔn dulnyaa wee ni na ki ti saa dandana na aabɔr. Ni baa dulnyaa aapepel mɔmɔk ni. Tiwansakpenn kina aaboln kee ŋa aa? Unii ubaa kee ŋun tiwan kina aaboln pu uu? 33Binib bibaa kee ŋun Uwumbɔr len tibɔr mmiigaal ni kina, ki beenin fu uu? 34Liwaal libaa kee buen litimbol yayan ni, ki ti nyan ni binib, ki di bi ŋa laanib, ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa nimi pu Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na aa? Ninimbil ni, le u nan di waapɔɔn sakpiin tun, ki joo ni iween, ni butɔb, ki ŋa iwaan, ni lijinjiir aatun, ki cha ijawaan aawan ŋa. 35Uwumbɔr ubaa le mɔk nimi kina, ke u kpiir mɔk nimi ke uma Uwumbɔr baan baanja le bi, ubaa aa ki bi ki kpee u pu. 36U nan cha ni ŋun waaneel pu paacham, ke u mɔk nimi tiwan, ki cha ni kan waamii mu bi chain na dulnyaa wee ni, le u len ni chee tibɔr, mmii ngbaan ponn ni. 37Waah gee niyaajatiib pu na, le u lee nimi, ki di waapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 38Naah tur koo binib ngbaan ponn ni na, le u nyaŋni ŋinibol ŋi kpa mpɔɔn jer nimi na, ke u di baatim tii nimi, le kitiŋ ngbaan laa beenin ye nimi yaan ki nan saa din wee. 39Nima pu na, teer din wee man, ki taa suln kpala ke Uwumbɔr le ye Uwumbɔr u joo paacham ni kitiŋ kee na. Uwumbɔr uken aa ki bi. 40Ni li joo waakaal imɔk m di tuk nimi din wee na, le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li bi mbamɔm tii nimi, ni niyaabitiib. Nima kan, ni ga li bi kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga di tii nimi na pu, ki li ye nimi yaan ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
Mbɔbɔryaan aatim mu bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb na aabɔr
41Moses nan nyan ntim mutaa Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl aawipuul wɔb siin, 42ke unii yaa peln ku uken kaa nyi kan, u san buen nima chee ki ŋmar. U yaa san buen ntim ngbaan kibaa ponn ni kan, baan ki ku u. 43Moses nan nyan Beser aatiŋ ki bi nteersakpiin aajool li bi taar na pu le siin Rubenn aamaal yaab; le ki nyan Ramof aatiŋ ki bi Gilead aapepel ni na siin Gad aamaal yaab; ki nyan Golann aatiŋ ki bi Basann aapepel ni na siin Manase aamaal yaab.
Moses aah nan piin ki mɔk bi Uwumbɔr Aakaal pu na
44Moses nan di Uwumbɔr aakaal, ni waamɔkm, tuk Israel aanib ngbaan. 45-46Baah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki nan fuu Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, liwipuul wɔb, kifataŋ ki dɔ tok Bef Peor aatiŋ na aapuwɔb, le u nan di ikaal ngbaan mɔk bi. Ni nan ye Amor yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Sihonn na aapepel ni la, uma le nan bi Hesbonn aatiŋ ni ki joo waanib. Moses ni Israel yaab aah nan nyan ni Ijipt buyoonn na, le bi nan nyaŋ u. 47Bi nan gaa waatiŋ ngbaan, ki kpee ubɔr Og u nan joo Basann aatiŋ na, u mu nan ye Amor yaab aabɔr, le ki bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb. 48Kitiŋ ngbaan nan yoor kina le ki ti ker Aroer aatiŋ ki bi Anonn Aamɔɔl aagbaan na, le ki yoor kina ti saa Sirionn Aajool chee, ŋŋangan wɔb, bi nan ki yin lijool ngbaan ke Hemonn la. 49Kitiŋ ngbaan nan ki bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl liwipuul wɔb aapepel ni la, le ki yoor kina ti ker N‑yaan Aanyusakpem aaŋangii wɔb, ki dii kina ti saa Pisga Aajool aataab, liwipuul wɔb.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Exodus 20.1-17)
1Moses called together the people of Israel and said:
Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully. 2The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai. 3That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today. 4The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire, 5but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
6I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
7Do not worship any god except me.
8 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 9 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 10But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
11 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
12 Show respect for the Sabbath Day—it belongs to me. 13 You have six days when you can do your work, 14but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work. 15This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
16 Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
17 Do not murder.
18 Be faithful in marriage.
19 Do not steal.
20 Do not tell lies about others.
21 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
22 When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me.
The People Were Afraid
(Exodus 20.18-21)
Moses said to Israel:
23When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me 24and said:
Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them. 25But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die. 26Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it? 27Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
28The Lord heard you and said:
Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve. 29I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
30Now, tell them to return to their tents, 31but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them.
Moses said:
32Israel, you must carefully obey the Lord's commands. 33Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr Aakaal kipiik na aabɔr
(Nnyam 20.1-17)
1Moses nan yin ni Israel aanib ngbaan, le bi kuun ni tɔb chee, le u bui bi ke, “Israel yaab, li pel man ikaal imɔk m ban m di tuk nimi din wee na. Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki bae i, ki li joo i mbamɔm, ki taa yii i. 2Sainai Aajool pu le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii titetiib, 3ni mu aa nan ye titetiib baanja le u nan puu tii, tipuur ngbaan ye timi bi laa beenin bi din wee na mu yaan la. 4Lijool ngbaan pu, Uwumbɔr nan len ni chee tibɔr, mmii ponn ni. 5N‑yoonn ngbaan, min le nan sil nimi ni Uwumbɔr aakaasisik ni, le ki tuk nimi waah len pu na, ba pu? ni nan san mmii ngbaan ijawaan, le kaa kaa ke ni buen lijool ngbaan paab.
“Le Uwumbɔr nan bui ke, 6‘Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, nin chee ni nan ye binaagbiib na.
7“‘Ni taa doon liwaal libaa ki kpee min Uwumbɔr pu.
8“‘Ni taa naan tiwan nibaa ki di naŋ paacham aawan nibaa, bee kitiŋ aawan nibaa, bee nnyun ni aawan nibaa, ke ni doon ni. 9Ni taa gbaan kitiŋ ke ni doon liwaal libaa, ba pu? min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, le maa ban ke m ni ubaa li kpaan yeh nimi. M ga daa binib bi nan mi na, ni baabim, ni biyaabitiib, ni bi mu aayaabitiib aatafal. 10M ga li gee binib churbakaa bi mu gee mi, ki kii tii maakaal na.
11“‘Ni taa yin maayimbil fam fam; min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga daa unii u yin maayimbil fam fam na aatafal.
12“‘Ni li nyuŋni Likpaakool daal aawiin, ke mu ye maawiin daal la, ke min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk nimi pu na. 13Ni kpa iwiin iloob le ni di tun nimi aatun, 14le winlole daal ye lifuur daal ke ni li joo dooni mi. Nwiin ngbaan daal kan, nimi, ni nimi aabim, ni nimi aanaagbiib, ni nimi aawakor, ni biwɔwɔm bi bi nimi aatiŋ ni na ubaa taa tun lituln. Cha nimi aanaagbiib fuur ke naah fuur pu na. 15Teer man ke ni mu nan ye binaagbiib le Ijipt aatiŋ ni, le min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di maapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan ni nimi. Nima pu le m bui nimi ke ni li joo Likpaakool daal mbamɔm.
16“‘Aa li pak aate ni aana, ke min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bui si pu na, nima kan, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii si, aan aa li bi ki yunn, kitiŋ ki m ga di tii si na ni.
17“‘Aa taa ku unii.
18“‘Aa taa gɔr kidagook.
19“‘Aa taa su kinaayuk.
20“‘Aa taa mɔn nnyamɔn paan unii ubaa.
21“‘Aa taa cha aanimbil li man aaŋeen aatɔ aadichal, bee upuu, bee waakpaakon, bee waanaagbiib, bee waawakor, bee waah kpa tiwan nimɔk na pu.’
22“Ikaal imina le Uwumbɔr nan di tii ni mɔmɔk, buyoonn ni nan kuun dan lijool ngbaan chee na. Waah nan len ni chee tibɔr nneel sakpiin, mmii ponn ni, ni ntaalangbam bɔmbɔm ponn ni na, le u nan di ikaal imina tii nimi. Waa ki di ibaa kpee i pu. U nan ŋmee i ŋitakpapepee ŋilee pu, le ki di i tii mi.
Baah san Uwumbɔr ijawaan pu pu na
(Nnyam 20.18-21)
23“N‑yoonn mu lijool ngbaan pu nan ye mmii ŋmeen, aan ni ŋun nneel pu mbɔmbɔɔn ponn ni na, le nimi aaninkpiib, ni nimi aanibol aayidam nan dan m chee, 24ki nan bui ke, ‘Tidindaan Uwumbɔr mɔk timi waapɔɔn sakpiin, ni waanyuŋ, buyoonn ti ŋun u len mmii ni na. Din wee, ti kan ke Uwumbɔr yaa len unii chee tibɔr kan, udaan ngbaan ga ŋmaa li beenin fu. 25Tɔ, taa ban ti li gbiir nkun. Mmii mue ga ku timi. Ti yaa ki ŋun Uwumbɔr len ti chee tibɔr lelee kan, ti ga sil kpo. 26Unibɔn ubaa kee ŋun Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na bi mmii ni ki len u chee tibɔr, aan udaan ki bi, ki kpa limɔfal aa? 27Moses, gir buen aan ki ti pel Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ga len tibɔr timɔk na, ki ki gir ni ki nan tuk timi waah len pu na. Ti ga pel ti, ki gaa ti mɔmɔk.’
28“N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ŋun kina na, le u bui mi ke, ‘M ŋun binib ngbaan aah len pu na; bi kpa mbamɔn. 29Bima yaa kpa nlandak ngbaan aaboln kina n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, ki yaa ga pak mi ki kii tii maakaal mɔmɔk kan, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii bi, ni biyaabitiib, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. 30Gir buen ti tuk bi ke bi gir kun bido ŋinampal. 31Sin Moses ma kan, gaar m chee do, aan m di maakaal, ni maamɔkm mɔmɔk tuk si. Aa di ikaal ngbaan mɔk binib ngbaan, nima kan, bi ga joo i mbamɔm, ki li bi kitiŋ ki m ban ke m di tii bi na ni.’
32“Nimi Israel yaab, ni pɔɔn nibaa man, aan ki li ŋani tiwan nimɔk Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bui ke ni ŋa na. Ni taa yii waakaal mubaa man. 33Ni li joo i mɔmɔk mbamɔm, aan nima kan, naah ban ni gaa kitiŋ ki aan ki li koo ki ponn ni na, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi, le ni ga yunn ki ponn ni.

english_text:
The Most Important Commandment
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land. 2And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws. 3Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
4 Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God! 5 So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength. 6 Memorize his laws 7and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 8Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them. 9Write these laws on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
Worship Only the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10 The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build, 11and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more, 12don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt. 13 Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
14Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you. 15If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you, 16 so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah. 17Always obey the laws that the Lord has given you 18-19and live in a way that pleases him. Then you will be able to go in and take this good land from your enemies, just as he promised your ancestors.
20Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
21Then you will answer:
We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free. 22We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else. 23The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors. 24-25That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
translation_text:
Nkaal kpaan
1“Ikaal imina le Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan bui mi, ke m di i mɔk nimi. Naah chaa koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni, ke ni ti li bi nima na, ni ti li joo i mbamɔm. 2Nimi ni niyaabitiib aah ga li bi limɔfal ni ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu na, ni li pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ki li joo waakaal i m di mɔk nimi na mbamɔm, aan ki yunn kitiŋ ngbaan ni. 3Nimi Israel yaab, li pel maah ban m di i mɔk nimi pu na, ki li joo i mbamɔm. Le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi, le ni ga ŋa litimbokpaan, ki li koo kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na ni, ke Uwumbɔr u ye tiyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na aah nan puu pu na.
4“Israel yaab, teer man tibɔr tee. Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le ye timi Aawumbɔr. Ubaa aa ki bi. 5Ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nimi aasui mɔmɔk ni, ni nimi aawiin mɔmɔk, ni nimi aapɔɔn mɔmɔk. 6Ni taa suln ikaal i m joo tuk nimi din wee na bɔr. 7Ni di i mɔk nimi aabim. Ni yaa ka linampal, bee ni yaa nyan buen nsan, bee ni yaa ka fuur, bee ni yaa bi tun lituln kan, ni li len yaabɔr. 8Ni di i gbin niŋaal pu, ki ŋmee i paan niyigbeer pu, aan ni li teer nimi. 9Ni ŋmee i paan nimi aadir aabisamɔi pu, ni nimi aatiŋ aagon aabisamɔi pu.
Limɔyiir aasurm
10“Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan puu tipuur ti tii niyaajatiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob pu na, u ga di kitiŋ ki kpa ntisakpem mu wiir, ki kpa liwangol, aan naa maa mu nibaa na, tii nimi. 11Ŋidichal ga li gbii tiwanyaan ni nimi nibaa aa di ŋa ŋi ponn ni na, inyunbun mu bi nima, ni mu aa ye nimi le gbii i, le ŋisubil aasui, ni olif aakpan aasui aasar ti nimi nibaa aa kon, kaa bun ti na, mu ga li bi nima. N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ti di kitiŋ ngbaan tii nimi, aan ni kpa tijikaar ki ji babr na kan, 12ni li nyi ki taa suln Uwumbɔr u nyan nimi Ijipt yaab aaŋaal ni na, nin chee ni nan ye binaagbiib na, aabɔr. 13Ni li pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki li dooni uma baanja, aan ki li puur nimi aapuur waayimbil baanja pu. 14Ni taa ki doon liwaal libaa; ni taa doon binib bi mann goln nima na aawaal libaa. 15Ni yaa dooni ŋiwaa kan, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ga dan ni pu ke mmii na, ki nan kuln nimi kookoo, ba pu? Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u bi ni chee na aa ban ke waanib ki li dooni nibaa ki kpee u pu.
16“Ni taa tɔŋ Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ke naah nan ŋa pu Masa aatiŋ ni na. 17Ni li nyi ki li joo ikaal imɔk u di tii nimi na. 18Uwumbɔr aah len ke ni li bi mbimbinyaan mu ni na, ni li ŋani kina man, le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi. Nima le ga ŋmaa cha ni gaa kitinyanyaan ki Uwumbɔr nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib na. 19Waah nan puu pu na, ni ga jenn nyan nimi aadim.
20“N‑yoonn mu choo na, nimi aabim yaa nan baa nimi ke, ‘Ba ŋa Tidindaan Uwumbɔr bui ke ti li joo waakaal ngbaan mɔmɔk kina?’ kan, 21ni tuk bi ke, ‘Ti nan ye binaagbiib le ki bi Ijipt aabɔr aaŋaal ni, le Uwumbɔr di waapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan ni timi. 22Tinimbil ni, le ti kan u ŋa iwaan, ni ijawaan aawan, ki daa Ijipt yaab, ni baabɔr, ni waayidam mɔmɔk aatafal. 23Uma le nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki tii timi lifuur, le ki joo ni timi do chee na; ki nan di kitiŋ kee tii timi, waah nan puu tipuur pu tii tiyaajatiib na. 24Uma Tidindaan Uwumbɔr bui timi ke ti li joo waakaal ngbaan mɔmɔk mbamɔm, ki li pak u, ke ti yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga li kii timi aatimbol, aan ki cha li li kpa tiwan mɔmɔk, 25ke ti yaa joo waakaal mɔmɔk mbamɔm, waah tuk timi pu na kan, usui ga li piin ti pu.’

english_text:
Force the Other Nations Out of the Land
(Exodus 34.11-16)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, the Lord your God will help you take the land of the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These seven nations have more people and are stronger than Israel, but when you attack them, 2the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them, 3and don't let your sons and daughters marry any of them. 4If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
5 So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire.
The Lord's Chosen People
Moses said:
6 Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own. 7You were the weakest of all nations, 8but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
9 You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations. 10But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you. 11So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today.
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
(Deuteronomy 28.1-14; Leviticus 26.3-13)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors. 13The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs. 14God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase. 15You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases.
Destroy the Nations and Their Gods
Moses said to Israel:
