16When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
17You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.” 18But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king. 19You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much. 20Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead. 21So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
22As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals. 23-24But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
25After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord, 26so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aanib
(Nnyam 34.11-16)
1“Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga di nimi koon kitiŋ ki ni cha ni ti gaa ki na ponn ni. Le ni yaa tur koo ki ponn ni kan, u ga jenn nyan ŋinibol pam. U ga jenn nyan Hef yaab, ni Girgas yaab, ni Amor yaab, ni Kanaann yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab. Ŋinibol ŋilole ngbaan wiir, ki kpa mpɔɔn jer nimi. 2N‑yoonn mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ti di binib ngbaan ŋa nimi aapɔɔn ni, aan ni nyaŋ bi na kan, ni ku doo bi kookoo. Ni taa ŋa bi nimaantɔtiib, ki taa li san bi kinimbaak. 3Ni taa yoor bibisatiib, ki taa cha nijapɔtiib mu yoor bi ponn ni aapiibim. 4Ba pu? ni yaa ŋa kina kan, bi ga cha nimi aabim yii Uwumbɔr, le ki dooni ŋiwaa. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ga fii ni pu, le u kuln nimi doo. 5Nima pu na, ni gbaa wii baawaa aatork aabimbin, ki gbaa wii baatakpal aawaa ŋi fɔk ke jaatɔlk na yuk yuk, ki gaa baapiiwaal li bi yin li ke Asera na aawaachur lii, ki see baawaa mɔmɔk mmii. 6Naah ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanib pu na, ni ŋa kina. Nimi le u nyan dulnyaa aanib mɔmɔk ni, ke ni li ye uma ubaa aanib.
7“Naa ye ke ni wiir le jer binib biken, nima le cha Uwumbɔr gee nimi ki nyan nimi ŋinibol mɔmɔk ni; nimi le par, kaa wiir dulnyaa wee ni. 8Uwumbɔr tee gee nimi, le ki ban ke u li joo tipuur ti u nan puu tii niyaajatiib na. Nima pu le u di waapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan nimi tinaagbiir ni, ki gaa nimi lii Ijipt yaab aabɔr chee. 9Ni teer ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr baanja le ye Uwumbɔr, le ki ŋani waah len pu na. U ga li joo waah puu tipuur ti na, ki ga mɔk ŋiniker lichur ŋi gee u ki joo waakaal na, waah kpa ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, 10ki mu ga daa binib bi nan u na aatafal. 11Nima pu na, maah mɔk nimi pu na, ni li joo mmɔkm ngbaan kina; maah di ikaal i mɔk nimi din wee na, ni li joo i mbamɔm.
Limɔkiir aanyoor
(Ikaal 28.1-14)
12“Ni yaa ŋun ki joo ikaal yee mbamɔm kan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga li beenin joo waah puu tipuur ti na, ki ga mɔk nimi waageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, ke waah nan puu pu tii niyaajatiib na. 13U ga li gee nimi ki ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, nima kan, ni ga pɔr kpee, ki li kpa mbim pam. U ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa nimi aasar, ni tijikaar, ni ndaan aasubil, ni olif aakpan pu; u ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, ki tii nimi tiwakor pam. U ga ŋa ni pu tinyoor tee mɔmɔk aaboln, kitiŋ ki pu u nan puu tii niyaajatiib ke u ga di tii nimi na. 14Binib bibaa aa ki bi dulnyaa wee ni, ki ga kan tinyoor ti aaboln u ga di tii nimi na. Nimi bijab, ni bipiib, ni nimi aawakor mɔmɔk ubaa aan gur kaan li kpa mbim. 15Uwumbɔr ga li kii nimi iween mɔmɔk chee, waan cha nkun aaween i aaboln nan lir Ijipt yaab pu na dan ni pu; u ga cha i dan nimi aadim ma pu. 16Ni ku ki kuln ŋinibol ŋimɔk Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di ŋa niŋaal ni na, ki taa san bi kinimbaak. Ni taa li dooni baawaa, kina aa ŋan, ŋi ga bii nimi.
17“Ni taa len nibaa chee ke ŋinibol ngbaan wiir jer nimi, naan ŋmaa jenn nyan ŋi. 18Ni taa li san ŋi ijawaan. Ni teer Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan ŋa Ijipt yaab aabɔr, ni waanib mɔmɔk pu na. 19Ni teer tiwanbir ti ninimbigbaŋ nan kan na, ni laasib, ni iwaan aawan, ni mpɔɔn sakpiin mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan di gaa nimi lii na. Waah nan ŋa pu ki bii Ijipt yaab na, u ga ki ŋa kina le ki kuln binib bi ni san bi ijawaan na. 20U ga cha ijawaan chuu bi; le binib bi san buen mbɔbɔryaan ni na, u ga kuln bi. 21Nima pu na, ni taa li san binib ngbaan ijawaan. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi ni chee. U ye Uwumbɔr sakpiin la, le ni ŋan ke ni li san u ijawaan. 22Naah tur koo ŋinibol ngbaan ponn ni pu na, u ga li jenn nyan ni bi sii sii la. Naan ŋmaa nyaŋ bi nfum mbaa, ni yaa ŋa kina kan, tipeewanbir ti bi na ga pɔr ki li muk nimi. 23Uwumbɔr ga di nimi aadim ŋa nimi aaŋaal ni, ki cha ijawaan chuu bi, le ni ti kuln bi doo. 24U ga di baabɔrb ŋa niŋaal ni, le ni ga ku bi; bi ga suln bibɔr. Ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa kiir nimi, le ni ga kuln bi mɔmɔk. 25Ni see baawaa mmii. Baah di tikunabr ni salmaa u paan ŋi pu na, ni taa li neen ŋi, ki taa yoor ŋi. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, naan li ŋan, ni ga bii nimi, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa gee ŋiwaa kpala. 26Ni taa joo ni ŋiwaa ngbaan ŋibaa nido, ni yaa ŋa kina kan, Uwumbɔr aah ga kuln ŋi pu na, u ga kuln ni mu kina la. Uwumbɔr aah ga kuln ŋiwaa ngbaan pu na, ni mu li nan ŋi, ki yii ŋi.

english_text:
The Lord Takes Care of You
Moses said:
1Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
2Don't forget how the Lord your God has led you through the desert for the past 40 years. He wanted to find out if you were truly willing to obey him and depend on him, 3 so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
4Over the past 40 years, your clothing hasn't worn out, and your feet haven't swollen. 5 So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children. 6Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
7The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills. 8-9You can dig for copper in those hills, and the stones are made of iron ore. And you won't go hungry. Wheat and barley fields are everywhere, and so are vineyards and orchards full of fig, pomegranate, and olive trees, and there is plenty of honey.
Don't Forget the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you. 11 Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them, 12you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in. 13You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
14But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free. 15Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink. 16He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
17When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.” 18Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
19-20But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
translation_text:
Kitinyaan ki Uwumbɔr ban u di tii waanib na
1“Ni li keei tii ikaal imɔk m di mɔk nimi din aataak kee na mbamɔm, nima kan, ni ga li kpa limɔfal, ki maa mbim, ki pɔr sakpen, aan nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa gaa kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib na. 2Ni teer ŋibin imonko ilee ŋi jer na ponn ni, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan loln ni pu nsan dandar mumina, nteersakpiin ni pu na. U nan di ŋimuk aabɔŋ tɔŋ nimi, ke u lik naah ga ŋa pu na, ki ki lik ke ni ga joo waakaal aan naan joo i. 3U nan cha ni chuun nkon, le u di tijikaar ti bi yin ti ke mana, aan nimi ni niyaajatiib aa nyi ti na kpiin nimi. U nan ŋa kina ke u mɔk nimi ke naa ye tijikaar baanja le ga ŋmaa tii unii limɔfal; limɔboln limɔk nyan ni Uwumbɔr aamɔb ni na le ga tii unii limɔfal. 4Naah chuun ŋibin imonko ilee ŋimina ponn ni na, nimi aawanpeenkaan aa kpo, le nimi aataa mu aa duun. 5Ni teer ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan sur nimi ki daa nitafal, ke ubo aate aah sur u pu na. 6Nima pu na, ni ŋa Uwumbɔr aah tuk nimi pu na, ni li dii waakaal aah mɔk nimi pu na, ki kii waamɔb. 7Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le joo nimi cha kitiŋ ki nyuun na ponn ni, kitiŋ ki kpa ŋimɔɔ, ni inyunbun, ni nnyun mu nyeeni nya kitiŋ ki puu cha tifatann, ni ŋigongon ni na, 8kitiŋ ki ŋani njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aabɔŋ aabɔŋ, ni olif aakpan aasubil, ni tisiir na. 9Kitiŋ ngbaan ni, nkon aan chuu nimi, le ni mu aan lann nibaa. Kaatakpasakpiin kpa tikur ŋi ponn ni, le ni ga ŋmaa kan kaagongon ni tikumann. 10Ni ga kan tijikaar mɔk aabɔŋ kitiŋ ngbaan ni ki ji bab; le ni ga doon Nidindaan Uwumbɔr kitinyaan ki u di tii nimi na pu.
Bi taa suln Uwumbɔr bɔr
11“Ni li nyi ki taa suln Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bɔr, ni taa yii waakaal imɔk m di tuk nimi din wee na. 12N‑yoonn mu ni ti kan ki jin bab, ki maa ŋidichanyaan ki koo ŋi ni, 13aan nimi aawakor moo pɔr kpee, aan ki kan tikunabr, ni salmaa, aan nimi aawan mɔmɔk moo kpee kan, 14ni li nyi ki taa li kpa kigaak, aan ki suln Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u nan nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, nin chee ni nan ye binaagbiib na bɔr. 15Uma le nan loln ni pu nsan, nteersakpiin mu bir na ni, nin chee inyoohn ni ikuub i kpa liluul sakpen na bi na. Kitikuun ki kaa kpa nnyun kpala na, le u nan cha nnyun nyan ni litakpajool ponn ni, le ni nyun. 16Nteersakpiin ngbaan ni, le u nan tii nimi tijikaar ti bi yin ti ke mana na, le ni jin, tijikaar ti niyaajatiib aa nan nyi ti na. U nan cha falaa pii nimi ke u ŋaŋ nimi; nima kan, naadoon na, ni yaa nan nyaŋ kan, u ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu. 17Nima pu na, ni taa dak ke nimi aapɔɔn pu le cha ni ŋa biwankpadam. 18Ni teer ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ŋa nimi biwankpadam; waah nan puu tipuur ti tii niyaajatiib na, le u beenin joo ti, ki ŋa kina. 19Ni taa suln Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bɔr aan ki fenn dii ŋiwaa, ki dooni ŋi, ki tun tii ŋi. Mbamɔn le m tuk nimi din wee na, ni yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga kuln nimi. 20Ni yaa kaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb kan, ni li nyi ke u ga kuln nimi, ke waah ban u kuln ŋinibol ŋi ni bi tur koo baatiŋ ni na pu na.

english_text:
Why the Lord Will Help Israel
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky. 2Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle. 3But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
4-6After the Lord helps you wipe out these nations and conquer their land, don't think he did it because you are such good people. You aren't good—you are stubborn! No, the Lord is going to help you, because the nations that live there are evil, and because he wants to keep the promise he made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
When Israel Made an Idol
(Exodus 32)
Moses said to Israel:
7Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
8At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you. 9-11 It happened during those 40 days and nights that I was on the mountain, without anything to eat or drink. He had told me to come up there so he could give me the agreement he made with us. And this agreement was actually the same Ten Commandments he had announced to you when he spoke from the fire on the mountain. The Lord had written them on two flat stones with his own hand. But after giving me the two stones, 12he said:
Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
13I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are. 14So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel.
Moses said:
15Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them. 16I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf. 17So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
18-20I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for 40 days and nights. You had committed a terrible sin by making that idol, and the Lord hated what you had done. He was angry enough to destroy all of you and Aaron as well. So I prayed for you and Aaron as I had done before, and this time the Lord answered my prayers.
21It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
22 You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah. 23 Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command. 24In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
25After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for 40 days and nights 26and prayed:
Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own. 27Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin. 28If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.” 29But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
translation_text:
Israel yaab aatafalaaŋun aabimbin
1“Israel yaab, li pel man. Din wee na, ni ban ni puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aan ki gaa ŋinibol ŋi wiir ki kpa mpɔɔn jer nimi na aatiŋ la. Baatim ye mukpaan la, le bi maa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ti nyan paacham na gob mu. 2Binib ngbaan fɔk ki kpa mpɔɔn. Bi ye ŋiniwɔk la, le ni ŋun ke ubaa aan ŋmaa faa bi butɔb. 3Ni ga kan, ki bee nibaa, ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga loln ni pu nsan, ke mmii mu pɔɔ na. Naah tur koo bi ni pu na, le u ga nyaŋ bi, aan ni jenn nyan bi woween, ki kuln bi, ke waah nan puu pu na.
4“Nidindaan Uwumbɔr yaa jenn bi tii nimi kan, ni taa dak nee aapuwɔb, ke naah ŋan sakpen pu na le cha u gaa baatiŋ ngbaan tii nimi. Naa ye kina, ni ye ke binib ngbaan aah kpa mbiin pu na le u ban u jenn nyan bi. 5Naa ye ke ni ye bininyaam ki ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na nima le cha u ban ni gaa baatiŋ. U ga jenn nyan bi, ba pu? bi ye mbiindam la, le u ki ban u gbiin tipuur ti u nan puu tii niyaajatiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob na. 6Ni li nyi mbamɔm ke naa ye ke ni ŋan ki ŋeer kitiŋ ngbaan le ga cha u gaa kitinyanyaan ngbaan tii nimi. Naa ye kina, ni ye tafalaaŋun aanib la.
7“Ni teer, ki taa suln naah nan bi nteersakpiin ni, ki ŋa Nidindaan Uwumbɔr liŋuul pu na. Nwiin mundaal ni nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki nan saa bundaal ni fuu ni do na, ni yii waamɔb. 8Sainai Aajool chee, ni nan ŋa Uwumbɔr liŋuul. Naah nan ŋa u liŋuul pu na nan ŋeer u kuln nimi. 9M nan jon Sainai Aajool paab, m ti gaa ŋitakpapapan ŋi pu Uwumbɔr nan ŋmee waakaal i u nan di tii nimi na. M nan bi nima iwiin ni tinyer imonko ilee, le kaa nan jin, ki mu aa nyun nibaa. 10Le Uwumbɔr nan di ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi pu u nan di ubaa aaŋaal ŋmee waah nan len ni chee tibɔr, mmii ni, bundaal ni nan kuun si lijool ngbaan chee na, tii mi. 11Mbamɔn, iwiin ni tinyer imonko ilee ngbaan aah jer na, le Uwumbɔr di ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi u nan ŋmee waakaal ŋi pu na tii mi.
12“Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, ‘Ŋa mala ki sunn lijool taab; saanib bi aa nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na yii mi, ki tun titunwanbir. Bi kpaan fenn ki cha maah tuk bi ke bi ŋa pu na, le ki ŋa liwaal tii bibaa.’
13“Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke, ‘M nyi binib ngbaan aah kpa tafalaaŋun pu na. 14Aa taa kiir mi. M ban ke m kuln bi, nima kan, ubaa aan ki teer bibɔr, le ki ga cha saamaal ŋa litimbol sakpeln li ga li pɔɔ ki jer bi na.’
15“Nima pu na, m nan ŋa mala, le ki sunn ni lijool ngbaan taab, ki joo ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi Uwumbɔr nan ŋmee waakaal ŋa ŋi pu na. Mmiigaal nan nyan ni lijool ngbaan paab. 16M nan kan ke ni kpaan yii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal i u di tii nimi na a, le ki tun titunwanbir u chee, ba pu? ni ŋa liwaal li bi ke unaajabo na tii nibaa, ki dooni li. 17Nima pu na, m nan di ŋitakpapapan ngbaan mee lii ninimbiin ni, le ŋi wii yak yak. 18Le m ki lir gbaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nwiin pu ni kinyeek, iwiin imonko ilee, kaa ji, kaa nyu nibaa. Naah nan tun titunwanbir Uwumbɔr chee, ki cha waaŋuul fii pu na le cha m nan ŋa kina. 19Uwumbɔr aah nan gee liŋuul sakpen pu na, le ijawaan nan chuu mi. Usui nan fii sakpen, le u ban ke u kuln nimi; le maah nan ŋa pu na, Uwumbɔr nan ki sɔŋ usui ki ŋun tii mi. 20Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii Aaronn pu, le u ban u ku u, nima pu na, m nan mee Uwumbɔr tii Aaronn mu n‑yoonn ngbaan. 21Naah nan ŋa titunwanbir aawan ni nan ye tikur aanaajabo na, m nan nyan ni ki di see mmii. M nan gbaa wii ni yak yak, ki nan ni le ni ti ŋa n‑yon, le m di mu mee ŋa mbun mu nyan ni lijool aapaacham ki choo taab na.
22“Ni nan ki ŋa Nidindaan Uwumbɔr liŋuul, buyoonn ni nan bi Tabera, ni Masa, ni Kiberof Hatafa aatim ni na. 23Buyoonn ni nan bi Kades Banea na, u nan bui nimi ke ni buen ti gaa kitiŋ ki u nan puu ke u ga di tii nimi na, le ni yii waamɔb, kaa tii u naadii, kaa kii waamɔb. 24Maah bee nimi bundaal ki nan saa din wee na, naa kii tii Uwumbɔr.
25“Maah bee ke Uwumbɔr ban u kuln nimi na, le m gbaan unimbiin ni, nwiin pu ni kinyeek, ki ti saa iwiin imonko ilee. 26M nan mee ke, ‘Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, taa kuln saanib bi aa di saapɔɔnsakpiin gaa bi lii, ki nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na. 27Teer ki taa suln saatutum Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob bɔr, ki taa gar binib ngbaan aatafalaaŋun aabimbin, ni baah kpa mbiin ki tun titunwanbir pu na. 28Ni yaa kaa ye kina kan, Ijipt yaab ga bui ke saa ŋmaa joo binib ngbaan fuu kitiŋ ki aa nan puu ke aa ga di tii bi na ni la. Bi ga bui ke saa nan gee saanib ngbaan, le ki di bi dan nteersakpiin ni, ke aa nan kuln bi. 29Ni ye mbamɔn ke binib bee le aa nyan bi ke bi li ye saanib, le ki di saapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni.’

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Exodus 34.1-10)
Moses said to the people:
1The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him. 2He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
3So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain, 4where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain.
After the Lord returned the stones to me, 5I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there.
Aaron Died
(Numbers 20.22-29)
Moses said to Israel:
6 Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest. 7Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams.
The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest
Moses said to Israel:
8 After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things. 9The Lord promised that he would always provide for the tribe of Levi, and that's why he won't give them any land, when he divides it among the other tribes.
The Lord Answered the Prayers of Moses
(Exodus 34.9,10,27-29)
Moses said to Israel:
10 When I had taken the second set of stones up the mountain, I spent 40 days and nights there, just as I had done before. Once again, the Lord answered my prayer and did not destroy you. 11Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.”
What the Lord Wants
Moses said:
12People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul, 13and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
14Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens. 15Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
16Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn. 17 The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind. 18 The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing. 19And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
20Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name. 21Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
22 When your ancestors went to live in Egypt, there were only 70 of them. But the Lord has blessed you, and now there are more of you than there are stars in the sky.
translation_text:
Moses aah nan ki gir ti gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal lelee pu na aabɔr
(Nnyam 34.1-10)
1“N‑yoonn ngbaan le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, ‘Kpii ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi naahn njan yee na, aan ki ŋa ŋikpan aadakaa mu, ki di ŋi ŋa u ponn ni. 2Dan m chee lijool paab, aan m nan ki ŋmee ŋitakpapapan ngbaan pu, ke maah nan ŋmee ŋima na pu, aan aa di lii wii na, aan aa di ŋi ŋa dakaa ngbaan ni.’
3“Nima pu na, m nan di lisiijal aadɔ le kpii dakaa ngbaan, ki kpii ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ke njan yee na, le ki di ŋi jon lijool paab. 4Uwumbɔr nan ŋmee ŋitakpapapan ngbaan pu tibɔr chachaan ti u nan ŋmee njan, aan ni ye waakaal kipiik i u nan di tii nimi, buyoonn ni nan kuun lijool ngbaan taab, aan u len ni chee tibɔr mmii ni na. Uwumbɔr nan di ŋitakpapapan ngbaan tii mi, 5le m fenn ki sunn ni lijool ngbaan taab. Uwumbɔr aah nan bui mi pu na, m nan di ŋi ŋa dakaa ngbaan ni, le ŋi beenin bi u ponn ni, ki nan saa din wee.”
Aaronn aah kpo pu na
6Le Israel yaab nan fii Jaakann yaab aanyunbun ibaa chee, ki buen Mosera aatiŋ ni. Nima chee le Aaronn nan kpo, le bi sub u kitiŋ ngbaan ni, le ujapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Eleasar na nan kal ute aajal pu, ki ye utotoor. 7Bi nan ki nyan nima chee ki fii buen Gudgoda aatiŋ ni, ki ki fii nima mu ki ti fuu Jotbata aatiŋ ni, nima chee nan kpa nnyun pam. 8Baah nan bi lijool ngbaan chee na, le Uwumbɔr nan nyan Liifai aanibol ke bi li lik Nkaal Aadakaa ngbaan, ki li tun bitotoorb aatuln tii u, ki li joo waayimbil ŋani tinyoor ŋani waanib pu. Liifai yaab laa beenin tun lituln ngbaan ki nan saa din wee. 9Kina pu le baa nan yakr kitiŋ tii Liifai yaab aanibol ke biken na. Baah nan gaa ipiin i na le ye ke bi nan kpa nsan ke bi li ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aatotoorb, ke waah nan puu pu na.
10Moses nan ki bui ke, “M nan bi lijool ngbaan aapaacham nwiin pu ni kinyeek, ki ti saa iwiin imonko ilee, ke maah nan ŋa njan pu na, ki gaŋni Uwumbɔr. Le Uwumbɔr ki ŋun tii mi; u nan kii ke waan ki kuln nimi. 11U nan bui mi ke m sunn ni, ki nan loln ni pu nsan, aan ni ŋmaa buen ti gaa kitiŋ ki u nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib na.
Uwumbɔr aah ban waanib li bi pu na
12“Israel yaab, li pel man Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban ni li bi pu na: Ni li dooni Uwumbɔr, ki li ŋani waah bui ke ni ŋa pu na. Ni li gee u, ki li joo nisui mɔmɔk tun waatuln. 13Ni li joo waakaal mɔmɔk. Din wee na, m ban m di i tii nimi aan i li kpa tinyoor ki toor nimi. 14Uwumbɔr le yeh paacham, ni dulnyaa, ni tiwan nimɔk bi u ni na. 15Uwumbɔr aah gee niyaajatiib sakpen pu na, le u nyan nimi baanja ŋinibol mɔmɔk ni, le ni beenin ye waanib ki nan saa din. 16Nima pu na, n‑yoonn mue ki joo cha, ni kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, ki di cha nimi aatafalaaŋun ngbaan. 17Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le jer dindatiib mɔmɔk, le ki kpa mpɔɔn mu ki jer ipɔɔn mɔmɔk. Waah ye usakpiin ki kpa mpɔɔn na, le ni ŋeer ke ti li san u ijawaan. Waa kpa imaagann, le kaa gaal igaŋgaŋlik. 18Uma le lik nkpobim, ni bikpopiib, ki gee biwɔwɔm bi koo ti chee na. Uma le tii bi tijikaar ni tiwanpeenkaan. 19Nima pu na, ni li gee biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na; ba pu? ni mu nan ye biwɔwɔm le Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 20Ni kii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb aan ki li dooni uma baanja. Ni li si chob ki dii u mbamɔm, ki li puur tipuur waayimbil baanja pu. 21Ni li pak u. Uma le ye nimi Aawumbɔr, le ninimbil kan waah ŋa lijinjiir aawan nimɔk ki tii nimi na. 22N‑yoonn mu niyaajatiib nan buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, bi nan ye binib imonko itaa ni kipiik baanja la, le dandana wee, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr cha ni wiir sakpen ke iŋmabi i bi kitaapaak na.

english_text:
If You Are Loyal to the Lord, He Will Bless You
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings. 2Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power 3 when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people. 4 And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
5You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here. 6 And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
7With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
8Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land 9that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time. 10It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops. 11But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven, 12because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
13 The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him, 14-15he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
16But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods, 17the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
18 Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them. 19Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 20Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates. 21Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
22Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants, 23he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack. 24 You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea. 25No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
26You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you? 27Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you. 28But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
29 After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal. 30You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
31Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there, 32be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah kpa mpɔɔn pu na
1“Ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki li joo waakaal n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 2Din wee, ni teer naah bee Uwumbɔr aabimbin, waah tun ŋitukpaan ŋi ni chee na pu. Naa ye nimi aabim le kan, nimi le nan kan ŋitukpaan ngbaan. 3Ni nan kan Uwumbɔr aah ye mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, ki tun ŋitukpaan, ni lijinjiir aatun pu na. Ni nan kan waah ŋa Ijipt aabɔr, ni waatiŋ mɔmɔk pu na. 4Ni nan kan Uwumbɔr aah nan kuln Ijipt aajab, ni baataan, ni itaan aatɔroku tiib pu na; u nan cha bi bee Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem ni, buyoonn bi nan san paa ni nimi pu na. 5Ni ki nyi Uwumbɔr aah nan ki ŋa tiwan nimɔk tii nimi nteersakpiin ni, aan ni nin fuu do na. 6Ni ki teer waah nan ŋa Datann, ni Abiram, bi nan ye Eliab aajapɔtiib, ki nyan ni Rubenn aataŋaal ni aanib pu na. Ni mɔmɔk aanimbil ni, le Uwumbɔr nan cha kitiŋ piir, le bi ni baamaal, ni baakookoo yaan, ni baanaagbiib, ni baawakor mɔmɔk lir ni ponn ni, le kitiŋ ki biin bi pu. 7Mbamɔn, nimi bimina le nan kan ŋitukpaan ŋimɔk Uwumbɔr nan tun na.
Tipuur aatiŋ aah kpa tinyoor ti na
8“Ni li joo waakaal i mɔmɔk m di mɔk nimi din wee na mbamɔm. Nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa puur limɔɔl aan ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki ni chaa koo ki ponn ni na. 9Le ni ga li bi kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na ni, aan Uwumbɔr nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib, ni biyaabitiib na pu. 10Kitiŋ ki ni ban ni gaa ki na aa bi ke Ijipt aatiŋ ki ni nan bi ki ponn ni na aah bi pu na. 11Ni yaa nan kon tijikaar nima chee kan, see ni pɔɔn nibaa ki lun nnyun gbir ti pu; tɔ, naah chaa koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni na, ki kpa ŋijoo, ni tifatann, le utaal ga nu ŋa nimi aajikaar pu. 12Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le joo kitiŋ ngbaan, ki lik ki n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
13“Kina pu na, ni li joo waakaal i m di tuk nimi din wee na mbamɔm, ki li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki li joo nisui mɔmɔk tun waah ban pu na. 14Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga cha utaal nu kitiŋ ngbaan pu, le ni yaa ti ŋeer unaalan, ni linimoogaal aayoonn kan, u ga cha utaal nu. Nima kan, ni ga li kpa njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan sakpen. 15Timoor ga li bi, nimi aawakor ŋmɔ. Ni ga kan naah ban tijikaar ti na mɔmɔk. 16Ni taa cha nibaa ŋmann nimi aan ni yii Uwumbɔr ki fenn dii ŋiwaa ki dooni ŋi. 17Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, Uwumbɔr ga gee ni pu liŋuul; waan ki cha utaal nu, le nimi aatiŋ ga kuur ki ti chaar jer, le nimi aajikaar aan ŋmaa ŋa. Hali kitiŋ ngbaan aah ye kitinyaan pu aan u di ki tii nimi na, naan ki yunn le ni ga kpo.
18“Ni teer ikaal ngbaan aabɔr, aan ki li joo i mbamɔm. Ni ŋmee i ki di gbin niŋaal pu, ki di buu tam niyigbeer mu pu, aan ki li teer ibɔr. 19Ni di i mɔk nimi aabim. Ni yaa bi linampal, bee ni yaa bi ligɔr kan, ni li len yaabɔr. Ni li len yaabɔr buyoonn ni ka fuur na, ni buyoonn ni bi tun lituln na. 20Ni ŋmee i paan nimi aadir aabisamɔi pu, ni nimi aatiŋ aagon aabisamɔi pu. 21Nima kan, nimi, ni nimi aabim ga li bi kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib na pu, ki yunn. Ni ga li bi ki ponn ni n‑yoonn mumɔk paacham ni taab ga li bi na.
22“Ni li nyi ki li joo ikaal i mɔmɔk m di mɔk nimi na mbamɔm. Ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki ŋa waakaal aah mɔk nimi pu na, ki li dii uma baanja. 23Le u ga jenn nyan ŋinibol ŋimɔk ni tur koo ŋi ponn ni na, le ni ga gaa ŋinibol kpaan ŋi kpa mpɔɔn jer nimi na aatiŋ. 24Nitaa aah taa kitiŋ ki mɔmɔk pu na ga li ye nimi yaan la. Nimi aatiŋ mɔk ga yoor nteersakpiin aaŋangii wɔb ki ti nya Lebanonn Aajool chee, ŋŋangan wɔb, le ki ga ki yoor Yufrates Aamɔɔl chee, liwipuul wɔb, ki ti ker Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem chee, liwilir wɔb. 25Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan puu pu na, u ga cha linibol limɔk ni fuu laatiŋ ni na aanib li san nimi ijawaan. Ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa kiir nimi kpala.
26“Lik man, din wee na, m ban ni lee naah gee tiwan ni na la, ni gee tinyoor le aan tibɔbir? 27Ni yaa kii, ki joo Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal i m joo tuk nimi din wee na kan, u ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu. 28Ni mu yaa yii waakaal, ki fenn dooni ŋiwaa kan, ni ga kan tibɔbir la. Teer man ke naa kee dii ŋiwaa, ni taa dii ŋi kpala. 29Uwumbɔr yaa joo ni nimi kitiŋ ki ni ban ni gaa ki na ni kan, ni sil Gerisim Aajool paab ki moon tinyoor aabɔr, ki sil Ebal Aajool paab ki moon tibɔbir aabɔr. 30(Ŋijoo ŋilee ngbaan bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb la, le ki bi Kanaann yaab bi bi Jɔɔdann aafataŋ ni na aapepel ni. Ŋi bi ki cha liwilir wɔb la, le kaa daa More aawaachur chee, ki bi Gilgal aatiŋ chee.) 31Ni ban ni puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, ki gaa kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban u di tii nimi na la. 32Buyoonn ni ti kal ki ponn ni doo na kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki li joo waakaal i mɔmɔk m joo tuk nimi din wee na mbamɔm.

english_text:
Only One Place To Worship the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
1Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land. 2But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees. 3 Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there. 4Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
5-19 Soon you will cross the Jordan, and the Lord will help you conquer your enemies and let you live in peace, there in the land he has given you. But after you are settled, life will be different. You must not offer sacrifices just anywhere you want to. Instead, the Lord will choose a place somewhere in Israel where you must go to worship him. All of your sacrifices and offerings must be taken there, including sacrifices to please the Lord and any gift you promise or voluntarily give him. That's where you must also take one tenth of your grain, wine, and olive oil, as well as the first-born of your cattle, sheep, and goats. You and your family and servants will eat your gifts and sacrifices and celebrate there at the place of worship, because the Lord your God has made you successful in everything you have done. And since Levites will not have any land of their own, you must ask some of them to come along and celebrate with you.
Sometimes you may want to kill an animal for food and not as a sacrifice. If the Lord has blessed you and given you enough cows or sheep or goats, then you can butcher one of them where you live. You can eat it just like the meat from a deer or gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat. But you must not eat the blood of any animal—let the blood drain out on the ground.
20-21The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want. 22It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
23-24 But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat. 25Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
26-27All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
28If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful.
Worship the Lord in the Right Way
Moses said:
29Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
30But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?” 31No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
32 Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
translation_text:
Baah ga li dooni Uwumbɔr nin chee na
1“Ni yaa bi kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Uwumbɔr na, ban u di ki tii nimi na ni kan, naah ga li joo ikaal i na sɔ. Li pel man yaah ye pu na: 2Ni kuln naah ban ni gaa kitiŋ ki na aanib ngbaan aah dooni baawaa nin chee na, nima le ye ŋijoofɔfɔk pu, ni ŋigongon pu, ni tiwaachur aasui taab. 3Ni gbaa wiir baatork aabimbin, ni baawaa aatakpal yak yak, ki see baapiiwaal Asera aanaŋ, aan ki gaa yikr baawaa mɔmɔk, nima kan, baan ki ŋmaa dan ŋaah bi nin chee na ki nan doon ŋi.
4“Binib ngbaan aah dooni baawaa pu na, ni mu taa li dooni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr kina aaboln. 5Nimi aanibol mɔmɔk aah ga kal nin chee na, Uwumbɔr ga nyan nibaa chee, le ni ga choo unimbiin ni, ki nan dooni u nima. 6Nima chee le ni ga toor nimi aatoor ti ni ga li joo seer mmii ni na, ni kitork kiken, ni naah ga nyan nimi aawan kipiik ponn ni nibaa ni tii Uwumbɔr na, ni nimi aapiin, ni ni yaa puu Uwumbɔr tipuur kan, naah ga pa pu na, ni nibaa aageehn aapiin, ni nimi aawakor aajan aabim aapar. 7Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u ŋa ni pu tinyoor na aanimbiin ni, le nimi, ni nimi aamaal mɔmɔk ga kpaan ki ji tiwanyaan nimɔk ni tun ki kan na.
8“N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, naah bi ŋani pu na, ni taa ki ŋa kina. 9N‑yoonn mu jer ki nan saa din wee na, ni mɔmɔk aah gee pu na, le ni dooni Uwumbɔr; ba pu? naa kee koo kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan bui ke u ga di tii nimi aan ni li koo nima, ki kan lifuur. 10N‑yoonn mu ni ti puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl doo na kan, Uwumbɔr ga cha ni gaa kitiŋ ngbaan, ki li bi nima. U ga li kii nimi, nimi aadim chee, le ni ga li kpa nsuudoon. 11Uwumbɔr ga nyan nibaa chee le tii timi, aan ti li dooni u nima, le maah mɔk nimi pu na, ni li joo ni nimi aapiin mɔmɔk: ni ye nimi aatork ki ni joo seer mmii ni na, ni kitork kiken, ni naah ga nyan nimi aawan kipiik ponn ni nibaa ni tii Uwumbɔr na, ni ipiin, ni ipiinkpaan i ni puu ke ni ga tii u na. 12Nima chee, le nimi, ni nimi aabim, ni nimi aatutum, ni Liifai yaab bi bi nimi aatim ni na li kpa mpopiin ki li mɔɔni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni. Ni teer ke Liifai yaab aan li kpa bibaa aakpaakon. 13Ni taa li toor nimi aatork naah gee nin chee na, 14ni mɔmɔk kpaan libuul chachaan li Uwumbɔr ga nyan nimi aanibol libaa aatiŋ ni na, ki li toor nima. Nima chee baanja le ni ga li toor nimi aatork ki ni ga see ki mmii ni na, ni tiwan nimɔk m bui nimi ke ni li ŋani na.
15“Nimi aawakor ma kan, ni ga ŋmaa kɔr ti nin chee ni bi na ki ŋmɔ. Uwumbɔr aah tii nimi pu na, ni ga ŋmaa kɔr naah gee pu na ki ŋmɔ. Unii umɔk bi chain na, ni u kaa bi chain na kan, ni ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ nimi aawakor, ke naah ku ipeeman ki ŋmɔ nimi aageehn pu pu na. 16Tɔ, ni taa kpaan ŋmɔ tiwakor ngbaan aanann aan nsin li bi ti ponn ni. Ni kɔr tiwakor ngbaan ki nyan taasin kpir kitiŋ, ke naah kpir nnyun pu na. 17Tiwan nimɔk ni di toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr na kan, ni taa ji tiwan ngbaan linampal: naah ga nyan nimi aajikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan kipiik ponn ni nibaa ni tii Uwumbɔr na, ni nimi aawakor aajan aabim, ni naah puu tipuur ke ni ga tii Uwumbɔr ipiin i na, ni nimi aageehn aapiin, ni ipiin iken na aapar, ni taa ji ni linampal. 18Nimi, ni nimi aabim, ki kpee nimi aatutum, ni Liifai yaab bi koo nimi aatim ni na, kpaan ki ji ipiin ngbaan aajikaar Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nin chee u nyan ke ni li dooni u na baanja. Ni li kpa mpopiin ki mɔɔni tiwan nimɔk ni ŋa na pu. 19Naah ga li bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki cha n‑yoonn mu na, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki taa suln Liifai yaab bɔr.
20“N‑yoonn mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr moo tii nimi kitiŋ kpee, ke waah nan puu pu na kan, ni ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ tinann, naah ban pu na. 21Naah dooni Uwumbɔr nin chee na yaa daa sakpen, aan ni yaa gee ke ni kɔr tiwakor ti Uwumbɔr tii nimi na tibaa, ki ŋmɔ linampal na kan, ni ga ŋmaa ŋa kina, maah tuk nimi pu na. 22Unii umɔk bi chain na, ni u kaa bi chain na ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan, ke naah ŋmɔ ipeeman aanann pu na. 23Ni taa tee kpaan ŋmɔ tiwakor ngbaan aanann aan nsin li bi ti ponn ni, ba pu? limɔfal bi nsin ponn ni la; ni taa kpaan ŋmɔ tinann ni limɔfal. 24Ni taa ji nsin, ni kɔr tiwakor ngbaan ki nyan nsin kpir kitiŋ, ke naah kpir nnyun pu na. 25Ni yaa joo ikaal ngbaan mbamɔm kan, Uwumbɔr ga li kpa mpopiin ni pu, le ni ga li ŋan tii nimi, ni nimi aamaal. 26Ni li joo ni Uwumbɔr aapiin, ni naah puu tipuur ke ni ga tii u ipiin i na, ki di i buen waah nyan nin chee ke ni li dooni u na. 27Ni di kitork ki ni ga di ki mɔmɔk see mmii ni, Uwumbɔr aabimbiln paab na toor tii u nima chee. Naah ga di tiwakor ti toor kitork na, ni nyan taasin kpir waabimbiln pu, aan ki ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan. 28Ni li joo ikaal imɔk m di tuk nimi na mbamɔm, le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi, ni niyaabitiib, ki joo cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, ba pu? ni yaa ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na kan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga li kpa mpopiin ni pu.
Ni taa yii Uwumbɔr ki li dii ŋiwaa
29“Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga kuln ŋinibol ŋimɔk ni ban ni koo ŋaatim ponn ni na mɔmɔk, le ni ga kal nima. 30Uwumbɔr yaa kuln ŋinibol ngbaan doo aan ni koo ŋaatim ni kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki taa li dii baah dooni ŋiwaa ŋi na; ba pu? ni ye nnikun la. Ni taa li ban ni bee baah dooni baawaa pu na aan ki mu li dooni Uwumbɔr kina. 31Ni taa li dooni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ke baah dooni baawaa pu na, ba pu? bi dooni baawaa ki ŋani tiwan ni kaa ŋan na aabɔŋ, le Uwumbɔr nan kina aabimbin. Hali bi joo baabim le kɔr toor kitork ki seer mmii ni, ŋibimbin paab tii ŋiwaa.
32“Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki ŋa maah bui nimi pu na mɔmɔk, ni taa di tiwan nibaa kpee maah mɔk nimi pu na, ki mu taa nyan nibaa mu.

english_text:
Don't Worship Other Gods
Moses said to Israel:
1-2Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.” 3If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul. 4You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling, 5because he rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
If a prophet tells you to disobey the Lord your God and to stop worshiping him, then that prophet is evil and must be put to death.
6-10 Someone else may say to you, “Let's worship other gods.” That person may be your best friend, your brother or sister, your son or daughter, or your own dear wife or husband. But you must not listen to people who say such things. Instead, you must stone them to death. You must be the first to throw the stones, then others from the community will finish the job. Don't show any pity.
The gods worshiped by other nations have never done anything for you or your ancestors. People who ask you to worship other gods are trying to get you to stop worshiping the Lord, who rescued you from slavery in Egypt. So put to death anyone who asks you to worship another god. 11And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
12After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns. 13You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them. 14You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country, 15you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too. 16-17Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors. 18That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
translation_text:
1“Unii u bui ke u ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr na, bee unii u nyi tidaŋ aatataa na yaa puu tipuur tii nimi ke u ga mɔk nimi lijinjiir aawan, 2ki ban ke u cha ni li dooni ŋiwaa kan, ni taa dii u. Hali waah puu tipuur ti na yaa ŋa kina kan, 3ni taa kii tii u. Naa kee dii ŋiwaa ngbaan. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban ke u di unii ngbaan tɔŋ nimi ki lik ke ni gee u nisui mɔmɔk ni aan naa gee u. 4Ni li dii Uwumbɔr aasan ki pak u. Ni ŋun tii u, ki li joo waakaal mɔmɔk; ni li dooni uma baanja, ki li ŋani waah len pu na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 5Tɔ, ubɔnabr ngbaan, bee unii u nyi tidaŋ aatataa na yaa bui nimi ke ni yii Uwumbɔr u nan nyan ni nimi Ijipt yaab aatiŋ ni, nin chee ni nan ye binaagbiib na kan, ni ku u. Unii ngbaan aaboln ye mbiindaan la, le ki pɔɔni ubaa ke u nyan nimi Uwumbɔr aasan mu u tuk nimi ke ni li dii mu na ni. Ni ku udaan ngbaan, nima kan, ni ga gaa nibaa titunwanbir chee lii.
6“Hali ni yaa ye aana aabo, bee aajapɔɔn, bee aabisal, bee aapuu u aa gee sakpen na, bee aajɔ u aa ni u aan ŋmaa yakr tɔb chee na, le yaa loon bui si ke ni li dooni ŋiwaa kan, aa taa kii tii u. Aa ni aayaajatiib aa kee dii ŋiwaa ngbaan. 7Nibaakan bi ponn ni ubaa yaa pɔɔn ubaa ke u ŋmann nimi ke ni li dooni biniyayam bi koo gbɔk nimi, bee binib bi bi dandar na aawaa kan, 8ni taa cha u ŋmann nimi aan ni san dii u, ni taa pel waah len pu na kpala. Ni taa san u kinimbaak kpala, ki taa biin u pu. 9Ni ku u. Sin u, u pue len aa chee kina na kan, aa piin ki li mae u ŋitakpal aan ki cha biken kpee aa pu. 10Ni mae ŋitakpal ku u, ba pu? u ban u ŋmann nimi aan ni yii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki nyan nimi tinaagbiir ni na la. 11Israel yaab mɔmɔk yaa ŋun naah ku u pu na kan, bi ga san ijawaan, le ubaa aan ki ŋa titunwanbir ngbaan aaboln.
12“N‑yoonn mu ni ti bi ntim mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di tii nimi na ni, 13nibaakan ni ga ŋun ke titunwanbirdam bi ye nido yaab na mu ŋmann binaabitiib kitiŋ ki ponn ni bi bi na, le ki cha bi dooni ŋiwaa, ŋiwaa ŋi naa kee doon ŋi na, 14ni yaa ŋun bi len kina aabɔr kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki fiir lik, ki bee ti mbamɔm; ti yaa ye mbamɔn kan, 15ni kpaan ki ku binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, ni baawakor mu. Ni kuln kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk. 16Ni kuun ni kitiŋ ngbaan aawan mɔmɔk nan kpaan kinyaŋ ni, ki see kitiŋ ngbaan ni kaawan mɔmɔk, aan ni li ye kitork aapiin ki tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. Ni cha kitiŋ ngbaan gaar kina ki li ye ŋilangben; ubaa taa ki maa kitiŋ ngbaan daalbaadaal. 17-18Ni taa yoor tiwan ni Uwumbɔr bui ke ni bii, kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, ki li joo nibaa; nima kan, Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln ga sɔŋ, le u ga san nimi kinimbaak. Ni yaa joo waakaal i m joo tuk nimi din wee na, ki ŋani waah gee pu na kan, le u ga san nimi kinimbaak, ki cha ni pɔr pam, ke waah nan puu pu tii niyaajatiib na.

english_text:
Don't Mourn like Other Nations
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you are the Lord's children, so when you mourn for the dead, you must not cut yourselves or shave your forehead. 2 Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods.
Animals That Can Be Eaten
(Leviticus 11.1-47)
3 Don't eat any disgusting animals.
4-5You may eat the meat of cattle, sheep, and goats; wild sheep and goats; and gazelles, antelopes, and all kinds of deer. 6It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
7But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean. 8And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
9You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water, 10and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
11You can eat any clean bird. 12-18But don't eat the meat of any of the following birds: eagles, vultures, falcons, kites, ravens, ostriches, owls, sea gulls, hawks, pelicans, ospreys, cormorants, storks, herons, and hoopoes. You must not eat bats. 19Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them. 20However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
21 You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest
Moses said:
22 People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest. 23Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
24But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest, 25then sell this part and take the money there instead. 26When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too. 27And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
28Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse. 29The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
translation_text:
Ikpowiil aakoobil
1“Ni ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanib la. Nima pu na, nimi aanii yaa kpo kan, ni taa di kijuk gii niwon nibaa chee, ki mu taa kuu niyigbeer pu aayikpir lii, ke ŋinibol ŋiken aah ŋani pu na. 2Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le yeh nimi, uma le nyan nimi binib bimɔk bi dulnyaa wee ponn ni na, ke ni li ye waanib.
Baah ga li kɔ tiwakor ti na aabɔr
(Liifai Yaab 11.1-47)
3“Tiwan nimɔk Uwumbɔr bui ke ni kɔ na kan, ni taa ji ni. 4Ni ga ŋmaa ji tiwakor timina: inaa, ni ipiih, ni iŋoob, 5ni ipeeyun, ni timoor ni aapiih, ni timoor ni aaŋoob, ni ipeeman. 6Ni ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ tiwakor ti aataabuseen yakr, aan ti ŋmɔ timoor ki ki biir ti na. 7Tiwakor ni ipeel i aataabuseen yakr aan ti biir timoor ki ŋmɔ na baanja le ni ga ŋmaa ji ti. Ni taa ji laakumii, ni sandee, ni ŋitakpal ponn ni aalapol. Tiwan ngbaan le kɔ, ni biir timoor ki ŋmɔ, ki mu aataabuseen aa yakr. 8Ni taa li ji igbeer. I kɔ la; ba pu? itaabuseen yakr, le i mu aa biir timoor ki ŋmɔ. Ni taa li ji tiwakor ni ipeel imina, ki mu taa meeh yaawankpol.
9“Ni ga ŋmaa ji ijan i kpa ŋikon ni tipɔkr na. 10Tiwan nimɔk bi nnyun ni kaa kpa ŋikon ni tipɔkr na, ni taa ji ni, ni li nyi ke ni kɔ.
11“Ni ga ŋmaa ji inyoon i kaa kɔ na. 12-18Inyoon i kɔ ke ni taa ji i na sɔ: ŋikaagii, ni ifiin, ni kaasaa tiib, ni inyoon i chur iken na, ni inyoon i mu bi ke kaasaa tiib na, ni nangba tiib, ni ŋikakaa, ni taataa tiib, ni inyoon i naahn ineepɔɔn na, ni inyumuil, ni tinanjenn.
19“Tiwayukaan nimɔk kpa ifeen ki fiir na mu kɔ, ni taa ji ni. 20Tiwayukaan ni bi, kaa kɔ na kan, ni ga ŋmaa ji ni.
21“Ni taa ji kiwakork ki kpo kibaa pu na. Ni ga ŋmaa di ki tii biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na, bee ni ga ŋmaa di kooh tii biwɔwɔm biken. Nimi ma kan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le yeh nimi; ni ye waanib la.
“Ni taa di upiih, bee uŋoob aabiin ŋaa waabo.
Baah ga yakr baawan tii Uwumbɔr pu na
22“Ni yaa kon ki chee nimi aajikaar kan, ni faa ti ŋikpuk kipiik, kipiik, ki ti nyan tibaa kipiik mɔmɔk ponn ni, libiln mɔmɔk ponn ni. 23Ni yaa nyan ti ki di kpaan kan, ni di buen Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nyan nin chee ke ni li dooni u na, ki ti ji naah nyan njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan, ni nimi aawakor aajan aabim aajim, unimbiin ni. Ni ŋa kina aan ki li nyuŋni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 24Nimi ngem yaa bi ntim mu daa nin chee Uwumbɔr nyan ke ni li dooni u, aan naan ŋmaa tun waah tii nimi tijikaar ti na aageln buen kan, naah ga ŋa pu na sɔ: 25Ni di nimi aajikaar ti ni nyan ke ni ti tii Uwumbɔr na kooh, aan ki di ŋimombil ngbaan buen nin chee ni mɔmɔk dooni Uwumbɔr na. 26Ni di ŋimombil ngbaan daa naah ban tiwan ni na. Ni ga ŋmaa daa naah ban tiwan ni na. Ni ga ŋmaa daa kiwakork, bee ŋisubil aadaan, bee tiwan nimɔk ni ban na. Le nimi, ni nimi aamaal ga ŋmaa kpaan ki ji tiwan ngbaan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, ki li kpa mpopiin.
27“Ni taa suln Liifai yaab bi bi nimi aatim ponn ni na bɔr, ba pu? baa kpa bibaa aakpaakon. 28Ŋibin ŋitaa mɔmɔk kan, ni ti kuun ni naah nyan tijikaar ponn ni kipiik kibaa ke ni di tii Uwumbɔr na, ki nan di bil nimi aatim ni. 29Tijikaar ngbaan le Liifai yaab, ni biwɔwɔm, ni nkpobim, ni bikpopiib bi bi nimi aatim ni na mu ga li ji. (Liifai yaab aa kpa bibaa aakpaakon.) Nima chee le bi ga dan ki nan kan baah ban tijikaar ti na. Ni li ŋani kina, nima kan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa nimi aatuln mɔmɔk pu.

english_text:
Loans
(Leviticus 25.1-7)
Moses said:
1-2Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment. 3This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
4-6No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
7 After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money. 8Instead, be kind and lend them what they need. 9Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty. 10You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
11 There will always be some Israelites who are poor and needy. That's why I am commanding you to be generous with them.
Setting Slaves Free
(Exodus 21.1-11)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If any of you buy Israelites as slaves, you must set them free after six years. 13And don't just tell them they are free to leave— 14give them sheep and goats and a good supply of grain and wine. The more the Lord has given you, the more you should give them. 15I am commanding you to obey the Lord as a reminder that you were slaves in Egypt before he set you free. 16But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.” 17Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
18Don't complain when you have to set a slave free. After all, you got six years of service at half the cost of hiring someone to do the work.
First-Born Animals
(Leviticus 27.26,27; Numbers 18.15-18)
Moses said to Israel:
19 If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep. 20Instead, each year you must take the first-born of these animals to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped. You and your family will sacrifice them to the Lord and then eat them as part of a sacred meal.
21But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God. 22You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some. 23 But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
translation_text:
Libilolole aabɔr
(Liifai Yaab 25.1-7)
1“Libilolole ngbaan yaa nan jer aan nimi Israel yaab ubaa yaa joo uken aapɔln kan, umombidaan taa ki cha u pa. 2Naah ga ŋa pu na sɔ: Unii umɔk pinn ŋimombil tii uŋeen aatɔ Israel yoo na kan, u taa ki cha u pa, umombidaan taa ki cha u pa tii u. Uwumbɔr ubaa le bui ke ni taa cha bi pa. 3Binib bi ye biwɔwɔm na ma kan, ni ga ŋmaa cha bi pa nimi aamombil ŋi bi pinn na, ni taa cha nimi aanib ma pa.
4“Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, kitiŋ ki ponn ni u ban u di tii nimi na. 5Ni yaa joo waakaal mbamɔm ki ŋa maah mɔk nimi din wee pu na kan, nimi aanii ubaa aan li ye ugiin. 6Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu ke waah nan puu pu na. Ni ga li kpa ŋimombil ki pinn tii ŋitimbol pam, le nimi Israel yaab ma kan, naan buen ubaa chee ki ti pinn bi ŋimombil. Ni ga li joo ŋitimbol pam, le litimbol libaa aan ŋmaa joo nimi Israel yaab ma.
7“Israel aanii ubaa yaa ye ugiin, ki bi ntim mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban u di tii nimi na kibaa ponn ni kan, ni taa kpa kukumɔŋ ki yii ke naan ter u. 8Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki li kpa tibulchinn ki pinn tii u, ni ŋeer waah ban pu na. 9Ni taa yii ki bui ke libiln li ni ga di cha pinn bipɔndam na peen a, naan ki tii u nibaa. Ni taa cha tilandakbir kina aaboln koo nisui ni. Ni yaa yii ke naan tii udaan kan, u ga wii ki yin Uwumbɔr naah ŋa u tiwan ni na pu, le Uwumbɔr ga chuu si taani. 10Tiin u, ki taa li kpa tilandakbir, ni kukumɔŋ, le Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa saatuln mɔmɔk pu. 11Mbamɔn, n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, nimi Israel yaab ngem ga li ye bigiim, kaan li kpa, le ki ga li ban nterm. Nima pu na, m ban ke ni li kpa tibulchinn ki ter bi.
Baah ga ŋa baanaagbiib pu na aabɔr
(Nnyam 21.1-11)
12“Nimi Israel yaab ponn ni, uja, bee upii yaa di ubaa kooh tii si, ke u li ye saanaagbiija, aan ni yaa nan saa ŋibin ŋiloob kan, aa di u lii, u li cha. N‑yoonn mu ŋibin ŋilole ti fuu na kan, aa cha u li cha. 13N‑yoonn ngbaan, aa yaa di u lii kan, aa taa cha u li gaan iŋaalpeen. 14Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tinyoor ŋa saawan ni mɔmɔk pu na, aa li kpa tibulchinn ki nyan ni ponn ni tiwan tii u. Tiwan ngbaan ngem le ye tiwakor, ni njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan. 15Teer ke ni mu nan ye binaagbiib le Ijipt aatiŋ ni, le Nidindaan Uwumbɔr gaa nimi lii, nima pu le m joo nkaal ngbaan tuk ni mu.
16“Tɔ, nibaakan saanaagbiija ngbaan aan li ban ke u nya aado; u ga li gee aa ni saamaal sakpen, le ki ban ke u li bi aado. 17Kina pu na, di u buen saadichal aanaakook aabisamɔb ki ti saa chir utafal; le u li gur koo ki ye saanaagbiija ki ti saa waakundaal. Ni ŋa nimi aanaagbiib bi ye bipiib na mu kina. 18Aa yaa cha saanaagbiija buen kan, aa taa cha ni li muk si, ba pu? waah tun pu tii si ŋibin ŋiloob ŋi jer na ŋeer ututunn u gaal lipal na aapal nfum mulee pu. Ni li ŋani kina, le Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa nimi aatuln mɔmɔk pu.
Baawakor aajan aabim aabɔr
19“Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki nyan nimi aanaa ni ipiih ni iŋoob aajan aabim nibaa; ni taa di inaa ngbaan tun lituln libaa, ki taa chee ipiih ngbaan aakor mu. 20Ŋibin mɔmɔk kan, ni di i buen nin chee ni dooni Uwumbɔr na, ki ti kɔr i, aan nimi, ni nimi aamaal kpaan ŋmɔ i, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni. 21Tɔ, nibaa yaa ŋa tiwakor ngbaan, nibaakan ki yaa wɔb, bee ki jɔb, bee ni nibaa chee yaa bii kan, ni taa di ki toor kitork tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. 22Ni ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ tiwakor kina aaboln linampal. Unii u bi chain, bee waa bi chain na kan, ni mɔmɔk ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ tiwakor ngbaan ke naah ŋmɔ ipeeman pu na. 23Ni taa di naasin ŋa tijikaar ki ji, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki di mu kpir ke naah kpir nnyun pu na.

english_text:
Passover
(Exodus 12.1-20; Leviticus 23.4-8)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt. 2The Passover sacrifice must be a cow, a sheep, or a goat, and you must offer it at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. 3-4Eat all of the meat of the Passover sacrifice that same night. But don't serve bread made with yeast at the Passover meal. Serve the same kind of thin bread that you ate when you were slaves suffering in Egypt and when you had to leave Egypt quickly. As long as you live, this thin bread will remind you of the day you left Egypt.
For seven days following Passover, don't make any bread with yeast. In fact, there should be no yeast anywhere in Israel.
5Don't offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town where you happen to live. 6It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt. 7Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
8Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord.
The Harvest Festival
(Exodus 34.22; Leviticus 23.15-21)
Moses said to Israel:
9 Seven weeks after you start your grain harvest, 10-11go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. 12Remember that you used to be slaves in Egypt, so obey these laws.
The Festival of Shelters
(Leviticus 23.33-43; Numbers 29.12-38)
Moses said to Israel:
13-15 After you have finished the grain harvest and the grape harvest, take your sons and daughters and all your servants to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
The Lord will give you big harvests and make you successful in everything you do. You will be completely happy, so celebrate this festival in honor of the Lord your God.
Three Festivals at the Place of Worship
(Exodus 23.14-17)
Moses said:
16Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord. 17The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be.
Treat Everyone with Justice
Moses said to Israel:
18-19 After you are settled in the towns that you will receive from the Lord your God, the people in each town must appoint judges and other officers. Those of you that become judges must be completely fair when you make legal decisions, even if someone important is involved. Don't take bribes to give unfair decisions. Bribes keep people who are wise from seeing the truth and turn honest people into liars.
20People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you.
Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones
Moses said to Israel:
21 When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah. 22 And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
translation_text:
Lakr‑jer Aajim aabɔr
(Nnyam 12.1-20)
1“Ni nyuŋ Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki li ji Lakr‑jer Aajim, Abib aaŋmal ni; uŋmal ngbaan ni aanyeek kibaa, le u nan nyan nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 2Ni kuun buen nin chee ni kpaani ki dooni Uwumbɔr na, ki kɔr nimi aawakor ponn ni ubaa ki ŋa Lakr‑jer aajikaar aan ki nyuŋ Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. 3Ni yaa ban ni ji tijikaar ngbaan kan, ni taa ŋmɔ boroboro u kpa boroboro aanyɔk na. N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, ni taa ŋmɔ boroboro u kpa boroboro aanyɔk na ki ti saa iwiin ilole, ke naah nan ban ni nya Ijipt aatiŋ ni woween ki ŋman pu na. Ni li ŋmɔ boroboro ngbaan aaboln; ni ga li yin u ke falaa aaboroboro la. Ni li teer nwiin mundaal ni nan nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ki ti nan jin falaa ki ponn ni na, n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 4Iwiin ilole ngbaan aayoonn, nimi aatiŋ ni aanii ubaa taa li kpa boroboro aanyɔk udo. Tiwakor ti ni kɔr njan aawiin daal, kijook wɔb na, ni mɔmɔk ŋmɔ nimi aawakor aanann doo kinyeek ngbaan.
5-6“Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban u di kitiŋ ki tii nimi na, ni mɔmɔk kɔr Lakr‑jer aawakor ngbaan, nin chee ni kpaani ki dooni u na. Ni ŋa kina nwiin aah lir buyoonn na; n‑yoonn ngbaan le ni nan nya Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 7Ni ŋaa tinann ngbaan nin chee ni dooni Uwumbɔr na, ki kpaan ŋmɔ ti mɔmɔk nima, aan kitaak yaa woln kan, ni mɔmɔk gir kun nido. 8Iwiin iloob i gur na, ni li ŋmɔ boroboro u kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na, aan winlole daal kan, ni mɔmɔk kpaan ki kuun ti doon Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki taa tun lituln libaa liyaadaal ngbaan.
Lijikaacheel aajim aabɔr
(Nnyam 34.22; Liifai Yaab 23.15-21)
9“Buyoonn ni piin ki bi chee nimi aajikaabim na kan, ni piin likpaakool ngbaan ni, ki kahn ti saa ŋikpaakoo ŋilole aan ki ji Lijikaacheel Aajim. 10Ni ŋa kina ki nyuŋ Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ni li joo ni nimi aageehn aapiin, ni ŋeer waah ŋa tinyoor ki tii nimi pu na aapiin. 11Nimi, ni nimi aamaal, ni nimi aatutum, ni Liifai yaab, ni biwɔwɔm, ni nkpobim, ni bikpopiib bi koo nimi aatim pu na mɔmɔk li kpa mpopiin Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni. Ni mɔmɔk ŋa kina nin chee ni kpaani ki dooni Uwumbɔr na. 12Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki li joo nkaal ngbaan mbamɔm, ki taa suln ke ni mu nan ye binaagbiib le Ijipt aatiŋ ni.
Tikakar Aajim aabɔr
(Liifai Yaab 23.33-43)
13“N‑yoonn mu ni ti poi nimi aajikaabim ki nyan ŋisubil aanyun doo na aapuwɔb, ni toor Tikakar Aajim aatork mu iwiin ilole. 14Nimi, ni nimi aabim, ni nimi aatutum, ni Liifai yaab, ni biwɔwɔm, ni nkpobim, ni bikpopiib bi koo nimi aatim ni na kpaan ji mu, ki li mɔɔni, ki li kpa mpopiin. 15Ni ŋa kina aajim nin chee ni kuuni ki dooni Uwumbɔr na, ki ti saa iwiin ilole, ki nyuŋ Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. Uwumbɔr aah ŋa ni pu tinyoor, nimi aatuln ponn ni, ki cha ni chee tijikaar sakpen pu na, ni ŋa njim ngbaan, ki li kpa mpopiin kina pu.
16“Nimi aatiŋ ni aajab mɔmɔk kuun dan nin chee ni dooni Uwumbɔr na, ki nan doon u nfum mutaa libiln libaa ni: Lakr‑jer Aajim, ni Lijikaacheel Aajim, ni Tikakar Aajim aayoonn. Uja mɔk li joo ni ipiin waah ŋman pu na, 17ni ŋeer Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tinyoor ŋa waatuln li pu na.
Biyidam aatuln aabɔr
18“Nyan bibɔjirb, ni biyidam kaan ntim mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di tii nimi na mɔmɔk ni. Binib ngbaan li ji tibɔr, ki taa li kpa imaagann. 19Bi taa di inyamɔn ni imaagann ji tibɔr, ki mu taa li gaal igaŋgaŋlik, ba pu? ŋimombil ga cha binib bi kpa nlan ki bi mbamɔm na jɔb, le kaan ki li nyi ibamɔn. 20Ni li ŋani nimi aawan mɔmɔk mbamɔm, ki li si chob, nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa koo kitiŋ ki ni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban u di ki tii nimi na ni, aan ki li bi ki ponn ni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
21“Ni yaa ŋa nimi aatork aabimbiln kan, ni taa di idɔ ŋa lipiiwaal Asera ki di siin gbaŋ li, 22ki taa di ŋitakpal kuun bil ke ŋi li ye ŋiwaa, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa gee ŋiwaa aabɔr.

english_text:
Sacrifices That Have Something Wrong with Them
Moses said to Israel:
1If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted!
Put To Death People Who Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
2-3 The Lord your God is giving you towns to live in. But later, a man or a woman in your town may start worshiping other gods, or even the sun, moon, or stars. I have warned you not to worship other gods, because whoever worships them is disobeying the Lord and breaking the agreement he made with you. 4So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty. 5-7 But you will need two or three witnesses—one witness isn't enough to prove a person guilty.
Get rid of those who are guilty of such evil. Take them outside your town gates and everyone must stone them to death. But the witnesses must be the first to throw stones.
Difficult Cases
Moses said to Israel:
8-12It may be difficult to find out the truth in some legal cases in your town. You may not be able to decide if someone was killed accidentally or murdered. Or you may not be able to tell whether an injury or some property damage was done by accident or on purpose. If the case is too difficult, take it to the court at the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped.
This court will be made up of one judge and several priests who serve at the Lord's altar. They will explain the law to you and give you their decision about the case. Do exactly what they tell you, or you will be put to death. 13When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court.
The King
Moses said:
14 People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
15Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
16 The king should not have many horses, especially those from Egypt. The Lord has said never to go back there again. 17 And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
18The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe. So, as soon as anyone becomes king, he must go to the priests and write out a copy of these laws while they watch. 19Each day the king must read and obey these laws, so that he will learn to worship the Lord with fear and trembling 20and not think that he's better than everyone else.
If the king completely obeys the Lord's commands, he and his descendants will rule Israel for many years.
translation_text:
1“Kiwakork yaa kaa ŋan, kaa kpa laafee kan, ni taa di ki toor kitork tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. Waa gee kina.
2“Nibaakan, ni ga ŋun ke nimi aatiŋ kibaa ponn ni uja, bee upii tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir ki bii waakaal, 3ki dooni ŋiwaa, bee nwiin, bee uŋmal, bee iŋmabi, ki yenn Uwumbɔr chee. 4Ni yaa ŋun kina aabɔr kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki lik tibɔr ngbaan ponn ni mbamɔm. Ni yaa ye mbamɔn ke titunwanbir ngbaan sil bi Israel aatiŋ ni kan, 5ni nyan udaan ngbaan kitiŋ aagbaan aan ki mee ŋitakpal ku u. 6Ni yaa kpa seeraadam bilee, bee ki jer kina, aan bi len ke tibɔr ngbaan gbii kan, ni ku u. Tɔ, ni yaa ye seeraadaan ubaa baanja kan, ni taa ku u. 7Ni cha seeraadam ngbaan pue mee u ŋitakpal, aan nimi bi gur na mu kpee bi pu, ki ku u. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga nyan titunwanbir ngbaan ni chee.
8“Nibaakan, tibɔr tibaa ga li pɔɔ, le bibɔjirb bi bi itingbaan ni na aan ŋmaa toor ti. Ni yaa ye nkun, bee kijaak, bee ubaa yaa tii uken titotonn, bee ubaa yaa gaa uken aawangol kan, ni di kina aabɔr buen nin chee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nyan aan ni mɔmɔk dooni u na, 9ki di tibɔr ngbaan ŋa bitotoorb bi ye Liifai yaab na, ni ubɔjir u bi lituln ni n‑yoonn ngbaan na aaŋaal ni. Bima le ga lik tibɔr ngbaan ni. 10Bi yaa lik ti ponn ni, ki bui nimi pu na kan, ni ŋa baah len pu na. 11Ni dii baah siin pu na mbamɔm, aan ki ŋa baah mɔk nimi pu na, ki ti doo. 12Unii u yii ubɔjir, bee utotoor u bi lituln ni liyaadaal ngbaan na aamɔb kan, ni ku u. Ni yaa nyan udaan ngbaan kina kan, ni ga nyan kina aatunwanbir, Israel aatiŋ ni. 13Unii umɔk ga ŋun tibɔr ngbaan na ga san ijawaan, le kaan kii ke u ŋa kina aatuln.
Baah ga dii pu ki nyan ubɔr na
14“Ni yaa ŋmaa nyaŋ ki gaa kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban u di tii nimi na aan ki kal doo kan, ni ga ban ubɔr ke ntim muken aah kpa bibɔrb pu na. 15Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki cha Uwumbɔr aah nyan unii u ke u li ye ubɔr na kal nnaan aajal pu. Ni cha nimi Israel yaab ponn ni ubaa ji nnaan ngbaan, u taa li ye uwɔwɔnja. 16Ubɔr ngbaan taa li kpa itaan sakpen ki di tii waajab, u mu taa cha bi buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ke u ti daa itaan; ba pu? Uwumbɔr bui ke waanib ponn ni ubaa taa ki gir buen kitiŋ ngbaan ni. 17Ubɔr ngbaan taa li kpa bipiib sakpen; ba pu? bi ga cha u yenn Uwumbɔr chee; u mu taa li ban tikunabr, ni salmaa ke u ŋa uwankpadaan. 18U yaa ŋa ubɔr kan, u pɔɔn ubaa ki li kpa Uwumbɔr aakaal, ni waamɔkm ni nyan ni bitotoorb Liifai yaab aagbaŋ ni na. 19U cha kigbaŋ ngbaan li bi u chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ki li karni ki, ki ti saa waamɔfal aadoon. Nima kan, u ga bee waah ga ŋa pu ki li nyuŋni Uwumbɔr ki kii waamɔb mbamɔm na. 20Nima kan, waan dakl ke u jer Israel yaab biken, ki yii Uwumbɔr aasan. Nima kan, u ga yunn nnaan ngbaan ponn ni, le uyaabitiib ga li joo nnaan ngbaan ki yunn pam.

english_text:
Special Privileges for Priests and Levites
(Numbers 18.8-32)
Moses said to Israel:
1The people of the Levi tribe, including the priests, will not receive any land. Instead, they will receive part of the sacrifices that are offered to the Lord, 2 because he has promised to provide for them in this way.
3When you sacrifice a bull or sheep, the priests will be given the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach. 4In addition, they will receive the first part of your grain harvest and part of your first batches of wine and olive oil. You must also give them the first wool that is cut from your sheep each year. 5Give these gifts to the priests, because the Lord has chosen them and their descendants out of all the tribes of Israel to be his special servants at the place of worship.
6Any Levite can leave his hometown, and go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, 7and then be a special servant of the Lord there, just like all the other Levites. 8Some Levites may have money from selling family possessions, and others may not. But all Levites serving at the place of worship will receive the same amount of food from the sacrifices and gifts brought by the people.
Don't Do Disgusting Things
Moses said to Israel:
9Soon you will go into the land that the Lord your God is giving you. The nations that live there do things that are disgusting to the Lord, and you must not follow their example. 10-11 Don't sacrifice your son or daughter. And don't try to use any kind of magic or witchcraft to tell fortunes or to cast spells or to talk with spirits of the dead.
12The Lord is disgusted with anyone who does these things, and that's why he will help you destroy the nations that are in the land. 13 Never be guilty of doing any of these disgusting things!
A Prophet like Moses
Moses said to Israel:
14You will go in and take the land from nations that practice magic and witchcraft. But the Lord your God won't allow you to do those things. 15 Instead, he will choose one of your own people to be a prophet just like me, and you must do what that prophet says. 16You were asking for a prophet the day you were gathered at Mount Sinai and said to the Lord, “Please don't let us hear your voice or see this terrible fire again—if we do, we will die!”
17Then the Lord told me:
Moses, they have said the right thing. 18So when I want to speak to them, I will choose one of them to be a prophet like you. I will give my message to that prophet, who will tell the people exactly what I have said. 19 Since the message comes from me, anyone who doesn't obey the message will have to answer to me.
20But if I haven't spoken, and a prophet claims to have a message from me, you must kill that prophet, and you must also kill any prophet who claims to have a message from another god.
Moses said to Israel:
21You may be asking yourselves, “How can we tell if a prophet's message really comes from the Lord?” 22You will know, because if the Lord says something will happen, it will happen. And if it doesn't, you will know that the prophet was falsely claiming to speak for the Lord. Don't be afraid of any prophet whose message doesn't come from the Lord.
translation_text:
Bitotoorb aawan aah ye ni na
1“Liifai aanibol, bi ye bitotoorb na, aan li kpa ikpaakon ke ŋinibol ŋiken na. Baah ga li ji tiwan ni na le ye ipiin, ni kitork ki binib joo ni nan tii Uwumbɔr na. 2Bi taa li kpa ikpaakon ke biken aah kpa pu na, baayimɔɔn le ye ke bi ye Uwumbɔr aatotoorb ke waah nan puu tipuur pu na.
3“N‑yoonn mu ni ti di kiwakork toor kitork na kan, ni di kibook, ni mmɔkpaween, ni lipuul tii bitotoorb. 4Ni di nimi aajan aajikaar tii bi, nima le ye njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan, ni ipiih aakor. 5Uwumbɔr le nyan nimi aanibol ponn ni Liifai yaab, ke bi li ye waatotoorb ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
