61-62The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages:
Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi.
The Jebusites
63 The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_text:
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ ki tii Juda aanibol na
1Kitiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii Juda aanibol na le paa na:
Kitiŋ ngbaan nan yoor kina ki ti saa ŋŋangii wɔb, ki di ti ker Sinn Aateersakpiin aaŋangii wɔb, ki di ti naa Edom aatiŋ mɔk. 2Kaanaanmɔk, ŋŋangii wɔb, nan yoor N‑yaan Aanyusakpem aaŋangii wɔb, 3ki di nyan ŋŋangii wɔb, Akrabim Aajool aasan chee, ki di buen Sinn Aateersakpiin ni. Kitiŋ ngbaan yoor ki dii Kades Banea aatiŋ ni, ŋŋangii wɔb, ki kpak Hesronn aatiŋ kina, ki ti ker Adar aatiŋ ni, ki fenn di kpaa Kaka wɔb, 4ki di buen Asmonn aatiŋ wɔb, le ki dii mbun mu bi Ijipt aatiŋ mɔk na, ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem nin chee kitiŋ mɔk doo na. Juda yaab aatiŋ, ŋŋangii wɔb aanaanmɔk le na.
5Liwipuul wɔb aanaanmɔk le nan ye N‑yaan Aanyusakpem, ki yoor kina ki dii nnyusakpem ngbaan aagbaan, ki ti saa nin chee Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl puu koo mu ponn ni na.
Kitiŋ ngbaan aah piin nin chee ŋŋangan wɔb na yoor Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aah doo nin chee na, 6ki yoor kina ki ti ker Bef Hogla aatiŋ mɔk, le ki dii buen kidunduŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann aafataŋ chee na aaŋangan wɔb, le ki dii kina buen Bohann, u nan ye Rubenn aajapɔɔn na, aatakpal chee, 7ki yoor ni Tibɔbir Aafataŋ mɔk, ki ti nyan Debir aatiŋ pu, le ki fenn ŋŋangan wɔb ki di kpaa Gilgal aatiŋ, ki ni Adumim Aajool Aasan lik tɔb na, ki bi kifataŋ aaŋangii wɔb na, le ki yoor kina ki buen Ensemes aanyunbun wɔb, ki nyan nima ti pii Enn Rogel, 8le ki bɔ nyan Hinom Aafataŋ ki bi ligongoln li Jebus yaab aatiŋ Jerusalem bi li paab na aaŋangii wɔb, le kimɔk ki yoor kina ki di dii ligongoln li bi Hinom Aafataŋ liwilir wɔb na paab, Refaim Aafataŋ aaŋangan wɔb, 9ki nyan nima chee, ki dii kina buen Neftoa Aanyunbun chee, le ki ti ker ntim mu bi Efronn Aajool chee na. Nima chee le ki fenn kpaa Baala aatiŋ ni; bi ki yin ki ke Kiriaf Jearim aatiŋ. 10Nima chee le ki mann gonn Baala aatiŋ liwilir wɔb, ki fenn kpaa ŋigongon aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Edom na, le ki di dii buen Jearim, bee Kesalonn, Aajool aaŋangan wɔb, ki di sunn taab ki ti ker Bef Semes, le ki dii Timna aatiŋ ni. 11Kitiŋ ngbaan aanaanmɔk ki yoor kina, ki dii buen ligongoln li bi Ekronn aaŋangan wɔb na, ki fenn kpaa Sikeronn, ki dii Baala Aajool aataab, le ki ti ker Jamnia aatiŋ, ki nan ti doo Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem chee la. 12Nima chee le nan ye kitiŋ ngbaan aawilir wɔb mɔk.
Kitiŋ ngbaan aah yoor ki ti ker nimɔk na, Juda aanibol aamaal mɔmɔk nan bi kima ponn ni la.
Kaleb aah nan nyaŋ Hebronn ni Debir aatim pu na
(Bibɔjirb 1.11-15)
13Uwumbɔr aah nan bui Josua ke u ŋa pu na, u nan di Juda aatiŋ aapepel nibaa chee tii Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb, u nan ye Juda aanibol aanii ubaa na. Bi nan di Hebronn aatiŋ, ki nan ye Aba u nan ye ŋiwɔk Anak yaab aate na aatiŋ le tii u. 14Kaleb nan jenn Anak aamaal mɔmɔk nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni, bi nan ye Sesai yaab, ni Ahimann yaab, ni Talmai yaab aanib la. 15U nan nyan nima chee le ki buen ti lir Debir aanib pu. Njan bi nan yin kitiŋ ngbaan ke Kiriaf Sefer aatiŋ la. 16Kaleb nan bui ke, “Uja u ga ŋmaa to butɔb ki nyaŋ Kiriaf Sefer aatiŋ na kan, m ga di mbisal Aksa tii udaan ngbaan u di u ŋa upuu.” 17Le Kaleb aakpel u bi nan yin u ke Kenas na aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u mu ke Otniel na, le nan nyaŋ kitiŋ ngbaan, le Kaleb di ubisal Aksa tii u, le u yoor u ki di ŋa upuu. 18Waah kunn u bundaal na, le Otniel bui upuu Aksa ke u mee ute kitiŋ ki ŋan na. Le Aksa buen ute chee, ki sunn ubon pu, le Kaleb baa u ke u ban ba. 19Le u giin bui u ke, “M ban kitiŋ ki kpa nnyun na la. Saah di kitiŋ ki tii mi na, ki bi nteer pu la.” Nima pu le Kaleb nan di paacham ni taab aanyunbun aatiŋ na tii u.
Ntim mu ye Juda aanibol aatim na
20Ntim mu Juda aanibol nan kan aan mu ye baatim na sɔ: 21ntim mu nan bi ŋŋangii wɔb ki nan ye baatim, ki nan bi Edom aatiŋ mɔk na le nan ye Kabseel, ni Eder, ni Jagur, 22ni Kina, ni Dimona, ni Adada, 23ni Kedes, ni Hasor, ni Itnann, 24ni Sif, ni Telem, ni Bealof, 25ni Hasor Hadata, ni Keriof Hesronn ki bi ki yin ki ke Hasor na, 26ni Amam, ni Sema, ni Molada, 27ni Hasar Gada, ni Hesmonn, ni Bef Pelet, 28ni Hasar Sual, ni Beerseba, ni Bisiotia, 29ni Baala, ni Iyim, ni Esem, 30ni Eltolad, ni Kesil, ni Homa, 31ni Siklag, ni Madmana, ni Sansana, 32ni Lebaof, ni Silim, ni Ayinn, ni Rimonn aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa moninko ni muwae la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
33Ntim mu nan bi ŋigongon aataab na le nan ye Estaol, ni Sora, ni Asna, 34ni Sanoa, ni Enn Ganim, ni Tapua, ni Enam, 35ni Jamuf, ni Adulam, ni Soko, ni Aseka, 36ni Saarayim, ni Aditayim, ni Gedera, ni Gederotayim aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa kipiik ni munaa, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
37Ntim mu nan ki kpee na le nan ye Senann, ni Hadasa, ni Migdal Gad, 38ni Dileann, ni Mispa, ni Jokteel, 39ni Lakis, ni Boskaf, ni Eglonn, 40ni Kabonn, ni Lamam, ni Kitlis, 41ni Gederof, ni Bef Dagonn, ni Naama, ni Makeda aatim: ntim ngbaan nan ti saa kipiik ni muloob la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
42Mu nan ki kpee na le ye Libna, ni Eter, ni Asann, 43ni Ifta, ni Asna, ni Nesib, 44ni Keila, ni Aksib, ni Maresa aatim: mu nan ti saa ntim muwae la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
45Ekronn aatiŋ mu nan bi, ki kpee itingbaan ni ntim mu bi gbɔk ki na, 46ni ntim mɔmɔk ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk Asdod aatiŋ na, ki yoor Ekronn mɔk ki ti ker Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem.
47Ntim mu nan ki bi na le nan ye Asdod ni Gasa aatim, ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na, le ki yoor kina ki ti ker mbun mu ye Ijipt aatiŋ mɔk na, ni Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem aagbaan.
48Ŋigongon aatiŋ, ni ntim mu nan bi nima chee na le nan ye Samir, ni Jatir, ni Soko, 49ni Dana, ni Kiriaf Sefer ki bi ki yin ki ke Debir na, 50ni Anab, ni Estemoa, ni Anim, 51ni Gosenn, ni Holonn, ni Gilo aatim: mu nan ti saa kipiik ni kibaa la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
52Ntim mu nan ki bi na le nan ye Arab, ni Duma, ni Esann, 53ni Janim, ni Bef Tapua, ni Afeka, 54ni Humta, ni Hebronn, ni Sior aatim: mu nan ti saa ntim muwae la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
55Ntim mu nan ki bi na le nan ye Maonn, ni Kamel, ni Sif, ni Juta, 56ni Jesreel, ni Jokdeam, ni Sanoa, 57ni Kayinn, ni Gibea, ni Timna aatim: mu nan ti saa ntim kipiik la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
58Ntim mu nan ki bi na le nan ye Halul, ni Bef Sur, ni Gedor, 59ni Maaraf, ni Bef Anof, ni Eltekonn aatim: mu nan ti saa ntim muloob la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
60Ntim mu nan ki bi na le nan ye Kiriaf Baal ki bi ki yin ki ke Kiriaf Jearim na, ni Raba aatim: mu nan ti saa ntim mulee la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
61Ntim mu nan bi nteersakpiin aatiŋ ni na le nan ye Bef Araba, ni Midinn, ni Sekaka, 62ni Nibsann, ni N‑yaan Aatiŋ, ni Enn Gedi: mu nan ti saa ntim muloob la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
63Juda aanib aa nan ŋmaa jenn nyan Jebus yaab bi nan bi Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni na. Jebus yaab laa beenin bi nima, Juda aanib chee.

english_text:
Ephraim's Land
1-4Ephraim and Manasseh are the two tribes descended from Joseph, and the following is a description of the land they received. The southern border of their land started at the Jordan River east of the spring at Jericho. From there it went west through the desert up to the hill country around Bethel. From Bethel it went to Luz and then to the border of the Archites in Ataroth. It continued west down to the land that belonged to the Japhlet clan, then went on to Lower Beth-Horon, Gezer, and the Mediterranean Sea.
5The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon 6-8and the Mediterranean Sea. Their northern border started on the east at Janoah, curved a little to the north, then came back south to Michmethath and Tappuah, where it followed the Kanah Gorge west to the Mediterranean Sea.
The eastern border started on the north near Janoah and went between Janoah on the southwest and Taanath-Shiloh on the northeast. Then it went south to Ataroth, Naarah, and on as far as the edge of the land that belonged to Jericho. At that point it turned east and went to the Jordan River. The clans of Ephraim received this region as their tribal land. 9Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
10 Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_text:
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ ki tii Efraim, ni Manase aanibol ligeln pu na
1Kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangii wɔb aanaanmɔk ki bi nan yakr tii Josef aamaal na, nan piin Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee ki bi Jeriko aatiŋ chee, Jeriko aanyunbun aawipuul wɔb, ki dii kina ti nyan nteersakpiin aatiŋ pu, ki yoor ni Jeriko mɔk ki buen ŋigongon aatiŋ ni, ki dii kina ti nyan Betel aatiŋ ni, 2ki yoor Betel aatiŋ mɔk ki di buen Lus aatiŋ mɔk, ki ti saa Atarof Adar aatiŋ, nin chee Ak yaab bi na, 3ki yoor kina buen liwilir wɔb, nin chee Jaflet yaab bi na, ki dii kina ti nyan Bef Horonn Aataab wɔb, le ki dii kina ti ker Geser aatiŋ ni, ki di ti doo Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem wɔb.
4Le Josef aamaal mu nan ye Efraim, ni Manase aanibol ligeln na gaa kitiŋ kee, ke ki li ye baatiŋ.
Efraim aanibol aatiŋ
5Kitiŋ ki nan ye Efraim aanibol aatiŋ na le na: baatiŋ mɔk nan yoor ni Atarof Adar, liwipuul wɔb, ki ti ker Bef Horonn aapaacham wɔb, 6le ki yoor nima chee ki ti ker Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk. Mikmetaf aatiŋ nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangan wɔb la. Liwipuul nima chee aanaanmɔk nan pɔr ki di kpaa Taanaf Silo aatiŋ wɔb, le ki jer nima ki di toŋ liwipuul wɔb, ki ti saa Janoa aatiŋ ni, 7le ki nyan Janoa nima ki di ti ker Atarof, ni Naara aatim mɔk, ki di ti fuu Jeriko aatiŋ ni, le ki ti doo Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee. 8Kitiŋ ngbaan nan ki nyan Tapua aatiŋ chee, ki di toŋ liwilir wɔb ki ti fuu Kana aanyunbun wɔb, le ki ti doo Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk. Kitiŋ ngbaan le bi nan di tii Efraim aanibol aamaal ke ki li ye baatiŋ, 9ki nan kpee ntim ni itingbaan i mu nan bi Manase aatiŋ ngbaan ponn ni aan bi yakr tii Efraim yaab mu na. 10Baa nan jenn nyan Kanaann yaab bi nan bi Geser aatiŋ ponn ni na, kina pu na, Kanaann yaab ngbaan kpaan bi Efraim yaab chee le ki nan saa din, bi nan tee muk bi ke bi li tun lituln ke binaagbiib na.

english_text:
Manasseh's Land West of the Jordan River
1-6 Manasseh was Joseph's oldest son, and Machir was Manasseh's oldest son. Machir had a son named Gilead, and some of his descendants had already received the regions of Gilead and Bashan because they were good warriors. The other clans of the Manasseh tribe descended from Gilead's sons Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. The following is a description of the land they received.
Hepher's son Zelophehad did not have any sons, but he did have five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. One day the clans that were descendants of Zelophehad's five daughters went to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders of Israel. The people of these clans said, “The Lord told Moses to give us land just as he gave land to our relatives.”
Joshua followed the Lord's instructions and gave land to these five clans, as he had given land to the five clans that had descended from Hepher's brothers. So Manasseh's land west of the Jordan River was divided into ten parts.
7The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring. 8The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
9-10Then the border went west to the Kanah Gorge and ran along the northern edge of the gorge to the Mediterranean Sea. The land south of the gorge belonged to Ephraim. And even though there were a few towns that belonged to Ephraim north of the gorge, the land north of the gorge belonged to Manasseh.
The western border of Manasseh was the Mediterranean Sea, and the tribe shared a border with the Asher tribe on the northwest and with the Issachar tribe on the northeast.
11Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands:
Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
12 But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them. 13When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave.
Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
14One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
15Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
16“Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
17“Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful, 18so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_text:
Manase aanibol ligeln li nan bi liwilir wɔb na aatiŋ
1Bi nan di kitiŋ ngbaan aapepel li bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb na tii Josef aajapɔpol u bi nan yin u ke Manase na aanibol ligeln libaa aamaal. Gilead aate u bi nan yin u ke Makir na, uma le nan ye Manase aajapɔpol, u nan ye uja u ŋmaa to likumbool na la, nima pu na, Gilead aatiŋ, ni Basann aatiŋ ki nan bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔdapuul liwipuul wɔb na le bi nan di tii u, 2le ki di kitiŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb na tii Manase aanibol aamaal ligeln li gur na. Baayimbil le paa na: Abieser, ni Helek, ni Asriel, ni Sekem, ni Hefer, ni Semida. Bi mɔmɔk nan ye Josef aajapɔɔn Manase aajapɔtiib la. Bi nan ye bidichajoob la. 3Selofehad nan ye Hefer aajapɔɔn la, le Hefer mu nan ye Gilead aajapɔɔn, le Gilead mu nan ye Makir aajapɔɔn, le Makir mu nan ye Manase aajapɔɔn, le Selofehad ma aa nan kpa ubijabo, u nan ma mpiibim ŋmeen la. Ubisatiib ngbaan aayimbil le paa na: Mala, ni Nowa, ni Hogla, ni Milka, ni Tirsa. 4Bi nan buen utotoor Eleasar, ni Nunn aajapɔɔn Josua, ni Israel yaab aaninkpiib biken chee, le ki ti bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke u tii timi kitiŋ, ke baah tii timi aamaal bi ye bijab na pu na, ki li ye timi aatiŋ.” Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr aah len pu na, bi nan tii Selofehad aabisatiib ngbaan mɔmɔk mu kitiŋ, ke baah tii baamaal aajab mɔmɔk kitiŋ pu na. 5Nima pu le Manase aanibol ma nan kan kitiŋ ngbaan nfum kipiik pu, ki kpee Gilead ni Basann aatim mu bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul wɔb na pu, 6ba pu? bi nan yakr kitiŋ ngbaan tii baamaal bi ye mbijabim, ni mpiibim na mu la. Bi nan di Gilead aatiŋ le tii Manase aanibol aamaal bi gur na.
7Manase aatiŋ mɔk nan yoor Aser aatiŋ ni, ki ti ker Mikmetaf ki bi Sekem aawipuul wɔb na. Le kimɔk nan ki yoor ŋŋangii wɔb ki kpee binib bi bi Enn Tapua na aatim mu. 8Kitiŋ ki mann gonn Tapua aatiŋ na nan ye Manase aanibol aamaal aatiŋ la, le Tapua aatiŋ kibaa nan ye Efraim aamaal aatiŋ. 9Kaanaanmɔk nan yoor kina ki ti ker Kana aanyunbun chee. Ntim mu nan bi nnyunbun ngbaan aaŋangii wɔb na nan ye Efraim aatim; mbamɔn, ntim ngbaan mu nan bi Manase aatingbaln ponn ni la. Manase aatiŋ mɔk nan yoor kina ki dii nnyunbun ngbaan aaŋangan wɔb, le ki nan doo Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk. 10Efraim aamaal le nan yeh ŋŋangii wɔb, le Manase aamaal mu nan yeh ŋŋangan wɔb, le Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem bi kitiŋ ngbaan aawilir wɔb. Aser aatiŋ nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan ŋŋangan ni liwilir aakaasisik ni, le Isakar aatiŋ nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan ŋŋangan ni liwipuul aakaasisik ni. 11Isakar ni Aser aakaasisik ni na, Manase le nan yeh Bef Sann, ni Ibleam aatim mu bi nima chee na, ki kpee ntim mu mann gonn nima na, ni Dor aatiŋ ki bi gbɔk nnyusakpem aagbaan na, ni Endor, ni Taanak, ni Megido aatim, ni ntim mu mann gonn mu na. 12Ibamɔn, Manase aanib ngbaan aa nan ŋmaa jenn nyan Kanaann yaab bi nan bi ntim ngbaan ni na, kina pu na, Kanaann yaab ngbaan laa beenin koo nima chee. 13Hali n‑yoonn mu Israel yaab nan moo pɔɔk na, baa nan jenn nyan Kanaann yaab mɔmɔk doo. Israel yaab nan tee muk bi le bi tun lituln tii bi.
Efraim aamaal ni Manase aamaal ligeln nan mee kitiŋ ki kpee
14Josef aamaal nan bui Josua ke, “Ba ŋa aa di kitiŋ ngbaan lipepel libaa baanja di tii timi? Uwumbɔr ŋa tinyoor ŋa ti pu, le ti pɔr pam.”
15Le Josua giin bui bi ke, “Ni yaa pɔr ki wiir sakpen le Efraim aagongon aatiŋ aa ŋeer nimi kan, ni li cha kipɔɔk ni, ki ti toor mpaan Peris yaab, ni Refa yaab aatim ni, ki tii nibaa.”
16Le bi giin bui u ke, “Ŋigongon aatiŋ ngbaan aa wiir ki ga fuu timi, le Kanaann yaab bi bi kifataŋ ni na: bi bi Bef Sann aatiŋ ni na, ni bi bi ki mann gonn ki na, ni bi bi Jesreel aafataŋ ni na kpa tikur aatɔroku mam la.”
17Le Josua bui binib bi ye Efraim aamaal, ni Manase aamaal bi bi liwilir wɔb na ke, “Mbamɔn, ni wiir pam le ki mu kpa mpɔɔn sakpen. Ni ŋan ke ti kpee nimi kitiŋ. 18Ŋigongon aatiŋ ngbaan ga li ye nimi yaan. Mbamɔn, ki ye kichook la, ni ga ŋmaa gaa ki, ki maa nima, ki di ki mɔmɔk ŋa nimi aatiŋ. Kanaann yaab ma kan, baah kpa tikur aatɔroku mam ki pɔɔ sakpen pu na, ni ga ŋmaa jenn nyan bi.”

english_text:
Joshua Gives Out the Rest of the Land
1After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent. 2There were still seven tribes without any land, 3-7so Joshua told the people:
The Judah tribe has already settled in its land in the south, and the Joseph tribes have settled in their land in the north. The tribes of Gad, Reuben, and East Manasseh already have the land that the Lord's servant Moses gave them east of the Jordan River. And the people of Levi won't receive land like the other tribes. Instead, they will serve the Lord as priests.
But the rest of you haven't done a thing to take over any land. The Lord God who was worshiped by your ancestors has given you the land, and now it's time to go ahead and settle there.
Seven tribes still don't have any land. Each of these tribes should choose three men, and I'll send them to explore the remaining land. They will divide it into seven regions, write a description of each region, and bring these descriptions back to me. I will find out from the Lord our God what region each tribe should get.
8Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
9The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh. 10Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided.
Benjamin's Land
11Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north. 12Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert. 13-14From there it went to Luz, which is now called Bethel. The border ran along the ridge south of Luz, then went to Ataroth-Orech and on as far as the mountain south of Lower Beth-Horon. At that point it turned south and became the western border. It went as far south as Kiriath-Baal, a town in Judah now called Kiriath-Jearim.
15Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring. 16From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
17At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe. 18The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley. 19Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River. 20The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border.
These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
21-24One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
25-28In the other region there were the following 14 towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town.
These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_text:
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ ki gur na pu na
1Baah nan nyaŋ ki gaa kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk doo na, le Israel yaab mɔmɔk kuun buen Silo aatiŋ ni, ki ti ŋa Uwumbɔr Aabool nima chee. 2Israel aanibol ŋilole le nan gur kaa kee kan baatim. 3Nima pu na, Josua nan bui Israel aanib ngbaan ke, “N‑yoonn mulamu aan ni ka kii ke ni buen ti yakr kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na, di tii nimi na? 4Ni nyan bijab bitataa ŋinibol ngbaan mɔmɔk ni, le m ga tun bi aan bi chuun ki dii kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki yakr ki tii bi mɔmɔk, baah ban pu na. Le bi ga gir ni m chee ki nan tuk mi baah yakr ki pu na. 5Bi yakr kitiŋ ngbaan ŋeer ŋiker ŋilole aapepel, Juda aanibol ga li bi kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangii wɔb la, le Josef aanibol ga li bi ŋŋangan wɔb. 6Ni ŋmee naah ban ni yakr kitiŋ pu na ŋiker ŋilole ŋa kigbaŋ ni, aan ki li joo ni m chee. Le m ga too inaan ki baa Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aan u mɔk mi linibol mɔmɔk ni laapepel. 7Mbamɔn, Liifai yaab ma kan, maan yakr kitiŋ kibaa tii bi ke nimi bi gur na aah ga kan pu na, ba pu? biyaan le ye ke bi ye Uwumbɔr aatotoorb. Gad, ni Rubenn, ni Manase aanibol ligeln bi bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul na mu kan kitiŋ ki bi liwipuul wɔb ngbaan na. Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses le nan di ki tii bi.”
8Bijab ngbaan nan buen bi ti yakr kitiŋ ngbaan, Josua aah mɔk bi pu na. U nan bui bi ke, “Ni buen kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ni, ki geei ki ŋiker ŋiker aan ki gir ni m chee man. Silo aatiŋ kee ponn ni, le m ga too inaan ki baa Uwumbɔr u mɔk mi maah ga yakr kitiŋ ngbaan pu na.” 9Nima pu na, bijab ngbaan nan buen kitiŋ ngbaan ni le ki ti ŋa ni mɔmɔk, ki ŋmee baah yakr ki ŋipepel ŋilole pu na, le ki ŋmee ntim ngbaan aayimbil ŋa ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni, le ki gir buen Josua chee, Silo aatiŋ ni. 10Le Josua too inaan ki baa Uwumbɔr, le u mɔk Josua waah ga di nin chee tii ŋinibol ngbaan mɔmɔk na.
Baah nan yakr nin chee tii Benjaminn aanibol na
11Bi nan pue yakr njan aatiŋ tii Benjaminn aamaal la. Baatiŋ nan dɔ Juda ni Josef aamaal aatim aakaasisik ni la. 12Ŋŋangan wɔb, baatiŋ aanaanmɔk le nan yoor ni Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl mɔk, ki di kina ti ker Jeriko aatiŋ aaŋangan wɔb, le ki nyan nima ki di buen liwilir wɔb, ki di dii ŋigongon aatiŋ ponn ni ki ti kar Bef Afenn aateersakpiin pu. 13Le kimɔk ki yoor kina ki di sunn buen Lus, bee Betel, aaŋangii wɔb, le ki di ti nyan Atarof Adar aatiŋ ni, ki di dii lijool libaa paab, li bi Bef Horonn Aataab aaŋangii wɔb. 14Kaanaanmɔk nan di kpaa niyayan, le ki fenn nyan ni lijool ngbaan aawilir wɔb ki di dii ŋŋangii wɔb, ki buen Kiriaf Baal, bee Kiriaf Jearim, ki nan ye Juda yaab aatiŋ la. Lipepel ngbaan le nan ye kitiŋ ngbaan aawilir wɔb. 15Le ŋŋangii wɔb aapepel mɔk nan piin Kiriaf Jearim aamɔgben mɔk, le ki di buen Neftoa aanyunbun chee, 16le ki ki di kina buen lijool li bi Hinom Aafataŋ chee, Refaim Aafataŋ aaŋangan wɔb na, le ki ki bɔ dii Hinom Aafataŋ aaŋangii wɔb, Jebus yaab aadunduŋ aaŋangii wɔb, le ki buen Enn Rogel aatiŋ chee, 17le ki fenn nima chee ki buen ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti fuu Enn Semes, le ki buen Gelilof aatiŋ ki tok Adumim Aasan na, le ki ki yoor nima ki buen Rubenn aajapɔɔn Bohann Aatakpal na chee, 18le ki jer buen kidunduŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann Aafataŋ chee na aaŋangan wɔb, le ki di kina buen kifataŋ ni, 19ki jer buen Bef Hogla aadunduŋ aaŋangan wɔb, le ki ti doo N‑yaan Aanyusakpem nin chee Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl puu ti lir na. Lipepel ngbaan le nan ye ŋŋangii wɔb aanaanmɔk. 20Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl mu le nan ye liwipuul wɔb aanaanmɔk. Ŋipepel ngbaan le nan ye Benjaminn aamaal aatiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii bi na aanaanmɔk.
21Ntim mu nan ye Benjaminn aamaal aatim na le paa na: Jeriko, ni Bef Hogla, ni Emek Kesis, 22ni Bef Araba, ni Semarayim, ni Betel, 23ni Afim, ni Para, ni Ofra, 24ni Kefar Amoni, ni Ofni, ni Geba aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan kpaan saa kipiik ni mulee, ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. 25Ntim mu nan ki kpee na le ye Gibeonn, ni Rama, ni Beerof, 26ni Mispa, ni Kefira, ni Mosa, 27ni Rekem, ni Irpeel, ni Tarala, 28ni Sela, ni Ha Elef, ni Jebus, bee Jerusalem, ni Gibea, ni Kiriaf Jearim aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa ntim kipiik ni munaa la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. Ntim mu Benjaminn aamaal nan gaa aan mu ye baatiŋ na le na.

english_text:
Simeon's Land
1Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders. 2-6 In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following 13 towns with their surrounding villages:
Beersheba, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Balah, Ezem, Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susah, Beth-Lebaoth, and Sharuhen.
7In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages:
Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
8Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
9Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon.
Zebulun's Land
10-12Zebulun was the third tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west at the edge of the gorge near Jokneam. It went east to the edge of the land that belongs to the town of Dabbesheth, and continued on to Maralah and Sarid. It took in the land that belongs to Chislothtabor, then ended at Daberath.
The eastern border went up to Japhia 13and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah 14and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
15Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
16This is the tribal land, and these are the towns and villages of the Zebulun clans.
Issachar's Land
17-23Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following 16 towns with their surrounding villages:
Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh.
Asher's Land
24-26Asher was the fifth tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans included the following towns:
Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph, Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal.
Asher's southern border ran from the Mediterranean Sea southeast along the Shihor-Libnath River at the foot of Mount Carmel, 27then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel, 28Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon. 29-31Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.
Asher had a total of 22 towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob.
Naphtali's Land
32-34Naphtali was the sixth tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west, where the tribal lands of Asher and Zebulun meet near Hukkok. From that point it ran east and southeast along the border with Zebulun as far as Aznoth-Tabor. From there the border went east to Heleph, Adami-Nekeb, Jabneel, then to the town called Oak in Zaanannim, and Lakkum. The southern border ended at the Jordan River, at the edge of the town named Jehudah. Naphtali shared a border with Asher on the west.
35-39The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included 19 towns with their surrounding villages. The following towns had walls around them:
Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, Enhazor, Iron, Migdalel, Horem, Beth-Anath, and Beth-Shemesh.
Dan's Land
40-46Dan was the seventh tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans included the following towns:
Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh, Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Azor, Beneberak, Gath-Rimmon, Mejarkon, and Rakkon.
Dan's tribal land went almost as far as Joppa. 47-48 Its clans received this land and these towns with their surrounding villages.
Later, when enemies forced them to leave their tribal land, they went to the town of Leshem. They attacked the town, captured it, and killed the people who lived there. Then they settled there themselves and renamed the town Dan after their ancestor.
Joshua's Land
49-51The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_text:
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ tii Simeonn aanibol pu na
1Simeonn aanibol le nan paan lelee le bi yakr kitiŋ tii bi. Kitiŋ ngbaan mɔk nan di kina ki ti ker Juda aanibol aatiŋ mɔk la. 2Ntim ngbaan le nan ye Beerseba, ni Seba, ni Molada, 3ni Hasar Sual, ni Bala, ni Esem, 4ni Eltolad, ni Betul, ni Homa, 5ni Siklag, ni Bef Makabof, ni Hasar Susa, 6ni Bef Lebaof, ni Saruhenn aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa ntim kipiik ni mutaa la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.
7Ntim munaa mumina mu nan ki bi: Ayinn, ni Rimonn, ni Eter, ni Asann, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. 8Itingbaan i nan kpee ki bi gbɔk mu na le nan yoor kina ki ti kpaan Baalaf Beer; bi ki yin ki ke Rama, ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na. Kitiŋ ki Simeonn aanibol nan gaa ki ye baatiŋ na le na. 9Juda aanibol aatiŋ aah wiir jer baah nan ban pu na, le bi nan gii baatiŋ ngbaan aapepel libaa tii Simeonn yaab.
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ tii Sebulunn aanibol pu na
10Sebulunn aanibol le nan paan taataa le bi yakr kitiŋ tii bi. Baatiŋ nan yoor kina ti ker Sarid aatiŋ mɔk, 11ki di nima chee ki buen liwilir wɔb kina ki ti saa Mareal aatiŋ, ki di kina ti ker Dabesef aatiŋ, ni mbun mu bi Jokneam aawipuul wɔb na. 12Sarid aapepel liken na, ki yoor kina ki di buen liwipuul ki ti ker Kislof Tabor aatiŋ aanaanmɔk, le ki yoor nima ti ker Daberaf, ki ti saa Jafia, 13le ki nyan nima ki di toŋ liwipuul wɔb ki ti ker Gaf Hefer ni Ef Kasinn aatim ni, ki fenn kpaa Nea aapepel, ki di kina ti saa Rimonn aatiŋ ni. 14Kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangan aapepel aanaanmɔk nan fenn kpaa Hanatonn aatiŋ wɔb, le ki di ti doo Iftael Aafataŋ ni. 15Kitiŋ ngbaan aatim le nan ki ye Kataf, ni Nahalal, ni Simronn, ni Idala, ni Betlehem aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa ntim kipiik ni mulee la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. 16Ntim, ni itingbaan ngbaan le nan bi kitiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii Sebulunn aanibol ke ki li ye baatiŋ na ponn ni.
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ tii Isakar aanibol pu na
17Isakar aanibol le nan paan nnaa le bi yakr kitiŋ tii bi. 18Baapepel aatim le nan ye Jesreel, ni Kesulof, ni Sunem, 19ni Hafarayim, ni Sionn, ni Anaharaf, 20ni Rabif, ni Kisionn, ni Ebes, 21ni Remef, ni Enn Ganim, ni Enn Hada, ni Bef Pases aatim. 22Baatiŋ aanaanmɔk nan ki di ti pii Tabor, ni Sahasuma, ni Bef Semes, le ki di ti doo Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl mɔk. Mu nan kpaan ntim kipiik ni muloob la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. 23Ntim, ni itingbaan ngbaan nan bi kitiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii Isakar aanibol ke ki li ye baatiŋ na ponn ni.
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ tii Aser aanibol pu na
24Aser aanibol le nan paan ŋŋmu, le bi nan yakr kitiŋ tii bi. 25Ntim mu nan bi baatiŋ ngbaan ni na le ye Helkaf, ni Hali, ni Betenn, ni Aksaf, 26ni Alam Melek, ni Amad, ni Misal. Liwilir wɔb na, ki nan di kina ti ker Kamel Aajool ni Sihor Libnaf aatiŋ mɔk. 27Kitiŋ ngbaan aawipuul mɔk nan di kina ti ker Bef Dagonn, le ki ti fuu Sebulunn aatiŋ mɔk, ki ti pii Iftael Aafataŋ ni, le ki buen ŋŋangan wɔb ki di ti keln Bef Emek ni Neyel aatim aasan, le ki yoor kina ŋŋangan wɔb le ki ti ker Kabul, 28ni Ebronn, ni Rehob, ni Hamonn, ni Kana aatim ni, le ki di ti pii kitikpaan Saidonn ni. 29Le kaanaanmɔk ki yoor ki fenn ki ti nyan Rama aatiŋ ni, ki di kina ti ker Taya aatiŋ ki bi maa ligoln mann gonn ki na, le ki fenn ti nyan Hosa aatiŋ ni, le ki ti doo Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk. Kitiŋ ngbaan aatim le nan ki ye Mahalab, ni Aksib, 30ni Uma, ni Afek, ni Rehob aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa ntim moninko ni mulee la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. 31Ntim, ni itingbaan ngbaan le nan bi kitiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii Aser aanibol ke ki li ye baatiŋ na ponn ni.
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ tii Naftali aanibol pu na
32Naftali aanibol le nan paan nloob le bi yakr kitiŋ tii bi. 33Baatiŋ aanaan nan di kina ti nyan Helef aatiŋ ni, ki di ti pii busub sakpiin bu bi Saananim aapepel ni na, ki di kina ti ker Adami Nekeb aatiŋ ni, ki yoor ti nyan Jamnia aatiŋ ni, le ki jer ti nyan Lakum aatiŋ ni, ki ti doo Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee. 34Nima chee le ki fenn ki di kina ki toŋ liwilir wɔb ki ti fuu Asnof Tabor aatiŋ ni, ki nyan nima ti ker Hukok aatiŋ ni, le ki ti pii Sebulunn aatiŋ mɔk ŋŋangii wɔb. Aser aatiŋ nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan aawilir wɔb, le Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl bi kitiŋ ngbaan aawipuul wɔb. 35Ntim mu bi nan maa ŋigon kiir mu na le nan ye Sidim, ni Ser, ni Hamaf, ni Rakaf, ni Kineref, 36ni Adama, ni Rama, ni Hasor, 37ni Kedes, ni Edrei, ni Enhasor, 38ni Yironn, ni Migdalel, ni Horem, ni Bef Anaf, ni Bef Semes aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa ntim kipiik ni muwae la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na. 39Ntim, ni itingbaan ngbaan le nan bi kitiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii Naftali aanibol ke ki li ye baatiŋ na ponn ni.
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ tii Dann aanibol pu na
40Dann aanibol le nan paan nlole le bi nan yakr kitiŋ tii bi. 41Ntim mu nan bi baatiŋ ponn ni na le nan ye Sora, ni Estaol, ni Ir Semes, 42ni Saalbim, ni Aijalonn, ni Itla, 43ni Elonn, ni Timna, ni Ekronn, 44ni Elteke, ni Gibetonn, ni Baalaf, 45ni Jehud, ni Bene Berak, ni Gaf Rimonn, 46ni Me Jakonn, ni Rakonn, ki kpee kitiŋ ki mann gonn Jopa aatiŋ na. 47N‑yoonn mu Dann aanibol nan kɔŋ baatiŋ na, le bi nan buen ti lir Lais yaab aatiŋ pu, ki ton bi butɔb, le ki nyaŋ bi, ki ku bi mɔmɔk, ki gaa kitiŋ ngbaan di ŋa baatiŋ. Bi nan kal nima, ki kpeln kitiŋ ngbaan aayimbil, ki di biyaaja Dann aayimbil yin ki. 48Ntim, ni itingbaan ngbaan le nan bi kitiŋ ki bi nan yakr tii Dann aanibol ke ki li ye baatiŋ na ponn ni.
Baah nan yakr kitiŋ ngbaan kookoo pu na
49N‑yoonn mu Israel yaab nan yakr kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk doo na, le bi nan yakr nibaa chee tii Nunn aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Josua na, aan kitiŋ ngbaan li ye waatiŋ. 50Bi nan di kitiŋ ki u nyan ke u gee ki na le di tii u. Kina le Uwumbɔr nan bui bi. Bi nan yin kitiŋ ngbaan ke Timnaf Sera, ki nan bi ŋigongon ponn ni la, ki bi Efraim yaab aatiŋ ni. U nan ki gir maa kitiŋ ngbaan le ki kal nima chee.
51Utotoor Eleasar, ni Nunn aajapɔɔn Josua, ki kpee Israel yaab aanibol aaninkpiib le nan yakr ntim ngbaan tii bi mɔmɔk; bi nan too inaan ki mee Uwumbɔr, Silo aatiŋ ni, Uwumbɔr aah bi Libool li ni na aabisamɔb chee. Kina le bi nan ŋa, le ki yakr kitiŋ ngbaan doo.

english_text:
The Safe Towns
(Numbers 35.9-15; Deuteronomy 19.1-13)
1 One day the Lord told Joshua:
2When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns. 3-4If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
5One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies. 6The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder.
Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
7The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns:
Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
8The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River:
Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
9These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_text:
Mbɔbɔryaan aatim
(Nkahm 35.9-34)
1Nee aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr nan len Josua chee, 2ke u bui Israel aanib ngbaan ke, “Maah nan bui Moses pu na, nyan mbɔbɔryaan aatim man. 3Unii yaa kaa nyi ki peln ku uken, aan utekpiir ngbaan aanii yaa ban u ku udaan kan, 4u san buen mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ ngbaan kibaa ponn ni, ki buen kitiŋ ngbaan aabisamɔb, nin chee bi ji binib tibɔr na, ki ti kpiir len kitiŋ ngbaan aaninkpiib chee tiwan ni u ŋa na. Le bi ga cha u li koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki tii u nibaa chee u li koo aan ki li bi nima. 5Nima kan, unii u ban u ke u ku u teen lipɔln na yaa dii u aan u san fuu kitiŋ ngbaan ni kan, kitiŋ ngbaan ni aanib taa kii ki di unii u san na tii unii u ban u teen lipɔln na. Ni ye ke binib ngbaan li kii u, ba pu? waa nyi le ki ku udaan ngbaan. 6Bi cha u li koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni aan bi ji waabɔr, bi yaa ŋa kina doo kan, u li bi nima ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu Utotoorninkpel ga kpo na. Nee aapuwɔb, unikur ngbaan ga ŋmaa gir buen udo aatiŋ ni, nin chee u nan san nyan ni na.”
7Nima pu na, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb na, bi nan nyan Kedes aatiŋ ki bi Galilee aatiŋ ni na la, ki nan bi ŋigongon aatiŋ ni, ki ye Naftali aanibol aatiŋ na, le ki ki nyan Sekem aatiŋ ki nan bi ŋigongon aatiŋ ni, ki ye Efraim aanibol aatiŋ na, le ki ki nyan Hebronn aatiŋ ki nan bi ŋigongon aatiŋ ni, ki ye Juda aanibol aatiŋ na, 8le Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul wɔb, nteersakpiin mu bi lijool li aapaacham bi taar na, Jeriko aawipuul wɔb na, bi nan nyan Beser aatiŋ ki bi Rubenn aanibol aatiŋ ni na, le ki ki nyan Ramof aatiŋ ki bi Gilead ni, ki bi Gad aanibol aapepel ni na, le ki ki nyan Golann aatiŋ ki bi Basann ni, ki bi Manase aanibol aapepel ni na. 9Ntim mu bi nan nyan, mu ye mbɔbɔryaan aatim ki tii Israel yaab mɔmɔk, ni biwɔwɔm bi nan koo bi chee na le bi na. Le unii umɔk aa nan nyi ki ku uken na kan, u ga ŋmaa san ti koo nima chee, ki ŋmar unii u ban u ku u teen lipɔln na chee; baan ŋmaa ku u see bi jin waabɔr waahr ki kan ke waabɔr bii a.

english_text:
Levi's Towns
1-2 While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
3Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi. 4The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive.
The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given 13 towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. 5The other members of the Kohath clans received 10 towns from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and West Manasseh. 6The clans that were descendants of Gershon were given 13 towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and East Manasseh. 7The clans that were descendants of Merari received 12 towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
8The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did.
Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
9-19The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given 13 towns and the pastureland around them. Nine of these towns were from the tribes of Judah and Simeon and four from Benjamin.
Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Holon, Debir, Ashan, Juttah, and Beth-Shemesh were from Judah and Simeon. Hebron, located in the hill country of Judah, was earlier called Arba's Town. It had been named after Arba, the ancestor of the Anakim. Hebron's pasturelands went along with the town, but its farmlands and the villages around it had been given to Caleb. Hebron was also one of the Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Gibeon, Geba, Anathoth, and Almon were from Benjamin.
Towns from Ephraim, Dan, West Manasseh
20-26The rest of the Kohath clans of the Levi tribe received ten towns and the pastureland around them. Four of these towns were from the tribe of Ephraim, four from Dan, and two from West Manasseh.
Shechem, Gezer, Kibzaim, and Beth-Horon were from Ephraim. Shechem was located in the hill country, and it was also one of the Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Elteke, Gibbethon, Aijalon, and Gath-Rimmon were from Dan.
Taanach and Jibleam were from West Manasseh.
Towns from East Manasseh, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali
27-33The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received 13 towns and the pastureland around them. Two of these towns were from the tribe of East Manasseh, four from Issachar, four from Asher, and three from Naphtali.
Golan in Bashan and Beeshterah were from East Manasseh.
Kishion, Daberath, Jarmuth, and En-Gannim were from Issachar.
Mishal, Abdon, Helkath, and Rehob were from Asher.
Kedesh in Galilee, Hammothdor, and Kartan were from Naphtali. Golan in Bashan and Kedesh in Galilee were also Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Towns from Zebulun, Reuben, Gad
34-40The rest of the Levi clans were descendants of Merari, and they received twelve towns with the pastureland around them. Four towns were from the tribe of Zebulun, four from Reuben, and four from Gad.
Jokneam, Kartah, Rimmonah, and Nahalal were from Zebulun.
Bezer, Jazah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath were from Reuben. Bezer was located in the desert flatlands east of the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer were from Gad.
Bezer and Ramoth in Gilead were Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
41-42The people of the Levi tribe had a total of 48 towns within Israel, and they had pastures around each one of their towns.
Israel Settles in the Land
43The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it. 44There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win. 45The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_text:
Baah nan nyan ntim mu tii Liifai aanibol na
1Liifai aanibol aaninkpiib nan buen utotoor Eleasar, ni Nunn aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Josua na, ni Israel yaab aaninkpiib biken chee, 2Silo aatiŋ ki bi Kanaann ni na, le ki ti bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke u tii timi ntim, ni kimopɔɔk, aan ti ni timi aawakor li koo nima.” 3Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr aah nan siin pu na, Israel yaab nan ban ntim, ni kimopɔɔk, bi mɔmɔk aapepel ni, ki tii Liifai aanibol ke bi ni baawakor li koo nima chee.
4Liifai aamaal mu nan ye Kohaf aataŋaal ni yaab na le bi nan pue tii ntim. Utotoor Aaronn aamaal nan kan ntim kipiik ni mutaa. Mu nan bi Juda, ni Simeonn, ni Benjaminn aanibol aapepel ni la. 5Kohaf aataŋaal aamaal i nan gur na, bi nan nyan ntim kipiik, mu nan bi Efraim, ni Dann, ni Manase aanibol li nan bi liwilir wɔb na aapepel ni le tii bi.
6Bi nan ban ntim kipiik ni mutaa le tii Gesonn aataŋaal ni aanib. Ntim ngbaan nan bi Isakar, ni Aser, ni Naftali, ni Manase aanibol li nan bi liwipuul wɔb na aapepel ni la.
7Bi nan nyan ntim kipiik ni mulee le tii Merari aataŋaal ni aanib. Ntim ngbaan nan bi Rubenn, ni Gad, ni Sebulunn aanibol aapepel ni la.
8Israel yaab aah nan too inaan ki mee Uwumbɔr, aan u mɔk bi baah ga nyan ntim ni timopɔr ki tii Liifai aanibol pu na le na, kina le u nan bui Moses ke bi ŋa.
9Ntim mu bi nan nyan Juda, ni Simeonn aanibol aapepel ni, 10ki di tii Aaronn aamaal mu ye Kohaf aataŋaal ni aanib, ki nyan ni Liifai aanibol ni na le paa na; bi nan pue nyan ntim tii bima la. 11Bi nan di Aba aatiŋ, ni kimopɔɔk ki mann gonn ki na le tii bi, le bi gur yin ki ke Hebronn, ki bi Juda aagongon aatiŋ ni la. Aba nan ye ŋiwɔk Anak yaab aayaaja. 12Mbamɔn, bi nan pue di kitiŋ ngbaan aakpaasar, ni itingbaan tii Jefune aajapɔɔn, u bi nan yin u ke Kaleb na, ke ki li ye waatiŋ.
13Ntim mu nan ki kpee Hebronn aatiŋ ki nan ye mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ kibaa na pu, bi nan di ntim ngbaan tii utotoor Aaronn aayaabitiib la: muma le ye Libna, 14ni Jatir, ni Estemoa, 15ni Holonn, ni Debir, 16ni Ayinn, ni Juta, ni Bef Semes, ni mu aamopɔr mu: mu nan ye ntim muwae, le ki bi Juda ni Simeonn aanibol aatim ni, bi nan di mu tii utotoor Aaronn aamaal ni yaab. 17Bi nan nyan Benjaminn aanibol aapepel ntim munaa le tii bi: ntim ngbaan le nan ye Gibeonn, ni Geba, 18ni Anatof, ni Almonn aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 19Ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan kpaan kipiik ni mutaa la, ni mu aamopɔr, bi nan di mu tii bitotoorb bi nan ye Aaronn aayaabitiib na la.
20Liifai aamaal ni yaab, bi nan ye Kohaf aataŋaal pu yaab biken na, bi nan nyan Efraim aapepel ni ntim mubaa tii bi mu. 21Bi nan tii bi ntim munaa la, muma le ye Sekem aatiŋ, ni kaamopɔɔk, ki nan bi ŋigongon aatiŋ ki nan ye Efraim aapepel, ki nan ye mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ kibaa na la, ni Geser, 22ni Kibsayim, ni Bef Horonn aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 23Bi nan nyan Dann aapepel mu ni ntim munaa le tii bi, muma le nan ye Elteke, ni Gibetonn, 24ni Aijalonn, ni Gaf Rimonn, ni mu aamopɔr. 25Bi nan nyan Manase aanibol aapepel li bi liwilir wɔb na ni ntim mulee le tii bi, muma le nan ye Taanak, ni Gaf Rimonn, ni mu aamopɔr. 26Bi nan di ntim kipiik ni mu aamopɔr le tii Kohaf aataŋaal pu yaab ngbaan.
27Liifai aanibol aaker li nan ye Gesonn aataŋaal pu yaab na mu, bi nan nyan ntim mulee le Manase aanibol aapepel li nan bi liwipuul wɔb na tii bi, muma le nan ye Golann aatiŋ ki nan bi Basann ni na, ki nan ye mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ kibaa la, ni Beestera aatiŋ, ni mu aamopɔr. 28Bi nan nyan ntim munaa Isakar aanibol aapepel ni tii bi, muma le nan ye Kisionn, ni Daberaf, 29ni Jamuf, ni Enn Ganim aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 30Aser aanibol aapepel ni, bi nan nyan ntim munaa le tii bi, muma le nan ye Misal, ni Abdonn, 31ni Helkaf, ni Rehob aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 32Naftali aanibol aapepel ni, bi nan nyan ntim mutaa le tii bi, muma le nan ye Kedes aatiŋ ki bi Galilee ni na, ni kaamopɔɔk, ki nan ye mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ kibaa la, ni Hamof Dor, ni Kartann aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 33Gesonn aataŋaal pu aamaal aabɔŋ mɔmɔk aah nan kan ntim pu na, nan kpaan kipiik ni mutaa la, ni mu aamopɔr mɔmɔk.
34Liifai aanibol aamaal i nan gur, ki nan ye Merari aataŋaal yaab na, bi nan nyan ntim munaa le Sebulunn aanibol aapepel wɔb tii bi, muma le nan ye Jokneam, ni Karta, 35ni Dimna, ni Nahalal, ni mu aamopɔr. 36Rubenn aanibol aapepel wɔb, bi nan nyan ntim munaa le tii bi, muma le nan ye Beser, ni Jahas, 37ni Kedemof, ni Mefaaf aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 38Gad aanibol aapepel wɔb, bi nan nyan ntim munaa le tii bi, muma le nan ye Ramof aatiŋ ki nan bi Gilead ni na, ni kaamopɔɔk, ki nan ye mbɔbɔryaan aatiŋ kibaa la, ni Mahanaim, 39ni Hesbonn, ni Jaser aatim, ni mu aamopɔr. 40Merari aataŋaal yaab mu aah nan kan ntim pu na, nan kpaan kipiik ni mulee la, ni mu aamopɔr mɔmɔk.
41-42Israel yaab aatiŋ aah nan bi ki ti ker pu na, bi nan di ntim imonko ilee ni muniin, ki kpee mu aamopɔr mɔmɔk le tii Liifai yaab.
Israel yaab aah nan gaa kitiŋ ngbaan pu na
43Uwumbɔr nan di kitiŋ ki u nan puu tii Israel yaab aayaajatiib ke u ga di ki tii bi na tii bi. N‑yoonn mu bi nan gaa kitiŋ ngbaan doo na, le bi nan kal nima chee. 44Uwumbɔr nan tii bi nsuudoon, kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ni, ke waah nan puu tii biyaajatiib pu na. Le baadim ponn ni ubaa kina aa ŋmaa ŋa bi nibaa, ba pu? Uwumbɔr le nan tii bi linyaŋ baadim mɔmɔk pu. 45Uwumbɔr nan cha tipuur timɔk u nan puu tii Israel yaab na mɔmɔk gbiin.

english_text:
The Two and a Half Tribes Return Home
1Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
2-3 You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives. 4The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
5Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
6-9You've become rich from what you've taken from your enemies. You have big herds of cattle, lots of silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and plenty of clothes. Take everything home with you and share with the people of your tribe.
I pray that God will be kind to you. You are now free to go home.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad started back to Gilead, their own land. Moses had given the land of Bashan to the East Manasseh tribe, so they started back along with Reuben and Gad. God had told Moses that these two and a half tribes should conquer Gilead and Bashan, and they had done so.
Joshua had given land west of the Jordan River to the other half of the Manasseh tribe, so they stayed at Shiloh in the land of Canaan with the rest of the Israelites.
10-11The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river.
When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done, 12the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes. 13But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes. 14Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
15Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
16 All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him? 17 Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin. 18Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again.
If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation. 19If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar. 20 Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
21The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
22The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar, 23and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
24-25We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.”
Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord. 26That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord. 27-29To build another altar for offering sacrifices would be the same as turning our backs on the Lord and rebelling against him. We could never do that! No, we built the altar to remind us and you and the generations to come that we will worship the Lord. And so we will keep bringing our sacrifices to the Lord's altar, there in front of his sacred tent. Now your descendants will never be able to say to our descendants, “You can't worship the Lord.”
But if they do say this, our descendants can answer back, “Look at this altar our ancestors built! It's like the Lord's altar, but it isn't for offering sacrifices. It's here to remind us and you that we belong to the Lord, just as much as you do.”
30-31Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
32Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes. 33The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
34The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_text:
Josua aah nan cha liwipuul wɔb aanibol gir kun pu na
1Josua nan yin Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln, ŋi ye liwipuul wɔb yaab na, nan kpaan ubaa chee. 2U nan bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses aah nan bui ke ni ŋa pu na, ni kii waamɔb ki ŋa ni mɔmɔk doo a, le ki kii maah bui ke ni ŋa pu na mɔmɔk. 3N‑yoonn mumina mɔmɔk, naa san cha nido yaab Israel yaab kpala. Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr mbamɔm. 4Dandana wee, waah nan puu pu na, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr tii niŋeen aatɔtiib Israel yaab biken nsuudoon a. Kina pu na, gir kun kitiŋ ki pu ni nan gaa ki ye nimi yaan na, kitiŋ ki bi liwipuul, Jɔɔdann aamɔɔdapuul wɔb na, kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses nan di tii nimi na. 5Ni chuu nibaa man, ki kii, ki li joo ikaal i Moses nan di mɔk nimi na: ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki ŋa waageehn, ki kii tii waakaal, ki li joo waasan mbamɔm, aan ki li dii u nisui ni, ni nimi aawiin mɔmɔk.” 6-8Josua nan mee Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa bi pu, le ki cha bi gir kun, le ki di tibɔr tee sur bi, “Ni joo liwangol le ki gir chaa kun: tiwakor, ni tikunabr, ni salmaa, ni tikumann, ni tikur, ki kpee tiwanpeenkaan pam. Naah gaa tiwan ni nimi aadim chee na, ni ti yakr ni tii niŋeen aatɔtiib biken.” Le bi siir buen.
Moses le nan di kitiŋ ki bi liwipuul, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔdapuul wɔb na tii Manase aanibol ligeln. Josua mu nan ban kitiŋ Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb, ki tii Manase aanibol ligeln li gur na, ŋinibol ŋiwae na chee.
9Kina le Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ki kpee Manase aanibol ligeln liken na, gir kun. Bi nan buen ki cha Israel yaab bi gur na, le bi gaar Silo aatiŋ ki bi Kanaann ni na, le ki chaa kun baatiŋ ni, bi yin ki ke Gilead. Kitiŋ ngbaan le Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke u di tii bi.
Kitork aabimbiln li bi nan maa Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee na
10N‑yoonn mu Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ki kpee Manase aanibol ligeln, bi ye liwipuul wɔb yaab na nan ti fuu Gelilof aatiŋ ni, ki nan bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb na, le bi maa kitork aabimbiln sakpeln nyanyaan libaa, limɔɔl chee nima. 11Tɔ, binib bibaa nan tuk Israel yaab biken na ke, “Li pel man, Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln maa kitork aabimbiln sakpeln libaa Gelilof aatiŋ ni, ni bi timi aapepel wɔb, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee.” 12Israel yaab biken na aah ŋun kina na, le bi mɔmɔk kuun dan Silo aatiŋ ni, ke bi buen ti to ŋinibol ngbaan butɔb.
13Le Israel aanib ngbaan nan tun Eleasar aajapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Fineas na, ke u buen Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln na aanib chee, Gilead aatiŋ ni. 14Israel yaab aaninkpiib bi nan ye bisalolm na kipiik le nan kpee Fineas pu, bi nan nyan liwilir wɔb aanibol aaninkpiib ni la, le bi mɔmɔk nan ye biyidam, baataŋaal ponn ni. 15Le bi ti fuu Gilead aatiŋ ni, Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln bi bi liwipuul wɔb na chee. 16Baah nan kpaan ki ye Uwumbɔr aanib aasalolm pu na, le bi bui bi ke, “Ba ŋa ni ŋa titunwanbir timina aaboln timi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr aanimbiin ni? Ni yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, le ki maa kitork aabimbiln limina tii nibaa, kaa di li tii Uwumbɔr. 17Ni teer taah nan tun titunwanbir ti Peor aatiŋ ni na; n‑yoonn ngbaan Uwumbɔr nan daa timi waanib aatafal ki cha iween lir ti pu, kina pu na, ti laa beenin ji kina aafalaa. Timi aatunwanbir ngbaan aa ŋeer aa? 18Ni yaa yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb din wee kan, u ga gee liŋuul Israel yaab mɔmɔk pu. 19Ni yaa kaan ŋmaa doon Uwumbɔr nimi aatiŋ ni kan, puur dan ti chee man, nin chee Uwumbɔr Aabool bi na, ki nan gaa timi aatim ngem. Ni taa yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, ki taa nya tipuwɔb ki nan ki maa kitork aabimbiln liken ki kpee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr yaan pu. 20Ni teer Sera aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Akann na bɔr, u nan yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb le ki yoor tiwan ni ye Uwumbɔr yaan na, le Uwumbɔr nan daa Israel yaab mɔmɔk aatafal, naa nan ye Akann baanja le nan kpo titunwanbir ngbaan pu.”
21Le Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln aanib nan giin bui liwilir wɔb aanibol aaninkpiib ke, 22“Uwumbɔr le ye Mpɔɔndaan. Uma le ye Uwumbɔr. Uwumbɔr le ye Mpɔɔndaan. Uma le ye Uwumbɔr. Uma le nyi tiwan ni pu ti ŋa kina na, le ti ban ni mu bee ni. Ni yaa ye ke ti tun titunwanbir Uwumbɔr chee, kaa kii waamɔb kan, ku timi man, ki taa cha ti ki li bi man. 23Ni yaa ye ke ti yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, le ki maa kitork aabimbiln ke ti li seer njikaabim aapiin, bee kimɔbaan aapiin kan, cha Uwumbɔr ubaa daa titafal. 24Aayii. Tiwan ni cha ti ŋa kina na le ye ke ti san ijawaan ke n‑yoonn mu choo na, niyaabitiib ga nan bui timi yaab ke, ‘Nimi aa ye Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr aanib, ba ŋa ni dii u? 25U di Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl le siin timi aatiŋ, ni nimi bi ye Rubenn, ni Gad aanibol yaab na aatiŋ mɔk. Naan ŋmaa dii Uwumbɔr.’ Nibaakan niyaabitiib ga bui tiyaabitiib kina, ki cha bi taa ki dii Uwumbɔr. 26Nima pu le ti maa kitork aabimbiln ngbaan, naa ye ke ti ban ti see kitork ki tii ipiin li pu la, 27ti ŋa kina ke ni li ye limɔkl ki tii nimi aanib, ni timi yaab, ki ki tii binib bi paa ni ti pu na, aan nima kan, timɔk kpaan ki li dooni Uwumbɔr, Waabool baan ni, ki li toor libimbiln baan pu kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ni kitork kiken, ni kimɔbaan aatork. Nimina le ga kiir niyaabitiib, bi taa len ke tiyaabitiib aan ŋmaa dii Uwumbɔr. 28Ti dak le ke ni yaa dan kina kan, tiyaabitiib ga ŋmaa bui ke, ‘Lik man, tiyaajatiib mu maa kitork aabimbiln li naan Uwumbɔr yaan na la. Baa maa li ke bi li seer kitork ki tii ipiin li pu, ni ye limɔkl le ki tii nimi ni timi aamaal.’ 29Mbamɔn, taan ŋmaa yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, ki mu aan yii ke taan ki dii u, ni mu aa ye ke ti maa libimbiln ti li toor kitork ki seer mmii ni, bee kitork kiken, bee njikaabim aatork li pu la. Taan ki maa kitork aabimbiln liken kpee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aabimbiln li si Waabool aanimbiin ni na.”
30Le Fineas u nan ye utotoor na, ni bijab kipiik bi ye ŋinibol ŋi bi Jɔɔdann aawilir wɔb na aayidam na ŋun Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln na aah len pu na, le ni mɔɔr bi. 31Le utotoor Eleasar aajapɔɔn Fineas nan bui ke, “Dandana wee, ti bee ke Uwumbɔr bi ti chee. Naa yii waamɔb, kina pu le ni nyan Israel yaab mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr aatafadaan ni.”
32Le Fineas ni biyidam ngbaan nan nyan Gilead aatiŋ ni, Rubenn ni Gad aanibol chee, ki gir buen Kanaann aatiŋ ni, ki buen Israel yaab biken chee, le ki ti ŋeer tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk tuk bi. 33Le ni mɔɔr Israel yaab mɔmɔk, le bi pak Uwumbɔr. Baa nan ki dak ke bi ga buen ti to Rubenn ni Gad yaab butɔb.
34Rubenn ni Gad yaab nan bui ke, “Libimbiln lee ye seeraa ke Uwumbɔr le ye Tidindaan.” Kina pu le bi nan yin libimbiln ngbaan ke, “Seeraa.”

english_text:
Joshua's Farewell Speech
1The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age. 2One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them:
I am now very old. 3You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land. 4-5There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
6Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
7Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods. 8Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
9When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you. 10 Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised. 11Be sure to always love the Lord your God. 12-13Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
14I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken. 15-16Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_text:
Josua aah nan di kookoo aabɔr ti chɔi bi na
1Naah bi cha na, le Uwumbɔr tii Israel yaab linyaŋ baadim pu, le bi kan nsuudoon. N‑yoonn ngbaan Josua nan por pam, 2nima pu na, u nan yin ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk, bi nan ye bininkpiib, ni bisalolm, ni bibɔjirb, ni biyidam bi joo binib ngbaan na, le ki nan bui bi ke, “Dandana wee, m por pam. 3Ni mɔmɔk kan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa ŋitimbol ŋimina mɔmɔk pu na. Nimi pu le u ŋa kina. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le jaa ni pu. 4M tii nimi ntim mu gur ke ni ga gaa, aan mu li ye nimi yaan na, le ki kpee ntim mu ti nyaŋ ki gaa, ki yoor Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl mɔk, liwipuul wɔb, ki ti ker Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk, liwilir wɔb na. 5Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga cha nimi aadim san nimi ijawaan, ki ga jenn nyan bi, le ni ga gaa baatim ke uma Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah puu tii nimi pu na. 6Kina pu na, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii waamɔb, ki ŋa Moses aakaal aagbaŋ aah tuk nimi ke ni ŋa pu na. Ni taa yii nkaal ngbaan mubaa, 7nima kan, naan di nibaa ŋmal biniyayam bi gur ki bi ni chee na ni, ki mu taa yin baawaa aayimbil, ki taa di ŋaayimbil puu tipuur, ki taa doon ŋiwaa ngbaan kpala, ki taa gbaan ŋinimbiin ni. 8Ni tee li dii Uwumbɔr mbamɔm, ke naah gaa u ki kii ki nan saa dandana wee pu na. 9Naah piin ki choo na, Uwumbɔr le cha ni nyaŋni ntikpaam, ni mpɔɔndam aanibol, ki nyani bi baatim ni, ubaa aa kee nyaŋ nimi. 10Ni ponn ni unibaan ga ŋmaa nyaŋ binib lichur; ba pu? Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le nyaŋni bi tii nimi, ke waah nan puu pu na. 11Li nyi man, aan ki li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. 12Ni yaa kaa si chob aan ki di nibaa kpaan ŋinibol ŋi gur na chee ki yoor bibisatiib kan, 13ni li nyi ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aan jenn nyan ŋinibol ngbaan, naah tur koo bi ponn ni pu na. Bi ga tee li ye ntafadaan le ni pu, ki li ye gaawɔb, ni libuul tii nimi. Le baah ga ŋa nimi falaa u na ga li wu nipuwɔb ke mbambaan na la, ki ga ki li wu ke ikokon le aah saar ninimbil ni na. Le ni ga li bi kina hali ki ti saa buyoonn ni ponn ni ubaa aan ti ki gur kitinyaan kimina ponn ni, kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di tii nimi na.
14“Dandana wee, ni ŋeer ke m kpo. Ni mɔmɔk nyi nisui ni, ni nimi aawiin ni, ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le tii nimi tiwanyaan nimɔk u puu ke u ga tii nimi na. Tipuur timɔk u puu na, u ŋa ti mɔmɔk; tibaa kina aa bee fam. 15Waah cha tipuur ngbaan mɔmɔk gbiin na, kina le u ga cha tifaan ngbaan mɔmɔk mu gbiin. 16Ni yaa kaa joo nkaal mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bui nimi ke ni li joo mu na, ki yaa dooni ŋiwaa kan, waaŋuul ga fii, le u ga daa nitafal, naan yunn le ni mɔmɔk ubaa kina aan ki gur kitinyaan ki u di tii nimi na ponn ni.”

english_text:
We Will Worship and Obey the Lord
1Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent. 2 Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel:
Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor. 3 But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants. 4 Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
5-6 Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea. 7Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched.
You lived in the desert for a long time, 8 then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land. 9 King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you. 10But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
11 You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all. 12 Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
13 You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
14Then Joshua told the people:
Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt. 15But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
16The people answered:
We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord. 17The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went. 18And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
19Joshua said:
The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it. 20If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
21But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
22Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?”
“Yes, it's true,” they answered.
23Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
24The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
25Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel 26and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem 27and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
28Joshua sent everyone back to their homes.
Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
29Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of 110. 30 The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
31As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
32 When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for 100 pieces of silver from Hamor, the founder of Shechem. The town and the field both became part of the land belonging to the descendants of Joseph.
33When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_text:
Josua aah nan len tibɔr Israel yaab chee Sekem aatiŋ ni pu na
1Josua nan kuun Israel aanibol ngbaan mɔmɔk dan ubaa chee Sekem aatiŋ ni. U nan yin baaninkpiib, ni baasalolm, ni baabɔjirb, ni baayidam, le bi mɔmɔk kuun ni Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni. 2Le Josua bui bi mɔmɔk ke, “Uwumbɔr u ye timi Israel yaab Aadindaan na aah len pu na sɔ: ‘N‑yoonn mu jer na, niyaajatiib nan bi Yufrates Aamɔɔdapuul le ki dooni ŋiwaa. Niyaajatiib ngbaan ubaa le nan ye Tera, u nan ye Abraham ni Nahor aate na. 3Le min Uwumbɔr nan yin niyaaja Abraham, ki nyan ni u Yufrates Aamɔɔdapuul, le u dan Kanaann aatiŋ kimina ponn ni. M nan tii u yaabitiib pam. Uma le nan ma Aisak, 4le Aisak mu ma Jakob ni Esɔ. Le m nan di ŋigongon aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Edom na ki di tii Esɔ, u li joo, le niyaaja Jakob ni waabim nan buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 5Le m nan tun Moses ni Aaronn, ki cha ntafadaan lir Ijipt yaab pu, ki nan nyan ni nitetiib nima chee. 6Maah nan nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, Ijipt yaab nan san paa bi pu, ki joo itaan ni tɔroku tiib, le nitetiib aah ti pii Nnyusakpem Mamam buyoonn na, 7le bi wii ki yin mi ke m nan ter bi, le m cha mbɔmbɔɔn dan bi ni Ijipt yaab aakaasisik ni. M nan cha Ijipt yaab bee nnyusakpem na ni. Ni nyi maah nan ŋa Ijipt yaab pu na mɔmɔk.
“‘Ni nan bi nteersakpiin ni, ni yunn pam. 8Le m nan joo ni nimi Amor yaab aatiŋ ni, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul wɔb. Bi nan ton nimi butɔb, le m cha ni nyaŋ bi. Ni nan gaa baatim, le naah tur koo bi ni na, m ku bi. 9Moab yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Balak, aan ute nan ye Sipor na, nan ton nimi butɔb. U nan tun unii, Beor aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Balaam na chee, ki bui u ke u puun lii ni pu, 10le maa kii tii Balaam, le u tee ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu. M nan ŋa kina le ki gaa nimi Balak aaŋaal ni lii. 11Le ni nan puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki dan Jeriko aatiŋ ni. Le Jeriko yaab ton nimi butɔb. Nee aapuwɔb, le Amor yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Girgas yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab mu nan ton nimi butɔb, le m nan cha ni nyaŋ bi mɔmɔk. 12Naah nan tur koo bi ponn ni pu na, m nan cha ijawaan koo bi, aan ni ŋmaa jenn nyan Amor yaab aabɔrb bilee ngbaan. Naa nan ye nimi aajaak aajum ni itɔi pu le ni nan ŋmaa nyaŋ. 13Min le di ikpaakon i naa nan kon i ponn ni kpala na tii nimi, le ki di ntim mu naa nan maa mu na tii nimi. Le dandana wee, ni bi ntim ngbaan ni, ki ji ndaan aasubil, ni olif aakpan aasubil aasui i mu naa nan bun i na.’”
14Josua nan ki bui bi ke, “Kina pu na, ni li nyuŋni Uwumbɔr, ki gaa u iŋaal ilee, ki li dii u mbamɔm. Ni di ŋiwaa ŋi niyaajatiib nan dooni ŋi Mesopotamia, ni Ijipt aatim ni na lii, aan ki dii Uwumbɔr baanja. 15Ni yaa kaa gee ke ni li dooni u kan, din wee, ni nyan naah ga dii u na; ni ga li dooni ŋiwaa ŋi niyaajatiib nan dooni ŋi Mesopotamia aatiŋ ni na aa? bee ni ga li dooni Amor yaab, bi ni bi baatiŋ ponn ni na le aawaa? M ni maamaal ma kan, ti ga li dii Uwumbɔr la.”
16Le binib ngbaan nan giin bui u ke, “Taan di Uwumbɔr lii kpala ki dii liwaal libaa. 17Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le nan nyan ni titetiib, ni timi, Ijipt yaab aanaagbiir ni, le ti kan lijinjiir aatun ŋi u tun na. Taah nan bi nin chee na mɔmɔk, uma le nan biin ti pu, le ŋinibol ŋimɔk ti koo bi ni na ubaa aa nan ŋa timi nibaa. 18Taah nan tur koo kitiŋ kee ni na, Uwumbɔr jenn nyan Amor yaab bimɔk nan bi do na, kina pu na, ti ga dii Uwumbɔr la, uma le ye Tidindaan.”
19Le Josua bui binib ngbaan ke, “Naan ŋmaa dii Uwumbɔr, ba pu? Uwumbɔr ye chain la, kaan di cha nimi aatunwanbir pinn nimi. U ye lipiipoln Aawumbɔr la, 20le ni yaa yii u, ki ban ni li dooni ŋiwaa kan, u ga daa nitafal. Hali waah nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu na, ni yaa dii liwaal libaa kan, u ga kuln nimi.”
21Le binib ngbaan bui Josua ke, “Aayii, ti ga sil li dii Uwumbɔr la.”
22Le Josua bui bi ke, “Nimi le ye nibaa aaseeraadam, ki len mbamɔn ke ni ga li dii Uwumbɔr la.”
Le bi giin bui u ke, “Mbamɔn, timi le ye tibaa aaseeraadam.”
23Le Josua bui bi ke, “Ni yaa ye kina kan, ni nyan ŋiwaa ŋi bi ni chee na man, aan ki puu ke ni ga sil dii Uwumbɔr u ye timi Israel yaab Aadindaan na.”
24Le binib ngbaan bui Josua ke, “Ti ga li dii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr la, ki ga kii waah len pu na.”
25Nima pu na, liyaadaal ngbaan le Josua nan cha bi puu tipuur kina, nima chee, Sekem aatiŋ ni, le ki tii bi nsurm ni ikaal, bi li dii. 26Josua nan ŋmee ikaal ngbaan Uwumbɔr aakaal aagbaŋ ponn ni. U nan yoor litakpasakpeln libaa, le ki di ŋum likpaln aasub taab, Uwumbɔr Aabool chee, 27le ki bui binib ngbaan ke, “Litakpal limina le ye timi aaseeraadaan. Litakpal ngbaan ŋun Uwumbɔr aah bui timi tibɔr ti na mɔmɔk. Kina pu na, lima le ye seeraa ki ga li teer nimi, ni taa yii nimi Aawumbɔr aamɔb.” 28Nee aapuwɔb, le Josua nan cha binib ngbaan mɔmɔk gir kun baah nyan ni ntim mu ponn ni na.
Josua ni utotoor Eleasar aah kpo pu na
29Nee aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr aatutunn Josua, u nan ye Nunn aajapɔɔn na kpo. U nan saa ŋibin nkub ni kipiik le ki nin kpo. 30Bi nan di u sub udo aatiŋ ki bi ŋigongon aatiŋ ni, aan bi yin ki ke Timnaf Sera na ni la. Kitiŋ ngbaan nan bi Efraim aatiŋ ni, Gaas Aajool aaŋangan wɔb la.
31Josua aah nan bi limɔfal ni, ki ti saa buyoonn u kpo na, Israel yaab nan dii Uwumbɔr mbamɔm, le waah kpo na, bi nan beenin dii u mbamɔm, ki ti saa buyoonn baaninkpiib bi nan kan Uwumbɔr aah nan ŋa lijinjiir aawan pu na, mu nan kpoi.
32Josef aah nan kpo Ijipt aatiŋ ni, aan Israel yaab joo ni waakpab i na, bi nan di i sub Sekem aatiŋ ni, kitiŋ ki Jakob nan daa Hamor aajapɔtiib chee na. Hamor nan ye Sekem aate la. Jakob nan daa kitiŋ ngbaan tikunabr aamombil nkub la. Josef aayaabitiib le nan jin ki lifaal.
33Aaronn aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Eleasar na mu nan kpo, le bi nan di u sub Gibea aatiŋ ki bi nan di ki tii ujapɔɔn Fineas, aan ki bi ŋigongon ni, Efraim yaab aapepel ni na.

english_text:
The Tribes of Judah and Simeon Fight the Canaanites
1After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
2“Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
3The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.”
Troops from Simeon came to help Judah. 4-5Together they attacked an army of 10,000 Canaanites and Perizzites at Bezek, and the Lord helped Judah defeat them. During the battle, Judah's army found out where the king of Bezek was, and they attacked there. 6The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes, 7and he said, “I've cut off the thumbs and big toes of 70 kings and made those kings crawl around under my table for scraps of food. Now God is paying me back.”
