translation_text:
Elkana ni waamaal aabɔr
1Uja ubaa nan bi, bi nan yin u ke Elkana, u nyan ni Efraim aamaal ponn ni la, le ki koo Rama aatiŋ ki bi Efraim aatiŋ ki ŋigongon wiir nima na ponn ni. Ute le nan ye Jeroham, le uyaaja mu nan ye Elihu, u nyan ni Tohu aamaal mu ye Suf aataŋaal na. 2Elkana nan kpa bipiib bilee la, bi nan yin ubaa ke Hana, ki yin uken ke Penina. Penina nan kpa bibilb, le Hana ma aa nan kpa ubaa. 3Libiln mɔmɔk ponn ni kan, Elkana nan nya Rama ki chaa Silo ti toor kitork, ki dooni Uwumbɔr u yeh mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na. Nima chee le Eli aajapɔtiib Hofni ni Fineas nan ye Uwumbɔr aatotoorb. 4N‑yoonn mumɔk Elkana yaa nan ti toor kitork na kan, u nan yakr tinann ngbaan tibaa tii upuu Penina, ki di tiken mu tii waabim mu. 5U nan gee upuu uken Hana na sakpen; tɔ, u nan tii u mu linankpiln libaa la, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa nan tii u ubo. 6Uyɔnn Penina nan ŋani u mbiin ni mbɔnyun, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa nan tii u ubo. 7Ni nan bi kina le ŋibin mɔmɔk; n‑yoonn mumɔk bi nan ti buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni na kan, Penina nan bii Hana aasui sakpen le u ti piin ki wii, ki yii kaan ji nibaa. 8Le uchal Elkana ga ti baa u ke, “Hana, ba ŋa si aa wii? Ba ŋa saan ji tijikaar? Ba ŋa aasui bii kina? Maa jer mbim kipiik aa chee ee?”
Utotoor Eli aah nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Hana pu pu na
9-10Nwiin mubaa daal, baah jin baajikaar doo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni, Silo aatiŋ ni na, le Hana fii. Usui nan bii sakpen, le u bi mee Uwumbɔr ki wii mpombiin pu. N‑yoonn ngbaan, utotoor Eli nan ka waakakaa chee mbisamɔb. 11Le Hana nan puu tipuur tii Uwumbɔr ke: “Uwumbɔr u yeh mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na, lik mi, saanaagbiipii. Lik ki kan maabɔr, ki teer mbɔr. Taa suln mbɔr. Aa yaa tii mi ubijabo kan, m puu ke m ga di u tii si u tun saatuln waamɔfal mɔmɔk ponn ni, ki taa kuu uyikpir.”
12Hana nan bi mee Uwumbɔr ni ti yunn pam, le Eli nan ka lik umɔgban. 13U nan bi mee suuna, le umɔgban deŋni, le tibɔr ma aa tee nyan ni. Kina pu le Eli nan dak ke u nyun ndaan gbii la, 14le ki bui u ke, “Di cha saadanyuwan ngbaan. Di cha lidanyul ki chuu aabaa suuna.”
15Le u gar u ke, “Aayii, maa gbii ndaan, maaninkpel. Maa nyun ndaan. Ni ye mi limukl la, le m bi mee limeel, ki kpiir maabɔr tuk Uwumbɔr. 16Taa dak ke m ye piifam ubaa la. Nsui le bii sakpen, le m bi mee kina pu.”
17Le Eli bui u ke, “Li cha ni nsuudoon, aan Israel yaab Aawumbɔr tii si saah mee u tiwan ni na.”
18Le Hana bui u ke, “Uwumbɔr cha aa li dak mbɔr tiwan ni ŋan na pu.” Le u siir buen, ki ti jin tijikaar, le usui piir.
Hana aah ma Samuel ki di u tii Uwumbɔr pu na
19Naah woln kichakpiik ni na, le Elkana ni waadichal fii mala, ki ki doon Uwumbɔr, le ki gir kun Rama aatiŋ ni. Tɔ, Elkana nan doon upuu Hana chee, le Uwumbɔr kii waameel. 20Kina pu na, ni nan ye le ke u di dek, ki maa ubijabo. U nan yin u ke Samuel, le ki kpiir len ke, “M mee u Uwumbɔr chee la.”
21N‑yoonn nan ki fuu ni ke Elkana ni waadichal buen Silo ki ti toor libiln libiln aatork tii Uwumbɔr, ni waah nan ki puu ubaa aapuur ti na. 22N‑yoonn mue na, le Hana aa nan buen. U nan bui uchal ke, “M yaa nan giin ubo libiil n‑yoonn mu na kan, le m ga kpaan di u buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni, nin chee u ga ti li bi ki ti saa waakun daal na.”
23Le Elkana kii ke, “Tɔ, ŋa nimɔk aa dak ke ni ŋan na; li bi linampal aan ki ti saa buyoonn aa ga giin u libiil na, ki cha Uwumbɔr sil aa pu aan saah puu tipuur ti na gbiin.” Nima pu le Hana nan gaar linampal ki lik waabo.
24Waah nan giin u libiil na, le u di u buen Silo, ki joo ŋibin ŋitaa aanaaja, ni n‑yon kuruwaa kipiik, ni ŋisubil aadaan lidabuul libaa. Samuel nan laa par, le u di u buen Silo, Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni. 25Baah kɔr unaaja ngbaan doo na, le bi di ubo ngbaan buen Eli chee. 26Le Hana bui u ke, “Gafara, maaninkpel. Aa bee mi ii? Min le ye upii u aa nan kan u si do ki bi mee Uwumbɔr na. 27M nan mee u ubo wee la, le u tii mi maah ban pu na. 28Kina pu le m joo ni u m nan di tii Uwumbɔr. N‑yoonn mumɔk u bi limɔfal ponn ni na, u ga li ye Uwumbɔr yoo la.”
Le bi doon Uwumbɔr nima chee.

english_text:
1 Hannah prayed:
You make me strong
and happy, Lord.
You rescued me.
Now I can be glad
and laugh at my enemies.
2No other god is like you.
And with you we are safer
than on a high mountain.
3I can tell those proud people,
“Stop your boasting!
Nothing is hidden from the Lord,
and he judges what we do.”
4Our Lord, you break
the bows of warriors,
but you give strength
to everyone who stumbles.
5People who once
had plenty to eat
must now hire themselves out
for only a piece of bread.
But you give the hungry more
than enough to eat.
A woman did not have a child,
and you gave her seven,
but a woman who had many
was left with none.
6 You take away life,
and you give life.
You send people down
to the world of the dead
and bring them back again.
7Our Lord, you are the one
who makes us rich or poor.
You put some in high positions
and bring disgrace on others.
8You lift the poor and homeless
out of the garbage dump
and give them places of honor
in royal palaces.
You set the world on foundations,
and they belong to you.
9You protect your loyal people,
but everyone who is evil
will die in darkness.
We cannot win a victory
by our own strength.
10Our Lord, those who attack you
will be broken in pieces
when you fight back
with thunder from heaven.
You will judge the whole earth
and give power and strength
to your chosen king.
Samuel Stays with Eli
11Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord.
Eli's Sons
12-13Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork. 14The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh. 15Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord.
Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
16Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.”
“No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
17Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry.
Hannah Visits Samuel
18The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment 19and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
20Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
21The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh.
Eli Warns His Sons
22Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel. 23-24“Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people. 25If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!”
But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father.
A Prophet Speaks to Eli
26 Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
27One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord:
When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am. 28-29 Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar.
But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
30I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me. 31The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
32Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young. 33If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death! 34 To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
35I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king. 36But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_text:
Hana aameel
1Le Hana mee Uwumbɔr ke:
“Uwumbɔr di mpopiin gbiin nsui ni,
waah ŋa pu tii mi na, nsui piir sakpen.
M laa maadim;
Uwumbɔr aah ter mi pu na tii mi mpopiin sakpen.
2Ubaa aa bi chain ke Uwumbɔr na;
ubaa aa bi ke uma na,
ukikiir ubaa aa bi ke timi Aawumbɔr na.
3Di cha nimi aapupuk ngbaan man;
ŋmin man nimi aagaak aamɔliin ngbaan;
ba pu? Uwumbɔr ye Uwumbɔr u nyi na la,
le ki nyi binib mɔmɔk aah ŋani pu na.
4Bijab bi pɔɔ na aatɔi kool la,
le bi kaa kpa mpɔɔn na moo pɔɔk.
5Binib bi nan kpa ki ji babr na
gur joo bibaa le kooh ki kpiini bibaa;
nkon aah nan joo bi na gur ji gunni la.
Upii u nan ye uŋoob na gur kpa mbim mulole la,
le upii u nan kpa mbim pam na aa ki kpa ubaa gur.
6Uwumbɔr ku la, le ki ki tii limɔfal;
u cha binib chaa kitekpiitiŋ ni, le ki tii binib limɔfal.
7U ŋani binib bibaa bigiim,
le ki ŋani biken biwankpadam.
U sunni bibaa taab, le ki ŋani biken binikpaam.
8U nyan ni bigiim titan ponn ni,
ki nyan ni binib bi kaa kpa na baanimbaak ponn ni.
U ŋani bi mbɔrbim aajɔtiib,
ki joo bi kaani binikpaam aakakaa chee.
Uwumbɔr le naan kitiŋ kee aatinyikl, le ki pɔɔ,
litinyikl lee pu le u naan dulnyaa.
9Waanib bi dii u mbamɔm na, u kii baamɔfal,
le bibiindam ma beer mbɔmbɔɔn ni.
Uja aan ŋmaa di ubaa aapɔɔn kan linyaŋ.
10Uwumbɔr aadim ga kuln;
u bi paacham ki ga teen bi pu ke utaal na.
Uwumbɔr le ga ji dulnyaa mɔmɔk tibɔr;
u ga tii waabɔr mpɔɔn,
u ga cha waah lee ubɔr u na kan linyaŋ.”
11Tɔ, Elkana gir kun Rama, le Samuel u laa ye ubo na gaar Silo, ki tun Uwumbɔr aatuln, utotoor Eli chee.
Eli aajapɔtiib aah bir pu na
12Eli aajapɔtiib nan ye bibiindam la. Bitafal aa nan bi Uwumbɔr ni, 13kaa nan bi ikaal i nan mɔk utotoor aah ga ban tiwan ni binib chee na ni. Baah nan labr ŋani pu na sɔ: unii yaa nan bi toor waatork kan, le utotoor aatutunn ga dan, ki joo ni nnanmoon mu yakr ŋipan ŋitaa na, buyoonn tinann ngbaan beenin tɔk mmii pu na, 14le u di nnanmoon ngbaan saa tinann ngbaan ponn ni, le nnanmoon ngbaan aah saa tuun tinann timɔk na ye utotoor aanann la. Israel yaab bimɔk choo Silo ki nan toor kitork na, bi nan ŋani bi mɔmɔk kina la; 15ki ki kpee na, waahr aan bi nin di nkpan na pu mmii ni mu ti wu doo na, utotoor aatutunn ngbaan ga dan ki nan bui unii u bi toor kitork ngbaan na ke, “Tii mi tinann tibaa m ti tii utotoor aan u pu; waan gaa saah ŋaa ti na, u ban tinankaab baanja la.”
16Udaan yaa bui ke, “Cha ti ŋa ikaal aah mɔk pu na waahr, ki pu nkpan aan aa nin lee saah ban pu na” kan, le utotoor aatutunn ngbaan ga bui ke, “Aayii. Di ti tii mi dandana wee. Aa yaa yii kan, m ga di mpɔɔn le lee ti.”
17Baah nan lik seen Uwumbɔr aatork pu na, Eli aajapɔtiib aatunwanbir ngbaan nan bir Uwumbɔr chee pam.
Samuel aah nan bi Silo ni pu na
18N‑yoonn mue na Samuel u nan laa ye ubo na nan beenin bi tun Uwumbɔr aatuln, ki pee libɔkul li bitotoorb peeni na. 19Libiln mɔmɔk kan, una nan luu libɔkul waatiir, le ki joo ti tii u, buyoonn u cheeni uchal ke u ti toor libiln libiln aatork na. 20Le Eli ga ŋa Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa Elkana ni upuu pu, ki bui Elkana ke, “Uwumbɔr tii si mbim muken upii wee chee aan bi leŋ naah di ubo u tii u na aaleleŋ.”
Nee aapuwɔb le bi gir kun.
21Uwumbɔr mu nan sil ŋa waanyoor ŋa Hana pu, le u nan ki ma mbijabim mutaa, ni mpiibim mulee. Samuel nan fii ki chikr Uwumbɔr aatuln ponn ni la.
Eli ni ujapɔtiib aabɔr
22N‑yoonn mue Eli nan por pam. U nan beenin ŋun ujapɔtiib aah nan ŋani Israel yaab mbiin pu na, ni baah kpaan doo bipiib bi tun lituln Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb na chee pu na. 23Le u bui bi ke, “Ba ŋa ni ŋani tiwan nimina mɔmɔk? Binib mɔmɔk tuk mi naah tun titunwanbir ti na la. 24Njapɔtiib, di cha man ni. Tiwan ni Uwumbɔr aanib len naabɔr na aa ŋan kpala. 25Unibɔn yaa tun uŋeen aatɔ taani kan, nibaakan Uwumbɔr ga san u kinimbaak, tɔ, ŋma ga ter unii u tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir na?”
Le baa pel bite aah len pu na, ba pu? Uwumbɔr nan siin ke u ku bi.
26Samuel nan beenin chikr cha, le ki kpa kipak binib ni Uwumbɔr mu chee.
Uwumbɔr kpiir Eli aadichal aabɔr len
27Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ubaa nan dan Eli chee ki joo ni Uwumbɔr aanaŋ yee ke: “Aayaaja Aaronn ni waadichal aah nan ye binaagbiib Ijipt aatiŋ aabɔr Faro chee na, m nan di mbaa mɔk Aaronn. 28Israel aamaal mɔmɔk ponn ni, m nan lee waadichal le ke bi li ye maatotoorb, ki li toor kitork libimbiln paab, ki see tiwan ni nu mɔ na, ki li pee bitotoorb aawanpeenkaan, ki li bi maadiik ni. M mu nan tii bi nsan ke bi li yeh kitork aanann ti bi joo seer mmii ponn ni na tibaa. 29Ni ki ŋa kinye aan ni ki lik waa kitork ni ipiin i m ban maanib chee na? Eli, ni ŋa kinye aan aa pak aajapɔtiib ki jer mi, ki cha bi ji maanib aatork aanann ti ŋan sakpen aan bi ba ban bi di tii mi na, ki moo filk cha? 30Min, Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le nan puu n‑yoonn mu jer na ke saadichal ni saamaal le ga li tun maatuln ke bitotoorb na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Le dandana wee m len ke maan ŋa nimi kina. Maah ga ŋa pu na sɔ, m ga nyuŋ binib bi nyuŋni mi na la, le ki lik seen binib bi lik mi fam na. 31Li pel, n‑yoonn choo le m ga ku binachipɔm bimɔk bi saadichal, ni saamaal ponn ni na, le uja ubaa taa ki li bi saadichal ni ki ti por. 32Ni ga li muk si le aa lik ki neen tinyoor ti m ga di tii Israel yaab biken na, le ubaa aan ki li bi saadichal ponn ni ki ti por. 33Tɔ, m ga cha aayaabitiib ponn ni ubaa gur, ki li tun maatuln ke utotoor na, le u mu ga nan jɔb aan utaakpab yɔl, le aayaabitiib bi gur na ga kpo mpɔɔnkun. 34Tiwan ni ga mɔk si ke maah len pu na ga gbiin na le ye ke aajapɔtiib bilee na, Hofni ni Fineas, ga kpaan kpo liwinbaal la. 35Le m ga lee utotoor u ga dii mi mbamɔm, ki ŋani tiwan nimɔk m ban na. M ga tii u yaabitiib bi ga li tun maatuln, maabɔr u m lee u na chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 36Aayaabitiib ponn ni u ŋmar na ga li chaa utotoor ngbaan chee le ki ti mee ŋimombil, ni tijikaar, le ki gaŋ u ke u cha u ter bitotoorb baatuln ni, aan ki kan nibaa ki ti kpiin ubaa.”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks to Samuel
1-2Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room, 3and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long 4when the Lord called out Samuel's name.
“Here I am!” Samuel answered. 5Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?”
“I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.”
Samuel went back.
6Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?”
Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
7The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice. 8When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?”
Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel. 9So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ”
Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
10The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!”
“I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
11The Lord said:
Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it! 12I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised. 13He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever. 14I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
15The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said. 16But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!”
“Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
17Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
18Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.”
The Lord Helps Samuel
19As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true. 20From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet. 21The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah di ubaa mɔk Samuel pu na
1N‑yoonn ngbaan na, buyoonn unachipɔnbo Samuel nan bi tun Uwumbɔr aatuln Eli chee na, Uwumbɔr aa nan ki joo waabɔr naŋni binib sakpen, kaa ki joo ubaa mɔk binib yɔl yɔl. 2Kinyeek kibaa le Eli, u kaa nan ki waa mbamɔm na, nan dɔ geen waadɔdoo chee, 3le Samuel mu dɔ nin chee Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa nan bi na. Waahr aan ni nin woln na, buyoonn karyaa aa nan kee junn na, 4le Uwumbɔr yin Samuel. Samuel nan kii ke, “Maaninkpel, m sɔ,” 5le ki san buen Eli chee ki ti bui ke, “Saah yin mi na, le m dan.”
Le Eli bui u ke, “Maa yin sin, gir ti doon.” Le Samuel gir buen ti doon.
6-7Le Uwumbɔr ki yin Samuel lelee. Ubo ngbaan aa nan nyi ke ni ye Uwumbɔr la, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa nan kee len u chee tibɔr daalbaadaal kina. Le u fii, ki ki buen Eli chee, ki ti bui u ke, “Saah yin mi na, le m dan.”
Le Eli ki bui u ke, “Maabo, maa yin sin, li cha ti doon.”
8Le Uwumbɔr ki yin Samuel taataa, le u fii, ki ki buen Eli chee, ki ti ki bui u ke, “Saah yin mi na, le m dan.”
N‑yoonn ngbaan le Eli bee ke ni ye Uwumbɔr le yin ubo ngbaan, 9le u ki bui u ke, “Gir ti doon; u yaa ki yin si kan, bui ke ‘Uwumbɔr, li len, saatutunn pel la.’” Le Samuel ki gir ti doon.
10Le Uwumbɔr dan nan sil nima, ki yin ke waah ti yin pu na ke, “Samuel, Samuel.”
Le Samuel kii ke, “Li len; saatutunn pel la.”
11Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Nwiin mubaa daal m ga ŋa Israel aanib tiwan nibaa, ni ga li kpa ijawaan, le unii umɔk ŋun ni pu na ga bir, kaan ŋmaa len tibaa. 12Nwiin ngbaan daal le m ga ŋa Eli aadichal tiwan nimɔk m bui ke m ga ŋa li na. 13M puen tuk u ke m ga daa waadichal aatafal ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na; ba pu? ujapɔtiib len mi tibɔr ti kaa ŋan na. Eli nyi ke bi ŋani kina, le kaa sur bi. 14Kina pu na, min le bui Eli ni waadichal ke kitork bee ipiin ibaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa nyan titunwanbir timina aatafadaan.”
15Samuel nan gaar dɔ le kitaak ti woln; le u fii ki piir Uwumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔi. Waa nan kaa ke u bui Eli tibɔr ti Uwumbɔr kpiir tuk u na. 16Eli nan yin u ke, “Maabo Samuel.”
Le Samuel kii ke, “Maaninkpel, m sɔ.”
17Le Eli baa u ke, “Uwumbɔr tuk si ke ba? Taa di tibaa bɔr mi. Aa yaa kaa bui mi waah tuk si pu na mɔmɔk kan, Uwumbɔr ga daa aatafal pam.” 18Kina pu le Samuel bui u ti mɔmɔk; waa nan di tibaa bɔr u. Le Eli bui ke, “Uma le ye Uwumbɔr. Cha u ŋa waah ban pu na.”
19Samuel aah chikr cha na, le Uwumbɔr nan bi u chee ki cha Samuel aah len pu na mɔmɔk gbiini kina. 20Kina pu le Israel aanib mɔmɔk, bi bi Israel aatiŋ ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni na bee ke Samuel nan sil ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr la. 21Uwumbɔr nan beenin joo ubaa mɔk Samuel, Silo aatiŋ ni, ki kpiir waabɔr tuk u nima chee. Samuel yaa len pu na kan, Israel aanib mɔmɔk pel la.

english_text:
1Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel.
The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest
One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek. 2The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about 4,000 of them.
3The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
4 The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest.
As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, 5brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook. 6The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?”
When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp, 7they were scared to death and said:
The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before. 8We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
9Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
10The Philistines did fight. They killed 30,000 Israelite soldiers, and all the rest ran off to their homes. 11Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured.
Eli Dies
12That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow. 13He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying.
Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting. 14-15He was 98 years old and blind, but he could hear everyone crying, and he asked, “What's all that noise?”
The soldier hurried over and told Eli, 16“I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.”
“Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
17“Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
18Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for 40 years.
19The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard, 20and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!”
She didn't pay any attention to them. 21-22Instead she kept thinking about losing her husband and her father-in-law. So she said, “My son will be named Ichabod, because the glory of Israel left our country when the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_text:
Bidim aah gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa pu na
1N‑yoonn ngbaan le Filistia yaab kuun ke bi tak Israel yaab, le Israel yaab mu gor ki kii bi. Israel yaab nan ti tiŋ kal Ebeneser ni la, le Filistia yaab mu tiŋ kal Afek ni. 2Filistia yaab le nan puen buen ti tak Israel yaab, le bi too butɔb sakpem nima, le bi nyaŋ Israel yaab ki ku binib ŋichur ŋinaa butɔb ngbaan ponn ni. 3Bijab bi nan ŋmar na aah nan fuu ni baah nan tiŋ ka nin chee na, le Israel aayidam bui ke, “Ni ŋa kinye aan Uwumbɔr cha Filistia yaab ngbaan nyaŋ timi din wee? Cha ti buen Silo man, ki ti yoor ni Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa, aan u dii timi buen ki ti gaa timi lii timi aadim chee.” 4Le bi tun binib Silo aatiŋ ni, ke bi ti yoor ni Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan u bi tiwan ni kpa ifeen na aapaacham na Aakaal Aadakaa. Le Eli aajapɔtiib bilee na, Hofni ni Fineas, mu dii buen.
5Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan aah fuu ni na, le Israel yaab faa kifuuk le kitiŋ ti dam. 6Filistia yaab ŋun kifuuk ngbaan pu le ki bui ke, “Li pel man Hiibru yaab ngbaan aakakaa chee aah kpa kifuuk pu na. Naatataa ye kinye?” Baah bee ke Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa le fuu ni Hiibru yaab chee na, 7le ijawaan chuu bi, le bi bui ke, “Liwaal libaa le dan bi chee. Ti bi tibɔr ni. Tiwan nee aaboln aa kee ŋa kina. 8Ŋma ga gaa timi ŋiwaapɔɔndam ŋee chee lii? Ŋiwaa ŋi nan ku doo Ijipt yaab nteer ponn ni na le bi na. 9Filistia yaab, moo boon man. Boon man ke bijab na, naa ye kina kan, ti ga kpaln Hiibru yaab aanaagbiib, ke baah nan ye timi aanaagbiib pu na. Kina pu na, boon man ke bijab na.”
10Filistia yaab nan nyal baan le ki nyaŋ Israel yaab, le bi san kun. Bi nan ku bi pam, bi nan ku Israel aajab ŋichur piitaa la, 11le ki gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa, ki ku Eli aajapɔtiib, Hofni ni Fineas.
Eli aah kpo pu na
12Benjaminn aamaal ponn ni aaja ubaa nan nyan ni butɔb ngbaan ni, ki san nan fuu Silo liyaadaal ngbaan. U nan daa kar waawanpeenkaan, ki di titan mu puŋ uyil ke ni mɔk usui aah bii pu na. 13Eli, u nan ka lijal pu nsan chee, aan Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aabɔr muk u sakpen na, nan ka lik nsan pu. Uja ngbaan nan di tibɔr ngbaan moon kitiŋ ponn ni, le ijawaan chuu binib mɔmɔk, le bi wii. 14Eli nan ŋun kifuuk ngbaan pu le ki baa ke, “Ba aafuuk bi na?” Le uja ngbaan san mala buen Eli chee ki ti bui u tibɔr ngbaan. 15Eli nan ye ŋibin imonko inaa ni kipiik ni ŋiniin aanii le n‑yoonn ngbaan, kaa ki waa mbamɔm. 16Uja ngbaan nan bui u ke, “M san ŋmar butɔb ni la, le ki san nyan ni nima, ki nan fuu ni do din.”
Le Eli baa u ke, “Maabo, ba ŋa?”
17Le u ki bui u ke, “Israel yaab san Filistia yaab chee; bi nyaŋ Israel yaab kookoo a. Ki ki kpee na, aajapɔtiib Hofni ni Fineas bee butɔb ni; le bi gaa ti chee Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa mu a.”
18Uja ngbaan aah pur Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aabɔr na, le Eli nyan lijal pu ki lir upuwɔb, mbisamɔb chee. U nan por pam, ki filk mu, le waah lir kina na usil koo, le u kpo. U nan ye Israel aayidaan ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee la.
Fineas aakpopii mu aah kpo pu na
19Eli aabipuu, Fineas aapuu, nan dek, ki nan yak timar. Waah ŋun ke bi gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa, ni uchooja ni uchal aakun aabɔr na, le imalween kpaan chuu u, le u ma. 20Waah ban u kpo na, le bipiib bi nan bi ter u na bui u ke, “Chuu aabaa. Aa kan ubijabo la.” Le u ŋmin, kaa gaar bi. 21U nan yin ubo ngbaan ke Ikabod, ki kpiir len laatataa ke, “Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn siir cha Israel yaab a;” ki joo mɔk baah gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa na, ni uchooja ni uchal aah kpo pu na. 22Le u bui ke, “Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn siir cha Israel yaab; ba pu? bi gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa a.”

english_text:
God Causes Trouble for the Philistines
1The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod. 2They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
3When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged. 4But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway. 5This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
6The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic. 7Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
8The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?”
“Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there, 9the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened, 10so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!”
The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
11The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.”
Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die, 12and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aah nan bi Filistia yaab chee pu na
1Filistia yaab aah jan ki gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa na, bi nan yoor u nyan Ebeneser aatiŋ ponn ni, ki di buen baatiŋ Asdod ni, 2ki di u buen baawaal Dagonn aadiik ponn ni, ki di u siin gbaŋ liwaal ngbaan. 3Naah woln kichakpinaanyeek ni na, le Asdod aanib kan ke liwaal Dagonn li nan si na lir chiŋ, ki dɔ kitiŋ, Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aanimbiin ni. Le bi fiin li siin laabuul ni. 4Naah ki woln kichakpinaanyeek ni na, bi ki kan ke liwaal ngbaan ki lir dɔ Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aanimbiin ni. N‑yoonn mumina ma liyil ni laaŋaal ilee mɔmɔk wii wii ki ti dɔ mbisamɔb chee; ni nan gur liwon baanja la. 5Nima pu le Asdod aawaal Dagonn aawaadam, ni binib bi dii li na aa taar mbisamɔb nima chee. Bi lakr ni pu le ki jer, ki nan saa din wee.
6Uwumbɔr nan daa Asdod yaab aatafal sakpen, le ni ŋa bi ijawaan. U nan cha iween i naahn ŋichakpelar ki ku bi na lir bi pu; le ŋisayik mu gbiin Asdod aatiŋ ni, ni ntim mu bi ki mann goln ki na. 7Baah kan tiwan ni bi ŋani bi na, le bi bui ke, “Israel yaab Aawumbɔr le bi dar timi ni timi aawaal Dagonn aatafal. Taan ki cha Waakaal Aadakaa ngbaan li bi do.” 8Kina pu le bi nan tun yin ni Filistia aabɔrb biŋmu ngbaan nan kpaan, ki baa bi ke, “Ti ga ŋa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa wee kinye?”
Le bi bui ke, “Di u buen Gaf aatiŋ ni man;” le bi di u buen Gaf aatiŋ ponn ni, ki mu ki ye Filistia yaab aatiŋ kiken la. 9Dakaa ngbaan aah fuu nima chee na, le Uwumbɔr ki daa nima yaab mu aatafal ki cha bipobil yuk. U nan cha iween i naahn ŋichakpelar na ki ku bi mu, mbim ni bininkpiib mɔmɔk. 10Le bi yoor Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan buen Filistia yaab aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Ekronn na ponn ni; le nima aanib teen ke, “Bi joo ni Israel yaab Aawumbɔr Aadakaa do, ke bi nan ku ti mɔmɔk la.” 11Le bi ki gir yin Filistia aabɔrb biŋmu na ki nan bui bi ke, “Giin man Israel yaab Aakaal Aadakaa buen waabuul ni, aan u taa ku timi ni timi aadichal ni yaab.” Ijawaan nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ponn ni; ba pu? Uwumbɔr nan bi dar bitafal sakpen. 12Binib bi kaa nan kpoi na, iween ngbaan nan duun duun bi, le binib ngbaan mee baawaa ke ŋi ter bi.

english_text:
1After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months, 2the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
3“Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
4“What should we send?” the Philistines asked.
The priests and fortunetellers answered:
There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have. 5So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops. 6Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
7Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn. 8Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
9Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
10The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn. 11Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
12The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
13The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
14-15The cows left the road and pulled the cart into a field that belonged to Joshua from Beth-Shemesh, and they stopped beside a huge rock. Some men from the tribe of Levi were there. So they took the chest off the cart and placed it on the rock, and then they did the same thing with the bag of gold rats and sores. A few other people chopped up the cart and made a fire. They killed the cows and burned them as sacrifices to the Lord. After that, they offered more sacrifices.
16When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
17That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. 18They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened.
The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
19Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed 70 of them. This made the people of Beth-Shemesh very sad, 20and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
21They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_text:
Baah di Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa giin pu na
1Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aah nan bi Filistia yaab aatiŋ ponn ni ki ti saa iŋmal ilole aapuwɔb na, 2le binib ngbaan yin ni bitotoorb, ni binib bi joo inyɔk tun lituln na, ki nan baa bi ke, “Ti ga ŋa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan kinye? Ti yaa di u ke ti di giin waah nyan ni nin chee na kan, ti ga di ba kpee u pu ki di u giin?”
3Le bi bui ke, “Ni yaa ga giin Israel yaab Aawumbɔr Aadakaa kan, ni ŋan ke ni tii ipiin i ga ti pa nimi aatunwanbir pu na. Dakaa ngbaan aan ŋmaa gir iŋaalkuun. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga pɔɔk, le ni ga bee naah ŋa pu aan u dar nitafal na.”
4Le binib ngbaan baa ke, “Ba aapiin aan ti ga di tun?”
Le bi bui ke, “Salmaa ŋisayik aanaŋ ŋiŋmu, ni salmaa ŋichakpelar aanaŋ ŋiŋmu, ubaa mɔmɔk le si Filistia yaab aabɔr ubaa mɔmɔk aasisii. Tibɔbir baan ngbaan le u nan di tun tii ni mɔmɔk, ni bibɔrb biŋmu ngbaan mu pu. 5Ni di salmaa naan ŋichakpelar ngbaan, ni ŋisayik ŋi bii nimi aatiŋ aajikaar na, ki di bunyuŋ tii Israel yaab Aawumbɔr. Nibaakan u ga di cha, kaan ki daa nimi, ni nimi aawaa aatafal, kaan ki bii nimi aatiŋ. 6Ba ŋa nitafal pɔɔ ke Ijipt aabɔr ni waanib aatafal aah nan pɔɔ pu na? Taa suln man Uwumbɔr aah nan ŋa bi falaa aan ki ti nin cha Israel yaab nyan baatiŋ ponn ni pu na. 7Kina pu na, ŋa man inaa aatɔroku pɔɔn, ki ban inaa ilee i baa kee cha i dar tɔroku daalbaadaal na, ki di tɔroku ngbaan tul i pu, ki jenn giin yaanaabi koon kinaabak ponn ni. 8Yoor man Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa di tɔŋ tɔroku ngbaan pu, ki di salmaa aawan aapiin i ni joo tun nimi aatunwanbir pu na ŋa dakaa ponn ni, ki di siin gbaŋ Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan, ki cha inaa ngbaan li dar tɔroku ngbaan cha, ubaa taa dii i, 9ki li si lik i, i li cha; i yaa di toŋ Bef Semes aatiŋ ni kan, ni mɔk ke Israel yaab Aawumbɔr le tun ni nimi tibɔbir sakpen ngbaan. I yaa kaa toŋ nima kan, ti ga bee ke naa ye uma le tun ni tibɔbir ngbaan, ti dan tibaa pu la.”
10Bi nan ŋa baah mɔk bi ke bi ŋa pu na: bi nan chuu inaa ilee le ki di tɔroku ngbaan tul i pu, le ki di inaabi laŋ kinaabak ponn ni. 11Bi nan di Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan ni dakaa u kpa salmaa aawan ngbaan na ŋa tɔroku ngbaan ponn ni. 12Inaa ngbaan nan siir le ki di toŋ Bef Semes ki kpaa tok ki, kaa par nsan ni nibaa chee. I nan cha le ki wooni. Filistia aabɔrb biŋmu ngbaan nan dii i ki ti saa Bef Semes aatiŋ mɔk.
13Bef Semes yaab nan bi chee tijikaar kifataŋ ponn ni, le ki yaar lik ki kan Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan. Baah nan kan u na, le ni mɔɔr bi naa ti sɔ. 14Le inaa ni tɔroku ngbaan di nan fuu bukpaab bubaa ni, bu nan ye uja u bi yin u ke Josua aan u koo Bef Semes ni na aakpaab la, le ki sil nima litakpasakpeln libaa chee. Le binib ngbaan chuu gaa nyan ŋikpan aatɔroku ngbaan ki kɔr inaa ngbaan toor kitork ki di see mmii ni tii Uwumbɔr. 15Le Liifai yaab chuu nyan Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa, ni dakaa u kpa salmaa aawan na mu, le ki di bi toŋ litakpasakpeln ngbaan pu. Le Bef Semes aanib toor kitork ki di see mmii ponn ni, ni kitork kiken, tii Uwumbɔr. 16Filistia aabɔrb biŋmu ngbaan nan si lik bi, le bi ŋa ni mɔmɔk ti doo, le bi gir kun Ekronn liyaadaal ngbaan.
17Filistia yaab aah nan tii Uwumbɔr salmaa aachakpelar aanaŋ aawan niŋmu ni ke ipiin i ga pa baatunwanbir pu na, nan si ntim muŋmu mue: Asdod, ni Gasa, ni Askelonn, ni Gaf, ni Ekronn aasisii la. 18Bi nan ki tii salmaa aasayik ŋiŋmu mu, libaa mɔmɔk nan si tii ntim mu Filistia aabɔrb biŋmu na nan joo mu na la, mu bi nan maa ŋigon gob na, ni itingbaan i kaa kpa ŋigon na. Litakpasakpeln li pu bi nan di Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa toŋ, aan li bi Josua u koo Bef Semes aatiŋ ponn ni na aakpaab ni na, beenin bi nima din wee ki ye seeraa.
19Uwumbɔr nan ku Bef Semes aajab imonko itaa ni kipiik, ba pu? bi nan lik Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan ponn ni la. Le binib ngbaan nan wii ikpowiil, Uwumbɔr aah tun bi litusakpeln pu na.
Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aah kun Kiriaf Jearim pu na
20Kina pu le Bef Semes aajab bui ke, “Ŋma ga ŋmaa sil Tidindaan Uwumbɔr u bi chain na aanimbiin ni? Ti ga di dakaa ngbaan buen la chee ki cha tibaa?” 21Le bi tun binib Kiriaf Jearim aanib chee ke bi ti len ke, “Filistia yaab di Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa giin ni. Dan ki nan yoor u man.”

english_text:
1 The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it, 2and it stayed there for 20 years.
During this time everyone in Israel was very sad and begged the Lord for help.
The People of Israel Turn Back to the Lord
3One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
4The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
5Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
6The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord.
The Philistines Attack Israel
7When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel.
The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming. 8“Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
9-10 Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away. 11The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
12-13The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them.
For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines. 14The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath.
Israel was also at peace with the Amorites.
Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
15Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life. 16Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people. 17Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_text:
1Le Kiriaf Jearim aajab buen ti yoor Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ki di buen uja ubaa u bi yin u ke Abinadab na aadichal, ligongoln paab, ki nan nyan ujapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Eleasar na ke u li lik dakaa ngbaan.
Samuel aah joo Israel yaab pu na
2Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa nan yunn Kiriaf Jearim aatiŋ ni pam, u nan pii nima ŋibin moninko. N‑yoonn mue na, Israel yaab mɔmɔk nan wii ki ban nterm Uwumbɔr chee la.
3Le Samuel bui Israel aanib ke, “Ni yaa ban ke ni fenn ki gir ni Uwumbɔr chee kan, see ni nyan ŋiwaa, ni liwaapii Astaate aanaŋ ŋi bi nikaasisik ni na, ki di nibaa tii Uwumbɔr kookoo, ki li dooni uma baanja, le u ga gaa nimi Filistia yaab aapɔɔn chee lii.” 4Kina pu le Israel yaab nyan ŋiwaa Baal ni Astaate mae, le ki dooni Uwumbɔr baanja.
5Le Samuel tun yin Israel yaab mɔmɔk ke bi ti kuun Mispa aatiŋ ni, le ki len ke, “M ga ti mee Uwumbɔr tii nimi, nima chee.” 6Kina pu le bi mɔmɔk kuun Mispa ni. Bi nan ban nnyun le ki kpir tii Uwumbɔr, le ki lul bumɔb liyaadaal, nwiin ti lir. Bi nan len ke, “Ti tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir.” Mispa ni, nima chee, le Samuel nan toor Israel yaab bi nan kpa tɔb tibɔr na aakaasisik ni.
7Filistia yaab aah ŋun ke Israel yaab kuun Mispa ponn ni na, le Filistia aabɔrb biŋmu na, ni baajab, fii buen ke bi ti tak bi. Israel yaab nan ŋun bi pu, le ijawaan chuu bi, 8le bi bui Samuel ke, “Li beenin mee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aan u gaa timi Filistia yaab bee chee lii.” 9Le Samuel kɔr upiih, ki toor kitork, ki di see mmii ponn ni tii Uwumbɔr, le ki mee Uwumbɔr ke u ter Israel yaab, le Uwumbɔr kii waameel ngbaan. 10Buyoonn Samuel bi toor kitork ngbaan na, le Filistia yaab dan ke bi nan tak bi. Libuul ngbaan ni, le Uwumbɔr teen paacham ke utaal na, bi pu. Le bilan ŋmal, le ijawaan chuu bi, le bi san. 11Le Israel aajab nyan Mispa ni, ki di paan Filistia yaab ngbaan pu, ki ti ban bi koo Bef Kar, ki ku bi ki cha.
12Samuel nan yoor litakpal ki di ŋum Mispa ni Senn aakaasisik ni, ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr le ter timi ki nan saa din,” le ki yin li ke, “Nterm Aatakpal.” 13Kina le Uwumbɔr nan nyaŋ Filistia yaab, le kaa ki cha bi koo ni Israel yaab aatiŋ ponn ni n‑yoonn mumɔk Samuel nan bi limɔfal ponn ni na. 14Filistia yaab nan giin Israel aatim mu bi Ekronn ni Gaf aatim aakaasisik ni aan bi nan jenn gaa na, tii Israel yaab, kina pu na, Israel yaab nan ki kan baatiŋ mɔmɔk. Le nsuudoon mu dan Israel yaab ni Kanaann yaab aakaasisik ni.
15Samuel le nan joo Israel yaab buyoonn u nan bi limɔfal ponn ni na. 16Libiln mɔmɔk ni kan, u nan chuun ki manni Betel, ni Gilgal, ni Mispa, ki toor binib bi kpa tɔb tibɔr na aakaasisik ni, 17le ki gir buen waatiŋ Rama ponn ni, nin chee u ti ki ye ubɔlen na. U nan maa kitork aabimbiln Rama aatiŋ ni tii Uwumbɔr.

english_text:
The People of Israel Want a King
1-2Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba. 3But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
4One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah 5 and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
6Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it. 7The Lord answered:
Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king. 8Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you. 9Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
10Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
11If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot. 12Some of them will be officers in charge of 1,000 soldiers, and others will be in charge of 50. Still others will have to farm the king's land and harvest his crops, or make weapons and parts for his chariots. 13Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
14The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials. 15He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
16The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work. 17He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves, 18and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
19-20The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
21Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said. 22“Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.”
Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_text:
Israel aanib aah ban ubɔr pu na
1Samuel aah nan ti por na, le u di ujapɔtiib ŋa bibɔlem Israel yaab ponn ni. 2Bi nan yin ujapɔpol ke Joel, le ki yin uwaatiir mu ke Abija. Bi nan ye bibɔlem Beerseba ponn ni la. 3Bi mu aa nan tee dii bite aasan. Baalandak nan ye le ke bi kan ŋimombil, kina pu na, bi nan gaal igaŋgaŋlik, kaa nan ji tibɔr mbamɔm.
4Le Israel aayidam mɔmɔk kuun tɔb, ki di buen Samuel chee Rama aatiŋ ni, 5le ki ti bui u ke, “Lik, aa bi por la, le aajapɔtiib mu aa dii saasan. Kina pu na, nyan ubɔr u ga li joo timi na, aan ti mu li kpa ubɔr ke ntim muken aah kpa pu na.” 6Baah nan ban pu na aa nan piir Samuel aasui, kina pu le u mee Uwumbɔr, 7le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Ŋun binib ngbaan aah len pu na mɔmɔk. Naa ye sin le bi yii, min le bi yii ke maa ye baabɔr. 8Ki nyan n‑yoonn mu m nyan ni bi Ijipt na, le bi fenn bipuwɔb tii mi, ki dooni ŋiwaa, le dandana wee bi bi ŋani si tiwan ni bi ŋani mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na. 9Kina pu na, ŋun tii bi, ki tee sak bi, ki kpiir tuk bi baabɔr ngbaan aah ga nan li ŋani bi pu na.”
10Le Samuel bui binib bi nan dan nan bui u ke u nyan ubɔr tii bi na Uwumbɔr aah len pu na mɔmɔk. 11Samuel nan kpiir tuk bi ke, “Kina le nimi aabɔr ngbaan ga nan li joo nimi: u ga di nijapɔtiib ŋa butɔb aajab; bibaa ga li ye butɔb aataan aatɔroku aatutum, biken mu ga li ye waatɔb aajab bi dik itaan pu na, le biken mu ga loln waataan aatɔroku mam pu nsan ki san. 12Bibaa ga li ye bijab lichur aaninkpiib, le biken mu ye bijab piiŋmu aaninkpiib. Nijapɔtiib le ga ko waakpaakon ni, ki chee waajikaar, ki mɔɔ waajawan, ni waataan aatɔroku mam aawan. 13Nibisatiib le ga li ŋani waatulalee mam, ki li ye waasaamɔm, ni bi ŋani maab na. 14U ga gaa nimi aakpaakon i ŋan na, ni ŋisubil aakpaakon i ŋan na, ni ŋikpan aasui i ŋan na ni chee, ki di tii waatun aaninkpiib. 15U ga nan gaa nimi aajikaar ni ndaan aasubil ŋigetek kipiik mɔmɔk ponn ni libaa, ki di tii waachiln ni aaninkpiib, ni bininkpiib bi gur na. 16U ga nan gaa nimi aanaagbiib, ni nimi aanaa, ni ibon i ŋan na le ni li tun waatun. 17U ga nan gaa nimi aawakor ŋigetek kipiik mɔmɔk ponn ni libaa. Le nimi nibaa ga ŋa waanaagbiib. 18N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, ni ga li wii nimi aabɔr u nimi nibaa lee u na aah ŋani nimi pu na, le Uwumbɔr aan gar nimi.”
19Binib ngbaan aa nan pel Samuel aah len pu na, le ki bui ke, “Aayii. Ti ban ubɔr la, 20aan ti mu li bi ke ŋitimbol ŋiken na, ki kpa tibaa aabɔr u ga li joo timi, ki loln ti pu nsan butɔb ni na.” 21Le Samuel nan pel baah len pu na mɔmɔk, le ki buen ti bui Uwumbɔr. 22Le Uwumbɔr gar u ke, “Ŋa baah ban pu na, ki tii bi ubɔr.” Le Samuel bui Israel aajab ngbaan mɔmɔk ke bi gir kun.

english_text:
Saul Meets Samuel
1Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah. 2Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
3Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
4Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys. 5Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
6“Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
7Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
8“I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
9-10“Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets.
Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived. 11As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
12“Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry 13and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
14They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
15The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel, 16“I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
17Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
18Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
19“I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions. 20Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
21“Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.”
Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
22Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About 30 people were there for the dinner, but Samuel gave Saul and his servant the places of honor. 23-24Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.”
The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.”
After Saul and Samuel had finished eating, 25they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house, 26and Saul slept there.
About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.”
Saul got up. He and Samuel left together 27and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.”

translation_text:
Sɔɔl aah kan Samuel pu na
1Uwankpadaan ubaa nan bi n‑yoonn ngbaan, bi nan yin u ke Kis, u ye Benjaminn aanibol aanii la. Ute le nan ye Abiel, le uyaaja ye Seror, ki ye Bekoraf aadiik ni aanii, ki ye Afia aataŋaal ponn ni aadichal. 2U nan kpa japɔɔn ubaa bi yin u ke Sɔɔl. Sɔɔl nan ye unachipɔɔn u ŋan na la, le ki nan paa Israel yaab aanii mɔmɔk pu liyil, le ki ŋan jer bi mɔmɔk.
3Kis aabon ibaa le nan wɔŋ, le u bui Sɔɔl ke, “Di maatutum ponn ni ubaa buen ti ban maabon ngbaan.” 4Bi nan buen Efraim aatiŋ ki ŋigongon wiir nima na, ni Salisa aapepel wɔb, le kaa kan i, kina pu le bi nyan nima ki buen Saalim aapepel mu, le kaa kan i nima mu. Le bi bɔ dii Benjaminn aapepel ponn ni, le kaa ki kan i. 5Baah nan ti fuu Suf aapepel na, le Sɔɔl bui waatutum ngbaan ke, “Cha ti gir kun linampal, naa yee kina kan, nte ga li gur dak ti pu la. Waan ki li dak ibon ngbaan pu.”
6Le ututunn ngbaan gar u ke, “Cha m dan waahr. Uja ubaa bi kitiŋ kee ponn ni ki ye Uwumbɔr aanii, le binib mɔmɔk nyuŋni u; ba pu? waah len pu na mɔmɔk gbiini la. Cha ti buen u chee; nibaakan u ga ŋmaa mɔk timi nin chee ibon ngbaan bi na.”
7Le Sɔɔl baa ke, “Ti yaa buen u chee kan, ti ga ti tii u ba? Tijikaar tibaa aa ki gur timi aatuln ponn ni, le taa ki kpa nibaa mu, aan ti kpa ba?”
8Le ututunn ngbaan gar u ke, “M kpa tikunabr aamombil siib. M ga ŋmaa di ŋima tii u, le u ga mɔk timi taah ga kan i nin chee na.”
9-11Le Sɔɔl kii u ke, “Ti ŋan. Ti li cha.” Le bi siir buen kitiŋ ki ponn ni Uwumbɔr aanii ngbaan koo na. Baah bi joi ligongoln ki cha kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, le bi ton bisapɔm bibaa nsan ni, bi nan cha bi ti lu nnyun. Le bi baa bisapɔm ngbaan ke, “Ukakann na bi kitiŋ ni ii?”
N‑yoonn ngbaan bi nan yin Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ke ukakann la, kina pu na, unii yaa nan ban u baa Uwumbɔr mbaa kan, u ga bui le ki, “Cha ti buen ukakann na chee.”
12-13Le bisapɔm ngbaan kii bi ke, “Een, u bi. Mbamɔn, uma le kpaan bi nimɔb pu na. Ni yaa chuun mala kan, ni ga pii u nsan ni. Ni yaa ti kpaan koo kitiŋ ponn ni kan, ni ga kan u. Din wee le u fuu ni kitiŋ ni do; ba pu? binib ngbaan ban bi toor kitork, kitork aabimbiln paab ligongoln pu la. Baah yin ni binib bi na aan ŋmaa piin tijikaar aajim see u fuu nima waahr, ba pu? uma le ga mee Uwumbɔr kitork ngbaan pu. Ni yaa buen dandana wee kan, ni ga kan u waahr aan u nin buen ligongoln pu ke u ti ji.” 14Le Sɔɔl ni waatutunn siir cha kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Baah ban bi koo ki ponn ni na, le bi kan Samuel chaa nyan ni, ki bi nsan pu, ki cha nin chee bi ga ti doon Uwumbɔr na.
15Ki nin woln bundaal aan Sɔɔl kan Samuel na, Uwumbɔr nan bui Samuel ke, 16“Fen kinakokoona, m ga fe tun ni uja ubaa aa chee. U nyan ni Benjaminn aanibol ponn ni la. Toor u ki di u kaan nnaan, u li joo maanib Israel yaab. Le u ga gaa bi Filistia yaab chee lii. M kan maanib ngbaan aafalaa, ki ŋun baah wii pu ki ban nterm na.”
17Samuel aah yaar tuu Sɔɔl pu na, le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Uja wee le m tuk si waabɔr na. Uma le ga joo maanib.” 18Le Sɔɔl buen Samuel u nan si gbɔk mbisamɔb na chee, le ki bui u ke, “Uninkpel, mɔk mi ukakann na aah koo nin chee na.”
19Le Samuel gar u ke, “Min le ye ukakann ngbaan. Loln man m pu nsan, ki li cha nin chee bi dooni Uwumbɔr na. Nimi bilee ngbaan ga ji m chee tijikaar din wee. Fen kichakpiik ni, le m ga fe gar mbaan mumɔk ni kpa ke ni baa mi na, ki nin cha ni li chaa kun. 20Ni yaa gur ibon i nan wɔŋ iwiin itaa i jer na aabɔr kan, taa cha ni li muk nimi; bi kan i a. Tɔ, ŋma aan Israel aanib ban sakpen? Ni ye sin la, sin ni aate aadichal.”
21Le Sɔɔl gar u ke, “M ye Benjaminn aanibol ni aanii la, le linibol ngbaan mu le ye li par sakpen Israel aanibol mɔmɔk ponn ni na. Le maadichal mu le aa ki kpa liyimbil linibol ngbaan ponn ni. Kina pu na, ni ŋa kinye aan aa len m chee tibɔr tee aaboln?”
22Le Samuel di Sɔɔl ni waatutunn ngbaan koo kidisakpeŋ kibaa ponn ni, le ki tii bi bininyuum aakakaa chee ŋijal, nin chee bicham ga nan li pii piitaa ki ka na. 23Le Samuel bui usaamɔnn ke, “Li joo ni linankpiln li m ba di tii si ke aa di bil mi na.” 24Le usaamɔnn ngbaan ti joo ni linankpiln li ye litaal aanann na, ki nan di siin Sɔɔl aanimbiin ni. Le Samuel bui Sɔɔl ke, “Lik, linankpiln li m ba di bil si na sɔ. Ŋmɔ li. M lee li bil si ke aa ni maacham bee nan kpaan aan aa ŋmɔ li.”
Le Sɔɔl ni Samuel nan kpaan ki jin tijikaar liyaadaal ngbaan. 25Baah fii nima ki buen kitiŋ ponn ni na, le bi tii Sɔɔl ndɔdooyaan kidiik paab, le u doon nima.
Samuel aah gor Sɔɔl ke u di u kaan nnaan pu na
26Kichakpinaanyeek ni le Samuel yin Sɔɔl kidiik aapaacham nima ke, “Fii, aan m chɔi si.” Le Sɔɔl fii, le u ni Samuel kpaan buen kitiŋ ponn ni. 27Baah ti ban bi nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, le Samuel bui Sɔɔl ke, “Bui ututunn ngbaan ke u loln ti pu nsan ki li cha.” Le ututunn ngbaan siir, le Samuel ki bui Sɔɔl ke, “Sil do siib, aan m bui si Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.”

english_text:
1Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him:
The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people. 2When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
3Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine. 4After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
5Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
6The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them. 7After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
8Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next.
Saul Goes Back Home
9As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said. 10When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
11Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
12 “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
13After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
14Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?”
Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
15“And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
16Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king.
The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
17Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord. 18When everyone had arrived, Samuel said:
The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
19God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
20Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe. 21Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
22The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?”
“Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
23The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else. 24“Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!”
The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
25Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
26God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him. 27But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_text:
1Le Samuel yoor likpasambil ki di mu kpir Sɔɔl aayil pu, ki moor utakpiln, le ki bui u ke, “Uwumbɔr le toor si ke aa li ye Israel aanib aajojoor. Sin le ga li joo waanib ki kii bi, baadim taa pii bi. Nimina le ga li ye seeraa u ga mɔk ke Uwumbɔr lee si ke aa li ye waanib aajojoor na: 2aa yaa nyan m chee do din ki cha kan, aa ga ti kan bijab bilee bibaa Rachel aakaakul chee, Selsa aatiŋ ni, ki bi Benjaminn aatiŋ ni na. Bi ga bui si ke saah nan bi ban ibon i na, bi kan i a, le aate aa ki dak i pu, ki gur dak sin pu la, le ki baa n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke, ‘M ga ŋa maabo aabɔr tee kinye?’ 3Aa yaa nyan nima chee kan, aa ga di ti saa Tabor aasusakpem bubaa chee, le ki ki kan bijab bitaa bibaa bi cha Betel ke bi ti toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr. Bi ponn ni ubaa ga li dar iŋoob i laa diin na itaa, le uken mu ga li tu ŋiboroboro kpin ŋitaa, le utatar na tu ŋisubil aadaan aadabuul. 4Bi ga doon si, le ki nyan ŋiboroboro kpin ŋilee tii si, le aa gaa. 5Aa yoor ti fuu Uwumbɔr Aagongoln li bi Gibea ni na, aa ga kan Filistia yaab kuun ki bi nima. Kitiŋ ngbaan aabisamɔb chee, aa ga kan Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib bibaa nyan ligongoln paab, Uwumbɔr aatork aabimbiln chee, ki sunn choo ki gbaa tibar ni ŋigangan, ki pii ŋiwul mam. Bi ga li bi pak Uwumbɔr, Waafuur Nyaan aapɔɔn pu. 6Libuul ngbaan ni le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan ga gbiin si, le aa ga kpaan bi chee, baah bi pak Uwumbɔr, Waafuur Nyaan aapɔɔn pu pu na, le ki ga kpaln uniyayan. 7Tiwan nee mɔmɔk yaa bi ŋani kan, ŋa Uwumbɔr aah mɔk si pu na mɔmɔk, uma le bi aa chee. 8Aa ga loln m pu nsan ki buen Gilgal, nin chee m ga nan pii si aan ki toor kitork ki ti ga di see mmii ni na, ni kimɔbaan aatork mu. Li kii mi nima ki ti saa iwiin ilole aan m nin dan ki nan mɔk si saah ga ŋa pu na.”
9Sɔɔl aah fenn ke u siir Samuel chee na, le Uwumbɔr tii u mbimbipɔm. Samuel aah nan bui u tibɔr ti mɔmɔk na nan ŋa kina liyaadaal ngbaan. 10Sɔɔl ni waatutunn aah nan ti fuu Gibea na, Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib bibaa nan tooh u nsan ni. Libuul ngbaan ni le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan nan gbiin u, le u buen ti kpaan bi chee ki bi pak Uwumbɔr, Waafuur Nyaan aapɔɔn pu. 11Binib bi nan puun nyi u na kan waah bi ŋani pu na, le ki baa tɔb ke, “Ba ŋa Kis aajapɔɔn wee? Sɔɔl mu kpaln Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr la aa?” 12Uja ubaa u koo nima na le ki baa ke, “Tɔ, ni dak ke bibɔnabr biken na aate ye ŋma?” Nimina pu le tibɔr timina nan piin ke, “Hali Sɔɔl mu kpaln Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr la aa?” 13Sɔɔl aah pak Uwumbɔr kina ki ti doo na, le u buen kitork aabimbiln chee, ligongoln paab.
14Sɔɔl aatewaa aah kan u ni ututunn ngbaan na, le u baa bi ke, “Ni buen la chee?”
Le Sɔɔl bui u ke, “Ti bi ban ibon ngbaan la. Taah kaa kan i na, le ti buen Samuel chee.”
15Le Sɔɔl aatewaa ki baa bi ke, “U ti bui nimi ke ba?”
16Le Sɔɔl ki bui u ke, “U ti bui timi ke bi kan i a,” le kaa bui utewaa Samuel aah bui u ke u ga ŋa ubɔr pu na ma.
Sɔɔl aah jin nnaan pu na
17Samuel nan kuun Israel yaab Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Mispa aatiŋ ni, 18le ki bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr u ye timi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui ke, ‘M nyan ni nimi Ijipt ponn ni, ki gaa nimi lii Ijipt yaab, ni binib bi mɔmɔk nan muk nimi na chee. 19Min le ye nimi Aawumbɔr, u nyan ni nimi tibɔr, ni ŋimuk mɔmɔk ponn ni na, le din wee ni yii mi, le ki bui mi ke m tii nimi ubɔr. Ni ŋan, kina pu na, kuun tɔb man, ki kal ŋinibol ŋinibol, ni imaal imaal, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni.’”
20Le Samuel cha linibol mɔmɔk nyan ni libaabaa, le Uwumbɔr nyan Benjaminn aanibol. 21Le Samuel cha laamaal nyan ni mubaabaa, le Uwumbɔr nyan Matri aamaal. Le Matri aajab nyan ni, le Uwumbɔr nyan Kis aajapɔɔn Sɔɔl. Le bi lik ban u, le kaa kan u, 22le bi baa Uwumbɔr ke, “Waa kee fuu ni ii?”
Le Uwumbɔr bui bi ke, “Sɔɔl le ti bi do wɔb na; u bɔr ŋitun aapuwɔb.”
23Le bi san ti nyan ni Sɔɔl, ki di dan binib ngbaan ponn ni; le bi kan ke u fɔk ki paa unii mɔmɔk pu liyil. 24Le Samuel bui binib ngbaan ke, “Uja u Uwumbɔr lee u na sɔ. Ubaa aa ki bi ti ponn ni ke uma na.”
Le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk teen ke, “Uwumbɔr tii ubɔr na limɔfal li fɔk na.”
25Samuel nan kpiir tuk binib ngbaan ubɔr aasan, ni waatun aah ye pu na, le ki ŋmee ni ŋa kigbaŋ ponn ni, ki di bil Uwumbɔr aadiik ni, le ki cha binib ngbaan mɔmɔk gir kun. 26Sɔɔl mu nan gir kun Gibea. Le bijab bi pɔɔ aan Uwumbɔr meeh bisui na dii u buen. 27Le nifam bibaa bui ke, “Umina ga ŋmaa ŋa ba tii timi?” Bi nan lik seen Sɔɔl, le kaa tii ni u ipiin ibaa. Le Sɔɔl aa len tibaa.

english_text:
Saul Rescues the Town of Jabesh in Gilead
1About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
2Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
3The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
4Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying. 5Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen.
“Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked.
They told him what the men from Jabesh had said. 6Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious. 7Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!”
The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together 8at Bezek. Saul had them organized and counted. There were 300,000 from Israel and 30,000 from Judah.
9Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued.
Everyone was encouraged! 10So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
11The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
12The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
13“No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.”
Saul Is Accepted as King
14“Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
15Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_text:
Sɔɔl aah nyaŋ Amonn yaab pu na
1N‑yoonn ngbaan, le Amonn aabɔrkpaan Nahas di waajab buen bi ti gob ki tak Jabes aatiŋ ki bi Gilead aapepel ponn ni na. Le Jabes aajab bui Nahas ke, “Cha ti ŋa kimɔbaan, aan aa li ye timi aajojoor.”
2Nahas nan gar bi ke, “Ni yaa cha m lokr nyan ni mɔmɔk aanimbigii aan ki jinn Israel yaab mɔmɔk inimɔɔn kan, ti ga ŋmaa ŋa kimɔbaan.”
3Le Jabes aajab aayidam bui ke, “Tiin timi iwiin ilole aan ti tun Israel aatim mɔmɔk ni. Ubaa yaa kaan ter timi kan, ti nin di tibaa tii si.”
4Ntuuntiib ngbaan aah nan ti fuu Gibea, nin chee Sɔɔl koo na, aan binib ngbaan ŋun tibɔr ngbaan na, le bi piin ki bi wii mpombiin pu. 5Sɔɔl nan laa nyan ni kisaak ki joo waanaa choo kun ni la, le ki baa ke, “Ba ŋa? Ba ŋa unii mɔmɔk wii?” Le bi bui u ntuuntiib bi nyan ni Jabes na aah len pu na. 6Sɔɔl aah ŋun kina na, le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan gbiin u, le u pɔɔk nyib, le usui fii, 7le u chuu inaa ilee ki ku i, ki chɔi chɔi yaanann, le ki di tun Israel aatim mɔmɔk ponn ni ki len ke, “Unii umɔk yii kaa dii Sɔɔl ni Samuel ki buen butɔb ni na kan, bi ga ŋa baanaa mu kina la.”
Israel aanib nan san ijawaan Uwumbɔr pu, le bi mɔmɔk kuun tɔb chee, kaa gann ubaa lii. 8Sɔɔl nan kuun bi mɔmɔk Besek ni la: Israel aanib nan ye ŋichur ikui itaa la, le Juda yaab ye ŋichur piitaa. 9Le bi bui Jabes aatuuntiib na ke, “Ti bui man nimi aanib ke waahr aan nwiin fe nan kal kaasisik ni na, bi ga fe gaa bibaa lii.” Jabes aanib aah ŋun kina na, le bisui piir ki ti nyaŋ, 10le bi bui Nahas ke, “Fen kan, ti ga fe di tibaa tii si, le aa ŋa timi saah gee pu na.”
11Kitaak aah ti bi wolni na, le Sɔɔl yakr waajab ŋigetek ŋitaa pu, le lichakpitaawoln bi buen baadim Amonn yaab aah kuun dɔ nin chee na, ki ti tak bi. Joo cha ni nwiin pu na, bi ku doo bi. Bijab bi ŋmar na nan san yaa tɔb chee, bimɔk san ban bibaa.
12Le Israel aanib bui Samuel ke, “Binib bi nan bui ke Sɔɔl taa li ye timi aabɔr na bi la chee? Di bi tii timi aan ti ku bi.”
13Le Sɔɔl bui ke, “Ubaa aan kpo din wee; ba pu? din wee le Uwumbɔr gaa Israel yaab lii.” 14Le Samuel mu bui bi ke, “Cha man ti mɔmɔk buen Gilgal ki ti ki gir kaan Sɔɔl nnaan.” 15Kina pu le bi mɔmɔk buen Gilgal. Nima chee, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, le bi ti ki kaan Sɔɔl nnaan. Bi nan toor kimɔbaan aatork tii Uwumbɔr, le Sɔɔl ni Israel aanib mɔmɔk kpaan jin kitork ngbaan nima chee.

english_text:
Samuel's Farewell Speech
1Samuel told the Israelites:
I have given you a king, just as you asked. 2You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
3 Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
4“No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
5Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.”
“That's true,” they replied.
6 Then Samuel told them:
The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders. 7Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
8 After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land. 9 But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
10 Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
11 The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked. 12 Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
13You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king. 14If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn! 15If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
16Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power. 17Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
18Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel. 19They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
20Samuel answered:
Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart. 21Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble. 22But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
23I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right. 24You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you. 25But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_text:
Samuel aah di tibɔr ti chɔi Israel yaab na
1Le Samuel bui Israel aanib ke, “M ŋa naah bui mi ke m ŋa pu na. M tii nimi ubɔr ke u li ye nimi aajojoor. 2N‑yoonn mue uma le ga li lolni ni pu nsan. M ma kan, n‑yikpir piir, le m por, le njapɔtiib bi ni chee. M nan ye nimi aayidaan tibir ni, ki nan saa din wee. 3Min le na. M yaa ŋa ubaa tibaa kan, galn mi man dandana wee, Uwumbɔr ni waah lee ubɔr u na aanimbiin ni. M gaa ubaa aanaa bee ubaa aabon aa? M jin ubaa pem pem, bee m muk ubaa aa? M gaa ubaa chee igaŋgaŋlik aa? M yaa ŋa nimina ponn ni nibaa kan, m ga pa maah gaa ni na.”
4Binib ngbaan gar u ke, “Aayii, saa jin timi pem pem, kaa muk timi; saa gaa ubaa chee nibaa.”
5Le Samuel giin kii bi ke, “Uwumbɔr, ni waah lee ubɔr u na le ye seeraadam din wee ke maa kpa taani ubaa.”
Le bi kii ke, “Een, Uwumbɔr le ye seeraadaan.”
6Le Samuel ki len ke, “Uwumbɔr le nan lee Moses ni Aaronn, le ki nyan ni niyaajatiib Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 7Tɔ, li si man naah si nin chee na, aan m galn nimi Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, ki teer nimi waah tun ŋitun sakpiin ŋi ki gaa nimi ni niyaajatiib lii na pu. 8Jakob ni waadichal aah nan buen Ijipt, aan Ijipt yaab ti muk bi na, niyaajatiib nan wii ki ban nterm Uwumbɔr chee, le u tun ni Moses ni Aaronn, le bi nan nyan bi Ijipt ponn ni, ki nan di bi kaan kitiŋ kee pu. 9Le binib ngbaan suln Bidindaan Uwumbɔr pu, le u mu cha Filistia yaab, ni Moab yaab aabɔr, ni Sisera, u ye Hasor aatiŋ aajab aaninkpel na, ni niyaajatiib jan, le bi nyaŋ niyaajatiib. 10Le bi wii ki yin Uwumbɔr ke u ter bi, ki bui ke, ‘Uwumbɔr, ti tun titunwanbir; ti fenn tipuwɔb tii si, ki dooni ŋiwaa ŋi bi yin ŋi ke Baal ni Astaate na. Gaa timi, timi aadim chee lii, aan ti li dooni si.’ 11Le Uwumbɔr nan tun ni Gideonn, le ki ki tun Barak, ki di Jefta paan ni, le ki nan di mi gbiln puwɔb. Ti mɔmɔk gaal nimi, nimi aadim chee lir, le ni bi nsuudoon ni. 12Naah nan kan ke Amonn yaab aabɔr Nahas ban u tak nimi na, le ni yii Uwumbɔr ke waa ki ye nimi aabɔr, le ki bui mi ke ni ban ubɔr le u li joo nimi.
13“Tɔ, ubɔr u ni lee u na sɔ do; nimi le ban u, le Uwumbɔr di u tii nimi. 14Nimi ni nimi aabɔr yaa nyuŋ Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ki tun tii u, ki ŋun tii u, ki dii waakaal, ki dii u mbamɔn kan, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii ni mɔmɔk. 15Ni yaa kaa ŋun tii Uwumbɔr, kaa dii waakaal kan, u ga fenn lir nimi ni nimi aabɔr pu la. 16Kina pu na, li si man naah si nin chee na, aan ki kan Uwumbɔr aah ban u ŋa tiwankpaan ni na. 17Ni ye lipeel la, naa ye ee? Tɔ, m ga mee Uwumbɔr, le u ga cha utaal nu ki li tar. Nimina yaa ŋa kan, ni ga bee ke ni tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir ti bir na, ke u tii nimi ubɔr.”
18Samuel nan mee limeel, le Uwumbɔr cha utaal nun ki tar liyaadaal ngbaan. Le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk san Uwumbɔr ni Samuel mu ijawaan, 19le ki bui Samuel ke, “Timi aaninkpel, ti gaŋ si, mee Aadindaan Uwumbɔr tii timi, aan ti taa kpo. Dandana wee ti bee ke taah ki ban ubɔr pu na le ye titunwanbir, ki kpee timi aatunwanbir tiken mɔmɔk pu.”
20Le Samuel bui ke, “Taa san ijawaan man. Naah tun titunwanbir sakpenn ti na, taa fenn nipuwɔb tii Uwumbɔr, li joo nisui mɔmɔk tun tii u man. 21Taa chuun dii ŋiwaa man, ŋi ye yɔli la. Ŋiwaa aan ŋmaa ter nimi, kaan ŋmaa gaa nimi lii mu, ba pu? ŋaa fu. 22Uwumbɔr puu tipuukpaan, kaan suln ni pu. U puu ke nimi le ga li ye waanib. 23M ma kan, Uwumbɔr taa cha m tun titunwanbir ke maan ki mee u tii nimi. M ga mɔk nimi nsan mu ŋan ke ni dii mu na. 24Kii tii Uwumbɔr man, ki di gaakii, ni nisui mɔmɔk tun tii u. Teer man litusakpeln li u tun tii nimi na. 25Ni mu yaa tee yii ki beenin tun titunwanbir kan, nimi, ni nimi aabɔr mɔmɔk ga kuln.”

english_text:
Saul Disobeys the Lord
1Saul was a young man when he became king, and he ruled Israel for two years. 2Then he chose 3,000 men from Israel to be full-time soldiers and sent everyone else home. Two thousand of these troops stayed with him in the hills around Michmash and Bethel. The other 1,000 were stationed with Jonathan at Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin.
