17Maika aajapɔɔn Matania, u aayaaja nan ye Sabdi, u ye Asaf aamaal ponn ni na. Uma le nan ye bilahngaab ni biwangbaab bi gaa ilahn ki dooni Uwumbɔr na aaninkpel.
Bakbukia le nan ye u paa Matania pu na.
Samua aajapɔɔn Abda, u aayaaja nan ye Galal u nyan ni Jedutunn aamaal ponn ni na.
18Liifai yaab bi nan koo Uwumbɔr aatiŋ Jerusalem ponn ni na nan ye binib ikui ilee ni imonko inaa ni binaa la.
Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiib bi mu nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni na aayimbil sɔ:
19Akub, ni Talmonn, ni baamaal nan ti kpaan binib nkub ni imonko itaa ni kipiik ni bilee, le ki koo Jerusalem ponn ni.
20Israel yaab bi gur na, ni bitotoorb bi gur na, ni Liifai yaab bi gur na, nan ti kal baalangben pu baatisakpem ni muwaatiir ponn ni Juda aatiŋ pu la. 21Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatutum nan koo Jerusalem aapepel li bi yin li ke Ofel na ponn ni la; le Siha ni Gispa nan ye baaninkpiib.
22Uja u nan lik Liifai yaab bi nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni na le nan ye Bani aajapɔɔn Usi, u aayaaja nan ye Hasabia na. Uyaajatiib biken le nan ye Matania ni Maika, le ki ye Asaf aamaal ponn ni aanii. Mmaal ngbaan le nan ye Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aalahngaab ni biwangbaab, n‑yoonn mu bi dooni Uwumbɔr na. 23Nnaan aakaal nan bi, ki mɔk imaal ngbaan aah ga li gaa ilahn ki gbaa tiwan Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni, iwiin mɔmɔk pu na.
24Mesesabel aajapɔɔn Petahia, u ye Sera aamaal ponn ni aanii ki ye Juda aanibol aanii na, le nan si Israel yaab aasisii Pesia aabɔr aadichal ni.
Binib bi nan bi ntim mu gur na ponn ni na aayimbil
25Binib ngbaan ponn ni pam le nan kal ntim mu bi gbɔk baasar na. Binib bi nan ye Juda yaab na nan kal Kiriaf Aba, ni Dibonn, ni Jekabseel, ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk ntisakpem mue na ni la. 26Bi nan ki kal Jesua, ni Molada, ni Bef Pelet, 27ni Hasar Sual aatim, ni Beerseba ponn ni, ni itingbaan i mann goln ki na mu ni. 28Bi nan kal Siklag aatikpaan ponn ni, ni Mekona ponn ni, ni kaatingbaan, 29ni Enn Rimonn ponn ni, ni Sora, ni Jamuf ponn ni, 30ni Sanoa, ni Adulam, ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk ntim mue na. Bi nan kal Lakis ni tisar ti bi gbɔk nima na, ni Aseka ponn ni, ni kaatingbaan ni. Naah bi pu na, Juda aanib nan kal lipepel li bi Beerseba aatiŋ ki bi liwipuul aaŋangii wɔb na, ni Hinom Aafataŋ ki bi liwipuul aaŋangan wɔb na aakaasisik ni la.
31Binib bi nan ye Benjaminn aanibol yaab na nan kal Geba, ni Mikmas, ni Ai, ni Betel, ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk nima na, 32ni Anatof, ni Nob, ni Anania, 33ni Hasor, ni Rama, ni Gitayim, 34ni Hadid, ni Seboyim, ni Nebalat, 35ni Lod, ni Ono, ni Bikpikpiib Aafataŋ ni la. 36Bi nan cha Liifai yaab bi nan ka Juda yaab aatiŋ pu na buen ti kal Benjaminn yaab chee la.

english_text:
A List of Priests and Levites
1Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, 2Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, 3Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, 4Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, 5Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, 6Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, 7Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
8The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise, 9while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses.
Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
10Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada. 11Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua.
Leaders of the Priestly Clans
12When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah, 13Meshullam of Ezra, Jehohanan of Amariah, 14Jonathan of Malluchi, Joseph of Shebaniah, 15Adna of Harim, Helkai of Meraioth, 16Zechariah of Iddo, Meshullam of Ginnethon, 17Zichri of Abijah, Piltai of Moadiah, 18Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah, 19Mattenai of Joiarib, Uzzi of Jedaiah, 20Kallai of Sallai, Eber of Amok, 21Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah.
The Priestly and Levite Families
22During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families. 23However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
24Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
25Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
26All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest.
Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
27When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. 28-29The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth. 30The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
31I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate. 32Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them. 33Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, 34Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, 35all of them blowing trumpets. Next, there was Zechariah of the Asaph clan 36and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law. 37When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
38The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall, 39Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard, 40where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders, 41as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets. 42Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers. 43God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem.
Preparation for Worship
44On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites.
Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites, 45 when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon. 46In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship. 47During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.

Foreigners Are Sent Away
1 On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God. 2 This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing. 3Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors.
Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
4The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms. 5So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
6This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king 7to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple. 8It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture. 9Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
10 I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest. 11I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs. 12 After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom. 13Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
14I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there.
The Sabbath
15 I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath. 16People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath. 17I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath! 18Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
19I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath. 20Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods. 21But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath. 22I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy.
God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this.
Mixed Marriages
23 I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. 24About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language. 25So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise:
In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners. 26 God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin. 27So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
28 Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
29I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
30Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites. 31I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple.
I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_text:
Israel yaab aah yakr biwɔwɔm chee pu na
1Bi nan karn Moses Aakaal mpɔɔn pu binib ngbaan aanimbiin ni, ki ti saa nin chee len ke Amonn yaab, ni Moab yaab taa kpaan Uwumbɔr aanib Israel yaab chee daalbaadaal na. 2Naah nan ye pu na le ye ke Amonn ni Moab yaab nan yii kaa tii Israel yaab tijikaar ni nnyun n‑yoonn mu bi nan nyan ni Ijipt ni ki choo kuni na. Bi nan tee labr pan ŋimombil tii ubɔɔ Balaam ke u puun lii Israel yaab pu, le timi Aawumbɔr cha tipuur ngbaan kpaln tinyoor ki tii Israel yaab. 3Israel yaab aanib aah ŋun bi karn nkaal ngbaan na, le bi yakr biwɔwɔm mɔmɔk nyan bikaasisik ni.
Nehemia aah giin tiwan mɔmɔk siin chob pu na
4Eliasib u ye utotoor, ki nan ye Uwumbɔr Aadichal aadir ti bi joo tijikaar ni tiwan niken siini na aaninkpel na, ni Tobia nan ye tɔb jɔtiib la. Baajɔtiik nan yunn. 5U nan di kidiik ki wiir na tii Tobia. Kidiik ngbaan nan ye kidiik ki ponn ni bi nan siini tijikaar ti binib tii Uwumbɔr na, ni Uwumbɔr aatulalee aayon, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aawan, ni ipiin i binib nan tii bitotoorb na; ni njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan aapiin i bi joo tii Liifai yaab, ni bilahngaab, ni biwangbaab, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiib na. 6Nimina aah nan bi ŋani kina na, maa nan bi Jerusalem aatiŋ ni; Babiloŋ aabɔr Ataksekes aanaan aabiln piitaa ni ŋilee ponn ni na, m nan gir buen u chee ke m ti bui u maah tun pu na. N‑yoonn siib aah jer na, le m nan ki mee u nsan 7ki gir ni Jerusalem. Maah nan ti kan ke Eliasib tii Tobia nsan u li koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal aadiik kibaa ponn ni na, ni nan gar mi sakpen. 8Liŋuul nan chuu mi sakpen, le m yoor Tobia aawan mɔmɔk mae lipaal. 9M nan cha bi toor kitork ki ŋa tidir ngbaan chain, ki di Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aawan, ni njikaabim aapiin, ni Uwumbɔr aatulalee aayon ki ki giin ni siin tidir ngbaan ponn ni.
10M nan ki ŋun ke Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aalahngaab, ni biwangbaab, ni Liifai yaab biken fii Jerusalem ki gir buen baasar ponn ni, ba pu? binib aa nan ki tii bi ni ga ŋeer bi bi kpiin bibaa na. 11M nan galn binib ngbaan aaninkpiib pam, baah nan cha Uwumbɔr Aadichal aatuln bee fam pu na. Le m nan ki giini Liifai yaab ni bilahngaab ni biwangbaab ngbaan baatuln ponn ni, Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. 12Le Israel aanib mɔmɔk ki piin ki joo ni baajikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan aapiin nan siini tidir ti ponn ni bi joo kina aawan siini na Uwumbɔr Aadichal chee. 13M nan di utotoor Selemia, ni Sadok, u nyi Nkaal mbamɔm na, ni Liifai aanii Padaya le kaan kiir tidir ngbaan, ki lee Sakur aajapɔɔn Hanann, u aayaaja nan ye Matania na ke u li ter bi. M nan kpa gaakii ke bijab ngbaan ga di ibamɔn yakr tiwan tii baatutuŋeertiib.
14Maawumbɔr, teer mbɔr, ki taa suln tiwan nimɔk m ŋa Saadichal ni aan aa kan idoon mbamɔm ki ponn ni na.
15N‑yoonn ngbaan le m kan Juda aanib bibaa mueni nyani ŋisubil aanyun Likpaakool daal. Biken mu joo njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni ŋisubil aabɔŋ, ni tiwan niken paani baabon pu ki joo cha Jerusalem ponn ni, le m sak bi ke bi taa ki kooh tiwan nibaa Likpaakool daal. 16Taya aajab bibaa nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni, le bi mu joo ni ijan ni tiwan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ ki di koo ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni ke bi nan kooh tii timi aanib Likpaakool daal. 17M nan galn Juu yaab aayidam le ki bui bi ke, “Lik man naah bi tun titunwanbir ti na. Ni bi koor Likpaakool daal aakoobil la. 18Tiwanbaan nee pu le Uwumbɔr nan daa niyaajatiib aatafal ki bii kitiŋ kee. Naah bi koor Likpaakool daal aakoobil kina na, le ni beenin ban ke ni moo di Uwumbɔr aaŋuul lii ni Israel pu.”
19Nima pu le m nan siin ke bi laŋ Jerusalem aabisamɔi nwiin mu ga woln Likpaakool daal na, buyoonn bi kan nwiin ban mu lir na, ki taa ki piir i, see Likpaakool daal ti jer. M nan di maajab bibaa le siin ibisamɔi ngbaan chee, ke bi taa cha unii ubaa joo ni tiwan nibaa koo ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni, Likpaakool daal. 20N‑yoonn n‑yoonn biwankoob bi kooh tiwan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ na, nan doo kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln aapuwɔb kinyeek ki ga woln Likpaakool daal na la. 21Le m nan sak bi ke, “Naah ka nima kii ke ni woln na ye fam la. Ni yaa ki ŋa kina daalbaadaal kan, m ga di mpɔɔn le di mɔk nimi.” Ki nyan n‑yoonn ngbaan, baa ki gir ni Likpaakool daal. 22M nan cha Liifai yaab toor kitork ki ŋa bibaa chain ki buen ti kii ibisamɔi ngbaan ke bi taa cha unii ubaa koor Likpaakool daal aakoobil.
Uwumbɔr, teer mbɔr nimina mu pu, ki san mi kinimbaak, saageehm sakpem pu.
23N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan ki kan ke Juu yaab aajab pam nan yoor Asdod, ni Amonn, ni Moab aapiib. 24Baabim ligetekr libaa nan len Asdod aatiŋ aanib aaliin, bee iliin yayan la, kaa nyi timi aaliin. 25M nan galn bijab ngbaan, ki puun lii bi pu, ki gbaa bi, ki dar gui biyikpir; le ki cha bi puu Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu ke bi ni baabim ni biwɔwɔm aan ki mɔn tɔb. 26M nan bui bi ke, “Biwɔwɔmpiib pu le Ubɔrkpaan Solomonn nan tun titunwanbir. U nan ye uja u pɔɔ jer ŋitimbol ŋiken aabɔrb na la, le Uwumbɔr nan gee u ki di u ŋa ubɔr Israel mɔmɔk pu, le u nan ti ki koo kinimbɔŋ kee ponn ni. 27Ni ban ke ti dii nimi ki yii timi Aawumbɔr aamɔb ki yoor biwɔwɔmpiib la aa?”
28Joyada aate le nan ye utotoorninkpel Eliasib, le Joyada aajapɔɔn ubaa nan tee yoor Sanbalat, u nyan Bef Horonn aatiŋ ponn ni na aabisal. Nima pu le m jenn nyan Joyada Jerusalem ponn ni.
29Uwumbɔr, teer binib ngbaan aah nan bii bitotoorb aatuln, ni tipuur ti aa nan puu ki tii bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab na.
30M nan nyan binib ngbaan tiwan nimɔk ye biwɔwɔm aawan na ponn ni; ki nan ŋa ikaal tii bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab ke unii mɔk li nyi waatuln; 31ki nan ban isan i ga cha idɔ i bi joo pu kitork aanann na aah ga fuu ni n‑yoonn mu na, ni binib mu aah ga li joo ni baajan aajikaabim aapiin ni njan aasubil ŋi puen puir na pu na.
Uwumbɔr, teer mbɔr, ki ŋa tinyoor ŋa m pu.

english_text:
Queen Vashti Disobeys King Xerxes
1-2 King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. 3During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came. 4For 180 days he showed off his wealth and spent a lot of money to impress his guests with the greatness of his kingdom.
5At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens. 6The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
7The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous 8and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
9While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
10By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas, 11to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was. 12The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
13-14The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
15The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
16Then Memucan told the king and the officials:
Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
17The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?” 18Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
19Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
20When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
21King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said, 22and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_text:
Ubɔrpii Fasti aah jinn Ubɔrkpaan Sekes inimɔɔn pu na
1-2Ubɔrkpaan Sekes nan ka waanaan aajal pu Susa aatiŋ ki ye Pesia aatiyil na, le ki lik ŋipepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole, ki nyan India aatingbaln ni ki ti saa Kus aatingbaln.
3Waah nan jin nnaan ki nan saa libiln tatar ni na, u nan ŋa njim sakpem tii waaninkpiib bi lik waanaan na. Pesia ni Media aatɔb aajab nan bi nima, ki kpee biyidam ni bininyuum bi bi ŋipepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole na mu. 4Njim ngbaan nan yunn ki ti saa iŋmal iloob, le u nan joo libɔrchiln ni aawangol, ni laanyaan, ni laapɔɔn mɔmɔk ki mɔk binib ngbaan.
5Nee aapuwɔb na, le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ki ŋa kina aajim ki tii bijab bi mɔmɔk bi litiyil Susa ni na, bigiim ni biwankpadam mɔmɔk. Njim mue mu nan yunn ki ti saa likpaakool libaa; bi nan ŋa mu libɔrchiln ni, nin chee ŋan sakpen na la. 6Bi nan di tikokonn aakekenbɔn ni ŋipiin le di toor lichiln ngbaan ni, ki di ŋitan ŋi ye mbɔm ni mmam na di gbin tikunabr aabuen pu ki di chuu ŋitakpanyaan aagon. Bi nan di ncheen ni ŋitakpanyaan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ le di nak lichiln ngbaan ni, ki di ŋiyikukul aajal ŋi fɔk aan bi di salmaa ni tikunabr ŋa ŋi na di siin. 7Bi nan nyu ndaan salmaa aayikur ni la, le ti mɔmɔk bi tibaabaa kaa kpaan; le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan di mbɔrdaan chann tichann. 8Ndaan aa nan kpa ke ubaa taa nyu waah gee pu na, ubɔrkpaan ngbaan nan bui libɔrchiln ni aatutum ke bi cha unii mɔk nyu waah ga ŋman pu na mɔk.
9Nimina aah bi ŋani na, le Ubɔrpii Fasti mu nan bi kibɔrnaakook ni ki ŋani kina aajim aaboln tii bipiib mu.
10Nwiin lolole daal, le ubɔr nan bi nyu ndaan ki kpa mpopiin, le ki tun ti yin ni waajab bi bi kpaa bi na ponn ni bilole, bi nan ye ubaa aanaagbiib na, Mehumann, ni Bista, ni Habona, ni Bigta ni Abagta, ni Setar, ni Kakas. 11U nan bui bi ke bi ti li joo ni Ubɔrpii Fasti, aan u li chik nnaan aayikpupuk. Ubɔrpii ngbaan nan ye upii u ŋan na la, le ubɔr ngbaan nan ban u di waanyaan di puk kipupuk waaninkpiib ni bimɔk nan dan njim ngbaan ni na chee. 12Binaagbiib ngbaan aah nan ti bui Ubɔrpii Fasti ke ubɔrkpaan yin u na, u nan yii kaa dan. Le ni chuu ubɔrkpaan ngbaan liŋuul pam.
13Tibɔr timina aaboln yaa nan ti dan kan, see ubɔr baa waaninkpiib bi sur u na, le ki nin ŋa waah ban pu na, kina pu le u nan yin ni bisusurb ngbaan, bima le ga nan bee waah ga ŋa pu na. 14Bijab bi nan ŋmaa sur u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, le nan ye Kasena, ni Setar, ni Admata, ni Tasis, ni Meres, ni Masena ni Memukann; Pesia ni Media aaninkpiib bilole bi joo tininkpir ti nyuun nnaan ngbaan ni na le na. 15U nan bui bi ke, “Min Ubɔrkpaan Sekes tun maanaagbiib Ubɔrpii Fasti chee ke u dan, le u yii maamɔb. Nkaal mɔk ke ti ŋa u kinye?”
16Le Memukann bui ubɔr ni waaninkpiib ke: “Ubɔrpii Fasti aa sii ubɔr baanja la, u sii waaninkpiib mu la; mbamɔn, u sii uja umɔk bi nnaan mue taab na la. 17Upii umɔk bi nnaan mue ni na yaa ŋun tibɔr tee kan, u ga piin ki li lik seeni uchal la. Bi ga bui ke, ‘Ubɔrkpaan Sekes tun yin Ubɔrpii Fasti, le u yii kaa buen u chee.’ 18Tɔ, Pesia ni Media aanaan ni aaninkpiib aapuutiib yaa ŋun tibɔr timina kan, bi ga piin ki bi tuk bichatiib, nwiin aa kee lir. Bipiib mɔmɔk aan ki li pak bichatiib, le nimina ga cha bichatiib aaŋuul fii bipuutiib pu. 19Mpɔɔndaan, ni yaa ga piir aasui kan, cha ni nyan aamɔb ni ke Fasti taa ki cha aanimbil kan u. Cha bi ŋmee kina ŋa Pesia ni Media aakaal ponn ni, aan ubaa taa ki kpeln ni. Tɔ, aa di Ubɔrpii aajal mu ki di tii upii u ŋeer li na. 20Aa yaa cha bi moon tibɔr tee ni kookoo nnaan sakpiin mue ni kan, upii mɔmɔk ga lik pak uchal, kaan bui ke u ye ugiin bee upɔɔl.”
21Ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ni waaninkpiib nan kii nsurm ngbaan; le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan nan ŋa Memukann aah nan len pu na. 22U nan tun ŋipepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole ngbaan ni, lipepel mɔk ni laaliin, ni laaŋmeen ni, ki len ke uja mɔmɔk li ye waadichal ni aayidaan, aan waah len pu na ŋa kina.

english_text:
Esther Becomes Queen
1After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her. 2Then the king's personal servants said:
Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women. 3You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments. 4Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen.
King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
5At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. 6 Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
7Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died. 8When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them.
Hegai was put in charge of all the women, 9and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
10Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him. 11He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
12The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes. 13When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters. 14In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
15-16Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
17Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti. 18In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts.
Mordecai Saves the King's Life
19When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official. 20He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
21Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him. 22Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out. 23King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_text:
Baah ŋa Esta Ubɔrpii pu na
1Nee aapuwɔb, ubɔr aaŋuul aah sɔŋ na, u nan beenin dak Fasti aah ŋa u pu na, ni u mu aah siin nkaal mu u pu na. 2Kina pu na, ubɔr aasusurb bi nan ŋɔk u pu sakpen na nan len ke, “Ba ŋa saa cha ti buen ki ti ban upii u ŋan kaa nyi uja na? 3Aa ga ŋmaa ban bininkpiib saanaan aapepel mɔmɔk ni, ki cha bi li joo ni bisapɔm bi ŋan na saapiichiln ni, Susa litiyil ni do. Di bi ŋa Hegai, bijab bi bi kpaa bi na ponn ni ubaa, u lik saapiib na aaŋaal ni, ki cha bi toor bi ki tii bi kinyaan, 4le aa nan nin nyan bi ponn ni usapɔɔn u aa gee u sakpen na ki di u kaan Fasti aajal pu.”
Ubɔr nan dakl ke nsurm ngbaan ŋan, le ki dii mu.
5Susa ponn ni, Juu aanii ubaa nan bi, bi yin u ke Modekai aan ute ye Jair; u nan nyan ni Benjaminn aamaal ponn ni, le ki ye Simei u nan ye Kis aajapɔɔn na aayaabil. 6U nan bi Ubɔrkpaan Nebukadnesar aah nan chur Juda Aabɔrkpaan Jehoyachinn ni waanib bi nyan Jerusalem, ki di buen Babiloŋ ni tinaagbiir na ponn ni. 7U nan kpa weesal ubaa, bi yin u ke Esta, le ki yin u ke Hadasa Hiibru yaab aaliin ni; u nan ye usapɔɔn u ŋan na la, ki kpa tiwon ti ye kinyaan aawon na. Ute ni una aah kpo na, le Modekai kpiin u ki di u ŋa ubisal.
8Ubɔrkpaan aah nan moon ki ban bisapɔm bi ŋan na ke bi li joo ni bi Susa ni na, Esta nan ye bi ponn ni ubaa. Bi nan di u mu di ŋa libɔrchiln ni, Hegai u lik lipiichiln na aaŋaal ni. 9Hegai nan gee Esta, le waanyaan nan chuu Hegai. Kina pu na, u nan piin waanyaan aabimbin aatuln mala, le ki tii u tijikaar ti ŋan na. U nan tii u kidiik ki ŋan jer ti mɔmɔk na lipiichiln ngbaan ni, ki tii u bisapɔm bi bi nyan ni bi libɔrchiln ni na ponn ni bilole, ke bi li tun tii u.
10Modekai aasurm pu na, Esta aa nan cha ubaa bee ke u ye Juu aanii la. 11Iwiin mɔmɔk Modekai nan chuun kpak lipiichiln ngbaan aabisamɔb, ke u lik Esta aah bi pu na, ni tiwan ni ga ŋa u na.
12Kinyaan aabimbin aajoom ngbaan nan yunn ki ti saa libiln libaa la; bi nan joo mir aakpan ŋmir bisapɔm ngbaan ki ti saa iŋmal iloob, le ki di nkpan mu nu mɔ na mu ki ŋmir bi ki ti saa iŋmal iloob. Nee aapuwɔb, le bi ga di usapɔɔn ubaabaa di koon Ubɔrkpaan Sekes chee. 13Waah ga nya lipiichiln ni pu ki buen libɔrchiln ni na, u ga ŋmaa peen waah gee tiwanpeenkaan ni na. 14Usapɔɔn ngbaan ga buen nima kijook la, le kitaak yaa woln kan, bi nyan u buen lipiichiln liken ni, u ti li bi Sasgas, u ye uja u bi kpaa u aan u lik ubɔr aapuutiib na aaŋaal ni. Uma aan ki buen ubɔr chee see ubɔr gee u sakpen aan ki tun yin u waayimbil aah ye pu na ke u dan u chee.
15Esta u ye Abihail aabisal, ki mu ye Modekai aaweesal, u u nan kpiin u ki di kpaln ubisal na aayoonn aah nan fuu ni ke u koo ubɔr chee na, u nan peen tiwan ni Hegai nan sur u ke u peen na la; le umɔk nan kan u na nan neen u. 16Tɔ, Sekes aanaan aabiln lolole ni, ŋmapiik ni, uŋmal u bi yin u ke Tebef na, le Esta nan koo Ubɔrkpaan Sekes chee libɔrchiln ni. 17Ubɔrkpaan nan gee u ki jer bisapɔm biken na mɔmɔk; le u nan kan ubɔr chee ngeehm ki jer biken na. U nan di kibɔryikpupuk chiŋ u ki ŋa u ubɔrpii, Fasti aajal pu. 18Le ubɔr nan ŋa njim sakpem ke u nyuŋ Esta, le ki yin waaninkpiib mɔmɔk. U nan tii waanaan mɔmɔk aanib nwiin mubaa ke ubaa taa tun lituln, le ki tii ipiin pam.
Modekai aah gaa ubɔr aamɔfal lii pu na
19N‑yoonn mue na, Modekai nan ye ubɔr aanaan ni aaninkpel ubaa la. 20Esta aa nan kee kpiir tuk ubaa ke u ye Juu aanii la. Modekai nan bui u ke u taa bui ubaa, le u kii waamɔb tibɔr tee pu, ke waah nan laa ye upiibo ki bi u chee ki keei waamɔb pu na.
21Buyoonn Modekai nan bi waatuln ni, libɔrchiln ni na, Bigtana ni Teres, bijab bi bi kpaa bi na ponn ni bilee, bi nan kii Ubɔr Sekes aadir aabisamɔi na, nan gee liŋuul ubɔr pu, ki kpokl ke bi ku u. 22Modekai nan ŋun tibɔr ngbaan le ki bui Ubɔrpii Esta, le u mu tuk ubɔr, ki mu bui u ke Modekai le kpiir ti tuk u. 23Bi nan fiir lik, ki kan ke tibɔr ngbaan nan gbii, kina pu na, bi nan leen bijab bilee ngbaan iŋmin ki ku bi. Ubɔr nan cha bi ŋmee tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk ŋa waanaan aagbann ponn ni.

english_text:
Haman Plans To Destroy the Jews
1Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag, 2and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai. 3When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command, 4he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
5Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him. 6And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
7It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
8 Then Haman went to the king and said:
Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them! 9Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
10The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him, 11“Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
12On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
13The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
14-15King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_text:
Hamann aah kpokl ke u kuln Juu aanib pu na
1Tiwan nee mɔmɔk aah ŋa ki jer na, le Ubɔrkpaan Sekes nan tii uja u bi yin u ke Hamann na tininkpir ti paa ubɔr pu na. Hamann aate le nan ye Hamedata, le uyaaja ye Agag. 2Waaninkpir ngbaan pu, ubɔr ngbaan nan siin nkaal ke waaninkpiib bimɔk tun waatuln na li gbaani ki pak u. Bi mɔmɔk nan ŋani kina, see Modekai baanja le nan yii, kaa ŋani kina. 3Ubɔr aaninkpiib bi gur na nan baa u ke ba ŋa u yii ubɔr aamɔb; 4ki nan pɔɔni bibaa iwiin mɔmɔk ke u li gbaani ki pak Hamann, le u yii kaan ŋun tii bi. U nan bui bi ke, “M ye Juu aanii la, kaan ŋmaa gbaan ki pak Hamann.” Kina pu na, bi nan bui Hamann tibɔr ngbaan ke bi lik Hamann aah ga ŋa Modekai aabimbin ngbaan pu na. 5Hamann aah bee ke Modekai aan gbaan ki pak u na, liŋuul nan chuu u pam; 6waah nan ki bee ke Modekai ye Juu aanii na, u nan ŋa nlandak ke waan daa Modekai baanja aatafal; u nan ŋa nlandak ke u ku Juu aanib bi mɔmɔk bi Pesia aanaan ni na.
7Njan aaŋmal, u bi yin u ke Nisann na ni, Ubɔrkpaan Sekes aabin kipiik ni ŋilee waanaan ni, le Hamann nan cha bi too inaan, bi yin inaan ngbaan ke “Purim”, aan u bee nwiin ni uŋmal u ni u ga ku Juu yaab na. Ŋmapiik ni ilee, bi yin u ke Adar na aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal le nan ti jin.
8Le Hamann nan bui ubɔr ke, “Linibol libaa bi ki yaa ki bi saanaan aapepel mɔmɔk ponn ni. Baah joo ikaal i na ni biken aakaal aa kpaa. Ki ki kpee na, baa kii saanaan aakaal; kina pu na, saan li gee ke kina aanib li bi. 9Mpɔɔndaan, ni yaa ga mɔɔr si kan, siin nkaal ke bi ku bi mɔmɔk. Aa yaa ŋa kina kan, m puu ke m ga ŋmaa tii nnaan aaninkpiib tikunabr aakur aamombil ŋi aanyunyuun ga pii ŋichur ikui itaa ni imonko ilee na, bi li joo tun nnaan mue aatuln.”
10Le ubɔr chuu ŋmaar waabɔmbik ki bi joo nyiir tigbann pu ke ni ye ubɔr aaseeraa na, ki di tii Juu yaab aadin Hamann u ye Hamedata aajapɔɔn, ki mu ye Agag aayaabil na. 11Le ubɔr bui u ke, “Binib ngbaan ni baamombil ye siyaan la; ŋa bi saah gee pu na.”
12Kina pu na, njan aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal le Hamann nan yin ubɔr aagbaŋmeeb le ki cha bi ŋmee tibɔr ti u ban na, nnaan ngbaan aaliin mɔmɔk ni, ni iliin ngbaan aaŋmeen ni, ke u tii bitinjoob mɔmɔk, ni biyidam mɔmɔk, ni nnaan aaninkpiib mɔmɔk. U nan ŋmee ti Ubɔrkpaan Sekes aayimbil pu la, ki di waabɔmbik nyii tibɔr ngbaan pu. 13Bitaasam le nan di tigbann ngbaan buen nnaan ngbaan aapepel mɔmɔk ni. Ti nan mɔk ke nwiin mubaa daal, Adar aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal kan, bi ku Juu yaab mɔmɔk, binachipɔm ni bi por na, ni bipiib ni bibilb mɔmɔk. Bi kɔr bi mɔmɔk ki taa san bi kinimbaak, ki gaa baawangol mɔmɔk. 14Tibɔr ngbaan nan ye unii mɔmɔk li nyi ti ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni, aan bi mɔmɔk gor ki li kii nwiin ngbaan daal.
15Ubɔr nan cha bi moon tibɔr ngbaan litiyil Susa ni, le bitaasam mu di ti buen ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni. Le ubɔr ni Hamann nan kal ki nyu ndaan, le litiyil Susa ma ponn ni nan ŋa yɔl yɔl.

english_text:
Mordecai Asks for Esther's Help
1When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping. 2But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace. 3 In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
4When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
5Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
6Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate, 7and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
8Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
9Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said. 10She answered, “Tell Mordecai 11there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
12When Mordecai was told what Esther had said, 13he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace. 14If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
15Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying, 16“Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
17Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_text:
Modekai aah ban Esta chee nterm pu na
1Modekai aah ŋun tibɔr ti mɔmɔk ŋa na, le u daa kar waawanpeenkaan mpombiin pu, le ki di tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na peen, ki di nfatan puŋ uyil, ki bɔ dii kitiŋ ni, ki wii ikpowiil mpombiin pu, 2ki ti fuu libɔrdichal aabisamɔb. Waa nan koo; ba pu? ni nan ye nkaal ke unii u pee tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na taa koo libɔrchiln ni. 3Nnaan ngbaan aapepel mɔmɔk ni, nin chee tibɔr ngbaan nan fuu na, nan ye ikpowiil le Juu yaab ni. Bi nan lul bumɔb, ki wii ikpowiil ki pee tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na ki dɔ nfatan ni.
4Esta aanaagbiisapɔm ni bijab bi bi kpaa bi na aah bui u Modekai aah ŋani pu na, ni nan bii usui pam. U nan ban tiwanpeenkaan tun tii Modekai ke u chuu peer tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na ki di waah di ni tii u na peen; le Modekai yii, kaa gaa ni. 5Le Esta yin ni ubɔr aah di uja u bi kpaa u tii u na, bi yin u ke Hatak na, le ki bui u ke u buen Modekai chee ki ti baa lik ke ba ŋa u. 6Hatak nan nyan buen Modekai chee kitiŋ ni, libɔrdichal aabisamɔb chee. 7Modekai nan bui u tiwan ni ŋa u na, ni Hamann aah nan puu ke bi yaa ku Juu yaab mɔmɔk kan, waah ga tii nnaan aaninkpiib ŋimombil ŋi bi li joo tun nnaan ngbaan aatuln na. 8U nan tii Hatak kigbaŋ ki bi nan tii Susa ni yaab ke bi ku doo Juu yaab mɔmɔk na. Modekai nan bui u ke u di ki ti tii Esta ki moo tuk u mbimbin ngbaan aah bi pu na, ki bui u ke u buen ubɔr chee ki ti gaŋ u waanib pu, ke ubɔr san bi kinimbaak. 9Tɔ, Hatak nan ŋa kina, 10le Esta nan di inaŋ yee giin Modekai chee ke: 11“Uja, bee upii yaa koo ponn ni aachiln ni ki kan ubɔr aan ubɔr ubaa aa yin udaan kan, udaan ngbaan aamɔfal junn le na. Nkaal ngbaan le na, unii mɔmɔk, ki nyan ubɔr aasusurb ni, ki ti saa binib bimɔk bi nnaan mue aapepel mɔmɔk ni na nyi kina. Tiwan ni ga ŋmaa cha unii ŋmar na le ye ke ubɔr yaa di waasalmaa aajaangbeek mɔk udaan kan, u ga ŋmar. Ni mu saa uŋmal ubaa le na le ubɔr nan tun yin mi.”
12Modekai aah ŋun Esta aanaŋ na, 13le u nan tii u nsurm ke, “Taa dak ke aa ma aah bi libɔrchiln ni na, aa ga nyan tibɔr ngbaan ni. 14Aa yaa ka ŋmin n‑yoonn mumina aaboln ni kan, nterm ga nyan ni paacham ki dan Juu yaab chee, aan bi ŋmar, le aa ma ga kpo, le aate aadichal ber. Ŋma ti ki nyi, nibaakan ni nan ye n‑yoonn mumina pu le bi di si ŋa ubɔrpii.”
15Esta nan giin kii Modekai ke, 16“Li cha ki ti kuun Juu yaab bimɔk bi Susa ni do na, ki cha ni mɔmɔk lul bumɔb man ki mee limeel tii mi. Ni taa nyu ki taa ji nwiin pu ni kinyeek ki ti saa iwiin itaa. M ni maanaagbiisapɔm mu ga ŋa kina. Nima aapuwɔb na, m ga buen ubɔr chee, hali ni yaa ye likoobil kan, m ga buen. M yaa ŋa kina, aan ni ye mi nkun kan, m kpo.”
17N‑yoonn ngbaan le Modekai siir ki ti ŋa Esta aah nan bui u ke u ŋa pu na mɔmɔk.

english_text:
Esther Invites the King and Haman to a Dinner
1Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway. 2He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her.
When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter, 3the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
4Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
5The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.”
The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner, 6and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
7-8Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.”
Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
9Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry, 10but he did not say a thing.
When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh 11and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him. 12Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow. 13But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
14Haman's wife and friends said to him, “Have a gallows built about 22 meters high, and tomorrow morning ask the king to hang Mordecai there. Then later, you can have dinner with the king and enjoy yourself.”
This seemed like a good idea to Haman, and he had the gallows built.
translation_text:
Esta aah ŋa njimkpaam tii ubɔrkpaan ni Hamann pu na
1Baah lul bumɔb ki ti saa iwiin itaa daal na, le Esta di nnaan aawanpeenkaan peen ki buen ti sil ubɔr aah bi lichiln li na aabisamɔb, ki lik libɔrjal aadiik ni. Ubɔr nan bi ki ponn ni, ki ka libɔrjal pu, ki lik ni mbisamɔb wɔb. 2Ubɔr aah kan Ubɔrpii Esta si lipaal na, le u nan lik ki faar u, le ki yoor salmaa aajaangbeek na mɔk ni u. Le Esta buen ti di uŋaal mee ki. 3Le ubɔr baa u ke, “Ubɔrpii Esta, aa ban ba? Bui mi saah ban tiwan ni na, le aa ga kan ni, hali ni yaa ye ke m di maanaan ligeln libaa tii si kan, m ga ŋa kina.”
4Le Esta gar u ke, “Ni yaa ga li mɔ si mpɔɔndaan kan, m ga li gee ke aa ni Hamann dan nan ji njim mu m bi ŋani m tii nimi na kinyeek kee.”
5Le ubɔr cha bi yin Hamann ke u dan mala, aan bi nan buen Esta aajim ngbaan ni. Le ubɔr ni Hamann buen Esta aajim ngbaan ni. 6Baah bi nyu ndaan buyoonn na le ubɔr ki bui u ke, “Bui mi saah ban tiwan ni na, aan ki kan ni. M ga tii si saah ban ni na, hali aa yaa ban maanaan ligeln libaa kan, m ga tii si.”
7Le Esta ki gar u ke, 8“Mpɔɔndaan, aa yaa san kinimbaak ki ga tii mi maah ban pu na kan, m ga li gee ke aa ni Hamann fe ki li ye maacham fen ki nan ki ji njim muken. N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga bui si maah ban tiwan ni na.”
Hamann aah kpokl ke u ku Modekai pu na
9Hamann aah nyan njim ngbaan ni na, le ni nan mɔ u, le ulan doon suuna. Le u kan Modekai mbisamɔb, le Modekai aa gar ke u fii gbaan ki pak u, le ni chuu Hamann liŋuul pam. 10Tɔ, u nan tee chuu ubaa le ki kun, le ki yin ni ujɔtiib di dan udo, le ki bui upuu Seres ke u mu nan kpee bi pu. 11U nan puk kipupuk bi chee, waah kpa liwangol pu na, ni waah kpa japɔtiib sakpen pu na, ni ubɔr aah tii u tininkpir ti na, ni waah nyuun ki jer ubɔr aaninkpiib biken pu na. 12Hamann nan ki len kpee ke, “Ubɔrpii Esta aa ki yin ubaa ki kpee mi ni ubɔr baanja le bi ti jin njim u chee, ki ki bui timi ke ti fe ki gir ni fen. 13Tɔ, Juu aanii Modekai yaa beenin ka libɔrchiln aabisamɔb kan, nimina mɔmɔk aa kpa mi tinyoor tibaa.”
14Le upuu ni ujɔtiib na mɔmɔk len ke, “Ba ŋa saa cha bi di ŋikpan kpaa tiwan ni fɔk sakpen na, ki ga pii ŋitaa imonko itaa ni kipiik ni ŋiŋmu na? Fen kichakpiik ni kan, aa bui ubɔr aan u cha bi leen Modekai iŋmin ni pu, le aa nin buen fen aajim ngbaan ni, ki li kpa mpopiin.” Hamann nan dakl ke baalandak ngbaan ŋan, le u cha bi kpaa tiwan ngbaan.

english_text:
The King Honors Mordecai
1That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king. 2 When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king, 3the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?”
“Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
4About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
5The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.”
“Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
6When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?”
Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor. 7So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man, 8get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress. 9Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
10The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
11Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
12Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame. 13Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.” 14They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_text:
Ubɔrkpaan aah nyuŋ Modekai pu na
1Kinyeek ngbaan ubɔr aa nan ŋmaa geen; le u cha waatutunn yoor ni nnaan aagbann ki nan karn ti tii u. 2Baah nan karn ti na aabɔr tibaa nan ye Modekai aah nan ŋun baah nan kpokl ke bi ku ubɔr pu na, nkpokl mu Bigtana ni Teres, bijab bi nan kii ubɔr aadir na nan kpokl na. 3Le ubɔr baa ke, “Kinye aan bi nan nyuŋ ki pan Modekai tibɔr tee pu?”
Waanaagbiib nan gar u ke, “Baa tii u nibaa.”
4Le ubɔr ki baa ke, “Maaninkpiib ponn ni ubaa bi do oo?”
N‑yoonn ngbaan Hamann nan koo ni lichiln ni, u nan dan ke u nan bui ubɔr aan u cha bi leen Modekai iŋmin tiwan ni u cha bi kpaa siin na pu. 5Le bi bui u ke, “Hamann le si do, ki kiir ke u kan si na.”
Le ubɔr bui ke, “Cha u koo ni man.”
6Le Hamann koo, le ubɔr bui u ke, “Unii ubaa bi le m gee ke m nyuŋ u. M ga ŋa u kinye?”
Le Hamann dakl uneen ni ke, “Ŋma tee ye aan ubɔr ban u nyuŋ u sakpen kina? Ni ye mi la.”
7-8Kina pu le u kii ubɔr ke, “Cha bi yoor ni ŋibɔrbɔkul nan peen kina aaja, ŋibɔkul ŋi si aabaa peeni na. Cha bi yoor saataan aagbayɔk nan chiŋ aabaa aataan, 9ki cha saaninkpiib ponn ni u kpa kipak na di tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan peen uja ngbaan, aan u diŋ utaan ngbaan pu, aan ki cha uninkpel ngbaan loln u pu nsan ki bɔ dii kitiŋ ponn ni, ki li moon ni ke, ‘Lik man ubɔr aah pan unii u u ban ke u nyuŋ u na pu na.’”
10Le ubɔr nan bui Hamann ke, “Fii mala ki ban tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan ni utaan, ki di ni tii Juu aanii Modekai. Ŋa saah len pu na mɔmɔk. Aa ga kan u ka libɔrdichal aabisamɔb.”
11Le Hamann ban tiwanpeenkaan ni utaan ngbaan, ki di tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan peen Modekai. Le Modekai diŋ utaan ngbaan pu, le Hamann loln u pu nsan ki di bɔ dii kitiŋ ni, ki mooni tuk binib ke, “Lik man ubɔr aah pan unii u u ban ke u nyuŋ u na pu na.”
12Baah doo na le Modekai gir buen libɔrdichal aabisamɔb; le Hamann ma siir mala ki kun, ni inimɔɔn ŋmeen. 13U nan bui upuu ni ujɔtiib na mɔmɔk tibɔr ti kan u na. Le upuu ni ujɔtiib bi kpa nlan na bui u ke, “Dandana wee, saapɔɔn gir cha Modekai chee la. U ye Juu aanii la, le saan ŋman u. U ga nyaŋ si.”
Hamann aah kpo pu na
14Baah laa bi len kina na, le libɔrchiln ni aajab bi bi kpaa bi na koo ni mala ki nan yoor Hamann buen Esta aajim na ponn ni.

english_text:
Haman Is Punished
1The king and Haman were dining with Esther 2and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
3Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want, 4because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
5“Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
6Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!”
Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
7The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden.
Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
8Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!”
As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head. 9Then Harbona, one of the king's personal servants, said, “Your Majesty, Haman built a gallows 22 meters high beside his house, so he could hang Mordecai on it. And Mordecai is the very one who spoke up and saved your life.”
“Hang Haman from his own gallows!” the king commanded. 10At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_text:
1Le ubɔr ni Hamann nan buen bi ti ji Esta chee njim lelee. 2Baah bi nyu ndaan na le ubɔr ki gir baa u ke, “Ubɔrpii Esta, ni ye ba aan aa ban? Bui mi aan ki kan ni. M ga ŋmaa tii si maanaan ligeln libaa.”
3Le Ubɔrpii Esta kii u ke, “Mpɔɔndaan, ni yaa ga li mɔ si aan aa tii mi maah mee pu na kan, maah ban tiwan ni na le ye m ni maanib aamɔfal. 4Bi di m ni maanib kooh ke bi ku timi. Ni yaa kaa ba ye linikul, ki yaa ba ye tinaagbiir kan, m ba ga li ŋmin kaan muk si; tɔ, ni ye le ke bi ku doo ti mɔmɔk.”
5Le Ubɔrkpaan Sekes baa Ubɔrpii Esta ke, “Ŋma ga kaa ki ŋa kina aawan? Uja ngbaan bi la chee?”
6Le Esta nan gar u ke, “Timi aadin u ban u ku timi na le ye utunwanbirdaan Hamann wee.”
Le Hamann gaar ka lik ubɔr ni ubɔrpii ijawaan ni. 7Le ubɔr di liŋuul nyii fii, ki nyan kidiik ngbaan ni, ki nyan lipaal ki ti koo libɔrchiln ni. Hamann nan bee ke ubɔr ban u daa utafal tibɔr ngbaan pu la, le ki gaar puwɔb ke u gaŋ Ubɔrpii Esta aan u gaa waamɔfal lii. 8N‑yoonn mu u lir gbaan Esta aajal li fɔk na pu ke u gaŋ u na, le ubɔr ki nyan ni lichiln ni ki koo ni kidiik ngbaan ni. Waah kan Hamann nima chee na, le u kaan lii ke, “Uja wee ban ke u chuu ubɔrpii nnimbil ni, mbaa aabɔrdichal ni, ki doon u chee la aa?”
Ubɔr ti len kina door na, le waakikiib di likekeln biin Hamann aanimbil wɔb. 9Le bi ponn ni ubaa, u bi yin u ke Habona na, bui ke, “Hamann ma kpaan kpaa ŋikpan ŋi fɔk sakpen na udo ke u leen Modekai u nan gaa si mpɔɔndaan aamɔfal lii na ŋi pu. Ŋaah fɔk pu na ye ŋitaa imonko itaa ni kipiik ni ŋiŋmu.”
Le ubɔr bui ke, “Ti di Hamann leen ŋi pu man.”
10Kina pu na, bi nan leen Hamann iŋmin, ŋikpan ŋi pu u nan kpaa ke u leen Modekai na. Le ubɔr aaŋuul nin sɔŋ.

english_text:
A Happy Ending for the Jews
1Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials 2and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
3Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!” 4King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther, 5and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed, 6and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
7King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews. 8 I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
9On the twenty-third day of Sivan, the third month, the king's secretaries wrote the law. They obeyed Mordecai and wrote to the Jews, the rulers, the governors, and the officials of all 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. The letters were written in every language used in the kingdom, including the Jewish language. 10They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
11-13In these letters the king said:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies.
A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
14-15Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth.
After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered, 16and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
17In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_text:
Baah bui Juu yaab ke bi li kii bibaa pu na
1Liyaadaal baan ngbaan le Ubɔrkpaan Sekes nan di Hamann, u nan ye Juu yaab aadin ngbaan na aawangol mɔmɔk di tii Ubɔrpii Esta. Esta nan bui ubɔr ke u ni Modekai ye unibaan la; nima pu na, liyaadaal ngbaan ki joo cha Modekai nan gur koo ubɔr chee waadiik ni la. 2Le ubɔr chuu ŋmaar waabɔmbik ki ye waamɔkl na, aan u nan chuu gaa Hamann chee na, di tii Modekai. Esta nan cha Modekai le lik Hamann aawangol li ubɔr nan di tii u na.
3Le Esta nan lir gbaan ubɔr aanimbiin ni, ki wii, ki len u chee tibɔr, ki nan gaŋ u ke u lik ki taa cha Hamann u ye Agag aayaabil na aalandawanbiik ki u nan siin ke bi ku Juu yaab mɔmɔk na tun lituln. 4Ubɔr nan di waasalmaa aajaangbeek na di mɔk u, le u fii sil ki bui ke, 5“Ni yaa ga li mɔ si mpɔɔndaan, aan aa yaa lik faar mi ki dak ke ni ŋan aa chee kan, m gaŋ si ke aa siin nkaal ke Hamann aah nan siin ikaal i na taa tun lituln; ikaal i Hamedata aajapɔɔn u aayaaja ye Agag na nan siin ke bi kuln Juu yaab, nnaan mue ni na. 6Tibɔbir timina yaa nan pii maanib, aan bi ku bi mɔmɔk doo kan, m ga ŋa mbaa kinye?”
7Le Ubɔrkpaan Sekes bui Ubɔrpii Esta ni Modekai, u ye Juu aanii na ke, “Lik man, m cha bi leen Hamann iŋmin, waah nan kpokl ke bi ku Juu yaab pu na pu, ki di waawangol di tii Esta. 8Tɔ, nkaal yaa siin ubɔr aayimbil pu, aan bi di nnaan aamɔkl aabɔmbik nyii mu pu kan, ubaa aan ki ŋmaa kpeln mu. Naah ga ŋa pu na le ye ke: Ŋmee kigbaŋ tii Juu yaab mɔmɔk naah gee pu na; ni ga ŋmee ki maayimbil pu, ki di nnaan aabɔmbik nyii mu pu.”
9Nimina nan ŋa ŋmataa, u bi yin u ke Sifann na aawiin moninko ni itaa daal la. Modekai nan yin ubɔr aagbaŋmeeb ki cha bi ŋmee tigbann tii Juu yaab, ni biyidam, ni nnaan aaninkpiib bimɔk bi nnaan aapepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole, ki nyan India aatingbaln, ki ti saa Kus aatingbaln ni na mɔmɔk. Tigbann na nan buen lipepel mɔmɔk, ni laaliin, ni laaŋmeen ni, ni Juu yaab, ni baaliin, ni baaŋmeen ni. 10Modekai nan cha bi ŋmee tigbann ngbaan ubɔrkpaan Sekes aayimbil pu la, le ki di nnaan aamɔkl aabɔmbik nyii ti pu. Binib nan di libɔrdichal ni aataan le ki di tigbann ngbaan buen mala ŋipepel ngbaan mɔmɔk ni.
11Tigbann ngbaan nan mɔk ke ubɔr tii Juu yaab nsan ntim mɔmɔk ni ke bi gor bibaa pu ki li kii bibaa. Bijab yaa nyan ni linibol limɔk ni ki ban bi tak bi ni bipuutiib ni baabim na kan, bi fii sil ki kiir bi, ki ku doo bi; bi ku bi mɔmɔk, ubaa taa gur, ki yoor baawangol. 12Nkaal ngbaan aatuln nan ga piin Pesia Aanaan ni nwiin mundaal Hamann nan siin ke bi ku doo Juu yaab na, ŋmapiik ni ilee, u bi yin u ke Adar na aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal la. 13Ni nan ye ke bi moon mu ke mu ye nkaal la, ki cha unii mɔmɔk li nyi mu ŋipepel ngbaan mɔmɔk ni, aan Juu yaab li kii bibaa baadim chee nwiin ngbaan daal. 14Ubɔr nan cha bitandam di libɔrdichal ni aataan di san mala bi ti di tigbann ngbaan tii. Litiyil Susa ni aanib mɔmɔk mu nan ŋun nkaal ngbaan pu.
15Tɔ, Modekai nan nyan libɔrchiln ngbaan ni, ki pee ŋibɔrbɔkul ŋi ŋmal nsiin ni mpem na, ni ŋikekenyaan ŋiken, ki chik salmaa aabɔryikpupuk ki ŋan sakpen na. Le Susa aatiŋ ni aasan mɔmɔk ni, binib faa mpopiin aafuuk; 16ba pu? Juu yaab bi bi ki ponn ni na nan kan mpopiin ni ŋŋmarm, ni mmɔɔn ni linyaŋ. 17Ntim mɔmɔk ni, ni ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni, nin chee bi nan karn ubɔr aakaal ngbaan na, Juu yaab nan kpa lifuur aawiin ki ji njim ki kpa mpopiin. Ibamɔn, binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na pam nan kpaln Juu aanib; ba pu? bi nan gur san bi ijawaan la.

english_text:
The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
1The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around, 2and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
3The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews. 4Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
5The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy. 6-10They killed 500 people in Susa, but they did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Haman had been one of the worst enemies of the Jews, and ten of his sons were among those who were killed. Their names were Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
11Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa. 12Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
13Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
14King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa. 15Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed 300 more people. But they still did not take anything that belonged to their enemies.
16-17On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed 75,000 of their enemies, but the Jews did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Then on the fourteenth day of the month the Jews celebrated with a feast.
18 On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth. 19This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other.
The Festival of Purim
20Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces 21and told them:
Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar, 22the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
23They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration.
The Reason for the Festival of Purim
24 Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
25Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged. 26Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast. 27Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do. 28From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
29Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast. 30Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the 127 provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said:
We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
31You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
32These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_text:
Juu yaab aah kuln baadim pu na
1Adar aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal nan fuu ni, nwiin mundaal nkaal na aatuln ga piin na, nwiin mundaal Juu yaab aadim nan ban bi kuln bi na. Le Juu yaab labr fenn lir bi pu ki nyaŋ bi. 2Juu yaab aakookoo yaan, nnaan ngbaan ni, bi nan gor bibaa ke bi tak unii umɔk nan pɔɔni ubaa ke u tii bi titotonn na. Ŋipepel mɔmɔk aanib nan san bi ijawaan la, le ubaa aa nan ŋman bi. 3Ibamɔn, nnaan ngbaan aapepel mɔmɔk aaninkpiib, ni biyidam, ni nnaan aanib, ni ŋaaninkpiib mɔmɔk nan kpee Juu yaab pu la; ba pu? bi mɔmɔk nan san Modekai ijawaan la. 4Nnaan ngbaan ni aanib mɔmɔk nan nyi ke Modekai gur ye mpɔɔn aanii le ki bi libɔrchiln ni, le waapɔɔn moo kpae. 5Kina pu na, Juu yaab nan ga ŋmaa ŋa baadim baah ban pu na. Bi nan di kijaak aajum le ki di tak bi, ki ku bi.
6Litiyil Susa ponn ni, Juu yaab nan ku binib ikui iŋmu la. 7-10Hamedata aajapɔɔn Hamann u nan ye Juu yaab aadin na aajapɔtiib kipiik bimina: Pasandata, ni Dalfonn, ni Aspata, ni Porata, ni Adalia, ni Aridata, ni Pamasta, ni Arisai, ni Aridai, ni Faisata nan bi baah ku binib bi na ponn ni. Bi mu aa nan tee yoor baawangol.
11Liyaadaal baan ngbaan le baah ku binib bimɔk Susa aatiŋ ni na aakahm nan fuu ubɔr chee. 12Le u bui Ubɔrpii Esta ke, “Susa aatiŋ ni baanja bi ku binib ikui iŋmu, le Hamann aajapɔtiib kipiik na mu kpee. Aa dak ke bi ga li ŋa kinye nnaan aapepel na mɔmɔk ni? Ni ye ba le aa ki ban? Saah ban ni na, aa ga kan ni. Bui mi saah ban ni na, aan ki kan ni.”
13Le Esta bui u ke, “Ni yaa ga li mɔ si mpɔɔndaan kan, cha Juu yaab bi bi Susa ni do na fe ki ŋa baah ŋa pu din na; ki mu cha bi di Hamann aajapɔtiib kipiik ngbaan aanikpol leen ŋikpan pu.” 14Ubɔr nan cha bi ŋa kina, le ki moon Susa ponn ni tibɔr ngbaan. Bi nan di Hamann aajapɔtiib kipiik ngbaan aanikpol leen ŋikpan pu, binib mɔmɔk aanimbil ni. 15Adar aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni inaa daal Juu yaab bi bi Susa ni na nan ki gor bibaa pu ki ki ku binib ikui itaa kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Liyaadaal ngbaan mu, baa nan ki yoor baah ku binib bi na aawangol.
16Juu yaab bi nan bi ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni na mu nan gor bibaa pu ki sil kiir umɔk tak bi na. Bi nan ku baadim ngbaan aanib ŋichur imonko itaa ni kipiik ni ŋiŋmu la. Bi mu aa nan yoor baah ku binib bi na aawangol. 17Bi nan tun kina Adar aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal la. Naah woln na, iwiin kipiik ni inaa daal na, ŋipepel ŋi bi igbaan na aanib aa nan ki ku binib, bi nan jin njim le ki mɔɔni. 18Juu yaab bima bi Susa ni na ma, nan jin njim ni lifuur aawiin, iwiin kipiik ni iŋmu daal la; ba pu? iwiin kipiik ni itaa daal, ni iwiin kipiik ni inaa daal le bima nan ku baadim, ki di cha kipiik ni iŋmu daal kaa ki ku. 19Nimina pu le Juu yaab bi koo itingbaan ni na ji njim, ki tii tɔb ipiin, ki kpa mpopiin, Adar aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni inaa daal.
Njim mu bi yin mu ke Purim na aabɔr
20Modekai nan ŋmee tiwan nimina mɔmɔk bil; ki ki ŋmee tigbann tii Juu yaab bimɔk duun Susa na, ni bimɔk bi ni daa na, Pesia aanaan mɔmɔk ni, 21ki bui bi ke bi li nyi ki di Adar aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni inaa, ni iwiin kipiik ni iŋmu daal libiln mɔmɔk ni, ŋa lifuur aawiin; 22ba pu? iwiin ngbaan daal le Juu yaab nan nyaŋ baadim; uŋmal ngbaan le nan ye uŋmal u mpombiin ni itaakpayɔl kpaln mpopiin ni mmɔɔn na. U nan bui bi ke iwiin ngbaan daal kan, bi li ji njim ki tii tɔb tijikaar aapiin, ki tii binib bi ye bigiim na mu. 23Le Juu yaab ngbaan nan dii Modekai aah bui bi pu na, le njim ngbaan di ŋa libiln mɔmɔk aakaal.
24Juu yaab aadin, Hamedata aajapɔɔn Hamann, u aayaaja ye Agag na, nan too inaan i bi yin i ke “Purim” na, ke u bee nwiin mu u ga di kuln Juu yaab na; u nan kpokl ke u kuln bi la. 25Le Esta nan buen ubɔr chee, le ubɔr siin nkaal mu bi ŋmee bil aan Hamann tee labr jin nkaal ngbaan aafalaa u u nan kpokl ke Juu yaab nan ji na; bi nan leen u ni ujapɔtiib ŋikpan pu. 26Nima pu le bi yin lifuur aawiin ngbaan ke Purim. Modekai aah nan ŋmee tigbann ti na pu, ni tiwan nimɔk nan ŋa bi na pu, 27le Juu yaab nan cha ni ŋa baakaal, ni biyaabitiib aakaal, ni unii umɔk kpaln Juu aanii na aakaal ke n‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni libiln mɔk ni kan, iwiin ilee ngbaan ga li ye lifuur ni njim aawiin ke Modekai aah nan mɔk bi pu na la. 28Ni nan ŋa nkaal ke Juu aadichal ŋi ga nan li bi n‑yoonn mu choo na, ki bi ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni ntim mɔmɔk ni na, li teer ki ŋa Modekai aah siin pu ki tii Purim aawiin ilee ngbaan ki joo cha na.
29Le Abihail aabisal, Ubɔrpii Esta, ni Modekai mu ŋmee kigbaŋ ki di waaninkpir aapɔɔn mɔmɔk nyii ki pu, Purim aabɔr ti Modekai puun ŋmee na pu. 30U nan ŋmee kigbaŋ ngbaan tii Juu yaab bimɔk bi ŋipepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole ŋi bi Pesia aanaan ni na. Kigbaŋ ngbaan nan mɔk ke Juu yaab li kpa nsuudoon ni limakl ke nibaa aan ŋa bi; 31ki mɔk bi ni biyaabitiib baah ga li nyi Purim aawiin ilee na pu na, ke baah ŋani bumɔb aalulm ni baapombiin aayoonn pu na. Modekai ni ubɔrpii Esta mɔmɔk le nan siin kina. 32Esta nan cha bi ŋmee Purim aabɔr ngbaan nnaan aagbaŋ pu la.

english_text:
The Greatness of Xerxes and Mordecai
1King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea. 2All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai. 3Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_text:
Ubɔrkpaan Sekes ni Modekai aah nan kpa mpɔɔn pu na
1Tɔ, Ubɔrkpaan Sekes nan siin mpɔɔn aakaal mu cha binib bimɔk bi waanaan ni na tun lituln tii nnaan ngbaan na. 2Waah nan tun iwaan aatuln li na, ni Modekai aah nan ti kan waaninkpir ti paa ubɔr pu na mɔmɔk bi Pesia ni Media aabɔrb aagbann ponn ni la. 3Ubɔr Sekes baanja le nan kpa tininkpir ki jer Juu aanii Modekai. Juu yaab mɔmɔk nan pak Modekai ki gee u sakpen. U nan tun ki ban waanib aabimbinyaan ni biyaabitiib aamɔfal la.

english_text:
Job and His Family
1Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
2Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters. 3He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pair of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a large number of servants. He was the richest person in the East.
4Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking. 5After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God.
Angels, the Lord, and Satan
6 One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them, 7the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Kinimbɔŋ aah tɔŋ Job pu na
1Uja ubaa nan bi Us aatiŋ ni, bi nan yin u ke Job. Job nan dooni Uwumbɔr le ki dii u mbamɔm. U nan ye uninyaan, le kaa gee titunwanbir aatuln. 2U nan kpa mbijabim mulole, ni mpiibim mutaa la, 3le ki kpa ipiih ŋichur ŋilole, ni laakumii tiib ŋichur ŋitaa, ni inaa lichur libaa, ni ibon mu ikui iŋmu. U nan ki kpa binaagbiib mu pam, le ki nan ye unii u kpa liwangol, ki jer binib bi mɔmɔk nan bi liwipuul wɔb na.
4Job aajapɔtiib nan nyan ni iwiin le ki ŋani njim, le bi mɔmɔk ti kpaan ki ji ubaa do. Bi nan yini bininkpatiib bitaa na mu aan bi nan ji bi chee. 5Njim ngbaan mubaa yaa ti jer ki woln kitaak na kan, Job ga fii lichakpitaawoln le ki toor kitork, waabim ngbaan ubaa mɔk pu. U dak ke nibaakan bi ponn ni ubaa ga li sii Uwumbɔr, ki tun u taani, kaa nyi, nima pu le u nan ŋani kina n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
6Nwiin mubaa daal le Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib dan ke bi nan di bibaa mɔk Uwumbɔr, le kinimbɔŋ mu ŋmal bi ponn ni. 7Le Uwumbɔr baa u ke, “Aa bi tun ba aatuln?”
Le kinimbɔŋ gar Uwumbɔr ke, “M nan bi kitiŋ pu, le ki kpak, ki chuun ti nya do, ki di ti nya do.”
8Le Uwumbɔr ki baa u ke, “Aa kan maatutunn Job aah bi pu na aan saa kan u? Ubaa aa ki bi kitiŋ pu ki kpa mbimbinyaan ki dii mi mbamɔm ke uma na. U dooni mi, le ki nyi kaa tun titunwanbir.”
9Le kinimbɔŋ gar u ke, “Job yaa kaa ba kan nibaa saadoon chee kan, u ba ga li dooni si ii? 10Aa kiir u ni waadichal, ni waah kpa tiwan nimɔk na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Aa ŋani saanyoor ŋani waatuln mɔmɔk pu, le ki tii u tiwakor ti ŋeer ki ga gaa litingbaln lee mɔmɔk na. 11Tɔ, aa yaa ba chuu gaa tiwan nimɔk u kpa na kan, u ba ga puun lii aa pu.”
12Le Uwumbɔr bui kinimbɔŋ ke, “Tɔ, m di waah kpa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na ŋa aaŋaal ni, aa mu taa di aaŋaal meeh Job ubaa.” Le kinimbɔŋ siir.
Job aabim ni liwangol aah kuln pu na
13Job aabim aah nan bi ujapɔpol do ji njim na, 14le ntuun san dan Job chee, ki nan bui ke, “Ti bi joo inaa ko nkpaakon, le ibon mu si gbɔk mmoŋmɔpaan mubaa ni. 15Libuul ngbaan ni le Seba yaab dan nan tak timi, ki sun i mɔmɔk. Bi ku saatutum mɔmɔk, min baanja le gur. Min baanja le san ŋmar ki dan m nan tuk si.”
16Waahr aan u ti len doo na, le ututunn uken dan nan bui ke, “Utaal teen ipiih ni bitutum pu, ki ku bi ni ipiih mɔmɔk. Min baanja le ŋmar ki dan m nan tuk si.”
17Waahr aan u ti len doo na, le ututunn uken mu fuu ni ki nan bui u ke, “Kaldii aaniker ŋitaa pu le dan ki nan tak timi, ki chur laakumii tiib buen, le ki ku saatutum mɔmɔk, see min baanja. Min baanja le san ŋmar ki dan m nan tuk si.”
18Waahr aan u mu ti len doo na, le ututunn uken mu ki fuu ni ki nan bui u ke, “Saabim bi aajapɔpol do bi ji njim, 19le kitaabuŋ nyan ni nteersakpiin wɔb, ki daa lidichal ngbaan lii, ki ku bi mɔmɔk. Min baanja le san ŋmar ki dan m nan tuk si.”
20Le Job fii sil, ki daa kar waawanpeenkaan nsuugar pu. U nan kuu uyil, le ki lir lichichikr, 21ki nan bui ke, “Baah nan ma mi na, maa nan joo ni nibaa, le ki ga nan kpo, kaa joo nibaa. Uwumbɔr nan tii, uma le ki gaa. Pak waayimbil man.”
22Job aa nan di tiwan nee mɔmɔk ŋa taani tii Uwumbɔr, kaa tun titunwanbir.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
