10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Kinimbɔŋ ki gir tɔŋ Job lelee
1Nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib nan ki kuun bi ti di bibaa mɔk Uwumbɔr na, kinimbɔŋ nan ki ŋmal bi ponn ni. 2Le Uwumbɔr baa u ke, “Aa buen la chee?”
Le kinimbɔŋ gar u ke, “M bi kitiŋ pu le ki kpak, ki chuun ti nya do, ki di ti nya do.”
3Le Uwumbɔr baa u ke, “Aa kan maatutunn Job aah bi pu na aan saa kan. Ubaa aa ki bi kitiŋ pu ki kpa mbimbinyaan ki dii mi mbamɔm ke uma na. U dooni mi, le ki nyi kaa tun titunwanbir. Aa nan muk mi ke m cha aa ti tak u, ntakn mu kaa kpa tataa na pu, le Job beenin kpa gaakii ke waah nan kpa pu na.”
4Le kinimbɔŋ gar u ke, “Unii ga ŋmaa di waawan mɔmɔk pa waamɔfal pu. 5Aa yaa ba cha iween ibaa pii u kan, u ba ga puun lii aa pu.”
6Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Tɔ, m di u ŋa aaŋaal ni, aa mu taa tee ku u.”
7Le kinimbɔŋ siir Uwumbɔr chee, ki ti cha ibuun baan baan Job aawon mɔmɔk pu. 8Job nan buen le ki ti kal litapuln pu, le ki pii lisanjaln ke u li joo kɔr waabuun ngbaan ni. 9Le upuu bui u ke, “Aa beenin dii Uwumbɔr ke saah nan dii u pu na la aa? Ba ŋa saan puun lii Uwumbɔr pu ki tee kpo?”
10Le Job gar u ke, “Aa si len bɔfam la. Uwumbɔr yaa tii ni timi tiwan ni ŋan na kan, ti gaal ni iŋaal ilee la. Ti ga ŋa kinye ki galn u buyoonn u tii timi tibɔbir na?” Job aah nan jin falaa sakpen tiwan nimɔk pu na, waa nan di tibaa tam Uwumbɔr.
Job aajɔtiib aah dan pu na
11Job aajɔtiib bitaa bibaa le nan ye Elifas, u nyan ni Temann aatiŋ ni na, ni Bildad, u mu nyan ni Sua aatiŋ pu na, ni Sofar, u mu nyan ni Naama aatiŋ pu na. Baah ŋun Job aah bi ji falaa u aaboln na, le bi bui ke bi buen ki ti sɔŋ usui. 12Baah laa bi ni dandar na, le bi waa Job, ki mu aa bee u. Baah ti bee u na, le bi piin ki wii, ki kaani, ki dar kar baawanpeenkaan mpombiin pu, le ki fai titan mae paacham, ni biyil pu, 13le ki kal kitiŋ u chee nima, ki ti saa iwiin ilole ni tinyer tilole, kaa len libɔbil libaa, ba pu? bi nan waa waah bi ji falaa pu na.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Job aah di tibɔr ti len Uwumbɔr chee na
1Kookoo le Job ti waar umɔb, ki puun lii nwiin mundaal bi nan ma u na pu.
Job
2-3Uwumbɔr, puun lii nwiin mundaal bi nan ma mi na,
puun lii kinyeek ki bi nan dik maapuul na pu.
4Uwumbɔr, cha liyaadaal ngbaan kpaln mbɔmbɔɔn.
Taa ki teer nwiin ngbaan bɔr daalbaadaal,
taa ki cha nwiihn woln mu pu daalbaadaal.
5Cha mu ŋa timm, ni mbɔmbɔɔn sakpiin,
cha ntaalangbam biin mu pu, ki duŋ nwiin.
6Chuu nyan kinyeek ngbaan libiln ngbaan ni,
ki taa ki cha bi kahn ki kpala;
7ŋa ki kinyeek ki kaa kpa tinyoor, ni mpopiin na.
8Bui binib bi punni lir iwiin pu na
ki nyi baah joo kipeewanbiik na pu na
ke bi puun lii liyaadaal ngbaan pu.
9Taa ki cha liŋmabil naanyuun li wiin,
taa cha kinyeek ngbaan li mak lichakpitaawoln pu.
10Puun lii kinyeek ngbaan pu, kaah cha bi ma mi
ki nyan mi siin tibɔbir, ni mpombiin ni na pu.
11M yaa nan ba kpo nna aaponn ni,
bee m kpo libuul li ni bi ma mi na kan, m ba gee.
12Ba ŋa nna nan di mi kaan utaaŋaayil pu?
Ba ŋa u nan cha m ŋaa waabiil?
13M yaa ba nan kpo n‑yoonn na kan,
m ba ga li bi lifuur ni le n‑yoonn mue,
14ki geeni ke bibɔrb ni bitinjoob bi ki gir maa
n‑yaayoonn na aabɔrdichal na.
15M ba ga li geeni ke bitinjoob bi di salmaa
ni tikunabr gbiin baadichal ni na,
16bee m ba ga li geeni ke libikpol li bi ma bil na.
17Likaakul ni kan, bibiindam joo cha baatunwanbir la,
le binib bi tun ki ti bak na kani lifuur li bi ban na,
18hali binib bi bi tiyondir ni na kan lifuur likaakul ni,
bi nyan tijar ni mmɔpɔɔn aabɔr ni.
19Biyimbidam, ni baah kaa nyi bibɔr na mɔmɔk bi nima,
le binaagbiib kani ŋŋmarm nima.
20Ba ŋa unii kpa limɔfal ki bi kinimbaak ni?
Ba ŋa binib bi bi mpombiin ni na kpa nwiihn?
21Bi kii nkun, le mu mu aa choo;
bi neen likaakul jer liwangol.
22Bi yaa kaa ti kpo aan bi sub bi kan, baa kpa mpopiin;
23Uwumbɔr di baataak ki ga woln na bɔr bi,
le ki gob bi ŋipepel mɔmɔk.
24Maah ga li ji pu na, le m joo wii ikpowiil,
kaan ŋmaa di cha kaa ker idun.
25Maah san tiwan ni mɔmɔk ijawaan sakpen na choo kina la.
26Maa kpa nsuudoon, kaa kpa lifuur, le maabɔbir aan doo.

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Njan aabɔgbaal
(Job 4.1–14.22)
Elifas aah len pu na
1-2Job, m yaa len tibɔr kan, saaŋuul ga fii m pu uu?
Maan li ka ŋmin kina ki cha.
3Aa bae binib pam tiwan
ki tii binib bi kaa kpa mpɔɔn na mpɔɔn.
4Unii umɔk bak, kaa ki kpa mpɔɔn, ki gbeer ke u lir na,
saamɔbon tii udaan ntaakpab pɔɔn, ke u fii sil.
5N‑yoonn mue na, sin le bi tibɔr ni,
le saa ki kpa mpɔɔn ke aa kiir ti.
6Aa nan dooni Uwumbɔr, kaa nan kpa tijɔŋ tibaa,
kina pu na, li kpa limakl ki li si chob.
7Dakl lik, ki tuk mi nin chee mbimbinyaandaan koo
linimaln ni na.
8M kan binib aah kon titunwanbir ke nkpaakon pu na,
ki bun mbiin ke njikaabim na pu na;
le ki tee nan chee mbiin, ni titunwanbir.
9Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ponn ni, u kuln bi ke kitaabuŋ na la.
10Bibiindam wii ki ŋuuni ke ichinn na la,
le Uwumbɔr kool baanyin, ki ŋmini bi chii.
11Ichinn aah kaa kan nibaa i ku ki ŋmɔ ki kpoi pu na,
kina le bi kpoi, le baabim yaa tɔb chee.
12N‑yoonn mubaa le ntuun nan loon suuna ki dan,
u nan loon suuna, le maa ŋun u pu kpala.
13Ni nan muk maageen ke kinyeek aadaŋ na la.
14M nan jii, le ki jiib; nwon mɔmɔk nan gbaa,
le ijawaan joo mi,
15libuln nan daa fol fol nnimbil wɔb,
le n‑yikpir fii sil ijawaan pu.
16M nan waa tiwan nibaa si nima;
m nan moo lik, kaa bee naah ye tiwan ni na.
Le m ŋun nneel pu liŋmiŋmiln ngbaan ni.
17“Unii ulau aa kpa tijɔŋ Uwumbɔr chee,
bee ŋma bi chain ki jer u naan u na?
18Uwumbɔr aa tii waatuuntiib naadii;
u kani waatuuntiib aataani.
19Aa dak ke u ga tii tiyakr aawanaankaan ni ye titan
ki ga ŋmaa puu ke kinaapipirk na naadii ii?
20Unii ga li ŋmaa kpa limɔfal kichakpiik ni, ki ga ŋmaa kpo aan ubaa aa nyi ubɔr le kijook nin joor.
21Waah kpa nimɔk na buen a; u kpo, kaa beenin kpa nlan.”

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1Job, teen mpɔɔn pu ki yin, ki lik ke ubaa ga kii
aan waan kii.
Uwumbɔr aatuun mubaa bi aan aa ga ŋmaa fenn buen
mu chee ee?
2Aa yaa ka dak ke ubaa aatafal aa bi aa ni ki ti kpo kan,
ni ye kijɔrk, ni maa‑kpa‑lan aawan le ke unii ŋa.
3M kan bijɔrb bi nan dak ke bi kan bibaa na,
le ki tee puun lii baadichal pu libuul ngbaan ni.
4Bijapɔtiib aan kan ŋŋmarm kpala;
le ubaa aa bi ki ga sil bichaŋ ni, libɔjil ni.
5Nkon aah joo binib bi na ga ji waajikaar,
ki kpaan ji tijikaar ti si ŋmal ikokon ni na,
le bikumɔndam ga yoor waawangol.
6Titunwanbir aa nyani titan ni,
le tibɔbir mu aa punni kitiŋ pu.
7Unibɔn le joo tibɔbir ubaa pu ke mmii aah pool pu na.
8M yaa ba ye sin kan, m ba ga fenn toŋ Uwumbɔr
le ki di maabɔr tuk u.
9Taan ŋmaa bee waah ŋani tiwankpaan ni na aatataa,
le waajinjiir aawan aa kpa ndoon.
10U cha utaal nu kitiŋ pu le ki tii ikpaakon nnyun.
11Mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr le fiini unii u sunn ubaa taab na paacham
le ki tii unii u wii ikpowiil na mpopiin.
12-13U bii beebeedam aah kpokl pu na,
le ki chur bibiindam, bibaa aatun ni,
le baa kani tinyoor baatun mɔmɔk ni,
14hali nwinkapiin pu kan, bi chuun baani mbɔmbɔɔn ni la.
15Le Uwumbɔr nyani ugiin nkun ni,
le ki gaal baah muk binib bi aan bi ban nterm na lir.
16U tii bigiim limakl, le ki ŋmini bibiindam chii.
17Uwumbɔr aah sur unii u na kpa mpopiin.
U yaa kae si kan, taa bui ke utafal aa bi aa ni la.
18Uwumbɔr poo ibuun i u tii na;
uma aaŋaal le tii si titotonn, le ki ki tii si laafee.
19N‑yoonn n‑yoonn pam le u ga nyan si titotonn ni.
20Likpasiil yaa fuu ni kan, uma le ga tii si limɔfal,
le ki kiir si aan butɔb aakun taa ku si.
21Uwumbɔr ga nyan si liyimbibiil ni;
le ki ga tii si ŋŋmarm libiil yoonn.
22Aa ga li laa tijar ni nkon le kaan san tipeewanbir ijawaan.
23Saakpaakon i aa ko na aan li kpa ŋitakpal;
tipeewanbir aan tak si kpala.
24Le aa ga li koo saadichal ni, ni nsuudoon ŋmeen;
le aa yaa yaar lik saapiih kan, aa ga kan ke i bi ŋŋmarm ni la.
25Saabim ga li wiir
ke timoor aah wiir kinaakpaamook ni pu na la.
26Aa ga por ke njikaabim mu biir ki kiir lijikaacheel na la.
27Job, ti di n‑yoonn pam le bae nimina.
Ni ye mbamɔn la, kina pu na, gaa ti.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Job aah len pu na
1-2Bi yaa ba ga ŋmaa ŋaŋ maabɔr ni maapombiin kan,
3ni ba li nyuun jer litambol li bi nnyusakpem aagbaan na,
kina pu na, taa cha maabɔfam ŋa si iwaan.
4Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan di ipiin too chaar mi,
le yaaluul yaa koo nwon ni.
Uwumbɔr lol waajawaan aawan kiir mi.
5Ubon yaa bi ŋmɔ timoor kan, u kpa mpopiin,
le unaa yaa bi ŋmɔ timocheekaan kan, u ŋmin.
6Tɔ, ŋma ga ŋmaa ji tijikaar ti kaa kpa n‑yaan ni mmɔɔn kpala na?
Ba aamɔɔn bi nkojekpan mu ye mupipim na ni?
7Kina aajikaar aa kpa mi kikpeek,
le tijikaar timɔk m ji na tii mi iween.
8Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr aan tii mi maah mee tiwan ni na?
Ba ŋa waan gar maameel?
9U yaa ba kii ki ku mi kan, m ba gee.
10M yaa ba nyi ke u ga kii kan, m ba ga yuk ki laani,
kaan teer iween sakpiin i joo mi na pu.
M nyi ke Uwumbɔr bi chain la; maa kee kpak waah len pu na.
11Ba aapɔɔn aan m kpa ki ga li beenin bi limɔfal ponn ni?
Ba ŋa m beenin bi limɔfal ni kaa kpa limakl?
12Bi di litakpal le naan mi ii? Maawon ye tikumann la aa?
13Maa ki kpa mpɔɔn ki ga di gaa mbaa lii;
Maan ŋmaa fenn toŋ nibaa chee ki kan ŋŋmarm.
14Tibɔbir kina aaboln ni kan, m ban jɔtiibamɔm la,
M yaa yii Uwumbɔr, bee maa yii u kan, m ban jɔtiibamɔm la.
15Le nimi njɔtiib ma ŋmanni mi
ke utaal yaa kaa nun kan, ikpen ibaa foor pu na la.
16Ikpen aanyun kpalni ŋitaanal la,
17le ntoton yaa fuu ni kan, ŋi wɔŋ, le mbufan foor ki dɔ nkuun.
18Le biwankoob bi chuun ban nnyun na ti wɔŋ,
bi chuun yiini le ki kpo nteersakpiin ni.
19Seba ni Tema aawankoob lik ban nnyun,
20le baamakl ti bee fam nkpenkuun chee.
21Ni bi ke nkpen ngbaan na le ki tii mi,
ni kan maadoon, le ijawaan pu ni sur nipuwɔb.
22Maa bui nimi ke ni tii mi ipiin ibaa,
kaa bui ke ni tii ubaa igaŋgaŋlik m pu,
23kaa bui nimi ke ni gaa mi udin, bee limukl libaa chee lii.
24Tɔ, mɔk mi, bui mi maataani aah ye pu na.
M ga li ŋmin ki pel aa chee.
25Tibɔbamɔnn kpa ŋuntii, le aa ma ka tool.
26Aa dak ke m ka pii libuln baanja la, maa len tibaa;
kina kan, ba ŋa aa gar maasuubiin aamɔbon?
27Aa too inaan unaagbiikpobo pu,
le ki di aajɔnyaan kan liwankpal.
28Lik mi mbamɔm. Maan gii si nnyamɔn.
29Aa buen ti chaar jer a. Taa ki tun beebee aatuln.
Taa ki bii mi. M kpa mbamɔn.
30Le aa ma dak ke m gii la,
aa dak ke maan ŋmaa gann ibamɔn ki cha inyamɔn la.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
1Unibɔn aamɔfal bi ke baah joo uja mpɔɔn
kooni butɔb aatuln ni pu na la,
ki naahn ŋŋaal aatuln li pɔɔ na,
2ki naahn unaagbiija aah neen mboon mu soon na pu na;
ki naahn ututunn aah kii waapar pu na.
3Uŋmal jer le uŋmal paan ni, le maa kpa limakl libaa;
tinyer mɔmɔk joo ni mi mpombiin la.
4M yaa doon ke m geen kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan aa cha kpala;
m dɔ binni kinyeek mɔk le ki neen kitaak aawoln.
5Ŋikpaambil le gbii nwon ni, nwon ye ŋibukak ŋmeen la;
tinar puu nya maabuun ni la.
6Maawiin jer le kaa joo ni limakl,
i san mala jer ke ukpaluul aakokonjal na.
7Uwumbɔr, teer ke maamɔfal ye kifuurk kibaa la;
maapopiin doo ni yunn a.
8Aa waa mi din, le kaan ki kan mi kpala.
Aa yaa ban mi kan, mui m buen a.
9-10Ntaalangbam aah yaani ki door pu na,
kina le unibɔn kpoi kaa ki gir ni;
le binib bi mɔmɔk nan nyi u na suln ubɔr.
11Maan li ka ŋmin; mmɔb ponn ni choŋ, le liŋuul joo mi.
M ga len la.
12Ba ŋa aa ka kii mi?
Aa dak ke m ye nnyusakpem ni aawanbiik la aa?
13M doo le ki pɔɔni mbaa ke m fuur;
m lik ban tiwan ni ga sɔŋ maaween na la.
14Le aa ma joo tidaŋ faani mi;
aa cha tidaŋ ti kpa ijawaan na mɔmɔk aabɔŋ choo m chee
15ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu m ga li ban ke m fik ki kpo na,
ki jer ke m li bi tiwon timina aaboln ni.
16M di cha a; m bak limɔfal lee ni a.
Di cha mi. Maamɔfal aa kpa tinyoor tibaa.
17Ba ŋa unibɔn aabɔr muk aa chee kina?
Ba ŋa aa gar waah tun pu na?
18Aa lik waabimbin kichakpiik mɔk ni,
le ki tɔŋni u ki lik n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
19Saan fenn lik nibaa wɔb siib aan m ŋmaa nab timɔɔtan aa?
20Sin kiyondiik aaninkpel,
maatunwanbir tii si titotonn la aa?
Ba ŋa aa too mi ipiin? M ye litusakpeln le tii si ii?
21Saan ŋmaa di cha pinn mi maatunwanbir aa?
Saan ŋmaa suln taani u m ŋani na aa?
Naan ki yunn le m koo likaakul ni,
le aa yaa ki ban mi kan, saan kan mi.

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Bildad aah len pu na
1-2Aa gboo doo oo?
3Uwumbɔr aa fenni ibamɔn; u tun ni ŋan na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
4Nibaakan, saabim tun Uwumbɔr taani la,
le u daa bitafal ŋeer baah tun pu na.
5Tɔ, fenn ki gaŋ Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan;
6le aa yaa si chob kaa kpa tijɔŋ tibaa kan,
Uwumbɔr ga dan ki nan ter si
ki giin saadichal siin saabimbinyaan ngbaan pu.
7Saawangol limɔk wɔŋ na aa ye nibaa.
Uwumbɔr aah ga tii si li n‑yoonn ngbaan na
ga jer lima ngbaan pel pel.
8Lik n‑yaajayoonn na aalan siib na;
dakl lik titetiib aah nan bae ibamɔn i na.
9Timi aamɔfal aa fɔk, le taa nyi nibaa kpala;
ti chuun jer kitiŋ pu ke tijunjunn na la.
10Tee cha n‑yaayoonn na aalandam bae si tiwan;
li pel baah ga li kpa pu bi len na.
11Timɔɔmoor aan ŋmaa muun nnyun aa kaa bi nin chee na;
ti bi kipuuk ni ŋmeen la.
12Nnyun yaa foor kan, tima le puen yɔl,
le ki laa par ke bi chee ti ki di tun lituln.
13Binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na bi kina la;
bi yaa suln Uwumbɔr bɔr kan, baamakl doo le na.
14Bi joo naadii tii nkokongaal la;
bi tii nandala aakokonn naadii la.
15Bi yaa di bibaa din nandala aakokonn kan,
ti ga ŋmaa ter bi ii?
Bi yaa ŋmaan chuu nkokongaal kan,
mu ga ŋmaa ter bi aan bi sil aa?
16Titunwanbirdam bunni ke timoor aah bunni nwindam ni pu na la,
bi bunni ke timoor aah bunni kisaak ni pu na la.
17Taanyaan fen joo ŋitakpal, le ki bub joo litakpal mɔk kin kin.
18Tɔ, chuu daa ŋɔb ti, le ubaa aan ki bee ke ti ba si nima.
19Mbamɔn, titunwanbir aamɔɔn kookoo le bi na;
bibaa le ga dan ki nan gaa baabuu ni.
20Le Uwumbɔr aan siir cha unii u tun ni ŋan na ma,
kaan tii titunwanbirdam mu nterm.
21U ga ki cha aa laa ki teen mpɔɔn pu,
22le ki tee ga cha binib bi nan si na ji inimɔɔn,
le bibiindam aadichal ga wɔŋ.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Job aah len pu na
1-2Mbamɔn, m puun ŋun kina aabɔr a.
Tɔ, unibɔn ga ŋa kinye aan ki ji tibɔr ki lii Uwumbɔr?
3Ŋma ga ŋmaa kpak u?
U ga ŋmaa baa mbaan kina ki ti saa lichur,
le ubaa aan ŋmaa giin u kpala.
4Uwumbɔr aalan ni waapɔɔn nyaŋ a,
unii ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋman u.
5U cha ŋijoo foor ŋaabuu ni kaa nyi ke ŋi foor,
le waaŋuul ponn ni kan, u kuln ŋi.
6Uwumbɔr cha kitiŋ puul le ki jii;
u damni jaatɔlk mam bi joo kitiŋ na.
7U ga ŋmaa chuu nwiin ke mu taa ki puu,
ki ga ŋmaa chuu iŋmabi ke i taa li wiin kinyeek.
8Ubaa aa nan ter Uwumbɔr le u taln kitaapaak;
ubaa aa nan ki ter u ke u taa taa nnyusakpem aapeewanbiik na diin nnyun ni.
9Uwumbɔr di iŋmabi i bi yin i ke Ipeel Kpaan,
ni Orionn, ni Pleyades, ni i bi ŋŋangii wɔb na leen kitaapaak.
10Taan ŋmaa bee waah ŋani tiwankpaan ni na aatataa,
le waajinjiir aatun aa kpa ndoon.
11Uwumbɔr jer m chee, le maa waa u.
12U yoor tiwan ni u ban na la, le ubaa aa ŋmaa chuu u;
ubaa aan kaa ki baa u ke, “Aa ŋani ba?”
13Uwumbɔr chur waaŋuul, u kuln waadim bi nan ter
nnyusakpem ni aapeewanbiik Rahab ke ki kpak u na.
14Kina pu na, m ga ŋa kinye aan ki kan ŋimɔbon ki di gar u?
15Hali maah kaa kpa taani ubaa na, maah ga ŋmaa ŋa pu na le ye
ke m gaŋ Uwumbɔr u ji mi tibɔr na ke u san mi kinimbaak.
16Hali u yaa tii mi nsan ke m len kan, maa dak ke u ga pel m chee.
17U cha kitaabuŋ daar yoor mi le ki ki tii mi titotonn,
le maa nyi maa tun taani u na.
18Waa tii mi lifuur; le ki cha maamɔfal ye mi mpombiin ŋmeen.
19M di linimaln mɔk Uwumbɔr aa?
M di u buen bibɔjirb chee ee? Ubaa ga ŋmaa cha u buen aa?
20Maa kpa taani le ki tun ni ŋan na,
tɔ, maamɔbon mu tee naahn ŋaah kpa na,
le maah len tibɔr timɔk na naahn taah bii mi le na.
21-22Maa kpa taani, m mu aatafal aa ki bi nibaa ni.
Maa ki neen limɔfal lee. Nibaa aa ki muk m chee;
ni yaa ye tibɔnyaan, bee libɔkpol kan,
Uwumbɔr ga kuln timi.
23Unii u kaa kpa taani na yaa kpaan lir ki kpo kan,
Uwumbɔr laa la.
24Uwumbɔr di dulnyaa wee tii bibiindam la.
U cha bibɔjirb mɔmɔk jɔb.
Uwumbɔr yaa kaa ŋa kina kan, ŋma ŋa?
25Maawiin san jer la, le i ponn ni mubaa kina aa ŋan.
26Maamɔfal jer mala ke buŋɔb bu ŋmaa chuun sakpen na la,
ki naahn likaagiil aah booni pu ke li ti chuu sandee na la.
27-28M yaa laa limɔmumukl ke m suln maaween bɔr kan,
le maafalaa mɔmɔk gir ban ni mi;
m nyi ke Uwumbɔr bui ke maabɔr bii a.
29Maabɔr aah bii na, ntafal ki bi bayaar ni?
30Bukiib bubaa aan ŋmaa finn nyan maatunwanbir.
31Uwumbɔr di mi mee lii tijɔŋ aatambuuk ni la,
le maawanpeenkaan gur san mi maah kpa inimɔɔn pu na.
32Uwumbɔr yaa ba ye unibɔn kan, m ba ga ŋmaa giin gar u;
ti ba ga ŋmaa buen bibɔjirb chee ki ti lik timi aanikpakpak ngbaan aabɔr.
33Tɔ, ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa yakr timi,
ubaa aa bi ki ga ji m ni Uwumbɔr tibɔr.
34Uwumbɔr, taa ki dar ntafal.
Taa ki cha saajawaan sakpiin ngbaan choo m chee.
35Maa san ijawaan,
maah nyi nsui ponn ni aabɔr na, m ga len.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
1M nuur limɔfal lee. Pel maapombiin aabɔr.
2Uwumbɔr, taa bui ke maabɔr bii.
Bui mi maabɔr aah bii pu na.
3Ni ŋan ke aa li kpa mbiin kina aa?
Ni ŋan ke aa lik seen tiwan ni sin aabaa naan ni na aa?
Ni ŋan ke aa tee laa limɔmumukl bibiindam aah kpokl pu na aa?
4Aa lik tiwan ke taah lik ni pu na la aa?
5Saamɔfal mu aa fɔk ke timi yaan na la aa?
6Kina kan, ba ŋa aa chur maatunwanbir mɔmɔk bilni,
ki tee mban ki ban maataani u mɔmɔk m kpa na?
7Aa nyi ke maabɔr ŋan; aa nyi ke ubaa aan ŋmaa gaa mi aa chee lii.
8Saaŋaal le naan ki maa mi,
le iŋaal baan ngbaan le ki bii mi doo dandana.
9Teer ke tiyakr le aa nan di naan mi;
aa ban ke aa ki gbaa wɔi mi ŋa titan la aa?
10Sin le tii nte mpɔɔn le u di kan mi,
sin le cha m biir nna aaponn ni.
11Sin le naan nwon le ti kpa ikpab ni ŋigir,
le ki di tinann ni ngban biin ikpab ngbaan pu.
12Aa tii mi limɔfal ni ngeehm mu kaa kpa ndoon na,
le saah joo mi pu na cha m fu.
13Le m bee dandana ke aa looni ki ban ke aa ku mi la.
14Aa nan pekr mi ki lik ke m ga tun titunwanbir aan maan tun,
le ki yii kaa di cha pinn mi.
15Libuul li ni aan m tun titunwanbir na, le m koo saabɔr ni,
le m yaa tee tun ni ŋan na kan, maa kani tipar tibaa.
M kpa kinimbaak, le ki ye inimɔɔn ŋmeen,
16hali m yaa kan tinyoor kan,
see aa taa taa chuu mi ke uchinn na;
le ki kpaan tun lijinjiir aatun ke aa di tii mi titotonn.
17Aa kpa m pu biseeraadam n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la;
le saah kpa liŋuul li m pu na moo kpae cha;
n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, aa kpokl m pu isapɔɔn la.
18Uwumbɔr, ba ŋa aa cha bi ma mi?
M yaa ba nan kpo ubaa aa kee kan mi kan, ni ba ŋan.
19M yaa ba nan nyan nna aaponn ni ki ti kpaan koo likaakul ni kan, ni ba ga li ŋan ke u kaa bi kpala na la.
20Di cha mi suuna. Maamɔfal aa kuln le na aa?
Cha m ji mmɔɔn n‑yoonn mu gur siib na ni.
21Libuul lee ni le m cha, kaan ki gir ni daalbaadaal;
m cha kitiŋ ki bɔɔn timm na ni la,
22kitiŋ ki ye mbɔmbɔɔn, ni tijunjunn, ni nlanŋmal na ni,
nima chee aawiihn mubaa ye mbɔmbɔɔn la.

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Sofar aah len pu na
1-2Ubaa aan gar bɔfam wee la aa?
Libɔlen sakpeln ga ŋmaa tii unii mbamɔn aa?
3Job, aa dak ke taan ŋmaa gar si la aa?
Aa dak ke saasiibiil ŋee ga cha ti li gur ka ŋmin la aa?
4Aa bui ke saah len pu na ye mbamɔn la;
aa bui ke aa ŋan Uwumbɔr chee la.
5Uwumbɔr yaa ba ga gar si kan, m ba gee kina sakpen.
6U ba ga bui si ke nlan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ wiir pam;
ke tiwan pam bi aan unibɔn aalan aan ŋmaa bee ni.
Uwumbɔr aa daa aatafal ki ŋeer saah tun pu na.
7Aa ga ŋmaa mɔk Uwumbɔr aapɔɔnsakpiin aanaanmɔk aa?
8Kitaapaak aa ye Uwumbɔr aanaanmɔk, le ki daa aa chee pam.
Uwumbɔr nyi bitekpiib do, le aa ma aa nyi nima.
9Uwumbɔr aapɔɔnsakpiin pee jer kitiŋ, ki waa jer nnyusakpem.
10Uwumbɔr yaa chuu si ki di si buen libɔjil kan,
ŋma bi ki ga ŋmaa nyii u pu?
11Uwumbɔr nyi binib bi kaa bi tibaa ni na;
u waa baatunwanbir mɔmɔk.
12Buyoonn timoor ni aabon ti ma aan ubo ngbaan aa bir na,
le bilatiirb mu ga kan nlan.
13Job, cha aapobil li si chob. Li ban Uwumbɔr.
14Nyan titunwanbir, ni taani saachiln ni,
15ki ki di ntaakpab pɔɔn, ni linimaln tii dulnyaa,
16le saamuk mɔmɔk ga nya aayil ni,
ke nwam mu jer aan bi suln mubɔr na.
17Le saamɔfal ga li wiin jer nwinkapiin pu aawiin,
le limɔfal ni aayoonn mu bɔɔn sakpen na ga woln ke lichakpitaawoln na.
18Aa ga li bi ŋŋmarm ni, ki li kpa limakl;
Uwumbɔr ga li kii si, ki tii si lifuur.
19Saan li san saadim;
binib pam le ga dan nan ban nterm aa chee.
20Le bibiindam ma ga lik ban ni ntaakpayɔl,
ki kan ke ŋŋmarm aa bi.
Baamakl libaa li bi na le ye ke nkun ga dan.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2Mbamɔn, nimi le ye binib mɔmɔk aaneel.
Ni yaa kpo kan, nlan mu kpoi diir nimi la.
3Le naah kpa nlan sakpen pu na, m mu kpa kina;
naa soor mi nibaa chee, unii mɔmɔk nyi naah len pu na.
4Njɔtiib bibaa gur laa mi la;
maa kpa taani, le maabimbin ŋan, le bi laa mi.
Uwumbɔr nan tee kii maameel n‑yoonn mubaa.
5Nimi aa kpa ŋimuk, le ki tee ŋani mi mbɔnyun;
unii ban u lir la, le ni ki faa u.
6Tɔ, binaayukb ni binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na bi nsuudoon ni,
bi bui ke Uwumbɔr bi biŋaal ni.
7Inyoon ni ipeel kpa tiwan sakpen i di mɔk nimi,
8mee kitiŋ ni nnyusakpem ni aawanfuurkaan aan ni tii nimi naalan.
9Tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk nyi ke Uwumbɔr aaŋaal le naan ni.
10Uwumbɔr le joo waawanaankaan aamɔfal;
unibɔn mɔk aamɔfal bi uma le aapɔɔn ni.
11Tɔ, nilambil aah neen tijikaar aalakm pu na,
kina le nitafal mu neen tibɔr aaŋum.
12-13Bininkpiib kpa nlan, Uwumbɔr ma kpa nlan ni mpɔɔn la.
Bininkpiib kpa ichiin;
le Uwumbɔr ma kpa ichiin ni mpɔɔn ke u di tun.
14Uwumbɔr yaa gbaa ber bil kan, ŋma ga ŋmaa maa,
ŋma ga ŋmaa nyan unii u Uwumbɔr chuu u piin na lii?
15Uwumbɔr yaa chuu utaal kan, le ntaaweel bi;
le u yaa chur nnyun lii ni kan, nwam nya.
16Uwumbɔr pɔɔ, le ki kani linyaŋ n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
binib bi ŋmanni na, ni baah ŋmanni binib bi na mɔmɔk bi waapɔɔn ni la.
17U nyani bitinjoob aalan, le ki cha bisalolm tun kijɔrk aatun.
18U nyani bibɔrb nnaan ni ki joo bi ŋani tiyondir ni;
19u sunni bitotoorb, ni binib bi bi mpɔɔn ni na taab.
20U cha baah tii binib bi naadii na ŋmini,
le ki nyani bininkpiib aalan bi chee.
21U jinni binib bi bi mpɔɔn ni na inimɔɔn,
le ki cha bitinjoob aapɔɔn door.
22U cha nwiihn chaa ŋibuu ŋi ponn ni bɔɔn ke nkun na.
23U tii ŋitimbol mpɔɔn sakpiin, le ki nan tee nyaŋ ki kuln ŋi.
24U cha ŋaasalolm ŋani bijɔrb, le ki cha bilan ŋmalni bi,
le bi chuun yiini ki ti wɔŋ;
25bi chuun baani mbɔmbɔɔn ni, le ki tuul ke bidagbiib na.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1-2Naah len pu na mɔmɔk, m puun ŋun kina.
M beer ti mɔmɔk aatataa; naah nyi pu na, m mu nyi kina la.
Maa ye nimi aamaasoor.
3Tɔ, m ni Uwumbɔr le kpa tibɔr, naa ye nimi;
m ban m ni uma le kpak tɔb.
4Ni joo inyamɔn le biini nimi aamaanyi pu;
ni naahn biteteeb bi kaan ŋmaa cha unii ubaa pɔɔk na la.
5Taa ki len tibaa man, ki cha ubaa dakl ke ni kpa nlan la.
6Li pel ki cha m ŋeer maabɔr man.
7Ba ŋa ni geei inyamɔn?
Ni dak ke nimi aanyamɔn ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr tinyoor la aa?
8Ni pɔɔni nibaa ke ni kpee u pu la aa?
Nimi le ga ji waabɔr bibɔjirb chee tii u uu?
9Uwumbɔr yaa lik nimi suuna kan,
u ga kan tiwanyaan nibaa ni chee ee?
Ni dak ke ni ga ŋmaa ŋmann Uwumbɔr
ke naah ŋmanni binib pu na la aa?
10Hali nimi aalandak aah bɔr pu na,
u ga sak nimi mbamɔm,
11le waapɔɔn ga cha ijawaan sakpiin chuu nimi.
12Nimi aayataŋak bi fam ke nfatan na la;
le nimi aanikpakpak wur lir ke tiyakr na.
13Ŋmin suuna man, ki tii mi nsan aan m len,
ki cha tiwan ni ga ŋa na ŋa.
14M kii ke m di maamɔfal paan talmaa.
15M ki kpa limakl libaa, Uwumbɔr yaa ba ga ku mi kan,
ni ba ga li ŋan.
M ban m ŋeer maabɔr tuk u la.
16Nibaakan, maayigbei ga gaa mi lii,
ba pu? ubiindaan ubaa aan kaa ki sil Uwumbɔr chee.
17Tɔ, li pel maabɔr aah ye pu na man.
18M gor ke m ŋeer maabɔr,
ba pu? m nyi ke m kpa mbamɔn.
19Uwumbɔr, aa choo aa nan galn mi la aa?
Aa yaa ba ŋa kina kan, ni ŋeer ke m ŋmin ki kpo.
20Cha m mee tiwan nilee; kii tii mi, aan m taa bɔr si;
21taa ki dar ntafal, ki taa di ijawaan sakpiin wɔb mi bil.
22Uwumbɔr, puen len waahr aan m gar si.
Aa yaa ti ki gee kan, aa cha m puen len aan aa gar mi.
23Maatunwanbir ye ba? M tun ba aataani?
Ba aabiil aan aa di bui ke maabɔr bii?
24Ba ŋa aa minn mi?
Ba ŋa aa ŋani mi ke maah ye saadin le na?
25Aa ban ke aa faan mi la aa?
M ye kifark la, aa bi tak kimokuun la.
26Aa joo tibɔr ti wu mponn ni na le galni mi,
hali maah nan laa ye ubo pu na aatun le aa joo galni mi.
27Aa di tikululn le baa ntaa;
aa lik maah yoor litaal limɔk na,
le ki lik ki nyi maataabuu.
28Nima pu le m wur lir ke busub bu bur na,
ki naahn ŋipɔbilee aabim aah ŋman libɔkul li na.

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1Bi ma ti mɔmɔk, ti ye tiwonkpir le kaa kpa uteter.
Ti mɔmɔk bi tibɔbir, ni kimɔfageŋ baan ni la.
2Ti muuni le ki gbaar mala ke nsupuun na;
ti wɔŋni ke tijunjunn na la.
3Uwumbɔr, aa fenn lik mi
le ki di mi buen libɔjil ni ke aa ti ji mi tibɔr aa?
4Tiwanyaan nibaa aan ŋmaa nyan ni unibɔn, tijɔŋdaan ni.
5Waamɔfal aafɔfɔk puun ŋaŋ dɔ ni daa,
aa nyi iŋmal imɔk u ga li bi limɔfal ni na.
Aa ŋaŋ ni siin, le ubaa aan ŋmaa kpeln ni.
6Taa ki lik u chee, ki di cha u suuna;
u yaa ga ŋman kan, cha u ji waamɔfapɔɔl ngbaan.
7Busub bu bi gaa gii bu na beenin kpa limakl;
bu ga ki ŋmaa bunn.
8Nibaakan, bu aasubon ga por,
le bu aasukpiil mu kuur sunn taab,
9nnyun yaa bi kan, bu ga ki bunn ke busub bu laa pɔɔn na.
10Le unibɔn ma kpo kan, waadoon le na;
u kee kpo kan, u ki bi la?
11Ŋimɔɔ aah geei kaan ki puu, aan tibɔr aanyun mu kuur pu na,
12kina le binib mu kpoi, kaan ki fii kpala.
N‑yoonn mumɔk kitaapaak ga li bi na,
baan ki finn daalbaadaal; baan ki finn baageen pu kpala.
13M ba ga li gee ke aa di mi bɔr bitekpiib do la;
cha m li bɔr aan saaŋuul ti sɔŋ waahr,
aan ki nin siin n‑yoonn mu aa ga teer mbɔr na.
14Unibɔn yaa kpo kan, u ga ki ŋmaa gir ni limɔfal ni ii?
Le m ma ga kiir n‑yoonn mu ŋan na;
m ga kiir aan tibɔr aayoonn mue ti jer doo.
15Le aa yin mi, le m kii,
le aasui ga piir min saawanaankaan pu.
16Le aa ga li lik litaal limɔk m ga yoor na,
kaan li chur maatunwanbir ma bilni.
17Aa ga di cha pinn mi ki suln tibɔr;
aa ga ber taani umɔk m tun na.
18N‑yoonn bi, le ŋijoo lir,
le ŋijoomɔju ŋi pɔɔ kib na foor ŋaabuu ni.
19Nnyun ga ŋmaa cha ŋitakpal donn,
le utaal sakpiin ga puu titan buen;
kina le aa kuln unibɔn aamakl kookoo.
20Aa nyaŋni unibɔn, le ki jenni u lir kookoo;
nkun ni, le unimbil wɔb paa paa igban.
21Ujapɔtiib kani bunyuŋ, le waa nyi;
le ubaa mu aan tuk u buyoonn bi ji inimɔɔn na.
22Ubaa aawon aaween,
ni ubaa aasuubiin baanja pu le u nyi.

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Lelee aabɔgbaal
(Job 15.1–21.34)
Elifas aah len pu na
1-2Job, bɔfam, bɔfam.
3Unii u kpa nlan na aan len tibɔr ke saah len pu na,
bee u di ŋimɔbon ŋi kaa kpa tataa na len ter ubaa.
4Aa yaa ba kpa aabaa aapɔɔn kan,
unii ubaa aa ba ga san Uwumbɔr, ubaa aa ba ga li dooni u.
5Saabɔlen le mɔk saah kpa mbiin pu na;
aa joo nlan aabɔlen le pɔɔni aabaa ke aa di saabiin bɔr.
6Maan ki li ka ke m galn si
saah len tibɔr timɔk na le galn si.
7Aa dak ke sin le bi nan puen ma aa?
Uwumbɔr aah nan naan ŋijoo na, aa nan bi ii?
8Aa nan jer ki ŋun ilandak i Uwumbɔr ŋa na aa?
Sin baanja le bi di unibɔn mɔmɔk aalan tii ii?
9Tiwan nibaa aa bi aa nyi ni aan tima aa nyi.
10Ti bae timi aalan bininkpiib bi pan iyikpipiin na chee la,
bijab bi nan bi aan bi nin ma aate na chee le ti bae.
11Uwumbɔr tii si mmɔɔn; ba ŋa aa beenin yiil mu?
Ti di mbɔdiim le len tii u suuna,
12le aasui fii, le aa lik timi ke saah ban aa nab timi le na.
13Aa gee Uwumbɔr pu liŋuul, le ki bui ke waa ki ye nibaa.
14Unibɔn ulau bi chain?
Ŋma ga li ŋan Uwumbɔr chee ki ti doo?
15Hali Uwumbɔr aa tii waatuuntiib naadii;
bima bibaa aa ŋan u chee ki ti doo.
16Le unibɔn nyu titunwanbir ke naah ye nnyun le na;
mbamɔn, unibɔn bii doo; unibɔn ye fam la.
17Job, li pel maah nyi pu na.
18Bilandam mɔk mi ibamɔn i bi bae bitetiib chee na,
kaa di tibɔr tibaa bɔr mi.
19Biwɔwɔm aa nan bi baatiŋ ni;
unii u ga nan ŋmann bi aan bi nya Uwumbɔr chee na aa nan bi.
20Ubiindaan u muk biken na,
ga li bi iween ni le waamɔfal mɔmɔk ni.
21U ga li ŋun ijawaan aaneel tar utafal ni,
le buyoonn u dak ke u fuur na, le binaayukb nan lir u pu.
22Waa kpa limakl ke u ga ŋmaa nya mbɔmbɔɔn ni,
ba pu? kijaak aajuk dɔ kii u nibaa chee ki ku u,
23le nangba mam ka kii waawon.
U nyi ke waataak ki ga woln na bɔɔn la;
24tibɔbir ti bi ke ubɔrpɔɔndaan ubaa na dɔ kiir u ke ti tak u la.
25Unii u fik kiŋanbik mɔk ki sii Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na aadoon le na.
26-27Unii ngbaan kpa kigaak ki yiil Uwumbɔr;
u di tafalaaŋun le chuu waapeln kin kin
ki ber ke u ni Uwumbɔr jan kijaak.
28Unii u nyaŋ ntim, ki gaa ŋidichal ŋi aadindatiib san na le na,
le butɔb ga nan kuln ntim ni ŋidichal ngbaan.
29Waan li ye uwankpadaan ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na;
waah kpa tiwan ni na aan yunn,
30le waan ŋmaa san ŋmar mbɔmbɔɔn chee.
U ga li naahn busub bu aabon wun mmii,
aan libuln daa bu aapuun buen na la.
31U yaa jɔr sakpen le ki di naadii tii titunwanbir kan,
titunwanbir le ga li ye waapar.
32U ga faan le waayoonn nin fuu;
u ga faan ke busub aabon na, kaan ki tuŋ kpala.
33U ga li naahn ŋisubil aasub bu aasubikar ker lir na la;
ki naahn olif aakpan aasub bu aapuun gbaar na.
34Binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na aan li kpa yaabitiib,
le mmii ga wun baah di igaŋgaŋlik maa ŋidichal ŋi na.
35Kina aanib le kpokl tibɔbir ki tun titunwanbir na;
bisui gbii ŋŋmann le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2M puun ŋun naah len pu na mɔmɔk a;
naah sɔŋni nsui pu na ye mi iween la.
3Ni ga li len kina kaan ŋmin la aa?
Nimi le yeh kookoo aamɔbon aa?
4Nimi le yaa ba ye mi le m mu ye nimi kan,
m ba ga len naah len pu na mɔmɔk.
M ba ga gbɔk n‑yil ke ulandaan na,
le ki di ŋimɔbon yaar yii ni pu.
5M ba ga di nsurm pɔɔk nitaakpab, ki li len sɔŋni nisui.
6Tɔ, maah len pu na ye fam la,
le m yaa ka ŋmin mu kan, maaween aa sɔŋni.
7Uwumbɔr, aa doo mi a; aa cha bi ku maadichal aanib.
8Sin le ye maadin, le ki chuu mi.
M gur ye ngban ni ikpab ŋmeen la,
le binib joo nima ŋani mi seeraa ke maabɔr aa ŋan.
9Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ni, le u dar par mi iŋaal ni ŋitaa;
u joo kinanaŋ le lik mi.
10Binib lik mi mbɔnyun aanimbilikl la;
bi lol goln mi le ki yur mi ntapam.
11Uwumbɔr di mi tii titunwanbirdam.
12M nan bi nsuudoon ni la, le Uwumbɔr nan chib chuu nneen ni,
ki di mi yur yur ki kool mi.
Uwumbɔr di unimbil kaan mi le pu,
13ki too mi ipiin i saa chaar mi ki tii mi titotonn
ŋipepel mɔmɔk na, le kaa kpaan san mi kinimbaak.
14U tii mi titotonn ki ki tii mi titotonn;
u tak mi ke butɔb aaja u waar kinanaŋ pu na la.
15M wii ikpowiil ki pee tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na,
le ki ka titan ni, kaa ki bi tibaa ni.
16M wii le nnimbil wɔb ti mann chaun,
nnimbil duun tigbingbinn,
17m mu aa kpa titunwanbir tibaa aagalm,
maameel li chaa Uwumbɔr chee na aa kpa tijɔŋ.
18Kitiŋ, taa di baah tun mi taani pu na bɔr.
Taa cha maah yin ki ban mbamɔn pu na ŋmin fam.
19Ubaa bi paacham, ki ga ŋmaa sil nchaŋ ni, ki len tii mi.
20Njɔtiib laa mi la; le nnimbil bar tinyunyunn tii Uwumbɔr.
21M ban ke ubaa gaŋ Uwumbɔr tii mi
ke unii aah gaŋni ujɔ pu pu na la.
22Maabin jer cha la,
le m chuun nsan mu kaa kpa ngirm na pu.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1Maamɔfal aadoon peen ni a. Maa ki ŋmaa fuur;
likaakul baanja le gur ye maamakl.
2M ka mpombiin ni, le ki lik binib aah ŋani mi yansara pu na.
3Uwumbɔr, m len ibamɔn la. Gaa maamɔboln.
Ubaa aa ki bi ki ga sil maah len pu na pu.
4Aa cha bi ŋa bilatiirb la;
taa ki cha bi nyaŋ mi n‑yoonn mue.
5Liyataŋakpokl na ni, unii kooh ujɔtiib ŋimombil pu,
le waabim nan ji naafalaa.
6Binib gur joo kina aayataŋakl ŋakl mi;
bi choo le ki nan tei timɔɔtan ŋani nnimbil wɔb.
7Maasuugar ti kpaan jɔb mi la;
le ŋŋaal ni ntaa gur naahn tijunjunn.
8Ni ŋa binib bi bui ke bi si chob na lijinjiir la;
le bi mɔmɔk bii mi ke maa nyi Uwumbɔr.
9Binib bi bui ke bi ye kipak aanib na moo kani ntaakpab pɔɔn
ke bima le kpa mbamɔn.
10Tɔ, bi mɔmɔk mu yaa kuun nan sil nnimbiin ni kan,
maan kan bi ponn ni ulandaan ubaa.
11Maawiin jer a; le maalandak bee fam; maamakl doo a.
12Le njɔtiib ma bui ke kinyeek le ye nwiin pu;
bi len ke nwiihn duun ni a,
le m ma nyi ke m gaar mbɔmbɔɔn ni la.
13Kitekpiitiŋ le gur ye maamakl,
nima chee le m ga doon ki geen mbɔmbɔɔn ni.
14M ga yin likaakul ke nte la;
le ki yin ŋikpaambil ŋi ŋmɔ mi na ke nna ni nninkpatiib.
15La chee aan maamakl ki bi? Ŋma waa libaa?
16M yaa sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni kan,
limakl aan dii mi buen nima.

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bildad aah gar pu na
1-2Job, binib bi bi ke sin na aan ŋmaa ŋmin la aa?
Aa yaa ba ŋmin ke aa pel kan, ti ba ga len aa chee tibɔr.
3Ni ye ba cha aa dak ke ti jɔr ke inaa na?
4Aa ki joo saaŋuul tii aabaa le titotonn.
Saaŋuul ga ŋmaa cha kitiŋ kpaln nkuun aa?
Uwumbɔr ga foor ŋijoo ke ni mɔɔr si ii?
5Ubiindaan aamii ga sil junn la;
mu aamiigaal aan ki gaa daalbaadaal.
6Karyaa u si waadiik ni na ga bɔnn timm.
7U nan si chob la, le dandana ma u chuun gbeer;
uma ubaa aasurm pu le u ga lir.
8U chuun le ki ti lir gaawɔb ni, le u chuu utaa;
9gaawɔb le chuu utaagbeln ki chɔb joo u kin kin.
10Kakpaklaa bɔr kitiŋ ki kii u; gaawɔb le pen waasan ni.
11Ijawaan sakpiin le mann goln ki kii u;
i dii u waah yoor litaal limɔk na ni.
12U nan kpa liwangol, le ki gur chuun nkon;
tibɔbir si kii u ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu.
13Kiweenwanbiik le yaa gaa uwon mɔmɔk ni,
le ki cha uŋaal ni utaa bur.
14Bi daa nyan u waadichal li ponn ni u nan bi ŋŋmarm ni na,
le ki dar u cha ke u ni Ubɔr Nkun ti kan tɔb.
15Bi yaa di chirbil yaa waadichal ni ki finn li kan,
unii umɔk gee na ga ŋmaa li koo li ni.
16Waasubon ni ŋipan yɔl ki kuur a.
17Waayimbil kuln udo, ni itingbaan mɔmɔk ni;
ubaa aa ki teer ubɔr.
18Bi ga jenn nyan u binib bi fu na aatiŋ ni,
bi ga jenn nyan u nwiihn ni ki di koon mbɔmbɔɔn ni.
19Waa kpa yaabitiib, waa kpa ubaa u ŋmar.
20Ki nya liwipuul ki ti saa liwilir,
unii umɔk ŋun u pu na aawon ga li jii ki gbeeni ijawaan pu.
21Bibiindam aadoon le na.
Binib bi kaa di Uwumbɔr yin nibaa na aadoon le na.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2Ba ŋa ni joo tibɔr tii mi iween?
3Ni seei mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
le kaa san inimɔɔn naah seei mi pu na pu.
4Hali m yaa galn le kan, kina ngbaan ŋa nimi ba?
5Ni dak ke ni soor mi la,
le ki len ke maabɔbir le ye maagalm aaseeraa.
6Naa waa ke Uwumbɔr le ŋa nimina aa?
Uma le pen gaawɔb ke u chuu mi.
7Maa kii waatunbir ngbaan pu, le ubaa mu aa pel;
ubaa aa ŋun maabamɔn aawiil pu.
8Uwumbɔr le laŋ nsan, le maa ŋmaa jer;
u di maasan bɔr mbɔmbɔɔn ni la.
9U yoor maawangol mɔmɔk buen, le ki bii maayimbil.
10U joo mi yur ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu la.
U chuu daa ŋɔb maamakl,
le ki di cha mi ke m yɔl ki kpo.
11Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii, le u bil ban mi;
u ŋani mi ke waadinkpaan na la.
12U cha waajab nan tak mi;
bi gbii ŋibuu gob maadichal.
13Uwumbɔr cha nnaabitiib yii mi;
m gur ye uchaan le binib bi nan nyi mi na chee;
14Ndoyaab ni njɔtiib mɔmɔk buen a.
15Binib bi nan ye maacham na suln mbɔr;
le maanaagbiipiib gur ŋani mi ke maah ye uchaan
ni uwɔwɔnja le bi chee na.
16M yaa ki yin maatutunn kan, waa keei;
hali m yaa gaŋ u ke u ter mi kan, waa gar mi.
17Mpuu aa ki ŋman maafuurk aanunun,
le nnaabitiib bibaa aa ki ŋɔŋni m chee.
18Mbim lik seeni mi, le ki yaa kan mi kan, bi laa.
19Njɔtiibamɔm gur nan mi la;
maah nan gee binib bi sakpen na le fenn lir m pu.
20Maagban gur lee maakpab pu la; m ŋmar siib kina la.
21Ni ye njɔtiib la. San mi kinimbaak man.
Uwumbɔr aaŋaal le faa mi bil.
22Ba ŋa ni muk mi ke Uwumbɔr aah ŋani pu na?
Naah muk mi pu na aa ŋeer aa?
23M ba neen ke ubaa ga ŋmaa teer maabɔr
ki ŋmee ti ŋa kigbaŋ ni;
24bee u di kichiln ŋmee maabɔr paan litakpal pu
aan ti li ŋmee dɔ nima ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
25Le m tee nyi ke ubaa bi paacham ki nan len maabɔr tii mi.
26Hali iween aah di maawon ŋman doo
aan m beenin bi na, m ga kan Uwumbɔr.
27Nnimbil ga kan u gbin gbin, le waan li ye uwɔwɔnja m chee.
28Naah bui ke, “Ti ga ŋa kinye ki saan u?” na, le ntaakpab yɔl.
Ni ban libɔkpiln le ke ni di tak mi.
29Tɔ, li san kijaak aajuk man,
li san kijaak aajuk ki joo ni Uwumbɔr aah gee liŋuul li titunwanbir pu na man,
aan ni bee ke ubaa bi ki ji binib tibɔr.

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Sofar aah gar pu na
1-2Job, aa bii nsui. Tɔ, nsui fii ke m gar si.
3Saah len pu na ye lisiibil la,
m mu nyi maah ga giin si pu na.
4Aa nyi gbin gbin ke n‑yaayoonn
mu unibɔn nan puen kal kitiŋ pu na,
5ubiindaan ubaa aa nan kani mpopiin ki cha dik dik.
6Nibaakan, u ga li ye unikpaan,
ki kpa liyimbil sakpen, nibaakan li ga ti tuu ntaalangbam,
7le libuln ga daa u buen ke titan na.
Binib bi nan nyi u na ga li gur baa ke u tee buen la chee?
8U ga wɔŋ ke tidaŋ ti aa daŋ kinyeek na la, le ubaa aan ki kan u.
9Ubaa aan ki kan u waah nan koo nin chee na;
10le waah nan sun tiwan ni bigiim chee na ga kpaln ujapɔtiib aapɔln.
11Uwon nan ye tinachipɔwon le ki pɔɔ nyaa,
le ti ga guun kpaln titan.
12-13Titunwanbir mirk u chee, le u kpob tibaa umɔb ni ki moor.
14Le tijikaar ngbaan ti tee toŋ uponn ni
ki to ke liluul mɔmɔk aah to pu na.
15Ubiindaan wulni liwangol li u nan sun li na la;
Uwumbɔr nyani li uponn ni, le ki gaa li.
16Utunwanbirdaan aah di tiwan ni nab na naahn liluul la;
ni ku u ke uwaa u kpa liluul na aah ku pu na la.
17Waan li bi ki kan buyoonn
n‑yaan ni nkpan ga nan li wiir ke limɔɔl aanyun na.
18U ga buen cha waah tun ki kan ni mɔmɔk na,
waan kan nsan ki ji waakpaal,
19ba pu? u nan muk bigiim kaa yin bi nibaa,
ki gaa ŋidichal ŋi bibaa maa ŋi na.
20Waakumɔŋ ti nyaŋ sakpen a.
21Waa ji ki gur nibaa lisambil ni,
le waawankam doo dandana.
22Waakam aah ga nyaŋ buyoonn na,
le falaa u bir na ga wɔb u bil.
23Cha u ji waah ban pu na mɔmɔk.
Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln ni le u ga daa utafal.
24U yaa ban u san ŋmar tikur aajuk chee kan,
tikumann aatɔm le ga too chaar u bil.
25Mpiin le saa chaar uwon na;
le waasin tuu mu aapinbim pu lir,
le ijawaan sakpiin chib chuu upobil.
26Waah kuun tiwan nimɔk bil na kuln a;
mmii mu unibɔn aaŋaal aa tuur mu na le ga wu waadichal.
27Paacham le kpiir kina aanii aatunwanbir pu,
le kitiŋ ji seeraa ke ti gbii.
28Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln li naahn nwam na le ga kuln
waawangol mɔmɔk.
29Ubiindaan aadoon le na,
Uwumbɔr aah di ndoon mu siin u na le na.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2Li pel maah len pu na;
maah ban mpopiin mu na le bi na.
3Tii mi nsan aan m len man,
m yaa ti doo aan ni yaa gee kan, ni laa mi.
4M ni unibɔn u ga kpo na aa kpa kijaak;
m kpa nsan ke maasuklaa doo.
5Lik mi man.
Nimina aa ŋeer ke ni cha ni li si lik ki ŋmin chii ii?
6M yaa dakl tiwan ni ŋa mi na pu kan,
nlan mɔk ŋmal la, le nwon gbaa le m jii.
7Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr cha titunwanbirdam kpa limɔfal,
ki cha bi por ki kani nkam?
8Bi kpa mbim ni yaabitiib,
le ki bi ki ti kan bi mɔmɔk aah chikr pu na.
9Uwumbɔr aa cha bi kani tibɔbir baadichal ni;
le baa nyi ijawaan sakpiin ibaa.
10Mbamɔn, baawakor mɔmɔk pɔr
le ki maa kaa kani falaa ubaa.
11Baabim san gbiir ke ipihbi na,
12le ki saar dii tibar ni kulufeeŋ mam.
13Bi bi nsuudoon ni le baamɔfal mɔmɔk ni,
le ki nan kpo suuna, kaa jin falaa ubaa.
14Bibiindam bui Uwumbɔr le ke u cha bi suuna;
baa ban ke bi bee waah ban bi tun pu na.
15Baa dak ke aa yaa tun tii Uwumbɔr kan, ni kpa tinyoor,
kaa nyi ke aa yaa mee u kan, ni kpa nterm.
16Bi dak ke bibaa aapɔɔn pu le bi kpa,
le m ma aan kii tii baalandak ngbaan.
17Ubiindaan aamii kee junn aa?
Bi ponn ni ubaa kee kan tibɔbir aa?
Uwumbɔr kee daa bibiindam aatafal waaŋuul ni
18ki daa bi buen ke kimook
bee kitaabuŋ aah daar titan cha pu na aa?
19Ni bui ke Uwumbɔr dar ubo aatafal ute aatunwanbir pu la.
M ma bui ke, cha Uwumbɔr daa titunwanbirdam aatafal;
cha u mɔk ke baatunwanbir pu le u ŋa kina.
20Cha titunwanbirdam kan bibaa aatafadaan;
Cha bi kan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aaŋuusakpeln.
21Unii aamɔfal yaa ti doo kan,
u ki dak waabim aapopiin pu uu?
22Unibɔn ga ŋmaa mɔk Uwumbɔr u ji binikpaam tibɔr na aa?
23-24Binib bibaa pɔɔ kina le ki ti saa baakun daal;
biwon soon bol bol le ki pɔɔ,
le bi kpa mpopiin ni nsuudoon ki ti kpo.
25Biken ma aa kpa mpopiin kpala;
bi bi le ki ti di mpombiin kpo.
26Le bi mɔmɔk mu tee kpoi le bi sui bi;
le ŋikpaambil pɔl bi mɔmɔk pu.
27M nyi tilandakwanbir ti ni kpa na.
28Ni baa le ke,
“Ujakpaan u nan tun titunwanbir na aadichal ki bi la?”
29Nimi ni binib bi chuun na aa kee gbaa tibɔr aa?
Naa nyi baah joo ni pu baasachun ngbaan ni na aa?
30Bundaal aan Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii aan u dar binib aatafal na,
bibiindam le ŋmar n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
31Ubaa aa bi ki ga galn ubiindaan,
bee u teen u waah tun pu na mɔmɔk.
32Bi yaa nan tu u cha kicheek ni,
nin chee bi si kii waakaakul mbamɔm na,
33binib churbakaa le chɔl dii u ki ye bijeendam,
le ki paar titan suuna biin uwon pu.
34Le nima pɔɔni nibaa ke ni di bɔfam sɔŋ nsui.
Inyamɔn ŋmeen le ni joo giini mi.

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Taataa Aabɔgbaal
(Job 22.1–27.23)
Elifas aah len pu na
1-2Unii ubaa bi, hali ulandaan bi
ki kpa tinyoor Uwumbɔr chee ee?
3Saatunyaan tii Uwumbɔr ba?
bee saabimbinyaan tii u ba aaterm?
4Naa ye ke saah san Uwumbɔr pu na
le cha u sak si ki jin si tibɔr.
5Naa ye kina, ni ye le ke aa tun titunwanbir sakpen.
6Ke aanaabo pa si waah joo si lipɔln li na,
see aa gaa waawanpeenkaan ki cha u uŋmeen.
7Aa yii kaa tii binib bi bak na nnyun,
kaa tii nkon aah joo bi na tijikaar.
8Aa nan di saapɔɔn ni saasisii gaa kitiŋ mɔmɔk.
9Aa nan yii kaa ter bikpopiib
le ki nan sun nkpobim aawan ki ŋa bi falaa.
10Kina pu na, ŋibugen le mann gob si na,
le ijawaan kpaan chuu si.
11Le ni bɔnn sakpen, le saa ki waa,
le nwam biin aa pu kookoo.
12Uwumbɔr bi paachapaacham
le ki gbuuni lik iŋmabi i bi paacham na.
13Le aa ki baa ke, “Uwumbɔr nyi ba?
ke ntaalangbam duk u, u ga ŋa kinye ki ji binib tibɔr?”
14Aa dak ke waah chuun kitaapaak pu na,
ntaalangbam mu gbii na duk u la.
15Aa sil ban ke aa dii isan i titunwanbirdam
puen dii na la aa?
16Nwam nan di bi puu buen le baayoonn nin fuu.
17Binib bee le nan yii Uwumbɔr
ki kpa lipobil ke waan ŋmaa ŋa bi nibaa.
18Tɔ, Uwumbɔr mu le nan tee cha bi ŋa biwankpadam,
maan ŋmaa bee bibiindam aalandak.
19Buyoonn Uwumbɔr daa bibiindam aatafal na,
bininyaam kpa mpopiin, le maa‑kpa‑taani‑dam laa.
20Bibiindam aah kpa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na kuln a,
le mmii wun tiwan ni mɔmɔk gur na.
21Tɔ, Job, cha aa ni Uwumbɔr ŋa nsuudoon aamɔbaan,
ki taa ki ŋani u ke saadin na.
Aa yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga ŋa waanyoor ŋa aa pu.
22Gaa waamɔkm mu u tii na; li joo waamɔbon aasui ni.
23Mbamɔn, gbaan aataŋaayil pu ki gir Uwumbɔr chee,
ki kuln titunwanbir ti mɔmɔk ŋa saadichal ni na.
24Di saasalmaa mae;
di saasalmaa u ŋan sakpen na ti mae mbufan ni.
25Cha Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan li ye saasalmaa,
ki cha u li ye tikunabr ti dɔ chun ki ye aayaar na.
26Le aa ga di naadii tii Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk
le ki bee ke uma le ye saapopiin mɔmɔk.
27Aa yaa mee u kan, u ga kii si,
le aa ga li joo tipuur ti aa puu na.
28Le aa ga kan tinyoor saatuln mɔk ni,
le nwiihn ga woln saasan ni.
29Uwumbɔr sunn bigaadam taab
le ki gaal binib bi sunn bibaa taab na lir.
30Saabɔr yaa ŋan kan, u ga gaa si lii,
Saah ŋani pu na yaa tok kan, u ga gaa si lii.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2M beenin len Uwumbɔr kaa kii tii u;
maan ki ŋmaa joo maawiil.
3M neen ke m ba li nyi maah ga ŋa pu ki ban kan u na,
ki ba li nyi nin chee m ga kan u na.
4M ba ga ŋeer maabɔr tuk u, ki len giin mbaa wɔb.
5M ban m bee waah ga len pu na la,
ki bee waah ga giin mi pu na.
6Uwumbɔr aan ŋmaa di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk ban mi.
Waan ŋa kina, u ga pel maah len pu na.
7Maa kpa beebee; m ni Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa gbaa maabɔr;
u ga bui ke m kpa mbamɔn ki nyan mi kookoo.
8M ban Uwumbɔr liwipuul wɔb, kaa kan u;
maah lik liwilir wɔb na, maa kan u nima chee mu.
9Uwumbɔr tun lituln ŋŋangan, ni ŋŋangii wɔb,
le maa ki kan u nima chee mu.
10Le Uwumbɔr tee nyi maah yoor litaal limɔk na;
u yaa tɔŋ mi kan, u ga kan ke maa kpa tijɔŋ tibaa.
11M dii nsan mu u lee na mbamɔm,
kaa yenn cha lipepel libaa.
12M ŋani Uwumbɔr aah len pu na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la;
m dii waageehn la, maa dii mbaa aasui aah ban pu na.
13Waa kpelni. Ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak u,
bee u nyii u pu ke u di cha waah ban u ŋa pu na.
14Waah siin ke u ŋa mi pu na, u ga ŋa kina;
waah siin siin ilandak sakpen pu na ponn ni nibaa le na;
15m san u, le nwon gbaa unimbiin ni.
16-17Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan kuln maataakpab pɔɔn a.
M san Uwumbɔr le ijawaan, naa ye mbɔmbɔɔn,
mbɔmbɔɔn le cha maa ki waa, m mu aa san mu ijawaan.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr aa siin libɔjil aawiin,
ba ŋa waa siin binib bi dii u na aabamɔn aawiin?
2Binib yoor upɔnja aatakpal foor ke bi moo kan kitiŋ;
le ki su ipiih ti kpae baapiih pu.
3Bi gaal nkpobim aabon,
le ki joo ukpopii aanaa ke see u ti pan waapɔln.
4Baa cha bigiim kani baabamɔn;
baatunwanbir pu le cha binib bi kaa kpa na san ti bɔrni.
5Kina pu na, bigiim chuun ban tijiir kipɔɔkuun ni
