ke timoor ni aabon na la;
baan ki ŋmaa kan tijikaar nibaa chee ki tii baabim.
6Ikpaakon i baa bun na ni, le bi ti chee,
le ki ker ŋisubil bibiindam aasui aasar ni.
7Bi doo kinyeek kaa kpa nibaa bi di biin bibaa pu,
nibaa aa bi, bi di kiir bibaa tiwoor chee.
8Utaal u nu ŋijoo pu na le gbaa bi,
le bi wuŋni ŋijootakpal taab.
9Mbipɔm bi kaa kpa tetiib na le titunwanbirdam chur ŋani baanaagbiib, le ki joo ugiin aabim pa waapɔln.
10See bigiim chuun tiwoor kaa kpa tiwanpeenkaan;
bi yaa bi chee tijikaar kan, bi li chee ti nkon.
11Bima le gbaa olif aakpan ki ŋmaani ŋisubil ki nyani ŋaanyun,
le nnyunyuu tee joo bi.
12Ntim ponn ni le binib bi kan titotonn na, ni binib bi bi kpoi na wii, le Uwumbɔr aa gaal baameel.
13Binib bi kaa gee nwiihn;
baa nyi mu aatataa, kaa cha mu aah cha nin chee na.
14Lichakpitaawoln le unikur finn ki cha u ti ku bigiim,
le kinyeek kan, u su.
15Uja u ye udagoor na ka kii liwimaln la;
le u poo biin unimbil wɔb ke ubaa taa bee u.
16Kinyeek le binaayukb koo ŋidichal ni,
le nwiin pu kan, bi bɔrni nwiihn.
17Bi san nwiin pu aawiihn la,
le mbɔmbɔɔn ma aa kpa bi ijawaan.
Sofar aah len pu na
18Le Sofar bui ke, “Nwam le joo ubiindaan cha,
le Uwumbɔr puun lii waatiŋ pu;
ubaa aa ki tun lituln waasui aasar ni.
19Ŋitaatakpal aah wɔŋni ntoton, ni ntaaweel ni pu na,
kina le utunwanbirdaan wɔŋni bimɔfadam aatiŋ pu.
20Hali una aa ki teer ubɔr;
ŋikpaambil le ŋman kuln u ke busub bu lir na.
21Waah nan ŋa bikpopiib falaa, kaa san bipiib bi kaa kpa
mbim na kinimbaak pu na le cha kina ŋa.
22Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn ni le u kuln bipɔɔndam;
Uwumbɔr tun, le ubiindaan kpo.
23Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa tii u ŋŋmarm, le ki tee lik u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
24Ubiindaan kani nkam ni yunni siib,
le naan yunn le u yɔl ke kimook na,
ki yɔl ke baah bar likalmaan li na.
25Ubaa ga ŋmaa nee ke nimina aa ye kina aa?
Ubaa ga ŋmaa kpak mi ke maabɔr aa gbii ii?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Bildad aah len pu na
1-2Uwumbɔr kpa mpɔɔn sakpen; unii mɔmɔk li san u;
U joo waapaacham nsuudoon ni la.
3Ŋma ga ŋmaa kahn waatuuntiib bi tun tii u na?
La chee bi, aan Uwumbɔr aawiihn aa wiin nima?
4Ŋma ye ki kpa mbimbinyaan ki bi chain Uwumbɔr chee?
5U chee kan, uŋmal ni iŋmabi aa wiin ki bi chain.
6Ŋmaninkabaa unibɔn, u ye tiwanfuurkaan na?
Unibɔn aa ye nibaa Uwumbɔr chee.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2Aa ye nterm nyaan le ki tii mi u ye ugiin u kaa kpa mpɔɔn na.
3Aa tii nsurm mu ŋan na le ki yakr saalan tii mi u ye ujɔr na.
4Aa dak ke ŋma ga pel saamɔbon ŋee?
Ŋma cha aa len tibɔr timina aaboln?
Bildad aah len pu na
5Bitekpiib aawiin bi nnyun ni, kitiŋ aataab le ki jii.
6Kitekpiitiŋ dɔ waa chain Uwumbɔr chee la;
libiil libaa aa duŋ ki u chee.
7Uwumbɔr le daa taln ŋŋangan wɔb aataapaak ki di kitiŋ laŋ,
nibaa aa joo ki.
8Uwumbɔr le cha nnyun gbiini ntaalangbam,
ki cha mu aanyunyuun aa ŋmaa puu mu.
9Uma le joo uŋmamɔn bɔrni ntaalangbam ni.
10U lol nkuul le gonn nnyusakpem paab
le ki yakr nwiin ni mbɔmbɔɔn tɔb chee.
11U yaa faan jaatɔlk mam bi joo kitaapaak na kan,
le ijawaan chuu bi, le biwon gbaa ki jii.
12Waapɔɔn le u nan di nyaŋ nnyusakpem;
U nan di waalan le ku nnyun ni aawanbiik Rahab.
13Waafuurk le woln kitaapaak chain,
le waaŋaal ku kiwanbiik ki nan san ki ŋmar na.
14Waapɔɔn aabɔr siib le na, tibɔlɔikaan ti ti ŋun na le na.
Ŋma ga ŋmaa bee mbamɔm Uwumbɔr aah pɔɔ sakpen pu na?

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
Job aah gar pu na
1-2M puu Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
ki yii waan tii mi ibamɔn ki cha maamɔfal choŋ na,
3ke waah cha m bi limɔfal ni n‑yoonn mumɔk na,
4maamɔb aan len tibɔbir daalbaadaal,
maalambil aan gii nnyamɔn daalbaadaal.
5Maan kii daalbaadaal ke nimi bijab bee kpa mbamɔn;
m ga li joo gbin gbin ke maa kpa taani le ki ti saa maakun daal.
6Maan di cha ki bui ke maabɔr bii daalbaadaal;
m nyi ke maa kpa taani.
7Cha binib bi mɔmɔk kpak mi ki jaa mi kijaak na
kan bibiindam ni titunwanbirdam aatafadaan.
8Uwumbɔr yaa ti ban u gaa binib bi kaa nyi u na aamɔfal kan,
ba aamakl aan bi ki kpa?
9Uwumbɔr ga ŋun baawiil tibɔbir yoonn aa?
10Ni ba ŋan ke bi li neen waah tii mpopiin mu na;
bi ba ga li mee u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
11Cha m mɔk si Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn aah nyaŋ pu na,
ki moo mɔk si Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah siin pu na.
12Aayii, maan mɔk si. Nimi nibaa kan kina;
ba pu aan ni ki gbaa bɔfam ngbaan?
Sofar aah len pu na
13Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan dar
bibiindam bi aabimbin pɔɔ na aatafal kina la.
14Nibaakan bi ga li kpa japɔtiib pam, le bi mɔmɔk ga kpo butɔb ni.
Baabim aa kani ki ji babr.
15Le iween ga ku bi ŋmar na,
le baakpopiib aan kpaan wii baakpuu.
16Nibaakan bibiindam aan ti ki li nyi baamombil mɔk
ki ga li kpa tiwanpeenkaan jer unii aah ban pu na;
17tɔ, uninyaan ubaa le ga nan peen tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan,
le ubamɔndaan ubaa nan gaa ŋimombil na.
18Bibiindam maa ŋidichal ke nandala aadiik na la,
ki naahn unaagbiija aah kaa libool li ponn ni kii ikpaakon ni na.
19N‑yoonn mubaa, bi ga li dɔ ki ye biwankpadam la,
le ki nan finn kan, bi ga kan ke baawankpal na buen a.
20Ijawaan sakpiin ga dan mala ke nwam na la;
le libuln ga nan daa bi kinyeek buen;
21liwipuul wɔb aabuln le ga ŋar bi ŋŋaan nyan baadichal ni;
22li ga daa bi pu, kaan li san bi kinimbaak,
le bi pɔɔni bibaa ke bi ŋmar.
23Libuln ga li wii yur bi le bi san, le ki joo libiil aapɔɔn faani bi.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
Nlan Aapak
1Baah gbii tikunabr ibuu i ponn ni na bi;
le baah toor nyani salmaa aajɔŋ nin chee na bi.
2Unibɔn gbii kitiŋ le nyani tikur,
le ki donni nyani tikumann ŋitakpal ni.
3Unibɔn fikr koo mbɔmbɔɔn sakpiin ni.
Bi koo kitiŋ taab taab ki lik, le ki gbii ban ŋitakpal mbɔmbɔɔn ni.
4Bi chaa nin chee daa aan ubaa aa koo nima na,
nin chee unibɔn aataal aa kee taa na,
Unibɔn gbii isan ŋitakpanyaan aabuu ni.
Nima chee le bi ti bi tun bibaa, ki chib joo iŋmin ibuu ni.
5Kitiŋ pu le tijikaar nyan,
le kitiŋ baan ngbaan aataab ye tikar ki wɔi lir.
6Kitiŋ aatakpal kpa ŋitakpanyaan, le kaatan mu kpa salmaa.
7Ukaa ubaa aa kani nsan mu cha ŋitakpanyaan aabuu ni na,
le nangba ubaa aa kee fii labr i pu.
8Uchinn, bee kipeewanbiik kibaa aa kee dii isakuun ngbaan.
9Unibɔn gbii ŋitakpapɔɔl, le ki gbii doo ŋijoo aataab.
10Baah lokr isan ŋitakpal ni na, le bi kani ŋitakpanyaan.
11Bi gbii ti nya ŋimɔɔyil, le ki nyani tiwan ni bɔr na mpaan pu.
12Tɔ, la chee aan aa ga ban kan nlan?
La chee aan ti ga bae ki bee tiwan aatataa?
13Saan ŋmaa kan nlan binib ni, ubaa aa nyi nlan aanyoor mbamɔm.
14Nnyusakpem aanyonyoon bui ke saan ŋmaa kan nlan nima.
15Saan ŋmaa di tikunabr ni salmaa daa mu.
16Mu aadaak jer salmaa u nyan chain na, ni ŋitakpanyaan aadaak.
17Bi ban mu jer salmaa, ki ban mu jer salmaa aasambil
bee salmaa aayikuuk.
18Nlan ŋan jer nleenyaan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ.
19Litakpanyaan li bi yin li ke topas na,
ni salmaa nyaan aan ŋmaa sil nlan chee.
20Kina pu na, nlan aah baa nin chee na bi la?
La chee aan ti ga bae ki bee tiwan aatataa?
21Tiwanfuurkaan nibaa aan ŋmaa kan mu,
hali unyoon u laani na aa waa mu.
22Hali nkun ni libiil len ke ni ŋun kakaan la.
23Uwumbɔr baanja le nyi nsan ngbaan,
uma le nyi nin chee aa ga ban kan nlan na,
24ba pu? uma le nyi kitiŋ aanaanmɔk,
ki waa tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi kitaapaak taab na.
25N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan tii libuln laapɔɔn,
ki siin nnyusakpem aawiwiir na;
26N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan nyan nin chee utaal ga nu,
ni isan i utaal aagbamgbam mu tar na ga dii na;
27N‑yoonn ngbaan le u nan kan nlan ki tɔŋ mu aanyaan,
le ki kii tii mu ke mu sil ŋan.
28Uwumbɔr nan bui unibɔn ke,
“Aa ga li san Uwumbɔr le ki nin kan nlan.
Aa ga fenn aapuwɔb tii titunwanbir le ki bee tiwan aatataa.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
Job aakookoo aabɔr ti u ŋeer na
1Job nan ki len:
Job
2Maamɔfal yaa ba ki bi ke n‑yoonn
mu Uwumbɔr nan joo mi na kan.
3Uwumbɔr nan bi m chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk n‑yaayoonn ngbaan,
le ki tii mi nwiihn m joo chuun libɔmbɔln ni.
4N‑yaayoonn ngbaan le m nan ye uwankpadaan na,
le Uwumbɔr aajɔtiik nan lik maadichal pu.
5Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan nan bi m chee n‑yaayoonn ngbaan,
le maabim mɔmɔk mann goln mi.
6Maanaa ni iŋoob nan kpa nnaabiin pam,
le maakpasɔi aasui nan muuni ŋitakpal ŋmeen aatiŋ pu.
7N‑yoonn mumɔk kitiŋ aaninkpiib ti kuun na kan,
m nan ka maabuul ni, bikaasisik ni.
8Binachipɔm yaa kan mi kan, see bi paar si n‑gbaan,
le bininkpiib fii sil ki tii mi lisil.
9Binib aasalolm ŋmin; 10hali binikpaam ŋmin chii.
11Unii umɔk nan kan mi, bee u ŋun m pu na kan,
u nan kpa lilambinyaan u len maah tun pu na pu.
12Bigiim yaa nan wii kan, m ter bi la;
m nan ter nkpobim bi kaa kpa unii u chee bi ga fenn buen na.
13Binib bi nan bi falaa kpaan ni na nan pak mi la,
le m ter bikpopiib le bi kan lifuur.
14M tun dii nsan le ki si chob.
15M nan ye ŋinimbil le ki tii bijoom,
le ki ye ŋitaa ki tii binib bi wɔb na.
16M nan bi ke te na le ki tii bigiim,
le ki si biwɔwɔm bi bi tibɔr ni na aapuwɔb.
17M nan kuln bibiindam aapɔɔn
le ki gaa baah muk binib bi na lii.
18M nan mak n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke m li kpa limɔfafɔfɔŋ
le ki nan kpo linampal, mpopiin ni.
19M nan bi ke busub bu aasubon kani nnyun n‑yoonn mɔmɔk
aan bu aapan soon limaln na.
20Unibɔn mɔmɔk nan pak mi la,
le m nan kpa mpɔɔn n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
21M yaa nan bi sur binib kan, binib nan ŋmin la,
le ki pel maah len pu na mbamɔm;
22le m yaa ti doo kan, baa kpa tibaa bi ki kpee.
Maabɔr nan koo ke ntaanyun mu too na aah koo kitiŋ pu na la;
23unii mɔk nan gaa ti iŋaal ilee
ke bikpaab aah gaal unaalantaal pu na.
24Buyoonn baa ti ki kpa lipobil na le m laa limɔmumukl ŋa bi;
le nnimbil wɔb aabimbin tii bi ntaakpab pɔɔn.
25Min le nan lolni nsan ki siini ni ga ŋa na;
m nan joo bi ke ubɔr aah joo waajab pu na la,
le ki tii bi mpopiin baasuugar ni.

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1Le maah kpeln binachipɔm bi na ka ŋani mi yaansara dandana.
Bitetiib aa nan bi tibaa ni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
le maa nan kii ke bi ni maabɔ kpaan ki kpaa maapiih.
2Bi nan ye binib bi kaa ki kpa mpɔɔn mubaa na la,
baa nan ki kpa mpɔɔn mubaa bi di tun lituln.
3Bi nan ye bigiim kaa kpa tijikaar,
le ki nyii isubonkuun kinyeek, limokpalunn libaa ni.
4Bi nan dar ŋɔi nteersakpiin ni aasufar ki ŋman ti,
bi nan kpaan ŋman tichachabɔnn.
5Unii mɔk nan joo tijar le jenni bi
ke baah tar binaayukb le pu na.
6Bi nan koo titakpalunn ni la,
bi nan koo ibuu i bi gbii ŋijoo aamɔgben na ni la.
7Bi nan bi timoor ni le ki tar ke ipeel na,
le ki gul doo isubi taab.
8Maabitibaanidam bi kaa kpa ŋiyimbil na,
bi nan jenn nyan bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu la.
9Tɔ, dandana le bi choo nan laa mi;
m gur ye yaansara aawan le bi chee.
10Bi lik seeni mi la; bi dak ke bi ŋan sakpen ki jer mi,
le ki kpaan choo nan tei timɔɔtan ŋani m pu.
11Uwumbɔr aah cha m diŋ kaa ki kpa mpɔɔn mubaa na,
le bi di liŋuusakpeln lir m pu.
12Liniwoln fii nan bib m pu la;
bi gor baakookoo aatakm la; le ki cha m chuun san.
13Bi kiir maah ga gɔnn nin chee na,
le ki pɔɔni bibaa ke bi kuln mi;
le ubaa aa bi ki ga nyii bi pu.
14Bi diir ŋibun ŋi bi ga kan na le ki koo ni
le ki san nan lir wɔi mi;
15Ijawaan le nyaŋ mi;
maayimbil buen ke litakpiln libaa aabuln na la,
le maawangol jer buen ke ntaalangbam na.
16Tɔ, m bi kpu le na; lifuur libaa aa bi maafalaa wee ni.
17Kinyeek kan, maakpab mɔmɔk wu la;
iween i ŋmɔ mi na aa door.
18Uwumbɔr chɔb chuu maabɔkul aaneen la,
le ki goŋ goŋ maawanpeenkaan.
19U di mi mee lii tikpakpar ni; titan soor mi.
20Uwumbɔr, m wii yin si, le saa gar mi kpala;
le m yaa ki mee si kan, aatafal aa bi m ni.
21Aa ŋani mi mbiin sakpen a; aa di saapɔɔn mɔmɔk le muk mi.
22Aa cha libuln daa mi buen a;
aa cha kitaabuŋ ki pɔɔ sakpen na le joo mi fiini.
23M nyi ke aa joo mi cha maakun ni la,
aa joo mi cha ndoon mu dɔ kii unii mɔmɔk na ni la.
24Ba ŋa aa tak unii u kuln kookoo
ki mee ban kinimbaak baanja na?
25Maa nan wii ter binib bi nan bi tibɔr ni na aa?
Nsui aa nan gar binib bi kaa nan kpa na pu uu?
26M nan mak ban mpopiin ni nwiihn la,
le tibɔbir ni mbɔmbɔɔn labr dan.
27Ilandak ni iween le daa par par mi;
Iwiin mɔmɔk kan, m kani falaa la.
28M chuun le ni bɔɔn mi, le nwindam aa choo kpala;
Kinipaak ni, le m si ki gaŋni ban nterm.
29Nneen bi suuna le kaa ki mɔ
ki naahn ikakal ni taataa aaneel.
30Nwon kpaln tibɔmbɔnn la; nwon ton kina kpan kpan.
31Nin chee m nan ŋun mpopiin aalahn pu na,
m gur ŋun ikpowiil ni iwiil pu la.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1M puu tipuukpaan le ke maan di lineel aanimbil lik
usapɔɔn daalbaadaal.
2Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ŋani timi ba?
U teeni unibɔn aatun kinye?
3U joo ni tibɔbir ni libiil le nan tii binib bi tun taani na.
4Uwumbɔr nyi maah tun pu na mɔmɔk;
u kani litaal limɔk m yoor na.
5M puu ke maa kee ŋa mbiin daalbaadaal,
kaa kee pɔɔn mbaa ke m ŋmann biken.
6Cha Uwumbɔr ŋaŋ mi tiwaŋaŋkaan bamɔnn ni,
ki kan maah kaa tun taani pu na.
7M yaa fenn mpuwɔb tii nsanyaan, bee m di mbaa tii kinimbɔŋ ki cha ŋŋaal meeh titunwanbir kan,
8cha maajikaar bii doo, bee aa cha biken ji tijikaar ti m bun na.
9Nlaasaab yaa koo ŋŋeen aatɔ aapuu ni,
ki yaa tam ki kii u waabisamɔb kan,
10cha mpuu ti mɔn uja yayan aasaa,
ki doon uja yayan aawandookaan pu.
11Nkun li ye kina aabiin aatafadaan.
12Ni ga li ye mmii sakpiin aabiil li ga di maawan
mɔmɔk wu na la.
13Maatutunn ubaa yaa nan len mi tibɔr kan,
m nan pel le ki ŋa u mbamɔm.
14M yaa kaa ba nan ŋa kina kan, m ba ga ŋa kinye
ki sil Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni?
Uwumbɔr yaa ba dan u nan ji mi tibɔr kan, m ba ga ŋa kinye?
15Uwumbɔr u naan mi na,
Uwumbɔr chachaan ngbaan le naan maatutum mu.
16Maa kee yii kaa ter bigiim;
kaa kee cha ukpopii dakl ke waa kpa uteter daalbaadaal,
17kaa ka ji tijikaar ki cha ukpobo chuun nkon.
18M joo bi maamɔfal mɔmɔk ni la.
19M yaa nan kan unii ban nterm,
ki kpa igiin sakpen kaa ŋmaa daa tiwanpeenkaan kan,
20m nan tii u baah di maapiih aakor luu tiwanpeenkaan ni na la.
Le u ga di usui mɔmɔk pak mi.
21M yaa nan jin ukpobo pem pem daalbaadaal
ki nyi ke m ga ti nya libɔjil ni kan,
22cha ŋŋaal kool kool; cha i par nya mbɔgbin pu.
23Maah san Uwumbɔr aatafadaan na,
maa nan ŋa kina aawan daalbaadaal.
24Maa kee tii liwankpal naadii, 25kaa kpa kigaak liwangol pu.
26Nwiin ni mu aawiin mɔmɔk pu, maa kee doon mu daalbaadaal,
kaa doon uŋmal ni waanyaan mɔmɔk pu.
27Ubaa aa kee ŋmann mi aan m nyuŋ ni
ki moor ŋŋaal ki pak ni.
28Kina aatunwanbir aatafadaan le ye nkun;
ti yiil Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan la.
29Maa kee kpa mpopiin maadim aafalaa ponn ni,
kaa mɔɔni buyoonn tibɔbir kan bi na.
30Maa kee bui Uwumbɔr ke u ku bi,
ki tun kina aatunwanbir daalbaadaal.
31Binib bi mɔmɔk tun maatuln na nyi
ke m gaal bicham n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la.
32M cha bisachum koo maadichal ni,
kaa kee cha bi doon kinyaŋ ponn ni lipaal.
33Binib biken pɔɔni bibaa ki joo baatunwanbir bɔrni la,
le mma aa kee bɔr maatunwanbir pu daalbaadaal.
34Maa kee san binib aah ga len pu na aanimɔɔn;
maa kee ka ŋmin, kaa kee bee kidiik ni, binib aalaar pu.
35Ubaa aan pel maah len pu na aa?
M puu ke libɔbil mɔk gbii la.
Cha Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan gar mi.
Maadim aah len mi tibɔr ti na yaa ba ŋmee dɔ
aan m waa ti kan,
36m ba ga di ti leen mbɔgbin pu ni limakl ŋmeen,
ki di ti chiŋ n‑yil pu ke kibɔryikpupuk na.
37M ba ga bui Uwumbɔr maah tun pu na mɔmɔk,
aan n‑yil li yaa unimbiin ni.
38M yaa nan sun kitiŋ ki m ko na, ki gaa ki ukpaakon daan chee,
39ki yaa jin tijikaar ti m ko nima chee na,
ki yaa cha bikpaab bi ko ki na ko nkon kan,
40cha njikaabim mu m bun nima na kpaln timoor ni ikokon.
Job aabɔr nan doo do la.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Elihu aah len pu na
(Job 32.1–37.24)
1Job aah nan tii naadii usui ni ke waah kpa taani na, bijab bitaa ngbaan aa nan ki kpa tibaa bi gar u. 2Tɔ, uja ubaa mu nan si nima, bi nan yin u ke Elihu. Elihu aaŋuul nan fii Job aah nan galni Uwumbɔr ki bui ke uma aabɔr le ŋan na pu. Elihu aate le nan ye Barakel u ye Bus aayaabil ki nyan ni Ram aataŋaal pu na. 3Waaŋuul nan ki fii Job aajɔtiib bitaa na mu pu. Baa nan ki nyi baah ga gar Job pu na, le ni naahn ke Uwumbɔr aabɔr le aa kaa ŋan na. 4Elihu le nan ye uwaatiir nima chee, kina pu na, u nan si ŋmin le unii mɔk ti len doo. 5Waah nan ti kan ke bijab bitaa ngbaan aa ki kpa tibaa bi gar Job na, le waaŋuul fii, 6le u piin ki len.
Elihu aah len pu na
M laa par, le nimi ma pɔɔk,
kina pu le ijawaan ba joo mi ke m tuk nimi maah dak pu na.
7M bui mbaa ke ni ŋan ke ni len,
ke nimi bininkpiib na di nimi aalan ki yakr tii tɔb.
8Tɔ, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan Aafuur Nyaan
le choo binib chee le ki tii bi nlan.
9Naa ye tipor le tii binib nlan,
le kaa ki ter bi ke bi bee tiwan ni tok na.
10Kina pu na, m ban ke ni pel m chee la;
cha m bui nimi maah dak pu na.
11M di limɔr le ki si buyoonn ni bi len na,
ki ŋmin suuna buyoonn ni bi ban nlan aabɔbil ni len na.
12M pel mbamɔm le ki ŋun naah nyaŋ nimi pu na;
naa ŋmaa kan tibɔr ti ni ga di len lii Job na.
13Ni ga ŋa kinye ki bui ke ni kan nlan?
Uwumbɔr le ga gar Job, ba pu? ni nyaŋ nimi a.
14Job ba len nimi le chee tibɔr, naa ye mi,
le maan giin u ngiin mu ni giin u na daalbaadaal.
15Job, baa kan ŋibɔbil bi di len; baa kpa ngarm ki ga tii si.
16Baah si ŋmin na, ni ŋan ke m li beenin si kii ii?
Bima le si na, kaa ki kpa tibaa bi len.
17Maan li si ŋmin, m ga tii mbaa aagarm dandana
ki bui si maah dak pu na.
18Ni ye mi kijejek le ke m len, maan ki ŋmaa chuu mbaa.
19M yaa kaa kan nsan m len kan,
m ga puu ke ndapɔm aatuun na la.
20Maan ki ŋman, m ga len la.
21Maan kpee ubaa pu kinikpakpak kee ponn ni;
maan di kimɔmɔɔn ŋa ubaa.
22Maa nyi kimɔmɔɔn.
M yaa ŋa kina kan, Uwumbɔr ga daa ntafal mala.

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1Tɔ, Job, li pel mbamɔm maah kpa timɔk m len na.
2M ga len maah joo pu na mɔmɔk.
3Maabɔbil mɔmɔk ye ibamɔn, le m len ibamɔn.
4Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan le naan mi ki tii mi limɔfal.
5Aa yaa ga ŋman kan, aa gar mi. Gor saanikpakpak.
6M ni sin ye tiwanbaan le Uwumbɔr chee,
tiyakr le u nan di ŋa ti mɔmɔk bilee.
7Kina na, saa kpa nsan ke aa li san mi; maan nyaŋ si.
8Tɔ, maah ŋun aa len tibɔr ti na sɔ:
9“Maabɔr aa bii; maa tun taani ubaa.
Maabɔr ŋan, le maa kpa titunwanbir.
10Le Uwumbɔr ban isan i u joo tak mi
ki ŋani mi ke udin na.
11U di tikululn le baa ntaa;
u lik maah yoor litaal limɔk na.”
12Job, le m ban m bui si ke taa gbii.
Uwumbɔr jer unibɔn mɔmɔk.
13Ba ŋa aa galni Uwumbɔr ke waa kee gar unii aabɔr?
14Tɔ, Uwumbɔr len le ki gir len,
ubaa mu aa pel waah len pu na.
15Binib yaa dɔ geen kinyeek kan,
le Uwumbɔr len tibɔr tidaŋ ni.
16U cha bi pel waah len pu na,
le ijawaan chuu bi waah sak bi pu na pu.
17Uwumbɔr len ke bi di cha titunwanbir aatum,
ki taa yoor kigaak.
18Waan cha bi kuln; u nyani bi nkun ni.
19Uwumbɔr joo iween le mɔk unii ni ŋan na,
le ki cha uwon mɔmɔk wu.
20Ubun aa neen tijikaar,
le tijikaar ti ŋan sakpen na ye u ipoween la.
21Le uwon donn ti doo; aa ga li waa waakpab mɔmɔk;
22le u gur bi ntekpiisan ni.
23Nibaakan Uwumbɔr aatuun ga dan nan ter u,
Nibaakan, Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib ŋichur ponn ni ubaa u teer
binib baatuln aah ye pu na le ga dan nan ter u.
24Linimbaasaln ni, le ntuun ngbaan ga bui ke, “Di u lii, naa ye ke u buen bitekpiib aatiŋ ni.
Saah ga di u lii pu na aapar sɔ.”
25Le uwon ga ki pɔnn ki pɔɔk;
26le u yaa mee limeel kan, Uwumbɔr ga kii waameel;
le u di mpopiin doon Uwumbɔr;
le Uwumbɔr ga ki gir ŋa waawan mbamɔm tii u.
27Le u ga sil binib ni ki len ke, “M tun titunwanbir.
Maa tun ni ŋan na, le Uwumbɔr tee di cha pinn mi.
28Waa cha m buen bitekpiib aatiŋ ni, le m beenin fu.”
29Uwumbɔr ŋani nimina n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
30u gaal unii aamɔfal lir, le ki tii u limɔfal aamɔɔn.
31Tɔ, Job, li pel maah bi len pu na; li ŋmin aan ki cha m len.
32Tɔ, aa yaa tee kpa tibaa aa len kan, cha m ŋun ti;
le aa yaa kpa mbamɔn kan, m ga kii ni mpopiin ke saabɔr ŋan.
33Naa ye kina kan, li ŋmin ki pel m chee,
le m mɔk si saah ga ŋa pu ki kan nlan na.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1-2Nimi bijab bimina kpa nlan, ni kpa nlan sakpen a;
li pel man maah bi len pu na.
3Aa yaa lak tijiir ti mɔ na lik kan, aa beer ti,
aa yaa ŋun nlan aamɔbon ma kan, saa beer ŋi.
4Ni ye timi aatuln le ke ti lik tibɔr ngbaan ni.
5Job bui ke waa kpa taani,
ke Uwumbɔr le yii kaa tii u waabamɔn.
6U baa le ke, “M ga ŋa kinye ki gii nnyamɔn,
ki bui ke m tun taani?
Maa tun titunwanbir, le ki mu tee kan iweenkpaan.”
7Ni kee kan Job aaboln aa?
Waa kee pak Uwumbɔr daalbaadaal.
8U gee bibiindam aabɔr le ki chuun diir titunwanbirdam.
9U len le ke aa yaa pɔɔni aabaa ke aa dii Uwumbɔr aageehn kan,
naa kpa tinyoor tibaa.
10Nimi binib bi kpa ŋuntii na, li pel m chee man.
Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga ŋmaa ŋa tiwan ni kaa ŋan na aa?
11U pa binib baah tun pu na pu, le ki ŋani bi tiwan ni ŋeer bi na.
12Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aa tun titunwanbir;
waa ŋani ubaa beebee aatuln.
13Uwumbɔr kan waapɔɔn ŋma chee? Ŋma di u ŋa dulnyaa aayidaan?
14Uwumbɔr yaa chuu gaa limɔfal aafuurk kan,
15unii u mɔmɔk kpa limɔfal na ba ga kpo le ki ki gir kpaln titan.
16Aa yaa kpa nlan kan, pel m chee.
17Uwumbɔr mbimbinyaan daan le aa bui ke waabɔr aa ŋan aa?
Aa dak ke waa gee ibamɔn aa?
18Bibɔrb ni bijojoob yaa kaa bi tibaa ni,
bee bi yaa kpa mbiin kan, Uwumbɔr bii baabɔr.
19Waa len tibɔr kpae bijojoob pu
kaa ter uwankpadaan ki cha ugiin,
ba pu? uma le naan unii mɔmɔk.
20Unii ga ŋmaa kpo kinyeek naa sɔk ntan.
Uwumbɔr gbaa binib bilni le bi kpoi;
waa joo mpɔɔn le ku binikpaam.
21U lik binib aah yoor litaal limɔk na.
22Mbɔmbɔɔn mubaa aa bi ki bɔɔn sakpen
ki ga ŋmaa bɔr titunwanbirdaan Uwumbɔr chee.
23Uwumbɔr aa ga li ban ke u siin n‑yoonn mu binib ga buen
u chee libɔjil na.
24Waan li ban ke u fiir lik bisalolm aabɔr waahr
aan ki nyan bi ki di biken kaan baabuu ni.
25Waah nyi baah tun pu na, u nyani bi le ki doo bi kinyeek.
26Binib aanimbil ni le u dar titunwanbirdam aatafal,
27ba pu? bi yii, kaa ki dii u ki suln waakaal mɔmɔk.
28Baabiin cha bigiim wii mpɔɔn yin Uwumbɔr,
le u ŋun baaterm aayim ngbaan.
29Uwumbɔr yaa yii ke waan ŋa nibaa kan,
ubaa aan ŋmaa galn u.
U yaa di ubaa bɔr kan, binib aan ki li kpa nterm.
30Ŋitimbol aan ki ŋmaa ŋa nibaa
aan bibiindam bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na taa joo bi.
31Job, aa kpiir saatunwanbir tuk Uwumbɔr
ki puu ke saan ki tun titunwanbir aa?
32Aa baa Uwumbɔr ke u mɔk si saataani,
ki kii ke aa ga di cha titunwanbir aa?
33Saah kaa kii tii Uwumbɔr aah ŋani pu na na,
aa dak ke u ga ŋa saah ban pu na aa?
Timina ye sin yaar la, naa ye min yaar;
bui timi saah dak pu na.
34Ulandaan mɔk ga sil kii mala;
unii umɔk kpa nlan na yaa ŋun maah len pu na kan,
35u ga bui ke Job aa nyi le ki gbaa,
ki bui ke waabɔr tibaa aa kpa tataa.
36Dakl lik Job aah len pu na mɔmɔk ni;
aa ga kan ke u len tibɔr ke utunwanbirdaan na la.
37U joo limɔyiir le kpae titunwanbir pu;
le ki ŋani Uwumbɔr mbɔnyun ti mɔmɔk aanimbil ni.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1-2Job, saa kpa nsan ke aa len Uwumbɔr chee ke saabɔr ŋan,
3bee aa baa Uwumbɔr ke, “Maatunwanbir muk si kinye?
Maah kaa tun titunwanbir na, m kan ba aanyoor?”
4M ban m giin aa ni aajɔtiib mɔk la.
5Lik kitaapaak. Lik ntaalangbam chee aah daa pu na.
6Aa yaa tun titunwanbir kan, naa ŋani Uwumbɔr nibaa.
Aa yaa tun taani ki ti saa pu na kan, taan ŋa u nibaa.
7Saabimbinyaan tii u ba aaterm?
Uwumbɔr aa ban nibaa aa chee.
8Aanibɔn ŋeen aatɔ le ji falaa saatunwanbir pu,
le ki ki kani nterm saaŋann pu.
9Binib yaa ji falaa kan, bi du la; le ki wii ban ke ubaa gaa bi lii,
10kaa tee cha Uwumbɔr u naan bi
ki cha bi gaa ilahn kinyeek na chee.
11Baa cha Uwumbɔr u cha ti kpa nlan ki jer tiwakor
ni inyoon na chee.
12Bi wii ban nterm, baagaak ni titunwanbir pu,
le Uwumbɔr aan gar bi.
13Baawiil ye fam la; Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aa waa bi
le kaa kpaan ŋun bi pu.
14Job, aa bui ke saa waa Uwumbɔr;
tɔ, ji limɔr, saabɔr bi u chee.
15Aa dak ke Uwumbɔr aa dar binib aatafal,
ke utafal bi titunwanbir ni siib kina la.
16Saah len pu na ye fam la;
ni ye mbamɔn ke saa nyi saah len pu na.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1-2Ji limɔr ki pel maah kpa pu m len
tii Uwumbɔr na siib kpee.
3Maalan nyaŋ a; m ga di maah nyi pu na le ki mɔk ke
Uwumbɔr u naan mi na ye ubamɔndaan la.
4Maah len pu aa chee na mɔk gbii la;
ulandaan le aa waa u si aa chee na.
5Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ a. Waa lik seeni ubaa;
tiwan nibaa aa bi aan waa nyi naatataa.
6Waa cha titunwanbirdam kpa limɔfafɔfɔŋ,
le ki ŋani bigiim mbamɔm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
7U kii binib bi aabimbin ŋan na;
u tii bi nsan le bi joo binib ke bibɔrb na
ki cha bi nyuŋni bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
8Binib yaa bi tikululn ni, ki ji baatuln aafalaa kan,
9Uwumbɔr mɔk bi baatunwanbir ni baagaak la.
10U cha bi ŋun waah sak bi pu na ke ni cha bi yii titunwanbir.
11Bi yaa kii tii Uwumbɔr ki dii u kan,
bi bi nsuudoon, ni nkam ni, le ki yunn ti chaar jer.
12Tɔ, bi yaa yii kan, le bi ga kpo maanyi ni,
le ki koo kitekpiitiŋ ni.
13Binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na aaŋuul fiir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
hali bi yaa kan ntafadaan kan,
baa mee Uwumbɔr ki ban nterm.
14Bi laa pɔɔn le ki kpo, inimɔɔn le ŋman ku bi.
15Le Uwumbɔr joo falaa mɔk binib ichiin,
le ki joo nsuubiin wolni binimbil.
16Uwumbɔr nyan si tibɔr ni, le ki cha aa bi ŋŋmarm ni;
u tii si tijikaar sakpen.
17Tɔ, dandana wee le aa kan ntafadaan mu ŋeer si na.
18Li nyi ki taa cha igaŋgaŋlik ŋmann si,
ki taa cha liwankpal di si yenn.
19Aa yaa wii ban nterm kan, naan li kpa si tinyoor tibaa;
saapɔɔn mɔmɔk aan ŋmaa ter si n‑yoonn mue.
20Taa li wii ban ke kinyeek fuu ni,
n‑yoonn mu ŋitimbol ga kuln na.
21Li nyi ki taa gir buen kinimbɔŋ aapepel;
saafalaa dan ke u nyan si nima chee la.
22Teer Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn aah nyaŋ pu na;
uma le ye umɔmɔkr kpaan ki jer bimɔmɔkb mɔmɔk.
23Ubaa aan ŋmaa bui Uwumbɔr waah ga ŋa pu na,
kaan ŋmaa galn u ke u tun titunwanbir.
24U kani kipak waatun mɔmɔk ni, n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la;
ni ye saatuln le ke aa mu pak u.
25Unibɔn mɔk kan waah tun pu na;
le ti tee ga li si dandar le ki lik.
26Taan ŋmaa bee waapɔɔn aah ti nyaŋ pu na,
kaan ŋmaa kahn waabin aah ye pu na.
27Uwumbɔr le nyani nnyun kitiŋ ni
le ki di mu kpaln ntaanyun.
28U cha utaal bar nya ntaalangbam ni
ki nu tii unibɔn mɔmɔk.
29Ubaa aa nyi ntaalangbam ngbaan aah chuun pu na,
kaa nyi utaal aah tar pu ki diir kitaapaak,
Uwumbɔr aah koo nin chee na.
30U cha utaal moor kitaapaak mɔmɔk ni,
le nnyusakpem aataab ma bɔɔn le kaa woln kpala.
31Kina le u joo binib le ki tii bi tijikaar ki ti nyaŋ.
32U di uŋaal le chuu ntaamii
le ki cha mu buen waah mɔk nin chee na.
33Utaal aah gbin pu na le mɔk ke kitaabuŋ choo,
le tiwakor nyi ke ki choo.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1Kitaabuŋ cha mpobil gbaa lib lib.
2Ni mɔmɔk li pel man Uwumbɔr aaneel,
li pel man utaal aah gbin ki nyani umɔb ni pu na.
3U cha utaal moor ki puur kitaapaak
ki nya kitiŋ lipepel libaa ki ti saa liken.
4Le uneel aah ŋuuni pu na nya,
ke utaal aah gbenni pu na aapɔɔnsakpiin,
le n‑yoonn ngbaan mɔmɔk na, mmii moor lak lak.
5Uwumbɔr aamɔboln pu le iwaan aawan ŋani,
lijinjiir aawan ni taan ŋmaa bee naatataa na ŋani.
6U cha ŋitaatakpal lir ni kitiŋ pu, ki cha utaal nu sakpen a.
7U chur unibɔn aatuln siini;
u mɔk bi waah ga ŋmaa tun pu na la.
8Ipeel chaa yaakookoo yaan ni la.
9Titaabunn aabuln nyani ŋŋangii wɔb,
le libusɔsoon li koo ikpab ni na nyani ŋŋangan wɔb.
10Uwumbɔr aafuurk cha nnyun kpaln ŋitaanal,
ki cha ŋi pɔɔk ke litakpal na.
11Utaal moor lak lak ntaalangbam ni,
12ki dii Uwumbɔr aageehn la.
Mu ŋani Uwumbɔr aah bui mu pu na ŋipepel mɔmɔk
dulnyaa wee ni.
13Uwumbɔr tuni utaal le u nan sɔŋni kitiŋ,
u ga ŋmaa di u daa unibɔn aatafal,
ki ga ŋmaa di u mɔk bi waaŋann.
14Job, sil siib, ki pel;
dakl lik lijinjiir aawan ni Uwumbɔr ŋani na.
15Aa nyi Uwumbɔr aah tii waamɔboln pu
ki cha utaal moor lak lak ntaalangbam ni na aa?
16Aa nyi ntaalangbam aah ŋa pu ki dee kitaapaak na aa?
Ni ye Uwumbɔr u nyi tiwan mɔmɔk na aawaan aatuln la.
17Ŋŋangii wɔb aabuln yaa muk kitiŋ le kan,
aa ga ji ntoton aafalaa.
18Aa ga ŋmaa ter Uwumbɔr aan u daa taln kitaapaak
ki cha ki li pɔɔ ke tikur ti joon kpal kpal na aa?
19Mɔk timi taah ga len Uwumbɔr chee pu na.
Nibaa aa bi tiyil ponn ni; taa nyi taah ga len pu na.
20Maan mee nsan ke m ni Uwumbɔr len tɔb chee tibɔr;
maan tii u nsan ke u kuln mi.
21Tɔ, dandana wee, le nwiihn mu bi kitaapaak na deer ŋinimbil,
mu wiin ki jer taah ga ŋmaa lik pu na;
le libuln ŋar kitaapaak woln chain.
22Nwiihn mu naahn salmaa na bi ŋŋangan wɔb,
le Uwumbɔr aapak chuu timi ijawaan.
23Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ sakpen, le taan ŋmaa duun ni u;
u kpa mbimbinyaan ki bi chob unibɔn chee.
24Kina pu na, naa kpa iwaan ke unii mɔmɔk san u ijawaan,
kina pu na, utafal aa bi binib bi bui ke bi kpa nlan na ni.

english_text:
The Lord Speaks
From Out of a Storm
1From out of a storm,
the Lord said to Job:
2Why do you talk so much
when you know so little?
3Now get ready to face me!
Can you answer
the questions I ask?
4How did I lay the foundation
for the earth?
Were you there?
5Doubtless you know who decided
its length and width.
6What supports the foundation?
Who placed the cornerstone,
7 while morning stars sang,
and angels rejoiced?
8 When the ocean was born,
I set its boundaries
9and wrapped it in blankets
of thickest fog.
10Then I built a wall around it,
locked the gates, 11and said,
“Your powerful waves stop here!
They can go no farther.”
Did You Ever Tell the Sun To Rise?
12Did you ever tell the sun to rise?
And did it obey?
13Did it take hold of the earth
and shake out the wicked
like dust from a rug?
14Early dawn outlines the hills
like stitches on clothing
or sketches on clay.
15But its light is too much
for those who are evil,
and their power is broken.
16Job, have you ever walked
on the ocean floor?
17Have you seen the gate
to the world of the dead?
18And how large is the earth?
Tell me, if you know!
19Where is the home of light,
and where does darkness live?
20Can you lead them home?
21I'm certain you must be able to,
since you were already born
when I created everything.
22Have you been to the places
where I keep snow and hail,
23until I use them to punish
and conquer nations?
24From where does lightning leap,
or the east wind blow?
25Who carves out a path
for thunderstorms?
Who sends torrents of rain
26on empty deserts
where no one lives?
27Rain that changes barren land
to meadows green with grass.
28Who is the father of the dew
and of the rain?
29Who gives birth to the sleet
and the frost
30that fall in winter,
when streams and lakes
freeze solid as a rock?
Can You Arrange Stars?
31 Can you arrange stars in groups
such as Orion
and the Pleiades?
32Do you control the stars
or set in place the Big Dipper
and the Little Dipper?
33Do you know the laws
that govern the heavens,
and can you make them rule
the earth?
34Can you order the clouds
to send a downpour,
35or will lightning flash
at your command?
36Did you teach birds to know
that rain or floods
are on their way?
37Can you count the clouds
or pour out their water
38on the dry, lumpy soil?
39When lions are hungry,
do you help them hunt?
40Do you send an animal
into their den?
41And when starving young ravens
cry out to me for food,
do you satisfy their hunger?
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah gar Job pu na
1Le Uwumbɔr aaneel nyan ni kitaabuŋ ni ki len Job chee tibɔr.
Uwumbɔr aah len pu na
2Aa mu ye ŋma ke aa di maanyi ni bɔfam tɔŋ maalan?
3Fii sil ke uja na ki giin maabaan mu m baa si na.
4Maah nan naan dulnyaa na, aa nan bi ii?
Aa yaa nyi sakpen kan, bui mi ti ponn ni.
5Ŋma nan siin waah ga li wiir pu na?
Ŋma nan di tiwaŋaŋkaan taln ti saa umɔk?
Aa nyi ngarm ngbaan mɔmɔk aa?
6Ba joo jaatɔlk tiib bi tik kitiŋ na?
Ŋma nan di dulnyaa aagolɔŋ ni aatakpal na baan?
7Liyaadaal ngbaan aachakpitaawoln
iŋmabi nan kpaan ki gaa ilahn,
le Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib tar mpɔɔn pu ni mpopiin.
8Nnyusakpem aah nan puu nyan ni kitiŋ aapuul ni na,
ŋma nan di ibisamɔi piin kiir mu?
9Min le nan di ntaalangbam biin nnyusakpem pu
ki di mu ŋa mbɔmbɔɔn ni.
10M nan daan nnyusakpem aanaanmɔk
ki di mu siin ibisamɔi i laŋ na aapuwɔb.
11M nan bui mu ke, “Sil nima ki taa ki foor.
Do le saanyunkpenn ti pɔɔ sakpen na ga sil.”
12Job, saamɔfal mɔmɔk ni,
aa kee bui kitaak kibaa ke ki woln aa?
13Aa kee bui kitaak ke ki chɔb chuu kitiŋ ki dam ki,
aan bibiindam nya ni baah bɔr nin chee na aa?
14Nwiin pu aawiihn le cha ŋigongon ni tifatann kpiir ni,
ki naahn tiwanpeenkaan aah tul tul pu na,
ki waa chain ke salmaa le aah tab tiyakr pu na.
15Nwiin pu aawiihn wiin sakpen bibiindam chee
ki cha baa ŋmaa tun mbiin aatun.
16Aa kee buen nnyusakpem taab aayayak aanyunbun na chee ee?
Aa kee chuun nnyusakpem taab aatiŋ pu uu?
17Ubaa kee mɔk si ibisamɔi i kiir kitekpiitiŋ ki bɔɔn na aa?
18Aa nyi dulnyaa aawiwiir aah ye pu na aa?
Aa yaa nyi kan, gar mi.
19Aa nyi nwiin aah nya ni nin chee na,
bee mbɔmbɔɔn aah nya ni nin chee na aa?
20Aa ga ŋmaa mɔk ni naah ga chuun ti saa nimɔk na,
bee aa ga ŋmaa giin ni ni la?
21M kpa limakl ke aa ga ŋman, ba pu? aa por sakpen
ki nan bi buyoonn dulnyaa nan naan na.
22Aa kee buen tidir ti ponn ni m siini
ŋitaanal ni itaapiin na chee ee?
23M siin ni ŋi kiir tibɔr yoonn la,
ŋi si kii butɔb ni kijaak aawiin la.
24Aa kee buen nwiin aah puur ni nin chee na
bee aa kee buen liwipuul aabuln aah nya ni nin chee na aa?
25Ŋma nan gbii nnyunsan tii utaal u bar kpir ni na?
Ŋma nan naan nsan tii utaal aah gbin kitaabuŋ ki ponn ni na?
26Ŋma cha utaal nu binib aah kaa koo nin chee na?
27Ŋma tii kitiŋ ki kuur aan nnyunyuu mu joo ki na nnyun
ki cha timoor punn?
28Utaal bee limaln kpa te ee?
29-30Ŋitaatakpal ni likpakpal, ni cha nnyun kpaln litakpal
ki cha nnyusakpem aapaacham pɔɔk na aana ye ŋma?
31Aa ga ŋmaa buu kiŋmabipaak kpaan tɔb ni ii?
bee aa ga ŋmaa sɔkr tiwan ni joo uŋmadar na lii la aa?
32Aa ga ŋmaa mɔk iŋmabi n‑yoonn mubaa ki ti saa muken aa?
ki ga ŋmaa mɔk iŋmabi i bi yin i ke Upeel sakpiin na ni yaabim nsan aa?
33Aa nyi ikaal i joo kitaapaak na aa?
Aa ga ŋmaa di ikaal ngbaan joo kitiŋ aa?
34Aa ga ŋmaa teen tuk ntaalangbam
ki cha mu cha utaal bar nnyun aa?
35Le aa yaa bui ntaamii ke mu li moor lak lak kan,
mu ga dan aa chee ki nan bui si ke mu ga tun saatuln aa?
36Ŋma tuk Nail aamɔɔl aanyoon na ke Nail ga nya nwam,
bee ŋma tuk ukooja ke utaal ga nu?
37Ŋma kpa nlan sakpen ki ga ŋmaa kahn ntaalangbam,
ki ga ŋmaa gbuun mu aan utaal bar nnyun kpir,
38aan kitangbaak ŋmaan ki pɔɔk?
39Aa ban tijikaar tii ichinn ke i ji, ki cha ichinn aabim ji babr
40buyoonn i dɔ bɔr yaatakpaluŋ ni,
bee buyoonn i dɔ yaadɔdooyaan ki kii na aa?
41Ŋma kpiini ikaabɔn buyoonn i bi kpak aan nkon joo i,
aan yaabim wii ban tijikaar m chee na?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
When Do Mountain Goats Give Birth?
1When do mountain goats
and deer give birth?
Have you been there
when their young are born?
* 2How long are they pregnant
3before they deliver?
4Soon their young grow strong
and then leave
to be on their own.
5Who set wild donkeys free?
6I alone help them survive
in salty desert sand.
7They stay far from crowded cities
and refuse to be tamed.
8Instead, they roam the hills,
searching for pastureland.
9Would a wild ox agree
to live in your barn
and labor for you?
10Could you force him to plow
or to drag a heavy log
to smooth out the soil?
11Can you depend on him
to use his great strength
and do your heavy work?
12Can you trust him
to harvest your grain
or take it to your barn
from the threshing place?
An Ostrich Proudly Flaps Her Wings
13An ostrich proudly
flaps her wings,
but not because
she loves her young.
14She abandons her eggs
and lets the dusty ground
keep them warm.
15And she doesn't seem to worry
that the feet of an animal
could crush them all.
16She treats her eggs as though
they were not her own,
unconcerned that her work
might be for nothing.
17I myself made her foolish
and without common sense.
18But once she starts running,
she laughs at a rider
on the fastest horse.
Did You Give Horses Their Strength?
19Did you give horses their strength
and the flowing hair
along their necks?
20Did you make them able
to jump like grasshoppers
or to frighten people
with their snorting?
21Before horses are ridden
into battle,
they paw at the ground,
proud of their strength.
22Laughing at fear, they rush
toward the fighting,
23while the weapons of their riders
rattle and flash in the sun.
24Unable to stand still,
they gallop eagerly into battle
when trumpets blast.
25Stirred by the distant smells
and sounds of war, they snort
in reply to the trumpet.
26Did you teach hawks to fly south
for the winter?
* 27Did you train eagles to build
28their nests on rocky cliffs,
29where they can look down
to spot their next meal?
30 Then their young gather to feast
wherever the victim lies.
translation_text:
1Aa nyi buyoonn ŋijoo paab aaŋoob maa na aa?
Aa kee kan upeeman aah bi maa pu na aa?
2Aa nyi yaapuu aah yunni pu aan i ti maa na aa?
Aa nyi n‑yoonn mu i ga maa na aa?
3Aa nyi buyoonn i ga doon
aan ki nuu yaabim lii dulnyaa ni na aa?
4Timoor ni le yaabim ŋani mpɔɔn, le ki siir kaan ki gir ni.
5Ŋma tii timoor ni aabon lifuur?
Ŋma nyani i lir ki cha i kpak?
6Min le di nteersakpiin tii i ke mu li ye ido,
le ki cha i koo n‑yaan aapaan ni.
7Yaa duuni ntim mu kpa kifuuk sakpen na chee,
le ubaa aan ŋmaa tiŋ i ki cha i tun lituln.
8Ŋijoo pu le ye yaah ŋmɔ timoor nin chee na,
nima chee le i lik ban tiwasɔnn mɔmɔk i ŋmɔ.
9Umonaa ga tun lituln tii si ii?
U ga li gee ke u sil saanaakook ni kinyeek aa?
10Aa ga ŋmaa di ŋŋmin leen ubaa ki cha u ko tii si ii?
Bee aa ga ŋmaa cha u kpar saasikpel tii si ii?
11Aa ga ŋmaa li mak waapɔɔnsakpiin pu
ki dakl ke u tun lituln li pɔɔ na tii si ii?
12Aa dak ke u ga ŋmaa kuun saah chee tijikaar ti na
ki faar njikaabim ŋipaa pu uu?
13Taataa aafeen gbaa mala mala pam.
Taataa ubaa mu aan ŋmaa fii ke uneepɔɔn na.
14Taataa too waajen bilni kitiŋ le ke titan aatoton cha
ŋi li ton.
15Waa nyi ke unii aataa ŋmaa taar wiil ŋi,
kaa nyi ke upeel ubaa ga ŋmaa wii ŋi.
16U ŋani ke ŋijen ngbaan aah kaa ye uyaan le na,
le utafal aa bi ŋi ni ke waatuln bee yooli.
17Min le ŋa u ujɔr kaa tii u nlan.
18Tɔ, u yaa piin litaasaln kan,
u ga ŋmaa laa utaan ni unii u jak u na mɔk.
19Job, sin le nan cha itaan kpa mpɔɔn sakpen
ki tii i itangbar i fɔk na aa?
20Sin le cha i yuk ke itoon na
ki joo yaah fɔi pu na faani binib aa?
21I kur kitangbaak kifataŋ ni,
i joo yaapɔɔn mɔmɔk le ber ti koo butɔb ni.
22Yaa nyi ijawaan aah ye pu na,
le kijaak aajuk aan ŋmaa cha i fenn ipuwɔb.
23Bijab bi jak i na aah joo tijawan ni na weeni
le ki moor nwiin ni lak lak.
24Itaan ngbaan aasui piir le iwon gbaa kpab kpab, le i tur cha.
Ukpiin yaa wii kan, yaa ki ŋmaa chuu ibaa.
25Ukpiin yaa wii nfum mubaa kan, le i fɔi,
i ŋun butɔb aanunun waahr le ki nin duun bu,
le ki ŋun bijab aaninkpiib aah len baajab chee pu na.
26Ukaa yaa taln ufeen toŋ ŋŋangii wɔb kan,
sin chee le u bae waah ga fii pu na aa?
27Likaagiil ga kiir si ke aa ti bui li
aan li nin ter laadil ŋijoo aapaacham aa?
28Li ŋani laadil ŋitakpafɔfɔk pu,
le ki cha ŋijoomɔgben na ye nin chee li ga kan ŋŋmarm na.
29Nima chee le li lik kɔnkɔni, ni dandar
ke li kan nibaa ki chuu ki ji.
30Ŋikaagii kuuni gonni liwankpol la,
le ŋaabim nyu liwankpol ngbaan aasin.

english_text:
The Lord Continues
I Am the Lord All-Powerful
* 1I am the Lord All-Powerful,
2but you have argued
that I am wrong.
Now you must answer me.
3Job said to the Lord:
4Who am I to answer you?
5I did speak once or twice,
but never again.
6Then out of the storm
the Lord said to Job:
7Face me and answer
the questions I ask!
8Are you trying to prove
that you are innocent
by accusing me of injustice?
9Do you have a powerful arm
and a thundering voice
that compare with mine?
10If so, then surround yourself
with glory and majesty.
* 11Show your furious anger!
Throw down and crush
12all who are proud and evil.
13Wrap them in grave clothes
and bury them together
in the dusty soil.
14Do this, and I will agree
that you have won
this argument.
I Created You
15I created both you
and the hippopotamus.
It eats only grass like an ox,
16but look at the mighty muscles
in its body 17and legs.
Its tail is like a cedar tree,
and its thighs are thick.
18The bones in its legs
are like bronze or iron.
19I made it more powerful
than any other creature,
yet I am stronger still.
20Undisturbed, it eats grass
while the other animals
play nearby.
* 21It rests in the shade of trees
along the riverbank
22or hides among reeds
in the swamp.
23It remains calm and unafraid
with the Jordan River rushing
and splashing in its face.
24There is no way to capture
a hippopotamus—
not even by hooking its nose
or blinding its eyes.
translation_text:
1-2Job, aa kpak Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan;
aa ga di cha le aan aa ga gar la?
Job aah gar pu na
3-4Uwumbɔr, m len kijɔrk aaliin la. M ga gar ke ba?
Maan ki pɔɔn mbaa ke m ki len tibaa kpee.
5M puun len jer maah ba ga len pu na a.
6Le Uwumbɔr ki len Job chee kitaabuŋ ni.
Uwumbɔr aah ki len pu na
7Fii sil ke uja na, ki gar maabaan.
8Aa ban ke aa mɔk ke maa bi chob,
ki bui ke maabɔr bii le aa ma yaar ŋan aa?
9Aa kpa mpɔɔn ke min na aa?
Aaneel ga li ŋmaa pɔɔ ke min yaan na aa?
10Ni yaa ye kina kan, di saanyuŋ ni limakl fii sil;
di mpɔɔn ni kipak biin aabaa pu.
11Lik binib bi kpa kigaak na; nyan saaŋuul ki sunn bi taab.
12Mbamɔn, lik bi, ki sunn ni bi taab;
doo bibiindam baah si nin chee na.
13Di bi mɔmɔk sub kitiŋ; baa bi kaan kitekpiitiŋ ni.
14Le m ga li ye u ga puen pak si
ki kii ke aabaa pu le aa nyaŋ na.
15Lik kipeewanbiik umɔɔpeel; min le naan u, ki naan aa mu,
u ŋmɔ timoor ke unaa na la.
16Tɔ, lik mpɔɔn mu bi uwon ni na,
ki lik mpɔɔn mu bi waagiin ni na.
17Waajuul si paacham ke santina aasub na la,
le ŋigir ŋi bi utaa ni na pɔɔ.
18Waakpab pɔɔ ke tikumann na la, le utaa bi ke ikudɔ na.
19Uma le ye iwaan aawan maawanfuurkaan mɔmɔk ni.
Min u naan u na baanja le ga ŋmaa nyaŋ u.
20Timoor ti ga kpiin u na muuni ŋigongon paab
nin chee ipeel gbiir na la.
21U doo ikokon taab la, le ki bɔrni timɔɔmoor ni, kipuuk ni.
22Ikokon ni tipugar ti si nkpen chee na
le tii u nkookoo yaan yaaboon ni.
23Waa san limɔɔl aanyunja ijawaan;
Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl aanyun yaa peei unimbil wɔb kan,
u ŋmin suuna la.
24Ŋma ga ŋmaa ŋum unimbil ki chuu u?
Ŋma ga ŋmaa pen gaawɔb chuu umɔfal?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
Can You Catch a Sea Monster?
1 Can you catch a sea monster
by using a fishhook?
Can you tie its mouth shut
with a rope?
2Can it be led around
by a ring in its nose
or a hook in its jaw?
3Will it beg for mercy?
4Will it surrender
as a slave for life?
5Can it be tied by the leg
like a pet bird
for little girls?
6Is it ever chopped up
and its pieces bargained for
in the fish-market?
7Can it be killed
with harpoons or spears?
8Wrestle it just once—
that will be the end.
9Merely a glimpse of this monster
makes all courage melt.
10And if it is too fierce
for anyone to attack,
who would dare oppose me?
11I am in command of the world
and in debt to no one.
12What powerful legs,
what a stout body
this monster possesses!
13Who could strip off its armor
or bring it under control
with a harness?
14Who would try to open its jaws,
full of fearsome teeth?
* 15Its back is covered
with shield after shield,
16firmly bound and closer together
17than breath to breath.
When This Monster Sneezes
18When this monster sneezes,
lightning flashes, and its eyes
glow like the dawn.
19Sparks and fiery flames
explode from its mouth.
20And smoke spews from its nose
like steam
from a boiling pot,
21while its blazing breath
scorches everything in sight.
22Its neck is so tremendous
that everyone trembles,
23the weakest parts of its body
are harder than iron,
24and its heart is stone.
25When this noisy monster appears,
even the most powerful
turn and run in fear.
26No sword or spear can harm it,
27and weapons of bronze or iron
are as useless as straw
or rotten wood.
28Rocks thrown from a sling
cause it no more harm
than husks of grain.
This monster fears no arrows,
29it simply smiles at spears,
and striking it with a stick
is like slapping it with straw.
30As it crawls through the mud,
its sharp and spiny hide
tears the ground apart.
31And when it swims down deep,
the sea starts churning
like boiling oil,
32and it leaves behind a trail
of shining white foam.
33No other creature on earth
is so fearless.
34It is king of all proud creatures,
and it looks upon the others
as nothing.
translation_text:
1Aa ga ŋmaa di njapiin chuu unyiib,
bee aa ga di ŋŋmin gbin ulambil aa?
2Aa ga ŋmaa di ŋŋmin ŋa umɔfal ni,
bee aa di njapiin lɔk ulakpak ni ii?
3U ga gaŋ si ke aa di u lii ii?
U ga gaŋ si ke aa san u kinimbaak aa?
4U ga puu tipuur tii si ki kii ke u ga li tun tii si
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na aa?
5Aa ga ŋmaa baa u ke unyoon u aa kpiini u na aa?
Aa ga ŋmaa baa u ke tiwan ni saanaagbiipiibim ga li gbiir na aa?
6Bijanbam ga kpak waadaak pu uu?
Binib bi tiir kitiirk na ga chɔi waanann ke bi ti tiir aa?
7Aa ga ŋmaa di ijan aakpaatunn too baan waagbaŋ
bee aa di kina aagbalk too chaar uyil aa?
8Di aaŋaal meeh u nfum mubaa, saan ki gir meeh lelee;
saan sunn kijaak ki ga dan na pu.
9Unii umɔk kan unyiib ngbaan na aataakpab yɔl le u lir kitiŋ.
10Aa yaa gbee kpir u kan, u bir sakpen;
ubaa aan kaa ki sil u chee.
11Ŋma ga ŋmaa tak u ki ŋmar?
Ubaa aa bi dulnyaa wee ni ki ga ŋa kina.
12Cha m tuk si waataa aabɔr, ki tuk si waah pɔɔ ti nyaŋ pu na.
13Ubaa aan ŋmaa kar waapaacham aagban,
bee u saa chaar waajaak aabɔkul li u pee na.
14Ŋma ga ŋmaa cha u waar umɔb u gbii ijawaan aanyin na?
15Upuwɔb ye kijaak aapen ŋiker ŋiker la,
le ki bub joo tɔb ki pɔɔ ke litakpal na.
16Libaa mɔk bub joo liken kin kin la, le libuln aan ŋmaa sakr jer.
17Ti mɔmɔk bub joo tɔb kin kin, le nibaa aan ŋmaa daa yakr ti.
18U yaa chiin ichiin kan, mmii moor la,
le unimbil nyakr ke nwiin aah bi puur pu na.
19Imiigaal gaal le ki nya ni umɔb ni, le mmiibil poor ki nya ni.
20Iŋmanyuu nya ni umɔfal ni
ke idɔ i bi wu likumbuul taab na la.
21Waafuurk cha mmii gaal la; le imiigaal yuk nya ni umɔb ni.
22Usil pɔɔ sakpen,
le unii umɔk to u nsan ni na san ijawaan.
23Waagban nibaa chee aa bi ki diin;
mu pɔɔ le kaa geei kpala ke tikur na.
24Upobil li pɔɔ ke litakpal na aa san ijawaan,
laa san nibaa, le ki pɔɔ ke kinaak na.
25U yaa fii sil kan, hali bipɔɔndam san ijawaan la;
ijawaan le ban i nyaŋ bi.
26Kijaak aajuk kibaa le aa bi ki ga ŋmaa tii u titotonn;
le kikpaatuŋ, bee mpiin, bee kigbalk mu aan ŋmaa ŋa u nibaa.
27Tikur diin u chee ke kimook na la,
le tikumann diin sɔk sɔk ke ndɔ mu bur na.
28Mpiin mubaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa cha u san;
le ŋitakpal ŋi yur u na naahn kimook la.
29Lichakukul bi u chee ke mmoon na la,
le binib yaa too u tikpaatunn kan, u laa la.
30Tikakr ti bi upɔtiŋ taab na bi ke ncheen na la;
ŋi geei tikpakpar aatiŋ ke likuul na la.
31U gbir nnyusakpem ke nnyuntom aah leer pu na,
le ki cha mu kpenni ke likpakumbuul na.
32U chuun le ki cha kipɔtiŋ taab piin ki paa u pu,
le ki cha nnyusakpem kpaln tipupur pipiin.
33Uŋeen aatɔ aa bi kitiŋ pu;
u ye tiwanfuurkaan ni kaa san ijawaan na.
34U lik seen ipeel i kpa kigaak sakpen na la;
uma le ye tiwakor mɔmɔk aabɔr.

english_text:
Job's Reply to the Lord
No One Can Oppose You
1Job said:
2No one can oppose you,
because you have the power
to do what you want.
3 You asked why I talk so much
when I know so little.
I have talked about things
that are far beyond
my understanding.
4 You told me to listen
and answer your questions.
5I heard about you from others;
now I have seen you
with my own eyes.
6That's why I hate myself
and sit here in dust and ashes
to show my sorrow.
The Lord Corrects Job's Friends
7The Lord said to Eliphaz:
What my servant Job has said about me is true, but I am angry with you and your two friends for not telling the truth. 8So I want you to go over to Job and offer seven bulls and seven goats on an altar as a sacrifice to please me. After this, Job will pray, and I will agree not to punish you for your foolishness.
9Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar obeyed the Lord, and he answered Job's prayer.
A Happy Ending
10 After Job had prayed for his three friends, the Lord made Job twice as rich as he had been before. 11Then Job gave a feast for his brothers and sisters and for his old friends. They expressed their sorrow for the suffering the Lord had brought on him, and they each gave Job some silver and a gold ring.
12The Lord now blessed Job more than ever; he gave him 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pair of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys.
13In addition to seven sons, Job had three daughters, 14whose names were Jemimah, Keziah, and Keren Happuch. 15They were the most beautiful women in that part of the world, and Job gave them shares of his property, along with their brothers.
16Job lived for another 140 years—long enough to see his great-grandchildren have children of their own— 17and when he finally died, he was very old.
translation_text:
1Le Job gar Uwumbɔr.
Job aah gar pu na
2Uwumbɔr, m nyi ke aa ye mpɔɔnsakpiindaan la;
ki nyi ke aa ga ŋmaa ŋa tiwan ni mɔmɔk aa ban na.
3Aa baa ke maa nyi nibaa ki ŋa kinye aan ki ti pen si nlan.
M len tiwan ni aabɔr maa nyi na
ki len ŋijinjii aawansakpenn ni maan ŋmaa bee naatataa na aabɔr.
4Aa bui mi ke m li pel aan aa len, ki pɔɔn mbaa ki gar saabaan.
5N‑yoonn mu jer na m nan nyi biken aah tuk mi pu na baanja la,
le dandana ma nnimbigbaŋ kan si.
6Kina pu na, inimɔɔn chuu mi maah len pu na mɔmɔk pu,
le m ka titan, ni nfatan ni, ki yii maatunwanbir.
Kookoo aabɔr
7Uwumbɔr aah len Job chee tibɔr ti doo na, le u bui Elifas ke, “Maaŋuul fii aa ni aajɔtiib bilee na pu, ba pu? naa len ibamɔn m pu ke maatutunn Job aah len pu na. 8Tɔ, dandana chuu man inaaja ilole ni ipihja ilole ki di buen Job chee, ki ti toor kitork tii nibaa pu. Job ga mee limeel tii nimi, le m ga kii waameel, ki taa jinn nimi inimɔɔn naah ŋeer pu na. Naa len ibamɔn m pu ke waah len pu na.”
9Elifas, ni Bildad, ni Sofar nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah bui bi ke bi ŋa pu na, le Uwumbɔr kii Job aameel.
10Tɔ, Job aah nan mee Uwumbɔr tii ujɔtiib bitaa ngbaan doo na, le Uwumbɔr ki tii u liwangol, ki tii u nfum mulee pu waah nan kpa pu na. 11Job aakpetiib, ni unaatiib, ni uninkpatiib, ni ujɔtiib mɔmɔk nan dan nan mann u ki jin njim u chee waadichal ni. Bi nan san u kinimbaak ki sɔŋ usui, tibɔbir ti Uwumbɔr di tii u na pu. Bi mɔmɔk ubaabaa nan tii u ŋimombil ni salmaa aabɔmbik.
12Uwumbɔr nan ŋa waanyoor ŋa Job pu waaninkpir ni, ki jer waah nan laa pɔɔn pu na. U nan tii Job ipiih ŋichur kipiik ni ŋinaa, ni laakumii tiib ŋichur ŋiloob, ni ŋinaayil ŋichur ŋilee, ni ibon lichur libaa. 13Job nan ma mbijabim bilole ni mpiibim mutaa. 14U nan yin ubisal upol ke Jemima, le ki yin u paa na ke Kesia, ki yin uwaatiir ke Kerenn Hapuk. 15Bipiib aa nan ki bi dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ponn ni ki ŋan ke Job aabisatiib na. Bite nan cha bi ni bininjatiib kpaan ki yakr waafaal la.
16Job nan ki bi nee aapuwɔb ki ti saa ŋibin nkub ni imonko ilee la, le ki nan kan uyaabitiib ni uyaabisɔsɔk, 17le ki nan por sakpen sakpen ki nin kpo.

english_text:
BOOK I
(Psalms 1–41)
The Way to Happiness
1God blesses those people
who refuse evil advice
and won't follow sinners
or join in sneering at God.
2Instead, they find happiness
in the Teaching of the Lord,
and they think about it
day and night.
3 They are like trees
growing beside a stream,
trees that produce
fruit in season
and always have leaves.
Those people succeed
in everything they do.
4That isn't true of those
who are evil—
they are like straw
blown by the wind.
5Sinners won't have an excuse
on the day of judgment,
and they won't have a place
with the people of God.
6The Lord protects everyone
who follows him,
but the wicked follow a road
that leads to ruin.
translation_text:
NJAN AAGBAŊ
(Ilahn 1–41)
Mpopiin bamɔnn
1Binib bi yii titunwanbirdam aasurm, kaa dii kinimbɔŋdam aabimbin,
kaa kpaani binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na chee na kpa mpopiin.
2Baah gee pu na le ye ke bi keei Uwumbɔr Aakaal aah len pu na,
le ki bae mu nwiin pu ni kinyeek.
3Bi naahn isui i si gbɔk nkpen na la;
i lu ŋisubionn mu ŋeer na la, le yaafar aa kuur.
Bi kani tinyoor baatuln mɔmɔk ni.
4Le titunwanbirdam ma aa bi kina kpala;
bi naahn tigbengbir ti libuln daar joo cha na la.
5Uwumbɔr ga bui ke kinimbɔŋdam aabɔr bii
ki taa cha bi kpaan uma Uwumbɔr aanib chee.
6Uwumbɔr le kiir ki joo bininyaam,
le titunwanbirdam ma cha baadoon ni.

english_text:
The Lord's Chosen King
1 Why do the nations plot,
and why do their people
make useless plans?
2The kings of this earth
have all joined together
to turn against the Lord
and his chosen king.
3They say, “Let's cut the ropes
and set ourselves free!”
4In heaven the Lord laughs
as he sits on his throne,
making fun of the nations.
5The Lord becomes furious
and threatens them.
His anger terrifies them
as he says,
6“I've put my king on Zion,
my sacred hill.”
7 I will tell the promise
that the Lord made to me:
“You are my son, because today
I have become your father.
8Ask me for the nations,
and every nation on earth
will belong to you.
9 You will smash them
with an iron rod
and shatter them
like dishes of clay.”
10Be smart, all you rulers,
and pay close attention.
11Serve and honor the Lord;
be glad and tremble.
12Show respect to his son
because if you don't,
the Lord might become furious
and suddenly destroy you.
But he blesses and protects
everyone who runs to him.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah lee ubɔr u na
1Ba ŋa ŋinibol kpokl ke ŋi yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb?
Ba ŋa binib dak ilandak i kaa kpa tinyoor na?
2Baabɔrb yiil Uwumbɔr aamɔb,
le baajojoob kpaani ki kpokl Uwumbɔr,
ni waah lee ubɔr u na pu.
3Bi len ke, “Cha ti gaa tibaa bi chee man,
cha ti di baasan mee man.”
4Le Uwumbɔr ka waabɔrjal pu paacham, ki laa bi,
ki ŋani bi yaansara, baalandak i kaa pɔɔ na pu.
5Le waaŋuul ponn ni u sak bi, ki di waaŋuul faan bi.
6U bui ke, “Maagongoln Sionn li bi chain na pu,
le m maa kaan maabɔr.”
7Ubɔr ngbaan len ke, “M ga moon Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.
U bui mi ke, ‘Sin le ye maabo, din wee le m ma si.
8Mee mi, aan m ga di ŋitimbol ngbaan mɔmɔk tii si;
kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk ga li ye sin yaan la.
9Aa ga di tikur aadabil gbaa kool bi;
aa ga gbaa wii bi yak yak ke tiyakr aabuul na la.’”
10Nimi bibɔrb, li pel man nsurm mue;
nimi dulnyaa aajojoob, bae man mbaem mue:
11Di ijawaan dii Uwumbɔr man,
12li gbeer man ki ti gbaan unimbiin ni;
naa ye kina kan, waaŋuul ga fii mala,
le ni ga kpo libuul ngbaan ni.
Binib bi mɔmɔk chaa u chee ti ban ke u kiir bi na kpa mpopiin.

english_text:
(Written by David when he was running from his son Absalom.)
An Early Morning Prayer
1 I have a lot of enemies, Lord.
Many fight against 2me and say,
“God won't rescue you!”
3But you are my shield,
and you give me victory
and great honor.
4I pray to you, and you answer
from your sacred hill.
5I sleep and wake up refreshed
because you, Lord,
protect me.
6Ten thousand enemies attack
from every side,
but I am not afraid.
7Come and save me, Lord God!
Break my enemies' jaws
and shatter their teeth,
8because you protect
and bless your people.
translation_text:
David nan ŋmee kigbaŋ kimina buyoonn u nan san waabo Absalom pu na
1Uwumbɔr, m kpa bidim sakpen a,
binib bi kaa gee mi na wiir sakpen a.
2Bi len mi, le ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr aan ter u.”
3Uwumbɔr, le sin le ye kijaak aapeln li kii mi tibɔbir chee na;
aa tii mi linyaŋ, ki pɔɔk ntaakpab.
4M yin Uwumbɔr ki ban nterm,
le u bi waagongoln li bi chain na pu ki keei maayim.
5M doo ki geeni, le Uwumbɔr ye maakikiir kinyeek mɔk.
6Maa san bidim ŋichur ŋichur ŋi mann gob mi na ijawaan.
7Uwumbɔr, dan. Maawumbɔr, gaa mi lii.
Sin le dar maadim mɔmɔk aatafal,
le baa ki kpa mpɔɔn mubaa bi tun mi titunwanbir.
8Linyaŋ nyani Uwumbɔr chee la, u ŋa waanyoor ŋa waanib pu.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.)
An Evening Prayer
1You are my God and protector.
Please answer my prayer.
I was in terrible distress,
but you set me free.
Now have pity and listen
as I pray.
2How long will you people
refuse to respect me?
You love foolish things,
and you run after
what is worthless.
3The Lord has chosen
everyone who is faithful
to be his very own,
and he answers my prayers.
4 But each of you
had better tremble
and turn from your sins.
Silently search your heart
as you lie in bed.
5Offer the proper sacrifices
and trust the Lord.
6There are some who ask,
“Who will be good to us?”
Let your kindness, Lord,
shine brightly on us.
7You brought me more happiness
than a rich harvest
of grain and grapes.
8I can lie down
and sleep soundly
because you, Lord,
will keep me safe.
translation_text:
Ubɔr David aah mee Uwumbɔr kijook pu na
1Maawumbɔr, maakikiir, m yaa mee si kan, kii mi.
Maah nan bi limukl ni na, aa nan ter mi.
San mi kinimbaak dandana wee, ki pel maameel.
2Nimi binib bimina, ni ga seei mi ki ti saa bayoonn?
Ni ga li gee tiwan ni kaa kpa tinyoor tibaa na,
ki chuun dii inyamɔn aawan ki ti saa bayoonn?
3Teer man ke Uwumbɔr le lee bininyaam ke bi li ye waanib,
le m yaa yin u ki ban nterm kan, u ŋun maayim ngbaan.
4Di cha titunwanbir, ki li jii ijawaan pu.
Ni yaa dɔ suuna nimi aawandookaan pu kan,
ni dakl lik nimina mbamɔm man.
5Toor man kitork ki tok na tii Uwumbɔr, ki di naadii tii u.
6Binib pam le mee ke:
“Uwumbɔr, moo tii timi saanyoor. San timi kinimbaak.”
7Le saah tii mi mpopiin mu na jer
baah ga di tijikaar ni ndaan sakpen kan mpopiin mu na.
8M yaa doon kan, le m geen suuna;
Uwumbɔr, sin baanja le kii mi mbamɔm.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use flutes.)
A Prayer for Help
1Listen, Lord, as I pray!
Pay attention when I groan.
2You are my King and my God.
Answer my cry for help
because I pray to you.
3Each morning you listen
to my prayer,
as I bring my requests to you
and wait for your reply.
4You are not the kind of God
who is pleased with evil.
Sinners can't stay with you.
5No one who boasts can stand
in your presence, Lord,
and you hate evil people.
6You destroy every liar,
and you despise violence
and deceit.
7Because of your great mercy,
I come to your house, Lord,
and I am filled with wonder
as I bow down to worship
at your holy temple.
8You do what is right,
and I ask you to guide me.
Make your teaching clear
because of my enemies.
9 Nothing they say is true!
They just want to destroy.
Their words are deceitful
like a hidden pit,
and their tongues are good
only for telling lies.
10Punish them, God,
and let their own plans
bring their downfall.
Get rid of them!
They keep committing crimes
and turning against you.
11Let all who run to you
for protection
always sing joyful songs.
Provide shelter for those
who truly love you
and let them rejoice.
12Our Lord, you bless those
who live right,
and you shield them
with your kindness.

(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.
)
A Prayer in Time of Trouble
1 Don't punish me, Lord,
or even correct me
when you are angry!
2Have pity on me and heal
my feeble body.
My bones tremble with fear,
3and I am in deep distress.
How long will it be?
4Turn and come to my rescue.
Show your wonderful love
and save me, Lord.
5If I die, I cannot praise you
or even remember you.
6My groaning has worn me out.
At night my bed and pillow
are soaked with tears.
7Sorrow has made my eyes dim,
and my sight has failed
because of my enemies.
8 You, Lord, heard my crying,
and those hateful people
had better leave me alone.
9You have answered my prayer
and my plea for mercy.
10My enemies will be ashamed
and terrified,
as they quickly run away
in complete disgrace.
translation_text:
Limukl aayoonn aameel
1Uwumbɔr, taa gee m pu liŋuul ki kae mi.
Taa daa ntafal saaŋuul ponn ni.
2Uwumbɔr, nwon mɔmɔk kpo a, san mi kinimbaak.
M bak sakpen a; pɔɔk ntaakpab,
3m bi limukl ponn ni la.
Uwumbɔr, aa ga yunn kinye aan ki nan nin ter mi?
4Uwumbɔr, dan nan gaa mi lii;
di saanimbaak nyan mi nkun ni.
5Ubaa aa teer aabɔr kitekpiitiŋ ni; ubaa aan ŋmaa pak si nima.
6Mpombiin cha nwon mɔmɔk kpo a;
maah wii kinyeek mɔmɔk pu na cha maawandookaan sɔŋ a,
tinyunyunn sɔŋ maayikukur a.
7Maadim aah cha m wii pu na duun duun nnimbil a,
le maa ki waa mbamɔm.
8Nimi kinimbɔŋdam, siir m chee man,
Uwumbɔr ŋun maah wii pu na;
9u pel maah wii ban nterm pu na, ki ga kii maameel.
10Maadim ga bee nlirm aanimɔɔn aah wu pu na;
libuul ngbaan ni le bilan ga ŋmal, le bi jenn yaa bi.

english_text:
(Written by David.
He sang this to the Lord because of Cush from the tribe of Benjamin.)
The Lord Always Does Right
1You, Lord God,
are my protector.
Rescue me and keep me safe
from all who chase me.
2Or else they will rip me apart
like lions attacking a victim,
and no one will save me.
3I am innocent, Lord God!
4I have not betrayed a friend
or had pity on an enemy
who attacks for no reason.
5If I have done any of this,
then let my enemies
chase and capture me.
Let them trample me to death
and leave me in the dirt.
