li tar mpopiin pu ki len, ki ki gir len ke,
“Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ a.
Usui piir waatutunn aah kan linyaŋ pu na pu.”
28Le m ga moon saatunyaan aabɔr ki li pak si nwiin
ni mu aalirm.

english_text:
(For the music leader by David, the Lord's servant.)
Human Sin and God's Goodness
1 Sinners don't respect God;
sin is all they think about.
2They like themselves too much
to hate their own sins
or even to see them.
3They tell deceitful lies,
and they don't have the sense
to live right.
4Those people stay awake,
thinking up mischief,
and they follow the wrong road,
refusing to turn from sin.
5Your love is faithful, Lord,
and even the clouds in the sky
can depend on you.
6Your decisions are always fair.
They are firm like mountains,
deep like the sea,
and all people and animals
are under your care.
7Your love is a treasure,
and everyone finds shelter
in the shadow of your wings.
8You give your guests a feast
in your house,
and you serve a tasty drink
that flows like a river.
9The life-giving fountain
belongs to you,
and your light gives light
to each of us.
10Our Lord, keep showing love
to everyone who knows you,
and use your power to save all
whose thoughts please you.
11Don't let those proud
and merciless people
kick me around
or chase me away.
12Look at those wicked people!
They are knocked down,
never to get up again.
translation_text:
Unibɔn aah kpa mbiin pu na
1Ubiindaan aasui ponn ni ye titunwanbir la;
u yii Uwumbɔr kaa pak u.
2U dak ke waah nyuun sakpen pu na,
Uwumbɔr aan ŋmaa kan waatunwanbir ki bui ke taa ŋan.
3Waabɔlen ye mbiin ŋmeen, le ki gbii inyamɔn;
waa ki kpa nlan, kaa ki ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na.
4U yaa dɔ kan, u dak ilandak i kaa ŋan na la;
waatun mɔmɔk aa ŋan, le kaa yiil titunwanbir aatuln.
Uwumbɔr aah ŋan pu na
5Uwumbɔr, saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na fuu paacham,
le saaŋann taln ti fuu kitaapaak.
6Saah ŋan sakpen pu na naahn ŋijoo aah paa pu na la;
le saabamɔn naahn nnyusakpem aah nyoo pu na.
Sin le lik unibɔn ni tiwakor mɔmɔk.
7Uwumbɔr, saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na
jer liwangol mɔmɔk la,
ti kan mbɔbɔryaan aa chee
ke ikoobi aah kani pu ina aafeen taab na.
8Saah tii timi tijikaar sakpen ti na le kpiini timi;
le ti nyu nnyun saaŋann aamɔɔ na ni.
9Sin chee le limɔfal mɔmɔk nya ni,
le saawiihn cha ti waa nwiihn.
10Tɔ, li beenin gee binib bi nyi si na, ki ŋa bininyaam tiŋann.
11Taa cha kigaadam tak mi,
ki taa cha bibiindam faan mi aan m san.
12Lik titunwanbirdam aah lir nin chee na.
Bi dɔ nima le kaa ki ŋmaa fii.

english_text:
(By David.)
Trust the Lord
1Don't be annoyed by anyone
who does wrong,
and don't envy them.
2They will soon disappear
like grass without rain.
3Trust the Lord and live right!
The land will be yours,
and you will be safe.
4Do what the Lord wants,
and he will give you
your heart's desire.
5Let the Lord lead you
and trust him to help.
6Then it will be as clear
as the noonday sun
that you were right.
7Be patient and trust the Lord.
Don't let it bother you
when all goes well for those
who do sinful things.
8Don't be angry or furious.
Anger can lead to sin.
9All sinners will disappear,
but if you trust the Lord,
the land will be yours.
10Sinners will soon disappear,
never to be found,
11 but the poor will take the land
and enjoy a big harvest.
12Merciless people make plots
against good people
and snarl like animals,
13but the Lord laughs and knows
their time is coming soon.
14The wicked kill with swords
and shoot arrows to murder
the poor and the needy
and all who do right.
15But they will be killed
by their own swords,
and their arrows
will be broken.
16It is better to live right
and be poor
than to be sinful and rich.
17The wicked will lose all
of their power,
but the Lord gives strength
to everyone who is good.
18Those who obey the Lord
are daily in his care,
and what he has given them
will be theirs forever.
19They won't be in trouble
when times are bad,
and they will have plenty
when food is scarce.
20Wicked people are enemies
of the Lord
and will vanish like smoke
from a field on fire.
21An evil person borrows
and never pays back;
a good person is generous
and never stops giving.
22Everyone the Lord blesses
will receive the land;
everyone the Lord curses
will be destroyed.
23If you do what the Lord wants,
he will make certain
each step you take is sure.
24The Lord will hold your hand,
and if you stumble,
you still won't fall.
25As long as I can remember,
good people have never
been left helpless,
and their children have never
gone begging for food.
26They gladly give and lend,
and their children
turn out good.
27If you stop sinning
and start doing right,
you will keep living
and be secure forever.
28The Lord loves justice,
and he won't ever desert
his faithful people.
He always protects them,
but destroys the children
of the wicked.
29God's people will own the land
and live here forever.
30Words of wisdom come
when good people speak
for justice.
31They remember God's teachings,
and they never take
a wrong step.
32The wicked try to trap
and kill good people,
33but the Lord is on their side,
and he will defend them
when they are on trial.
34Trust the Lord and follow him.
He will give you the land,
and you will see
the wicked destroyed.
35I have seen brutal people
abuse others and grow strong
like trees in rich soil.
36Suddenly they disappeared!
I looked, but they were gone
and no longer there.
37Think of the bright future
waiting for all the families
of honest, innocent,
and peace-loving people.
38But not a trace will be left
of the wicked
or their families.
39The Lord protects his people,
and they can come to him
in times of trouble.
40The Lord helps his people
and saves them from the wicked
because they run to him.
translation_text:
Bibiindam ni bininyaam aadoon aah ga li bi pu na
1Taa cha bibiindam aabɔr muk si;
taa li kpa lipiipoln binib bi tun taani na pu.
2Bi ga wɔŋ ke timoor ti kuur na la;
bi ga kpoi ke tisufar ti yɔl na la.
3Di naadii tii Uwumbɔr, ki li ŋani ni ŋan na;
li bi kitiŋ kee pu ki li kpa limɔfal.
4Li ban saamɔɔn Uwumbɔr chee, le u ga tii si aasui aah ban pu na.
5Di aabaa tii Uwumbɔr; di naadii tii u, aan u ter si;
6U ga cha saah ŋan pu na li wiin ke nwiin pu aawiin na.
7Ji limɔr ki li kii Uwumbɔr aah ga ŋa pu na;
taa cha binib bi kani nkam na,
bee bi kani tinyoor baatunwanbir aatun ponn ni na aabɔr li muk si.
8Taa cha nsuubiin ni liŋuul aabɔr nyaŋ si; ni ga di si buen tibɔr ni la.
9Binib bi di naadii tii Uwumbɔr na le ga li yeh kitiŋ kee,
le Uwumbɔr ga jenn nyan bibiindam ma.
10Naan yunn le bibiindam ga wɔŋ; aa ga lik ban bi,
ki mu aan kan bi;
11binib bi sunn bibaa taab na le ga li yeh kitiŋ kee,
ki ji tinyoor ni nsuudoon aamɔɔn.
12Ubiindaan kpokl ki ban uninyaan la, le ki lik u ni kinanaŋ.
13Le Uwumbɔr ma laa bibiindam, ba pu?
u nyi ke naan yunn le bi kuln.
14Bibiindam ŋɔi baajaak aajum le ki moo pel baatɔi
ke bi ku bigiim bi kaa kpa nibaa na,
ke bi kɔr binib bi tun ni ŋan na;
15le bibaa aajaak aajum ga ku bi, le baatɔi mu ga kool.
16Uninyaan aah kpa siib ni na jer bibiindam mɔmɔk aawangol,
17ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga gaa bibiindam aapɔɔn,
le ki tee li kiir bininyaam.
18Uwumbɔr le kiir binib bi keei waamɔb na,
bima le ga li yeh kitiŋ kee
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
19N‑yoonn yaa kaa nan ki ŋan kan, baan ji falaa;
le nkon aayoonn kan, bi ga li kpa ni ŋeer bi na.
20Le bibiindam ma ga tee kpoi,
Uwumbɔr aadim ga wɔŋ ke nsupuun na la;
bi ga wɔŋ ke iŋmanyuu na la.
21Ubiindaan yaa pinn tiwan kan, waa ki teeni,
le uninyaan ma tii waapiin usui mɔmɔk.
22Uwumbɔr aah ŋa waanyoor ŋa binib bi pu na
le ga li yeh kitiŋ kee,
le waah puun lii binib bi pu na ma ga yaa koo timoor ni.
23Uwumbɔr le mɔk unii nsan mu u ga dii na,
le ki kii binib bi unimbil gbiin bi na.
24Bi yaa lir kan, baan doon kitiŋ, ba pu? Uwumbɔr le ter bi.
25Dandana m ye uninkpel la; m yunn pam,
le maa kee kan ke Uwumbɔr siir cha bininyaam,
ki mu aa kee kan ke baabim chuun mee tijiir.
26N‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, bi tii la,
le ki pinni tii binib biken kaa gaal nibaa,
le baabim mu ye bi tinyoor.
27Fenn aapuwɔb tii titunwanbir, ki li ŋani ni ŋan na,
le aayaabitiib nan li bi kitiŋ kee pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
28ba pu? Uwumbɔr gee tiwan ni ŋan na la,
kaa siir cha waanib bi dii u mbamɔm na.
U kii bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le ki ga jenn nyan bibiindam ma.
29Bininyaam le ga li yeh kitiŋ kee,
ki ga li bi ki pu ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
30Uninyaan aamɔbon ye nlan la, le ki kpa ibamɔn n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
31U joo Waawumbɔr aakaal usui ni la, le kaa yenni i chee.
32Ubiindaan lik uninyaan aah chuun pu na la,
le ki pɔɔni ubaa ke u ku u;
33le Uwumbɔr aan di u ŋa waadim aaŋaal ni,
ki mu aan cha bi bui ke waabɔr aa ŋan,
buyoonn bi bi ji u tibɔr na.
34Li kpa Uwumbɔr pu limakl, ki kii tii waamɔbon;
waah ga nyuŋ si pu na le ye ke u di kitiŋ kee tii si,
le aa ga kan ke u jenn nyan bibiindam.
35M nan nyi ubiindaan ubaa, le u nan kpa mbiin ni ti nyaŋ;
u nan ti jer binib mɔmɔk pu
ke Lebanonn aasui i fɔk sakpen na la;
36Puwɔb le m nan ki jer nima le waa nan ki bi;
m nan ban u le kaa ki kan u.
37Lik bee uninyaan, lik unii u ŋan na mbamɔm
unii u kpa nsuudoon na kpa yaabitiib la,
38le titunwanbirdam ma kulni la, le bi ŋar biyaabitiib ŋŋaan.
39Uwumbɔr le gaal binib bi ŋan na lir, le ki kii bi tibɔbir aayoonn.
40U ter bi le ki gaal bi lir; u gaal bi bibiindam chee lir,
ba pu? bi chaa u chee ti ban nterm.

english_text:
(A psalm by David to be used when an offering is made.)
A Prayer in Times of Trouble
1When you are angry, Lord,
please don't punish me
or even correct me.
2You shot me with your arrows,
and you struck me
with your hand.
3My body hurts all over
because of your anger.
Even my bones are in pain,
and my sins 4are so heavy
that I am crushed.
5Because of my foolishness,
I am covered with sores
that stink and spread.
6My body is twisted and bent,
and I groan all day long.
7Fever has my back in flames,
and I hurt everywhere.
8I am worn out and weak,
moaning and in distress.
9You, Lord, know every one
of my deepest desires,
and my noisy groans
are no secret to you.
10My heart is beating fast.
I feel weak all over,
and my eyes are red.
11Because of my sickness,
no friends or neighbors
will come near me.
12All who want me dead
set traps to catch me,
and those who want
to harm and destroy me
plan and plot all day.
13I am not able to hear
or speak a word;
14I am completely deaf
and can't make a sound.
15I trust you, Lord God,
and you will do something.
16I said, “Don't let them laugh
or brag when I slip and fall.”
17I am about to collapse
from constant pain.
18I told you my sins,
and I am sorry for them.
19Many deadly and powerful
enemies hate me,
20and they repay evil for good
because I try to do right.
21You are the Lord God!
Stay nearby
and don't desert me.
22You are the one who saves me.
Please hurry and help.
translation_text:
Falaadaan aameel
1Uwumbɔr, taa di liŋuul daa ntafal.
2Saapiin tii mi titotonn; aa faa mi lii kitiŋ.
3Saaŋuul pu, le m bi iween sakpiin ni;
maatunwanbir pu le nwon mɔmɔk kpaln iween ŋmeen.
4M bi beer maatunwanbir ti wiir ke nwam na ponn ni la;
ti ye lituln li nyuun sakpen na le ki tii mi.
5Maajɔrk pu, le maabuun bur ki nu.
6M gur boo la, m lir kookoo a; m wii le nwiin ti lir.
7Nwon mɔmɔk ton sakpen la, le maa ki daa nkun.
8Nwon mɔmɔk kpo, le m lir kookoo,
nsui mɔmɔk bii a, le m ker iween aadun.
9Uwumbɔr, aa nyi maah ban ni na; aa ŋun maadun mɔmɔk pu.
10Mpobil gbaa la, le maapɔɔn mɔmɔk doo,
le nnimbil aa ki waa chain.
11Maabuun pu, njɔtiib, ni binib bi koo gbɔk mi na
aan ki duun ni mi;
hali maachiln ni yaab gur daa mi la.
12Binib bi ban bi ku mi na pen mi gaawɔb mam la,
le binib bi ban bi tii mi titotonn na pɔɔni bibaa ke bi doo mi; n‑yoonn mɔmɔk bi kpokl ban mi la.
13M gur naahn utafakpaa la, le kaa ki ŋun,
ki naahn ubir kaa ki ŋmaa len.
14M bi ke uja u kaa ŋun, kaa gar na la.
15Uwumbɔr, le m tii sin ma naadii.
Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, le sin ma ga gar mi.
16Taa cha maadim aasui piir maasuubiin pu;
taa cha bi li kpa kipupuk maalirm pu.
17Nwon wu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la, le m ban m lir.
18M kpiir maatunwanbir ti tii mi nsuubiin na la.
19Maadim kpa laafee le ki pɔɔ; binib pam le nan mi fam.
20Binib bi joo mbiin pa tiŋann na bii maayimbil
buyoonn m pɔɔni mbaa ke m li ŋani ni ŋan na.
21Uwumbɔr, taa siir cha mi; Maawumbɔr, taa li daa mi.
22Uwumbɔr u gaal mi lir na, ter mi dandana wee.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for Jeduthun, the music leader.)
A Prayer for Forgiveness
1I told myself, “I'll be careful
not to sin by what I say,
and I'll muzzle my mouth
when evil people are near.”
2I kept completely silent,
but it did no good,
and I hurt even worse.
3I felt a fire burning inside,
and the more I thought,
the more it burned,
until at last I said:
4“Please, Lord,
show me my future.
Will I soon be gone?
5You made my life short,
so brief that the time
means nothing to you.
“Human life is but a breath,
6and it disappears
like a shadow.
Our struggles are senseless;
we store up more and more,
without ever knowing
who will get it all.
7“What am I waiting for?
I depend on you, Lord!
8Save me from my sins.
Don't let fools sneer at me.
9You treated me like this,
and I kept silent,
not saying a word.
10“Won't you stop punishing me?
You have worn me down.
11You punish us severely
because of our sins.
Like a moth, you destroy
what we treasure most.
We are as frail as a breath.
12“Listen, Lord, to my prayer!
My eyes are flooded with tears,
as I pray to you.
I am merely a stranger
visiting in your home
as my ancestors did.
13Stop being angry with me
and let me smile again
before I am dead and gone.”
translation_text:
Falaadaan aah kpiir waatunwanbir pu na
1M len ke, “M ga chuu mbaa maatuln chee,
ki taa cha nlambil di mi koon titunwanbir ni.
Buyoonn titunwanbirdam bi m chee na kan,
maan len tibaa.”
2M nan ŋmin suuna, kaa len tibaa,
hali maa len litunyaan libaa aabɔr. Le maafalaa moo kpae,
3le maalandak ban i ku mi.
M yaa moo dak ilandak kan,
le ni moo muk mi; le m nan baa ke,
4“Uwumbɔr, maamɔfal fɔk kinye? Bayoonn aan m ga kpo?
Bui mi maamɔfal aah ga kuln n‑yoonn mu na.”
5Aa kuln maamɔfal mala.
Aa chee kan, maamɔfal aayoonn aa ye nibaa.
Mbamɔn, unibɔn aamɔfal aa jer litakpiln libaa aabuln,
6li ye kijunjuŋ la. Waatuln mɔmɔk ye fam la;
u ban liwangol bilni, kaa tee nyi u ga li yeh li na.
7Uwumbɔr, ni ki ye ba aan m ga mak ni pu?
M mak sin pu la.
8Nyan mi maatunwanbir mɔmɔk ni, ki taa cha bijɔrb laa mi.
9M ga li ŋmin, kaan len tibaa, ba pu?
Sin le cha m ji falaa wee.
10Taa ki daa ntafal kpee; saagbar ban ti ku mi la.
11Saah ga kae unii pu na, le aa joo dar utafal waatunwanbir pu,
le ki bii waah gee tiwan ni na
ke ŋipandakur aah bii likekeln pu na.
Mbamɔn, unibɔn aa jer litakpiln libaa aabuln.
12Uwumbɔr, ŋun maameel, ki ŋun maawiil;
m yaa wii kan, dan ki nan ter mi.
Aa chee, m yunn siib ke uchaan na le dulnyaa wee ni,
ke n‑yaajatiib aah nan bi pu na la.
13Di cha mi suuna aan m kan mpopiin siib waahr
aan m nin buen ki taa ki gir ni.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
A Prayer for Help
1I patiently waited, Lord,
for you to hear my prayer.
You listened 2and pulled me
from a lonely pit
full of mud and mire.
You let me stand on a rock
with my feet firm,
3and you gave me a new song,
a song of praise to you.
Many will see this,
and they will honor and trust
you, the Lord God.
4You bless all of those
who trust you, Lord,
and refuse to worship idols
or follow false gods.
5You, Lord God, have done
many wonderful things,
and you have planned
marvelous things for us.
No one is like you!
I would never be able to tell
all you have done.
6 Sacrifices and offerings
are not what please you;
gifts and payment for sin
are not what you demand.
But you made me willing
to listen and obey.
7And so, I said, “I am here
to do what is written
about me in the book,
where it says,
8‘I enjoy pleasing you.
Your Law is in my heart.’ ”
9When your people worshiped,
you know I told them,
“Our Lord always helps!”
10When all your people met,
I did not keep silent.
I said, “Our Lord is kind.
He is faithful and caring,
and he saves us.”
11You, Lord, never fail
to have pity on me;
your love and faithfulness
always keep me secure.
12I have more troubles
than I can count.
My sins are all around me,
and I can't find my way.
My sins outnumber
the hairs on my head,
and I feel weak.
13Please show that you care
and come to my rescue.
Hurry and help me!
14Disgrace and confuse
all who want me dead;
turn away and disgrace
all who want to hurt me.
15Embarrass and shame
everyone who says,
“Just look at you now!”
16Our Lord, let your worshipers
rejoice and be glad.
They love you for saving them,
so let them always say,
“The Lord is wonderful!”
17I am poor and needy,
but, Lord God,
you care about me,
and you come to my rescue.
Please hurry and help.
translation_text:
Kipak aalahn
1M nan ka suuna le ki kii Uwumbɔr aaterm;
le u pel m chee ki ŋun maawiil.
2U daa nyan mi mbuu mu bir na ni,
u nyan mi tikpakpar ti nyoo na ponn ni,
ki di mi kaan litakpal li paa na pu, le nibaa aan ki pii mi nima.
3U nan mɔk mi nlahnpɔɔn ke m gaa,
nlahn mu m ga gaa pak uma Uwumbɔr na.
Binib bi kan kina na pam ga li san u, ki di naadii tii u.
4Binib bi di naadii tii Uwumbɔr, kaa dii ŋiwaa,
kaa kpaani binib bi dii ŋiwaa na chee na,
bima le kpa mpopiin sakpen.
5Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, aa ŋa tiwan pam tii timi;
ubaa aa bi ke sin na.
Aa dak ke aa ga ŋa iwaan aatun tii timi,
maa nan ŋmaa len ŋi mɔmɔk pu, ŋaakahm wiir sakpen a.
6Saa ban tiwakor ni tijikaar aatork;
saa ban ke m di tiwakor toor kitork ki di see mmii kitork aabimbiln paab tii si,
kaa ban ke m toor kitork titunwanbir pu,
aa tee tii mi ŋitafal ke m ŋun tii si,
7kina pu le m gar ke, “M sɔ.
Saah ban ke m li ŋani pu na bi Nkaal Aagbaŋ ponn ni la.
8Maawumbɔr, m gee sakpen ke m ŋa saageehn,
m joo saamɔkm nsui ni la.”
9Uwumbɔr, saanib mɔmɔk aakuun ni,
le m len tibɔnyaan ke aa gaa timi lii.
Aa nyi ke m ga li len ti, kaan di cha.
10Maa di tibɔnyaan ngbaan di bɔr, n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan,
m len saah ŋan sakpen ki ter mi pu na la.
Maan li si ŋmin saanib mɔmɔk aakuun ni,
m ga len saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na,
ni saah si chob pu na aabɔr.
11Uwumbɔr, m nyi ke saan di cha kaan san mi kinimbaak.
Saageehm, ni saah si chob pu na le ga li kii mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
Limeel li ban nterm na
(Ilahn 70)
12Tibɔr pam le mann goln mi, tibɔbir ti maan ŋmaa kahn ti na.
Maatunwanbir chuu mi a, le maa ki waa;
ti wiir jer n‑yil paab aayikpir, le ntaakpab yɔl.
13Uwumbɔr, gaa mi lii. Ter mi dandana wee.
14Cha binib bi ban ke bi ku mi na aalan ŋmal aan bi lir kookoo.
Cha binib bi aasui piir maah bi tibɔr ni pu na di inimɔɔn labr.
15Cha binib bi laa mi na kan nsuubiin baalirm pu.
16Cha binib bimɔk choo aa chee na kan mpopiin ni mmɔɔn.
Cha binib bimɔk dooni si saah gaa bi lii pu na
len n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke, “Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ a.”
17Uwumbɔr, nwon yɔl, le m ye ugiin, le saa suln mbɔr.
Sin le ye Maawumbɔr u gaal mi lir na, ŋa mala ki nan ter mi.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
A Prayer in Time of Sickness
1You, Lord God, bless everyone
who cares for the poor,
and you rescue those people
in times of trouble.
2You protect them
and keep them alive.
You make them happy here
in this land,
and you don't hand them over
to their enemies.
3You always heal them
and restore their strength
when they are sick.
4I prayed, “Have pity, Lord!
Heal me, though I have sinned
against you.”
5My vicious enemies ask me,
“When will you die
and be forgotten?”
6When visitors come,
all they ever bring
are worthless words,
and when they leave,
they spread gossip.
7My enemies whisper about me.
They think the worst,
8and they say,
“You have some fatal disease!
You'll never get well.”
9 My most trusted friend
has turned against me,
though he ate at my table.
10Have pity, Lord! Heal me,
so I can pay them back.
11Then my enemies
won't defeat me,
and I will know
that you really care.
12You have helped me
because I am innocent,
and you will always
be close to my side.
13 You, the Lord God of Israel,
will be praised forever!
Amen and amen.
translation_text:
Ubun aameel
1Binib bi aatafal bi bigiim wɔb na, bima le kpa mpopiin;
Uwumbɔr ga ter bi buyoonn bi bi tibɔr ni na.
2Uwumbɔr ga li kii bi le ki bɔr baamɔfal mbamɔm.
U ga cha bi li kpa mpopiin kitiŋ kee pu;
waan cha baadim aapɔɔn pii bi.
3Bi yaa bun kan, Uwumbɔr ga ter bi ki cha bi pɔɔk.
4M len ke, “Uwumbɔr, m tun si titunwanbir;
san mi kinimbaak ki tii mi laafee.”
5Maadim len mi tibɔr ti kaa ŋan na.
Bi ban ke m kpo aan binib suln m bɔr la.
6Binib bi choo nan manni mi na ye binyamɔndam la;
bi chuun ban maabɔbir la,
le ki di buen ni kookoo ki ti len ti.
7Binib bimɔk kaa gee mi na looni tuk tɔb maabɔr la,
bi dakl lik maabɔr ti kaa ŋan kpala na la.
8Bi len le ke, “Waabunbunn ngbaan nyaŋ u a;
waan ki fii daalbaadaal.”
9Hali njɔnyaan, u m tii u naadii sakpen na,
aan m ni u kpaan ni ji lisambil libaa ni na,
uma le fii sil m pu.
10Uwumbɔr, san mi kinimbaak,
ki tii mi laafee, aan m teen maadim.
11Baan nyaŋ mi, le m ga bee ke aasui piin m pu.
12Aa ga ter mi, ba pu? m ŋani ni ŋan na la;
aa ga cha m li bi aanimbiin ni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
13Pak timi Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr man.
Li pak u man dandana, ni n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
Amii amii.
LELEE AAGBAŊ
(Ilahn 42–72)

english_text:
BOOK II
(Psalms 42–72)
(A special psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
Longing for God
1As a deer gets thirsty
for streams of water,
I truly am thirsty
for you, my God.
2In my heart, I am thirsty
for you, the living God.
When will I see your face?
3Day and night my tears
are my only food,
as everyone keeps asking,
“Where is your God?”
4Sorrow floods my heart,
when I remember
leading the worshipers
to your house.
I can still hear them shout
their joyful praises.
5Why am I discouraged?
Why am I restless?
I should trust you, Lord.
I will praise you again
because you help me,
6and you are my God.
I am deeply discouraged,
and so I think about you
here where the Jordan begins
at Mount Hermon
and at Mount Mizar.
7Your vicious waves
have swept over me
like an angry ocean
or a roaring waterfall.
8Every day, you are kind,
and at night
you give me a song
as my prayer to you,
the God of my life.
9You are my mighty rock.
Why have you forgotten me?
Why must enemies mistreat me
and make me sad?
10Even my bones are in pain,
while all day long
my enemies sneer and ask,
“Where is your God?”
11Why am I discouraged?
Why am I restless?
I trust you, Lord!
And I will praise you again
because you help me,
and you are my God.
translation_text:
Unii u kaa bi waatiŋ ni na aameel
1Uwumbɔr, upeeman aah ban mbun mu aanyun soon na pu na,
kina le m mu ban si.
2Sin Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, m wii ban si la;
bayoonn aan m ga ŋmaa buen aanimbiin ni ki ti doon si?
3M wii nwiin pu ni kinyeek la, le maanyunyunn ye maajikaar;
n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, maadim baa mi le ke,
“Saawumbɔr ngbaan bi la?”
4M yaa teer n‑yoonn mu jer na aabɔr kan, le nsui bii,
n‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan dii kinipaak buen Uwumbɔr do ki loln bi pu nsan na,
kinipaak ngbaan aasui nan piin,
le bi gaa ilahn ki tar ki pak Uwumbɔr.
5Ba ŋa nsui aa piin? Ba ŋa nsui bii kina?
M mak Uwumbɔr pu la, le m ga ki pak u,
uma le ye Maawumbɔr u gaal mi lir na.
6-7Maah bi tinaagbiir aatiŋ ni na,
nsui bii la, kina pu le m di maalandak ŋa u ni.
U di mpombiin aanyunkpenn le biin nsui pu,
nlanŋmal ŋmeen le choo m chee ke nwam na,
ki naahn nnyun mu nya ni Hemonn, ni Misar Aajoo paab
ki puu lir ni Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl ni na.
8Uwumbɔr tii mi waageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na nwiin pu, aan m nan li kpa limeel aalahn kinyeek
ki gaa mee Uwumbɔr u tii mi limɔfal na.
9M len Uwumbɔr u ye maakikiir na chee ke, “Ba ŋa aa suln mbɔr?
Ba ŋa m beenin ji falaa, maadim aah ŋa mi mbiin pu na pu?”
10Baasiibil le doo mi.
Bi baa mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke, “Saawumbɔr ngbaan bi la?”
11Ba ŋa nsui aa piin? Ba ŋa nsui bii kina?
M mak Uwumbɔr pu la, le m ga ki pak u,
uma le ye Maawumbɔr u gaal mi lir na.

english_text:
A Prayer in Times of Trouble
1Show that I am right, God!
Defend me against everyone
who doesn't know you;
rescue me from each
of those deceitful liars.
2I run to you for protection.
Why do you turn me away?
Why must enemies mistreat me
and make me sad?
3Send your light and your truth
to guide me.
Let them lead me to your house
on your sacred mountain.
4Then I will worship
at your altar because you
make me joyful.
You are my God,
and I will praise you.
Yes, I will praise you
as I play my harp.
5Why am I discouraged?
Why am I restless?
I trust you, Lord!
And I will praise you again
because you help me,
and you are my God.
translation_text:
Unii u kaa bi waatiŋ ni na aameel
1Uwumbɔr, bui ke maabɔr ŋan,
ki len tii mi binib bi kaa dii si na chee;
nyan mi binyamɔndam ni titunwanbirdam aaŋaal ni.
2Sin le ye u kii mi na; ba ŋa aa siir cha mi?
ba ŋa m beenin ji falaa, maadim aah ŋa mi mbiin pu na pu?
3Cha saawiihn ni saabamɔn dan;
cha ni loln m pu nsan ki giin ni mi saagongoln li bi chain na pu,
ki ti fuu saadichal, li ponn ni aa koo na,
4le m ga buen saatork aabimbiln chee;
sin Uwumbɔr chee le m kani mpopiin.
Uwumbɔr, Maawumbɔr, m ga gbaa maabeek ki gaa ilahn pak si.
5Ba ŋa nsui aa piin? Ba ŋa nsui bii kina?
M mak Uwumbɔr pu la, le m ga ki pak u,
uma le ye Maawumbɔr u gaal mi lir na.

english_text:
(A special psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
A Prayer for Help
1Our God, our ancestors told us
what wonders you worked
and we listened carefully.
2You chased off the nations
by causing them trouble
with your powerful arm.
Then you let our ancestors
take over their land.
3Their strength and weapons
were not what won the land
and gave them victory!
You loved them and fought
with your powerful arm
and your shining glory.
4You are my God and King,
and you give victory
to the people of Jacob.
5By your great power,
we knocked our enemies down
and trampled on them.
6I don't depend on my arrows
or my sword to save me.
7But you saved us
from our hateful enemies,
and you put them to shame.
8We boast about you, our God,
and we are always grateful.
9But now you have rejected us;
you don't lead us into battle,
and we look foolish.
10You made us retreat,
and our enemies have taken
everything we own.
11You let us be slaughtered
like sheep,
and you scattered us
among the nations.
12You sold your people
for little or nothing,
and you earned no profit.
13You made us look foolish
to our neighbors;
people who live nearby
insult us and sneer.
14Foreigners joke about us
and shake their heads.
15I am embarrassed every day,
and I blush with shame.
16But others mock and sneer,
as they watch my enemies
take revenge on me.
17All this happened to us,
though we didn't forget you
or break our agreement.
18We always kept you in mind
and followed your teaching.
19But you crushed us,
and you covered us
with deepest darkness
where wild animals live.
20We did not forget you
or lift our hands in prayer
to foreign gods.
21You would have known it
because you discover
every secret thought.
22 We face death all day for you.
We are like sheep on their way
to be slaughtered.
23Wake up! Do something, Lord!
Why are you sleeping?
Don't desert us forever.
24Why do you keep looking away?
Don't forget our sufferings
and all our troubles.
25We are flat on the ground,
holding on to the dust.
26Do something! Help us!
Show how kind you are
and come to our rescue.
translation_text:
Limeel li ban nterm na
1Uwumbɔr, tiyaajatiib bui timi,
le titafal ŋun saah nan tun ŋitukpaan ŋi baayoonn mu jer ki yunn na.
2Sin aabaa le nan jenn nyan binib bi kaa dii si na,
ki di saanib kaan baatiŋ pu.
Aa nan daa binib ngbaan aatafal ki cha saanib kan tinyoor.
3Saanib aa nan di baajaak aajum le nyaŋ ki gaa kitiŋ ngbaan;
baa nan di bibaa aapɔɔn le di kan linyaŋ ngbaan;
ni nan ye sin aapɔɔn pu la;
saah nan bi bi chee pu na le nan cha bi nyaŋ,
le ki mɔk ke aa gee bi.
4Sin le ye Maawumbɔr ni maabɔr; aa tii saanib linyaŋ,
5le ti joo saapɔɔn nyaŋni timi aadim.
6Maa mak maatɔm pu, kaa mak maajaak aajuk pu
ke ni gaa mi lii;
7le sin ma gaa timi, timi aadim aaŋaal ni lii,
le ki nyaŋ binib bi kaa gee timi na.
8Ti ga pak si n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
ki li dooni si ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
9Le dandana wee aa yii timi ki cha bi nyaŋ timi.
Saa ki diir timi aajab chaa butɔb ni.
10Aa cha timi aadim jenn timi, le ki yoor timi aawangol.
11Aa cha bi kɔr timi ke ipiih na la, aa cha ti yaa koo ntiyayam ni.
12Aa di saanib kooh kidaak ki kaa pɔɔ na kaa kan tinyoor tibaa.
13Timi ni binib bi koo gbɔk tɔb na kani saah ŋani timi pu na,
le bi ŋani timi mbɔnyun ki laa timi.
14Aa di timi ŋa yaansara aawan le ŋitimbol ŋiken chee;
bi laa timi le ki gbakr biyil.
15N‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, m bi inimɔɔn ni la;
16maah ŋun maadim ni binib bi nan mi na aasiibil ni tilaar pu na
m ye unimɔɔnii la.
17Nimina mɔmɔk ŋa timi n‑yoonn mu taa suln aabɔr
kaa bii tipuukpaan ti aa nan puu tii timi na.
18Taa nyan aapuwɔb, taa yii saamɔbon.
19Le aa siir cha timi tipeewanbir aakaasisik ni;
aa siir cha timi mbɔmbɔɔn sakpen ponn ni la.
20Ti yaa ba di cha kaa ki dooni si, timi Aawumbɔr,
ki mee liwaal libaa kan,
21aa ba ga bee, ba pu? aa nyi tisui aah bi pu na.
22Tɔ, sin pu le bi ku timi iwiin mɔmɔk,
le ti naahn ipiih i bi ban bi ti kɔr i na la.
23Uwumbɔr, finn ngeen pu. Ba ŋa aa dɔ geen?
Fii sil paacham. Taa yii timi kookoo.
24Ba ŋa aa joo aabaa bɔrni timi?
Taa suln timi aafalaa ni timi aamuk bɔr.
25Ti lir wɔb ki dɔ kitiŋ la; ti lir ki dɔ titan ponn ni la.
26Dan nan ter timi.
Gaa timi lii, saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu.

english_text:
(A special psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader. To the tune “Lilies.” A love song.)
For a Royal Wedding
1My thoughts are filled
with beautiful words
for the king,
and I will use my voice
as a writer would use
pen and ink.
2No one is as handsome as you!
Your words are always kind.
That is why God
will always bless you.
3Mighty king, glorious ruler,
strap on your sword
4and ride out in splendor!
Win victories for truth
and mercy and justice.
Do fearsome things
with your powerful arm.
5Send your sharp arrows
through enemy hearts
and make all nations fall
at your feet.
6 You are God, and you will rule
forever as king.
Your royal power
brings about justice.
7You love justice and hate evil.
And so, your God chose you
and made you happier
than any of your friends.
8The sweet aroma of the spices
myrrh, aloes, and cassia
covers your royal robes.
You enjoy the music of harps
in palaces decorated
with ivory.
9Daughters of kings are here,
and your bride stands
at your right side,
wearing a wedding gown
trimmed with pure gold.
10Bride of the king,
listen carefully to me.
Forget your own people
and your father's family. 11The king adores you.
He is your master,
so do what he desires.
12All of the richest people
from the city of Tyre
will try to influence you
13with precious treasures.
Your bride, my king,
has inward beauty,
and her wedding gown is woven
with threads of gold.
14Wearing the finest garments,
she is brought to you,
followed by her young friends,
the bridesmaids.
15Everyone is excited,
as they follow you
to the royal palace.
16Your sons and your grandsons
will also be kings
as your ancestors were.
You will make them rulers
everywhere on earth.
17I will make your name famous
from now on,
and you will be praised
forever and ever.
translation_text:
Ubɔr aabɔndinn aalahn
1Ŋimɔbonyaan le gbii nsui ni,
le m naan nlahn mue m tii ubɔr.
Nlambil gor ke li di nlahn lii
ke ugbaŋmeer nyaan aagbaŋmeemoon aah ga ŋmee pu na.
2Sin ubɔr le ŋan jer bijab mɔmɔk; aa ye unii u ŋmaa len na la.
Uwumbɔr ŋani tinyoor ŋani aa pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la.
3Ubɔr sakpiin, di saajaak aajuk peen; aa kpa mpɔɔn ni kipak.
4Di mpɔɔn buen ki ti kan mbamɔn ni mbimbinyaan aanyaŋ.
Saapɔɔn le ga cha aa kan linyaŋ sakpeln.
5Saapiin ka pam, i too chaar saadim aapobil,
le ŋitimbol lir gbaani aanimbiin ni.
6Nnaan mu Uwumbɔr di tii si na ga li bi
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
Aa joo saanib mbamɔm la;
7aa gee lituln li ŋan na, le ki nan titunwanbir.
Kina pu le Uwumbɔr u ye Saawumbɔr na lee si
ki tii si mpopiin ki jer bibɔrb biken.
8Tulalee tiib bi bi yin bi ke mir ni alos na le gbii saakeken pu;
le bilahngaab ni biwangbaab bi ŋibɔrchin ŋi bi di iluub aanyin
di toor ŋi na ponn ni ki pak si.
9Bibɔrb aabisatiib ŋmal bipiib bi bi saachiln ni na,
le ubɔrpii si libɔrjal chee aaŋangii wɔb,
ki pee salmaa nyaan aaleen.
10Ubɔr aabɔndinn, li pel maah len pu na,
suln saanib, ni aado yaab bɔr.
11Saanyaan le ga cha ubɔr li gee si;
uma le ye saaninkpel, kina pu na, kii waamɔb.
12Taya aatiŋ aanib ga joo ni si ipiin,
biwankpadam ga dan nan ban ke bi piir aasui.
13Ubɔr aabɔndinn u mu ye ubɔr aabisal na koo ni ki ŋan sakpen a.
Bi di salmaa aakokonn le luu waabɔkul.
14U pee waabɔkul li ŋmal ŋitanyaan na,
le bi di u buen ubɔr chee, le unaakoontiib dii u,
le bi mu ti fuu ubɔr ngbaan chee.
15Bi di mpopiin ni mmɔɔn le ti koo libɔrchiln ni.
16Sin maabɔr, m ga tii si japɔtiib pam,
le bi nan gaa aayaajatiib aanaan,
le aa ga ŋa bi kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aajojoob.
17Maalahn le ga cha saayimbil li bi
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na,
le binib mɔmɔk ga li pak si n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

english_text:
(A special song by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
God Is Our Mighty Fortress
1God is our mighty fortress,
always ready to help
in times of trouble.
2And so, we won't be afraid!
Let the earth tremble
and the mountains tumble
into the deepest sea.
3Let the ocean roar and foam,
and its raging waves
shake the mountains.
4A river and its streams
bring joy to the city,
which is the sacred home
of God Most High.
5God is in that city,
and it won't be shaken.
He will help it at dawn.
6Nations rage! Kingdoms fall!
But at the voice of God
the earth itself melts.
7The Lord All-Powerful
is with us.
The God of Jacob
is our fortress.
8Come! See the fearsome things
the Lord has done on earth.
9God brings wars to an end
all over the world.
He breaks the arrows,
shatters the spears,
and burns the shields.
10Our God says, “Calm down,
and learn that I am God!
All nations on earth
will honor me.”
11The Lord All-Powerful
is with us.
The God of Jacob
is our fortress.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr bi ti chee
1Uwumbɔr le ye timi aakikiir, ni timi aapɔɔn,
tibɔr aayoonn mɔmɔk kan, u gor le ki ter timi.
2Kina pu na, taan san ijawaan,
hali kitiŋ yaa dam aan ŋijoo ber lir nnyusakpem aataab kan,
taan san ijawaan;
3hali nnyusakpem yaa fii ti lir aan ŋigongon dam kina pu kan,
taan san ijawaan.
4Limɔɔl libaa le bi, ki joo ni mpopiin nan tii Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aatiŋ ki ponn ni waadichal bi na.
5Uwumbɔr bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni,
kina pu na, kaan bii daalbaadaal;
lichakpitaawoln le u ga dan nan ter ki.
6Ijawaan chur ŋitimbol, le nnaan mɔmɔk jii;
Uwumbɔr tar, le kitiŋ bunn doo.
7Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bi ti chee;
uma u nan ye Jakob Aawumbɔr na le ye timi aabɔbɔryaan.
8Dan nan lik man Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tiwan ni na.
Lik man waah ŋa lijinjiir aawan ni kitiŋ pu na.
9U cha butɔb door dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni;
U kool itɔi, ki bii tikpaatunn, ki seer kijaak aapen mmii.
10U len ke, “Di cha kijaak man, ki bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr,
m ye ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aayidaan,
ni dulnyaa mɔmɔk aayidaan.”
11Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bi ti chee;
uma u nan ye Jakob Aawumbɔr na le ye timi aabɔbɔryaan.

english_text:
(A psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
God Rules the Nations
1All of you nations,
clap your hands and shout
joyful praises to God.
2The Lord Most High is fearsome,
the ruler of all the earth.
3God has put every nation
under our power,
4and he chose for us the land
that was the pride of Jacob,
his favorite.
5God goes up to his throne,
as people shout
and trumpets blast.
6Sing praises to God our King,
7the ruler of all the earth!
Praise God with songs.
8God rules the nations
from his sacred throne.
9Their leaders come together
and are now the people
of Abraham's God.
All rulers on earth
surrender their weapons,
and God is greatly praised!
translation_text:
Ujojoorkpaan
1Binib mɔmɔk, faa ŋibambaan mpopiin pu man.
Gaa ilahn mpɔɔn pu ki pak Uwumbɔr man.
2Li san man Uwumbɔr u kpa mpɔɔn jer mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na;
u ye ubɔrkpaan la, le ki joo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk.
3U cha ti nyaŋ binib; u cha ti joo ŋitimbol ŋiken.
4U lee kitiŋ ki ti ga li bi ki pu na tii timi,
liwangol li ye waah gee binib bi na yaan na.
5Uwumbɔr jon kal waabɔrjal pu.
Mpopiin aafuuk ni kakaan mam wii n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr cha paacham na la.
6Gaa ilahn pak Uwumbɔr man; u ye timi aabɔr, gaa ilahn pak u man.
7Uwumbɔr le ye dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk aabɔr;
di ilahn pak u man.
8Uwumbɔr ka waabɔrjal li bi chain na pu;
u joo ŋitimbol mɔmɔk.
9Ŋitimbol aajojoob kuun ni unimbiin ni,
ke bi ye uma Uwumbɔr u Abraham nan dii u na aanib la.
Uwumbɔr kpa mpɔɔn jer bijab mɔmɔk; waanijoom nyaŋ a.

english_text:
(A song and a psalm by the clan of Korah.)
The City of God
1The Lord God is wonderful!
He deserves all praise
in the city where he lives.
His holy mountain,
2 beautiful and majestic,
brings joy to all on earth.
Mount Zion, truly sacred,
is home for the Great King.
3God is there to defend it
and has proved to be
its protector.
4Kings joined forces
to attack the city,
5but when they saw it,
they were terrified
and ran away.
6They trembled all over
like women giving birth
7or like seagoing ships
wrecked by eastern winds.
8We had heard about it,
and now we have seen it
in the city of our God,
the Lord All-Powerful.
This is the city that God
will let stand forever.
9Our God, here in your temple
we think about your love.
10You are famous and praised
everywhere on earth,
as you win victories
with your powerful arm.
11Mount Zion will celebrate,
and all Judah will be glad,
because you bring justice.
12Let's walk around Zion
and count its towers.
13We will see its strong walls
and visit each fortress.
Then you can say
to future generations,
14“Our God is like this forever
and will always guide us.”
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aatiŋ Sionn
1Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ sakpen, ni ŋan ke ti li pak u mbamɔm,
waagongoln li bi chain na paab.
2Uwumbɔr aajool Sionn fɔk paacham, le ki ŋan;
Ubɔrkpaan ngbaan aatiŋ joo ni mpopiin le nan tii dulnyaa mɔmɔk.
3Uwumbɔr mɔk ke lifuur bi u chee,
waatiŋ ki bi maa ŋigon kiir ki na ponn ni.
4Bibɔrb nan kuun tɔb ki dan ke bi nan tak Sionn Aajool.
5Tɔ, baah nan kan li na,
le ni ŋa bi iwaan; ijawaan nan chuu bi, le bi san.
6Ijawaan ni falaa sakpiin le nan chuu bi nima chee,
ke upii u ban u maa ubo na,
7ki naahn buŋɔb aah yeŋni kitaabuŋ ni pu na.
8Ti ŋun Uwumbɔr aah tun pu na,
le dandana ma kan, tinimbil kani waatun, waatiŋ ni.
Uma le ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan;
u ga cha lifuur li bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni,
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
9Uwumbɔr, Saadichal ponn ni le ti dakl saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu.
10Binib bi bi ni mɔmɔk na pak si la,
le saayimbil yaa ki buen kitiŋ kee aapepel mɔmɔk ni.
Ibamɔn pu le aa joo saanib;
11Cha Sionn aanib li kpa mpopiin.
Aa ji tibɔr ni ibamɔn la; cha mpopiin li bi Juda aatim pu.
12Uwumbɔr aanib, chuun mann Sionn aatiŋ man,
ki kahn kaadifɔfɔŋ ngbaan;
13moo lik man kaagon ŋi bi maa gob ki na,
ni tidir ti kpa mpɔɔn na mbamɔm,
aan ki nan bui binib bi paa ni puwɔb na ke,
14“Uwumbɔr umina ye timi Aawumbɔr
le ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
Uma le ga mɔk timi nsan ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

english_text:
(A psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
Don't Depend on Wealth
1Everyone on this earth,
now listen to what I say!
2Listen, no matter who you are,
rich or poor.
3I speak words of wisdom,
and my thoughts make sense.
4I have in mind a mystery
that I will explain
while playing my harp.
5Why should I be afraid
in times of trouble,
when I am surrounded
by vicious enemies?
6They trust in their riches
and brag about
all their wealth.
7You cannot buy back your life
or pay off God!
8It costs far too much
to buy back your life.
You can never pay God enough
9to stay alive forever
and safe from death.
10 We see that wise people die,
and so do stupid fools.
Then their money is left
for someone else.
11The grave will be their home
forever and ever,
although they once had land
of their own.
12Our human glory disappears,
and, like animals, we die.
13Here is what happens to fools
and to those who trust
the words of fools:
14They are like sheep
with death as their shepherd,
leading them to the grave.
In the morning God's people
will walk all over them,
as their bodies lie rotting
in their home, the grave.
15But God will rescue me
from the power of death.
16Don't let it bother you
when others get rich
and live in luxury.
17Soon they will die
and all their wealth
will be left behind.
18We humans are praised
when we do well,
and all of us are glad
to be alive.
19But we each will go down
to our ancestors,
never again to see
the light of day.
20Our human glory disappears,
and, like animals, we die.
translation_text:
Aa yaa di naadii tii liwangol kan ni ye kijɔrk la
1Ni mɔmɔk li pel man tibɔr tee,
binib bi mɔmɔk bi ni kookoo na,
2binikpaam ni biwaatiib mɔmɔk,
biwankpadam ni bigiim mɔmɔk, li pel man.
3Nsui ga li nyoo pam; m ga len nlan aabɔr.
4M ga labr koo ŋiyataŋak ni la,
le ki di kibeek gbaa kpiir ŋaatataa.
5Linimaln ni, buyoonn maadim mann goln mi na kan,
maa san ijawaan;
6kaa san titunwanbirdam bi di naadii tii baawangol,
ki puur tipupuur baawankpal sakpeln ngbaan pu na ijawaan.
7Unii aan ŋmaa pa ki gaa ubaa aamɔfal;
waan ŋmaa pa Uwumbɔr waamɔfal pu,
8ba pu? unibɔn aamɔfal aadaak pɔɔ sakpen a.
Waah ga di tiwan ni pa na ga li par
9ke ni taa cha u koo likaakul ni,
ki tii u limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.
10Unii mɔk kani ke binib bi kpa nlan na mu kpoi,
ke bijɔrb ni bilatiirb na la.
Bi mɔmɔk kpoi le ki cha baawangol siini biyaabitiib.
11Baakaakul ga li ye bido ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na;
nima chee le bi ga li bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
bi mu nan tee kpa bibaa aatim n‑yoonn mubaa.
12Unii aawangol aan ŋmaa nyan u nkun ni;
u ga nan kpo ke kiwakork na la.
13Lik man tiwan ni ŋani binib bi tii bibaa naadii na,
lik man binib bi bui ke bi bab liwangol na aadoon,
14bi ga nan kpo ke ipiih na la, nkun le ga nan li ye u kpaa bi na.
Binib bi aabimbin ŋan na ga laa bi,
buyoonn biwon bi bur kitekpiitiŋ ki daa bido na ni.
15Le Uwumbɔr ga gaa mi lii, u ga nyan mi nkun aapɔɔn ni.
16Unii yaa kan liwangol kan, taa cha aasui bii,
hali ki ti saa buyoonn waawangol ngbaan moo kpee na;
17U yaa nan kpo kan, waan ŋmaa yoor li buen ubaa chee;
waawangol aan dii u koo likaakul ni.
18Hali unii yaa bui ke nibaa aa muk u
aan binib pak u kina pu kan,
19u ga nan ti pii uyaajatiib nkun ni,
nin chee mbɔmbɔɔn aan doo na.
20Unii aawangol aan ŋmaa nyan u nkun ni,
u ga nan kpo ke kiwakork na la.

english_text:
(A psalm by Asaph.)
What Pleases God
1From east to west,
the powerful Lord God
has been calling together
everyone on earth.
2God shines brightly from Zion,
the most beautiful city.
3Our God approaches,
but not silently;
a flaming fire comes first,
and a storm surrounds him.
4God comes to judge his people.
He shouts to the heavens
and to the earth,
5“Call my followers together!
They offered me a sacrifice,
and we made an agreement.”
6The heavens announce,
“God is the judge,
and he is always honest.”
7My people, I am God!
Israel, I am your God.
Listen to my charges
against you.
8Although you offer sacrifices
and always bring gifts,
9I won't accept your offerings
of bulls and goats.
10Every animal in the forest
belongs to me,
and so do the cattle
on a thousand hills.
11I know all the birds
in the mountains,
and every wild creature
is in my care.
12If I were hungry,
I wouldn't tell you,
because I own the world
and everything in it.
13I don't eat the meat of bulls
or drink the blood of goats.
14I am God Most High!
The only sacrifice I want
is for you to be thankful
and to keep your word.
15Pray to me in time of trouble.
I will rescue you,
and you will honor me.
16But to the wicked I say:
“You don't have the right
to mention my laws or claim
to keep our agreement!
17You refused correction
and rejected my commands.
18You made friends
with every crook you met,
and you liked people who break
their wedding vows.
19You talked only about violence
and told nothing but lies;
20you sat around gossiping,
ruining the reputation
of your own relatives.”
21When you did all this,
I didn't say a word,
and you thought,
“God is just like us!”
But now I will accuse you.
22You have ignored me!
So pay close attention
or I will tear you apart,
and no one can help you.
23The sacrifice that honors me
is a thankful heart.
Obey me, and I, your God,
will show my power to save.
translation_text:
Saah ga li dooni Uwumbɔr mbamɔm pu na
1Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len na;
u yin kitiŋ kee pu yaab mɔmɔk ki nyan liwipuul
ki ti saa liwilir wɔb.
2Uwumbɔr wiin Sionn aatiŋ ki ŋan sakpen na ni.
3Timi Aawumbɔr choo, le kifuuk dii u;
mmii mu gaal mpɔɔn pu na le loln u pu nsan,
le libuln li pɔɔ sakpen na mann goln u.
4U yin paacham, ni taab, ke ni nan li ye seeraadam
ki kan waah ga ji waanib tibɔr pu na.
5U bui ke, “Kuun ni maanib bi kpa gaakii
ki di kitork puu tipuur tii mi na tii ni mi.”
6Paacham len ke Uwumbɔr aabimbin ŋan, ke uma le ye ubɔjir.
7“Maanib, li pel man, aan m len tibɔr,
M ga kpiir sin Israel yaab pu.
Min le ye Uwumbɔr, m ye nimi Aawumbɔr la.
8Maa galni nimi kitork ni nimi aatork ki ni joo seer mmii ni tii mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu la,
9ki mu aa ban nimi aasar ponn ni aanaaja, ni iŋoob nimi aaŋoob ni;
10tiwakor timɔk bi kichook ni na ye min yaan la,
le inaa imɔk bi ŋigongon ŋichur ŋichur pu na mu ye min yaan.
11Min le yeh inyoon imɔk bi timoor ni na,
ni tiwan nimɔk fu ki bi tikpaasar ni na.
12Nkon yaa ba joo mi kan, maa ba ga tuk nimi, ba pu?
dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk, ni nimɔk bi u ni na ye min yaan la.
13M ŋmɔ inaaja aanann la aa? M nyu iŋoob aasin la aa?
14Cha man idoon baanja li ye kitork ki ni joo tii mi na,
ki tii mi Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan tiwan nimɔk
ni puu ke ni ga tii mi na.
15Tibɔr yaa dan kan,
ni yin mi le m ga gaa nimi lii aan ni ga pak mi.”
16Le Uwumbɔr bui bibiindam ma ke,
“Ba ŋa ni cha maakaal bi nimɔb ni?
Ba ŋa ni len maah puu tipuur ti na aabɔr?
17Ni yii, ke m taa mɔk nimi buyoonn ni yenn na;
ni yii maamɔbon.
18Ni yaa kan unaayuk umɔk na kan, le ni kpaan kpaln ujɔtiib,
le ki mu diir bidagoob.
19N‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, ni gor ki ban ke ni len tibɔbir la;
le ki mɔni inyamɔn n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
20Ni gor n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke ni galn nina aabim la,
ki ban ke ni kan baataani.
21Ni ŋani nimina mɔmɔk, le maa len tibaa,
kina pu le ni dakl ke m mu bi kina la.
Tɔ, dandana ma kan, m ban m galn nimi la,
ki nyan tibɔr ngbaan lipaal tii nimi.
22Nimi bi yii mi na, li pel man tibɔr tee,
naa ye kina kan, m ga ku doo nimi,
le ubaa aan li bi ki ga gaa nimi lii.
23Idoon le ye kitork ki ga nyuŋ mi na,
le m ga sil gaa binib bimɔk kii maamɔb na lii.”

english_text:
(For the music leader. A psalm by David when the prophet Nathan came to him after David had been with Bathsheba.)
A Prayer for Forgiveness
1 You are kind, God!
Please have pity on me.
You are always merciful!
Please wipe away my sins.
2Wash me clean from all
of my sin and guilt.
3I know about my sins,
and I cannot forget
the burden of my guilt.
4 You are really the one
I have sinned against;
I have disobeyed you
and have done wrong.
So it is right and fair for you
to correct and punish me.
5I have sinned and done wrong
since the day I was born.
6But you want complete honesty,
so teach me true wisdom.
7Wash me with hyssop
until I am clean
and whiter than snow.
8Let me be happy and joyful!
You crushed my bones,
now let them celebrate.
9Turn your eyes from my sin
and cover my guilt.
10Create pure thoughts in me
and make me faithful again.
11Don't chase me away from you
or take your Holy Spirit
away from me.
12Make me as happy as you did
when you saved me;
make me want to obey!
13I will teach sinners your Law,
and they will return to you.
14Keep me from any deadly sin.
Only you can save me!
Then I will shout and sing
about your power to save.
15Help me to speak,
and I will praise you, Lord.
16Offerings and sacrifices
are not what you want.
17The way to please you
is to be truly sorry
deep in our hearts.
This is the kind of sacrifice
you won't refuse.
18Please be willing, Lord,
to help the city of Zion
and to rebuild its walls.
19Then you will be pleased
with the proper sacrifices,
and we will offer bulls
on your altar once again.
translation_text:
Ubɔr David nan yoor Uria aapuu Batseba ki doon u chee, le Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Natann mɔk u waataani. Nee aapuwɔb le David naan nlahn mue.
1Uwumbɔr, san mi kinimbaak,
saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu.
Saanimbaasaln sakpeln pu, finn nyan maatunwanbir.
2Finn nyan maabɔbir mɔmɔk
ki cha m nyan maatunwanbir ni chain.
3M bee maataani mɔmɔk, n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan,
m nyi maatunwanbir bɔr.
4M tun si titunwanbir, sin baanja le m tun titunwanbir,
ki ŋani tiwan ni ye aa chee tibir na,
kina pu na, aa yaa jin mi tibɔr kan, ni ŋan,
aa kpa mbamɔn ke aa bui ke maabɔr bii.
5N‑yoonn mu bi ma mi na, le m kpa titunwanbir,
ki nyan nwiin mundaal bi ma mi na,
le m ye titunwanbirdaan.
6Saah ban pu na le ye mbimbinyaan, ni ibamɔn;
di saalan gbiin mi.
7Nyan mi maatunwanbir ni, aan m nya chain;
finn mi, aan m piir chain ke tikokonn na.
8Cha mpopiin ni mmɔɔn gbiin mi,
le saah kool mi doo pu na nsui ga ki piir.
9Taa cha aanimbil kan maatunwanbir,
ki finn nyan maabɔbir mɔmɔk.
10Uwumbɔr, naan nsui mu ŋan na tii mi,
ki di nsuupɔɔn mu ga kii saamɔb na tii mi.
11Taa jenn mi aanimbiin ni kookoo;
taa chuu nyan Saafuur Nyaan m chee.
12Gaa mi lii, aan m ki kan mpopiin,
ki cha m li ye unii u keei saamɔb na,
13le m ga mɔk titunwanbirdam saakaal aan bi fenn gir ni aa chee.
14Uwumbɔr, taa junn maamɔfal. Nya mi tibɔbir ni,
aan m di mpopiin moon saah kpa mbimbinyaan pu na.
15Uwumbɔr, ter mi aan m ŋmaa len ki pak si.
16Aa yaa ba ban kitork kan, m ba ga toor kitork tii si;
saa neen kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni tii si na.
17Uwumbɔr, saatork ki aa gee na le ye nsui mu sunn mubaa taab
ki ŋmaa kpiir mu aatunwanbir na.
18Uwumbɔr, san Sionn aanib kinimbaak ki ter bi,
ki gir maa Jerusalem aagon.
19N‑yoonn ngbaan le aasui ga piir kitork baamɔŋ,
ni timi aatork ki ti joo seer mmii ni tii si na pu,
le bi ga kɔr inaaja toor kitork saatork aabimbiln paab.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. He wrote this when Doeg from Edom went to Saul and said, “David has gone to Ahimelech's house.”)
God Is in Control
1 You people may be strong
and brag about your sins,
but God can be trusted
day after day.
2You plan brutal crimes,
and your lying words cut
like a sharp razor.
3You would rather do evil
than good, and tell lies
than speak the truth.
4You love to say cruel things,
and your words are a trap.
5God will destroy you forever!
He will grab you and drag you
from your homes.
You will be uprooted
and left to die.
6When good people see
this fearsome sight,
they will laugh and say,
7“Just look at them now!
Instead of trusting God,
they trusted their wealth
and their cruelty.”
8But I am like an olive tree
growing in God's house,
and I can count on his love
forever and ever.
9I will always thank God
for what he has done;
I will praise his good name
when his people meet.
translation_text:
Edom aaja Doeg nan tuk Ubɔr Sɔɔl ke David ni Ahimelek kpokl ban u, nee aapuwɔb le David naan nlahn mue.
1Unikpaan, ba ŋa aa kpa kipupuk saatunwanbir pu?
Uwumbɔr aageehm aa kpa ndoon.
2Aa ban isan ke aa kuln biken; saalambil ka ke kijukaŋ na la.
N‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, aa naani inyamɔn la.
3Aa gee titunwanbir ki jer litunyaan, ki gee inyamɔn jer mbamɔn.
4Sin unyamɔndaan, aa gee ke aa li joo saamɔbon bii biken aasui.
5Kina pu le Uwumbɔr ga kuln si, u ga yoor si ki nya saadichal ni.
U ga nyan si binib bi kpa limɔfal dulnyaa wee na ni.
6Binib bi aabimbin ŋan na ga kan kina,
le ijawaan ga chuu bi; le bi ga laa si ki bui ke,
7“Lik, uja u kaa nan di Uwumbɔr yin nibaa na sɔ,
u nan lik waawangol pu la,
ki dak ke mbiin le ga tii u lifuur ki gaa u lii.”
8Le mma bi ke olif aakpan aasub bu si Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na;
m kpa waageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu limakl.
9Uwumbɔr, m ga li dooni si n‑yoonn mɔmɔk
saah ŋa pu tii mi na pu.
Saanib aanimbil ni le m ga len ke aa ŋan.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. To the tune “Mahalath.”
)
No One Can Ignore God
1 Only a fool would say,
“There is no God!”
People like that are worthless!
They are heartless and cruel
and never do right.
2From heaven God
looks down to see
if anyone is wise enough
to search for him.
3But all of them
are crooked and corrupt.
Not one of them does right.
4Won't you lawbreakers learn?
You refuse to pray,
and you gobble up
the people of God.
5But you will be terrified
worse than ever before.
God will scatter the bones
of his enemies,
and you will be ashamed
when God rejects you.
6I long for someone from Zion
to come and save Israel!
Our God, when you bless
your people again,
Jacob's family will be glad,
and Israel will celebrate.
translation_text:
Unibɔn aabiin aah bi pu na
(Ilahn 14)
1Bijɔrb le bui bibaa ke, “Uwumbɔr aa bi.”
Bi mɔmɔk ye beebeedam la, le ki tun ŋitun ŋi kaa ŋan na;
ubaa aa bi ki tun lituln li ŋan na.
2Uwumbɔr bi paacham le ki lik ni unibɔn pu taab,
ke u lik ke bibaa bi ki kpa nlan ki dii u aan baa bi.
3Le bi mɔmɔk fenn bipuwɔb tii u, bi mɔmɔk aa ŋan.
Ubaa aa bi ki tun lituln li ŋan na, ubaa baanja aa bi.
4Le Uwumbɔr baa ke, “Baa nyi la aa?
Titunwanbirdam bee aa nyi la aa?
Bi su maanib kinaayuk le ki ji, le kaa dooni mi kpala.”
5Tɔ, ijawaan mu tee ga chuu bi, ke yaah kaa kee chuu bi pu na;
ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga di waanib aadim aakpab yaa.
Uwumbɔr yii bi, kina pu le Israel yaab ga nyaŋ bi kookoo.
6M mee Uwumbɔr ke linyaŋ ga nya ni Sionn
ki dan Israel yaab chee.
Uwumbɔr yaa tii Israel yaab nkam kan,
bi ga li kpa mpopiin sakpen.

english_text:
(For the music leader. Use with stringed instruments. A special psalm that David wrote when the people of Ziph went to Saul and said, “David is hiding here with us.”)
Trusting God in Times of Trouble
1 Save me, God, by your power
and prove that I am right.
2Listen to my prayer
and hear what I say.
3Cruel strangers have attacked
and want me dead.
Not one of them cares
about you.
4You will help me, Lord God,
and keep me from falling;
5you will punish my enemies
for their evil deeds.
Be my faithful friend
and destroy them.
6I will bring a gift
and offer a sacrifice
to you, Lord.
I will praise your name
because you are good.
7You have rescued me
from all my troubles,
and my own eyes have seen
my enemies fall.
translation_text:
Buyoonn Sif yaab nan tuk Ubɔr Sɔɔl ke David bɔr baapepel ponn ni na, le David naan nlahn mue.
1Uwumbɔr, di saapɔɔn gaa mi lii; di saapɔɔn sakpiin na nya mi.
2Uwumbɔr, ŋun maameel; pel maabɔr.
3Kigaadam le choo bi nan tak mi;
mbiindam bi aatafal aa bi sin Uwumbɔr ni na le ban bi ku mi.
4Uwumbɔr mu le ye u ter mi na. Uma Uwumbɔr le ye maakikiir.
5Uwumbɔr di maadim aatunwanbir giin daa bitafal.
U tun waah siin pu na, nima le u ga kuln bi.
6Uwumbɔr, m ga di mpopiin le toor kitork tii si,
saah ŋan pu na le ga cha m li dooni si.
7Aa nyan mi maabɔr mɔmɔk ni, le m kan maadim aah lir pu na.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. Use with stringed instruments.)
Betrayed by a Friend
1Listen, God, to my prayer!
Don't reject my request.
2Please listen and help me.
My thoughts are troubled,
and I keep groaning
3because my enemies attack
with loud shouts.
They treat me terribly
and hold angry grudges.
4My heart is racing fast,
and I am afraid of dying.
5I am trembling with fear,
completely terrified.
6I wish I had wings
like a dove,
so I could fly far away
and be at peace.
7I would go and live
in some distant desert.
8I would quickly find shelter
from howling winds
and raging storms.
9Confuse my enemies, Lord!
Upset their plans.
Cruelty and violence
are all I see in the city,
10and they are like guards
on patrol day and night.
The city is full of trouble,
evil, 11and corruption.
Troublemakers and liars
freely roam the streets.
12My enemies are not the ones
who sneer and make fun.
I could put up with that
or even hide from them.
13But it was my closest friend,
the one I trusted most.
14We enjoyed being together,
when we went with others
to your house, our God.
15All who hate me are controlled
by the power of evil.
Sentence them to death
and send them down alive
to the world of the dead.
16I ask for your help, Lord God,
and you will keep me safe.
17Morning, noon, and night
you hear my concerns
and my complaints.
18I am attacked from all sides,
but you will rescue me
unharmed by the battle.
19You have always ruled,
and you will hear me.
You will defeat my enemies
because they won't turn
and worship you.
20My friend turned against me
and broke his promise.
21His words were smoother
than butter, and softer
than olive oil.
But hatred filled his heart,
and he was ready to attack
with a sword.
22Our Lord, we belong to you.
We tell you what worries us,
and you won't let us fall.
23But what about those people
who are cruel and brutal?
You will throw them down
into the deepest pit
long before their time.
I trust you, Lord!
translation_text:
Uja aajɔ aah bii u aan u mee limeel li na
1Uwumbɔr, ŋun maameel,
taa fenn aapuwɔb tii maah gaŋni si pu na.
2Pel m chee ki kii maayim; maamuk cha nwon yɔl la.
3Ijawaan joo mi maadim aah faani mi pu na la,
bibiindam aamuk ku mi a.
Bi joo ni mi tibɔr la; baaŋuul fii m pu, le bi nan mi.
4Ijawaan le joo mi, le nkun aajawaan ku mi.
5Ijawaan chuu mi, le nwon jii, ijawaan nyaŋ mi a.
6M yaa ba kpa ifeen ke linanjel na,
m ba ga fii buen dandar, ki ti ban lifuur nima chee.
7M ba ga fii buen dandar,
ki ti maa maadichal nteersakpiin pu.
8M ba ga ŋa mala ki kan nin chee m ga di n‑yil peŋ na,
aan libupɔɔl ni kitaabuŋ taa pii mi.
9Uwumbɔr, cha maadim aalan ŋmal aan bi taa ŋmaa len.
M waa tijar, ni kifuuk, kitiŋ ngbaan ni;
10ni mann goln ki, nwiin pu ni kinyeek,
ki joo ni titunwanbir ni tibɔr.
11Libiil le bi ni kookoo,
limukl ni ŋŋmann le gbii ki ponn ni.
12Ni yaa ba ye ke maadin le laa mi kan, m ba ga ŋmaa joo ti;
ni yaa ba ye ke unii u kpak mi na le bi kpa kipupuk kan,
m ba ga ŋmaa di mbaa bɔr.
13Le ni tee ye sin njɔ la,
m ni u diir tɔb na, ki ye njɔ bamɔnn na.
14M ni uma nan gbaa tibaa aabɔr,
ki kpaani ki dooni Uwumbɔr waadichal ni.
15Cha maadim kpo aan baayoonn taa kee fuu;
cha bi laa li fu ki sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni.
Tibir bi bido, ni bisui ni la.
16Le m yin Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ke u ter mi, le u ga gaa mi lii.
17Maamuk ni maadun chaa u chee kichakpiik ni,
ni nwiin pu, ni kinyeek, le u ga ŋun maaneel pu.
18U ga giin ni mi butɔb bumɔk m ni maadim bi maa nyi bi mɔk na jaa na ni.
19Uwumbɔr u joo binib ki nyan dulnyaa aah piin buyoonn na
ga ŋun m pu ki nyaŋ bi,
ba pu? bi yii, kaa kpeln baabimbin, kaa san u mu.
20Maajan aajɔ le tak ujɔtiib, u bii waah puu tipuur ti na a.
21Waamɔbon nan mɔ ke tisiir na, le uponn ni ma tee to;
waamɔbon nan sɔŋni unii aasui ke nkpapem na,
le ki tee geei ke kijaak aajuk ki ka na.
22Di saamuk di tii Uwumbɔr, le u ga kiir si,
waan cha bi nyaŋ binib bi aabimbin ŋan na.
23Uwumbɔr, sin ma ga joo ni binikurb,
ni binyamɔndam ngbaan baakaakul ni
aan baamɔfal ligeln nin doo.
Mma kan, m ga di naadii tii sin la.

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “A Silent Dove in the Distance.”
A special psalm by David when the Philistines captured him in Gath.)
A Prayer of Trust in God
1 Have pity, God Most High!
My enemies chase me all day.
2Many of them are pursuing
and attacking me,
3but even when I am afraid,
I keep on trusting you.
4I praise your promises!
I trust you and am not afraid.
No one can harm me.
5Enemies spend the whole day
finding fault with me;
all they think about
is how to do me harm.
6They attack from ambush,
watching my every step
and hoping to kill me.
7They won't get away
with these crimes, God,
because when you get angry,
you destroy people.
8You have kept record
of my days of wandering.
You have stored my tears
in your bottle
and counted each of them.
9When I pray, Lord God,
my enemies will retreat,
because I know for certain
that you are with me.
10I praise your promises!
11I trust you and am not afraid.
No one can harm me.
12I will keep my promises
to you, my God,
and bring you gifts.
13You protected me from death
and kept me from stumbling,
so that I would please you
and follow the light
that leads to life.
translation_text:
Buyoonn Filistia yaab nan chuu David na, u naan nlahn mue la.
1Uwumbɔr, san mi kinimbaak, ba pu? binib ban mi ni linimaln la;
maadim muk mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la.
2Maadim tak mi kina le nwiin ti lir.
Binib bi tak mi na wiir sakpen a.
3Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan,
buyoonn ijawaan ti joo mi na le m kpa aa pu gaakii.
4M kpa Uwumbɔr pu gaakii le kaa san ijawaan;
m pak u waah puu tipuur ti na pu.
Unibɔn aan ŋmaa ŋa mi nibaa.
5Maadim ban tibɔr tii mi kina le nwiin ti lir;
n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, bi ban isan le ke bi tii mi titotonn.
6Bi kuuni tɔb le ki bɔrni ki lik maah ŋani tiwan ni mɔmɔk na,
ki mak ke bi ku mi.
7Uwumbɔr, daa bitafal, baatunwanbir pu,
nyaŋ binib ngbaan buyoonn saaŋuul fii na.
8Aa nyi naah muk mi pu na; aa nyi maanyunyunn aakahm,
aa ŋmee ti ŋa saagbaŋ ni.
9Bundaal m ti yin si na kan, maadim ga fenn bipuwɔb.
M nyi ke Uwumbɔr bi m chee.
10M pak waah puu tipuur ti na, 11m kpa uma pu le gaakii,
kaan li san ijawaan, unibɔn aan ŋmaa ŋa mi nibaa.
12Uwumbɔr, maah puu ke m ga tii si pu na, m ga ŋa kina;
m ga tii si maadoon aapiin;
13ba pu? sin le nyan mi nkun ni, kaa cha maadim nyaŋ mi.
Kina pu na, m bi Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni,
nwiihn mu wiin binib bi kpa limɔfal na ni la.

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
A special psalm by David when he was in the cave while running from Saul.)
Praise and Trust in Times of Trouble
1 God Most High, have pity on me!
Have mercy. I run to you
for safety.
In the shadow of your wings,
I seek protection
till danger dies down.
2I pray to you, my protector.
3You will send help from heaven
and save me,
but you will bring trouble
on my attackers.
You are faithful,
and you can be trusted.
4My enemies are fierce,
much worse than lions!
They have spears and arrows
instead of teeth,
and they have sharp swords
instead of tongues.
5May you, my God, be honored
above the heavens;
may your glory be seen
everywhere on earth.
6 Enemies set traps for my feet
and struck me down.
They dug a pit in my path,
but fell in it themselves.
7I am faithful to you,
and you can trust me.
I will sing and play music
for you, my God.
8I feel wide awake!
I will wake up my harp
and wake up the sun.
9I will praise you, Lord,
for everyone to hear,
and I will sing hymns to you
in every nation.
10Your love reaches higher
than the heavens;
your loyalty extends
beyond the clouds.
11May you, my God, be honored
above the heavens;
may your glory be seen
everywhere on earth.
translation_text:
David nan naan nlahn mue buyoonn u nan san nyan Ubɔr Sɔɔl chee ki koo kitakpaluŋ ni na.
1San mi kinimbaak, Uwumbɔr, san mi kinimbaak;
ba pu? m dan aa chee ki ban ŋŋmarm la.
Saafeen ponn ni le m kani lifuur
ki ti saa buyoonn ŋimuk sakpiin ga ti jer doo na.
2M yin Uwumbɔr u kpa mpɔɔn jer mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na.
M yin Uwumbɔr u tii mi maah ban tiwan nimɔk na.
3U ga li bi paacham le ki kii maayim ki gaa mi lii;
u ga nyaŋ binib bi muk mi na.
Uwumbɔr ga mɔk mi waageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na
ki ga ŋa waah puu ke u ga ŋa pu na.
4Maadim mann gonn mi la, bi naahn ichinn i ŋmɔ binib na la.
Baanyin naahn tikpaatunn ni ipiin la;
le baalambil bi ke kijaak aajum mu ka na.
5Uwumbɔr, mɔk saah pɔɔ sakpen pu na kitaapaak ni,
ki mɔk saapak kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu.
6Maadim di kipɔɔk le pen mi ke ki chuu mi;
ntaakpayɔl le nyaŋ mi.
Bi gbii libuul bil maasan ni, le ki labr lir li ponn ni bibaa.
7Uwumbɔr, m kpa limakl, m ga gaa ilahn ki pak si.
8M ga fii sil, m ga moo pel maabar,
m ga gaa ilahn lichakpitaawoln.
9Uwumbɔr, m ga doon si ŋitimbol ni; m ga pak si binib ni.
10Saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na fuur paacham;
le saaŋann taln ti fuu kitaapaak.
11Uwumbɔr, mɔk saah pɔɔ sakpen pu na kitaapaak ni,
ki mɔk saapak kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
)
A Prayer When All Goes Wrong
1Do you mighty people talk
only to oppose justice?
Don't you ever judge fairly?
2You are always planning evil,
and you are brutal.
3You have done wrong and lied
from the day you were born.
4Your words spread poison
like the bite of a cobra
5that refuses to listen
to the snake charmer.
6My enemies are fierce
as lions, Lord God!
Shatter their teeth.
Snatch out their fangs.
7Make them disappear
like leaking water,
and make their arrows miss.
8Let them dry up like snails
or be like a child that dies
before seeing the sun.
9Wipe them out quicker
than a pot can be heated
by setting thorns on fire.
10Good people will be glad
when they see the wicked
getting what they deserve,
and they will wash their feet
in their enemies' blood.
11Everyone will say, “It's true!
Good people are rewarded.
God does indeed rule the earth
with justice.”
translation_text:
Limeel li ban ke Uwumbɔr daa bibiindam aatafal na
1Nimi bibɔjirb, ni kee jin tibɔr ibamɔn ni ii?
Ni ji binib mɔmɔk aabɔr mbamɔm aa?
2Aayii. Ni dak titunwanbir ti ni ga ŋmaa ŋa na pu baanja la,
le ki tun mpɔɔn aatunwanbir kitiŋ kee pu.
3Titunwanbirdam tun tiwan ni kaa ŋan na le baamɔfal aayoonn mɔmɔk;
bundaal bi ma bi na le bi piin ki geei inyamɔn.
4Bi kpa liluul ke iwaa na la, le ki ŋeeb bitafal
5ke saapa u kaan ŋun binib bi ŋmanni iwaa ki chur i na aaneel na, ni kina aanib bi kpa nlan na aaneel.
6Uwumbɔr, kool ichinnbir ngbaan aanyin.
7Cha bi wɔŋ ke nnyun mu bi foor na;
cha bi yɔl ke timoor ti dɔ nsan ni na.
8Cha bi li bi ke naawor mam bi bunn ki kpaln kijɔŋjɔŋ na.
Cha bi taa kan nwiin ke ubo u kpo una aaponn ni ki nyan ni na.
9Bi ga per bi ke timoor na, aan bi nin bee;
Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln ponn ni le u pii bi libuln buen aan bi beenin fu.
10Uwumbɔr yaa daa mbiindam aatafal kan,
le ni piir binib bi aabimbin ŋan na aasui,
le bi ga lul bibiindam aasin ponn ni ki jer.
11Le binib ga bui ke,
“Uwumbɔr sil pa binib bi aabimbin ŋan na tipar;”
ki ki len ke, “Uwumbɔr u ji dulnyaa yaab tibɔr na sil bi.”

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
A special psalm by David when Saul had David's house watched so that he could kill him.)
A Prayer for Protection
1 Save me, God! Protect me
from enemy attacks!
2Keep me safe from brutal people
who want to kill me.
3Merciless enemies, Lord,
are hiding and plotting,
hoping to kill me.
I have not hurt them
in any way at all.
4But they are ready to attack.
Do something! Help me!
Look at what's happening.
5 Lord God All-Powerful,
you are the God of Israel.
Punish the other nations
and don't pity those terrible
and rebellious people.
6My enemies return at evening,
growling like dogs
roaming the city.
7They curse, and their words
cut like swords,
as they say to themselves,
“No one can hear us!”
8You, Lord, laugh at them
and sneer at the nations.
9You are my mighty fortress,
and I depend on you.
10You love me and will let me
see my enemies defeated.
11Don't kill them,
or everyone may forget!
Just use your mighty power
to make them tremble
and fall.
You are a shield
for your people.
12My enemies are liars!
So let them be trapped
by their boastful lies.
13Get angry and destroy them.
Leave them in ruin.
Then all the nations will know
that you rule in Israel.
14Those liars return at evening,
growling like dogs
roaming the city.
15They search for scraps of food,
and they snarl
until they are stuffed.
16But I will sing about
your strength, my God,
and I will celebrate
because of your love.
You are my fortress,
my place of protection
in times of trouble.
17I will sing your praises!
You are my mighty fortress,
and you love me.
translation_text:
Ubɔr Sɔɔl nan tun bijab bibaa, ke bi ti li kii David aadichal, aan bi ku u, le David naan nlahn mue.
1Maawumbɔr, gaa mi maadim chee lii;
li kii mi aan binib bi tak mi na taa pii mi.
2Gaa mi titunwanbirdam chee lii;
Chuu gaa mi binikurb chee lii.
3Uwumbɔr, lik baah dɔ kii mi pu ke bi ku mi na;
bibiindam le bi kuuni ki ban mi.
Naa ye ke m tun titunwanbir, bee taani ubaa la,
4kaa ki ye maataani pu le bi san ban bi tak mi.
5Ndindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, fii sil ki nan ter mi;
Israel yaab Aawumbɔr, si aabaa waa.
Fii sil ki daa binib bi kaa dii saasan na aatafal.
Taa san titunwanbirdam bi fii sil aa pu na kinimbaak.
6Kijook kan, le bi gir ni,
ki san gbii ŋinyin ke ibɔ na kitiŋ ponn ni.
7Li pel baah seei ki faani pu na.
Baanyin bi ke kijaak aajum na le bimɔi ni,
le ki dak ke ubaa aa pel bi chee la.
8Uwumbɔr, le sin ma laa bi;
aa ŋani binib bi kaa dii saasan na mbɔnyun la.
9M kpa limakl saapɔɔn pu;
Uwumbɔr, sin le ye maabɔbɔryaan.
10Maawumbɔr gee mi, ki ga nan ter mi;
u ga cha m kan maadim aah ga lir pu na.
11Uwumbɔr, taa ku bi ki cha maanib suln baatafadaan bɔr.
Uwumbɔr u kii timi na, di saapɔɔn yaa bi ki nyaŋ bi.
12Tibɔbir bi bimɔi ni, le baamɔbon mɔmɔk ye tibɔbir la;
cha baagaak di bi koon tibɔr ni,
Baah puuni ki geei inyamɔn pu na,
13kuln bi pel pel saaŋuul ponn ni.
Kina kan, unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke Uwumbɔr le joo Israel aanib,
ki joo unii mɔmɔk kitiŋ kee pu.
14Kijook le maadim gir ni,
ki san gbii ŋinyin ke ibɔ na kitiŋ ponn ni;
15bi san kpak ke ibɔ i chuu kpak ban tijikaar na la,
i yaa kaa jin bab kan, le i ŋuuni.
16Le mma ga gaa ilahn ki mɔk saah pɔɔ pu na;
saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu,
m ga gaa ilahn mpɔɔn pu kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni.
Aa chee le m bɔrni,
linimaln aayoonn kan, aa chee le m bɔrni.
17Maakikiir, m ga pak si. Maabɔbɔryaan le ye Uwumbɔr,
Uwumbɔr u gee mi na.

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “Lily of the Promise.” A special psalm by David for teaching. He wrote it during his wars with the Arameans of northern Syria,
when Joab came back and killed twelve thousand Edomites
in Salt Valley.)
You Can Depend on God
1 You, God, are angry with us!
We are rejected and crushed.
Make us strong again!
2You made the earth shake
and split wide open;
now heal its wounds
and stop its trembling.
3You brought hard times
on your people,
and you gave us wine
that made us stagger.
4You gave a signal to those
who worship you,
so they could escape
from enemy arrows.
5Answer our prayers, God!
Use your powerful arm
and give us victory.
Then the people you love
will be safe.
6Our God, you solemnly promised,
“I would gladly divide up
the city of Shechem
and give away Succoth Valley
piece by piece.
7The lands of Gilead
and Manasseh are mine.
Ephraim is my war helmet,
and Judah is the symbol
of my royal power.
8Moab is merely my washbasin.
Edom belongs to me,
and I shout in triumph
over the Philistines.”
9Our God, who will bring me
to the fortress,
or lead me to Edom?
10Have you rejected us
and deserted our armies?
11Help us defeat our enemies!
No one else can rescue us.
12You will give us victory
and crush our enemies.
translation_text:
Ubɔr David nan to Siria yaab bi nyan ni Naharaim ni Soba aatim ni na butɔb, le waajab aaninkpel Joab gir ki nan ku Edom aatiŋ aajab ŋichur kipiik ni ŋilee, n‑yaan aafataŋ ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan le David naan nlahn ngbaan, ke u mɔk waanib.
1Uwumbɔr, aa yii timi, le ki nyaŋ timi;
aa nan gee liŋuul ti pu, dandana ma kan, gir gaa timi.
2Aa cha kitiŋ jii, le ki cha ki gii ki taa nween;
dandana ma kan, toor ki, ba pu? ki bi lir la.
3Aa cha saanib jin falaa sakpen a.
Ti chuun gbeer ke taah nyun ndaan le na.
4Aa sak binib bi san si na, aan baadim taa nyaŋ bi.
5Ŋun timi aameel, di saapɔɔn gaa timi lii,
aan saah gee binib bi na ŋmar.
6Uwumbɔr bi waadichal li bi chain na ni ki len ke,
“M ga di linyaŋ yakr Sekem aatiŋ
ki yakr Sukof aafataŋ tii maanib.
7Gilead ni Manase aatim ye min yaan la;
Efraim aatiŋ le ye maakur aayikpupuk,
le Juda ye maabɔr aajaangbeek.
8Moab aatiŋ le ga li ye maasapeek.
M ga di maanaatak di mee paan Edom pu,
ki mɔk ke ki ye mbaa aatiŋ la.
M nyaŋ Filistia aatiŋ le ki teen mpɔɔn pu.”
9Uwumbɔr, ŋmaa ga di mi buen
kitiŋ ki bi maa ŋigon gob ki na ponn ni?
Ŋma ga cheen mi Edom aatiŋ ponn ni?
10Aa sil yii timi la aa?
Saan ki dii timi aajab buen butɔb ni ii?
11Ter timi, timi aadim chee; unibɔn aaterm aa ye nibaa.
12Uwumbɔr yaa bi ti chee kan, ti ga nyaŋ,
u ga nyaŋ timi aadim.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use with stringed instruments.)
Under the Protection of God
1Please listen, God,
and answer my prayer!
2I feel hopeless,
and I cry out to you
from a faraway land.
Lead me to the mighty rock
high above me.
3You are a strong tower,
where I am safe
from my enemies.
4Let me live with you forever
and find protection
under your wings, my God.
5You heard my promises,
and you have blessed me,
just as you bless everyone
who worships you.
6Let the king have a long
and healthy life.
7May he always rule
with you, God, at his side;
may your love and loyalty
watch over him.
8I will sing your praises
forever, God, and will always
keep my promises.
translation_text:
Nkiirm aameel
1Uwumbɔr, ŋun maawiil, li pel maameel.
2Buyoonn maa bi linampal aan nsui bii na, le m yin si.
Di mi buen mbɔbɔryaan mu ŋan na chee,
3ba pu? sin le ye u kii mi na,
ki ye u pɔɔ ki kii mi maadim chee na.
4Cha m li bi saadichal ni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
cha m bɔr aaŋmaŋ ni ki ŋmar.
5Uwumbɔr, aa ŋun maah puu tipuur ti na,
le ki tii mi binib bi nyuŋni si na aawan.
6Moo di ŋibin kpee ubɔr aamɔfal pu;
cha u li bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
7Uwumbɔr, cha u li bi aanimbiin ni ki joo waanib n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
li joo saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, ni saaŋann na kii u.
8Le m ga li gaa ilahn ki pak si
n‑yoonn mumɔk m tii si maah puu pu iwiin mɔmɔk aatork ni na.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for Jeduthun, the music leader.)
God Is Powerful and Kind
1Only God can save me,
and I calmly wait for him.
2God alone is the mighty rock
that keeps me safe
and the fortress
where I am secure.
3I feel like a shaky fence
or a sagging wall.
How long will all of you
attack and assault me?
4You want to bring me down
from my place of honor.
You love to tell lies,
and when your words are kind,
hatred hides in your heart.
5Only God gives inward peace,
and I depend on him.
6God alone is the mighty rock
that keeps me safe,
and he is the fortress
where I feel secure.
7God saves me and honors me.
He is that mighty rock
where I find safety.
8Trust God, my friends,
and always tell him
each of your concerns.
God is our place of safety.
9We humans are only a breath;
none of us are truly great.
All of us together weigh less
than a puff of air.
10Don't trust in violence
or depend on dishonesty
or rely on great wealth.
11I heard God say two things:
“I am powerful,
12 and I am very kind.”
The Lord rewards each of us
according to what we do.
translation_text:
Li mak Uwumbɔr aakiirm ni
1M jin limɔr le ki kii Uwumbɔr ke u gaa mi lii;
uma baanja pu le m ga ŋmaa nyii ki sil.
2Uma baanja le kii ki gaal mi lir;
uma le kii mi, le ubaa aan ŋmaa nyaŋ mi.
3Ni mɔmɔk ga li tak unii, ni ti yunn kinye?
unii u bi ke ligoln li taa taa iween na.
4Ni ban ke ni nyan u waah bi nin chee ki kpa kipak na,
le ki jinn u inimɔɔn; ni geei inyamɔn le ni mɔ nimi.
Ni len tinyoor aabɔlen la,
le nisui ponn ni ma kan, ni puuni lir u pu.
5Uwumbɔr baanja pu le m nyii ki bi; m kpa u pu limakl.
6Uma baanja le kii mi, ki gaal mi lir;
uma le kii mi, le ubaa aan ŋmaa nyaŋ mi.
7Maaŋmarm ni maapak bi Uwumbɔr chee la;
u pɔɔ le ki ye u kii mi na; u ye maabɔbɔryaan la.
8Maanib, tii Uwumbɔr naadii n‑yoonn mɔmɔk man.
Bui u nimi aamuk mɔmɔk man,
ba pu? uma le ye timi aabɔbɔryaan.
9Unibɔn naahn litakpiln libaa aabuln la;
binikpaam ni biwaatiib mɔmɔk aa kpa tinyoor.
Di bi tɔŋ likakl pu, le aa ga bee ke baa nyuun kpala,
libuln nyuun jer bi.
10Taa tii mbimbinpɔɔl naadii;
taa li mak ke nnaayupɔɔn ga tii si tinyoor tibaa;
hali saawangol yaa moo kpae kan, taa li ka nyiibaa li pu.
11M ŋun ni jer nfum mubaa Uwumbɔr len ke mpɔɔn ye uyaan la,
12ki ki len ke waageehm bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
Uwumbɔr, si aabaa le pa unii waatuln aah ŋeer pu na.

english_text:
(A psalm by David when he was in the desert of Judah.)
God's Love Means More than Life
1 You are my God. I worship you.
In my heart, I long for you,
as I would long for a stream
in a scorching desert.
2I have seen your power
and your glory
in the place of worship.
3Your love means more
than life to me,
and I praise you.
4As long as I live,
I will pray to you.
5I will sing joyful praises
and be filled with excitement
like a guest at a banquet.
6I think about you, God,
before I go to sleep,
and my thoughts turn to you
during the night.
7You have helped me,
and I sing happy songs
in the shadow of your wings.
8I stay close to you,
and your powerful arm
supports me.
9All who want to kill me
will end up in the ground.
10Swords will run them through,
and wild dogs will eat them.
11Because of you, our God,
the king will celebrate
with your faithful followers,
but liars will be silent.
translation_text:
Ubɔr David nan naan nlahn mue buyoonn u nan bi Judea aateersakpiin ni na.
1Uwumbɔr, sin le ye Maawumbɔr, le m neen si.
Nsui, ni nwon mɔmɔk ban si ke kitiŋ ki kuur,
ki laa itiween, kaa kpa nnyun na aah ban nnyun pu na la.
2Cha m kan si saadichal ni,
cha m kan saah kpa mpɔɔn, ni kipak pu na.
3Saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na ŋan jer limɔfal,
kina pu le m ga pak si.
4Maah bi limɔfal ponn ni n‑yoonn mumɔk na,
le m ga li dooni si,
m ga yoor ŋŋaal paacham ki li mee si.
5M ga bab ke maah jin tijikaar ti ŋan sakpen na le na,
le m ga gaa mpopiin aalahn ki pak si.
6M yaa dɔ tiwandookaan pu kan, m teer aabɔr la;
kinyeek mɔmɔk kan, m dak sin pu la;
7ba pu? sin le ter mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
Aaŋmaŋ taab le m ga gaa mpopiin aalahn.
8M bub joo si la, le aaŋaal tii mi ŋŋmarm.
9Binib bi ban ke bi ku mi na ga sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni.
10Butɔb ponn ni le bi ga ku bi, le takɔ mam ŋmɔ biwon.
11Uwumbɔr aah tii ubɔr linyaŋ pu na, le u ga li mɔɔni.
Binib bi puur tipuur Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu na ga pak u,
le binyamɔndam ma aamɔi ga ŋmin.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
Celebrate because of the Lord
1Listen to my concerns, God,
and protect me
from my enemies' threats.
2Keep me safe from secret plots
of corrupt and evil gangs.
3Their words cut like swords,
and their cruel remarks
sting like sharp arrows.
4They fearlessly ambush
and shoot innocent people.
5They are determined to do evil,
and they tell themselves,
“Let's set traps!
No one can see us.”
6They make evil plans and say,
“We'll commit a perfect crime.
No one knows our thoughts.”
7But God will shoot his arrows
and quickly wound them.
8They will be destroyed
by their own words,
and everyone who sees them
will tremble with fear.
9They will be afraid and say,
“Look at what God has done
and keep it all in mind.”
10May the Lord bless his people
with peace and happiness
and let them celebrate.
translation_text:
Limeel li ban nkiirm na
1Uwumbɔr, m bi tibɔr ni la, ŋun maameel.
M san maadim ijawaan la, gaa maamɔfal lii.
2Li kiir mi aan bibiindam aah gor kiir mi pu na taa pii mi,
nyan mi titunwanbirdam bi wiir na ni.
3Bi luuni baalambil ŋi ka ke kijaak aajum na la,
le ki len tibɔbir ti tok kaa yenni ke ipiin na.
4Bi mooni baanyamɔn kaa san inimɔɔn kpala;
bi joo inyamɔn le kulni bininyaam.
5Bi pɔɔni tɔb aataakpab, baalandak i kaa ŋan na ponn ni,
bi kpokl nin chee bi ga pen baagaawɔb mam na la.
Bi len le ke, “Ubaa aan kan timi.”
6Bi kpokl ilandak i kaa ŋan na, le ki bui ke,
“Ti kpokl titunwanbir aalandak i ŋan sakpen a.”
Saan ŋmaa bee unibɔn aasui, ni waalandak aatataa.
7Le Uwumbɔr too bi waapiin,
libuul ngbaan ni le bi kani titotonn.
8Baamɔbon ngbaan pu le u ga kuln bi;
le binib bimɔk kan bi na ga gbɔk biyil.
9Bi mɔmɔk ga san ijawaan;
bi ga li dak Uwumbɔr aah tun pu na
le ki tuk binib waabimbin aah bi pu na.
10Binib bimɔk aabimbin ŋan na ga li mɔɔni
Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu na pu.
Bi ga kan u chee ŋŋmarm; bininyaam mɔmɔk ga pak u.

english_text:
(A psalm by David and a song for the music leader.)
God Answers Prayer
1Our God, you deserve praise
in Zion, where we keep
our promises to you.
2Everyone will come to you
because you answer prayer.
3When our sins get us down,
you forgive us.
4You bless your chosen ones,
and you invite them
to live near you
in your temple.
We will enjoy your house,
the sacred temple.
5Our God, you save us,
and your fearsome deeds answer
our prayers for justice!
You give hope to people
everywhere on earth,
even those across the sea.
6You are strong,
and your mighty power
put the mountains in place.
7You silence the roaring waves
and the noisy shouts
of the nations.
8People far away marvel
at your fearsome deeds,
and all who live under the sun
celebrate and sing
because of you.
9You take care of the earth
and send rain to help the soil
grow all kinds of crops.
Your rivers never run dry,
and you prepare the earth
to produce abundant grain.
10You water all its fields
