and level the lumpy ground.
You send showers of rain
to soften the soil
and help the plants sprout.
11Wherever your footsteps
touch the earth,
a rich harvest is gathered.
12Desert pastures blossom,
and mountains celebrate.
13Meadows are filled
with sheep and goats;
valleys overflow with grain
and echo with joyful songs.
translation_text:
Kipak ni idoon
1Uwumbɔr, ni ŋan ke ti pak si Sionn aatiŋ ni,
ki li joo taah puu tipuur ti tii si na,
2ba pu? aa keei limeel mɔmɔk.
3Binib ga nya ni kookoo ki dan aa chee, baatunwanbir pu.
Timi aataani nyaŋ timi la,
le aa ma joo cha pinni timi aataani.
4Saah lee binib bi ke bi li koo saadichal ni na kpa mpopiin.
Tiwanyaan ni bi saadichal ponn ni,
ki ye Lidichal ngbaan aanyoor na ga tii timi mpopiin.
5Saah tii timi linyaŋ li na le ye ke aa keei timi aayim,
le ki tun lijinjiir aawan ki gaal timi lir.
Dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni aanib,
ni binib bi bi nnyusakpem aapuwɔb na tii si naadii.
6Saapɔɔn pu le aa di ŋijoo siin ŋaabuu ni,
ki mɔk saapɔɔn sakpiin.
7Aa cha nnyusakpem ŋmini chii;
ki cha mu aanyunkpenn ŋmini chii;
binib yaa faa kifuuk kan, le aa ŋmin bi chii.
8Saah tun ŋitun sakpiin ŋi na cha dulnyaa mɔmɔk san si la.
Saabimbin joo ni mpopiin, le ki nyan ni kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu.
9Saah gee kitiŋ pu na, le aa cha utaal nu;
aa cha ki nyuun le ki kpa tijikaar.
Aa cha nnyun gbiini ikpen; aa tii kitiŋ tijikaar.
Saah ŋani ni pu na sɔ:
10Aa cha utaal nu ikpaakon i bi toor bil na ponn ni pam,
le i sɔŋ mbamɔm.
Aa cha titaapupur sɔŋni kitiŋ,
ki cha tijikaar ti laa punn na muuni.
11Saaŋann tii tinyoor sakpen a.
Aa yaa buen nimɔk na kan, nkam le bi.
12Kimopɔɔk mɔmɔk ni ye tiwakor ŋmeen la;
le ŋigongon mɔmɔk pu ye mpopiin ŋmeen.
13Ipiih le gbii nkpaatan aatiŋ ni;
tifatann mɔmɔk ni ye njikaabim la.
Tiwan mɔmɔk tar le ki gaa mpopiin aalahn.

english_text:
(A song and a psalm for the music leader.)
Shout Praises to God
1Tell everyone on this earth
to shout praises to God!
2Sing about his glorious name.
Honor him with praises.
3Say to God, “Everything you do
is fearsome,
and your mighty power makes
your enemies come crawling.
4You are worshiped by everyone!
We all sing praises to you.”
5Come and see the fearsome things
our God has done!
6 When God made the sea dry up,
our people walked across,
and because of him,
we celebrated there.
7His mighty power rules forever,
and nothing the nations do
can be hidden from him.
So don't turn against God.
8All of you people,
come praise our God!
Let his praises be heard.
9God protects us from death
and keeps us steady.
10Our God, you tested us,
just as silver is tested.
11You trapped us in a net
and gave us heavy burdens.
12You sent war chariots
to crush our skulls.
We traveled through fire
and through floods,
but you brought us
to a land of plenty.
13I will bring sacrifices
into your house, my God,
and I will do what I promised
14when I was in trouble.
15I will sacrifice my best sheep
and offer bulls and goats
on your altar.
16All who worship God,
come here and listen;
I will tell you everything
God has done for me.
17I prayed to the Lord,
and I praised him.
18If my thoughts had been sinful,
he would have refused
to hear me.
19But God did listen
and answered my prayer.
20Let's praise God!
He listened when I prayed,
and he is always kind.
translation_text:
Kipak ni idoon aalahn
1Binib mɔmɔk, di mpopiin pak Uwumbɔr mpɔɔn pu man.
2Gaa ilahn ki nyuŋ waayimbil, ki tii u kinyuŋ aapak.
3Bui Uwumbɔr ke, “Saah ŋa tiwan ni na nyaŋ a.
Saapɔɔn nyaŋ, le saadim san ijawaan ki gbaani aanimbiin ni.
4Unii umɔk bi kitiŋ kee pu na dooni si la;
bi gaa ilahn ki pak si; bi gaa ilahn ki pak saayimbil.”
5Dan ki nan lik man
Uwumbɔr aah ŋa waatusakpeln li binib ponn ni na.
6U cha nnyusakpem kpaln kitikuun;
tiyaajatiib chuun bitaa pu le ki puur limɔɔl.
Nima chee le ti nan mɔɔni waah tun pu na pu.
7U joo waapɔɔn lik binib pu
ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na,
ki cha unimbil paa ŋitimbol mɔmɔk pu.
Taa cha ubaa nya upuwɔb.
8Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk, pak timi Aawumbɔr man;
cha unii mɔmɔk ŋun nimi aapak pu.
9Uma le cha ti kpa limɔfal kaa cha ti lir.
10Uwumbɔr, aa tɔŋ timi;
baah pu tikunabr mmii ni pu ki nyani tijɔŋ na,
kina le aa tɔŋ timi.
11Aa cha ti lir gaawɔb mam ponn ni
ki di ŋitun ŋi nyuun na paan ti pu.
12Aa cha timi aadim taa taa ti pu;
ti chuun mmii ni nwam ponn ni,
le dandana ma aa joo ni timi nan kaan lifuur ponn ni.
13M ga joo ni kitork ki bi ga di see mmii ni na saadichal ni,
m ga tii si maah puu pu na.
14Maah nan bi tibɔr ni ki bui ke m ga tii si pu na, m ga tii si ni.
15M ga tii ipiih aan bi di see mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln paab;
m ga toor inaaja ni iŋoob aatork,
le yaaŋmanyuu fii buen kitaapaak.
16Binib bi mɔmɔk nyuŋ Uwumbɔr na, dan ki nan pel man,
aan m bui nimi waah tun pu tii mi na.
17M nan wii ki ban nterm u chee; m di ilahn pak u.
18M yaa nan ba di maatunwanbir bɔr nsui ni kan,
Uwumbɔr aa ba ga pel m chee.
19Tɔ, Uwumbɔr tee pel m chee; u pel maameel.
20M pak Uwumbɔr, ba pu? waa yii maameel,
kaa munn mi waageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.

english_text:
(A psalm and a song for the music leader. Use with stringed instruments.)
Tell the Nations To Praise God
1Our God, be kind and bless us!
Be pleased and smile.
2Then everyone on earth
will learn to follow you,
and all nations will see
your power to save us.
3Make everyone praise you
and shout your praises.
4Let the nations celebrate
with joyful songs,
because you judge fairly
and guide all nations.
5Make everyone praise you, God,
and shout your praises.
6Our God has blessed the earth
with a wonderful harvest!
7Pray for his blessings
to continue
and for everyone on earth
to worship our God.
translation_text:
Idoon aalahn
1Uwumbɔr, san timi kinimbaak ki ŋa saanyoor ŋa ti pu,
2aan dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk li nyi saah gee timi pu na,
aan ŋitimbol mɔmɔk kan saaŋmarm.
3Uwumbɔr, cha binib pak si; cha binib mɔmɔk pak si.
4Cha ŋitimbol li kpa mpopiin ki gaa mpopiin aalahn;
ba pu? aa joo ibamɔn le ji binib tibɔr,
le ki mɔk litimbol mɔmɔk kitiŋ kee pu saasan.
5Uwumbɔr, cha binib pak si; cha binib mɔmɔk pak si.
6Kitiŋ nyan kaajikaar;
Uwumbɔr, timi Aawumbɔr ŋa waanyoor ŋa ti pu.
7Uwumbɔr ŋa waanyoor ŋa ti pu;
Cha binib bi bi ni kookoo na nyuŋ u.

english_text:
(A psalm and a song by David for the music leader.)
God Will Win the Battle
1Do something, God!
Scatter your hateful enemies.
Make them turn and run.
2Scatter them like smoke!
When you come near,
make them melt
like wax in a fire.
3But let your people be happy
and celebrate because of you.
4Our God, you are the one
who rides on the clouds,
and we praise you.
Your name is the Lord,
and we celebrate
as we worship you.
5Our God, from your sacred home
you take care of orphans
and protect widows.
6You find families
for those who are lonely.
You set prisoners free
and let them prosper,
but all who rebel will live
in a scorching desert.
7You set your people free,
and you led them
through the desert.
8 God of Israel,
the earth trembled,
and rain poured down.
You alone are the God
who rules from Mount Sinai.
9When your land was thirsty,
you sent showers
to refresh it.
10Your people settled there,
and you were generous
to everyone in need.
11You gave the command, Lord,
and a chorus of women told
what had happened:
12“Kings and their armies
retreated and ran,
and everything they left
is now being divided.
13And for those who stayed back
to guard the sheep,
there are metal doves
with silver-coated wings
and shiny gold feathers.”
14God All-Powerful, you scattered
the kings like snow falling
on Mount Zalmon.
15Our Lord and our God,
Bashan is a mighty mountain
covered with peaks.
16Why is it jealous of Zion,
the mountain you chose
as your home forever?
17When you, Lord God, appeared
to your people at Sinai,
you came with thousands
of mighty chariots.
18 When you climbed
the high mountain,
you took prisoners with you
and were given gifts.
Your enemies didn't want you
to live there,
but they gave you gifts.
19We praise you, Lord God!
You treat us with kindness
day after day,
and you rescue us.
20You always protect us
and save us from death.
21Our Lord and our God,
your terrible enemies
are ready for war,
but you will crush
their skulls.
22You promised to bring them
from Bashan
and from the deepest sea.
23Then we could wash our feet
in their blood,
and our dogs could chew
on their bones.
24We have seen crowds marching
to your place of worship,
our God and King.
25Singers come first,
and then the musicians,
surrounded by young women
playing tambourines.
26They come shouting,
“People of Israel,
praise the Lord God!”
27The small tribe of Benjamin
leads the way,
followed by the leaders
from Judah.
Then come the leaders
from Zebulun and Naphtali.
28Our God, show your strength!
Show us once again.
29Then kings will bring gifts
to your temple
in Jerusalem.
30Punish that animal
that lives in the swamp!
Punish that nation
whose leaders and people
are like wild bulls.
Make them come crawling
with gifts of silver.
Scatter those nations
that enjoy making war.
31Force the Egyptians to bring
gifts of bronze;
make the Ethiopians hurry
to offer presents.
32Now sing praises to God!
Every kingdom on earth,
sing to the Lord!
33Praise the one who rides
across the ancient skies;
listen as he speaks
with a mighty voice.
34Tell about God's power!
He is honored in Israel,
and he rules the skies.
35The God of Israel is fearsome
in his temple,
and he makes us strong.
Let's praise our God!
translation_text:
Litimbol aanyaŋ aalahn
1Uwumbɔr fii sil ki cha waadim yaa tɔb chee.
Binib bi kaa gee u na lir le ki san.
2Libuln aah daar iŋmanyuu cha pu na, kina le u jenni bi cha;
nsiigban aah donni mmii chee pu na,
kina le bibiindam kulni Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni.
3Le bininyaam ma kpa mpopiin ki mɔɔni unimbiin ni,
bi kpa mpopiin le ki tar mmɔɔn pu.
4Gaa ilahn tii Uwumbɔr man, gaa ilahn ki pak waayimbil man;
toor nsan tii Uwumbɔr u chuun ntaalangbam pu na man.
Waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr, cha nisui li piin unimbiin ni man.
5Uwumbɔr u bi waadichal li bi chain na ponn ni na lik nkpobim, le ki kii bikpopiib.
6U tii binib bi kaa kpa ubaa na nkookoo yaan,
le ki nyani biyom kooni mpopiin aafuur ni,
le binib bi yii waamɔb na ma
ga li bi kitiŋ ki kaa kpa nibaa na ponn ni.
7Uwumbɔr, saah nan cheen saanib buyoonn,
ki nan di bi bɔ dii nteersakpiin ni na,
8kitiŋ nan dam, le utaal nyan ni kitaapaak ki lir ni,
ba pu? Uwumbɔr u nan len Sainai Aajool pu na le nan choo,
Israel yaab Aawumbɔr le nan choo.
9Aa nan cha utaasakpiin nun, le saatiŋ ki nan sar na ki gir,
10le saanib maa baadichal nima chee;
saaŋann sakpenn pu le aa tii bigiim baah ban pu na.
11Uwumbɔr tii nsan, le bipiib pam moon tibɔr ngbaan ke,
12“Bibɔrb ni baajab san la.”
Bipiib bi nan bi linampal na yakr bijab aah jan ki gaa tiwan ni na.
13Nima le ye baah di tikunabr naan ŋinanjel ŋi,
aan ki di salmaa boon ŋifeen na.
(Ba nan ŋa aan nimi bibaa gaal
ipiih aabɔkpur ponn ni butɔb daal?)
14Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah nan yaa bibɔrb
Salmonn Aajool pu na, u nan cha ŋitaanal lir nima chee.
15Basann aajool ye lijool sakpeln la,
lijool li kpa ŋijoomɔju sakpen na.
16Ba ŋa aa bi saajoomɔju sakpiin ngbaan paab
ki lik seen lijool li Uwumbɔr lee ke u li bi nima na?
Uwumbɔr ga li bi nima chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
17Uwumbɔr ga di waataan aatɔroku mam ŋichur ŋichur bi kpa mpɔɔn na
nyan ni Sainai aajool ki nan koo ni nin chee bi chain na.
18U joo binaagbiib pam ki chaa paacham;
u gaal ipiin binib bi yii waamɔb na chee.
Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga li bi nima.
19Pak Uwumbɔr man, u tu timi aatun iwiin mɔmɔk na;
uma le ye Uwumbɔr u gaal timi lir na.
20Timi Aawumbɔr le ye Uwumbɔr u gaal binib lir na;
uma le ye Tidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyani timi nkun ni na.
21Uwumbɔr ga sil wii waadim aayil,
u ga wii binib bi tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na aayil.
22Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M ga giin ni nimi aadim ki nya ni Basann;
M ga giin nyan ni bi nnyusakpem aataab,
23aan ni lul baasin ponn ni ki jer,
aan nimi aabɔ ga ŋmaa lakr yaa gee pu na.”
24Uwumbɔr, binib mɔmɔk kan saanyaŋ aasachuln,
bi kan Uwumbɔr, u ye maabɔr na, aasachuln li u di koo
waadichal ponn ni na.
25Bilahngaab le loln nsan, le biwangbaab paa puwɔb,
le bisapɔm bi gbaa ŋidabun na bi kaasisik ni.
26“Pak Uwumbɔr, waanib aakuun ni man;
Nimi bimɔk ye Jakob aayaabitiib na, pak Uwumbɔr man.”
27Njan, Benjaminn aanibol li par sakpen na le loln nsan,
le Juda aayidam ni baanib paan bi pu,
le Sebulunn ni Naftali aayidam paan.
28Uwumbɔr, mɔk saapɔɔn, mɔk saapɔɔn mu aa di tun timi pu,
29ki nyan Saadichal li bi Jerusalem ponn ni,
nin chee bibɔrb joo ni si baapiin na.
30Kae kipeewanbiik Ijipt u bi likal ni na;
kae ŋitimbol ŋi ye inaaja ni yaanaabi na,
ki ti saa buyoonn bi mɔmɔk ga nan gbaan
ki tii si tikunabr aapiin na.
Yaa binib bi gee butɔb na.
31Bininkpiib ga nya ni Ijipt ki dan;
Kus yaab ga yoor biŋaal paacham ki mee Uwumbɔr.
32Dulnyaa wee ni aanaan, gaa ilahn tii Uwumbɔr man,
gaa ilahn ki pak uma Uwumbɔr
33u chuun n‑yaayoonn na aataapaak ni na.
Li pel man waah tar mpɔɔn pu pu na.
34Moon Uwumbɔr aah kpa mpɔɔn pu na;
waanaan aapɔɔn le joo Israel yaab, waapɔɔn bi kitaapaak ni.
35Uwumbɔr aah nyan waadichal ni ki choo pu na kpa ijawaan la.
Uma le ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr.
U tii waanib mpɔɔn ni tiwon aapɔɔn.
Pak Uwumbɔr man.

english_text:
(By David for the music leader. To the tune “Lilies.”)
God Can Be Trusted
1Save me, God!
I am about to drown.
2I am sinking deep in the mud,
and my feet are slipping.
I am about to be swept under
by a mighty flood.
3I am worn out from crying,
and my throat is dry.
I have waited for you
till my eyes are blurred.
4 There are more people
who hate me for no reason
than there are hairs
on my head.
Many terrible enemies
want to destroy me, God.
Am I supposed to give back
something I didn't steal?
5You know my foolish sins.
Not one is hidden from you.
6 Lord God All-Powerful,
ruler of Israel,
don't let me embarrass anyone
who trusts and worships you.
7It is for your sake alone
that I am insulted
and blush with shame.
8I am like a stranger
to my relatives
and like a foreigner
to my own family.
9 My love for your house
burns in me like a fire,
and when others insult you,
they insulted me as well.
10I cried and went without food,
but they still insulted me.
11They sneered at me
for wearing sackcloth
to show my sorrow.
12Rulers and judges gossip
about me,
and drunkards make up songs
to mock me.
13But I pray to you, Lord.
So when the time is right,
answer me and help me
with your wonderful love.
14Don't let me sink in the mud,
but save me from my enemies
and from the deep water.
15Don't let me be
swept away by a flood
or drowned in the ocean
or swallowed by death.
16Answer me, Lord!
You are kind and good.
Pay attention to me!
You are truly merciful.
17Don't turn away from me.
I am your servant,
and I am in trouble.
Please hurry and help!
18Come and save me
from my enemies.
19You know how I am insulted,
mocked, and disgraced;
you know every one
of my enemies.
20I am crushed by insults,
and I feel sick.
I had hoped for mercy and pity,
but there was none.
21 Enemies poisoned my food,
and when I was thirsty,
they gave me vinegar.
22 Make their table a trap
for them and their friends.
23Blind them with darkness
and make them tremble.
24Show them how angry you are!
Be furious and catch them.
25 Destroy their camp
and don't let anyone live
in their tents.
26They cause trouble for people
you have already punished;
their gossip hurts those
you have wounded.
27Make them guiltier than ever
and don't forgive them.
28 Wipe their names from the book
of the living;
remove them from the list
of the innocent.
29I am mistreated and in pain.
Protect me, God,
and keep me safe!
30I will praise the Lord God
with a song
and a thankful heart.
31This will please the Lord
better than offering an ox
or a full-grown bull.
32When those in need see this,
they will be happy,
and the Lord's worshipers
will be encouraged.
33The Lord will listen
when the homeless cry out,
and he will never forget
his people in prison.
34Heaven and earth
will praise our God,
and so will the oceans
and everything in them.
35God will rescue Jerusalem,
and he will rebuild
the towns of Judah.
His people will live there
on their own land,
36and when the time comes,
their children will inherit
the land.
Then everyone who loves God
will also settle there.
translation_text:
Nterm aawiil
1Uwumbɔr, gaa mi lii. Nnyun ti saa nneen ni mɔk la;
2M bi chɔi tikpakpar ni,
nin chee kitiŋ aa bi ntaal ga taa na la;
M bi nnyun mu nyoo na ni la,
le tinyunkpenn ban ti di mi muin.
3Maah yin si pu ki ban nterm na le nneel ti waab,
le nneen ni gur wu.
Maah lik pu ki ban saaterm na, le nnimbil aa ti ki waa.
4Binib bi nan mi fam na wiir jer tiyikpir ti bi n‑yil pu na,
Maadim mɔni inyamɔn le paani mi,
bi kpa mpɔɔn le ki ban bi ku mi.
Bi cha m joo tiwan ni maa sun na le giini tii.
5Uwumbɔr, aa waa maatunwanbir;
aa nyi maah tun kijɔrk aatuln pu na.
6Ndindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan,
taa cha m joo ni inimɔɔn nan tii binib bi gaa si kii na.
Israel yaab Aawumbɔr,
taa cha m joo ni inimɔɔn nan tii binib bi dooni si na.
7Sin pu le bi seei mi, le m gur ye unimɔɔnii.
8M gur naahn uchaan le ndo yaab chee,
ki naahn uwɔwɔnja nna aabim chee.
9Maah neen saadichal pu na bi ke mmii le aah wu mponn ni na;
ŋisiibil ŋi ye sin yee na choo min chee la.
10M sunn mbaa taab ki lulni bumɔb, le binib seei mi;
11m pee ŋikpokeken, le bi laa mi.
12Bi kaa kitiŋ ponn ni le ki len mi, le bidanyurb naani mi ilahn.
13Uwumbɔr, le m ma ga mee si;
Uwumbɔr, kii mi buyoonn aa gee na.
Saageehm sakpiin pu, kii maayim, ba pu?
aa joo saapuur ti aa puu ke aa ga gaa binib lii na.
14Nyan mi maah bi chɔi tikpakpar ti ponn ni na;
gaa mi maadim chee lii, nyan mi nnyun nyonyoon mue ni.
15Taa cha nwam ngbaan biin m pu;
taa cha m sunn buen nnyun nyonyoon ni,
ki taa cha m sunn buen likaakul ni.
16Uwumbɔr, saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, ŋun maayim;
di saah san kinimbaak sakpen pu na fenn lik mi.
17Taa di aabaa bɔr saatutunn,
m bi tibɔr sakpenn ni la, kii maayim dandana.
18Dan ki nan gaa mi lii; nyan mi maadim chee.
19Aa nyi baah seei mi pu na,
ki nyi baah jinni mi inimɔɔn ki bii mi pu na,
aa nyi maadim mɔmɔk.
20Ŋisiibil le bii nsui, le ntaakpab yɔl.
M nan mak ke ubaa ga san mi kinimbaak, le ubaa aa gar,
m nan mak ke ubaa ga nan sɔŋ nsui, le kaa kan ubaa,
21Nkon aah nan chuu mi buyoonn na,
le bi di njinn ŋa maajikaar ni;
nnyunyuu aah chuu mi buyoonn na,
le bi di tiwanyukaan ni mɔɔn na tii mi.
22Cha baajikaar aajim kpaln baadoon;
cha baawaatork kpaln baalirm.
23Cha ijoon chuu bi mɔmɔk, cha bipuwɔb taa li pɔɔ.
24Cha saaŋuul lir bi pu; cha saaŋuusakpeln nyaŋ bi.
25Cha baakookoo yaan kpaln tilangbenn,
taa cha ubaa gur baadichal ni.
26Bi ŋani saah daa binib bi aatafal na mbiin;
le ki joo saah tii binib bi titotonn na aafalaa mooni.
27Ŋmee baatunwanbir mɔmɔk bil,
taa cha bi kan saaŋmarm siib kina.
28Ber baayimbil limɔfal aagbaŋ ni; taa cha bi kpaan saanib ni.
29Tɔ, iween ni itaakpayɔl le joo mi;
Uwumbɔr, fiin mi siin ki gaa mi lii.
30M ga di nlahn le pak Uwumbɔr;
m ga di idoon le moon waah kpa mpɔɔn pu na.
31Nimina le ga mɔɔr Uwumbɔr ki jer inaa aatork,
ki jer unaaja u filk na aatork.
32Binib bi bi limukl ni na yaa kan kina kan, bisui ga piir;
le binib bi dooni Uwumbɔr na aataakpab ga pɔɔk.
33Uwumbɔr ŋun binib bi kaa kpa na aayim,
kaa suln waanib bi bi kiyondiik ni na aabɔr.
34Paacham ni kitiŋ, pak Uwumbɔr man,
nnyusakpem ni tiwanfuurkaan nimɔk bi mu ni na mu pak u.
35U ga gaa Jerusalem lii ki gir maa Juda aatim.
Waanib le ga li koo nima ki li yeh kitiŋ ngbaan;
36le waatutunn aayaabitiib nan ji kaafaal,
le binib bi gee u na li koo nima.

english_text:
(By David for the music leader. To be used when an offering is made.)
God Is Wonderful
1Save me, Lord God!
Hurry and help.
2Disappoint and confuse
all who want to kill me.
Turn away and disgrace
all who want to hurt me.
3Embarrass and shame those
who say, “We told you so!”
4Let your worshipers celebrate
and be glad because of you.
They love your saving power,
so let them always say,
“God is wonderful!”
5I am poor and needy,
but you, the Lord God,
care about me.
You are the one who saves me.
Please hurry and help!
translation_text:
Limeel li ban nterm na
(Ilahn 40.13-17)
1Uwumbɔr, gaa mi lii, ter mi dandana wee.
2Cha binib bi ban ke bi ku mi na aalan ŋmal aan bi lir.
Cha binib bi aasui piin maafalaa pu na di inimɔɔn gir bipuwɔb.
3Cha binib bi laa mi na aataakpab yɔl aan bi lir.
4Cha binib bi choo aa chee na li kpa mpopiin ni mmɔɔn.
Cha binib bi dooni si saah gaa bi lii pu na li len n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke, “Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ sakpen a.”
5Nwon yɔl, le maa kpa nterm mubaa;
Uwumbɔr, dan m chee dandana.
Uwumbɔr, sin le ye u gaal mi lir na, san mala ki nan ter mi.

english_text:
A Prayer for God's Protection
1I run to you, Lord,
for protection.
Don't disappoint me.
2You do what is right,
so come to my rescue.
Listen to my prayer
and keep me safe.
3Be my mighty rock, the place
where I can always run
for protection.
Save me by your command!
You are my mighty rock
and my fortress.
4Come and save me, Lord God,
from vicious and cruel
and brutal enemies!
5I depend on you,
and I have trusted you
since I was young.
6I have relied on you
from the day I was born.
You brought me safely
through birth,
and I always praise you.
7Many people think of me
as something evil.
But you are my mighty protector,
8and I praise and honor you
all day long.
9Don't throw me aside
when I am old;
don't desert me
when my strength is gone.
10My enemies are plotting
because they want me dead.
11They say, “Now we'll catch you!
God has deserted you,
and no one can save you.”
12Come closer, God!
Please hurry and help.
13Embarrass and destroy
all who want me dead;
disgrace and confuse
all who want to hurt me.
14I will never give up hope
or stop praising you.
15All day long I will tell
the wonderful things you do
to save your people.
But you have done much more
than I could possibly know.
16I will praise you, Lord God,
for your mighty deeds
and your power to save.
17You have taught me
since I was a child,
and I never stop telling about
your marvelous deeds.
18Don't leave me when I am old
and my hair turns gray.
Let me tell future generations
about your mighty power.
19Your deeds of kindness
are known in the heavens.
No one is like you!
20You made me suffer a lot,
but you will bring me
back from this deep pit
and give me new life.
21You will make me truly great
and take my sorrow away.
22I will praise you, God,
the Holy One of Israel.
You are faithful.
I will play the harp
and sing your praises.
23You have rescued me!
I will celebrate and shout,
singing praises to you
with all my heart.
24All day long I will announce
your power to save.
I will tell how you disgraced
and disappointed those
who wanted to hurt me.
translation_text:
Ujaninkpel aameel
1Uwumbɔr, m dan aa chee ki ban nkiirm la,
taa cha ubaa nyaŋ mi kpala.
2Saabimbinyaan pu, ter mi ki gaa mi lii. Pel m chee ki ter mi.
3Li ye maakikiir u m mak u pu na,
ki li bi ke kitiŋ ki bi maa ŋigon gob ki na, ki li kii mi;
sin chee le m ga ŋmaa bɔr aan aa li kii mi.
4Maawumbɔr, gaa mi bibiindam chee lii,
nyan mi bibiindam ni titunwanbirdam aapɔɔn ni.
5Uwumbɔr, sin pu le m kpa limakl;
maah nan laa ye ubo pu na, le m nan di naadii tii si.
6Sin pu le m nyii maamɔfal mɔmɔk ni;
baah ma mi bundaal na, le aa piin ki kii mi.
M ga pak si n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
7Maamɔfal ye limɔkl le ki tii binib pam;
ba pu? sin le ye maakikiir u pɔɔ na.
8M pak si ni nwiin aah ga ti lir pu na,
ki mooni saapak aah bi pu na.
9N‑yoonn mu m por na, taa yii mi;
taa yii mi n‑yoonn mu maa ki kpa mpɔɔn na.
10Maadim ban bi ku mi la; bi len le ki kpokl m pu.
11Bi len le ke, “Uwumbɔr siir cha u a;
cha ti li dii u man ki ti chuu u, ubaa aa bi ki ga gaa u lii.”
12Uwumbɔr, taa li daa m chee;
Maawumbɔr, ŋa mala ki nan ter mi.
13Cha binib bi tak mi na lir ki kuln pel pel.
Cha binib bi pɔɔni bibaa ke bi tii mi iween na ji inimɔɔn.
14Sin pu le m ga li kpa limakl n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
m ga pak si, ki moo pak si.
15M ga bui binib saah kpa tiŋann pu na;
m ga li len saah gaal binib lir pu na
ki ti saa nwiin aah ga lir pu na,
tɔ, ni mu tee jer maah ga ŋmaa bee pu na.
16Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, m ga pak saapɔɔn;
m ga moon sin baanja aaŋann le pu.
17Maah nan laa ye ubo pu na, le aa mɔk mi saatun,
le m beenin len saatun sakpiin ŋi aa tun na.
18Uwumbɔr, n‑yoonn mu m por aan n‑yil bi piir na,
taa siir cha mi.
Li bi m chee aan m moon saapɔɔn aah nyaŋ pu na
tii n‑yoonn mu choo na aanib mɔmɔk.
19Uwumbɔr, saabimbinyaan fuur kitaapaak,
aa tun ŋitun ŋi nyaŋ na, ubaa aa bi ke si na.
20Aa cha tibɔbir ni falaa dan m pu,
le aa ga ki giin ni maapɔɔn, saan cha m kpo.
21Aa ga moo tii mi mpɔɔn ki jer njan na; aa ga ki sɔŋ nsui.
22M ga sil di kibeek gaa ilahn ki pak si.
Maawumbɔr, m ga pak si saaŋann sakpenn pu.
M ga di maabeek tii sin u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr
u bi chain na kipak.
23Buyoonn m bi gbaa kibeek pak si na,
le m ga li tar mpopiin pu;
saah gaa mi lii pu na, le m ga li pak si.
24M ga li len binib chee saah kpa tiŋann sakpen pu na,
ki ti saa nwiin aah ga lir pu na; ba pu?
binib bi pɔɔn bibaa ke bi tii mi titotonn na lir,
le ki jin inimɔɔn.

english_text:
(By Solomon.)
A Prayer for God To Guide and Help the King
1Please help the king
to be honest and fair
just like you, our God.
2Let him be honest and fair
with all your people,
especially the poor.
3Let peace and justice rule
every mountain and hill.
4Let the king defend the poor,
rescue the homeless, and crush
everyone who hurts them.
5Let the king live forever
like the sun and the moon.
6Let him be as helpful as rain
that refreshes the meadows
and the ground.
7Let the king be fair
with everyone,
and let there be peace
until the moon
falls from the sky.
8 Let his kingdom reach
from sea to sea,
from the Euphrates River
across all the earth.
9Force the desert tribes
to accept his rule,
and make his enemies
crawl in the dirt.
10Force the rulers of Tarshish
and of the islands
to pay taxes to him.
Make the kings of Sheba
and of Seba bring gifts.
11Make other rulers bow down
and all nations serve him.
12Do this because the king
rescues the homeless
when they cry out,
and he helps everyone
who is poor and in need.
13The king has pity
on the weak and the helpless
and protects those in need.
14He cares when they hurt,
and he saves them from cruel
and violent deaths.
15Long live the king!
Give him gold from Sheba.
Always pray for the king
and praise him each day.
16Let cities overflow with food
and hills be covered with grain,
just like Mount Lebanon.
Let the people in the cities
prosper like wild flowers.
17May the glory of the king
shine brightly forever
like the sun in the sky.
Let him make nations prosper
and learn to praise him.
18 Lord God of Israel,
we praise you.
Only you can work miracles.
19We will always praise
your glorious name.
Let your glory be seen
everywhere on earth.
Amen and amen.
20This ends the prayers
of David, the son of Jesse.
translation_text:
Nlan mu Ubɔr Solomonn nan naan mu na.
1-2Uwumbɔr, mɔk ubɔr aan u di ibamɔn ji binib tibɔr;
yakr saabamɔn tii u, aan u di ibamɔn joo saanib,
ki di tiŋann joo binib bi bi muk bi na.
3Cha nwankam ni tiŋann li bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu;
4Cha ubɔr ji bigiim aabɔr mbamɔm,
ki ter binib bi kaa kpa na, ki nyaŋ binib bi muk bi na.
5Cha saanib li dooni si ni ti yunn ke nwiin aah ga yunn pu na.
Cha bi li dooni si ni ti yunn ke uŋmal aah ga yunn pu na,
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
6Cha ubɔr li bi ke utaal aah nu ikpaakon i pu na,
ki naahn titaapupur aah pui kitiŋ pu pu na.
7Cha tiŋann li bi waayoonn,
ki cha nwankam li bi ki yunn ke uŋmal aah ga yunn pu na.
8Waanaan ga taln ti saa ni mɔmɔk,
ki nya Yufrates aamɔɔl ni ki ti saa kitiŋ aanaanmɔk.
9Nteersakpiin pu aanib ga gbaan unimbiin ni;
waadim ga tar lir kitiŋ, unimbiin ni.
10Speenn aatiŋ, ni ŋidik pu aabɔrb ga tii u ipiin;
Arabia ni Itiopia aatim aabɔrb ga joo ni ipiin.
11Bibɔrb mɔmɔk ga gbaan unimbiin ni;
ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ga li dii uma la.
12Bigiim bi wii yin u na, u gaal bi lir,
ki ter binib bi kaa kpa aan binib yii bi na.
13U san bigiim ni binib bi kaa kpa mpɔɔn na kinimbaak;
u gaal binib bi kaa kpa na aamɔfal lir.
14U nyani bi ŋimuk ni mbimbin mu pɔɔ na ni;
baamɔfal ye liwangol le u chee.
15Uwumbɔr tii ubɔr limɔfal li fɔk na.
Cha Arabia yaab tii u salmaa;
cha bi mee limeel tii u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
cha Uwumbɔr aanyoor li bi u pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
16Cha tijikaar li bi waatiŋ pu;
cha tijikaar li bi ŋigongon pu, ke Lebanonn aagongon pu na.
Cha binib li gbii ntim ponn ni,
ke timoor aah gbii ikpaakon ni pu na.
17Taa cha ubɔr aayimbil kuln;
cha waayimbil yunn ke nwiin aah ga yunn pu na.
Cha bi mee Uwumbɔr aan u ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu
ke waah ŋa tinyoor ŋa ubɔr pu pu na.
18Pak Uwumbɔr u ye timi Israel yaab Aadindaan na.
Uma baanja le tun ŋitusakpiin ngbaan.
19Li pak waayimbil li kpa kipak na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk man.
Cha waapak gbii dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk.
Amii, amii.
20Jese aajapɔɔn David aameel mɔmɔk le na.
TAATAA AAGBAŊ
(Ilahn 73–89)

english_text:
BOOK III
(Psalms 73–89)
(A psalm by Asaph.)
God Is Good
1God is truly good to Israel,
especially to everyone
with a pure heart.
2But I almost stumbled and fell,
3because it made me jealous
to see proud and evil people
and to watch them prosper.
4They never have to suffer,
they stay healthy,
5and they don't have troubles
like everyone else.
6Their pride is like a necklace,
and they commit sin more often
than they dress themselves.
7Their eyes bulge with fat,
and their minds are flooded
with foolish thoughts.
8They sneer and say cruel things,
and because of their pride,
they make violent threats.
9They dare to speak against God
and to order others around.
10God will bring his people back,
and they will drink the water
he so freely gives.
11Only evil people would say,
“God Most High cannot
know everything!”
12Yet all goes well for them,
and they live in peace.
13What good did it do me
to keep my thoughts pure
and refuse to do wrong?
14I am sick all day,
and I am punished
each morning.
15If I had said evil things,
I would not have been loyal
to your people.
16It was hard for me
to understand all this!
17Then I went to your temple,
and there I understood
what will happen
to my enemies.
18You will make them stumble,
never to get up again.
19They will be terrified,
suddenly swept away
and no longer there.
20They will disappear, Lord,
despised like a bad dream
the morning after.
21Once I was bitter
and brokenhearted.
22I was stupid and ignorant,
and I treated you
as a wild animal would.
23But I never really left you,
and you hold my right hand.
24Your advice has been my guide,
and later you will welcome me
in glory.
25In heaven I have only you,
and on this earth
you are all I want.
26My body and mind may fail,
but you are my strength
and my choice forever.
27All-Powerful Lord God,
those who stay far from you
will be lost,
and you will destroy those
who are unfaithful.
28It is good for me
to be near you.
I choose you as my protector,
and I will tell about
your wonderful deeds.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah kpa ibamɔn pu na
1Uwumbɔr sil kpa Israel yaab pu tiŋann,
u kpa binib bi aasui ponn ni ŋan na pu tiŋann.
2Le ni tee gur siib ke maamakl u pu ga doo;
maah tii u naadii u na gur siib u doo la.
3Maah kan ke bibiindam aatuln mɔmɔk kpa tinyoor na,
le m nan kpa bigaadam pu lipiipoln.
4Baa ji iween aafalaa; bi pɔɔ le ki kpa laafee.
5Baa ji falaa ke binib biken na;
baa kani tibɔbir ti biken kani na.
6Kina pu le bi di kigaak ŋa nneeleen ki di peen,
ki di mbimbinpɔɔl ŋa tiwanpeenkaan;
7tibɔbir le nyani bisui ni, le baalandak
ye mbiin aalandak ŋmeen la.
8Bi laa binib biken, le ki len tibɔbir;
bi kpa kigaak, le ki kpokl ke bi muk biken.
9Bi len Uwumbɔr u bi paacham na tibɔbir,
le ki tii binib bi bi kitiŋ pu na kigaak aatun,
10ki cha Uwumbɔr aanib fenn buen bi chee,
ki ti kpaan kii baah len pu na mala.
11Bi len le ke, “Uwumbɔr aan li nyi;
Mpɔɔndaan u bi paacham na aan bee.”
12Bibiindam bi kina la.
Bi kpa sakpen, le ki moo kani n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
13Maah cha maabimbin ŋan aan maa tun titunwanbir na
ye fam la aa?
14Uwumbɔr, aa cha m jin falaa le nwiin ti lir;
aa dar ntafal kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni.
15M yaa len kina aabɔr kan,
maa ba ga li tun ke saanib ponn ni ubaa na.
16M pɔɔn mbaa ke m dakl lik tibɔr ngbaan ponn ni,
le ti pɔɔ ti nyaŋ mi.
17Le m ti baan di ti buen Saadichal ni.
Nima chee le m bee tiwan ni ga ŋa bibiindam na.
18Aa ga di bi siin nin chee ŋar na,
ki cha bi lir ki kuln kookoo.
19Libuul ngbaan ni le bi kuln,
baah ga ti doo pu na ga li kpa ijawaan.
20Bi naahn tidaŋ ti aa daŋ kinyeek,
ki woln kichakpiik ni ki suln ti na la;
Uwumbɔr, aa yaa fii sil paacham kan, le bi wɔŋ.
21Buyoonn maalandak nan bii nsui
aan mmɔb ponn ni choŋ na,
22m nan jɔr ke kiwakork na la;
maa nan kee bee saabimbin.
23Tɔ, m mu nan beenin bi gbɔk si, le aa di aaŋaal chuu mi.
24Aa di saamɔkm le mɔk mi nsan,
le nimina aadoon na, aa ga nan di kinyuŋ le gaa mi.
25M ki kpa ba paacham kaa ye sin?
Maah kpa sin na, maa ki ban nibaa kitiŋ do.
26Nibaakan, maalandak ni nwon ga yɔl,
le Uwumbɔr ma ye maapɔɔn;
uma le ye tiwan ni m ban n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.
27Binib bi yii si na ga sil kuln;
aa ga doo binib bi nyan aapuwɔb na.
28Mma chee kan, ni ŋan ki ti nyaŋ ke m li duun Uwumbɔr;
ni ŋan ti nyaŋ ke m kan Ndindaan Uwumbɔr chee nkiirm,
ki moon waah ŋa pu na mɔmɔk.

english_text:
(A special psalm by Asaph.)
A Prayer for the Nation in Times of Trouble
1Our God, why have you
completely rejected us?
Why are you so angry
with the ones you care for?
2Remember the people
you rescued long ago,
the tribe you chose
for your very own.
Think of Mount Zion,
your home;
3walk over to the temple
left in ruins forever
by those who hate us.
4Your enemies roared like lions
in your holy temple,
and they have placed
their banners there.
5It looks like a forest
chopped to pieces.
6They used axes and hatchets
to smash the carvings.
7They burned down your temple
and badly disgraced it.
8They said to themselves,
“We'll crush them!”
Then they burned every one
of your meeting places
all over the country.
9There are no more miracles
and no more prophets.
Who knows how long
it will be like this?
10Our God, how much longer
will our enemies sneer?
Won't they ever stop
insulting you?
11Why don't you punish them?
Why are you holding back?
12Our God and King,
you have ruled
since ancient times;
you have won victories
everywhere on this earth.
13 By your power you made a path
through the sea,
and you smashed the heads
of sea monsters.
14 You crushed the heads
of the monster Leviathan,
then fed him to wild creatures
in the desert.
15You opened the ground
for streams and springs
and dried up mighty rivers.
16You rule the day and the night,
and you put the moon
and the sun in place.
17You made summer and winter
and gave them to the earth.
18Remember your enemies, Lord!
They foolishly sneer
and won't respect you.
19You treat us like pet doves,
but they mistreat us.
Don't keep forgetting us
and letting us be fed
to those wild animals.
20Remember the agreement
you made with us.
Violent enemies are hiding
in every dark corner
of the earth.
21Don't disappoint those in need
or make them turn from you,
but help the poor and homeless
to shout your praises.
22Do something, God!
Defend yourself.
Remember how those fools
sneer at you all day long.
23Don't forget the loud shouts
of your enemies.
translation_text:
Limeel li ga gaa litimbol lii na
1Uwumbɔr, ba ŋa aa san cha mi kina?
Aa gee aabaa aanib pu liŋuul li kaa kpa ndoon na la aa?
2Teer saanib bi aa nan lee bi n‑yoonn mu jer na pu,
saanib bi aa nan nyan ni bi tinaagbiir ni
ke bi nan li ye saanibol na.
Teer Lijool Sionn, nin chee aa nan koo na bɔr.
3Chuun baah ber ntim mu kookoo na pu;
timi aadim bii doo tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi Saadichal ni na.
4Saadim teen mpɔɔn pu Saadichal ni, baah kan linyaŋ pu na pu;
bi di baatuutaa mam ŋum nima chee
ke ni li ye limɔkl ki tii baanyaŋ ngbaan.
5Bi naahn bijab bi gaar isui na la
li ki joo baachɔm gaar isui lir.
6Bi di baachɔm ni ligagaar fɔfɔk gbaa wiir
baah di idɔ ŋa Saadichal aawan mɔmɔk ni na.
7Bi wɔb Saadichal lii, le ki see li mmii;
bi di tijɔŋ koo nin chee bi dooni si na.
8Bi nan ban ke bi wɔi timi kookoo la;
bi see nin chee mɔk bi chain kitiŋ kee pu na mmii.
9Timi aawan nimɔk ye kitork aawan na buen a;
saabɔnabtiib aa ki gur,
le ubaa aa nyi nimina aah ga yunn ki ti saa pu na.
10Uwumbɔr, timi aadim ga laa si ki saa bayoonn?
Bi ga li seei si ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na la aa?
11Ba ŋa aa yii kaa ter timi?
Ba ŋa aa di aaŋaal bɔɔb aabaa ki si?
12Uwumbɔr, mpiin na, sin le nan ye timi aabɔr;
n‑yoonn, n‑yoonn pam le aa gaa timi lii.
13Aa di saapɔɔn sakpiin le di yakr nnyusakpem,
le ki wii nnyusakpem ponn ni aapeewanbiik aayil,
14aa wii nnyusakpem ponn ni aapɔɔndaan aayil,
ki cha nteersakpiin ponn ni aapeel ŋman waawon.
15Aa cha uyayak aanyunbun puu;
aa cha ŋimɔɔ ŋi wiir na foor ki kuur.
16Aa naan nwiin pu ni kinyeek;
ki mɔk nwiin ni uŋmal naakakaa chee;
17aa mɔk kitiŋ kaanaanmɔk;
aa ŋa kitotoŋ ni tiwoor aayoonn.
18Uwumbɔr, teer ke saadim laa si,
li nyi ke baa dii si, le ki lik si fam.
19Taa di saanib bi kaa kpa uteter na
tii baadim bi ye bibiindam na;
taa suln saanib bi bi ban bi ku bi na bɔr.
20Teer saah nan puu tipuur ti tii timi na bɔr.
Mbimbin mu pɔɔ na bi kitiŋ kee pu ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu la.
21Taa cha baah muk binib bi na ji inimɔɔn;
cha bigiim ni binib bi kaa kpa na pak si.
22Uwumbɔr, fii sil ki len saabɔr.
Teer ke binib bi kaa dii si na laa si le nwiin ti lir.
23Taa suln saadim aaŋuul aajar ti bi ŋmɔ na bɔr,
taa suln saadim aayoonn mɔmɔk aafuuk bɔr.

english_text:
(A psalm and a song by Asaph for the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
)
Praise God for All He Has Done
1Our God, we thank you
for being so near to us!
Everyone celebrates
your wonderful deeds.
2You have set a time
to judge with fairness.
3The earth trembles,
and its people shake;
you alone keep
its foundations firm.
4You tell every bragger,
“Stop bragging!”
And to the wicked you say,
“Don't boast of your power!
5Stop bragging! Quit telling me
how great you are.”
6Our Lord and our God,
victory doesn't come
from the east or the west
or from the desert.
7You are the one who judges.
You can take away power
and give it to others.
8You hold in your hand
a cup filled with wine,
strong and foaming.
You will pour out some
for every sinful person
on this earth,
and they will have to drink
until it is gone.
9But I will always tell about
you, the God of Jacob,
and I will sing your praise.
10Our Lord, you will destroy
the power of evil people,
but you will give strength
to those who are good.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr le ye ubɔjir
1Uwumbɔr, ti dooni si, ti dooni si.
Ti mooni saah kpa mpɔɔn sakpen pu na,
ki tuk binib saah tun ŋitusakpiin ŋi na aabɔr.
2Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M siin n‑yoonn mu m ga ji binib tibɔr na,
m ga di ibamɔn le ji bi tibɔr ngbaan.”
3Tɔ, tiwanfuurkaan mɔmɔk aawon yaa gbaa,
aan kitiŋ kibaa mu jii kan, m ga cha kaatinyik li pɔɔ kin kin.
4M ga bui bibiindam ke bi taa li kpa kigaak;
5M ga bui bi ke bi di cha kipupuk.
6Libɔjil aa nyani liwipuul, kaa nyani liwilir,
kaa nyani ŋŋangan, kaa nyani ŋŋangii wɔb;
7Uwumbɔr le ji tibɔr,
u bii bibaa aabɔr, le ki bui biken ke baabɔr ŋan.
8Uwumbɔr joo kiyikuuk uŋaal ni,
kiyikuuk ngbaan gbii ndapɔɔl mu ye waaŋuul na la.
U bar mu, le bibiindam mɔmɔk nyun mu;
bi nyun mu mɔmɔk pel pel.
9Le mma ga li beenin len Uwumbɔr u Jakob mu nan dii u na aabɔr,
ki ga li gaa ilahn ki pak u.
10U ga wii bibiindam aapɔɔn,
le ki tee moo kpee binib bi aabimbin ŋan na mpɔɔn.

english_text:
(A song and a psalm by Asaph for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.)
God Always Wins
1You, our God,
are famous in Judah
and honored in Israel.
2Your home is on Mount Zion,
the city of peace.
3There you destroyed
fiery arrows, shields, swords,
and all the other weapons.
4You are more glorious than
the eternal mountains.
5Brave warriors were robbed
of what they had taken,
and now they lie dead,
unable to lift an arm.
6God of Jacob, when you roar,
enemy chariots and horses
drop dead in their tracks.
7Our God, you are fearsome,
and no one can oppose you
when you are angry.
8From heaven you announced
your decisions as judge!
And all who live on this earth
were terrified and silent
9when you took over as judge,
ready to rescue
everyone in need.
10Even the most angry people
will praise you
when you are furious.
11Everyone, make your promises
to the Lord your God
and do what you promise.
The Lord is fearsome,
and all his servants
should bring him gifts.
12God destroys the courage
of rulers and kings
and makes cowards of them.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr u nyaŋni na
1Juda aatiŋ yaab mɔmɔk nyi Uwumbɔr bɔr;
Israel yaab nyuŋni waayimbil.
2Udo le ye Jerusalem; u koo Sionn Aajool paab la.
3Nima chee le u kool waadim aapiin, u kool baajaak aapen ni njum;
mbamɔn, u kool baajawan mɔmɔk.
4Uwumbɔr, saapak nyaŋ sakpen a.
Aa nan kpa nnaan aapɔɔn buyoonn aa nan nyan ni ŋijoo paab
nin chee aa nyaŋ saadim na.
5Baajab bi nan kaar na nan lann baawan mɔmɔk
ki gur dɔ geen ntekpiigeen;
baapɔɔn ni baalan mɔmɔk nan ye fam la.
6Uwumbɔr u tiyaaja Jakob mu nan dii u na, saah nan faan bi buyoonn na,
baataan ni binib bi dik i pu na nan lir ki kpoi.
7Uwumbɔr, binib mɔmɔk san si ijawaan la.
Buyoonn saaŋuul ti fii na kan,
ubaa aan ki ŋmaa sil aanimbiin ni.
8Aa bi paacham le ki cha binib mɔmɔk bee ke aa ga ji bi tibɔr
le ijawaan nan chuu dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk,
9n‑yoonn mu aa fii sil ke aa ji tibɔr
ki gaa baah muk binib bi na lii na, le ni ŋmin chii.
10Unibɔn aaŋuul moo joo ni kipak le nan tii si,
binib bi ŋmar butɔb ni na ga li ji saajim.
11Tiin Uwumbɔr naah puu ke ni ga tii u pu na;
ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk bi ki duun na,
li joo ni ipiin nan tii u man.
Uwumbɔr cha unibɔn san u ijawaan;
12u sunn biyidam bi kpa kigaak na taab
ki cha bibɔrkpaam san u ijawaan sakpen.

english_text:
(A psalm by Asaph for Jeduthun, the music leader.)
In Times of Trouble God Is with His People
1I pray to you, Lord God,
and I beg you to listen.
2In days filled with trouble,
I search for you.
And at night I tirelessly
lift my hands in prayer,
refusing comfort.
3When I think of you,
I feel restless and weak.
4Because of you, Lord God,
I can't sleep.
I am restless
and can't even talk.
5I think of times gone by,
of those years long ago.
6Each night my mind
is flooded with questions:
7“Have you rejected me forever?
Won't you be kind again?
8Is this the end of your love
and your promises?
9Have you forgotten
how to have pity?
Do you refuse to show mercy
because of your anger?”
10Then I said, “God Most High,
what hurts me most
is that you no longer help us
with your mighty arm.”
11Our Lord, I will remember
the things you have done,
your miracles of long ago.
12I will think about each one
of your mighty deeds.
13Everything you do is right,
and no other god
compares with you.
14You alone work miracles,
and you have let nations
see your mighty power.
15With your own arm you rescued
your people, the descendants
of Jacob and Joseph.
16The ocean looked at you, God,
and it trembled deep down
with fear.
17Water flowed from the clouds.
Thunder was heard above
as your arrows of lightning
flashed about.
18Your thunder roared
like chariot wheels.
The world was made bright
by lightning,
and all the earth trembled.
19You walked through the water
of the mighty sea,
but your footprints
were never seen.
20You guided your people
like a flock of sheep,
and you chose Moses and Aaron
to be their leaders.
translation_text:
Itaakpayɔl yoonn aasuudoon
1M wii mpɔɔn pu ki yin Uwumbɔr,
m wii mpɔɔn pu, le u ŋun maawiil pu.
2Limukl yoonn le m mee Uwumbɔr.
Kinyeek ni kitaak aawoln pu,
m yoor ŋŋaal paacham le ki mee u, le kaa tee kani nsuudoon.
3M yaa ka ki dak Uwumbɔr aabɔr kan, le m faa liŋuun;
m yaa ka dak suuna kan, le nwon yɔl ti lir.
4U cha m dɔ waa le kitaak ti woln;
ni muk mi sakpen, le maa ti ki ŋmaa len tibɔr.
5M dakl lik iwiin i jer na; le ki teer ŋibin ŋi jer n‑yaayoonn na.
6M dɔ kinyeek ki dak ilandak sakpiin la;
m dɔ suuna, le ki baa mbaa tibɔr timina;
7“Uwumbɔr ga li yiil timi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la aa?
Waan ki li kpa mpopiin ti pu uu?
8U di cha kaa ki tii timi ngeehm la aa?
Waah puu tipuur ti na aa ki si la aa?
9Uwumbɔr suln kaa ki san kinimbaak la aa?
Liŋuul le gaa kinimbaak aabuul ni ii?”
10Le m bui ke, “Tiwan ni wu mi sakpen na le ye nimina;
ke Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aa ki ter timi ke waah nan ter timi n‑yoonn mu jer na.”
11Uwumbɔr, m ga teer saah tun ŋitukpaan ŋi na bɔr;
m ga teer ŋitukpaan ŋi aa tun n‑yoonn mu jer na bɔr.
12M ga kal ki dakl lik tiwan ni mɔmɔk aa ŋa na,
m ga kal suuna ki dakl lik saatukpaan ngbaan.
13Uwumbɔr, saah ŋa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na bi chain la,
liwaal libaa aa bi ki kpa mpɔɔn ke sin na.
14Sin le ye Uwumbɔr u tun iwaan aatun na;
aa mɔk ŋitimbol saapɔɔn sakpiin.
15Aa di saapɔɔn gaa Jakob ni Josef aayaabitiib bi ye saanib na lii.
16Uwumbɔr, nnyun aah kan si na, le ijawaan chuu mu,
le nnyusakpem aataab deŋni,
17le ntaalangbam bar nnyun kpir ni,
le utaal nyan kitaapaak ki teen ni,
le utaal moor ni kookoo lak lak.
18Utaal aah tar pu na buen ni kookoo a,
le utaal aah moor pu na cha dulnyaa mɔmɔk woln chain;
le kitiŋ dam ki jii.
19Aa chuun tinyunkpenn ni ki jer;
aa lul nnyusakpem mu nyoo na ni ki puur,
le ubaa aa kan saataabuu.
20Aa loln saanib pu nsan ke upihdaan na,
ki cha Moses ni Aaronn joo bi.

english_text:
(A special psalm by Asaph.)
What God Has Done for His People
1My friends, I beg you
to listen as I teach.
2 I will give instruction
and explain the mystery
of what happened long ago.
3These are things we learned
from our ancestors,
4and we will tell them
to the next generation.
We won't keep secret
the glorious deeds
and the mighty miracles
of the Lord.
5God gave his Law
to Jacob's descendants,
the people of Israel.
And he told our ancestors
to teach their children,
6so that each new generation
would know his Law
and tell it to the next.
7Then they would trust God
and obey his teachings,
without forgetting anything
God had done.
8They would be different
from their ancestors,
who were stubborn, rebellious,
and unfaithful to God.
9The warriors from Ephraim
were armed with arrows,
but they ran away
when the battle began.
10They broke their agreement
with God,
and they turned their backs
on his teaching.
11They forgot all he had done,
even the mighty miracles
12 he did for their ancestors
near Zoan in Egypt.
13 God made a path in the sea
and piled up the water
as he led them across.
14 He guided them during the day
with a cloud,
and each night he led them
with a flaming fire.
15 God made water flow
from rocks he split open
in the desert,
and his people drank freely,
as though from a lake.
16He made streams gush out
like rivers from rocks.
17But in the desert,
the people of God Most High
kept sinning and rebelling.
18 They stubbornly tested God
and demanded from him
what they wanted to eat.
19They challenged God by saying,
“Can God provide food
out here in the desert?
20It's true God struck the rock
and water gushed out
like a river,
but can he give his people
bread and meat?”
21When the Lord heard this,
he was angry and furious
with Jacob's descendants,
the people of Israel.
22They had refused to trust him,
and they had doubted
his saving power.
23But God gave a command
to the clouds,
and he opened the doors
in the skies.
24 From heaven he sent grain
that they called manna.
25He gave them more than enough,
and each one of them ate
this special food.
26God's mighty power
sent a strong wind
from the southeast,
27and it brought birds
that covered the ground,
like sand on the beach.
28Then God made the birds fall
in the camp of his people
near their tents.
29God gave his people
all they wanted,
and each of them ate
until they were full.
30But before they had swallowed
the last bite,
31God became angry and killed
the strongest and best
from the families of Israel.
32But the rest kept on sinning
and would not trust
God's miracles.
33So he cut their lives short
and made them terrified.
34After he killed some of them,
the others turned to him
with all their hearts.
35They remembered God Most High,
the mighty rock
that kept them safe.
36But they tried to flatter God,
and they told him lies;
37 they were unfaithful
and broke their promises.
38Yet God was kind.
He kept forgiving their sins
and didn't destroy them.
He often became angry,
but never lost his temper.
39God remembered that they
were made of flesh
and were like a wind
that blows once
and then dies down.
40While they were in the desert,
they often rebelled
and made God sad.
41They kept testing him
and caused terrible pain
for the Holy One of Israel.
42They forgot about his power
and how he had rescued them
from their enemies.
43God showed them all kinds
of wonderful miracles
near Zoan in Egypt.
44 He turned the rivers of Egypt
into blood,
and no one could drink
from the streams.
45 He sent swarms of flies
to pester the Egyptians,
and he sent frogs
to cause them trouble.
46 God let worms and grasshoppers
eat their crops.
47 He destroyed their grapevines
and their fig trees
with hail and floods.
48Then he killed their cattle
with hail
and their other animals
with lightning.
49God was so angry and furious
that he went into a rage
and caused them great trouble
by sending swarms
of destroying angels.
50God released his anger
and slaughtered them
in a terrible way.
51 He killed the first-born son
of each Egyptian family.
52 Then God led his people
out of Egypt
and guided them in the desert
like a flock of sheep.
53 He led them safely along,
and they were not afraid,
but their enemies drowned
in the sea.
54 God brought his people
to the sacred mountain
that he had taken
by his own power.
55 He made nations run
from the tribes of Israel,
and he let the tribes
take over their land.
56 But the people tested
God Most High,
and they refused
to obey his laws.
57They were as unfaithful
as their ancestors,
and they were as crooked
as a twisted arrow.
58God demanded all their love,
but they made him angry
by worshiping idols.
59So God became furious
and completely rejected
the people of Israel.
60 Then he deserted his home
at Shiloh, where he lived
here on earth.
61 He let enemies capture
the sacred chest
and let them dishonor him.
62God took out his anger
on his chosen ones
and let them be killed
by enemy swords.
63Fire destroyed the young men,
and the young women were left
with no one to marry.
64Priests died violent deaths,
but their widows
were not allowed to mourn.
65Finally the Lord woke up,
like a soldier
startled from a drunken sleep.
66God scattered his enemies
and made them ashamed
forever.
67Then the Lord decided
not to make his home
with Joseph's descendants
in Ephraim.
68Instead he chose the tribe
of Judah,
and he chose Mount Zion,
the place he loves.
69There he built his temple
as lofty as the mountains
and as solid as the earth
he made to last forever.
70 The Lord God chose David
to be his servant and took him
from tending sheep
71and from caring for lambs.
Then God made him the leader
of Israel, his own nation.
72David treated the people fairly
and guided them with wisdom.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr ni waanib
1Maanib, li pel maamɔkm man,
ki pel maah ban m len pu na mbamɔm.
2M ban m di nlan aabɔr le len
ki kpiir tuk nimi n‑yaayoonn na aabɔbɔrkaan,
3tibɔr ti ti ŋun ki nyi ti na, tibɔr ti tiyaajatiib tuk timi na.
4Ti ga cha timi aabilb li nyi ti.
Ti ga bui tiyaabitiib
Uwumbɔr aah kpa mpɔɔn ki tun liyimbil aatun ŋi na,
ni iwaan aatun ŋi u tun na.
5U tii Jakob aayaabitiib, Israel yaab, ŋikoobil ni ikaal.
U nan bui tiyaajatiib tibɔr ke bi mɔk baabilb waakaal,
6aan biyaabitiib mu ga nan ŋmaa bee i
ki mu nan di i mɔk baabilb.
7Bi yaa ŋa kina kan, bi mu ga nan kii tii Uwumbɔr,
kaan suln waah tun pu na;
bi mu ga tee li ŋani waakaal aah len pu na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
8Baan li bi ke biyaajatiib na,
kaan li ye binib bi yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki nyan upuwɔb na.
Baan li ye binib bi kaa gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii mbamɔm,
kaan ŋmaa nyii u pu ki sil n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.
9Efraim yaab nan joo itɔi ni ipiin, le ki nan tee san butɔb daal.
10Baa nan joo tipuur ti bi nan puu tii Uwumbɔr na;
bi yii, kaa joo waakaal.
11Bi suln waah tun pu na,
iwaan aatun ŋi u nan tun aan bi kan na, bi suln ŋibɔr.
12Biyaajatiib nan si lik, le Uwumbɔr tun iwaan aatun
Soann aapaan mu bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na.
13U nan yakr nnyusakpem nfum mulee pu, ki di bi dii mu ni jer;
u nan cha nnyun fii sil ke ŋigon na.
14Nwiin pu kan, u nan loln bi pu nsan, ntaalangbam ponn ni la,
le ki ye mmii ki wiin ki loln bi pu nsan kinyeek,
ni kitaak aah ga ti woln pu na.
15U bɔɔl ŋitakpal nteersakpiin ni,
ki cha nnyun nyan ni nin chee nyoo na ki tii bi, bi nyun.
16U cha nkpen puu nyan ni litakpal ni,
ki cha nnyun puu ke limɔɔl na,
17le bi yii, ki beenin tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir,
le ki yii uma Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aamɔb,
nteersakpiin ngbaan ni.
18Bi nyi le ki tɔŋ Uwumbɔr
ki bui ke u tii bi tijikaar ti bi ban na.
19Bi nan len Uwumbɔr le ki bui ke,
“Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa tii timi tijikaar nteersakpiin ni ii?
20Ni ye mbamɔn ke u faa litakpal,
le nnyun puu nyan ni ke nwam na;
tɔ, u ga ŋmaa tii timi tijikaar aa?
u ga ŋmaa tii timi waanib tinann mu uu?”
21Uwumbɔr aah ŋun waanib len kina na, le waaŋuul fii,
le u di mmii tak bi, le waaŋuul moo fii bi pu,
22ba pu? baa nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii
kaa tii naadii ke u ga ŋmaa gaa bi lii.
23Le u len kitaapaak chee tibɔr
ki bui ke kaabisamɔi chuu piir;
24le ki tii bi njikaabim mu nyan ni paacham na,
ki cha tijikaar ti bi yin ti ke mana na lir ni ke bi ji.
25Kina pu le bi nan jin Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib aajikaar,
le Uwumbɔr tii bi baah ban pu na mɔmɔk.
26U nan ki cha liwipuul wɔb aabuln daa,
ki cha waapɔɔn fiin ŋŋangii wɔb aabuln,
27ki cha inyoon lir ni kitiŋ ki wiir ke limɔɔtambol na,
le waanib chur i;
28i nan lir baakakaa chee, baah doo nin chee na.
29Le binib ngbaan nan jin ki ŋman ki bab;
Uwumbɔr nan tii bi baah ban pu na.
30Tɔ, baakpeek aa nan kee doo; bi nan beenin ji,
31le Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii bi pu,
le u ku baajab bi pɔɔ sakpen ki ye Israel yaab aanachipɔm na.
32Nimina mɔmɔk aapuwɔb, binib ngbaan
nan beenin tun titunwanbir;
Waajinjiir aatun na mɔmɔk aapuwɔb na
baa nan beenin tii u naadii.
33Le u kuln baawiin ke kifuurk kibaa na,
ki di tibɔbir kuln baamɔfal.
34Buyoonn u ti ku bi ponn bibaa na,
le bi gur na tee fenn gir ni u chee,
ki yii titunwanbir ki di bisui mɔmɔk mee u.
35Bi nan teer ke Uwumbɔr le ye baakikiir,
ki teer ke uma Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na le ter bi.
36Tɔ, baamɔbon tee ye inyamɔn la; baabɔr mɔmɔk aa gbiini.
37Baa nan dii waah len pu na;
baa nan joo baah nan puu tipuur ti tii u na.
38Le Uwumbɔr ma nan san waanib kinimbaak.
U nan di cha pinn bi baatunwanbir kaa kuln bi.
N‑yoonn n‑yoonn pam le waa di waaŋuul tun lituln,
ki chuu waaŋuusakpeln.
39U nan teer ke bi ye binibɔm la,
ki naahn libuln li daar jer cha na la.
40N‑yoonn mɔmɔk ni, bi nan yiil waamɔb nteersakpiin ni la;
N‑yoonn mɔmɔk bi nan bii usui la.
41Bi tɔŋni Uwumbɔr, ki ki gir tɔŋni u,
ki cha uma Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na aasui bii.
42Bi suln waapɔɔnsakpiin bɔr,
ni nwiin mundaal u nan gaa bi baadim chee lii na,
43ni bundaal u nan tun waatukpaan
Soann aapaan mu bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na bɔr.
44U nan cha ŋimɔɔ kpaln nsin,
le Ijipt yaab aa nan ki kpa nnyun bi nyu.
45U nan tun ni tisibir nan lii bi pu, le ti muk bi,
ni ŋipulaatal ŋi bii baatiŋ na.
46U cha itoon dan nan di baajikaar ŋman
ki bii baakpaakon doo.
47U cha ŋitaatakpal lir ki kool baadaan aasubil,
ni baasubil ŋiken aasui.
48U cha ŋitaatakpal le ku baanaa
ki cha utaal aah moor pu na ku tiwakor ti gur na.
49Waaŋuusakpeln ponn ni le u nan cha nkun aatuuntiib dan
ki nan bii bi pam.
50Waa ki chuu waaŋuul, kaa di cha baamɔfal;
u cha iween ku bi.
51U nan ku bima Ijipt yaab aadichadaan mɔk aajan aabijabim,
52le ki nin cheen waanib nyan ke upihdaan na,
ki mɔk bi nsan, nteersakpiin ni.
53U nan cheen bi mbamɔm, le ijawaan aa nan joo bi;
u cha nnyusakpem nan biin baadim pu, ki di bi buen.
54U nan di bi nan fuu waatiŋ ki bi chain na pu,
u di bi nan fuu ŋijoo ŋi pu uma ubaa nan jan ki gaa ŋi na.
55Waanib aah tur koo ni pu na le u jenn
ntim ngbaan aanib le ki yakr baatim tii Israel aanibol
ki di bido tii waanib ngbaan.
56Le bi tee nyan Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aapuwɔb,
ki tɔŋ u; baa nan joo waakaal;
57bi tee nyan upuwɔb kaa dii waah len pu na ke biyaajatiib na,
kaa si chob ke mpiin mu gɔr na.
58Bi nan cha waaŋuul fii baah dooni ŋiwaa nin chee na pu,
ki cha usui fii baawaa ngbaan pu.
59Uwumbɔr aah kan kina na, le waaŋuul fii,
le u yii waanib kookoo.
60U nan nyan cha Waabool li nan bi Silo aatiŋ ni
ki nan ye Waadichal li ponn ni u nan koo tikaasisik ni na.
61U nan cha timi aadim nyaŋ timi ki gaa Nkaal Aadakaa
u ye waapɔɔn ni kipak aamɔkl na.
62Waaŋuul nan fii waanib pu pam, le u cha baadim ku bi.
63Binachipɔm nan kpoi butɔb ni
le bipiisapɔm aa ki kan ubaa bi mɔn.
64Bitotoorb nan kpoi mpɔɔkun la,
le baakpopiib aa nan kpa nsan ke bi wii baakpuu.
65Nee aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr nan fii ke waah finn ngeen pu le na;
u nan bi ke unachipɔɔn u nyun ndaan aan ni mɔɔr u na.
66U nan jenn waadim giin inimɔɔn aalirm mu kaa kpa ndoon na ni.
67U nan tee yii Josef aayaabitiib; waa nan lee Efraim aanibol.
68U nan tee lee Juda aanibol,
ni Sionn Aajool li u gee mbamɔm na la.
69Nima chee le u maa Waadichal ke udo ni bi paacham na;
u nan cha li nyal sil ke kitiŋ kibaa aah si chob pu
aan nibaa aa ŋmaa ŋa ki,
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na la.
70U nan lee waatutunn David la.
U nan ti nyan ni u kinaakpaamook ni,
71nin chee u bi kpaa waapiih na,
le ki di u ŋa Israel yaab aabɔr, Uwumbɔr aanib aapihdaan.
72David nan di lineen le ki joo bi,
ki loln bi pu nsan, ki nan kpa nlan.

english_text:
(A psalm by Asaph.)
Have Pity on Jerusalem
1 Our God, foreign nations
have taken your land,
disgraced your temple,
and left Jerusalem in ruins.
2They have fed the bodies
of your servants
to flesh-eating birds;
your loyal people are food
for savage animals.
3All Jerusalem is covered
with their blood,
and there is no one left
to bury them.
4Every nation around us
sneers and makes fun.
5Our Lord, will you keep on
being angry?
Will your angry feelings
keep flaming up like fire?
6Get angry with those nations
that don't know you
and won't worship you!
7They have gobbled up
Jacob's descendants
and left the land in ruins.
8 Don't make us pay for the sins
of our ancestors.
Have pity and come quickly!
We are completely helpless.
9Our God, you keep us safe.
Now help us! Rescue us.
Forgive our sins
and bring honor to yourself.
10Why should nations ask us,
“Where is your God?”
Let us and the other nations
see you take revenge
for your servants who died
a violent death.
11Listen to the prisoners groan!
Let your mighty power save all
who are sentenced to die.
12Each of those nations sneered
at you, our Lord.
Now let others sneer at them,
seven times as much.
13Then we, your people,
will always thank you.
We are like sheep
with you as our shepherd,
and all generations
will hear us praise you.
translation_text:
Limeel li ga ban litimbol aaŋmarm na
1Uwumbɔr, binib bi kaa nyi si na koo ni saatiŋ ni.
Bi bii Saadichal li bi chain na,
le ki cha Jerusalem gur ye tilangbenn.
2Bi cha nangba mam gbaa saanib aawon,
ipeel le ŋman saatutum aanann.
3Bi cha saanib aasin nyan ke nnyun na;
nsin nan puu ni kookoo Jerusalem ponn ni ke nnyun na la,
le unii aa nan gur ke u sub ŋinikpol.
4Ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln timi na seei timi la;
bi laa timi le ki ŋani timi mbɔnyun.
5Uwumbɔr, saaŋuul ga li bi ti pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la aa?
Saaŋuul ga li beenin gaal ke mmii na la aa?
6Cha li fenn lir binib bi kaa dooni si na pu,
Cha li fenn lir binib bi kaa mee limeel tii si na pu,
7ba pu? bima le ku saanib; bi kuln saatingbaln a.
8Taa di tiyaajatiib aatunwanbir daa timi aatafal.
San timi kinimbaak dandana wee; taa ki kpa limakl libaa.
9Uwumbɔr, ter timi, ki gaa timi lii;
sin aabaa aanyuŋ pu, gaa timi lii,
ki di cha timi aatunwanbir pinn timi.
10Ni ŋa kinye aan ŋitimbol baa timi ke,
“Nimi Aawumbɔr bi la chee?”
Ŋitimbol aah cha saatutum aasin nyan pu na,
cha ti kan saah ga daa bitafal pu na.
11Li pel binib bi bi tiyondir ponn ni na aah ker idun pu na,
ki di saapɔɔn mu nyaŋ na nyan binib bi bi siin
ke bi ku bi na lii.
12Uwumbɔr, pa ŋitimbol ŋi seei si ŋisiibil mɔmɔk aabɔŋ na
nfum mulole pu baah seei si pu na.
13Le timi saanib bi ye saadiik ni yaab na,
ga doon si ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na,
ki li pak si n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ki cha.

english_text:
(A psalm by Asaph for the music leader. To the tune “Lilies of the Agreement.”)
Help Our Nation
1 Shepherd of Israel, you lead
the descendants of Joseph,
and you sit on your throne
above the winged creatures.
Listen to our prayer
and let your light shine
2for the tribes of Ephraim,
Benjamin, and Manasseh.
Save us by your power.
3Our God, make us strong again!
Smile on us and save us.
4 Lord God All-Powerful,
how much longer
will the prayers of your people
make you angry?
5You gave us tears for food,
and you made us drink them
by the bowlful.
6Because of you,
our enemies who live nearby
laugh and joke about us.
7Our God, make us strong again!
Smile on us and save us.
8We were like a grapevine
you brought out of Egypt.
You chased other nations away
and planted us here.
9Then you cleared the ground,
and we put our roots deep,
spreading over the land.
10Shade from this vine covered
the mountains.
Its branches climbed
the mighty cedars
11and stretched to the sea;
its new growth reached
to the river.
12Our Lord, why have you
torn down the wall
from around the vineyard?
You let everyone who walks by
pick the grapes.
13Now the vine is gobbled up
by pigs from the forest
and other wild animals.
14God All-Powerful,
please do something!
Look down from heaven
and see what's happening
to this vine.
15With your own hands
you planted its roots,
and you raised it
as your very own.
16Enemies chopped the vine down
and set it on fire.
Now show your anger
and destroy them.
17But help the one who sits
at your right side,
the one you raised
to be your very own.
18Then we will never turn away.
Put new life into us,
and we will worship you.
19 Lord God All-Powerful,
make us strong again!
Smile on us and save us.
translation_text:
Limeel li ban ke litimbol gir sil litaa pu na
1Israel yaab Aakikiir, li pel ni ti chee;
sin u lolni saanib pu nsan na, ŋun ni ti chee.
Sin u ka saabɔrjal pu, tiwan ni kpa ifeen na aapaacham,
2di aabaa mɔk Efraim, ni Benjaminn, ni Manase aanibol.
Mɔk timi saapɔɔn, ki nan gaa timi lii.
3Uwumbɔr, giin ni timi aabaa chee.
San timi kinimbaak, aan ti ŋmar.
4Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan,
ni ga yunn kinye aan saaŋuul ti sɔŋ saanib aameel pu?
5Aa tii timi mpombiin le ke ti ji
ki tii timi tinyunyunn kiyikusakpeŋ ni ke ti nyu.
6Aa cha ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln timi na jaa timi aatiŋ pu;
timi aadim seei timi la.
7Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, giin ni timi aabaa chee.
San timi kinimbaak, aan ti ŋmar.
8Aa nan di ŋisubil aasub nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni;
aa nan jenn nyan ŋinibol le ki di bu ŋum baatiŋ ni.
9Aa nan beer mpaan tii bu ke bu muun;
busub ngbaan aanyaan nan chɔb baan,
le bu taln gaa kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu.
10Bu aaboon nan biin ŋigongon pu;
le bu aapan too chaar santina aasui i fɔk sakpen na pu.
11Bu nan taln bu aapan ti fuu Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem na chee,
ki ti ki saa Yufrates aamɔɔl ni.
12Ba ŋa aa chuu ber idɔ i aa nan di gob bu na?
Unii umɔk jer bu chee dandana wee na ga ŋmaa su bu aasubil;
13ipɔɔgbeer le ga taa taa ŋaasubil pu, le ipeel ga li joo ŋi ŋmɔ.
14Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, fenn lik ni timi.
Aa bi paacham; li lik ni timi; dan ki nan gaa timi saanib lii.
15Ti ye saasubil aasub bu aa nan ŋum
aan bu laa ye buwaatiir,
aan aa cha bu kpa mpɔɔn na, dan ki nan gaa timi lii.
16Timi aadim gaa bu lii a, le ki see bu mmii;
di saaŋuul lik bi ki kuln bi.
17Li kii ki kaan binib bi aa lee
aan bi ye linibol li aa tii mpɔɔn na.
18Taan ki fenn tipuwɔb tii si daalbaadaal;
cha ti li kpa limɔfal aan ki pak si.
19Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan,
giin ni timi aabaa chee.
San timi kinimbaak, aan ti ŋmar.

english_text:
(By Asaph for the music leader.
)
God Makes Us Strong
1Be happy and shout to God
who makes us strong!
Shout praises to the God
of Jacob.
2Sing as you play tambourines
and the lovely sounding
stringed instruments.
3 Sound the trumpets and start
the New Moon Festival.
We must also celebrate
when the moon is full.
4This is the law in Israel,
and it was given to us
by the God of Jacob.
5The descendants of Joseph
were told to obey it,
when God led them out
from the land of Egypt.
In a voice unknown to me,
I heard someone say:
6“I lifted the burden
from your shoulder
and took the heavy basket
from your hands.
7 When you were in trouble,
I rescued you,
and from the thunderclouds,
I answered your prayers.
Later I tested you
at Meribah Spring.
8“Listen, my people,
while I, the Lord,
correct you!
Israel, if you would only
pay attention to me!
9 Don't worship foreign gods
or bow down to gods
you know nothing about.
10I am the Lord your God.
I rescued you from Egypt.
Just ask, and I will give you
whatever you need.
11“But, my people, Israel,
you refused to listen,
and you would have nothing
to do with me!
12So I let you be stubborn
and keep on following
your own advice.
13“My people, Israel,
if only you would listen
and do as I say!
14I, the Lord, would quickly
defeat your enemies
with my mighty power.
15Everyone who hates me
would come crawling,
and that would be the end
of them.
16But I would feed you
with the finest bread
and with the best honey
until you were full.”
translation_text:
Kitork aajim aalahn
1Uwumbɔr u ye timi aakikiir na pu,
di mpopiin teen mpɔɔn pu man;
gaa kipak aalahn tii Uwumbɔr. Uma le tiyaaja Jakob mu nan dii.
2Piin ŋigangan aagbaam man, ki li gbaa ŋidabun man;
li joo tibar mɔmɔk aabɔŋ gbaa ki gaa ilahn i mɔ na man.
3Pii kakaan njim ngbaan pu,
uŋmapɔɔn aayoonn, ni uŋmapiin aayoonn.
4Nimina ye nkaal le ki tii Israel yaab; Jakob Aawumbɔr le siin mu.
5Buyoonn u nan tak Ijipt yaab na, le u nan di mu tii Israel yaab.
M ŋun nneel mubaa bi len ke,
6“M chuu gaa nimi aatun ŋi nyuun na;
m cha ni tuur nimi aatun ŋi nyuun ki ye ŋitambil na bil.
7Buyoonn ni nan bi tibɔr ni na, le ni nan yin mi,
le m gaa nimi lii.
M nan bi maabɔbɔryaan mu ye kitaabuŋ ni na,
le ki kii nimi aayim ngbaan.
M nan tɔŋ nimi Meriba aanyunbun na chee.
8Maanib, li pel man tibɔr ti m joo sur nimi na;
Israel yaab, m ba gee sakpen ke ni li ŋun tii mi.
9Ni taa ki doon liwaal libaa kpala.
10Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na.
Waar nimɔi man, aan m kpiin nimi.
11Le maanib aa ŋun tii mi;
Maanib Israel yaab aa kii tii mi.
12Kina pu le m cha bi kpa tafalaaŋun
le ki ŋani baah gee pu na.
13M ba gee sakpen ke maanib li kpa ŋuntii ki tii mi;
m ba gee sakpen ke bi li keei maamɔb.
14M ba ga ŋa mala ki nyaŋ baadim, ki daa bi mɔmɔk aatafal.
15Binib bi nan mi na ba ga san ijawaan
ki nan gbaan nnimbiin ni;
baatafadaan aa ba ga li kpa ndoon.
16Le m ba ga di njikaabim mu ŋan sakpen na kpiin nimi
ki cha ni ji tisiir ti bab.”

english_text:
(A psalm by Asaph.)
Please Do Something, God!
1When all the other gods
have come together,
the Lord God judges them
and says:
2“How long will you
keep judging unfairly
and favoring evil people?
3Be fair to the poor
and to orphans.
Defend the helpless
and everyone in need.
4Rescue the weak and homeless
from the powerful hands
of heartless people.
5“None of you know
or understand a thing.
You live in darkness,
while the foundations
of the earth tremble.
6 “I, the Most High God, say
that all of you are gods
and also my own children.
7But you will die,
just like everyone else,
including powerful rulers.”
8Do something, God!
Judge the nations of the earth;
they belong to you.

(A song and a psalm by Asaph.)
God Rules All the Earth
1Our God, don't just sit there,
silently doing nothing!
2Your hateful enemies
are turning against you
and rebelling.
3They are sly, and they plot
against those you treasure.
4They say, “Let's wipe out
the nation of Israel
and make sure that no one
remembers its name!”
5All of them fully agree
in their plans against you,
and among them are
6Edom and the Ishmaelites;
Moab and the Hagrites;
7Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek;
Philistia and Phoenicia.
8Even Assyria has joined forces
with Moab and Ammon.
9 Our Lord, punish all of them
as you punished Midian.
Destroy them, as you destroyed
Sisera and Jabin
at Kishon Creek 10near Endor,
and let their bodies rot.
11 Treat their leaders as you did
Oreb and Zeeb,
Zebah and Zalmunna.
12All of them said, “We'll take
God's valuable land!”
13Our God, scatter them around
like dust in a whirlwind.
14Just as flames destroy forests
on the mountains,
15pursue and terrify them
with storms of your own.
16Make them blush with shame,
until they turn and worship
you, our Lord.
17Let them be forever ashamed
and confused.
Let them die in disgrace.
18Make them realize that you
are the Lord Most High,
the only ruler of earth!
translation_text:
Limeel li ban ke Israel yaab nyaŋ baadim na
1Uwumbɔr, taa li ŋmin; taa li si suuna ki ŋmin kina.
2Lik, saadim fii sil aa pu la, le binib bi nan si na fii sil aa pu.
3Bi bi looni ki kpokl saanib pu la;
saah kii binib bi na, le bi bi kpokl bi pu.
4Bi len le ke, “Dan man aan ti ti bii doo Israel yaab aatimbol,
aan ubaa taa ki teer bi pu
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
5Bi kpokl le ki kii tii tɔb, le ki ŋa limaantɔl ki fii sil aa pu;
6Edom ni Ismael yaab kpaani la;
le Moab yaab ni Hagar yaab kpaan;
7le Gebel yaab, ni Amonn yaab, ni Amalek yaab kpaan,
le Filistia ni Taya yaab mu kpaan.
8Asiria yaab mu kpee Amonn ni Moab yaab
bi ye Lot aayaabitiib na pu, ki pɔɔ pam.
9Ŋa bi ke saah nan ŋa Midiann yaab,
ni Sisera, ni Jabinn pu, Kisonn Aamɔɔl ni pu na.
10Aa nan nyaŋ bi Endor aatiŋ pu, le bi dɔ nima ki ti bur.
11Ŋa baayidam ke saah nan ŋa Oreb ni Seeb pu na;
nyaŋ baasalolm ke saah nan nyaŋ Seba ni Salmuna pu na.
12Bi mɔmɔk nan len ke “Ti ga gaa kitiŋ ki ye Uwumbɔr aatiŋ na.”
13Uwumbɔr, yaa bi ke kitangbaak na,
cha bi yaa ke libuln aah yaani timoor pu na.
14Mmii aah wu kichook pu na,
ni mmiigaal aah cha ŋigongon paab gaal mmii pu na,
15di saataabuŋ ki pɔɔ na jenn bi,
ki cha saabuŋ ki kpa ijawaan na faan bi.
16Uwumbɔr, cha bi kpaln binimɔɔndam,
ki cha bi bee saah kpa mpɔɔn pu na.
17Cha bi lir ki san ijawaan ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na;
cha bi kpoi nnimɔɔnkun.
18Cha bi bee ke sin baanja le ye Uwumbɔr,
ki ye kitiŋ kee aayidaan u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na.

english_text:
(For the music leader.
A psalm by the clan of Korah.)
The Joy of Worship
1 Lord God All-Powerful,
your temple is so lovely!
2Deep in my heart I long
for your temple,
and with all that I am
I sing joyful songs to you.
3 Lord God All-Powerful,
my King and my God,
sparrows find a home
near your altars;
swallows build nests there
to raise their young.
4You bless everyone
who lives in your house,
and they sing your praises.
5You bless all who depend
on you for their strength
and all who deeply desire
to visit your temple.
6When they reach Dry Valley,
springs start flowing,
and the autumn rain fills it
with pools of water.
7Your people grow stronger,
and you, the God of gods,
will be seen in Zion.
8 Lord God All-Powerful,
the God of Jacob,
please answer my prayer!
9You are the shield
that protects your people,
and I am your chosen one.
Won't you smile on me?
10One day in your temple
is better than a thousand
anywhere else.
I would rather serve
in your house,
than live in the homes
of the wicked.
11Our Lord and our God,
you are like the sun
and also like a shield.
You treat us with kindness
and with honor,
never denying any good thing
to those who live right.
12 Lord God All-Powerful,
you bless everyone
who trusts you.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr Aadichal aaneen
1Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, m gee Saadichal sakpen.
2M gee sakpen ke m li bi li ponn ni.
M neen ke m li bi Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni.
M di nsui mɔmɔk gaa mpopiin aalahn tii Uwumbɔr
u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.
3Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan u ye maabɔr ni Maawumbɔr na,
iyaar ŋa yaanyandil la, le naakpaa mam kpa bido,
baabim bi duun saatork aabimbiln la.
4Binib bi koo Saadichal ni na kpa mpopiin,
le ki gaa ilahn ki pak si n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
5Binib bi aapɔɔn nyan ni aa chee na kpa mpopiin,
le bi neen ke bi chuun buen Sionn Aajool paab.
6Baah dii Baka aafatankuun ni ki jer na,
le nima chee kpaln uyayak aanyunbun ŋmeen;
le unaalantaal cha tibɔr gbiin nima.
7Baah cha na le bi moo pɔɔk;
bi ga kan dindatiib mɔmɔk Aawumbɔr Sionn pu.
8Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, ŋun maameel.
Uwumbɔr u n‑yaaja Jakob nan dii u na, li pel.
9Uwumbɔr, ŋa saanyoor ŋa timi aabɔr u sin aabaa lee u na pu.
10M yaa bi Saadichal ponn ni nwiin mubaa kan,
ni ŋan jer ke m li bi nibaa chee iwiin lichur;
m yaa si Maawumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔb kan,
ni soor ni ke m li koo bibiindam do.
11Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le ye timi aakikiir,
ni timi aabɔr u kpa kipak sakpen na,
u ŋani timi tiŋann ki tii timi bunyuŋ.
Binib bi aabimbin ŋan na,
waa cha bi lanni tiwanyaan nibaa.
12Uwumbɔr, Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan,
binib bi tii si naadii na kpa mpopiin.

english_text:
(A psalm by the clan of Korah for the music leader.)
A Prayer for Peace
1Our Lord, you have blessed
your land
and made all go well
for Jacob's descendants.
2You have forgiven the sin
and taken away the guilt
of your people.
3Your fierce anger is no longer
aimed at us.
4Our Lord and our God,
you save us!
Please bring us back home
and don't be angry.
5Will you always be angry
with us and our families?
6Won't you give us fresh life
and let your people be glad
because of you?
7Show us your love
and save us!
8I will listen to you, Lord God,
because you promise peace
to those who are faithful
and no longer foolish.
9You are ready to rescue
everyone who worships you,
so that you will live with us
in all your glory.
10Love and loyalty
will come together;
goodness and peace
will unite.
11Loyalty will sprout
from the ground;
justice will look down
from the sky above.
12Our Lord, you will bless us;
our land will produce
wonderful crops.
13Justice will march in front,
making a path
for you to follow.
translation_text:
Litimbol aameel li ban mbimbinyaan na
1Uwumbɔr, aa san saatiŋ kinimbaak;
aa ki cha Israel yaab kan liwankpal.
2Aa di saanib aatunwanbir pinn bi,
ki di baataani mɔmɔk pinn bi.
3Aa di cha kaa ki gee bi pu liŋuul,
ki chuu saaŋuusakpeln na.
4Uwumbɔr u gaal timi lir na,
giin ni timi aabaa chee, ki cha aasui li piin ti pu.
5Saaŋuul timi pu aan doo la aa?
Saaŋuul aa kpa ndoon la aa?
6Ki tii timi mpɔɔn, aan timi saanib ga pak si.
7Uwumbɔr, mɔk timi saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na,
ki tii timi saaŋmarm aaterm.
8M bi pel Ndindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na la;
u puu ke u ga tii timi waanib nsuudoon;
ti mu taa ki gir buen timi aajɔrk ponn ni.
9Mbamɔn, binib bi nyuŋni u na, u ga sil gaa bi lii,
le waapɔɔn ga li bi timi aatiŋ ni ki gaa timi lii.
10Ngeehm ni ibamɔn ga chuu tɔb;
le mbimbinyaan ni nsuudoon ga bob tɔb.
11Unibɔn aanaadii bi taab ki likni paacham,
le Uwumbɔr aabimbinyaan bi paacham ki likni taab.
12Uwumbɔr ga tii timi liwankpal, le timi aatiŋ ŋa tijikaar pam.
13Mbimbinyaan le ga loln Uwumbɔr pu nsan, ki toor nsan tii u.

english_text:
(A prayer by David.)
A Prayer for Help
1Please listen, Lord,
and answer my prayer!
I am poor and helpless.
2Protect me and save me
because you are my God.
I am your faithful servant,
and I trust you.
3Be kind to me!
I pray to you all day.
4Make my heart glad!
I serve you,
and my prayer is sincere.
5You willingly forgive,
and your love is always there
for those who pray to you.
6Please listen, Lord!
Answer my prayer for help.
7When I am in trouble, I pray,
knowing you will listen.
8No other gods are like you;
only you work miracles.
9 You created each nation,
and they will all bow down
to worship and honor you.
10You perform great wonders
because you alone are God.
11Teach me to follow you,
and I will obey your truth.
Always keep me faithful.
12With all my heart I thank you.
I praise you, Lord God.
13Your love for me is so great
that you protected me
from death and the grave.
14Proud and violent enemies,
who don't care about you,
have ganged up to attack
and kill me.
15But you, the Lord God,
are kind and merciful.
You don't easily get angry,
and your love
can always be trusted.
16I serve you, Lord,
and I am the child
of one of your servants.
Look on me with kindness.
Make me strong and save me.
17Show that you approve of me!
Then my hateful enemies
will feel like fools,
because you have helped
and comforted me.
translation_text:
Limeel li ban nterm na
1Uwumbɔr, pel m chee ki kii maayim,
ba pu? maa kpa uteter, kaa kpa mpɔɔn mu.
2Maah keei saamɔb pu na, nyan mi nkun ni;
gaa mi lii, m ye saatutunn u tii si naadii na la.
3Aa ye Maawumbɔr la, san mi kinimbaak;
m mee si le nwiin ti lir.
4Uwumbɔr, tii mi saatutunn mpopiin,
ba pu? maameel chaa aa chee paacham.
5Aa kpa ti pu tiŋann le ki joo cha pinni timi aatunwanbir;
saageehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na bi binib bi mee si na chee.
6Uwumbɔr, pel maameel; ŋun maah wii ki ban nterm pu na.
7Saah keei maameel pu na,
le m yin si buyoonn m bi tibɔr ni na.
8Uwumbɔr, liwaal libaa aa bi ke sin na,
ubaa aa kee ŋa tiwan ni aa ŋa na.
9Saah naan ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk na ga dan
ki nan gbaan aanimbiin ni;
bi ga pak saah tun ŋitukpaan ŋi na.
10Saapɔɔn nyaŋ, le aa tun ŋitukpaan;
sin baanja le ye Uwumbɔr.
11Uwumbɔr, mɔk mi saah ban ke m tun pu na,
le m ga kii saamɔb mbamɔm;
mɔk mi saasan aan m di nsui mɔmɔk tun saatuln.
12Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, m ga di nsui mɔmɔk pak si,
m ga li mooni saah tun ŋitukpaan ŋi na pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
13Saageehm mu aa kpa m pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na nyaŋ sakpen a.
Aa nyan mi likaakul ni.
14Uwumbɔr, bigaadam choo ki ban mi la;
bibiindam le kuun ki ban bi ku mi,
bi ye binib bi aatafal aa bi aa ni na la.
15Uwumbɔr, le aa ma ye Uwumbɔr u san kinimbaak
ki kpa ngeehm na, ki kpa suklaa ni tiŋann,
ki ŋani saah puu ke aa ga ŋa pu na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
16San mi kinimbaak ki fenn lik ni mi;
gaa mi lii ki tii mi mpɔɔn, ba pu?
m ye saatutunn ki tun tii si ke unaagbiija na.
17Uwumbɔr, mɔk mi saaŋann aamɔkl;
binib bi nan mi na yaa kan ke aa ter mi
ki tii mi mmɔɔn kan, bi ga ji inimɔɔn.

english_text:
(A psalm and a song by the clan of Korah.)
The Glory of Mount Zion
1Zion was built by the Lord
on the holy mountain,
2and he loves that city
more than any other place
in all of Israel.
3Zion, you are the city of God,
and wonderful things
are told about you.
4Egypt, Babylonia, Philistia,
Phoenicia, and Ethiopia
are some of those nations
that know you,
and their people all say,
“I was born in Zion.”
5God Most High will strengthen
the city of Zion.
Then everyone will say,
“We were born here too.”
6The Lord will make a list
of his people,
and all who were born here
will be included.
7All who sing or dance will say,
“I too am from Zion.”
translation_text:
Jerusalem aapak
1Uwumbɔr maa waatiŋ ligongoln li bi chain na pu la.
2U gee Jerusalem aatiŋ jer Israel aatim mɔmɔk.
3Uwumbɔr aatiŋ, li pel waah len tibɔnyaan ti aa pu na.
4“M yaa ban m ŋmee ŋitimbol ŋi kii maamɔb na aayimbil bil kan, m ga di Ijipt ni Babiloŋ aayimbil mu kpee;
m ga kahn Filistia yaab, ni Taya yaab,
ni Kus yaab kpee Jerusalem aanib pu.”
5Bi ga len ke ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ye Sionn yaan la,
le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔndaan ga tii Sionn mpɔɔn.
6Uwumbɔr ga ŋmee binib mɔmɔk aayimbil
ki kpee Jerusalem aanib pu.
7Bi waa liwaal le ki gaa nlahn ke,
“Sionn ponn ni le timi aanyoor mɔmɔk bi.”

english_text:
(A song and a psalm by the clan of Korah for the music leader. To the tune “Mahalath Leannoth.”
A special psalm by Heman the Ezrahite.)
A Prayer When You Can't Find the Way
1You keep me safe, Lord God.
So when I pray at night,
2please listen carefully
to each of my concerns.
3I am deeply troubled
and close to death;
4I am as good as dead
and completely helpless.
5I am no better off
than those in the grave,
those you have forgotten
and no longer help.
6You have put me in the deepest
and darkest grave;
7your anger rolls over me
like ocean waves.
8You have made my friends turn
in horror from me.
I am a prisoner
who cannot escape,
9and I am almost blind
because of my sorrow.
Each day I lift my hands
in prayer to you, Lord.
10Do you work miracles
for the dead?
Do they stand up
and praise you?
11Are your love and loyalty
announced in the world
of the dead?
12Do they know of your miracles
or your saving power
in the dark world below
where all is forgotten?
13Each morning I pray
to you, Lord.
14Why do you reject me?
Why do you turn from me?
15Ever since I was a child,
I have been sick
and close to death.
You have terrified me
and made me helpless.
16Your anger is like a flood!
And I am shattered
by your furious attacks
17that strike each day
and from every side.
18My friends and neighbors
have turned against me
because of you,
and now darkness
is my only companion.
translation_text:
