Min baanja le daa taln kitaapaak;
maah nan naan kitiŋ kee na, ubaa aa nan ter mi.
25M ŋani bibɔɔb bijɔrb,
ki cha baabɔr ti bi len ke ti ga ŋa na beer fam.
M yii binimbiwolm aalan,
ki mɔk ke baalan ye kijɔrk la.
26Le maatutunn ma yaa len ke tiwan ni ga ŋa na kan,
bee m yaa ti ki tun ni maatuun
ke u nan kpiir maalandak tuk binib kan,
m cha ilandak ngbaan ni tibɔr ngbaan gbiini la.
M tuk Jerusalem ke binib ga ki gir koo ni ki ponn ni,
ki ga gir maa Juda aatisakpem na mɔmɔk.
Ntisakpem ngbaan ga fii nyan ni mu aah nan ber pu na ni.
27Maamɔb aamɔboln le m ga di foor nnyusakpem.
28Le m ga bui ubɔrkpaan Sairus ke,
‘Sin le ga joo maanib;
aa ga ŋa maah ban ke aa ŋa pu na:
aa ga cha bi ki gir maa Jerusalem,
ni Maadichal aadinyikl mu.’”

english_text:
Cyrus Obeys the Lord's Commands
1The Lord said to Cyrus, his chosen one:
I have taken hold
of your right hand
to help you capture nations
and remove kings from power.
City gates will open for you;
not one will stay closed.
2As I lead you,
I will level mountains
and break the iron bars
on bronze gates of cities.
3I will give you treasures
hidden in dark
and secret places.
Then you will know that I,
the Lord God of Israel,
have called you by name.
4Cyrus, you don't even know me!
But I have called you by name
and highly honored you
because of Israel,
my chosen servant.
5Only I am the Lord!
There are no other gods.
I have made you strong,
though you don't know me.
6Now everyone from east to west
will learn that I am the Lord.
No other gods are real.
7I create light and darkness,
happiness and sorrow.
I, the Lord, do all this.
8Tell the heavens
to send down justice
like showers of rain.
Prepare the earth
for my saving power
to sprout and produce justice
that I, the Lord, create.
The Lord's Mighty Power
The Lord said:
9 Israel, you have no right
to argue with your Creator.
You are merely a clay pot
shaped by a potter.
The clay doesn't ask,
“Why did you make me this way?
Where are the handles?”
10Children don't have the right
to demand of their parents,
“What have you done
to make us what we are?”
11I am the Lord, the Creator,
the holy God of Israel.
Do you dare question me
about my own nation
or about what I have done?
12I created the world
and covered it with people;
I stretched out the sky
and filled it with stars.
13I have done the right thing
by placing Cyrus in power,
and I will make the roads easy
for him to follow.
I am the Lord All-Powerful!
Cyrus will rebuild my city
and set my people free
without being paid a thing.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Alone Can Save
14My people, I, the Lord, promise
that the riches of Egypt
and the treasures of Ethiopia
will belong to you.
You will force into slavery
those tall people of Seba.
They will bow down and say,
“The only true God is with you;
there are no other gods.”
15People of Israel,
your God is a mystery,
though he alone can save.
16Anyone who makes idols
will be confused
and terribly disgraced.
17But Israel, I, the Lord,
will always keep you safe
and free from shame.
Everyone Is Invited
18The Lord alone is God!
He created the heavens
and made a world
where people can live,
instead of creating
an empty desert.
The Lord alone is God;
there are no others.
19The Lord did not speak
in a dark secret place
or command Jacob's descendants
to search for him in vain.
The Lord speaks the truth,
and this is what he says
20to every survivor
from every nation:
“Gather around me!
Learn how senseless it is
to worship wooden idols
or pray to helpless gods.
21“Why don't you get together
and meet me in court?
Didn't I tell you long ago
what would happen?
I am the only God!
There are no others.
I bring about justice,
and have the power to save.
22“I invite the whole world
to turn to me and be saved.
I alone am God!
No others are real.
23 I have made a solemn promise,
one that won't be broken:
Everyone will bow down
and worship me.
24They will admit that I alone
can bring about justice.
Everyone who is angry with me
will be terribly ashamed
and will turn to me.
25I, the Lord, will give
victory and great honor
to the people of Israel.”
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr lee ubɔrkpaan Sairus
1Uwumbɔr lee Sairus ke u ŋa u ubɔrkpaan.
U lee u ke u to butɔb ki nyaŋ ŋitimbol;
u tun u ke u ti nyan bibɔrb baanaan ni;
Uwumbɔr le ga piir ntisakpem aabisamɔi tii u.
Uma Uwumbɔr bui Sairus ke,
2“Min mbaa le ga toor saasan tii si,
m ga ber ŋijoo ni ŋigongon ŋi ŋa taar.
M ga kool baah di tikur ŋa ibisamɔi i na mɔmɔk.
3M ga nyan ni liwangol mbɔmbɔɔn ni ki nan tii si,
le aa bee ke min le sil ye Uwumbɔr,
ki bee ke Israel yaab Aawumbɔr ngbaan le yin si ke Sairus.
4M lee si ke aa ter maatutunn Israel aanibol,
binib bi m lee bi na.
Saa nyi mi, le m lee si ki cha aa kan kipak ni nnyuŋ.
5Min le ye Uwumbɔr, uken aa ki bi.
Saa nyi mi; m mu tee ga tii si mpɔɔn mu aa ban na.
6M ga ŋa kina ki cha dulnyaa mɔmɔk aanib bee ke
min le ye Uwumbɔr, ke uken aa ki bi.
7Min le naan nwiihn ni mbɔmbɔɔn mu;
min le joo ni tinyoor ni tibɔbir mu.
Min Uwumbɔr le ŋani nimina mɔmɔk.
8M ga cha linyaŋ nyan ni kitaapaak ke ntaanyun na;
le kitiŋ ga waar kimɔb ki gaa,
le ki kpaln lifuur ni ibamɔn ŋmeen.
Min Uwumbɔr ga cha nimina ŋa.”
Uwumbɔr le ye u naani tiwan mɔmɔk na
9Tiyakr aabuul li bi ke ŋibuu ŋiken na
ga ŋmaa kpak uyakmaal kinikpakpak aa?
Tiyakr aan ŋmaa baa uyakmaal ke u bi ŋani ba?
Libuul aan ŋmaa bui unii u
maa li na ke waa nyi nibaa.
10Ŋma ga ŋmaa baa ute ni una ke,
“Ba ŋa ni ŋa mi kina?”
11Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aadindaan u bi chain
ki ŋani n‑yoonn mu laa choo na waah gee pu na bui ke:
“Naa kpa nsan ke ni baa mi maabim aabɔr,
bee ni tuk mi maah ga ŋa pu na.
12Min le naan kitiŋ kee, le ki naan unibɔn ke u li bi ki pu.
Mbaa aapɔɔn pu le m di daa taln kitaapaak;
min le mɔk nwiin, ni uŋmal, ni iŋmabi naah ga ŋa pu na.
13Min mbaa le pɔɔk ubɔrkpaan Sairus aataakpab
ke u tun maatuln ki cha tiwan mɔmɔk sil chob.
M ga naar isan imɔk u chuun i pu aan i gɔr na.
U ga gir maa maatiŋ Jerusalem, ki gaa maanib lii.
Ubaa aa tii u ipiin ke u di tun lituln limina.”
Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.
14Uwumbɔr bui Israel yaab ke,
“Ijipt ni Kus aatim aawangol ga kpaln nimi yaan la,
le Seba aatiŋ aajab bi fɔk
sakpen na ga ŋa nimi aanaagbiib;
ni ga di tikululn le di dar bi buen.
Bi ga gbaan ninimbiin ni le ki gaŋ nimi ki bui ke,
‘Uwumbɔr bi ni chee, uma baanja le ye Uwumbɔr.
15Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u gaal waanib lir na,
u ye Uwumbɔr u bɔrni ubaa pu na la.
16Binib bi naani ŋiwaa na ga ji inimɔɔn;
bi mɔmɔk ga ji inimɔɔn.
17Le Uwumbɔr gaa Israel yaab ma lii,
le Israel yaab aanyaŋ aan li kpa ndoon;
Israel aanib aan ji inimɔɔn daalbaadaal.’”
18Uwumbɔr le naan kitaapaak, uma baanja le ye Uwumbɔr.
Uma le ŋaŋ ki naan kitiŋ kee,
u ŋa ki ki pɔɔ ki ga yunn pam.
Waa nan ŋa ki kitiŋ ki bi yɔli kaa kpa nibaa na.
U nan ŋa ki ke nin chee binib ga li koo na la.
Uma le len ke, “Min le ye Uwumbɔr,
uken aa ki bi ki kpee m pu.
19Maa bɔrni ki len maabɔr,
kaa joo maah ban m ŋa pu na mu bɔrni.
Maa nan ban ke Israel yaab lik ban mi,
kitiŋ ki kaa kpa nibaa na ni.
Min le ye Uwumbɔr, le ki len ibamɔn;
m cha ibamɔn nya mpaan pu.”
Dulnyaa Aawumbɔr ni Babiloŋ aawaa
20Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Kuun ni man tɔb chee, nimi ŋitimbol mɔk aanib;
nimi bi ga ŋmar litimbiil ngbaan aalirm ni na;
li joo ni man nibaa aan bi nan ji nimi tibɔr.
Binib bi kuun ŋiwaa ŋi bi di isui kpii ŋi na,
ki dooni ŋiwaa ŋi kaan ŋmaa gaa bi lii na,
binib ngbaan aa nyi nibaa kpala.
21Dan man ki nan di nimi aabɔr bil bibɔjirb chee;
ki cha binib bi si nipuwɔb na kpokl tɔb.
Ŋma nan len n‑yaayoonn na tiwan ni ga ŋa na?
Naa nan ye min Uwumbɔr aa?
Min le ye Uwumbɔr u ŋan ki gaal waanib lir na.
Uken aa ki bi.
22Nimi binib bi mɔmɔk bi dulnyaa wee ni na,
fenn gir ni m chee dandana aan ki ŋmar man.
Min baanja le ye Uwumbɔr u bi na.
23Maah puu tipuur ti na gbii,
kaan kpeln daalbaadaal.
M sil puu mbaa pu ke:
Unibɔn mɔmɔk ga dan nan gbaan nnimbiin ni,
ki puu ke waan nyan mpuwɔb daalbaadaal.
24Bi ga len ke min baanja pu
le unii ga ŋmaa kan linyaŋ ni mpɔɔn;
le bimɔk gee m pu liŋuul na ga ji inimɔɔn.
25Min Uwumbɔr ga gaa Israel aayaabitiib mɔmɔk lii,
le bi ga tii mi kipak.

english_text:
Babylonia's Gods Are Helpless
The Lord said:
1The gods Bel and Nebo
are down on their knees,
as wooden images of them
are carried away
on weary animals.
2They are down on their knees
to rescue the heavy load,
but the images are still taken
to a foreign country.
3You survivors in Israel,
listen to me, the Lord.
Since the day you were born,
I have carried you along.
4I will still be the same
when you are old and gray,
and I will take care of you.
I created you. I will carry you
and always keep you safe.
5Can anyone compare with me?
Is anyone my equal?
6Some people hire a goldsmith
and give silver and gold
to be formed into an idol
for them to worship.
7They carry the idol
on their shoulders,
then put it on a stand,
but it cannot move.
They call out to the idol
when they are in trouble,
but it doesn't answer,
and it cannot help.
8Now keep this in mind,
you sinful people.
And don't ever forget it.
The Lord Alone Is God
9I alone am God!
There are no other gods;
no one is like me.
Think about what happened
many years ago.
10From the very beginning,
I told what would happen
long before it took place.
I kept my word 11and brought
someone from a distant land
to do what I wanted.
He attacked from the east,
like a hawk swooping down.
Now I will keep my promise
and do what I planned.
12You people are stubborn
and far from being safe,
so listen to me.
13I will soon come to save you.
I am not far away
and will waste no time;
I take pride in Israel
and will save Jerusalem.
translation_text:
1Babiloŋ aawaa aadoon le na.
Bel ni Nebo nan ye ŋiwaa ŋi bi nan dooni ŋi na la,
le dandana ma bi di ŋi buu paan ibon pu,
ŋi gur ye ŋitun ŋi nyuun na le ki tii ibon i bak na.
2Ŋiwaa ngbaan aa ŋmaa gaa ŋibaa lii,
bi nyaŋ ŋi ki di ŋi buen a.
Babiloŋ aawaa aadoon le na.
3“Jakob aayaabitiib, nimi Israel yaab ponn ni bimɔk ŋmar na,
li pel m chee man.
Buyoonn bi nan ma nimi na,
min le nan joo nimi.
4Min le ye nimi Aawumbɔr u joo nimi na
ki ti saa buyoonn ni ga por aan niyil piir na.
Min le naan nimi le ki ga li joo nimi,
min le ga ter nimi ki gaa nimi lii.”
5Min Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ŋma aan ni ga di mi ŋaŋ udaan?
Ubaa ki bi ke min na aa?
6Binib piir baamombil aataakɔr ki nyan salmaa;
bi ŋaŋni tikunabr aanyunyuun.
Bi ga ban uchaa aan u mɔɔ bi liwaal;
le ki gbaan ki doon li.
7Bi ga yoor li ki di buŋ bibɔgbin pu,
ki ti di li siin, le li si nima,
kaan ŋmaa chuun buen nibaa chee.
Unii yaa mee li kan, laan ŋmaa kii,
kaan ŋmaa nyan u tibɔbir ni.
8Nimi titunwanbirdam, teer man tibɔr timina;
dakl lik maah ŋa pu na man.
9Teer man tibɔr ti nan ŋa n‑yoonn na;
tii naadii man ke min baanja le ye Uwumbɔr,
ke ubaa aa ki bi ke min na.
10Mpiin na le m nan len tiwan ni ga dan na;
n‑yoonn mu jer na m nan len tiwan ni ga ŋa na.
M nan len ke maalandak aan bee yɔli,
ke m ga ŋa maah dak pu na mɔmɔk.
11M bi yin ni uja ubaa ke u nya ni liwipuul wɔb;
u ga boon ni ke kaasaa na ki nan ŋa maah dak pu na.
Min le len, le ni ga ŋa kina.
12Nimi binib bi aatafal pɔɔ
aan ni dak ke linyaŋ chee daa na,
li pel ni m chee man.
13M joo linyaŋ aawiin mar ni la, mu aa ki daa kpala.
Maanyaŋ aan ki yunn kpala.
M ga gaa Jerusalem aatiŋ lii,
ki joo ni Israel yaab kipak nima.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Fall
The Lord said:
1 City of Babylon,
You are delicate
and untouched,
but that will change.
Surrender your royal power
and sit in the dirt.
2Start grinding grain!
Take off your veil.
Strip off your fancy clothes
and wade across rivers.
3You will suffer the shame
of going naked,
because I will take revenge,
and no one can escape.
4I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the holy God of Israel.
I am their Savior.
5Babylon, be silent!
Sit in the dark.
No longer will nations
accept you as their queen.
6I was angry with my people.
So I let you take their land
and bring disgrace on them.
You showed them no mercy,
but were especially cruel
to those who were old.
7You thought that you
would be queen forever.
You didn't care what you did;
it never entered your mind
that you might get caught.
8 You think that you alone
are all-powerful,
that you won't be a widow
or lose your children.
All you care about is pleasure,
but listen to what I say.
9Your magic powers and charms
will suddenly fail,
then you will be a widow
and lose your children.
10You hid behind evil
like a shield and said,
“No one can see me!”
You were fooled by your wisdom
and your knowledge;
you felt sure that you alone
were in full control.
11But without warning,
disaster will strike—
and your magic charms
won't help at all.
12Keep using your magic powers
and your charms
as you have always done.
Maybe—just maybe—
you will frighten somebody!
13You have worn yourself out,
asking for advice
from those who study the stars
and tell the future
month after month.
Go ask them how to be saved
from what will happen.
14People who trust the stars
are as helpless as straw
in a flaming fire.
No one can even keep warm,
sitting by a fire
that feeds only on straw.
15These are the fortunetellers
you have done business with
all of your life.
But they don't know
where they are going,
and they can't save you.
translation_text:
Babiloŋ aabɔjil
1Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Babiloŋ aatiŋ, sunn ni saabɔrjal pu,
ki nan kal kitiŋ, titan ni.
N‑yoonn mubaa aa nan naahn upii u kaa nyi uja na la,
kitiŋ ki ubaa aa kee nyaŋ ki na,
le dandana ma, saa ki pɔɔn, kaa ki ŋan mu.
Aa gur ye unaagbiipii la.
2Chuu labr kinaak ngbaan.
Nan n‑yon.
Chuu nyan saah di likekeln li bii aanimbil wɔb na.
Chuu gbabr saakekenyaan ngbaan.
Chuu kuun saawando mam ki puur ikpen.
3Binib ga kan saah chuun aaŋmeen pu na;
bi ga kan ke bi jinn si inimɔɔn ki sunn si taab.
M mu ga giin si mbiin mu aa ŋa mi na,
le ubaa aan ŋmaa bui mi ke m di cha si.”
4Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na le gaal timi lir.
Waayimbil le ye ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan.
5Uwumbɔr bui Babiloŋ aatiŋ ke,
“Kal suuna mbɔmbɔɔn ni,
ubaa aan ki yin si ke ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aapiibɔr.
6M nan gee liŋuul maanib pu;
ki ŋa bi ke baa kaa ye maanib le na:
M nan di bi ŋa saapɔɔn ni, le saa san bi kinimbaak;
hali aa nan muk binib bi por na.
7Aa nan dak ke aa ga li ye upiibɔr le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,
kaa di tibaa ŋa aasui ni,
kaa dakl lik naah ga nan doo pu na.
8Li pel nimina, sin u gee mmɔɔn sakpen na,
sin u dak ke aa pɔɔ ki ŋmar na.
Aa bui ke aa kpa mpɔɔn ke Uwumbɔr na,
ke ubaa aa ki bi ke sin na.
Aa nan dak ke saan ŋa ukpopii daalbaadaal, kaan lann mbim.
9Naan yunn, liwinbaal le aa ga lann tiwan nilee ngbaan mɔmɔk.
Hali saah kpa inyɔk i na aan ter si,
le aa ga lann chal ni mbim mɔmɔk.
10Aa nan dak ke aa ŋmar saatunwanbir ni a;
aa nan nyi ke ubaa aan kan si.
Saalan ni saachiin le ŋmann si koon timoor ni,
le aa bui aabaa ke,
‘M ye Uwumbɔr la,
ubaa aa ki bi ke min na.’
11Tibɔbir ga dan aa pu,
le saanyɔk ngbaan mubaa aan ŋmaa kiir ti.
Nfum mubaa le tibɔbir ga lir ni aa pu,
tibɔbir ti saa kee dakl ti pu
daalbaadaal na le ga lir aa pu.
12Li joo saanyɔk mɔmɔk, ki chaa bibɔɔb chee;
saah fii ubo pu na le aa nan ŋani kina.
Nibaakan, ni ga ŋmaa ter si siib;
nibaakan, aa ga ŋmaa faan saadim.
13Hali saah kani nsurm mumɔk na, saa kpa mpɔɔn mubaa.
Cha saanib bi lik iŋmabi ki buu tibɔɔr na dan ki nan gaa si lii,
bima le bui ke bi ye binib bi bae iŋmabi,
ki nyi kitaapaak aapepel mɔmɔk,
ki tuk si uŋmal ki ti saa uŋmal tiwan ni ga ŋa si na.
14Bi ga li bi ke tigbengbir na la, le mmii ga wu ti.
Baan ŋmaa gaa bibaa lii,
imiigaal ngbaan ga li ton bi chee sakpen,
naan li ye mmii mu ton pulpul aan bi wor mu na.
15Binib bi lik iŋmabi ki buu tibɔɔr
aan aa di aabaa tii bi saamɔfal
mɔmɔk ni na aan ŋmaa ter si.
Bi ga san ki buen baah nyi nin chee na ki cha si,
hali bi ponn ni ubaa aan gur ke u gaa si lii.”

english_text:
The Lord Corrects His People
1People of Israel,
you come from Jacob's family
and the tribe of Judah.
You claim to worship me,
the Lord God of Israel,
but you are lying.
2You call Jerusalem your home
and say you depend on me,
the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel.
3Long ago I announced
what was going to be,
then without warning,
I made it happen.
4I knew you were stubborn
and hardheaded.
5And I told you these things,
so that when they happened
you would not say,
“The idols we worship did this.”
6You heard what I said,
and you have seen it happen.
Now admit it's true!
I will show you secrets
you have never known.
7Today I am doing something new,
something you cannot say
you have heard before.
8You have never been willing
to listen to what I say;
from the moment of your birth,
I knew you would rebel.
The Lord Warns Israel
9I, the Lord, am true to myself;
I will be praised for not punishing
and destroying you.
10I tested you in hard times
just as silver is refined
in a heated furnace.
11I did this because of who I am.
I refuse to be dishonored
or share my praise
with any other god.
12 Israel, my chosen people,
listen to me.
I alone am the Lord,
the first and the last.
13With my own hand
I created the earth
and stretched out the sky.
They obey my every command.
The Lord Speaks to the Nations
14Gather around me, all of you!
Listen to what I say.
Did any of your idols
predict this would happen?
Did they say that my friend
would do what I want done
to Babylonia?
15I was the one who chose him.
I have brought him this far,
and he will be successful.
16Come closer and listen!
I have never kept secret
the things I have said,
and I was here
before time began.
It Is Best To Obey the Lord
By the power of his Spirit
the Lord God has sent me
17with this message:
People of Israel,
I am the holy Lord God,
the one who rescues you.
For your own good,
I teach you, and I lead you
along the right path.
18How I wish that you
had obeyed my commands!
Your success and good fortune
would then have overflowed
like a flooding river.
19Your nation would be blessed
with more people
than there are grains of sand
along the seashore.
And I would never have let
your country be destroyed.
20 Now leave Babylon!
Celebrate as you go.
Be happy and shout
for everyone to hear,
“The Lord has rescued
his servant Israel!
21He led us through the desert
and made water flow from a rock
to satisfy our thirst.
22 But the Lord has promised
that none who are evil
will live in peace.”
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr le ye n‑yoonn mu choo na Aadindaan
1Nimi Israel aanib bi ye Juda aayaabitiib na,
li pel man tibɔr tee:
Ni puu tipuur Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu,
ki bui ke ni dooni nimi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr la,
le naa bi nisui ni kpala.
2Le ni tee mak ke ni ye Uwumbɔr aatisakpeŋ aanib la,
le ki tii Israel yaab Aawumbɔr naadii;
waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan.
3Uwumbɔr bui Israel yaab ke,
“N‑yoonn mu jer na le m nan len tiwan ni ga ŋa na;
le m kpaan cha ni ŋa.
4M nan nyi ke nitafal ga li pɔɔ ke kikurk na,
kaan li kool ke tikumann aakur na.
5Le m nan puun len nimi aabimbin aah bi pu na n‑yoonn mu jer na,
ki mooni tibɔr aan ti nin ŋa,
ke m kiir nimi aan ni taa bui ke nimi aawaa le ŋa ti.
6Tibɔr timɔk m nan puun len ke ti ga ŋa na mɔmɔk ŋa kina;
kina pu na, ni ga kii ke maah nan len pu na ye ibamɔn.
Dandana ma, m ga bui nimi tiwachann ni ga dan na la,
tiwan ni maa nan kpiir mɔk nimi na.
7Dandana baanja le m bi cha ni ŋani;
kina aawan aa kee ŋa.
Ni yaa ba ŋa kan, ni ba ga bui ke ni puun nyi ni pu a.
8M nan nyi ke naa ye binib bi unii ga gaa nimi ki kii na,
ke unii mɔk nyi ni pu,
ke ni ye binib bi kaa kii tii biken na la.
Kina pu le naa ŋun kina aabɔr,
nima le cha nitafal aa cheen kina aabɔr daalbaadaal.
9Maah ban ke binib nyuŋ maayimbil na,
nima le m chur maaŋuul;
m kiir li ke m taa kuln nimi la.
10M tɔŋ nimi falaa aamii ni,
ke baah pu tikunabr mmii ni pu na,
le ki kan ke naa kpa tinyoor tibaa.
11Maah ŋani tiwan nimɔk na, m ŋani mbaa pu la.
Maa ban ke m bii maayimbil,
kaa ban ke ubaa yakr m chee kipak;
ki ga li ye min baanja aapak la.”
Sairus, unii u Uwumbɔr lee ke u li ye usaloln na
12Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Israel aanib, binib bi m yin bi na, li pel m chee,
Min le ye Uwumbɔr u ye mpiin ngbaan, ni ndoon ngbaan na, Uwumbɔr baan ngbaan.
13Maaŋaal le nan naan taab aatinyikl, ki daa taln kitaapaak.
M yaa yin kitiŋ ni kitaapaak kan,
ni choo mala le ki nan sil nnimbiin ni.
14Ni mɔmɔk kuun ni man ki nan pel.
Ŋiwaa ngbaan ponn ni libaa aa nan ŋmaa len
ke uja u m lee u na ga nan tak Babiloŋ aatiŋ;
u ga ŋa maah tuk u ke u ŋa pu na.
15Min le nan len ki yin u;
m loln u pu nsan ki cha u kan maah ban pu na.
16Dandana, foor mar ni m chee man ki nan pel maah ga len pu na.
Ki nyan mpiin ngbaan m len maabɔr chain la,
le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk m cha maah len pu na gbiini.”
Tɔ, Ndindaan Uwumbɔr tii mi Waafuur Nyaan le ki tun mi.
Uwumbɔr aah ga ter waanib pu na
17Nimi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na,
Uwumbɔr u gaal nimi lir na bui ke;
“Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u ban ke u mɔk nimi mbimbinyaan,
ki mɔk nimi nsan mu pu ni ga dii na.
18Ni yaa nan ba pel maah tuk nimi pu na kan,
le tinyoor ba ga li puu choo ni chee,
ke nkpen mu aanyun aa foor na.
Linyaŋ ba ga dan ni chee,
ke nnyusakpem aanyunkpenn na la.
19Niyaabitiib ba ga li wiir ke limɔɔtambol na la,
le m ba ga li kii bi, ubaa taa bii bi.”
20Nya Babiloŋ ni man, li cha man, ni fuur a.
Li kpa mpopiin man ki moon tibɔpɔnn ngbaan,
cha bi ŋun ni kookoo man ke,
“Uwumbɔr gaa waatutunn Israel aanibol lii a.”
21Uwumbɔr aah nan di waanib dii nteersakpiin mu ton
ki kuun na ni na, baa nan kan nnyunyuu aafalaa.
U nan cha nnyun nyan ni litakpal ni ki tii bi;
u nan gaa lar litakpal ngbaan le nnyun puu nyan ni.
22Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Titunwanbirdam aa kpa nsuudoon.”

english_text:
The Work of the Lord's Servant
1 Everyone, listen,
even you foreign nations
across the sea.
The Lord chose me
and gave me a name
before I was born.
2 He made my words pierce
like a sharp sword
or a pointed arrow;
he kept me safely hidden
in the palm of his hand.
3The Lord said to me,
“Israel, you are my servant;
and because of you
I will be highly honored.”
4I said to myself,
“I'm completely worn out;
my time has been wasted.
But I did it for the Lord God,
and he will reward me.”
5Even before I was born,
the Lord God chose me
to serve him and to lead back
the people of Israel.
So the Lord has honored me
and made me strong.
6 Now the Lord says to me,
“It isn't enough for you
to be merely my servant.
You must do more than lead back
survivors from the tribes
of Israel.
I have placed you here as a light
for other nations;
you must take my saving power
to everyone on earth.”
The Lord Will Rescue His People
7Israel, I am the holy Lord God,
the one who rescues you.
You are slaves of rulers
and of a nation
who despises you.
Now this is what I promise:
Kings and rulers will honor you
by kneeling at your feet.
You can trust me! I am your Lord,
the holy God of Israel,
and you are my chosen ones.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
8 This is what the Lord says:
I will answer your prayers
because I have set a time
when I will help
by coming to save you.
I have chosen you
to take my promise of hope
to other nations.
You will rebuild the country
from its ruins,
then people will come
and settle there.
9You will set prisoners free
from dark dungeons
to see the light of day.
On their way home,
they will find plenty to eat,
even on barren hills.
10 They won't go hungry
or get thirsty;
they won't be bothered
by the scorching sun
or hot desert winds.
I will be merciful
while leading them along
to streams of water.
11I will level the mountains
and make roads.
12Then my people will return
from distant lands
in the north and the west
and from the city of Syene.
The Lord's Mercy
13Tell the heavens and the earth
to celebrate and sing;
command every mountain
to join in the song.
The Lord's people have suffered,
but he has shown mercy
and given them comfort.
14The people of Zion said,
“The Lord has turned away
and forgotten us.”
15The Lord answered,
“Could a mother forget a child
who nurses at her breast?
Could she fail to love an infant
who came from her own body?
Even if a mother could forget,
I will never forget you.
16A picture of your city
is drawn on my hand.
You are always in my thoughts!
17“Your city will be built faster
than it was destroyed—
those who attacked it
will retreat and leave.
18Look around! You will see
your people coming home.
As surely as I live,
I, the Lord, promise
that your city with its people
will be as lovely as a bride
wearing her jewelry.”
Jerusalem's Bright Future
19Jerusalem is now in ruins!
Nothing is left of the city.
But it will be rebuilt
and soon overcrowded;
its cruel enemies
will be gone far away.
20Jerusalem is a woman
whose children were born
while she was in deep sorrow
over the loss of her husband.
Now those children
will come and seek room
in the crowded city,
21and Jerusalem will ask,
“Am I really their mother?
How could I have given birth
when I was still mourning
in a foreign land?
Who raised these children?
Where have they come from?”
22 The Lord God says:
“I will soon give a signal
for the nations
to return your sons
and your daughters
to the arms of Jerusalem.
23The kings and queens
of those nations
where they were raised
will come and bow down.
They will take care of you
just like a slave
taking care of a child.
Then you will know
that I am the Lord.
You won't be disappointed
if you trust me.”
The Lord Is on Our Side
24Is it possible to rescue victims
from someone strong
and cruel?
25But the Lord has promised
to fight on our side
and to rescue our children
from those strong
and violent enemies.
26He will make those cruel people
dine on their own flesh
and get drunk from drinking
their own blood.
Then everyone will know
that the Lord is our Savior;
the powerful God of Israel
has rescued his people.
translation_text:
Israel le ye ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aawiihn
1Nimi ŋitimbol ŋi bi dandar na, li pel man,
nimi binib bi koo dandar na, li pel man.
Waahr aan bi nin ma mi na, le Uwumbɔr nan lee mi,
ki di mi siin ke m li ye waatutunn.
2U cha maamɔliin ka ke kijaak aajuk na.
U nan joo mi uŋaal ni ki bɔr mi.
U naan mi ke mpiin mu ka ki ŋeer bi too mu na la.
3U nan bui mi ke, “Israel aanibol, sin le ye maatutunn;
sin pu, le binib mɔmɔk ga pak mi.”
4Le m bui ke, “M tun pam, le naa kpa tinyoor.
Maapɔɔn mɔmɔk doo a, le maa nyan tinyoor tibaa.”
Le m tee kpa limakl ke Uwumbɔr ga sil mpuwɔb;
u ga pa mi maah tun pu na pu.
5Waahr aan bi nin ma mi na, Uwumbɔr nan nyan mi siin;
u nan ŋa mi waatutunn ke m giin ni waanib,
ke m giin ni waanib Israel yaab bi yaa na.
Uwumbɔr nyuŋni mi; uma le tii mi mpɔɔn.
6Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“M kpa lituln li pɔɔ na ke sin maatutunn tun.
Naa ye ke aa giin Israel yaab
bi ŋmar na aapɔɔn tii bi baanja,
m ga cha aa li ye ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aawiihn
ki tii dulnyaa aanib mɔmɔk nsan ke bi ŋmar.”
7Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain, ki gaal bi lir na
bui baah lik unii u fam na,
aan ŋinibol mɔmɔk yii u,
aan u ye bitinjoob aanaagbiija na ke:
“Bibɔrb ga kan ke aa nyan saamuk ni
le ki ga fii sil ki tii si kipak;
Kitiŋ aajojoob mu ga kan kina,
le ki gbaan kitiŋ ki nyuŋ si.”
Uwumbɔr aah lee waatutunn pu na le ga cha kina ŋa;
Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain
na joo waah puu tipuur ti na la.
Jerusalem aah gir sil mpɔɔn pu pu na
8Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke,
“Ni yaa ŋeer ke m gaa nimi lii kan,
le m ga san nimi kinimbaak, aan ki pel nimi aameel.
M ga li kii nimi ki joo nimi
le ki puu tipuur tii binib mɔmɔk, nimi pu.
M ga cha ni ki gir kal nimi aatiŋ ki dɔ fam dandana na pu.
9M ga bui biyom ke, ‘Li cha man, ni fuur a,’
ki bui binib bi bi mbɔmbɔɔn ni na ke,
‘Dan nwiihn ni man.’
Bi ga li naahn ipiih i ŋmɔ timoor ŋigongon paab na la;
10nkon ni nnyunyuu aan ki chuu bi.
Le nwiin, ni nteersakpiin pu aatotoŋ aan ki see bi,
ba pu? u gee bi na le ga li joo bi.
U ga mɔk bi uyayak aanyunbun chee.
11M ga naan nsan mu waa na ŋijoo paab,
ki toor nsan tii maanib aan bi dii.
12Maanib ga nyan ni dandar,
bi ga nya ni ŋŋangan wɔb ni liwilir wɔb,
ki nya ni Aswann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na.”
13Kitaapaak ni taab, li gaa mpopiin aalahn man.
Cha ŋijoo li gaa ilahn man.
Uwumbɔr ga sɔŋ waanib aasui;
u ga san waanib bi bi falaa ni na kinimbaak.
14Le Jerusalem aanib bui ke,
“Uwumbɔr san cha timi a.
Waa ki nyi ti bɔr.”
15Le Uwumbɔr gar ke,
“Upii ga ŋmaa suln waabo bɔr,
kaan li gee ubo u u ma na aa?
Hali upii yaa suln waabo bɔr kan, mma aan suln ni bɔr.
16Jerusalem, maan ŋmaa suln nibɔr.
M ŋmee nimi aayimbil paan ŋŋaal pu.
17Binib bi ga ki gir maa Jerusalem aatiŋ siin na ga fuu ni dandana,
le binib bi nan bii si na ga nya.
18Fenn ki lik tiwan ni bi ŋani na.
Saanib bi kuuni tɔb chee, ki choo kun ni la.
Maah po ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu na,
kina le aa ga li kpa limakl saanib pu,
ke ubɔndinn aah mak waaleenyaan pu pu na.
19Saatingbaln nan bii ki kuln, le dandana ma li ga li par
ki tii binib bi choo bi nan koo li ponn ni na.
Le binib bi nan kuln saatingbaln ngbaan na
ga li gur daa aa chee.
20Saanib bi bi ti ma bi tinaagbiir ponn ni na
ga nan bui si daalbaadaal ke,
‘Kitiŋ kee par sakpen a.
Kpee timi kitiŋ aan ti koo ki ni.’
21Le aa ga bui ke;
‘Ŋma ma mbim mue mɔmɔk tii mi?
Maabim nan wɔŋ, le maa nan ki ŋmaa ma biken.
Bi nan di mi buen tinaagbiir ni;
ŋma kpiin mbim mue?
M nan gur mbaa baanja la,
mbim mue mɔmɔk nyan ni la chee?’”
22Tidindaan Uwumbɔr bui waatimbol ke:
“M ga tii ŋitimbol limɔkl
aan bi kunn ni saabim.
23Bibɔrkpaam ga li naahn aatetiib la;
le bipiibɔrb naahn aanatiib.
Bi ga sunn bibaa taab aanimbiin ni ki nyuŋ si;
bi ga sunn bibaa taab ki mɔk si baapak,
le aa bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr;
unii umɔk ka kii maaterm na aan lir.”
24Aa ga ŋmaa gaa butɔb aaja chee
waah gaa tiwan ni kijaak ni na aa?
Aa ga ŋmaa gaa biyom mbiindaan chee ee?
25Le Uwumbɔr giin kii ke,
“Kina le sil ga ŋa.
Bi ga gaa butɔb aaja chee biyom,
ki gaa ubiindaan chee waah gaa tiwan ni kijaak ni na.
Unii umɔk tak si na, m ni udaan ga jan,
le m ga gaa saabim lii.
26M ga cha binib bi muk si na ku tɔb ki ŋmɔ tɔb;
bi ga nyun tɔb aasin gbii ke baah nyun ndaan le na.
Le unibɔn mɔmɔk bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr u gaal si lir
ki cha aa fuur na.
Bi ga bee ke min le ye Israel yaab
Aawumbɔr u kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na.”

english_text:
The Lord's Power To Punish
1 The Lord says, “Children,
I didn't divorce your mother
or sell you to pay debts;
I divorced her and sold you
because of your sins.
2I came and called out,
but you didn't answer.
Have I lost my power
to rescue and save?
At my command oceans and rivers
turn into deserts;
fish rot and stink
for lack of water.
3I make the sky turn dark
like the sackcloth
you wear at funerals.”
God's Servant Must Suffer
4The Lord God gives me
the right words
to encourage the weary.
Each morning he awakens me
eager to learn his teaching;
5he made me willing to listen
and not rebel or run away.
6 I let them beat my back
and pull out my beard.
I didn't turn aside
when they insulted me
and spit in my face.
7But the Lord God keeps me
from being disgraced.
So I refuse to give up,
because I know
God will never let me down.
8 My protector is nearby;
no one can stand here
to accuse me of wrong.
9The Lord God will help me
and prove I am innocent.
My accusers will wear out
like moth-eaten clothes.
10None of you respect the Lord
or obey his servant.
You walk in the dark
instead of the light;
you don't trust the name
of the Lord your God.
11Go ahead and walk in the light
of the fires you have set.
But with his own hand,
the Lord will punish you
and make you suffer.
translation_text:
1Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ni dak ke m jenn maanib lii
ke uja aah jenni upuu lir pu na la aa?
Seeraa aagbann ti ga mɔk ke m jenn bi lii na bi la?
Ni dak ke m di nimi kooh ŋa tinaagbiir ni
ke uja aah kooh waabim ŋani tinaagbiir ni pu na la aa?
Aayii, ni nan buen tinaagbiir ni nimi aatunwanbir pu la;
nimi aabakaa pu le m nan jenn nimi buen.
2Ba nan ŋa maanib yii kaa kii tii mi
buyoonn m nan buen m ti gaa bi lii na?
Ba nan ŋa baa kii buyoonn m nan yin bi na?
Maa ki kpa mpɔɔn m di gaa bi lii la aa?
Maamɔliin baanja le ga cha nnyusakpem foor,
ki cha ŋimɔɔ mɔmɔk kpaln kitikuun,
le ŋaajan kpo nnyunyuu pu.
3M ga ŋmaa cha kitaapaak bɔln,
ke kaah bi wii binib bi kpo na aakpowiil le na.”
Uwumbɔr aatutunn aah pak u pu na
4Tidindaan Uwumbɔr mɔk mi maah ga len pu na
aan ki pɔɔk binib bi aataakpab yɔl na aataakpab.
U cha m jek ke m pel
waah ban u mɔk mi pu na kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni.
5Uwumbɔr tii mi ntafaŋum,
le m kii kaa yii waamɔb,
kaa fenn mpuwɔb tii u.
6M di mpuwɔb tii binib bi gbaa mi na.
Maa nan bui binib bi seei mi ki dar gui maalangbaln aakor
ki teei timɔɔtan lɔi mi na ke bi di cha.
7Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ter mi pu na,
baasiibil aan ŋa mi nibaa.
M gor mbaa ki kii ke m gaa ŋi,
m nyi ke maan ji inimɔɔn,
8ba pu? Uwumbɔr bi m chee,
ki ga mɔk ke maa tun taani ubaa.
Ŋma ga ŋmaa galn mi?
Udaan cha ti kpaan ki buen libɔjil ni.
U li joo ni ngalm mu u kpa na.
9Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le si mpuwɔb.
Ŋma ki bi ki ga mɔk ke maabɔr aa ŋan?
Bi mɔmɔk ga wɔŋ doo;
bi ga wɔŋ ke ŋikpandakur aah ŋman likekeln li na
aah ga char char pu na la.
10Nimi bi mɔmɔk pak Uwumbɔr ki kii waatutunn aabɔr na,
nibaakan ni ga li chuun isan i bɔɔn na ni,
ni mu tee tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr naadii,
ki li mak u pu.
11Nimi bi mɔmɔk dak ke ni bii biken doo na,
nimi nibaa aalandak ngbaan le ga doo nimi.
Uwumbɔr ubaa le ga cha kina ŋa;
ni ga ji falaa sakpen.

english_text:
The Lord Will Bring Comfort
1 If you want to do right
and obey the Lord,
follow Abraham's example.
He was the rock from which
you were chipped.
2God chose Abraham and Sarah
to be your ancestors.
The Lord blessed Abraham,
and from that one man
came many descendants.
3Though Zion is in ruins,
the Lord will bring comfort,
and the city will be as lovely
as the garden of Eden
that he provided.
Then Zion will celebrate;
it will be thankful
and sing joyful songs.
The Lord's Victory Will Last
4The Lord says:
You are my people and nation!
So pay attention to me.
My teaching will cause justice
to shine like a light
for every nation.
5Those who live across the sea
are eagerly waiting
for me to rescue them.
I am strong and ready;
soon I will come to save
and to rule all nations.
6Look closely at the sky!
Stare at the earth.
The sky will vanish like smoke;
the earth will wear out
like clothes.
Everyone on this earth
will die like flies.
But my victory will last;
my saving power never ends.
7If you want to do right
and obey my teaching
with all your heart,
then pay close attention.
Don't be discouraged
when others insult you
and say hurtful things.
8They will be eaten away
like a moth-eaten coat.
But my victory will last;
my saving power
will never end.
A Prayer for the Lord's Help
9Wake up! Do something, Lord.
Be strong and ready.
Wake up! Do what you did
for our people long ago.
Didn't you chop up
Rahab the monster?
10Didn't you dry up the deep sea
and make a road for your people
to follow safely across?
11Now those you have rescued
will return to Jerusalem,
singing on their way.
They will be crowned
with great happiness,
never again to be burdened
with sadness and sorrow.
The Lord Gives Hope
12I am the Lord, the one
who encourages you.
Why are you afraid
of mere humans?
They dry up and die like grass.
13I spread out the heavens
and laid foundations
for the earth.
But you have forgotten me,
your Lord and Creator.
All day long you were afraid
of those who were angry
and hoped to oppress you.
Where are they now?
14Everyone crying out in pain
will be quickly set free;
they will be rescued
from the power of death
and never go hungry.
15I will help them
because I am your God,
the Lord All-Powerful,
who makes the ocean roar.
16I have told you what to say,
and I will keep you safe
in the palm of my hand.
I spread out the heavens
and laid foundations
for the earth.
Now I say, “Jerusalem,
your people are mine.”
A Warning to Jerusalem
17 Jerusalem, wake up! Stand up!
You've drunk too much
from the cup filled
with the Lord's anger.
You have swallowed every drop,
and you can't walk straight.
18Not one of your many children
is there to guide you
or to offer a helping hand.
19You have been destroyed
by war and by famine;
I cannot comfort you.
20The Lord your God is angry,
and on every street corner
your children lie helpless,
like deer trapped in nets.
21You are in trouble and drunk,
but not from wine.
So pay close attention
22to the Lord your God,
who defends you and says,
“I have taken from your hands
the cup filled with my anger
that made you drunk.
You will never be forced
to drink it again.
23Instead I will give it
to your brutal enemies,
who treated you like dirt
and walked all over you.”
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr sɔŋ Jerusalem yaab aasui
1Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Li pel man, nimi bi ban ke ni ŋmar na,
nimi bi choo m chee ki ban nterm na, li pel man.
Dakl ki lik man litakpal li ponn ni ni nyan ni na,
nin chee m nan gbii nyan nimi na.
2Dakl ki lik man niyaaja Abraham aabɔr,
ni Sara, niyaa u ma nimi na.
Maah nan yin Abraham na, waa nan kpa ubo,
le m tii mmɔɔnyunsɔm ŋa upuu pu ki tii u mbim;
m cha uyaabitiib wiir sakpen.
3M ga san Jerusalem yaab kinimbaak,
ni bimɔk koo kaalangbenn ni na.
Kitiŋ ngbaan gur ye nteer la,
le m ga ŋa ki tikpin aasaak;
ki ga li naahn maah nan ŋa ki Edenn ni na la.
Mpopiin ni mmɔɔn ŋmeen le ga li bi ki ni,
le bi ga li gaa kipak ni idoon aalahn ki pak mi.
4Maanib, li pel man,
li pel maah len pu na man:
M joo maamɔkm tii ŋitimbol mɔmɔk;
maakaal ga woln binimbil.
5M ga dan mala ki nan gaa bi lii;
n‑yoonn mu m ga di nyaŋ binib na ŋɔŋni a.
Min mbaa le ga li joo ŋitimbol mɔmɔk.
Ntim mu bi dandar na aanib ka kii mi ke m dan;
bi ka kii mi, ki kpa limakl ke m ga nan gaa bi lii.
6Waan lik kitaapaak ngbaan;
lik taab mu,
kitaapaak ngbaan ga wɔŋ ke iŋmanyuu na;
le kitiŋ mu ga ji deer ki ti doo ke likekekpokl na,
le kaanib ga kpoi ke tisibir na.
Le maah ga joo ni ŋŋmarm mu na aan li kpa ndoon;
maanyaŋ mu aan li kpa ndoon.
7Li pel man, nimi bi nyi tiwan ni ye mbamɔn na,
binib bi di maamɔkm ŋa bisui ni na, li pel man.
Binib yaa ŋani nimi mbɔnyun ki seei nimi kan,
ni taa san ijawaan;
8bi ga dur ke ŋikpandakur aah ŋman likekeln li na
aah ga dur pu na la.
Le maah ga joo ni ŋŋmarm mu na aan li kpa ndoon;
maanyaŋ ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
9Uwumbɔr, fii ki ter timi.
Di saapɔɔn gaa timi lii;
ter timi ke saah nan ŋa pu n‑yaayoonn na.
Sin le nan chɔi chɔi nnyusakpem ni aapeewanbiik Rahab.
10Ni nan ki ye sin le cha nnyusakpem aanyun foor
le ki ŋa nsan mu ponn ni,
aan saah nan bi gaal binib bi lir na ŋmaa puur.
11Saah gaa binib bi lii na ga di mpopiin fuu Jerusalem,
ki ga li gaa ilahn ki tar ni mpopiin.
Bi ga li kpa mpopiin n‑yoonn mɔmɔk;
bi ga nya kinimbaak, ni mpombiin ponn ni
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
12Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Min le pɔɔk nitaakpab.
Ba ŋa ni san unibɔn u ga kpo na ijawaan?
Ba ŋa ni san unibɔn u ga kpo mala ke timoor na?
13Ni suln Uwumbɔr u naan nimi na bɔr aa?
Uma le nan daa taln kitaapaak, ki baan kitiŋ aatinyikl.
Ba ŋa ni san ijawaan n‑yoonn mɔmɔk
binib bi muk nimi na aaŋuul pu,
ki san binib bi ban bi ku doo nimi na?
Baaŋuul aan ki pii nimi daalbaadaal.
14Binib bi ye biyom na, m ga gaa bi lii dandana;
bi ga kan limɔfal li fɔk na,
ki kan tijikaar timɔk bi ban na.
15Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr;
Min le kur nnyusakpem,
le ki cha mu aanyunkpenn kpa kifuuk,
Maayimbil le ye ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan.
16Min le daa taln kitaapaak,
le ki baan kitiŋ aatinyik;
le m bui Jerusalem yaab ke, ‘Nimi le ye maanib.
M tii nimi maamɔkm, le ki joo ŋŋaal kii nimi.’”
Jerusalem aafalaa aadoon
17Fii sil, Jerusalem yaab,
fii sil man.
Nyal ki fii sil man paacham.
Ni jin ntafadaan aafalaa
u Uwumbɔr gee liŋuul ki tii nimi ke ni ji na;
ni jin falaa ngbaan, le u cha ni chuun gbeer.
18Ubaa aa bi ki ga mɔk nimi nsan,
ubaa aa ki bi nimi aanib ponn ni ki ga dar nimi.
19Tibɔbir nfum mulee le lir ni pu:
butɔb bii nimi aatiŋ kookoo,
le nimi aanib kpoi nkon.
Ubaa aa bi u san nimi kinimbaak.
20Nimi aanib aa ki kpa mpɔɔn, le ki lir kitiŋ ponn ni,
ŋilɔlɔk mɔmɔk ni;
bi naahn ukpan aataŋ aah chuu ikulun i na la.
Bi kan Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na.
21Nimi Jerusalem aanib bi ji falaa na,
nimi bi chuun gbeer ke naah nyun ndaan le na,
22Nidindaan Uwumbɔr si nipuwɔb ki bui ke,
“M bi nyani falaa u m nan di tii nimi maaŋuul ponn ni na la.
Naan ki ji falaa u cha ni chuun gbeer
ke naah nyun ndaan le na.
23M ga di falaa ngbaan tii binib bi muk nimi na la,
binib bi nan cha ni doon titan ni, kitiŋ ponn ni na,
aan bi taa taa ni pu ke naah ye titan le na,
bima le ga ji falaa ngbaan.”

english_text:
Jerusalem Can Celebrate
1 Jerusalem, wake up!
Stand up and be strong.
Holy city of Zion,
dress in your best clothes.
Those foreigners who ruined
your sacred city
won't bother you again.
2Zion, rise from the dirt!
Free yourself from the rope
around your neck.
Suffering Will End
3The Lord says:
My people, you were sold,
but not for money;
now you will be set free,
but not for a payment.
4Long ago you went to Egypt
where you lived
as foreigners.
Then Assyria was cruel to you,
5 and now another nation
has taken you prisoner
for no reason at all.
Your leaders groan with pain,
and day after day
my own name is cursed.
6My people, you will learn
who I am and who is speaking
because I am here.
A Message of Hope for Jerusalem
7 What a beautiful sight!
On the mountains a messenger
announces to Jerusalem,
“Good news! You're saved.
There will be peace.
Your God is now King.”
8Everyone on guard duty,
sing and celebrate!
Look! You can see the Lord
returning to Zion.
9Jerusalem, rise from the ruins!
Join in the singing.
The Lord has given comfort
to his people;
he comes to your rescue.
10The Lord has shown all nations
his mighty strength;
now everyone will see
the saving power of our God.
A Command To Leave Babylon
11 Leave the city of Babylon!
Don't touch anything filthy.
Wash yourselves. Be ready
to carry back everything sacred
that belongs to the Lord.
12You won't need to run.
No one is chasing you.
The Lord God of Israel
will lead and protect you
from enemy attacks.
The Suffering Servant
13The Lord says:
My servant will succeed!
He will be given great praise
and the highest honors.
14Many were horrified
at what happened to him.
But everyone who saw him
was even more horrified
because he suffered until
he no longer looked human.
15 My servant will make
nations worthy to worship me;
kings will be silent
as they bow in wonder.
They will see and think about
things they have never seen
or thought about before.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr ga gaa Jerusalem yaab lii
1Jerusalem, ki pɔɔk, ki ki li nyuun ke saah nan bi pu na.
Uwumbɔr aatiŋ ki bi chain na,
di saakekenyaan gbab.
Binib bi dii ŋiwaa ki kpa tijɔŋ na aan ki koo aa ponn ni.
2Sin Jerusalem, gbuk gaa aabaa lii.
Fii nyan titan ni ki kal saabɔrjal pu.
Nimi Sionn aanib bi ye binaagbiib na, chuu gbinn tikululn ti bi di baa nimi na.
3Tidindaan Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke, “Naah nan kpaln binaagbiib na, ubaa aa nan pan ni pu ŋimombil; kina pu na, ni yaa ban ni nya tinaagbiir ngbaan ni kan, ubaa aan ki pa ŋimombil. 4Buyoonn ni nan fii buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki ti kpaln biwɔwɔm na, nibaa aasui ni le ni nan ŋa kina; le Asiria yaab nan nan chuu nimi mpɔɔn, ki di buen kaa pan nibaa. 5Tiwanbaan ngbaan le ki ŋa Babiloŋ ni mu: ni ye binaagbiib la, le baa pan ni pu tipar tibaa. Binib bi joo nimi na puk tipupukr ki mak ki lik seeni mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 6N‑yoonn choo le ni ga bee ke m sil ye Uwumbɔr ki bui nimi tibɔr tee.”
7Ni ga li kpa mpopiin ke ntuun ga nyan ni ŋijoo paab,
ki joo ni tibɔnyaan ti tii nsuudoon na.
U mooni linyaŋ ki bui Sionn aatiŋ ke,
“Saawumbɔr le joo dulnyaa.”
8Binib bi kii kitisakpeŋ ngbaan na bi tar,
baah kpa mpopiin pu na,
le bi kpaan ki tar.
Binimbil waa Uwumbɔr aah ki gir choo Sionn pu na.
9Nimi Jerusalem aalangbenn, fii ki li tar mpopiin pu,
Uwumbɔr gaa waatiŋ lii, ki sɔŋ waanib aasui.
10Uwumbɔr ga di waapɔɔn mu bi chain na gaa waanib lii,
le dulnyaa aanib mɔmɔk kan.
11Nimi bimɔk joo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aawan na,
nya Babiloŋ ni man.
Taa cha tijɔŋ aawan nibaa meeh nimi;
li bi chain ki nya man.
12N‑yoonn mumina ma kan, naan li ban mala ke ni nya;
naan li ban ke ni san ŋmar.
Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga cheen nimi
aan ki li kii nimi ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu.
Ututunn u ji falaa na
13Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Maatutunn ga nyaŋ waatuln;
bi ga nyuŋ u sakpen.
14Lijinjiir nan chuu binib bi nan kan u na;
u nan char char,
kaa ti ki naahn unibɔn.
15U mu ga ŋa ŋinibol pam chain,
u pu le bibɔrb ga li ka waa bimɔi, kaa kpa tibaa bi len.
Bi ga kan tiwan ni unii ubaa aa mɔk bi na,
ki bee tiwan ni baa ŋun ni pu na aatataa.”

english_text:
What God's Servant Did for Us
1 Has anyone believed us
or seen the mighty power
of the Lord in action?
2Like a young plant or a root
that sprouts in dry ground,
the servant grew up
obeying the Lord.
He wasn't some handsome king.
Nothing about the way he looked
made him attractive to us.
3He was hated and rejected;
his life was filled with sorrow
and terrible suffering.
No one wanted to look at him.
We despised him and said,
“He is a nobody!”
4He suffered and endured
great pain for us,
but we thought his suffering
was punishment from God.
5 He was wounded and crushed
because of our sins;
by taking our punishment,
he made us completely well.
6 All of us were like sheep
that had wandered off.
We had each gone our own way,
but the Lord gave him
the punishment we deserved.
7 He was painfully abused,
but he did not complain.
He was silent like a lamb
being led to the butcher,
as quiet as a sheep
having its wool cut off.
8He was condemned to death
without a fair trial.
Who could have imagined
what would happen to him?
His life was taken away
because of the sinful things
my people had done.
9 He wasn't dishonest or violent,
but he was buried in a tomb
among cruel, rich people.
10The Lord decided his servant
would suffer as a sacrifice
to take away the sin
and guilt of others.
Now the servant will live
to see his own descendants.
He did everything
the Lord had planned.
11By suffering, the servant
will learn the true meaning
of obeying the Lord.
Although he is innocent,
he will take the punishment
for the sins of others,
so that many of them
will no longer be guilty.
12 The Lord will reward him
with honor and power
for sacrificing his life.
Others thought he was a sinner,
but he suffered for our sins
and asked God to forgive us.
translation_text:
1Le binib ngbaan giin kii ke,
“Ŋma ba ga pak tibɔr ti ti len dandana na?
Ŋma ba ga dak ke Uwumbɔr aaŋaal bi tibɔr tee ni?
2Ni nan ye Uwumbɔr aageehn ke waatutunn nyal sil
ke busub bu si nteer pu ki kpa inyaan na.
Waa kpa kinyaan ni bunyuŋ ni ga cha binib li neen u na.
Nibaa aa nan bi u chee ki ŋan,
nibaa aa bi, ki ga daa timi dan u chee.
3Ti lik u fam ki yii u;
u nan kan falaa ni iween.
Ubaa aa ban ke u lik kan u,
ti suln ubɔr ke waah kaa ye nibaa le na.
4Le u kaa ki gaa falaa u ba ye timi yoo na,
ni iween i ti ba ga kan na.
Le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ti nan dak ke waafalaa sakpiin ngbaan
mɔk ke Uwumbɔr bi dar utafal waatunwanbir pu la.
5Timi aatunwanbir pu le bi gbaa u, le uwon ŋa ibuun.
Waah gaa timi aatafadaan pu na, le Uwumbɔr cha ti pɔɔk,
Ti kan laafee waah gaa tigbar ti na pu la.
6Ti mɔmɔk naahn ipiih i yenn na la,
timɔk cha taah gee niwɔb na,
le Uwumbɔr di titunwanbir ngbaan aafalaa tun u,
ntafadaan ngbaan ba ŋeer timi la.
7Bi nan ŋa u mbiin pam,
le u gaa ni mɔmɔk suuna;
waa nan waar umɔb ki len tibaa.
U nan ŋmin ke baah ban bi kɔr upihbo kan, u ŋmin pu na la,
ki naahn ke baah ban bi chee upiih aakokor kan, u ŋmin pu na, waa nan waar umɔb ki len tibaa.
8Bi nan chuu u ki jin u tibɔr,
ki di u buen bi ti ku u, le unii ubaa aan ŋmaa len uyaabitiib pu.
Timi aanib aatunwanbir pu le bi nan ku u.
9Bi nan ban ke u ni titunwanbirdam nan kpaan likaakul la,
u ni biwankpadam le bi nan kpaan di sub;
ba pu? waa nan ŋa titunwanbir aatuln libaa,
hali waa nan mɔn nnyamɔn mubaa.”
10Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Ni nan ye maageehn le ke u ji falaa;
waakun nan ye kitork ki ga joo ni chapinn na la.
Le ni tii u nsan u kan uyaabitiib;
u ga li kpa limɔfal li fɔk na,
aan maah ban pu na ŋa uma pu.
11U yaa jin falaa kan, nee aapuwɔb le u ga kan mpopiin;
le ki ga bee ke waa jin falaa fam.
Maatutunn bamɔnn u m gee u na ga gaa binib pam aatafadaan
le m di cha pinn bi baatunwanbir.
12Le m ga tii u nkakaa mu nyuun na lipepel li bi bininyuum,
ni mpɔɔndam aakaasisik ni na.
U di waamɔfal tii waageehn pu,
ki yakr titunwanbirdam chee baapal.
U gaa titunwanbirdam pam aasisiiyaan,
ki mee Uwumbɔr ke u di cha pinn bi.”

english_text:
A Promise of the Lord's Protection
1 Sing and shout,
even though you have never
had children!
The Lord has promised that you
will have more children
than someone married
for a long time.
2Make your tents larger!
Spread out the tent pegs;
fasten them firmly.
3You and your descendants
will take over the land
of other nations.
You will settle in towns
that are now in ruins.
4Don't be afraid or ashamed
and don't be discouraged.
You won't be disappointed.
Forget how sinful you were
when you were young;
stop feeling ashamed
for being left a widow.
5The Lord All-Powerful,
the Holy God of Israel,
rules all the earth.
He is your Creator and husband,
and he will rescue you.
6You were like a young wife,
brokenhearted and crying
because her husband
had divorced her.
But the Lord your God says,
“I am taking you back!
7I rejected you for a while,
but with love and tenderness
I will embrace you again.
8For a while, I turned away
in furious anger.
Now I will have mercy
and love you forever!
I, your protector and Lord,
make this promise.”
The Lord Promises Lasting Peace
9 I once promised Noah that I
would never again destroy
the earth by a flood.
Now I have promised that I
will never again get angry
and punish you.
10 Every mountain and hill
may disappear.
But I will always be kind
and merciful to you;
I won't break my agreement
to give your nation peace.
The New Jerusalem
11 Jerusalem, you are sad
and discouraged,
tossed around in a storm.
But I, the Lord,
will rebuild your city
with precious stones;
for your foundation
I will use blue sapphires.
12Your fortresses
will be built of rubies,
your gates of jewels,
and your walls of gems.
13 I will teach your children
and make them successful.
14You will be built on fairness
with no fears of injustice;
every one of your worries
will be taken far from you.
15I will never send anyone
to attack your city,
and you will make prisoners
of those who do attack.
16Don't forget that I created
metalworkers who make weapons
over burning coals.
I also created armies
that can bring destruction.
17Weapons made to attack you
won't be successful;
words spoken against you
won't hurt at all.
My servants, Jerusalem is yours!
I, the Lord, promise
to bless you with victory.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah gee Israel yaab pu na
1Jerusalem, aa nan bi ke upii u kaa kpa mbim na la,
le dandana ma aa ga ŋmaa teen ki gaa ilahn ni mpopiin.
Dandana aa ga kan mbim
ki jer upii u aachal aa kee buen nibaa chee ki cha u na.
2Wii saadiik ki maa ki waa sakpen na,
cha ŋipal li fɔk ki cha ilɔkdɔ mu li pɔɔ.
3Aa ga moo ban kitiŋ kpee saatiŋ pu ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu;
saanib ga ki gaa ntim mu ŋitimbol ŋiken nan gaa bi chee na.
Ntisakpem mu binib san cha mu na ga ki gbiin binib.
4Taa san ijawaan man;
naan ki ji inimɔɔn;
ubaa aan ki lik seen nimi.
Aa ga suln saah kaa nan si chob pu na aabɔr,
ki suln buyoonn aa nan gur ka ke ukpopii na mu.
5U naan si na ga li bi ke chal na le aa chee,
waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan.
Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na le ga gaa si lii,
uma le ye dulnyaa mɔmɔk aayidaan.
6Israel aatimbol, aa naahn
upiisapɔɔn u aachal san cha u
aan ilandak joo u na la.
Le Uwumbɔr di si giin ni u chee ki bui ke:
7“M nan san cha si siib; le ki ga ki di ngeehm yoor si.
8M nan di liŋuul le ki san cha si siib,
le m ga di maageehm mɔk si
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
Kina le Uwumbɔr u gaa si lii na len.
9“Nowa aayoonn na m nan puu tipuur ke
nwam aan ki ji kitiŋ kee.
Le dandana m ki puu ke maan ki gee liŋuul aa pu:
maan ki kae si, kaan ki daa aatafal mu.
10Nibaakan ŋijoo ni ŋigongon ga wur lir,
le maageehm mu m kpa tii si na aan doo;
maah puu tipuur ke m ga tii si nsuudoon na,
m ga li beenin joo ti.”
Kina le Uwumbɔr u gee si na len.
Jerusalem u ga li bi n‑yoonn mu choo na
11Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Jerusalem, sin u kpa kinimbaak na, kitiŋ ki kaa kpa uteter,
kaa kpa ubaa aan u sɔŋ kisui na,
m ga di ŋitakpanyaan le ki ki di maa saadinyikl.
12M ga di ŋitakpanyaan ŋi ŋan na le di maa saadir ti fɔk na,
ki di ŋitakpal ŋi moor ke mmii na maa ibisamɔi,
ki di ŋitakpanyaan ŋi kpa kidaak na maa ligoln li gob si na.
13Min mbaa le ga mɔk saanib maasan,
ki tii bi liwangol ni nsuudoon.
14Ibamɔn ni lituln li ŋan na le ga tii si mpɔɔn.
Aa ga fuur limukl ni mbiin pu.
15Unii yaa tak si kan, maa nyi udaan aabɔr;
unii umɔk ban si kijaak na ga lir.
16Min le naan uchaa u tuur mmii ki mɔɔ tijawan na.
Min le ki naan butɔb aaja u joo tijawan ku na.
17Le tijawan nibaa aan ŋmaa tii si titotonn;
aa ga li kpa ngarm ki tii unii umɔk galn si na.
M ga li si maatutum aapuwɔb ki tii bi linyaŋ.”
Uwumbɔr le len kina.

english_text:
The Lord's Invitation
1 If you are thirsty,
come and drink water!
If you don't have any money,
come, eat what you want!
Drink wine and milk
without paying a cent.
2 Why waste your money
on what really isn't food?
Why work hard for something
that doesn't satisfy?
Listen carefully to me,
and you will enjoy
the very best foods.
3 Pay close attention!
Come to me and live.
I will promise you
the eternal love and loyalty
that I promised David.
4I made him the leader and ruler
of the nations;
he was my witness to them.
5You will call out to nations
you have never known.
And they have never known you,
but they will come running
because I am the Lord,
the holy God of Israel,
and I have honored you.
God's Words Are Powerful
6Turn to the Lord!
He can still be found.
Call out to God! He is near.
7Give up your evil ways
and your evil thoughts.
Return to the Lord our God.
He will be merciful
and forgive your sins.
8The Lord says:
“My thoughts and my ways
are not like yours.
9Just as the heavens
are higher than the earth,
my thoughts and my ways
are higher than yours.
10 “Rain and snow fall from the sky.
But they don't return
without watering the earth
that produces seeds to plant
and grain to eat.
11That's how it is with my words.
They don't return to me
without doing everything
I send them to do.”
God's People Will Celebrate
12When you are set free,
you will celebrate
and travel home in peace.
Mountains and hills will sing
as you pass by,
and trees will clap.
13Cypress and myrtle trees
will grow in fields
once covered by thorns.
And then those trees will stand
as a lasting witness
to the glory of the Lord.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aanimbaak
1Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Dan man, unii umɔk nnyunyuu joo u na, nnyun le na do.
Nimi bimɔk aa kpa ŋimombil na,
dan man, nan daa tijikaar ki ji man.
Dan man, nan daa ndaan ni nnaabiin man,
naan pa limombil libaa.
2Ba ŋa ni joo ŋimombil daa tiwan ni kaan gbiin lipuul na?
Ba ŋa ni ji nimi aapal aan nkon beenin joo nimi?
Li pel ki ŋa maah len pu na man,
aan ki ji tijikaar ti mɔ sakpen na.
3Maanib, li pel dandana man,
ki dan m chee man,
dan man m chee ki nan kan limɔfal.
M ga puu tipuur ti kaan doo na tii nimi,
ki tii nimi tinyoor ti m nan puu
Ubɔr David ke m ga tii u na.
4M nan ŋa u ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aayidaan;
le ki cha bi kan maapɔɔn aah bi pu na u pu.
5Dandana ni ga kuun biwɔwɔm aatimbol;
n‑yoonn mubaa, baa nan nyi nimi,
le dandana ma bi ga san ki nan kpaan ni chee.
Min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, nimi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr
u bi chain na ga cha nimina mɔmɔk ŋa kina;
m ga nyuŋ nimi ki tii nimi liyimbil.”
6Fenn toŋ Uwumbɔr ki mee u man,
n‑yoonn mu u laa duun nimi na.
7Cha bibiindam di cha baah bi mbiin mu ni na
ki kpeln baalandak.
Cha bi fenn toŋ Tidindaan
Uwumbɔr u san binib kinimbaak ki cha pinni titunwanbir mala na.
8Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Maalandak aa ye nimi yoo,
le maabimbin mu ni nimi yoo aa kpaan.
9Kitaapaak aah daa kitiŋ pu na,
kina le maabimbin ni
maalandak ŋan jer nimi yoo.
10Maamɔboln naahn likpakpal ni utaal u nyani kitaapaak
ki nan sɔŋni kitiŋ na, ki cha tijikaar muuni,
ki tii binib njikaabim mu bi bu na, ni tijikaar bi ji.
11Kina le ga li ye ŋimɔbon ŋi m ga len na,
ŋaan yii maah ban ke ŋi ŋa pu na;
ŋi ga ŋa tiwan nimɔk m tun ŋi ke ŋi ti ŋa na.
12Ni ga di mpopiin le ki di nya Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni;
bi ga cheen nimi nya kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ni mpopiin la.
Le ŋijoo ni ŋigongon ga teen ilahn lii;
isui mu ga di mpopiin teen mpɔɔn pu.
13Lisalaasiil aasui le ga li gur bi
ikokon aah nan bi nin chee na;
le ikpasɔi muun nin chee ikokon nan si na.
Limɔkl limina ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na,
ki teer nimi, min Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu na.”

english_text:
All Nations Will Be Part of God's People
1The Lord said:
Be honest and fair!
Soon I will come to save you;
my saving power will be seen
everywhere on earth.
2I will bless everyone
who respects the Sabbath
and refuses to do wrong.
3Foreigners who worship me
must not say,
“The Lord won't let us
be part of his people.”
Men who are unable
to become fathers
must no longer say,
“We are dried-up trees.”
4 To them, I, the Lord, say:
Respect the Sabbath,
obey me completely,
and keep our agreement.
5Then you will be like monuments
in my temple with your names
written on them.
This will be much better
than having children,
because these monuments
will stand there forever.
6Foreigners will follow me.
They will love me and worship
in my name;
they will respect the Sabbath
and keep our agreement.
7 I will bring them
to my holy mountain,
where they will celebrate
in my house of worship.
Their sacrifices and offerings
will always be welcome
on my altar.
Then my house will be known
as a house of worship
for all nations.
8I, the Lord, promise
to bring together my people
who were taken away,
and let them join the others.
God Promises To Punish Israel's Leaders
9Come from the forest,
you wild animals!
Attack and gobble up
your victims.
10You leaders of Israel
should be watchdogs,
protecting my people.
But you can't see a thing,
and you never warn them.
Dozing and daydreaming
are all you ever do.
11You stupid leaders are a pack
of hungry and greedy dogs
that never get enough.
You are shepherds
who mistreat your own sheep
for selfish gain.
12You say to each other,
“Let's drink till we're drunk!
Tomorrow we'll do it again.
We'll really enjoy ourselves.”
translation_text:
Ŋinibol mɔmɔk ga li ye Uwumbɔr aanib la
1Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke, “Li ŋani man tiwan ni ŋan ki tok na, ba pu? naan ki yunn le m ga gaa nimi lii. 2Binib bimɔk joo maakpaakool daal mbamɔm, kaa bii mu na, m ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu. M ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa binib bimɔk aa tun titunwanbir na pu.”
3Uwɔwɔnja u kpaan Uwumbɔr aanib chee na taa bui ke, “Uwumbɔr aan cha m ni waanib kpaan doon u.”
Baah kpaa uja u na taa dak ke waah kaan ŋmaa maa mbim na, waan ŋmaa ŋmal Uwumbɔr aanib ni. 4Uwumbɔr bui kina aaja ke, “Aa yaa pak mi ki joo maakpaakool daal mbamɔm, ki ŋani maah gee pu na, ki gaa ki kii maah puu tipuur ti na kan, 5saayimbil ga yunn Maadichal ni, ni maanib ni, ki jer saah ba ga li kpa mbijabim ni mpiibim pu na. Baan suln aabɔr kpala.”
6Le Uwumbɔr bui biwɔwɔm bi kpaln waanib, ki gee u ki dii u na, ki joo waakpaakool daal, ki gaa waah puu tipuur ti na ki kii mbamɔm na ke: 7“M ga di nimi dan Sionn, maagongoln li bi chain na pu, ki tii nimi mpopiin Maameen Aadichal ni, ki gaa nimi aapiin aatork ki ni toor maabimbiln paab na. Bi ga yin Maadichal ke Mmeen Aadichal, nin chee ŋinibol mɔmɔk mee mi na la.”
8Tidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyan ni waanib Israel yaab tinaagbiir ni na, puu ke u ga nyan binib biken nan kpee bi pu.
Uwumbɔr bii Israel yaab aaninkpiib
9Uwumbɔr bui biwɔwɔm aatimbol ke ŋi dan ke tipeewanbir na ki nan di waanib nab. 10U bui ke, “Israel yaab aakikiirb mɔmɔk ye bijoom la. Ni ye baatuln ke bi sur maanib, le baa nyi nibaa. Bi naahn ibɔja i kaa gbei na la, bi po dɔ geen la, le ki daŋni tidaŋ. Bi gee ngeen jer tiwan mɔmɔk. 11Bi naahn ibɔ i kaa ji babr na la. Bi ye bisalolm bi kaa kpa nlan na. Bi mɔmɔk ŋani baah gee pu na la, le ki ban bibaa aanyaan. 12Bi len le ke, ‘Cha ti ban man ndaan; aan ki nyu taah gee pu na. Fen ga fe li mɔ jer din.’”

english_text:
God's Faithful People Suffer
1God's faithful people
are dragged off and killed,
and no one even cares.
Evil sweeps them away,
2but in death they find peace
for obeying God.
The Lord Condemns Idolatry
3You people are unfaithful!
You go to fortunetellers,
and you worship idols.
Now pay close attention!
4Who are you making fun of?
Who are you sneering at?
Look how your sins
have made fools of you.
5All you think about is sex
under those green trees
where idols are worshiped.
You sacrifice your children
on altars built in valleys
under rocky slopes.
6You have chosen to worship
idols made of stone;
you have given them offerings
of wine and grain.
Should I be pleased?
7You have spread out your beds
on the tops of high mountains,
where you sacrifice to idols.
8Even in your homes
you have placed pagan symbols
all around your huge beds.
Yes, you have rejected me,
sold yourselves to your lovers,
and gone to bed with them.
9You smear on olive oil
and all kinds of perfume
to worship the god Molech.
You even seek advice
from spirits of the dead.
10Though you tired yourself out
by running after idols,
you refused to stop.
Your desires were so strong
that they kept you going.
11Did you forget about me
and become unfaithful
because you were more afraid
of someone else?
Have I been silent so long
that you no longer fear me?
12You think you're so good,
but I'll point out the truth.
13Ask your idols to save you
when you are in trouble.
Be careful though—
it takes only a faint breath
to blow them over.
But if you come to me
for protection,
this land and my holy mountain
will always belong to you.
The Lord Helps the Helpless
14The Lord says,
“Clear the road!
Get it ready for my people.”
15 Our holy God lives forever
in the highest heavens,
and this is what he says:
Though I live high above
in the holy place,
I am here to help those
who are humble
and depend only on me.
16My people, I won't stay angry
and keep on accusing you.
After all, I am your Creator.
I don't want you to give up
in complete despair.
17Your greed made me furious.
That's why I punished you
and refused to be found,
while you kept returning
to your old sinful ways.
18I know what you are like!
But I will heal you, lead you,
and give you comfort,
until those who are mourning
19 start singing my praises.
No matter where you are,
I, the Lord, will heal you
and give you peace.
20The wicked are a restless sea
tossing up mud.
21 But I, the Lord, have promised
that none who are evil
will live in peace.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah bii Israel yaab aawaa pu na
1Bininyaam kpoi, le ubaa aa ŋmaa bee naah ŋa pu aan bi kpoi na, le naa ti ki muk unii ubaa. Unii ubaa aa bee ke Uwumbɔr le nya bininyaam dulnyaa wee ni ke bi taa ki ji falaa. 2Binib bi aabimbin ŋan na yaa kpo kan, bi kani nsuudoon ni lifuur, nkun ni.
3Nimi titunwanbirdam, dan do man aan Uwumbɔr nan ji nimi tibɔr. Nimi ni bibɔɔb, ni bidagoob, ni pateer tiib ye tiwanbaan la, ubaa aa jer uken. 4Ŋma aan ni ŋani u yaansara? Ŋma aan nimi binyamɔndam yuul? 5Ni doo bipiib chee tiwaachur ni, ke ni dooni ŋiwaa ŋi kpa mmaal na la. Ni joo nimi aabim ti toor kitork titakpalunn ni, ikpen aafataŋ ni. 6Ni yoor ŋitakpal ŋi ŋan na nima chee, le ki ti dooni ŋi ke ŋi ye nimi aawaa. Ni bar ndaan kpir ŋi pu ke ni tii ŋi ipiin la, ki tii ŋi njikaabim mu aapiin. Ni dak ke nsui piin nimina mɔmɔk pu uu? 7Ni chaa ŋijoo paab ti toor kitork le ki doo bipiib chee nima. 8Ni joo nimi aanyɔbombom ki joo siini nimi aabisamɔi. Ni yii mi, le ni ni nibɔtiib, bi ni pa bi ŋimombil waahr aan ki nin doon bi chee na yiir nimi aawanpeenkaan, ki jon ti dɔ nimi aawandookaan ni wiir na pu. Nima chee le ni ŋani naah gee pu na. 9Ni ŋmir nimi aatulalee ni nimi aakpan le ki chaa ti dooni liwaal Molek. Ni yaa ban ŋiwaa kan, ni ga tun binib bi buen dandar, hali kitekpiitiŋ ni. 10Ni muk nibaa ki lik ban ŋiwaa ŋiken, kaan di cha. Ni dak ke nimi aawaabir ngbaan tii nimi mpɔɔn la, kina pu na, naa bakr kpala.
11Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ŋiwaa ŋi cha ijawaan chur nimi na ye ŋma, le ni tuk mi inyamɔn aabɔr ki suln m pu kookoo? Maah ŋmin suuna kaa ki gar nimi ni yunn sakpen na, le naa ki pak mi ii? 12Ni dak ke naah ŋani pu na le ŋan, le m ga nyan nimi aatuln mɔmɔk mpaan pu, le nimi aawaa ngbaan aan ŋma gaa nimi lii. 13Ni yaa wii ki ban nterm kan, ni cha nimi aawaa ngbaan ter nimi. Litakpiln libaa aabuln le ga daa ŋi di buen. Le binib bi gaa mi ki kii na ma ga li bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu ki ga li dooni mi Maadichal ni.”
Uwumbɔr aah puu ke u ga tii waanib laafee pu na
14Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Cha maanib gir ni m chee. Chuu nyan tiwan nimɔk laŋ baasan na. Naan nsan ki gor mu siin man.
15“Min le ye paacham Aawumbɔr u bi chain ki bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na. M bi nin chee paa ki bi chain na la, le ki mu ki bi binib bi sunn bibaa taab aan bisui bii buyoonn bi bee ke bi tun titunwanbir na chee, ki ga pɔɔk bitaakpab ki sɔŋ bisui. 16M tii maanib limɔfal, kina pu na, maan ki galn bi ki gee liŋuul bi pu ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. M yaa ŋa kina kan, bi ga fik. 17Baatunwanbir ni baakumɔŋ pu le m nan gee bi pu liŋuul, le ki nan daa bitafal ki san cha bi. Le baa nan kpeln, ki beenin dii baasan.
18“M kan baah ŋa pu na, m mu tee ga tii bi laafee. M ga loln bi pu nsan ki ter bi, ki ga sɔŋ binib bi wii na aasui. 19M tii binib bi duun na, ni binib bi dandar na mɔmɔk nsuudoon. M ga tii maanib laafee. 20Tɔ, bibiindam ma naahn nnyusakpem mu kaa ŋmaa doo suuna na, mu aanyunkpenn joo ni tijɔŋ ni tikpakpar na la. 21Titunwanbirdam aa kpa nsuudoon.” Uwumbɔr aah len pu na le na.

english_text:
True Religion
1Shout the message!
Don't hold back.
Say to my people Israel:
You've sinned! You've turned
against the Lord.
2Day after day, you worship him
and seem eager to learn
his teachings.
You act like a nation
that wants to do right
by obeying his laws.
You ask him about justice,
and say you enjoy
worshiping the Lord.
3You wonder why the Lord
pays no attention
when you go without eating
and act humble.
But on those same days
that you give up eating,
you think only of yourselves
and abuse your workers.
4You even get angry
and ready to fight.
No wonder God won't listen
to your prayers!
5Do you think the Lord
wants you to give up eating
and to act as humble
as a bent-over bush?
Or to dress in sackcloth
and sit in ashes?
Is this really what he wants
on a day of worship?
6I'll tell you
what it really means
to worship the Lord.
Remove the chains of prisoners
who are bound unjustly.
Free those who are abused!
7 Share your food with everyone
who is hungry;
share your home
with the poor and homeless.
Give clothes to those in need;
don't turn away your relatives.
8Then your light will shine
like the dawning sun, and you
will quickly be healed.
Your honesty will protect you
as you advance,
and the glory of the Lord
will defend you from behind.
9When you beg the Lord for help,
he will answer, “Here I am!”
Don't mistreat others
or falsely accuse them
or say something cruel.
10Give your food to the hungry
and care for the homeless.
Then your light will shine
in the dark;
your darkest hour will be
like the noonday sun.
11The Lord will always guide you
and provide good things to eat
when you are in the desert.
He will make you healthy.
You will be like a garden
that has plenty of water
or like a stream
that never runs dry.
12You will rebuild those houses
left in ruins for years;
you will be known
as a builder and repairer
of city walls and streets.
13But first, you must start
respecting the Sabbath
as a joyful day of worship.
You must stop doing and saying
whatever you please
on this special day.
14Then you will truly enjoy
knowing the Lord.
He will let you rule
from the highest mountains
and bless you with the land
of your ancestor Jacob.
The Lord has spoken!
translation_text:
Kimɔlul ki ye mbamɔn na
1Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Li tar man mpɔɔn pu naah gee pu na. Bui maanib Israel yaab baatunwanbir pu. 2Binib bee dooni mi iwiin mɔmɔk, ki len ke bi neen ke bi li nyi maabimbin ki kii maakaal. Bi bui ke bi ban m tii bi ikaal i bi chob na la, ki bui ke bi neen ke bi li dooni mi.”
3Binib ngbaan baa ke, “Ba ŋa ti lulni bumɔb, le Uwumbɔr aatafal aa bi ti ni? Ba ŋa ti sunn tibaa taab, le waa pel ti chee?”
Uwumbɔr bui bi ke, “Mbamɔn aah ye pu na le ye ke n‑yoonn mu ni lul bumɔb na, le ni bi ban nibaa aageehn le ki muk nimi aatutum. 4Nimi aamɔlul aayoonn le ni waar le ki kpak ki jaa. Ni dak ke kimɔlul kimina aaboln ga cha m pel nimi aameel aa? 5Ni yaa lul bumɔb kan, le ni muk nibaa, le ki tiin niyil ke kimook ki yɔl na, ki di tiwan ni saak kuub na aakekeln yar, ki di nfatan yɔk yɔk ŋi pu, ki doon paan. Nimina le ni yin bumɔb aalulm aa? Ni dak ke nima ngbaan ga piir nsui ii?
6“Maah ban kimɔlul ki aaboln na sɔ: Chuu nyan man limukl aakululn ti ni di buu bigiim na, ni inyamɔn aatuln li ni di tun bi na bi pu, ki cha bi li chuun bibaa pu. 7Yakr man nimi aajikaar tii nkon aah joo binib bi na, ki piir nimi aadichal tii bigiim bi kaa kpa nkookoo yaan na. Tii binib bi kaa kpa nibaa peeni na bi peen, ki li joo nido yaab man.
8“N‑yoonn ngbaan le maaŋann ga dan ni chee ki wiin ke kichakpiik ni aawiin na, le nimi aabuun mɔmɔk ga yann mala. M ga li bi ni chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ki gaa nimi lii; maah ga li bi ni chee pu na ga li kii nimi ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu. 9Le ni yaa mee mi kan, m ga kii nimi aameel. Ni yaa yin mi kan, m ga kii nimi.
“Ni yaa kuln limukl, ni lik‑seen, ni tibɔbir mɔmɔk, 10ki yaa tii nkon aah joo binib bi na tijiir, ki cha binib bi lann na mu kan kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan le mbɔmbɔɔn mu maln goln nimi na ga daa labr nwiihn mu wiin ke nwiin pu aawiin na. 11Le m ga li kii nimi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ki tii nimi tiwan ni ŋan na. M ga cha ni li kpa laafee ki pɔɔ. Ni ga li bi ke tikpin aasaak ki kaa lann nnyun na la, ki naahn uyayak aanyunbun mu kaa foor na. 12Jerusalem aanib ga ki gir maa nimɔk nan ye tilangbenn n‑yoonn mu jer na, ki ki gir maa ŋidinyik ŋi nan puen bi na pu. Binib mɔmɔk ga bee nimi ke ni ye binib bi ki gir maa ŋigon ŋi lir na, ki ki fiini ŋidichal ŋi lir na siini na la.”
Likpaakool daal aajoom aanyoor
13Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Aa yaa joo likpaakool daal ke nwiin mu bi chain na, kaa ban aabaa aanyoor nwiin ngbaan daal; aa yaa pak maawiin mu bi chain na, kaa buen lisachuln, kaa tun lituln, kaa len bɔyɔlyɔl nwiin ngbaan daal kan, 14aa ga kan mpopiin mu nyan ni saah tun maatuln pu na ni. M ga cha dulnyaa mɔmɔk li pak si, le aa ga ji mmɔɔn, kitiŋ ki m nan di tii aayaaja Jakob na pu. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
Social Injustice Is Condemned
1The Lord hasn't lost
his powerful strength;
he can still hear
and answer prayers.
2Your sins are the roadblock
between you and your God.
That's why he doesn't answer
your prayers
or let you see his face.
3Your talk is filled with lies
and plans for violence;
every finger on your hands
is covered with blood.
4You falsely accuse others
and tell lies in court;
sin and trouble are the names
of your children.
5You eat the deadly eggs
of poisonous snakes,
and more snakes crawl out
from the eggs left to hatch.
You weave spider webs,
6but you can't make clothes
with those webs
or hide behind them.
You're sinful and brutal.
7 You hurry off to do wrong
or murder innocent victims.
All you think about is sin;
you leave ruin and destruction
wherever you go.
8You don't know how
to live in peace
or to be fair with others.
The roads you make are crooked;
your followers cannot find peace.
The People Confess Their Sins
9No one has come to defend us
or to bring about justice.
We hoped for a day of sunshine,
but all we found
was a dark, gloomy night.
10We feel our way along,
as if we were blind;
we stumble at noon,
as if it were night.
We can see no better
than someone dead.
11We growl like bears
and mourn like doves.
We hope for justice and victory,
but they escape us.
12How often have we sinned
and turned against you,
the Lord God?
Our sins condemn us!
We have done wrong.
13We have rebelled and refused
to follow you.
Our hearts were deceitful,
and so we lied;
we planned to abuse others
and turn our backs on you.
14Injustice is everywhere;
justice seems far away.
Truth is chased out of court;
honesty is shoved aside.
15Everyone tells lies;
those who turn from crime
end up ruined.
The Lord Will Rescue His People
When the Lord noticed
that justice had disappeared,
he became very displeased.
16 It disgusted him even more
to learn that no one
would do a thing about it.
So with his own powerful arm,
he won victories for truth.
17 Justice was the Lord's armor;
saving power was his helmet;
anger and revenge
were his clothes.
18Now the Lord will get furious
and do to his enemies,
both near and far,
what they did to his people.
19He will attack like a flood
in a mighty windstorm.
Nations in the west and the east
will then honor and praise
his wonderful name.
20 The Lord has promised to rescue
the city of Zion
and Jacob's descendants
who turn from sin.
21The Lord says: “My people,
I promise to give you my Spirit
and my message.
These will be my gifts to you
and your families forever.
I, the Lord, have spoken.”
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr aah bii binib ngbaan baatunwanbir pu pu na
1Taa dak man ke Uwumbɔr aa kpa mpɔɔn ke u gaa nimi lii, bee u kpaa sakpen, kaan ki ŋun naah yin u pu ki ban nterm na. 2Ni ye nimi aatunwanbir pu le waa ŋun nimi aayim ngbaan. Nimi aatunwanbir le yakr nimi Uwumbɔr chee naa ŋmaa dooni u. 3Ni ye binyamɔndam, binib bi ban kijaak na, ni binikurb la.
4Naa kpa ibamɔn, ki mu joo tibɔr chaa bibɔjirb chee. Ni si inyamɔn pu le ke ni di ji tibɔr ngbaan. Ni joo nimi aalandak ki ban ke ni di tun biken titotonn. 5-6Nimi aalandak i kaa ŋan na bir ke ujagen aajen na la. Faa wii li, le uwaa ga nyan ni li ponn ni. Nimi aalandak i bir ngbaan na aan tii nimi tinyoor tibaa, i naahn likekeln li bi di nandala aakokon luu li na la. 7N‑yoonn mɔmɔk ni dak ke ni ŋa ni kaa ŋan na la, le naa taani kpala kina aaŋam. Naa sii ki dakl lik waahr aan ki nin ku unii u kaa tun taani ubaa na. Nin chee mɔk ni jer na ye mbiin ŋmeen la, 8le unii umɔk bi nin chee ni bi na kan, udaan aa kee kan lifuur. Naah ŋani nimɔk na aa kpa ibamɔn. Ni dii nsan mu gɔr na la, le unii umɔk dii nsan ngbaan na aan kan lifuur.
Binib aah kpiir baatunwanbir pu pu na
9Binib ngbaan bui ke, “Dandana ti bee naah ŋa pu aan Uwumbɔr aan gaa timi binib bi muk timi na chee lii na. Ti mak nwiihn pu le ti li chuun dii, le ni ye mbɔmbɔɔn ŋmeen la, 10le ti chuun tuul ke bijoom na. Ti chuun nwiin pu le ki gbeer, ke naah ye kinyeek le na, ki naahn ke taah bi kitekpiitiŋ ni le na. 11Ijawaan joo timi, le tiwon yɔl. Ti neen ke Uwumbɔr nan nyan timi limukl ni, ni tiwan ni kaa ŋan na ponn ni, le nibaa aa ŋani.
12“Uwumbɔr, taah tun si titunwanbir ti na nyaŋ. Timi tibaa aataani galni timi la. Ti nyi taah tun pu na mɔmɔk. 13Ti yii si, kaa si aapuwɔb, kaa dii saasan. Ti muk biken, ki fenn tipuwɔb tii si. Timi aalandak, ni timi aamɔliin mɔmɔk ye inyamɔn la. 14Ibamɔn daa ti chee, kaan ŋmaa mar ni timi. Binib aah wiir nin chee na, mbamɔn gbeer la, kaan ŋmaa kan mpaan nima. 15Mbamɔn par sakpen, le unii umɔk di cha titunwanbir aaŋam na ga kan ke uma le titunwanbirdam muk.”
Uwumbɔr gor ke u gaa waanib lii
Uwumbɔr kan nimina, le naa mɔɔr u, ibamɔn aah kaa bi pu na. 16Ni gar u pam ke ubaa aa bi u ter baah muk binib bi na. Kina pu na, u ga di ubaa aapɔɔn le di gaa bi lii, ki ji linyaŋ ngbaan. 17U ga di mbimbinyaan mu bi ke tikur ti bii kibiŋ pu na, ki li chik tikur aayikpupuk ki ye waapɔɔn mu gaa binib lii na, ki li kpa iniman ki daa binib aatafal baah ŋa biken falaa pu na. 18U ga daa waadim aatafal baah tun taani ki ŋeer pu na, ni binib bi bi dandar aatim ni na mu. 19Ki nya liwipuul ki ti saa liwilir wɔb, bi ga li san u ni waapɔɔn. U ga dan ke limɔɔl li puu mala mala na la, ki naahn libuln li pɔɔ na.
20Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke, “M ga dan Jerusalem ki nan sil nichaŋ ni, ki nan gaa nimi bi yii nimi aatunwanbir na lii, 21ki cha m ni nimi puu tipuur tii tɔb. M di maapɔɔn ni maakaal tii nimi ke ni li ye nimi yaan ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, ki nya din ki joo cha na, ni ga kii maamɔb ki mɔk nimi aabim, ni niyaabitiib ke bi kii maamɔb ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu choo na.”

english_text:
A New Day for Jerusalem
1Jerusalem, stand up! Shine!
Your new day is dawning.
The glory of the Lord
shines brightly on you.
2The earth and its people
are covered with darkness,
but the glory of the Lord
is shining upon you.
3Nations and kings
will come to the light
of your dawning day.
Crowds Are Coming to Jerusalem
The Lord said:
4 Open your eyes! Look around!
Crowds are coming.
Your sons are on their way
from distant lands;
your daughters are being carried
like little children.
5When you see this,
your faces will glow;
your hearts will pound
and swell with pride.
Treasures from across the sea
and the wealth of nations
will be brought to you.
6Your country will be covered
with caravans of young camels
from Midian and Ephah.
The people of Sheba
will bring gold and spices
in praise of me, the Lord.
7Every sheep of Kedar
will come to you;
rams from Nebaioth
will be yours as well.
I will accept them as offerings
and bring honor to my temple.
8What is that sailing by
like clouds
or like doves flying home?
9On those distant islands
your people are waiting
for me, the Lord.
Seagoing ships lead the way
to bring them home
with their silver and gold.
I, the holy Lord God of Israel,
do this to honor your people,
so they will honor me.
Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
The Lord said:
10Jerusalem, your city walls
will be rebuilt by foreigners;
their rulers will become
your slaves.
I punished you in my anger;
now I will be kind
and treat you with mercy.
11 Your gates will be open
day and night
to let the rulers of nations
lead their people to you
with all their treasures.
12Any nation or kingdom
that refuses to serve you
will be wiped out.
13Wood from Lebanon's best trees
will be brought to you—
the pines, the firs,
and the cypress trees.
It will be used in my temple
to make beautiful the place
where I rest my feet.
14 The descendants of enemies
who hated and mistreated you
will kneel at your feet.
They will say, “You are Zion,
the city of the Lord,
the holy One of Israel.”
15You were hated and deserted,
rejected by everyone.
But I will make you beautiful,
a city to be proud of
for all time to come.
16You will drain the wealth
of kings and foreign nations.
You will know that I,
the mighty Lord God of Israel,
have saved and rescued you.
17I will bring bronze and iron
in place of wood and stone;
in place of bronze and iron,
I will bring gold and silver.
I will appoint peace and justice
as your rulers and leaders.
18Violence, destruction, and ruin
will never again be heard of
within your borders.
“Victory” will be the name
you give to your walls;
“Praise” will be the name
you give to your gates.
19 You won't need the light
of the sun or the moon.
I, the Lord your God,
will be your eternal light
and bring you honor.
20Your sun will never set
or your moon go down.
I, the Lord, will be
your everlasting light,
and your days of sorrow
will come to an end.
21Your people will live right
and always own the land;
they are the trees I planted
to bring praise to me.
22Even the smallest family
will be a powerful nation.
I am the Lord,
and when the time comes,
I will quickly do all this.
translation_text:
Jerusalem aah ga kan kipak n‑yoonn mu choo na pu na
1Jerusalem, fii sil, ki li wiin ke nwiin na;
Uwumbɔr aanyuŋ aah wiin chain pu na bi wolni aa pu.
2Ŋitimbol ŋiken pu ga li ye mbɔmbɔɔn la,
le Uwumbɔr aawiihn ga woln aa ma pu;
waah wiin chain pu na ga li bi aa chee.
3Ŋitimbol ga kuun dan saawiihn chee,
le bibɔrb san dan saataak ki bi wolni na chee.
4Lik goln aabaa ki kan tiwan ni bi ŋani na:
Saanib bi kuuni ke bi kun ni la.
Aajapɔtiib ga nyan ni dandar;
Bi ga yoor aabisatiib ŋmam ke baah ŋmamni mbim pu na la.
5Aa ga kan nimina, le aasui piir chak chak.
Aawon ga li gbaa aasui aah piir pu na pu.
Bi ga li joo ni ŋitimbol aawangol ki nan tii si;
ŋitimbol ngbaan aawangol ga puur nnyusakpem ki pii ni si.
6Laakumii tiib pam ga ki nyan ni Midiann, ni Efa aatim ni
ki fuu ni.
Bi nyan ni Seba, ki joo ni salmaa ni tulalee.
Binib ga len tibɔnyaan ngbaan,
bi ga len Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu na.
7Bi ga joo ni Kedar ni Nebayof aapiih mɔmɔk
nan tii Jerusalem yaab ke bi di toor ipiin aatork
Uwumbɔr aabimbiln paab aan ni piir usui.
Uwumbɔr ga moo nyuŋ
Waadichal ki jer laah nan kan pu na.
8Ni ye ba aaŋɔsakpiin ki san mala mala ke ntaalangbam na,
ki naahn ŋinanjel le aah choo kun ni na?
9Ni ye iŋɔi i nyan ni dandar na la,
i joo ni Uwumbɔr aanib le choo kun ni.
Bi joo ni salmaa ni tikunabr la,
ke bi nan di nyuŋ timi Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr
u bi chain ki cha ŋitimbol pak timi waanib na aayimbil.
