10Uwumbɔr bui Jerusalem ke,
“Biwɔwɔm le ga ki gir maa saagon,
le baabɔrb li ye saanaagbiib.
Maaŋuul ponn ni le m nan daa nitafal,
le dandana wee ma m ga mɔk nimi maanimbaasaln,
ni maah gee nimi pu na.
11Jerusalem aagon aabisamɔi aan ki piin nwiin pu ni kinyeek,
le ŋinibol aabɔrb ga li joo ni baawangol ki ponn ni.
12Le ŋinibol ŋi kaa tun lituln tii nimi na ga kuln kookoo.
13Binib ga di bunaasub ni lisalaasiil
ni isui imɔk bi Lebanonn
aachook ni ki ŋan ki pɔɔ na
giin maa sin Jerusalem,
ki ŋa Maadichal kinyaan, ki moo nyuŋ maatiŋ.
14Binib bi muk si na aajapɔtiib ga
dan ki nan gbaan kitiŋ aanimbiin ni.
Binib bimɔk nan lik seen si n‑yoonn mu jer na
ga dan nan gbaan kitiŋ ki doon si.
Bi ga yin si ke ‘Uwumbɔr aatiŋ’, ki ki yin si ke,
‘Sionn, Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na aatiŋ’.
15Ubaa aan ki lik si fam, kaan ki li nan si,
kitiŋ ki baanib nan san cha ki aan ki ye tilangbenn na.
M ga tii si mpɔɔn ni kinyaan
nin chee mmɔɔn ga li bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.
16Ŋitimbol ni bibɔrb le ga li tun tii si,
ke ubo aana aah kpiini u pu aan u ti chikr na.
Aa ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr le gaa si lii;
min Israel yaab Aawumbɔr
Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na le gaa si lii kookoo.
17Buyoonn ni ban mbɔman na
m ga tii nimi salmaa,
buyoonn ni ban tikur ni idɔ na,
m ga tii nimi tikunabr ni mbɔman,
le buyoonn ni ban litakpal na,
m ga tii nimi tikur.
Binib bi joo nimi na aan ki li muk nimi;
m ga cha bi di ibamɔn ni nsuudoon le di joo nimi.
18Naan ki ŋun tijar aafuuk pu daalbaadaal;
libiil aan ki dan nimi aatiŋ ni daalbaadaal.
M ga li kii nimi ke ligoln na la;
ni ga pak mi, maah gaa nimi lii pu na pu.
19Nwiin aan ki li ye nimi aawiihn nwiin pu,
le uŋmal mu aan ki li ye nimi aawiihn kinyeek;
min Uwumbɔr le ga li ye nimi aawiihn mu kaan junn na,
maanyuŋ aawiihn le ga li wiin ni pu.
20Nimi aapombiin aayoonn ga doo.
Min Uwumbɔr le ga li ye nimi aawiihn mu kaan junn na,
ki ye nwiihn mu wiin ki yunni
jer nwiin ni uŋmal aawiihn na.
21Jerusalem aanib mɔmɔk ga li tun ŋitun ŋi tok chob na la,
ki ga li yeh kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
Min le naan bi ki kaan bi
ke bi kpiir maapɔɔn mɔk unibɔn mɔmɔk.
22Hali Jerusalem aadichawaatiir li bi ki bi suuna na
ga kpaln litimbol li kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na la.
N‑yoonn mu ŋeer na yaa fuu ni kan,
m ga cha kina ŋa woween.
Min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
The Good News of Victory
1 The Spirit of the Lord God
has taken control of me!
The Lord has chosen and sent me
to tell the oppressed
the good news,
to heal the brokenhearted,
and to announce freedom
for prisoners and captives.
2 This is the year
when the Lord God
will show kindness to us
and punish our enemies.
The Lord has sent me
to comfort those who mourn,
3especially in Jerusalem.
He sent me to give them flowers
in place of their sorrow,
olive oil in place of tears,
and joyous praise
in place of broken hearts.
They will be called
“Trees of Justice,”
planted by the Lord
to honor his name.
4Then they will rebuild cities
that have been in ruins
for many generations.
5They will hire foreigners
to take care of their sheep
and their vineyards.
6But they themselves will be
priests and servants
of the Lord our God.
The treasures of the nations
will belong to them,
and they will be famous.
7They were terribly insulted
and horribly mistreated;
now they will be greatly blessed
and joyful forever.
The Lord Loves Justice
8I, the Lord, love justice!
But I hate robbery
and injustice.
My people, I solemnly promise
to reward you
with an eternal agreement.
9Your descendants will be known
in every nation.
All who see them will realize
that they have been blessed,
by me, the Lord.
Celebrate and Shout
10 I celebrate and shout
because of my Lord God.
His saving power and justice
are the very clothes I wear.
They are more beautiful
than the jewelry worn
by a bride or groom.
11The Lord will bring about
justice and praise
in every nation on earth,
like flowers blooming
in a garden.
translation_text:
Ŋŋmarm aabɔnyaan
1Tidindaan Uwumbɔr di Waafuur Nyaan gbiin mi,
u lee mi ki tun mi ke m tuk bigiim tibɔnyaan tee;
u tun mi ke m nan sɔŋ binib bi kpa mpombiin na aasui,
ki tuk binaagbiib ke m gaa bi lii a,
ki tuk biyom mu ke bi kan bibaa a.
2U tun ni mi ke m nan moon ke n‑yoonn fuu ni,
buyoonn Uwumbɔr ga gaa
waanib lii ki nyaŋ waadim na.
U tun ni mi ke m nan sɔŋ binib bi wii na aasui,
3ke m nan tii binib bi wii Sionn ni na mpopiin ni nsuudoon,
bi taa ki wii, ki gaa kipak aalahn, ni taa li ye ikpowiil.
Bi ga li naahn isui i Uwumbɔr ubaa bun i na la.
Bi mɔmɔk ga li ŋani tiwan ni si chob na la,
le binib ga pak Uwumbɔr, waah tun pu na pu.
4Bi ga gir maa ntim mu nan gur ye tilangbenn na.
5Maanib, biwɔwɔm le ga li ye nimi aanaagbiib.
Bima le ga li kpaa nimi aawakor,
ki ko nimi aasar,
ni nimi aadaan aasui aasar ni.
6Le binib ga li nyi nimi, ke ni ye Uwumbɔr aatotoorb,
timi Aawumbɔr aatutum.
Ni ga ji ŋitimbol ŋiken aawangol,
ki li mak ke ni ye nimi yaan la.
7Nimi aanimɔɔn doo a.
Ni ga li bi nibaa aatiŋ ni la,
le nimi aawangol moo kpee
aan nimi aapopiin mu aan li kpa ndoon.
8Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“M gee ibamɔn le kaa gee limukl ni titunwanbir.
Maah ye mbamɔndaan na,
m ga pa maanib,
le ki puu tipuur ti kaan doo na tii bi.
9Maanib ga li kpa liyimbisakpeln ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ni;
unii umɔk kan bi na ga bee
ke bi ye binib bi m ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu na la.”
10Jerusalem mɔɔni Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu tii u na pu.
U gor ubaa ke usapɔɔn u ban u kun uchal do na
aah gor ubaa pu pu na la.
Uwumbɔr di ŋŋmarm ni linyaŋ di peen u.
11Njikaabim aah ŋani pu ki ti punn ki muuni na,
kina le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ga gaa waanib lii,
le ŋitimbol mɔmɔk pak u.

english_text:
Jerusalem Will Be Saved
1Jerusalem, I will speak up
for your good.
I will never be silent
till you are safe and secure,
sparkling like a flame.
2Your great victory will be seen
by every nation and king;
the Lord will even give you
a new name.
3You will be a glorious crown,
a royal headband
for the Lord your God.
4Your name will no longer be
“Deserted and Childless,”
but “Happily Married.”
You will please the Lord;
your country
will be his bride.
5Your people will take the land,
just as a young man
takes a bride.
The Lord will be pleased
because of you,
just as a husband is pleased
with his bride.
6Jerusalem, on your walls
I have stationed guards,
whose duty it is
to speak out day and night,
without resting.
They must remind the Lord
7and not let him rest
till he makes Jerusalem strong
and famous everywhere.
8The Lord has given his word
and made this promise:
“Never again will I give
to your enemies
the grain and grapes
for which you struggled.
9As surely as you harvest
your grain and grapes,
you will eat your bread
with thankful hearts,
and you will drink your wine
in my temple.”
10People of Jerusalem,
open your gates!
Repair the road to the city
and clear it of stones;
raise a banner to help
the nations find their way.
11 Here is what the Lord has said
for all the earth to hear:
“Soon I will come to save
the city of Zion
and to reward you.
12Then you will be called,
‘The Lord's Own People,
The Ones He Rescued!’
Your city will be known
as a good place to live
and a city full of people.”
translation_text:
1M ga len ki pɔɔk Jerusalem yaab aataakpab;
maan di cha limeel ni pu see ni ŋmar,
le nimi aaŋann li wiin
ke kinyeek aamii aah wiin pu na.
2Jerusalem, ŋitimbol ga kan saatunyaan.
Ŋaabɔrb ga kan saawangol,
le aa ga li kpa liyimbipɔln,
liyimbil li Uwumbɔr ubaa ga tii si na.
3Aa ga li ŋan ki wiin chain
ke tiwan ni kpa kidaak saakpen na,
ki ga li bi ke kibɔryikpupuk na le Uwumbɔr chee.
4Ubaa aan ki yin si ke,
“Baah yii u na,”
kaan ki yin saatiŋ ke,
“Upii u aachal san cha u na.”
Saayimbipɔln le ga li ye ke, Hefsiba.
Le saatiŋ mu yoo li ye ke, Bula,
ba pu? Uwumbɔr aanimbil gbiin si,
ki ga li bi ke chal na le ki tii saatiŋ.
5Unachipɔɔn aah yoor upii u kaa nyi uja na pu na,
kina le Uwumbɔr u naan si na ga yoor si ŋa upuu.
Unachipɔɔn aah yoor ubɔɔn aan ni mɔ u pu na,
kina le Uwumbɔr aasui ga li piin aa pu.
6Sin Jerusalem, saagon paab le m ga kaan bikikiib;
bi taa li ŋmin nwiin pu ni kinyeek mu.
Bi li teer Uwumbɔr tipuur ti u puu na,
ki taa cha u suln ti.
7Bi taa cha u fuur kpala ki ti saa
buyoonn u ga ki giin Jerusalem siin kaasisiiyaan,
ki ŋa ki kitiŋ ki dulnyaa mɔmɔk pak na.
8Uwumbɔr puu tipuur ti pɔɔ na,
le waapɔɔn pu u ga ŋa waah puu pu na ke:
“Saadim aan ki di saajikaabim ŋa baajikaar,
le biwɔwɔm mu aan ki nyu nimi aadaan.
9Nimi bi bun ki nan chee nimi aajikaabim na,
le ga nan ji ŋaasaa aan ki pak Uwumbɔr.
Nimi bi ŋum ki lik ndaan aasubil
aasui na, le ga nyu ŋaadaan
min Uwumbɔr Aadichal aachin ni.”
10Jerusalem aanib, nya kitiŋ ngbaan ni man,
ki naan nsan kiir nimi aanib bi gir choo kun ni na.
Naan nsan mu waa na man; nyan ŋitakpal mɔmɔk man,
ki siin limɔkl aan ŋitimbol mɔmɔk bee ke
11Uwumbɔr bi mooni kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu ke:
“Bui Jerusalem aanib ke
Uwumbɔr choo u nan gaa nimi lii,
ki joo ni binib bi u gaa bi lii na.”
12Bi ga li yin nimi ke,
“Uwumbɔr aanib bi bi chain na,”
ki ki yin nimi ke,
“Binib bi Uwumbɔr gaa bi lii na.”
Bi ga yin Jerusalem ke,
“Kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr gee ki na,”
ki ki yin ki ke,
“Kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr aan suln ki bɔr na.”

english_text:
The Lord's Victory over the Nations
1 Who is this coming
from Bozrah in Edom
with clothes stained red?
Who is this hero marching
in his glorious uniform?
“It's me, the Lord!
I have won the battle,
and I can save you!”
2What are those red spots?
Your clothes look stained
from trampling on grapes.
3 “I alone trampled the grapes!
None of the nations helped.
I trampled nations in my anger
and stained my clothes
with their blood.
4I did this because I wanted
to take revenge—
the time had come
to rescue my people.
5 No one was there to help me
or to give support;
my mighty arm won the battle,
strengthened by my anger.
6In my fury I trampled on nations
and made them drunk;
their blood poured out
everywhere on earth.”
The Lord's Goodness to His People
7I will tell about the kind deeds
the Lord has done.
They deserve praise!
The Lord has shown mercy
to the people of Israel;
he has been kind and good.
8The Lord rescued his people,
and said, “They are mine.
They won't betray me.”
9It troubled the Lord
to see them in trouble,
and his angel saved them.
The Lord was truly merciful,
so he rescued his people.
He took them in his arms
and carried them all those years.
10Then the Lord's people
turned against him and made
his Holy Spirit sad.
So he became their enemy
and attacked them.
11But his people remembered
what had happened
during the time of Moses.
Didn't the Lord bring them
and their leaders
safely through the sea?
Didn't he give them
his Holy Spirit?
12 The glorious power of the Lord
marched beside Moses.
The Lord will be praised forever
for dividing the sea.
13He led his people across
like horses running wild
without stumbling.
14His Spirit gave them rest,
just as cattle find rest
when led into a valley.
The name of the Lord was praised
for doing these things.
A Prayer for Mercy and Help
15Please, Lord, look down
from your holy and glorious
home in the heavens
and see what's going on.
Have you lost interest?
Where is your power?
Show that you care about us
and have mercy!
16 Our ancestors Abraham and Jacob
have both rejected us.
But you are still our Father;
you have been our protector
since ancient times.
17Why did you make us turn away
from you, our Lord?
Why did you make us want
to disobey you?
Please change your mind!
We are your servants,
your very own people.
18For a little while,
your temple belonged to us;
and now our enemies
have torn it down.
19We act as though you
had never ruled us
or called us your people.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah nyaŋ ŋitimbol pu na
1“Ŋma ye u nyan ni Bosra aatiŋ ki bi Edom ni na ki choo na? Ŋma ye u pee tiwanyaan ni man na, ki chuun ni mpɔɔn ŋmeen ki choo na?”
Uwumbɔr u kpa mpɔɔn sakpen ki ga ŋmaa gaa unii lii na le choo ke u nan moon waanyaŋ.
2“Ba ŋa waawanpeenkaan man sakpen kina, ki naahn ke waah bi nyani ŋisubil aanyun ke u di ŋaa ndaan le na?”
3Le Uwumbɔr kii ke, “M taa taa ŋitimbol ngbaan ke ndaan aasubil na la, le ubaa aa dan nan ter mi. Maaŋuul ponn ni le m taa taa bi pu, le baasin meeh meeh maawanpeenkaan. 4Le m dakl ke n‑yoonn mu m ga di gaa maanib lii na fuu ni a; ni ŋeer ke m daa baadim aatafal. 5Maah nan lik kaa kan ubaa u ter mi na, ni nan ŋa mi iwaan pam. Le maaŋuul pɔɔk ntaakpab, le m nyaŋ maadim mbaa. 6Maaŋuul ponn ni le m nan taa taa ŋitimbol ki yaa ŋaanib ki di baamɔfal aasin kpir kitiŋ.”
Uwumbɔr aah gee Israel yaab pu na
7Le m bui ke m ga len Uwumbɔr aageehm aah kaa door pu na;
m ga pak u waah ŋa pu tii timi na pu.
U ŋa tinyoor ti nyuun na ŋa Israel yaab pu, waageehm,
ni waanimbaasaln pu.
8Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Bi ye maanib la; baan ŋmann mi.” 9Kina pu le u nyan bi baafalaa ni. Naa nan ye waatuun, uma Uwumbɔr ubaa le nan gaa bi lii. Waageehm ni waanimbaasaln pu le u gaa bi lii. N‑yoonn mu jer na le u nan kii bi, 10le bi nan yii u ki nyan upuwɔb, le ni tii Waafuur Nyaan mpombiin. Kina pu le Uwumbɔr kpaln baadin, le ki jan bi kijaak.
11Le bi teer n‑yoonn mu jer na, Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses aayoonn, le ki baa ke, “Uwumbɔr u nan nyan waanib aaninkpiib nnyusakpem ni na bi la chee dandana wee? Uwumbɔr u nan di Waafuur Nyaan tii Moses na bi la chee? 12-13Uwumbɔr u nan tii Moses waapɔɔn sakpiin ki nan yakr nnyusakpem nfum mulee aan waanib dii jer, ki ti kan liyimbil li kaa kpa ndoon ki tii ubaa na bi la chee?”
Uwumbɔr aah nan loln bi pu nsan na, bi nan chuun ke timoor ni aataan na, kaa gbeer nibaa. 14Baah peer inaa chaa kifataŋ ki kpa timoor na ponn ni pu na, kina le Uwumbɔr tii waanib lifuur. U loln waanib pu nsan ki cha waayimbil kan bunyuŋ.
Linimbaasaln ni nterm aameel
15Uwumbɔr, saah bi paacham nin chee ni bi chain ki kpa kipak na, san timi kinimbaak. Saalandak mu aa nan kpa ti pu na bi la chee? Saapɔɔn bi la chee? Saageehm ni saanimbaasaln bi la chee? Taa suln tibɔr. 16Sin le ye tite. Tiyaajatiib Abraham ni Jakob aa ki nyi timi, le sin Uwumbɔr ma le ye tite u gaal timi lir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na. 17Ba ŋa aa cha ti yenn saasan chee? Ba ŋa aa cha titafal pɔɔ sakpen kina aan ti fenn tipuwɔb tii si? Gir ni, saanib bi ye saatutum ki ye sin yaab n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na chee.
18Timi aadim nan jenn nyan timi saanib bi bi chain na n‑yoonn mubaa, ki gbaa wii Saadichal. 19Aa ŋani timi ke sin le aah kaa nan joo timi n‑yoonn mubaa na, le ni naahn ke taah kaa nan ye saanib n‑yoonn mubaa le na.

english_text:
1Rip the heavens apart!
Come down, Lord;
make the mountains tremble.
2Be a spark that starts a fire
causing water to boil.
Then your enemies will know
who you are;
all nations will tremble
because you are nearby.
3Your fearsome deeds
have completely amazed us;
even the mountains shake
when you come down.
4 You are the only God
ever seen or heard of
who works miracles
for his followers.
5You help all who gladly obey
and do what you want,
but sin makes you angry.
Only by your help
can we ever be saved.
6We are unfit to worship you;
each of our good deeds
is merely a filthy rag.
We dry up like leaves;
our sins are storm winds
sweeping us away.
7No one worships in your name
or remains faithful.
You have turned your back on us
and let our sins melt us away.
8You, Lord, are our Father.
We are nothing but clay,
but you are the potter
who molded us.
9Don't be so furious
or keep our sins
in your thoughts forever!
Remember that all of us
are your people.
10Every one of your towns
has turned into a desert,
especially Jerusalem.
11Zion's glorious and holy temple
where our ancestors praised you
has been destroyed by fire.
Our beautiful buildings
are now a pile of ruins.
12When you see these things,
how can you just sit there
and make us suffer more?
translation_text:
1Uwumbɔr, aa yaa ba daa kar ntaalangbam ki sunn ni kan, m ba ga li gee kina. Ŋijoo ba ga kan si, le ijawaan chuu ŋi le ŋi dam. 2Ŋi ga li gii ke nnyuntom aah leer pu na la. Dan ki nan kpiir saapɔɔn mɔk saadim, ki cha ŋitimbol aawon li gbaa aanimbiin ni. 3N‑yoonn mubaa aa nan sunn ni ki nan ŋa lijinjiir aawan ni taa nan dak ni pu na; ŋijoo nan kan si le ki san ijawaan ki dam. 4Ubaa aa kee kan, bee u ŋun Uwumbɔr uken pu u bi ke sin, u ŋani ŋitun ŋee aaboln tii binib bi mak aa pu na. 5Aa yin binib bi gee ke bi li ŋani ni ŋan na, binib bi teer saah ban pu na, ke bi dan aa chee. Aa nan gee ti pu liŋuul, le ti nan beenin tun titunwanbir; hali saaŋuusakpeln ponn ni ti nan beenin tun titunwanbir ki nyan ni n‑yaajayoonn. 6Ti mɔmɔk tun titunwanbir; hali tima aah dak ke taah tun pu na ŋan sakpen na ye tijɔŋ le ki ti doo. Timi aatunwanbir pu, ti naahn tifar ti kuur aan libuln daar cha na la. 7Ubaa aa fenn toŋ ni si ki mee si; ubaa aa chaa aa chee ki ban nterm. Aa di aabaa bɔr ti chee, ki di timi mee, timi aatunwanbir pu.
8Uwumbɔr, sin le ye tite. Timi le ye tiyakr, le aa ye uyakmaal. Sin le naahn timi, 9kina pu na, taa gee ti pu liŋuusakpeln timi aatunwanbir pu. Ti ye saanib la. San timi kinimbaak. 10Ubaa aa ki bi saatim mu nan bi chain na ponn ni, le Jerusalem mu kpaln tilangbenn, 11le Saadichal li bi chain ki ŋan aan tiyaajatiib nan dooni si nima na, wun mmii a. Taah nan gee nin chee mɔmɔk na kpaln tilangbenn la. 12Uwumbɔr, nimina mɔmɔk aa muk si ii? Aa ga cha ti ji falaa ki ti jer taah ga ŋman pu na aan aa li ka ŋmin aa?

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish the Guilty
1 I, the Lord, was ready
to answer even those
who were not asking
and to be found by those
who were not searching.
To a nation that refused
to worship me,
I said, “Here I am!”
2 All day long I have reached out
to stubborn and sinful people
going their own way.
3They keep making me angry
by sneering at me,
while offering sacrifices
to idols in gardens
and burning incense
to them on bricks.
4They spend their nights
hiding in burial caves;
they eat the meat of pigs,
cooked in sauces
made of stuff unfit to eat.
5And then they say to others,
“Don't come near us!
We're dedicated to God.”
Such people are like smoke,
irritating my nose all day.
6I have written this down;
I won't keep silent.
I'll pay them back
just as their sins deserve.
7I, the Lord, will make them pay
for their sins and for those
of their ancestors—
they have disgraced me
by burning incense
on mountains.
8Here is what the Lord says:
A cluster of grapes
that produces wine
is worth keeping!
So, because of my servants,
I won't destroy everyone.
9I have chosen the people
of Israel and Judah,
and I will bless them
with many descendants.
They will settle here
in this land of mountains,
and it will be theirs.
10 My people will worship me.
Then the coastlands of Sharon
and the land as far
as Achor Valley
will turn into pastureland
where cattle and sheep
will feed and rest.
11What will I, the Lord, do
if any of you reject me
and my holy mountain?
What will happen to you
for offering food and wine
to the gods you call
“Good Luck” and “Fate”?
12Your luck will end!
I will see to it that you
are slaughtered with swords.
You refused to answer
when I called out;
you paid no attention
to my instructions.
Instead, you did what I hated,
knowing it was wrong.
13I, the Lord God, will give
food and drink to my servants,
and they will celebrate.
But all of you sinners
will go hungry and thirsty,
overcome with disgrace.
14My servants will laugh and sing,
but you will be sad
and cry out in pain.
15I, the Lord God, promise
to see that you are killed
and that my chosen servants use
your names as curse words.
But I will give new names
to my servants.
16I am God! I can be trusted.
Your past troubles are gone;
I no longer think of them.
When you pray for someone
to receive a blessing,
or when you make a promise,
you must do it in my name.
I alone am the God
who can be trusted.
The Lord's New Creation
17 I am creating new heavens
and a new earth;
everything of the past
will be forgotten.
18Celebrate and be glad forever!
I am creating a Jerusalem,
full of happy people.
19 I will celebrate with Jerusalem
and all its people;
there will be no more crying
or sorrow in that city.
20No child will die in infancy;
everyone will live
a very long life.
Anyone a hundred years old
will be considered young,
and to die younger than that
will be considered a curse.
21My people will live
in the houses they build;
they will enjoy grapes
from their own vineyards.
22No one will take away
their homes or vineyards.
My chosen people will live
to be as old as trees,
and they will enjoy
what they have earned.
23Their work won't be wasted,
and their children won't die
of dreadful diseases.
I will bless their children
and their grandchildren.
24I will answer their prayers
before they finish praying.
25 Wolves and lambs
will graze together;
lions and oxen
will feed on straw.
Snakes will eat only dirt!
They won't bite or harm anyone
on my holy mountain.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr daa binib bi yii u na aatafal
1Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M nan gor ki kii ke m kii maanib aameel, le bi yii kaa mee. M nan gor ki kii ke bi kan mi, le bi yii kaa pɔɔni bibaa ke bi ban mi. Litimbol ngbaan aa nan mee mi kpala, hali m nan gor ki kii ke m kii baameel n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke, ‘Min le na do; m ga ter nimi.’ 2N‑yoonn mɔmɔk m nan gor ki kii ke m gaa maanib, le bi yii ki tun titunwanbir ki dii bibaa aasan. 3Bi ŋani mi liŋuul, kaa san inimɔɔn. Bi toor tisamoor ki seer nnyɔknii ŋiwaabimbin pu. 4Kinyeek kan, bi chaa titakpalunn ni, ni ŋikaakul ponn ni le ti buu tibɔɔr bitekpiib chee. Bi ŋmɔ ugbeer, ki nyu baah di tiwakor ti toor tii ŋiwaa na aakpinyun mu bi di tinann seen mu ni na, 5le ki bui ke, ‘Taa mar ti chee; ti bi chain jer si, aa kpa tijɔŋ, taa meeh timi.’ Le m bui ke, ‘Min ni binib ngbaan aaboln aan kpaan, m gee liŋuul li bi ke mmii mu kaan junn na le bi pu.’
6“M puun siin baatafadaan, ki ŋmee maah ga ŋa bi pu na bil. Maan suln baah ŋa pu na aabɔr, m ga teen bi 7baatunwanbir ni biyaajatiib aatunwanbir pu. Bi seer nnyɔknii tiwaachur ni ŋigongon paab ki len tibɔbir m pu. Kina pu na, m ga daa bitafal ki ŋeer baah tun pu na la.”
8Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Ubaa aan bii ndaan aasubil ŋi ŋan na; baah ŋani ŋi pu na sɔ, bi di ŋi ŋa ŋisubil aadaan la. Kina le maan ku doo maanib mɔmɔk, m ga gaa binib bi tun maatuln na lii. 9M ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa Israel yaab ponn ni bi ye Juda aamaal aanib na, le biyaabitiib ga nan li yeh maajoo pu aatiŋ. Bi ye maanib bi m nyan bi na, ki mu ye maatutum. Bima le ga li koo nima. 10Bi ga li dooni mi aan ki di baawakor di buen Saronn, ni bi liwilir wɔb na, ni Tibɔbir Aafataŋ ki bi liwipuul wɔb na ti ti ŋmɔ timoor.
11“Le nimi bi yii mi na ma kan, naan li bi kina, nimi bi yii maagongoln Sionn li bi chain na, ki dooni ŋiwaa Gad ni Meni, ŋiwaa ŋi ni bui ke ŋi kpa liyimɔɔn na, ki siin nimi aabimbin aah ga li doo pu na. 12Ni ga li ye nimi aadoon le ke ni kpo mpɔɔkun, ba pu? naa nan kii buyoonn m yin nimi na, kaa pel maah len pu na mu. Ni yii, kaa kii maamɔb, le ki tun titunwanbir, 13le m ban m bui nimi ke binib bi dooni mi ki kii maamɔb na ga li kpa pam bi ji ki nyu, nimi ma kan, nkon ni nnyunyuu ga li joo nimi. Bi ga li kpa mpopiin, le nimi ga ji inimɔɔn. 14Bi ga di mpopiin gaa ilahn, le nimi ga wii, nisui aah ga li bii pu na. 15Maanib bi m nyan bi na ga li joo nimi aayimbil le puuni lir binib pu, ke bi li bee fam ke nimi na. Min, Bidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga ku nimi, le ki tii binib bi kii maamɔb na liyimbipɔln. 16Unii umɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na yaa ban tinyoor kan, u ga cha Uwumbɔr u ŋani waah len pu na le ŋa tinyoor ŋa u pu. Umɔk ban u puu tipuur na ga di Uwumbɔr u ŋani waah len pu na aayimbil le puu tipuur. N‑yoonn mu jer na aabɔbir mɔmɔk ga kuln.”
Dulnyaa pɔɔn
17Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “M ki bi naani kitipɔŋ ni kitaapaapɔŋ la. Ubaa aan ki teer n‑yoonn mu jer na aabɔr. 18Cha nisui li piin aan ni li mɔɔni maah ban m naan ni na pu. Maah ban m naan Jerusalem pɔɔn u na ponn ni ga li ye mmɔɔn ŋmeen la, le kaanib ga li kpa mpopiin. 19Min mbaa ga li kpa mpopiin Jerusalem ni kaanib pu. Iwiil aan li bi nima, ubaa aan li yin uken ki ban nterm nima. 20Mbim aan ki kpo tibipɔnn ni, le binib mɔmɔk ga fuu baakundaal le ki nin kpo. Binib bi ti saa ŋibin nkub ki kpo na ga laa li ye binachipɔm la. Binib bi kpo kaa fuu ŋibin nkub na ga li ye limɔkl ke m daa bitafal la. 21-22Binib ga maa ŋidichal ki koo ŋi ponn ni bibaa, uniyayan aan koo ŋi ponn ni. Bi ga bu ndaan aasubil aasui ki nyu yaadaan, uniyayan aan nyu mu. Maanib ga li bi ki yunn ke isui na la. Bi ga ji nimɔk bi tun ki kan na aamɔɔn. 23Baah tun ŋitun ŋi na ga li kpa tinyoor, le baabim aan kan tibɔbir tibaa. M ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi ni biyaabitiib pu ki joo cha. 24Waahr aan bi nin mee mi doo na, m ga kii baameel. 25Takɔ tiib ni ipihbi ga kpaan ji; ichinn ga ŋmɔ timoor ke inaa aah ŋmɔ pu na, le iwaa mu aan ki li bir. Maagongoln Sionn li bi chain na pu, nibaa aan li bi li paab ki bir.”

english_text:
True Worship
1 The Lord said:
Heaven is my throne;
the earth is my footstool.
What kind of house
could you build for me?
In what place will I rest?
2I have made everything;
that's how it all came to be.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The people I treasure most
are the humble—
they depend only on me
and tremble when I speak.
3You sacrifice oxen to me,
and you commit murder;
you sacrifice lambs to me
and dogs to other gods;
you offer grain to me
and pigs' blood to idols;
you burn incense to me
and praise your idols.
You have made your own choice
to do these disgusting things
that you enjoy so much.
4You refused to answer
when I called out;
you paid no attention
to my instructions.
Instead, you did what I hated,
knowing it was wrong.
Now I will punish you
in a way you dread the most.
The Lord Will Help Jerusalem
5If you tremble
when the Lord speaks,
listen to what he says:
“Some of your own people hate
and reject you because of me.
They make fun and say,
‘Let the Lord show his power!
Let us see him
make you truly happy.’
But those who say these things
will be terribly ashamed.”
6Do you hear that noise
in the city and those shouts
coming from the temple?
It is the Lord shouting
as he punishes his enemies.
7 Have you ever heard of a woman
who gave birth to a child
before having labor pains?
8Who ever heard of such a thing
or imagined it could happen?
Can a nation be born in a day
or come to life in a second?
Jerusalem is like a mother
who gave birth to her children
as soon as she was in labor.
9The Lord is the one
who makes birth possible.
And he will see that Zion
has many more children.
The Lord has spoken.
10If you love Jerusalem,
celebrate and shout!
If you were in sorrow
because of the city,
you can now be glad.
11She will nurse and comfort you,
just like your own mother,
until you are satisfied.
You will fully enjoy
her wonderful glory.
12The Lord has promised:
“I will flood Jerusalem
with the wealth of nations
and make the city prosper.
Zion will nurse you at her breast,
carry you in her arms,
and hold you in her lap.
13I will comfort you there
like a mother
comforting her child.”
14When you see this happen,
you will celebrate;
your strength will return
faster than grass can sprout.
Then everyone will know
that the Lord provides help
for his servants,
but he is angry
with his enemies.
15The Lord will come down
like a whirlwind
with his flaming chariots.
He will be furiously angry
and punish his enemies
with fire.
16The Lord's fiery sword
will bring justice
everywhere on this earth
and execute many people.
A Threat and a Promise
17Some of you get yourselves ready and go to a garden to worship a foreign goddess. You eat the meat of pigs, lizards, and mice. But I, the Lord, will destroy you for this.
18I know everything you do and think! The time has now come to bring together the people of every language and nation and to show them my glory 19by proving what I can do. I will send the survivors to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Meshech, Tubal, Javan, and to the distant islands. I will send them to announce my wonderful glory to nations that have never heard about me.
20They will bring your relatives from the nations as an offering to me, the Lord. They will come to Jerusalem, my holy mountain, on horses, chariots, wagons, mules, and camels. It will be like the people of Israel bringing the right offering to my temple. 21I promise that some of them will be priests and others will be helpers in my temple. I, the Lord, have spoken.
22 I also promise that you will always have descendants and will never be forgotten, just as the new heavens and the new earth that I create will last forever. 23On the first day of each month and on each Sabbath, everyone will worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
24 My people will go out and look at the dead bodies of those who turned against me. The worms there never die, the fire never stops burning, and the sight of those bodies will be disgusting to everyone.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr ga ji ŋitimbol tibɔr
1Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Kitaapaak le ye maabɔrjal, le kitiŋ ye ntaa aah taa ni pu na. Ni ga maa ba aadichal aaboln ki tii mi, ba aapaan ni ga kan tii mi aan m li koo nima? 2Min mbaa le nan naan dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk. Nsui piin binib bi sunn bibaa taab aan bisui bii baatunwanbir pu, ki san mi ki kii maamɔb na pu.
3“Binib ngbaan ŋani baah gee pu na la. Bi yaa di unaaja toor kitork, bee bi yaa ti ki di unibɔn le di toor kitork kan, naa muk bi; bi yaa di upihbo di toor, bee bi yaa di ubɔ toor kan, bi dak ke ni kpaa la; baajikaabim aapiin ni baagbeer aasin aapiin ye bi chee tiwan nibaa la; baah seer tulalee aayon tii Uwumbɔr pu na, ni baah dooni ŋiwaa pu na ye bi chee tiwan nibaa la. Nimina mɔmɔk aa kpa bi chee tibɔbir. Baah dooni Uwumbɔr baageehn wɔb pu na mɔ bi, le ki nu Uwumbɔr chee. 4Kina pu na, m ga cha tibɔbir lir bi pu. Baah san tiwan ni ijawaan na le ga kan bi, ba pu? maah nan yin bi na, baa nan kii, kaa nan pel buyoonn m len bi chee na. Bi nan yii maamɔb ki tun titunwanbir.”
5Nimi bi san Uwumbɔr ki kii waamɔb na, li pel man waah len pu na: “Naah gaa mi ki kii pu na, nimi aanib bibaa nan nimi, kaa ban bi kpaan ni chee. Bi laa nimi ki len ke, ‘Cha Uwumbɔr mɔk waapɔɔn ki gaa nimi lii, aan ti kan naah ga li mɔɔni pu na.’ Le bima bibaa le ga ji inimɔɔn. 6Li pel man, kifuuk sakpeŋ ki bi kitiŋ ponn ni na, ni ki bi Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na, ki ye Uwumbɔr aah bi dar waadim aatafal pu na aafuuk la.
7“Maatiŋ ki bi chain na bi ke upii u ma ubo, kaa kan imalween na la. 8Ubaa kee kan, bee u ŋun kina aabɔr aa? Litimbol kee naan liwinbaal aa? Sionn aan ji falaa ni yunn le litimbol ngbaan nin naan. 9Taa dak ke m ga cha maanib kan imalween kaan maa.” Uwumbɔr le len kina.
10Li mɔɔni man Jerusalem pu.
Nimi bimɔk gee kitiŋ kee na,
cha nisui li piin u pu,
nimi bimɔk nan wii kaakpowiil na,
li mɔɔni ter ki man.
11Ni ga ji kaawangol ke ubo aah ŋaa una aabiil pu na.
12Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M ga joo ni nimi liwangol li kaan doo na; litimbol mɔmɔk aawangol ga li choo ni chee ke limɔɔl li kaa foor na la. Ni ga li naahn upii aah ŋaani waabo, ki joo u uŋaal ni, ni ngeehm pu na la. 13M ga sɔŋ nisui, Jerusalem ni, ke upii aah sɔŋni waabo aasui pu na la. 14Ni yaa kan nimina ŋa kan, ni ga mɔɔr nimi ki tii nimi mpɔɔn ni laafee. Le ni bee ke min Uwumbɔr ter binib bi kii maamɔb na, ki mɔk maadim maaŋuul.”
15Uwumbɔr ga di mmii le dan. U ga dan mala ke kibuŋ na le ki nan daa waah gee binib bi pu liŋuul na aatafal. 16U ga di mmii ni kijaak aajuk le di daa dulnyaa aanib bi aabɔr bii u chee na aatafal, le pam ga kpo.
17Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Binib bi toor bibaa ki dooni ŋiwaa, ki chɔl ki chaa ti toor tisamoor, ki ŋmɔ ugbeer, ni ŋilapol, ni tijikaar ti kaa ŋan na aadoon peen ni a. 18M nyi baalandak ni baatun. M choo m nan kuun litimbol mɔmɔk aanib la. Bi yaa kuun ni kan, bi ga kan maapɔɔn aah ga ŋmaa tun pu na, 19ki bee ke min le dar bitafal.
“Le m ga gaa bi ponn ni bibaa lii ki tun bi ŋitimbol, ni ntim mu daa kaa kee ŋun maayimbil pu, ki mu aa kee kan maapɔɔn na: ki ye Speenn aatiŋ, ni Libia, ni Lidia aatim ni, nin chee kpa bijab bi ŋmaa too itɔi na, ni Tubal ni Griis aatim ni. Ŋitimbol ŋee ponn ni le bi ga moon maapɔɔn. 20Bi ga giin joo ni nimi aatiŋ aanib ki nyan ni ŋitimbol ngbaan ni ke ipiin na la, ki nan tii mi. Bi ga joo ni bi itaan, ni ibon, ni laakumii tiib pu, ni itaan aatɔroku tiib pu, ki di dan maagongoln li bi chain na pu, ke Israel yaab aah joo ni njikaabim aapiin choo Jerusalem, min Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, ŋisambil ŋi bi chain na ponn ni pu na la. 21M ga ŋa bi ponn ni bibaa bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab.
22“Kitaapaapɔŋ ni kitipɔŋ aah ga yunn maapɔɔn pu pu na, kina le niyaabitiib ni nimi aayimbil ga yunn. 23Uŋmapɔɔn aajim, ni Likpaakool daal aakuun mɔmɔk ponn ni, ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aanib ga dan Jerusalem do le nan doon mi.” Uwumbɔr le len kina. 24“Bi yaa gir chaa kun kan, bi ga kan binib bi yii maamɔb na aanikpol. Ŋikpaambil ŋi ŋmɔ biwon na aan kpo daalbaadaal, le mmii mu wu bi na mu aan junn. Unibɔn umɔk kan bi na ga sur upuwɔb.”

english_text:
1My name is Jeremiah. I am a priest, and my father Hilkiah and everyone else in my family are from Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. This book contains the things that the Lord told me to say. 2 The Lord first spoke to me in the thirteenth year that Josiah was king of Judah, 3 and he continued to speak to me during the rule of Josiah's son Jehoiakim. The last time the Lord spoke to me was in the fifth month of the eleventh year that Josiah's son Zedekiah was king. That was also when the people of Jerusalem were taken away as prisoners.
The Lord Chooses Jeremiah
4The Lord said:
5“Jeremiah, I am your Creator,
and before you were born,
I chose you to speak for me
to the nations.”
6I replied, “I'm not a good speaker, Lord, and I'm too young.”
7“Don't say you're too young,” the Lord answered. “If I tell you to go and speak to someone, then go! And when I tell you what to say, don't leave out a word! 8I promise to be with you and keep you safe, so don't be afraid.”
9The Lord reached out his hand, then he touched my mouth and said, “I am giving you the words to say, 10and I am sending you with authority to speak to the nations for me. You will tell them of doom and destruction, and of rising and rebuilding again.”
11The Lord showed me something in a vision. Then he asked, “What do you see, Jeremiah?”
I answered, “A branch of almonds that ripen early.”
12“That's right,” the Lord replied, “and I always rise early to keep a promise.”
13Then the Lord showed me something else and asked, “What do you see now?”
I answered, “I see a pot of boiling water in the north, and it's about to spill out toward us.”
14The Lord said:
I will pour out destruction
all over the land.
15Just watch while I send
for the kings of the north.
They will attack and capture
Jerusalem and other towns,
then set up their thrones
at the gates of Jerusalem.
16I will punish my people,
because they are guilty
of turning from me
to worship idols.
17Jeremiah, get ready!
Go and tell the people
what I command you to say.
Don't be frightened by them,
or I will make you terrified
while they watch.
18My power will make you strong
like a fortress
or a column of iron
or a wall of bronze.
You will oppose all of Judah,
including its kings and leaders,
its priests and people.
19They will fight back,
but they won't win.
I, the Lord, give my word—
I won't let them harm you.
translation_text:
Jeremia aah nan ŋmee pu na sɔ:
1Kigbaŋ kimina ponn ni aabɔr ye Jeremia aabɔr la. U nan ye Hilkia aajapɔɔn, ki mu nan ye bitotoorb bi nan bi Anatof aatiŋ ki bi Benjaminn aapepel ni na ponn ni ubaa la. 2Uwumbɔr nan len Jeremia chee tibɔr, buyoonn Amonn aajapɔɔn Josia nan ye Juda aabɔr na aabin kipiik ni litatar ponn ni na la, 3le ki ki gir len u chee buyoonn Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim mu nan ye ubɔr na. Nee aapuwɔb na, Uwumbɔr nan ki len u chee n‑yoonn n‑yoonn pam, ki ti saa Josia aajapɔɔn Sedekia aanaan ni aabin kipiik ni libaa ni. Libiln ngbaan aaŋmaŋmu ni, le bidim nan nyaŋ Jerusalem yaab ki chur bi buen tinaagbiir ni.
Uwumbɔr aah yin Jeremia pu na
4Uwumbɔr nan bui mi Jeremia ke, 5“M nan nyan si waahr le ki nin tii si limɔfal, le waahr aan bi nin ma si na, m nan lee si ke aa li ye maabɔnabr tii ŋitimbol.”
6Le m gar u ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, maa ŋmaa len; m laa par sakpen.”
7Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, “Taa bui ke aa par sakpen. Li cha maah tun si binib bi chee na, ki ti bui bi maah bui si ke aa len pu na mɔmɔk. 8M ga li bi aa chee ki kii si. Taa san bi ijawaan. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
9Nee aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr taln uŋaal ki di meeh mmɔgban, le ki bui mi ke, “Li pel, m bi tii si tibɔr ti aa ga len na la. 10Din wee, m tii si mpɔɔn ŋitimbol ni nnaan pu ke aa ber, ki tur ŋi lii, ki nyaŋ ki kuln ŋi, ki ki maa ki siin ŋi.”
Tibɔkpiirkaan tilee
11Uwumbɔr nan baa mi ke, “Jeremia, aa waa ba?”
Le m gar u ke, “M waa busub bu bi yin bu ke ‘Ka kii’ na aasubon la.”
12Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, “Ni ye mbamɔn, le m ka kii ke m ŋa maah len ke m ga ŋa pu na.”
13Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee. U nan baa mi ke, “Aa ki waa ba ki kpee?”
Le m gar u ke, “M waa likumbuul aah tok ŋŋangan wɔb ki kpinni ki ban li lir ni lipepel lee wɔb pu na.”
14Le u nan bui mi ke, “Libiil le bi ŋŋangan wɔb ki kpinni kina choo binib bi mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ kee pu na, 15ba pu? m bi yin ŋitimbol ŋi bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ke ŋi dan la. Ŋaabɔrb ga di baabɔrjal siin Jerusalem aabisamɔi chee, ki siin mann goln kaagon, ki siin mann goln Juda aatim muken na mu. 16M ga daa maanib aatafal, baatunwanbir pu; bi yii mi, ki toor kitork tii ŋiwaa, ki naan ŋiwaa ki dooni ŋi. 17Jeremia, gor ki buen ti bui bi maah bui si ke aa len pu na mɔmɔk. Taa san bi ijawaan dandana wee, naa ye kina kan, buyoonn aa bi bi chee na, le m ga cha ijawaan chuu si. 18-19Jeremia, li pel. Kitiŋ kee pu aanib mɔmɔk—Juda aabɔrb, ni bininkpiib, ni bitotoorb, ga li kpak si. Tɔ, din wee le m bi tii si mpɔɔn mu aa ga di sil kiir bi na; aa ga li bi ke kitiŋ ki bi maa ŋigon kiir ki na la, ki naahn tikur aagoln, ki bi ke tikumann aagoln na. Baan ŋmaa nyaŋ si, ba pu? m ga li bi aa chee ki kiir si. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
Israel's Unfaithfulness
1The Lord told me 2to go to Jerusalem and tell everyone that he had said:
When you were my young bride,
you loved me and followed me
through the barren desert.
3You belonged to me alone,
like the first part of the harvest,
and I severely punished
those who mistreated you.
4Listen, people of Israel,
5and I, the Lord, will speak.
I was never unfair
to your ancestors,
but they left me
and became worthless
by following worthless idols.
6Your ancestors refused
to ask for my help,
though I had rescued them
from Egypt
and led them through
a treacherous, barren desert,
where no one lives
or dares to travel.
7I brought you here to my land,
where food is abundant,
but you made my land filthy
with your sins.
8The priests who teach my laws
don't care to know me.
Your leaders rebel against me;
your prophets
give messages from Baal
and worship false gods.
The Lord Accuses His People
9I will take you to court
and accuse you
and your descendants
* 10of a crime that no nation
has ever committed before.
Just ask anyone, anywhere,
from the eastern deserts
to the islands in the west.
11You will find that no nation
has ever abandoned its gods
even though they were false.
I am the true and glorious God,
but you have rejected me
to worship idols.
12Tell the heavens
to tremble with fear!
13You, my people, have sinned
in two ways—
you have rejected me, the source
of life-giving water,
and you've tried to collect water
in cracked and leaking pits
dug in the ground.
14People of Israel,
you weren't born slaves;
you were captured in war.
15Enemies roared like lions
and destroyed your land;
towns lie burned and empty.
16Soldiers from the Egyptian towns
of Memphis and Tahpanhes
have cracked your skulls.
17It's all your own fault!
You stopped following me,
the Lord your God,
18and you trusted the power
of Egypt and Assyria.
19Your own sins will punish you,
because it was a bitter mistake
for you to reject me
without fear of punishment.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
20Long ago you left me
and broke all ties between us,
refusing to be my servant.
Now you worship other gods
by having sex
on hilltops or in the shade
of large trees.
21You were a choice grapevine,
but you have become
a wild, useless vine.
Israel Is Stained with Guilt
22The Lord said:
People of Israel,
you are stained with guilt,
and no soap or bleach
can wash it away.
23You deny your sins
and say, “We aren't unclean.
We haven't worshiped Baal.”
But think about what you do
in Hinnom Valley.
You run back and forth
like young camels,
as you rush to worship one idol
after another.
24You are a female donkey
sniffing the desert air,
wanting to mate
with just anyone.
You are an easy catch!
25Your shoes are worn out,
and your throat is parched
from running here and there
to worship foreign gods.
“Stop!” I shouted,
but you replied, “No!
I love those gods too much.”
26You and your leaders
are more disgraceful
than thieves—
you and your kings,
your priests and prophets
27worship stone idols
and sacred poles
as if they had created you
and had given you life.
You have rejected me,
but when you're in trouble,
you cry to me for help.
28Go cry to the gods you made!
There should be enough of them
to save you,
because Judah has as many gods
as it has towns.
Israel Rebels against the Lord
29The Lord said to Israel:
You accuse me of not saving you,
but I say you have rebelled.
30I tried punishing you,
but you refused
to come back to me,
and like fierce lions
you killed my prophets.
31Now listen to what I say!
Did I abandon you in the desert
or surround you with darkness?
You are my people,
yet you have told me,
“We'll do what we want,
and we refuse
to worship you!”
32A bride could not forget
to wear her jewelry
to her wedding,
but you have forgotten me
day after day.
33You are so clever
at finding lovers
that you could give lessons
to a prostitute.
34You killed innocent people
for no reason at all.
And even though their blood
can be seen on your clothes,
35you claim to be innocent,
and you want me to stop
being angry with you.
So I'll take you to court,
and we'll see who is right.
36When Assyria let you down,
you quickly ran to Egypt,
but you'll find no help there,
37and you will leave
in great sadness.
I won't let you find help
from those you trust.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah neen Israel yaab pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke m di tibɔr tee 2moon tuk Jerusalem yaab mɔmɔk.
“M teer saah nan laa par ki kpa gaakii pu na,
ki teer saah nan laa mɔn tichar ki gee mi pu na;
aa nan dii mi nteersakpiin ni,
kitiŋ ki ponn ni ubaa aa kee bun tijikaar na.
3Israel yaab, ni ye min baanja yaab la;
ni nan ye maawangokpaan la.
M nan cha unii umɔk tii nimi titotonn na
kan falaa ni iween.
Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Israel yaab aayaajatiib aatunwanbir
4Nimi Jakob aayaabitiib, Israel aanibol, pel Uwumbɔr aabɔr man.
5Uwumbɔr bui ke:
“Ngalm mulamu aan niyaajatiib nan di galn mi?
Ba nan cha bi fenn bipuwɔb tii mi?
Bi nan dooni ŋiwaa ŋi kaa bi tibaa ni na
le ki mu kpaln maabitibaanidam bibaa.
6Bitafal aa nan bi m ni,
hali maah nan nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni,
ki di bi bɔ dii kipɔɔk ni,
kitiŋ ki ye nteersakpiin, ni litambol,
ki kuur ki kpa tiwanbir aan ubaa aa koo nima na;
aan ubaa mu aa chuun nima chee na,
bitafal aa nan bi m ni.
7M nan joo ni bi kitiŋ ki nyuun na pu,
ke bi nan ji kaajikaar ni kaawamɔɔn mɔmɔk.
Le bi labr ki ŋa maatiŋ tijɔŋ;
bi bii kitiŋ ki m nan di tii bi na.
8Bitotoorb aa nan ŋmaa baa ke, ‘Uwumbɔr bi la chee?’
Min mbaa aatotoorb aa nan nyi mi.
Bitinjoob nan yii mi ki nyan mpuwɔb;
le maabɔnabtiib nan joo uwaaja Baal aayimbil le nabr tibɔr
ki dooni ŋiwaa ŋi kaa bi tibaa ni na.
Uwumbɔr aah kpa tibɔr ti waanib pu na
9“Le min Uwumbɔr ga ki len maanib aah ŋani pu na.
M ga tii biyaabitiib ngalm.
10Buen liwilir wɔb, Saiprus aadikl pu man,
ki tun ubaa buen liwipuul wɔb, Kedar aatiŋ ni.
Ni ga kan ke kina aawan aaboln aa kee ŋa.
11Litimbol libaa aa kee kpeln laawaa ŋi kaa ye nibaa na,
le maanib ma di min Uwumbɔr u tii bi liyimbil na
kpeln ŋiwaa ŋi kaan ŋmaa ŋa nibaa tii bi na.
12Kina pu le m bui kitaapaak ke ki dam aan ni li kpa ijawaan,
ki li kpa iwaan ni lijinjiir,
13maanib aah tun titunwanbir tilee ti na pu.
Bi fenn bipuwɔb tii mi,
ni bi ke bi yii uyayak aanyunbun mu aanyun ŋan na,
le ki gbii bibaa aabun
ŋi kpa iween, kaan ŋmaa joo nnyun na.
Israel yaab aah kaa kpa gaakii pu na
14“Israel yaab aa ye binaagbiib;
baa nan ma bi lii tinaagbiir ni.
Tɔ, ni ŋa kinye aan baadim tee mban ki ban bi?
15Bi ŋuuni bi pu ke ichinn na la;
bi cha baatiŋ kpaln nteersakpiin,
le baatim kpaln tilangbenn,
ubaa aa ki bi mu ponn ni.
16Mbamɔn, bijab bi nyan ni Ijipt aatim Memfis ni Tapanes na
gbaa wiil biyil a.
17Israel yaab, nimi le joo ni nimina niyil pu.
Ni yii min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr,
buyoonn m nan cheeni nimi cha na.
18Ni dak ke ni yaa gir buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni
ki ti nyun Nail aamɔɔl ponn ni aanyun kan,
ni ga kan ba aanyoor?
Ni dak ke ni yaa buen Asiria
ki ti nyun Yufrates aamɔɔl aanyun kan,
ni ga kan ba aanyoor?
19Nimi nibaa aatunwanbir le ga daa nitafal,
le naah fenn nipuwɔb tii mi pu na ga bii nimi.
Ni ga bee ke ni yaa yii min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr,
kaa ki tii mi naadii kan, naa ŋan, ki mu ga li wu.
Min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.”
Israel yaab aah yii kaa dooni Uwumbɔr pu na
20Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le len ke,
“Israel yaab, naah yii maamɔb na, ni yunn pam;
ni yii, kaa kii maamɔb, kaa dooni mi.
Ni dooni ŋiwaa ŋi ni bui ke ŋi kpa timar na
ŋigongon ŋi paa na pu,
ni bususoom mɔmɔk taab.
21M nan bun nimi ke lisubinyaan
li aasub ga li ŋan na la.
Tɔ, lik naah tun pu na.
Ni naahn ŋisubil aasub bu bur na la.
22Hali ni yaa di bukiib bu ŋun njeen mbamɔm na fu nnyun kan,
m ga li beenin waa nimi aajɔŋ aataani.
23Ni ga ŋa kinye ki bui ke naa bii nibaa,
ki len ke naa kee doon liwaal Baal?
Lik naah nan tun titunwanbir ti kifataŋ ni na;
lik naah tun pu na.
Ni naahn timoor ni aalaakumii u ban u jon
ki san yɔl yɔl,
24ki san kpak nteersakpiin ni na la.
U yaa ban u jon kan, ŋma ga ŋmaa chuu u?
Laakumiija u ban u jon u na aan ŋa falaa ubaa;
n‑yoonn mumɔk u ban u jon na kan, u kani u.
25Israel yaab, naah bi san ban
ŋiwaa pu na le cha nitaa deer,
le nineen ni mu kuur.
Le ni bui ke, ‘Aayii. Taan ki fenn tipuwɔb.
Ti gee ŋiwaa aabɔr pam,
le ki ga li san dii ŋi.’”
Israel yaab ŋeer ntafadaan
26Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Nimi Israel aanib, ni nimi aabɔrb, ni bininkpiib, ni nimi aatotoorb, ni bibɔnabtiib mɔmɔk ga ji inimɔɔn ke baah chuu unaayuk kan, u ji inimɔɔn pu na la. 27Sin u bui ke aate ye busub, le litakpal mu ye aana na ga ji inimɔɔn. Naah fenn nipuwɔb tii mi, kaa fenn ki dii mi pu na, le ga cha kina ŋa. Le ni yaa tee bi tibɔr ni kan, ni bui ke m dan nan gaa nimi lii.
28“Naah naan ŋiwaa ŋi tii nibaa na bi la chee? Ŋi yaa ga ŋman kan, ni cha ŋi nyan nimi tibɔr ni buyoonn ni bi ti ni na. Juda aanib, naah kpa ntim sakpen pu na, kina le ni kpa ŋiwaa mu. 29Nimi aabɔr ti muk nimi na ye kinye? Ba ŋa ni nyan mpuwɔb? 30M daa nitafal, le naa ŋa nimi nibaa; naan kii ke m sur nimi. Ni ku maabɔnabtiib ke uchinn u aaŋuul fii na la. 31Israel aanib, li pel maah len pu na man. M bi ke nteersakpiin mu bɔɔn ki kpa tiwanbir na le ni chee ee? Tɔ, ni ŋa kinye aan ni bui ke ni ga ŋa naah gee pu na, ke naan ki gir ni m chee kpala? 32Upiisapɔɔn ga ŋmaa suln waaleenyaan pu uu? Ubɔndinn mu ga ŋmaa suln waakekenyaan pu uu? Le maanib ma aah suln m pu pu na, saan ŋmaa kahn iwiin ngbaan. 33Ni sil nyi naah ga ban bɔtiib pu na. Hali bipiib bi joo bibaa kooh na ga ŋmaa bae ni chee. 34Bigiim ni maa‑kpa‑taani‑dam aasin le bi nimi aawanpeenkaan pu, naa ye binaayukb aasin.
“Le nimina mɔmɔk aapuwɔb na, 35ni bui ke, ‘Taa tun taani ubaa. Mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aan ki fii ti pu.’ Le min Uwumbɔr ga daa nitafal, naah bui ke naa tun taani ubaa pu na. 36Ni di nibaa ŋa dafir aanib, naah chuun dii ŋitimbol ŋiken aawaa pu na pu. Ijipt yaab ga jinn nimi inimɔɔn ke Asiria yaab aah nan ŋa nimi pu na. 37Ni ga di inimɔɔn le fenn nipuwɔb tii Ijipt yaab. Min Uwumbɔr le yii naah tii binib bi naadii na; naan kan tinyoor tibaa bi chee.”

english_text:
Sin and Shame
1The Lord said to the people of Israel:
If a divorced woman marries,
can her first husband
ever marry her again?
No, because this
would pollute the land.
But you have more gods
than a prostitute has lovers.
Why should I take you back?
2Just try to find one hilltop
where you haven't gone
to worship other gods
by having sex.
You sat beside the road
like a robber in ambush,
except you offered yourself
to every passerby.
Your sins of unfaithfulness
have polluted the land.
3So I, the Lord, refused
to let the spring rains fall.
But just like a prostitute,
you still have no shame
for what you have done.
4You call me your father
or your long-lost friend;
5you beg me to stop being angry,
but you won't stop sinning.
The Lord Asks Israel To Come Back to Him
6 When Josiah was king, the Lord said:
Jeremiah, the kingdom of Israel was like an unfaithful wife who became a prostitute on the hilltops and in the shade of large trees. 7-8I knew that the kingdom of Israel had been unfaithful and committed many sins, yet I still hoped she might come back to me. But she didn't, so I divorced her and sent her away.
Her sister, the kingdom of Judah, saw what happened, but she wasn't worried in the least, and I watched her become unfaithful like her sister. 9The kingdom of Judah wasn't sorry for being a prostitute, and she didn't care that she had made both herself and the land unclean by worshiping idols of stone and wood. 10And worst of all, the people of Judah pretended to come back to me. 11Even the people of Israel were honest enough not to pretend.
12Jeremiah, shout toward the north:
Israel, I am your Lord—
come back to me!
You were unfaithful
and made me furious,
but I am merciful,
and so I will forgive you.
13Just admit that you rebelled
and worshiped foreign gods
under large trees everywhere.
14You are unfaithful children,
but you belong to me.
Come home!
I'll take one or two of you
from each town and clan
and bring you to Zion.
15Then I'll appoint wise rulers
who will obey me,
and they will care for you
like shepherds.
16You will increase in numbers,
and there will be no need
to remember the sacred chest
or to make a new one.
17The whole city of Jerusalem
will be my throne.
All nations will come here
to worship me,
and they will no longer follow
their stubborn, evil hearts.
18Then, in countries to the north,
you people of Judah and Israel
will be reunited,
and you will return to the land
I gave your ancestors.
19I have always wanted
to treat you as my children
and give you the best land,
the most beautiful on earth.
I wanted you to call me “Father”
and not turn from me.
20But instead, you are like a wife
who broke her wedding vows.
You have been unfaithful to me.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People Confess Their Sins
The Lord said:
21Listen to the noise
on the hilltops!
It's the people of Israel,
weeping and begging me
to answer their prayers.
They forgot about me
and chose the wrong path.
22I will tell them, “Come back,
and I will cure you
of your unfaithfulness.”
They will answer,
“We will come back, because you
are the Lord our God.
23On hilltops, we worshiped idols
and made loud noises,
but it was all for nothing—
only you can save us.
24Since the days of our ancestors
when our nation was young,
that shameful god Baal has taken
our crops and livestock,
our sons and daughters.
25We have rebelled against you
just like our ancestors,
and we are ashamed of our sins.”
translation_text:
Israel yaab aah yii Uwumbɔr pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan bui ke, “Uja yaa yii upuu, le u yaa fii ki ti mɔn uja uken kan, waan ti ki ŋmaa gaa ni u. Nimina ga bii kitiŋ kee kookoo la. Tɔ, Israel yaab, ni kan bɔtiib pam, le ki tee ki ban ke ni gir ni m chee. 2Lik ŋigongon paab man. Nibaa chee aa gur aan naa tun lituln ke udagoor na. Ni nan sii nsan chee ki kii nibɔtiib, ke nteersakpiin ponn ni aanib aah sii pu ki kii ubaa ke bi ku u na la. Ni di nimi aadagook bii kitiŋ kee. 3Nima pu le utaal aa nan ki nu, le utakuutaal mu aa nan ki nu. Ni sil naahn bidagoob la; naa san inimɔɔn.
4“Le ni bui mi dandana wee ke, ‘Aa ye tite la, le taah nan ye mbim pu na, aa nan gee timi, ki beenin gee timi. 5Saaŋuul aan li feei n‑yoonn mɔmɔk; saan gee ti pu liŋuul ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.’ Israel yaab, ni len kina, le ki tee tun titunwanbir timɔk ni ga ŋman na.”
Ni ŋan ke Israel yaab ni Juda yaab yii baatunwanbir
6Josia aah nan ye ubɔr buyoonn na, le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Aa kan Israel yaab bi bi ke bipiidagoob na aah tun pu na aa? Bi fenn bipuwɔb tii mi, le ki tun lituln ke bidagoob na ligongoln limɔk paa na pu, ni bususoom mɔk taab. 7M nan dak ke bi yaa ŋa nimina mɔmɔk kan, bi ga ki gir ni m chee. Le bi yii, kaa gir ni, le bina aabitiib Juda yaab bi kaa kpa gaakii na kan ni mɔmɔk. 8Juda aanibol mu nan kan ke m yii Israel aanibol, ki jenn u lii; ba pu? u nan fenn upuwɔb tii mi ki kpaln udagoor. Le Juda, u ye Israel aana aabo u nyan mpuwɔb na aa nan san ijawaan. U mu nan kpaln udagoor, 9kaa nan san inimɔɔn kpala. U nan bii kitiŋ ngbaan, le ki dooni ŋitakpal ni isui. 10Nee mɔmɔk aapuwɔb na, Israel aana aabo Juda, u nyan mpuwɔb na ŋmann ke u gir ni m chee la; waa nan si chob. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
11Le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke u nyi ke Israel yaab fenn bipuwɔb tii u, bi mu tee soor Juda yaab bi nya upuwɔb na. 12U nan bui mi ke m buen ki ti bui Israel yaab ke, “Israel yaab bi nyan mpuwɔb na, gir ni m chee man. M ye unimbaasaln la, le maaŋuul aan fii; maaŋuul aan fii ni pu ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. 13Kii ke ni tun taani, ke ni nyan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aapuwɔb. Kpiir ke ni di nimi aageehn tii ŋiwaa, bususoom mɔmɔk taab, kaa kii maamɔb. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.
14“Nimi bi nyan mpuwɔb na, gir ni man; ni ye maanib la. M ga nyan ni ponn ni ubaabaa kitiŋ mɔmɔk ni, ki nyan bilelee ntaŋaal mɔmɔk ni, ki di nimi giin ni Sionn Aajool paab. 15M ga ban bijojoob bi kii maamɔb na le tii nimi, le bi ga di nlan ni ŋuntii joo nimi. 16Le ni yaa nan wiir kitiŋ ngbaan pu kan, binib aan ki len Maakaal Aadakaa bɔr. Baan ki len waabɔr, kaan ki teer u bɔr; baan ki li ban u, kaan ki ŋa uken teen waabuul ni. 17N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, bi ga li gur yin Jerusalem ke ‘Uwumbɔr Aabɔrjal’ la, le ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ga kuun nima ki doon mi. Baan ki ŋa bisui i bir ki kpa maaŋuntafal na aah mɔk bi ke bi ŋa pu na. 18Israel yaab ga buen ti kpee Juda yaab pu, le bi mɔmɔk ga nya tinaagbiir ni, ŋŋangan wɔb aatiŋ na ponn ni, ki gir ni kitiŋ ki m nan di tii niyaajatiib ke ki li ye biyaan na pu.”
Uwumbɔr aanib aah dooni ŋiwaa pu na
19Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Israel yaab, m nan ban ke m gaa nimi ke njapɔɔn na la,
ki tii nimi mpopiin aatiŋ,
dulnyaa wee ni aatiŋ ki ŋan ntim mɔmɔk ni na.
M nan ban ke ni li yin mi ke nite la,
ki taa ki fenn nipuwɔb tii mi daalbaadaal.
20Le ni bi ke upii u nyan uchal aapuwɔb na,
le ni mu nyan mpuwɔb kina.
Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
21Israel yaab aah suln Bidindaan Uwumbɔr pu
ki tun titunwanbir aatuln na,
le kifuuk faa ŋijoo paab,
ki ye Israel yaab aah wii ki gaŋni pu na aafuuk la.
22Nimi bi mɔmɔk fenn nipuwɔb tii Uwumbɔr na, gir ni man;
u ga tii nimi laafee, ki cha ni ki sil upuwɔb.
Ni bui ke, “Mbamɔn, ti ban ti gir ni Uwumbɔr chee la, ba pu? uma le ye timi Aawumbɔr. 23Taah dooni ŋiwaa ŋigongon paab pu na aa kpa timi nterm mubaa. Timi Israel yaab aaterm nyani Tidindaan Uwumbɔr baanja chee la. 24Le inimɔɔn aawaal Baal na aadoon pu cha ti lann ipiih, ni inaa, ni japɔtiib, ni bisatiib, ni tiwan nimɔk tiyaajatiib nan tun ki kan n‑yaajayoonn na. 25Ti ga doon kitiŋ le ki cha timi aanimɔɔn biin ti pu. Timi ni tiyaajatiib tun Tidindaan Uwumbɔr titunwanbir le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk; taa kii waamɔb daalbaadaal.”

english_text:
How Israel Can Return to the Lord
1The Lord said:
Israel, if you really want
to come back to me, get rid
of those disgusting idols.
2Make promises only in my name,
and do what you promise!
Then all nations will praise me,
and I will bless them.
3 People of Jerusalem and Judah,
don't be so stubborn!
Your hearts have become hard,
like unplowed ground
where thornbushes grow.
4With all your hearts,
keep the agreement
I made with you.
But if you are stubborn
and keep on sinning,
my anger will burn like a fire
that cannot be put out.
Disaster Is Coming
The Lord said:
* 5“Sound the trumpets, my people.
Warn the people of Judah,
‘Run for your lives!
6Head for Jerusalem
or another walled town!’
“Jeremiah, tell them I'm sending
disaster from the north.
7An army will come out,
like a lion from its den.
It will destroy nations
and leave your towns empty
and in ruins.”
8Then I told the people
of Israel,
“Put on sackcloth!
Mourn and cry out,
‘The Lord is still angry
with us.’ ”
9The Lord said,
“When all this happens,
the king and his officials,
the prophets and the priests
will be shocked and terrified.”
10I said, “You are the Lord God. So why have you fooled everyone, especially the people of Jerusalem? Why did you promise peace, when a knife is at our throats?”
The Coming Disaster
11-12When disaster comes, the Lord will tell you people of Jerusalem,
“I am sending a windstorm
from the desert—
not a welcome breeze.
And it will sweep you away
as punishment for your sins.
13Look! The enemy army
swoops down like an eagle;
their cavalry and chariots
race faster than storm clouds
blown by the wind.”
Then you will answer,
“We are doomed!”
14But Jerusalem, there is still time
for you to be saved.
Wash the evil from your hearts
and stop making sinful plans,
15before a message of disaster
arrives from the hills of Ephraim
and the town of Dan.
16-17The Lord said,
“Tell the nations that my people
have rebelled against me.
And so an army will come
from far away
to surround Jerusalem
and the towns of Judah.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
18“People of Judah,
your hearts will be in pain,
but it's your own fault
that you will be punished.”
Jeremiah's Vision of the Coming Punishment
19I can't stand the pain!
My heart pounds,
as I twist and turn in agony.
I hear the signal trumpet
and the battle cry of the enemy,
and I cannot be silent.
20I see the enemy defeating us
time after time,
leaving everything in ruins.
Even my own home
is destroyed in a moment.
21How long will I see enemy flags
and hear their trumpets?
22I heard the Lord say,
“My people ignore me.
They are foolish children
who do not understand
that they will be punished.
All they know is how to sin.”
23After this, I looked around.
The earth was barren,
with no form of life.
The sun, moon, and stars
had disappeared.
24The mountains were shaking;
25no people could be seen,
and all the birds
had flown away.
26Farmland had become a desert,
and towns were in ruins.
The Lord's fierce anger
had done all of this.
The Death of Jerusalem
27-28The Lord said:
I have made my decision,
and I won't change my mind.
This land will be destroyed,
although not completely.
The sky will turn dark,
and the earth will mourn.
29Enemy cavalry and archers
shout their battle cry.
People run for their lives
and try to find safety
among trees and rocks.
Every town is empty.
30Jerusalem, your land
has been wiped out.
But you act like a prostitute
and try to win back your lovers,
who now hate you.
You can put on a red dress,
gold jewelry, and eye shadow,
but it's no use—
your lovers are out to kill you!
31I heard groaning and crying.
Was it a woman giving birth
to her first child?
No, it was Jerusalem,
gasping for breath
and begging for help.
“I'm dying!” she said.
“They have murdered me.”
translation_text:
Titunwanbir aayiim aayim
1Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel yaab, ni yaa ban ni fenn kan, ni fenn dan m chee. Ni yaa di cha nsan mu kpa tijɔŋ na ki kii maamɔb kan, 2ni ga ŋmaa puu tipuur maayimbil pu. Le ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ga bui mi ke m ŋa maanyoor ŋa bi pu, ki ga pak mi.”
3Uwumbɔr bui Juda ni Jerusalem aanib ke, “Kpar nimi aasikpil ŋi kaa kpar na; taa di nimi aajikaabim bu ŋmal ikokon ponn ni man. 4Li joo man tipuur ti ni nan puu tii mi Uwumbɔr na. Nimi Juda ni Jerusalem aanib, di nibaa tii mi man. Ni yaa kaa ye kina kan, maaŋuul ga fii ke mmii na, titunwanbir ti ni tun na pu. Li ga fii, le ubaa aan li bi ki sɔŋ li.”
Baah ga loon Juda pu na aafaan
5Pii ikpiin kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu man.
Teen mpɔɔn pu aan unii mɔmɔk ŋun.
Tuk Juda ni Jerusalem aanib libiil li choo Juda pu na
ke bi san buen ntim mu bi maa ŋigon gob mu na ni.
6Mɔk Sionn aatiŋ aasan man.
Li san ban nimi aamɔfal man. Taa taan man.
Uwumbɔr nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb ki joo libiil choo.
7Uchinn aah nyani waabɔbɔryaan ni pu na,
kina le unii u bii ŋitimbol na nyan ni.
U choo u nan bii Juda aatiŋ la.
Juda aatim ga kpaln tilangbenn la,
le ubaa aan ŋmaa koo mu ni.
8Kina pu na, di tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na peen,
ki li wii ki kaani,
Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln aah
kaan fenn cha Juda pu na pu.
9Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, bibɔrb ni baaninkpiib aawon ga yɔl, lijinjiir ga chuu bitotoorb, le maabɔnabtiib ga li gur waa bimɔi.”
10Le m bui ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, aa ŋmann Jerusalem aanib kookoo a. Aa bui bi ke nsuudoon ga li bi, le kijaak aajuk ka bineen ni.”
11N‑yoonn choo, le bi ga nan bui Jerusalem aanib ke libuln li ton sakpen na nyan nteersakpiin ni ki choo bi chee. Laan li ye libuln li bi suuna ki daar tigbengbir cha na. 12Libuln li Uwumbɔr ga cha li dan na ga li pɔɔ jer lima ngbaan. Uwumbɔr ubaa le bi dar waanib aatafal.
Bidim aah ga mann goln Juda pu na
13Lik man, udin le choo ke ntaalangbam na. Waajaak aataan, ni yaatɔroku mam bi ke kinaakpaajabuŋ na la, le waataan ŋmaa san mala mala jer ŋikaagii. Ti kuln a. Timi aamɔfal junn a.
14Jerusalem aanib, finn nyan tibir ti bi nisui ni na, aan ki ŋmar. Ni ga li dak tilandakwanbir ki ti saa bayoonn?
15Ituun nyan Dann yaab, ni Efraim yaab aagongon ni, le ki nan moon tibɔbir ngbaan. 16Bi dan bi nan sak ŋitimbol ki bui Jerusalem ke bidim nyani dandar ki choo. Bidim ngbaan ga gbaa ikaa Juda aatim pu, 17ki ga lul goln Jerusalem ke bijab bi si kii nkpaakon na; ba pu? kaanib nyan Uwumbɔr aapuwɔb. Uwumbɔr le len kina.
18Juda yaab, naah bi mbimbin mu na, ni ŋitun ŋi ni tun na le cha ni joo ni nima nibaa pu. Nimi aatunwanbir le joo ni falaa umina; ti saa chaar nipobil a.
Jeremia aasui aah bii waanib pu pu na
19Iween sakpen yee.
Maan ŋmaa joo iween ngbaan. Mpobil yuk a.
Mpobil gbaa mpɔɔn pu la.
Maan ŋmaa ŋmin suuna,
m ŋun ikpiin aawiil ni butɔb aakuun pu.
20Libiil libaa dii liken la;
kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ber doo a.
Libuul ni le bi bii timi aadir doo;
le ki gbaa wiil ti mɔmɔk.
21M ga li ŋun butɔb aafuuk pu ki ti saa bayoonn,
ki li ŋun ikpiin aawiil pu kina ki cha?
22Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Maanib ye bijɔrb la,
baa nyi mi.
Bi naahn mbim mu kaa kpa nlan na la;
baa kpa ntafaŋum.
Bi nyi titunwanbir aatuln sakpen,
le kaa tee nyi tiwan ni ŋan na aaŋam.”
Uwumbɔr aah kpiir libiil li choo na mɔk Jeremia pu na
23M nan lik kitiŋ,
le ki kan ke ki nan ye kitikuun ŋmeen la.
M nan waan lik paacham, le kaa waa nwiihn.
24M nan lik ŋijoo, le ŋi mɔmɔk nan jii,
le ŋigongon yuk ti nya do ki ti nya do.
25M nan kan ke unii aa ki bi nibaa chee;
hali inyoon nan fii buen a.
26Kitiŋ ki nan nyuun ki kpa tijikaar na
nan kpaln nteersakpiin la;
kaatim nan ber doo, Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln pu.
27Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan bui ke kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk ga kpaln nteersakpiin la,
u mu aan tee bii ki doo.
28Kitiŋ ga wii ikpowiil,
le kitaapaak bɔnn timm.
Uwumbɔr le len, kaan kpeln waalandak.
U siin waah ga ŋa pu na,
kaan ki fenn upuwɔb.
29Binib mɔmɔk yaa nan ŋun bitandam ni bipindam pu kan, bi ga san.
Bibaa ga san buen kichook ni,
biken mu ga jon ŋijootakpal ni.
Ntim mɔmɔk ponn ni ga li ye nkuun la,
le ubaa aan ki koo mu ni.
30Jerusalem aanib, ni kuln a.
Ba ŋa ni pee ŋikekenyaan?
Ba ŋa ni gbin nleenyaan
ki di nkpanyaan boon ninimbil wɔb?
Ni toor nibaa fam la.
Nibɔtiib yii nimi le ki ban bi ku nimi.
31M ŋun iwiil pu
ke upii u ban u maa na aah wii pu na,
iwiil i bi ke upii u ban u maa waajan aabo na aawiil.
Jerusalem aanib aawiil le bi na,
bi pɔɔni bibaa ke bi fuur la,
ki taln biŋaal ki wii ke,
“Timi aamɔfal junn a.
Bi choo bi nan ku timi la.”

english_text:
Is Anyone Honest and Faithful?
The Lord said to me:
1“Search Jerusalem
for honest people
who try to be faithful.
If you can find even one,
I'll forgive the whole city.
2Everyone breaks promises
made in my name.”
3I answered, “I know
that you look for truth.
You punished your people
for their lies,
but in spite of the pain,
they became more stubborn
and refused to turn back
to you.”
4Then I thought to myself,
“These common people
act like fools,
and they have never learned
what the Lord their God
demands of them.
5So I'll go and talk to the leaders.
They know what God demands.”
But even they had decided
not to obey the Lord.
6The people have rebelled
and rejected the Lord
too many times.
So enemies will attack
like lions from the forest
or wolves from the desert.
Those enemies will watch
the towns of Judah,
and like leopards
they will tear to pieces
whoever goes outside.
Enemies Will Punish Judah
The Lord said:
7People of Judah,
how can I forgive you?
I gave you everything,
but you abandoned me
and worshiped idols.
You men go to prostitutes
and are unfaithful
to your wives.
8You are no better than animals,
and you always want sex
with someone else's wife.
9Why shouldn't I punish
the people of Judah?
10I will tell their enemies,
“Go through my vineyard.
Don't destroy the vines,
but cut off the branches,
because they are the people
who don't belong to me.”
11In every way, Judah and Israel
have been unfaithful to me.
* 12Their prophets lie and say,
“The Lord won't punish us.
We will have peace
and plenty of food.”
13They tell these lies in my name,
so now they will be killed in war
or starve to death.
14I am the Lord God All-Powerful.
Jeremiah, I will tell you
exactly what to say.
Your words will be a fire;
Israel and Judah
will be the fuel.
15People of Israel,
I have made my decision.
An army from a distant country
will attack you.
I've chosen an ancient nation,
and you won't understand
their language.
16All of them are warriors,
and their arrows bring death.
17This nation will eat your crops
and livestock;
they will leave no fruit
on your vines or fig trees.
And although you feel safe
behind thick walls,
your towns will be destroyed
and your children killed.
Israel Refused To Worship the Lord
18The Lord said:
Jeremiah, the enemy army won't kill everyone in Judah. 19And the people who survive will ask, “Why did the Lord our God do such terrible things to us?” Then tell them:
I am the Lord,
but you abandoned me
and worshiped other gods
in your own land.
Now you will be slaves
in a foreign country.
20Tell these things to each other,
you people of Judah,
you descendants of Jacob.
21 You fools! Why don't you listen
when I speak?
Why can't you understand
22 that you should worship me
with fear and trembling?
I'm the one who made the shore
to hold back the ocean.
Waves may crash on the beach,
but they can come no farther.
23You stubborn people have rebelled
and turned your backs on me.
24You refuse to say,
“Let's worship the Lord!
He's the one who sends rain
in spring and autumn
and gives us a good harvest.”
25That's why I cannot bless you!
* 26A hunter traps birds
and puts them in a cage,
but some of you trap humans
and make them your slaves.
27You are evil, and you lie and cheat
to make yourselves rich.
You are powerful
28and prosperous,
but you refuse to help the poor
get the justice they deserve.
29You need to be punished,
and so I will take revenge.
30Look at the terrible things
going on in this country.
I am shocked!
31Prophets give their messages
in the name of a false god,
my priests don't want
to serve me,
and you—my own people—
like it this way!
But on the day of disaster,
where will you turn for help?
translation_text:
Jerusalem aanib aatunwanbir
1Jerusalem aanib, san dii nimi aatiŋ ponn ni man.
Lik lik man. Cha nimi nibaa aanimbil kan.
Lik lik kinyaŋ ponn ni man.
Ni ŋmaa kan unii ubaa aan u tun ni ŋan na
ki pɔɔni ubaa ke u kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb aa?
Ni yaa ga kan kina aanii kan,
Uwumbɔr ga di cha Jerusalem yaab aatunwanbir pinn bi.
2Ni bui ke ni dooni Uwumbɔr la,
le nisui aa joo kina.
3Mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr sil lik ban mbimbinyaan la.
U nan faa nimi, le naa sɔŋ nisui;
u nan taa taa ni pu,
le ni yii kaa bae.
Ni nan kpa tafalaaŋun, kaa di cha titunwanbir aatuln.
4Le m nan dak ke, “Binib bee ye bigiim ni maanyidam la.
Bi tun kijɔrk aatuln la;
baa nyi Baawumbɔr aah gee pu na,
baa nyi Uwumbɔr aah ban bi tun pu na.
5M ga buen binib bi bi mpɔɔn ni na chee
le ti ti gbaa tibɔr.
Nibaakan, bima ga li nyi Baawumbɔr aah gee pu na,
bima ga li nyi Uwumbɔr aah ban ke bi ŋa pu na.”
Le bi mu mɔmɔk yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki nyan upuwɔb.
6Nima pu le ichinn ga nya ni kichook ni ki nan ku bi;
le takɔ mam ga nya ni nteersakpiin ni ki nan daa par par bi,
le inaamuun ga li chuun tee mban baatim ponn ni.
Binib ngbaan yaa nyan lipaal kan, i ga daa par par bi;
ba pu? baatunwanbir wiir sakpen a,
le bi fenn bipuwɔb tii Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.
7Le Uwumbɔr baa ke,
“Ni ga ŋa kinye aan m di maanib aatunwanbir cha pinn bi?
Bi yii mi ki siir cha mi, le ki dooni ŋiwaa.
M kpiin maanib le bi jin ti bab,
le ki tee fii ti tun kidagook aatuln
le ki chuun dii bipiib bi joo bibaa kooh na.
8Bi nan bi ke itanja i bi kpiin i
mbamɔm aan i ban i jon na la,
bi mɔmɔk san ban tɔb aapuutiib la.
9M taa daa bitafal nimina pu
ki teen kina aatimbol aa?
10M ga tun ni bidim le bi nan pir maanib aasubil aasui lir,
ki taa tee kuln i kookoo.
M ga bui bi ke bi pir isubon lir,
ba pu? isubon ngbaan aa ye min yee.
11Israel ni Juda aanib nyan mpuwɔb la.
Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Uwumbɔr aah yii Israel yaab pu na
12Uwumbɔr aanib yii u ki bui ke, “Mbamɔn, waan sil ŋa nibaa. Tibɔbir aan dan ti pu; butɔb ni nkon aan lir ti pu.” 13-14Bi nan bui ke Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr na aa ye nibaa, bi po ye tiloor ti gbii libuln ŋmeen na, le kaa kpa Uwumbɔr aabɔr tibaa bi tuk bi. Le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui mi ke, “Jeremia, binib bee aah len pu na pu, le m ga cha maabɔr li bi aamɔb ni ke mmii na. Le binib ngbaan ga li bi ke idɔ na, mmii ngbaan ga wu bi.”
15Israel aanib, Uwumbɔr ban ke dandar aatimbol le dan nan tak nimi. Li ye n‑yaayoonn na aatimbol le ki pɔɔ, le naa nyi laaliin. 16Laajab bi too itɔi na pɔɔ sakpen, le ki ku binib, kaa san kinimbaak. 17Bi ga di nimi aajikaar ni njikaabim nab; bi ga ku nijapɔtiib ni nibisatiib. Bi ga nan kɔr nimi aawakor mɔmɔk, ki kuln nimi aasubil aasui mu. Baajab ga nan ber naah maa ŋigon kiir ntim mu ki mak mu pu na mɔmɔk.
18Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Hali n‑yoonn ngbaan kan, maan kuln maanib kookoo. 19Bi yaa baa ke ba ŋa m tun kina mɔmɔk kan, sin Jeremia, bui bi ke baah fenn bipuwɔb tii mi ki dooni ŋiwaa bibaa aatiŋ pu na, kina le bi ga ti tun lituln tii biwɔwɔm kitiŋ ki kaa ye bibaa aatiŋ na pu.”
Uwumbɔr aah sak waanib pu na
20Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Bui Jakob aayaabitiib, Juda aanib ke: 21Li pel man, nimi bijɔrb ni bilatiirb bi kpa ŋinimbil kaa waa na, ki kpa ŋitafal kaa ŋun na. 22Min le ye Uwumbɔr; ba ŋa naa san mi? Ba ŋa naa jii nnimbiin ni? M di litambol le bil kiir nnyusakpem, ke mu aanaanmɔk le na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Nnyusakpem aanyun ga fii too paacham, mu mu aan ŋmaa jer mu aanaanmɔk, le tinyunkpenn ga ŋmaa fii ti lir ni kifuuk, ti mu aan ŋmaa jer buen nibaa. 23Le nimi ma kan, ni kpa tafalaaŋun kaa si mpuwɔb, ni paar le ki siir cha mi. 24Naa ŋa nlandak daalbaadaal ke ni nyuŋ mi, hali maah tii nimi useetaal ni utakuutaal mɔmɔk pu, ki tii nimi lijikaacheel aayoonn pu libiln mɔmɔk na, naa nyuŋni mi. 25Le nimi aatunwanbir cha nimina mɔmɔk nyan niŋaal ni.
26“Titunwanbirdam koo maanib chee, ki doo kiir ke bijab bi di gaawɔb mam pen tinann na, le bima pen gaawɔb mam bi chur binib na. 27Ukpan aah chur inyoon gbiini waalook ni pu na, kina le bi di tiwan ni bi chur binib ki gaal mpɔɔn na gbiin baadichal ni. Nima pu le bi kpa mpɔɔn ni liwangol kina, 28le ki ji babr ki filk. Baatunwanbir aa kpa taadoon. Baa joo nkpobim ni bigiim aabamɔn tii bi.
29“Le min Uwumbɔr ga daa bitafal tiwan nee mɔmɔk pu; m ga teen litimbol ngbaan. 30Ijawaan ni lijinjiir aawan ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan pu; 31maabɔnabtiib geei inyamɔn ŋmeen la; le bitotoorb di bibaa aapɔɔn le joo binib, le maanib gee kina la. Tɔ, nimina mɔmɔk ti doo kan, bi ga ŋa kinye?”

english_text:
A Warning for the People of Jerusalem
The Lord said:
1Run for your lives,
people of Benjamin.
Get out of Jerusalem.
Sound a trumpet in Tekoa
and light a signal fire
in Beth-Haccherem.
Soon you will be struck
by disaster from the north.
2Jerusalem is a lovely pasture,
3but shepherds will surround it
and divided up,
then let their flocks
eat all the grass.
4Kings will tell their troops,
“If we reach Jerusalem
in the morning,
we'll attack at noon.
But if we arrive later,
5we'll attack after dark
and destroy its fortresses.”
6I am the Lord All-Powerful,
and I will command these armies
to chop down trees
and build a ramp up to the walls
of Jerusalem.
People of Jerusalem,
I must punish you
for your injustice.
7Evil pours from your city
like water from a spring.
Sounds of injustice and violence
echo within your walls;
victims are everywhere,
wounded and dying.
8Listen to me,
you people of Jerusalem
and Judah.
I will abandon you,
and your land will become
an empty desert.
9I will tell your enemies
to leave your nation bare
like a vine stripped of grapes.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
Jeremiah's Anger
10I have told the people
that you, Lord,
will punish them,
but they just laugh
and refuse to listen.
11Your anger against Judah
flames up inside me,
and I can't hold it in
much longer.
The Lord's Anger Will Sweep Everyone Away
The Lord answered:
Don't hold back my anger!
Let it sweep away everyone—
the children at play
and all adults,
young and old alike.
12 I'll punish the people of Judah
and give to others
their houses and fields,
as well as their wives.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
13Everyone is greedy and dishonest,
whether poor or rich.
Even the prophets and priests
cannot be trusted.
14 All they ever offer
to my deeply wounded people
are empty hopes for peace.
15They should be ashamed
of their disgusting sins,
but they don't even blush.
And so, when I punish Judah,
they will end up on the ground,
dead like everyone else.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People of Judah Rejected God's Way of Life
16The Lord said:
My people, when you stood
at the crossroads,
I told you, “Follow the road
your ancestors took,
and you will find peace.”
But you refused.
17I also sent prophets
to warn you of danger,
but when they sounded the alarm,
you paid no attention.
18So I tell all nations on earth,
“Watch what I will do!
19My people ignored me
and rejected my laws.
They planned to do evil,
and now the evil they planned
will happen to them.”
20People of Judah,
you bring me incense from Sheba
and spices from distant lands.
You offer sacrifices of all kinds.
But why bother?
I hate these gifts of yours!
21So I will put stumbling blocks
in your path,
and everyone will die,
including parents and children,
neighbors and friends.
An Army from the North
22The Lord said,
“Look toward the north,
where a powerful nation
has prepared for war.
23Its well-armed troops are cruel
and never show mercy.
Their galloping horses sound
like ocean waves
pounding on the shore.
This army will attack you,
lovely Jerusalem.”
24Then the people said,
“Just hearing about them
makes us tremble with fear,
and we twist and turn in pain
like a woman giving birth.”
25The Lord said,
“Don't work in your fields
or walk along the roads.
It's too dangerous.
The enemy is well armed
26and attacks without warning.
So mourn, my people, as though
your only child had died.
Wear clothes made of sackcloth
and roll in the ash pile.”
The Lord's People Must Be Tested
The Lord said:
27Jeremiah, test my people
as though they were metal.
28And you'll find they are hard
like bronze and iron.
They are stubborn rebels,
always spreading lies.
* 29-30Silver can be purified
in a fiery furnace,
but my people are too wicked
to be made pure,
and so I have rejected them.
translation_text:
Bidim aah gob Jerusalem pu na
1Benjaminn aanib, li san ban ŋŋmarm man. San nya Jerusalem ni man. Pii ukpiin Tekoa aatiŋ ni, ki tuur limɔkl aamii Bef Hakerem aatiŋ ni man. Tibɔbir ni libiil ban ni nya ni ŋŋangan wɔb ki dan la. 2Jerusalem aatiŋ ŋan, le ki mu bii a; 3bibɔrb ni baajab ga kuun kal nima la. Bi ga ŋa baagban aaboo ki maln kitiŋ ngbaan, le bi mɔmɔk ga kuun kal baah gee nin chee na. 4Bi ga bui ke, “Gor ki ti tak Jerusalem man. Gor man. Nwiin aakaasisik ni le ti ga ti tak ki;” le ki ga tee bui ke, “Ti taan sakpen a, nwiin ban mu lir la, le ijooboon moo fɔk cha. 5Ti ga nan tak ki kinyeek la; ti ga ber kaadir ti pɔɔ ki fɔk na.”
6Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le cha bibɔrb ngbaan pir isui ki maa ŋibimbin ke bi gob Jerusalem. U bui ke, “Kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni aah gbii limukl sakpen pu na, le m ga daa kitafal. 7Liboln ni aah kpa nnyunpɔm pu na, kina le Jerusalem ni kpa titunwanbir pɔnn. M ŋun kijaak ni libiil pu kitiŋ ngbaan ni; m kani iween ni ibuun ŋmeen la. 8Jerusalem aanib, cha tibɔbir timina li ye nsurm ki tii nimi, naa ye kina kan, m ga di nimi lii, m ga cha nimi aatiŋ kpaln nteersakpiin, nin chee ubaa aa koo na.”
Israel yaab aah yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb pu na
9Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan nan bui mi ke, “Bi ga pir Israel yaab pel pel ke ŋisubil aasui i bi ker ŋisubil doo i pu na la. N‑yoonn laa bi, kina pu na, gaa saah ga ŋmaa gaa bi lii na.”
10Le m gar ke, “Ŋma ga pel m chee buyoonn m bi len bi chee tibɔr ki sur bi na? Bi kpa tafalaaŋun, kaan pel saabɔr ti m joo nabr bi na; bi laa saabɔr la. 11Uwumbɔr, saaŋuul aah fii bi pu pu na wu nsui ni ke mmii na, le maa ki ŋmaa joo li.”
Uwumbɔr ki bui mi ke, “Cha maaŋuul pii mbim mu bi kitiŋ ponn ni na, ni binachipɔm aakuun mɔmɔk ni. Baadim ga di chatiib ni puutiib buen, kaan di cha bininkpiib ni binib bi por pam na mu. 12Bi ga di baadichal, ni baakpaakon, ni bipuutiib tii binib bibaa la. M ban m daa kitiŋ kee pu aanib aatafal la. 13Binib bi pɔɔ na, ni bi kaa pɔɔ na mɔmɔk pɔɔni bibaa ke bi di beebee le kan ŋimombil, hali maabɔnabtiib ni bitotoorb ji binib ngbaan la. 14Bi ŋani ke maanib aabuun aah kaa ye nibaa le na. Bi len le ke, ‘Ni mɔmɔk ŋan,’ le naa ŋan kpala. 15Baa nan san inimɔɔn, baajɔŋ aatun ŋee pu. Aayii, baa nan san inimɔɔn kpala; baa kpaan nyi baah ga mɔk pu ke inimɔɔn joo bi na. Kina pu le bi mu ga lir ke biken aah lir pu na; m yaa nan daa bitafal kan, baadoon le ga li bi na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Israel yaab aah yii Uwumbɔr aasan pu na
16Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke, “Sil isayakr ki li lik man. Baa ki bee man n‑yaayoonn na aasanbim ni nsanyaan na aah nan bi nin chee na. Li chuun mu pu man, ki kan lifuur.”
Le bi bui ke, “Ayii, taan ŋa kina.” 17Le Uwumbɔr ban bikikiib ke bi li pel n‑yoonn mu ukpiin ga nan wii na. Le bi mu bui ke, “Taan pel.”
18Le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Nimi ŋitimbol, li pel man, ki bae tiwan ni ban ni ŋa maanib na chee. 19Kitiŋ, li pel. Maanib aabeebee aatuln pu le m ban m joo ni libiil nan lii bi pu, ba pu? bi yii maamɔkm kaa tii maabɔr naadii. 20Ntafal aa bi tulalee aayon mu nyan ni Seba, aan bi joo nan tii mi na, kaa bi tulalee mam bi nyan ni dandar na ni. Maan gaa baapiin, ni kitork ki bi joo tii ni mi na. 21M ga cha binib bee gbeer ki lir. Tetiib ni baabim ga kpo, le jɔtiib ni maantɔtiib mu ga kpo.”
Ŋŋangan wɔb aajab aah nan lir Israel yaab pu pu na
22Uwumbɔr len ke, “Bijab nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb aatiŋ ni ki choo; litimbol ngbaan pɔɔ sakpen le ki gor kii butɔb. 23Bi yoor baatɔi ni kijaak aajum; bi kpa mbiin kaa san kinimbaak. Baataan aafuuk bi ke nnyusakpem aafuuk na la. Bi gor ke bi to Jerusalem butɔb.”
24Le Jerusalem aanib bui ke, “Ti ŋun tibɔr ngbaan, le tiwon yɔl ti lir kitiŋ, ijawaan ni iween chuu timi ke upii u ban u maa na aamalween aah wu pu na la. 25Taa ki kaa ke ti buen itingbaan ni, bee isan pu ki ti tun lituln; ba pu? timi aadim joo tijawan, le ijawaan bi ni kookoo.”
26Le Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke, “Di tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na peen, ki di nfatan pɔŋ nibaa. Li wii ikpowiil ke lijapɔnbaal aah kpo kan, bi wii pu na; ba pu? unii u choo u nan bii doo nimi na ga fuu ni n‑yoonn mu naa dak u pu na la. 27Jeremia, tɔŋ maanib ke baah pu tikur mmii ni pu na ki lik ke bi bi kinye. 28Bi mɔmɔk ye maaŋuntafaldam bi kaa si unii aachaŋ ni na la, bitafal pɔɔ ke tikumann ni tikur na la. Bi mɔmɔk ji binib la, le ki chuun joo biken aabɔr mooni. 29Nchaamii gaal sakpen, le tikur ti kaa ŋan na aa ŋmaa donni ki puu buen. Unii yaa ki bi toor maanib kan, ni ye fam la; ba pu? titunwanbirdam na aa nyan bi ni. 30Min, Uwumbɔr aah yii maanib na, le bi ga li gur yin bi ke tigbengbir ti kaa kpa tinyoor na.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple
(Jeremiah 26.1-6)
1-3The Lord told me to stand by the gate of the temple and tell the people who were going in that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
