Teer maah nan dan aa chee ki nan gaŋ si bi pu ke aa taa daa bitafal saaŋuul ponn ni pu na. 21Tɔ, Uwumbɔr, cha nkon ku baabim; cha bi kpoi butɔb ni. Cha baapiib lann bichatiib ni baabim; cha iween ku bijab, aan baanachipɔm mu kpoi butɔb ni. 22Cha kinipaak nan loon bi ki gaa baawangol; cha ijawaan chuu bi aan bi wii mpɔɔn pu. Bi gbii libuul bil mi ke m nan lir li ponn ni, ki pen mi gaawɔb mam. 23Tɔ, Uwumbɔr, aa nyi baah kpokl pu ke bi ku mi na. Taa di baatunwanbir cha pinn bi, ki taa di cha baataani. Buyoonn saaŋuul fii na kan, mee bi lii ki nyaŋ bi.”

english_text:
Jeremiah and the Clay Jar
1The Lord said:
Jeremiah, go to the pottery shop and buy a clay jar. Then take along some of the city officials and leading priests 2 and go to Hinnom Valley, just outside Potsherd Gate. Tell the people that I have said:
3I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and you kings of Judah and you people of Jerusalem had better pay attention. I am going to bring so much trouble on this valley that everyone who hears about it will be shocked. 4-5 The people of Judah stopped worshiping me and made this valley into a place of worship for Baal and other gods that have never helped them or their ancestors or their kings. And they have committed murder here, burning their young, innocent children as sacrifices to Baal. I have never even thought of telling you to do that. 6So watch out! Someday this place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley!
7You people of Judah and Jerusalem may have big plans, but here in this valley I'll ruin those plans. I'll let your enemies kill you, and I'll tell the birds and wild animals to eat your dead bodies. 8I will turn Jerusalem into a pile of rubble, and every passerby will be shocked and horrified and will make insulting remarks. 9And while your enemies are trying to break through your city walls to kill you, the food supply will run out. You will become so hungry that you will eat the flesh of your friends and even of your own children.
10Jeremiah, as soon as you have said this, smash the jar while the people are watching. 11Then tell them that I have also said:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warn you that I will shatter Judah and Jerusalem just like this jar that is broken beyond repair. You will bury your dead here in Topheth, but so many of you will die that there won't be enough room.
12-13I will make Jerusalem as unclean as Topheth, by filling the city with your dead bodies. I will do this because you and your kings have gone up to the roofs of your houses and burned incense to the stars in the sky, as though they were gods. And you have given sacrifices of wine to foreign gods.
Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple Courtyard
14I went to Topheth, where I told the people what the Lord had said. Then I went to the temple courtyard and shouted to the people, 15“Listen, everyone! Some time ago, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, warned you that he would bring disaster on Jerusalem and all nearby villages. But you were stubborn and refused to listen. Now the Lord is going to bring the disaster he promised.”
translation_text:
Libuul li wii na aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke m buen ti daa tiyakr aabuul. U nan ki bui mi ke m cha binib ngbaan aayidam bibaa, ni bitotoorb bi por na bibaa li dii mi, 2aan m di bi dii mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Kisanjaŋ Aabisamɔb na, ki di buen Hinom Aafataŋ ni. Nima chee le m ga ti di waah ga di waabɔr ti tuk mi na nabr bi. 3Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke m len ke, “Juda aabɔrb, ni Jerusalem aanib, li pel man, min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na aah kpa pu m len na. M ban m joo ni tibɔbir nan lii libuul lee pu, le unii umɔk ŋun ti pu na aapobil ga yuk. 4Binib ngbaan aah fenn bipuwɔb tii mi ki bii do, ki toor kitork tii ŋiwaa ŋi bima bibaa, ni biyaajatiib, ni Juda aabɔrb aa nan nyi ŋibɔr kpala na pu, le ga cha m ŋa kina. Binib bi kaa kpa taani ubaa na aasin le bi di bii do, 5le ki maa liwaal Baal aabimbin ke bi li joo baabim toor kitork ki seer mmii ni ŋipaab tii li. Maa nan bui bi daalbaadaal ke bi ŋa kina; kina aa nan kpaan koo n‑yil ponn ni. 6Kina pu na, n‑yoonn ga fuu ni le baan ki yin do ke Tofef, bee Hinom Aafataŋ. Bi ga li gur yin do ke Linikul Aafataŋ ni la. 7Do le m ga bii Juda ni Jerusalem aanib aalandak mɔmɔk. M ga cha baadim nyaŋ bi, ki ku bi butɔb ni. Le m ga di ŋinikpol ngbaan tii inyoon, ni ipeel, i di ŋa tijikaar. 8Maah ga joo ni tibɔbir ti nan lii do na ga ŋa unii umɔk jer do na lijinjiir ni iwaan. 9Bidim ga gob kitiŋ ngbaan ki ban ke bi ku kaanib. Baah ga gob ki pu na ga li bir sakpen, le binib bi bi ki ponn ni na ga ŋmɔ tɔb ki kpaan ŋmɔ bibaa aabim.”
10Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke m di libuul na yu wii bijab bi dii mi buen na aanimbil ni, 11ki bui bi ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke, “M ga wii kitiŋ kee, ni binib bee, aan ni li bi ke tiyakr aabuul lee aah wii pu kaan ki kpaan pu na. Binib aah kaan ki kan mpaan pu ki sub baanib na, bi ga sub binib Tofef Aafataŋ kee ni. 12M puu ke m ga ŋa kitiŋ kee, ni kaanib ke Tofef do na. 13Jerusalem aadichal, ni Juda aabɔrb aadichal, ni ŋidichal ŋi mɔmɔk pu bi nan seer tulalee aayon tii iŋmabi, ni nin chee bi nan joo ndaan kpir tii ŋiwaa na mɔmɔk pu, ga li kpa tijɔŋ ke Tofef na la.”
14Le m nan siir Tofef, nin chee Uwumbɔr nan tun mi ke m ti moon waabɔr na. M nan buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal aachiln ni le ki ti bui binib ngbaan ke 15Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na le len ke, “M ga cha ntafadaan dan kitiŋ kee, ni ntim mu bi gbɔk ki na pu, ke maah len ke m ga ŋa pu na, ba pu? bi kpa tafalaaŋun, kaa pel maah tuk bi pu na.”

english_text:
Pashhur Arrests Jeremiah
1Pashhur son of Immer was a priest and the chief of temple security. He heard what I had said, 2and so he hit me. Then he had me arrested and put in chains at the Benjamin Gate in the Lord's temple. 3The next day, when Pashhur let me go free, I told him that the Lord had said:
No longer will I call you Pashhur. Instead, I will call you Afraid-of-Everything. 4You will be afraid, and you will bring fear to your friends as well. You will see enemies kill them in battle. Then I will let the king of Babylonia take everyone in Judah prisoner, killing some and dragging the rest away to Babylonia. 5He will clean out the royal treasury and take everything else of value from Jerusalem.
6Pashhur, you are guilty of telling lies and claiming they were messages from me. That's why I will let the Babylonians take you, your family, and your friends as prisoners to Babylonia, where you will all die and be buried.
Jeremiah Complains to the Lord
7You tricked me, Lord,
and I was really fooled.
You are stronger than I am,
and you have defeated me.
People never stop sneering
and insulting me.
8You have let me announce
only injustice and death.
Your message has brought me
nothing but insults
and trouble.
9Sometimes I tell myself
not to think about you, Lord,
or even mention your name.
But your message burns
in my heart and bones,
and I cannot keep silent.
10I heard the crowds whisper,
“Everyone is afraid.
Now's our chance
to accuse Jeremiah!”
All of my so-called friends
are just waiting
for me to make a mistake.
They say, “Maybe Jeremiah
can be tricked.
Then we can overpower him
and get even at last.”
11But you, Lord,
are a mighty soldier,
standing at my side.
Those troublemakers
will fall down and fail—
terribly embarrassed,
forever ashamed.
12 Lord All-Powerful,
you test those who do right,
and you know every heart
and mind.
I have told you my complaints,
so let me watch you
take revenge on my enemies.
13I sing praises to you, Lord.
You rescue the oppressed
from the wicked.
14 Put a curse on the day I was born!
Don't bless that day.
15Put a curse on the man
who told my father, “Good news!
You have a son.”
16May that man be like the towns
you destroyed without pity.
Let him hear shouts of alarm
in the morning
and battle cries at noon.
17He deserves to die
for not killing me
before I was born.
Then my mother's body
would have been my grave.
18Why did I have to be born?
Was it just to suffer
and die in shame?
translation_text:
Jeremia ni utotoor Pasur aajaak
1Imer aajapɔɔn Pasur, u nan ye bitotoorb bi bi Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aayidaan na aah ŋun maah bi mooni tibɔr ngbaan na, 2le u bui ke bi gbaa mi, ki di tikululn baa mi kaan mbisamɔb mu bi Uwumbɔr Aadichal chee, aan bi yin mu ke Benjaminn Aabisamɔb na. 3Kitaak aah woln aan Pasur cha bi chuu baar mi lii na, le m bui u ke, “Uwumbɔr le aa nan yin si ke Pasur. Waah nan tii si liyimbil li na le ye ke ‘Ijawaan bi ni kookoo.’ 4Uwumbɔr ubaa le len ke, ‘M ban m cha aa li ye ijawaan aawan ki tii sin aabaa ni aajɔtiib la, le baadim ga di kijaak aajum ku bi aanimbil ni. M ga di Juda aanib mɔmɔk di ŋa Babiloŋ aabɔr aapɔɔn ni; u ga chur bibaa tinaagbiir buen waatiŋ pu, le ki ku biken mu. 5M ga ki cha baadim nan gaa kitiŋ kee aawangol mɔmɔk mpɔɔn, ki gaa kaawan mɔmɔk, ni ikpaakon, hali ki gaa Juda aabɔrb aawangol, ki di ni mɔmɔk buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni. 6Sin Pasur ma, ni saadichal kan, bi ga chur ni mu tinaagbiir buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni. Nima chee le aa ga ti kpo le bi sub sin ni aajɔtiib bi mɔmɔk aa nan geei inyamɔn pam tuk bi na.’”
Jeremia aah di waabɔr tuk Uwumbɔr pu na
7Uwumbɔr, aa ŋmann mi la, ki nan sil ŋmann mi.
Aa pɔɔ ki jer mi, le ki nyaŋ mi.
Unii mɔmɔk laa mi la, bi ŋani mi yaansara le nwiin ti lir.
8M yaa ban m len tibɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan,
m tar ke, “Kijaak, libiil.”
Uwumbɔr, maah joo saabɔr mooni na pu,
le bi lik mi fam, ki ŋani mi mbɔnyun.
9Le m yaa tee bui ke, “M ga suln Uwumbɔr bɔr,
kaan ki len tibɔr waayimbil pu” kan,
le saabɔr bi ke mmii na ki wu nsui ni.
M pɔɔni mbaa ke m taa len ti,
le kaa ti ki ŋmaa joo ti.
10M ŋun binib mɔmɔk looni len ke,
“Ijawaan aabɔr bi ni mɔmɔk la.
Cha ti di waabɔr buen bininkpiib chee man.”
Hali njɔtiibamɔm ka kiir maalirm la.
Bi len le ke, “Nibaakan ti ga ŋmaa ŋmann u,
le ki chuu u ki teen u.”
11Uwumbɔr, le si ma si mpuwɔb, ki kpa mpɔɔn ni linyaŋ,
le binib bi muk mi na ga lir.
Baah kaan kan baah ban pu na,
le ga cha bi kpaln binimɔɔnib
ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
12Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, le aa ma joo ibamɔn tɔŋni binib,
aa nyi tiwan ni bi bisui, ni baalandak ni na.
Kina pu na, cha m kan saah ga teen maadim pu na,
ba pu? m di maabɔr ŋa sin le aaŋaal ni.
13Gaa ilahn tii Uwumbɔr man. Pak Uwumbɔr man.
U gaal bigiim titunwanbirdam chee lir.
14Puun lii nwiin mundaal bi nan ma mi na pu.
Suln nwiin mundaal nna nan ma mi na bɔr.
15Puun lii uja u nan ti bui nte ke,
“Ni ye ubijabo la, aa kan ubijabo,”
ki cha usui piir na pu.
16Cha u li bi ke ntim mu Uwumbɔr kuln mu,
kaa san mu kinimbaak na.
Cha u li ŋun iween aawiil pu kichakpiik ni
ki ŋun butɔb aakuun pu nwiin aakaasisik ni,
17waah kaa nan ku mi nna aaponn ni pu na pu.
Tɔ, nna aaponn ni le ba ga li ye maakaakul.
18Bi nan ma mi ke m nan ŋa ba?
Bi nan ma mi ke m nan li bi
tibɔr, ni kinimbaak ŋmeen ni,
le ki ti kpo nnimɔɔnkun aa?

english_text:
The Lord Will Fight against Jerusalem
1King Zedekiah of Judah sent for Pashhur son of Malchiah and for a priest named Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. Then he told them, “Talk with Jeremiah for me.”
So they came to me and said, 2 “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”
3-7I told them that the Lord God of Israel had told me to say to King Zedekiah:
The Babylonians have surrounded Jerusalem and want to kill you and your people. You are asking me to save you, but you have made me furious. So I will stretch out my mighty arm and fight against you myself. Your army is using spears and swords to fight the Babylonians, but I will make your own weapons turn and attack you. I will send a horrible disease to kill many of the people and animals in Jerusalem, and there will be nothing left to eat. Finally, I will let King Nebuchadnezzar and his army fight their way to the center of Jerusalem and capture everyone who is left alive, including you and your officials. But Nebuchadnezzar won't be kind or show any mercy—he will have you killed! I, the Lord, have spoken.
8 Then I told them that the Lord had said:
People of Jerusalem, I, the Lord, give you the choice of life or death. 9The Babylonian army has surrounded Jerusalem, so if you want to live, you must go out and surrender to them. But if you want to die because of hunger, disease, or war, then stay here in the city. 10I have decided not to rescue Jerusalem. Instead, I am going to let the king of Babylonia burn it to the ground. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Warns the King of Judah
* 11Pay attention, you that belong
to the royal family.
12Each new day, make sure
that justice is done,
and rescue those
who are being robbed.
Or else my anger will flame up
like a fire that never goes out.
13Jerusalem,
from your mountaintop
you look out over the valleys
and think you are safe.
But I, the Lord, am angry,
14and I will punish you
as you deserve.
I'll set your palace on fire,
and everything around you
will go up in smoke.
translation_text:
Jeremia aah len Jerusalem aalirm aabɔr pu na
1Juda aabɔr Sedekia nan tun ni Malkia aajapɔɔn Pasur, ni Maaseya aajapɔɔn Sefania, u ye utotoor na m chee ke, 2“Ti gaŋ si ke aa len Uwumbɔr chee tibɔr tii timi, Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar ni waajab aah bi gob timi aatiŋ pu na pu. So they came to me and said, 2 “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”
3-7I told them that the Lord God of Israel had told me to say to King Zedekiah:
The Babylonians have surrounded Jerusalem and want to kill you and your people. You are asking me to save you, but you have made me furious. So I will stretch out my mighty arm and fight against you myself. Your army is using spears and swords to fight the Babylonians, but I will make your own weapons turn and attack you. I will send a horrible disease to kill many of the people and animals in Jerusalem, and there will be nothing left to eat. Finally, I will let King Nebuchadnezzar and his army fight their way to the center of Jerusalem and capture everyone who is left alive, including you and your officials. But Nebuchadnezzar won't be kind or show any mercy—he will have you killed! I, the Lord, have spoken.
8 Then I told them that the Lord had said:
People of Jerusalem, I, the Lord, give you the choice of life or death. 9The Babylonian army has surrounded Jerusalem, so if you want to live, you must go out and surrender to them. But if you want to die because of hunger, disease, or war, then stay here in the city. 10I have decided not to rescue Jerusalem. Instead, I am going to let the king of Babylonia burn it to the ground. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Warns the King of Judah
* 11Pay attention, you that belong
to the royal family.
12Each new day, make sure
that justice is done,
and rescue those
who are being robbed.
Or else my anger will flame up
like a fire that never goes out.
13Jerusalem,
from your mountaintop
you look out over the valleys
and think you are safe.
But I, the Lord, am angry,
14and I will punish you
as you deserve.
I'll set your palace on fire,
and everything around you
will go up in smoke.
translation_text:
Jeremia aah len Jerusalem aalirm aabɔr pu na
1Juda aabɔr Sedekia nan tun ni Malkia aajapɔɔn Pasur, ni Maaseya aajapɔɔn Sefania, u ye utotoor na m chee ke, 2“Ti gaŋ si ke aa len Uwumbɔr chee tibɔr tii timi, Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar ni waajab aah bi gob timi aatiŋ pu na pu. Nibaakan, Uwumbɔr ga tun waajinjiir aatuln libaa tii timi, ki cha Nebukadnesar gir upuwɔb.”
3Le Uwumbɔr len m chee tibɔr, le m tuk baah tun ni bijab bi m chee na 4ke bi ti bui Sedekia ke Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Sedekia, m ban m nyaŋ saajab bi bi jaa Babiloŋ aabɔr ni waajab kijaak na la. M ga kuun saajab aajawan bil kitiŋ aakaasisik ni. 5M ga di maapɔɔn mɔmɔk, ni maaŋuusakpeln na mɔmɔk jan si kijaak. 6M ga ku unii umɔk bi kitiŋ kee ponn ni na; m ga di iween i bir na le ku binib ni tiwakor mɔmɔk. 7Sin ma kan, aa ni saaninkpiib, ni binib bi ŋmar butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween ngbaan ni na, m ga cha Ubɔr Nebukadnesar, ni nimi aadim bi ban bi ku nimi na chur nimi. Nebukadnesar ga ti ku nimi. Waan di cha ni ponn ni ubaa, kaan san ubaa kinimbaak. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
8Le Uwumbɔr ki bui mi ke m tuk binib ngbaan ke, “Li pel man, min Uwumbɔr ban ke ni lee isan ilee yee ponn ni mubaa la; nsan mu cha limɔfal ni na, ni nsan mu cha nkun ni na. 9Unii umɔk gaar kitiŋ ngbaan ni na ga kpo butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween ni. Le uma nyan ki ti di ubaa tii Babiloŋ aanib bi bi tak kitiŋ ngbaan na kan, waan kpo, u ga ŋmar. 10M siin ke maan cha kitiŋ kee ŋmar, m siin ke m kuln ki la. M ga di ki tii Babiloŋ yaab aabɔr le u see ki mmii. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Juda aanaanjirb aah ga kan ntafadaan mu na
11-12Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke m di tibɔr timina tuk Juda aanaanjirb, bi ye Ubɔr David aayaabitiib na ke: “Li pel man, min Uwumbɔr aah kpa pu m len na. Cha ni li ye nimi aatuln ke ibamɔn li bi idaa mɔmɔk. Sil man unii u uken bi ji u na aapuwɔb. Ni yaa kaa ŋa kina kan, titunwanbir ti ni tun na ga cha maaŋuul fii ki wu ke mmii mu baan ŋmaa junn mu na. 13Nimi Jerusalem yaab ka ŋibɔrjal paab, le tifatann bi ni taab, le ni bi ke litakpal li ŋub kitiŋ ki dɔ taar na aah bi pu na. Le m ga jan nimi kijaak. Ni bui ke ubaa aan ŋmaa tak nimi, kaan ŋmaa bɔ nimi aajab ni ki jer. 14M ga daa nitafal naah tun pu na pu. M ga see nimi aabɔrchiln mmii, le mmii ngbaan ga wu tiwan ni mɔmɔk duun li na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish the King of Judah
1-3The Lord sent me to the palace of the king of Judah to speak to the king, his officials, and everyone else who was there. The Lord told me to say:
I am the Lord, so pay attention! You have been allowing people to cheat, rob, and take advantage of widows, orphans, and foreigners who live here. Innocent people have become victims of injustice, and some of them have even been killed. But now I command you to do what is right and see that justice is done. Rescue everyone who has suffered from injustice.
4If you obey me, the kings from David's family will continue to rule Judah from this palace. They and their officials will ride in and out on their horses or in their chariots. 5 But if you ignore me, I promise in my own name that this palace will lie in ruins. 6Listen to what I think about it:
The palace of Judah's king
is as glorious as Gilead
or Lebanon's highest peaks.
But it will be as empty
as a ghost-town
when I'm through with it.
7I'll send troops to tear it apart,
and its beautiful cedar beams
will be used for firewood.
8People from different nations will pass by and ask, “Why did the Lord do this to such a great city as Jerusalem?” 9Others will answer, “It's because the people worshiped foreign gods and broke the agreement that the Lord their God had made with them.”
King Jehoahaz
The Lord said:
10King Josiah is dead,
so don't mourn for him.
Instead, mourn for his son
King Jehoahaz,
dragged off to another country,
never to return.
11-12 Jehoahaz became king of Judah after his father King Josiah died. But Jehoahaz was taken as a prisoner to a foreign country. Now I, the Lord, promise that he will die there without ever seeing his own land again.
King Jehoiakim
The Lord told me to say:
* 13King Jehoiakim, you are doomed!
You built a palace
with large rooms upstairs.
14You put in big windows
and used cedar paneling
and red paint.
But you were unfair
and forced the builders to work
without pay.
* 15More cedar in your palace
doesn't make you a better king
than your father Josiah.
He always did right—
he gave justice to the poor
and was honest.
16That's what it means
to truly know me.
So he lived a comfortable life
and always had enough
to eat and drink.
17But all you think about
is how to cheat
or abuse or murder
some innocent victim.
18 Jehoiakim, no one will mourn
at your funeral.
They won't turn to each other
and ask,
“Why did our great king
have to die?”
19You will be given a burial
fit for a donkey;
your body will be dragged
outside the city gates
and tossed in the dirt.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
King Jehoiachin and the People of Jerusalem
The Lord told me to say:
20People of Jerusalem,
the nations you trusted
have been crushed.
Go to Lebanon and weep;
cry in the land of Bashan
and in Moab.
21When times were good,
I warned you.
But you ignored me,
just as you have done
since Israel was young.
22Now you will be disgraced
because of your sins.
Your leaders will be swept away
by the wind,
and the nations you trusted
will be captured and dragged
to a foreign country.
23Those who live in the palace
paneled with cedar
will groan with pain
like women giving birth.
24 King Jehoiachin, son of Jehoiakim, even if you were the ring I wear as the sign of my royal power, I would still pull you from my finger. 25I would hand you over to the enemy you fear, to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army, who want to kill you. 26You and your mother were born in Judah, but I will throw both of you into a foreign country, where you will die, 27longing to return home.
28Jehoiachin, you are unwanted
like a broken clay pot.
So you and your children
will be thrown into a country
you know nothing about.
29Land of Judah, I am the Lord.
Now listen to what I say!
30Erase the names
of Jehoiachin's children
from the royal records.
He is a complete failure,
and so none of them
will ever be king.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeremia aah nan di tibɔr ti tuk Juda aanaanjirb na
1-2Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke m buen Juda aabɔr, u ye Ubɔr David aayaabil na aabɔrdichal ni, ki ti tuk ubɔr ngbaan, ni waaninkpiib, ni Jerusalem aanib ke bi li pel Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ke, 3“Min Uwumbɔr bui ke ni li ŋani tiwan ni ŋan ki ye ibamɔn na. Ni sil unii u uken bi ji u na aapuwɔb. Taa ŋa biwɔwɔm, ni nkpobim, ni bikpopiib mbiin; ki taa ku binib bi kaa tun taani ubaa na do chee na. 4Ni yaa sil ŋani maah tuk nimi pu na kan, Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ga li beenin ji nnaan. Le bima, ni baaninkpiib, ni baanib ga li diir ibisamɔi yee, ki bi itaan aatɔroku mam ni, ki dik itaan pu, ki nya libɔrdichal lee ni. 5Tɔ, ni yaa kaa ŋani maah tuk nimi pu na kan, m puu tii nimi ke libɔrdichal limina ga ber doo ki kpaln lilangbeln. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.
6“M chee kan, Juda aanaan aadichal ŋan ke Gilead aatiŋ, ni Lebanonn aajoo na la; le m ga ŋa li nin chee ubaa aan ŋmaa koo na. 7M ban m tun ni bijab aan bi nan kuln li. Bi mɔmɔk ga joo ni baachɔm, ki nan gaa geei laagonyaan ŋi bi di santina aadɔ ŋa ŋi na lii, ki di i mee ŋa mmii ni.
8“Nee aapuwɔb le biwɔwɔm pam ga jer, le ki baa tɔb ke ba ŋa min Uwumbɔr ŋa kitisakpeŋ kee kina. 9Le bi ga gar ke ni bii nimi ni nimi Aawumbɔr aamɔbaan, ki dooni ŋiwaa ki tun tii ŋi na le cha u ŋa kina.”
Jeremia aah nan di Joahas aabɔr ti len na aabɔr
10Juda aanib, taa wii Ubɔr Josia pu man;
taa wii waakpuul man.
Li wii ujapɔɔn Joahas pu;
bi ga nan chuu u di buen,
le waan ki gir ni daalbaadaal,
waan ki kan kitiŋ ki pu bi nan ma u na.
11Uwumbɔr aah len Josia aajapɔɔn Salum u nan ka ute aajal pu ki ye Juda aabɔr na aabɔr ti na sɔ, “U nyan do, kaan ki gir ni daalbaadaal. 12Baah di u buen kitiŋ ki ni na le u ga ti kpo nima, le kaan ki kan kitiŋ kimina daalbaadaal.”
Jeremia aah nan di Jehoyakim aabɔr ti len na sɔ
13Uja u di beebee maa waadichal,
ki moo maa kpae li pu inyamɔn pu
aan waanib tun lituln fam, kaa gaal tipar na aamɔfal junn a.
14Uja u len ke,
“M ga maa lidichasakpeln ki cha paacham aadir li waa pam,”
le ki ŋa takolu mam waadichal pu,
ki di santina aakpan kpaa bi,
le ki di tiwamann boon bi na aamɔfal junn a.
15Aa yaa di santina maa saadichal
ke li li ŋan jer biken yaan kan,
kina ga ŋmaa ŋa si ubɔrnyaan ki jer biken aa?
Aate nan jin waamɔɔn
u nan bi chob ki kpa ibamɔn,
le ki nan kan tinyoor waatuln mɔmɔk ni.
16U nan jin bigiim aabɔr ibamɔn pu,
le waawan mɔmɔk nan kpa nsan.
Kina le mɔk ke unii sil nyi Uwumbɔr.
17Le aa ma le ban saakumɔŋ aanyoor baanja;
aa ku binib bi kaa kpa taani ubaa na,
le ki joo mbimbinpɔɔl muk saanib.
Uwumbɔr le len kina.
18Le Uwumbɔr nan len Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim, u nan ye Juda aabɔr na aabɔr ke,
“Ubaa aan wii waakpuul, kaan len ke,
‘Ni kpa mpombiin sakpen, njɔ, ni kpa mpombiin sakpen a.’
Ubaa aan wii u pu, kaan moo u pu ke, ‘Maaninkpel, maabɔr.’
19Bi ga di ubon aakpuul aanyuŋ le di fuul u di buen
ki ti di u mee Jerusalem aabisamɔi aapuwɔb.”
Jeremia aah di Jerusalem aalirm aabɔr ti len na sɔ
20Jerusalem aanib, li cha Lebanonn aatiŋ pu, ki ti li tar man;
li cha Basann aatiŋ pu ki li wii man;
li bi Moab aajoo pu ki yin man,
ba pu? bi nyaŋ nimaantɔtiib a.
21Naah nan laa kpa liwangol buyoonn na,
le Uwumbɔr nan len ni chee
le ni yii kaa pel.
Nimi aatuln le bi na, nimi aamɔfal aayoonn mɔmɔk ni;
naa kee kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb.
22Naah tun titunwanbir pu na,
le libuln ga daa nimi aayidam buen,
le bidim ga chur nimaantɔtiib butɔb ni tinaagbiir,
le nimi aatiŋ jin inimɔɔn.
23Ni kaa santina bi bi joo ni bi nyan ni Lebanonn aatiŋ
ni na ponn ni le ki fuur;
tɔ, iween i wu ke upii
aamalween na yaa nan pii nimi kan,
le ni ga ŋa kinimbaak aanib.
Uwumbɔr aah ga daa Jehoyachinn aatafal pu na
24Uwumbɔr nan bui Juda Aabɔr Jehoyakim aajapɔɔn Jehoyachinn ke, “Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu na, hali aa yaa ba ye kibɔmbik ki ŋmaa ŋŋangii aaŋanbik pu na kan, 25m ba ga ŋmaar si tii binib bi ban bi ku si, aan aa san bi ijawaan na. M ga di si tii Ubɔr Nebukadnesar ni waajab la. 26M ga jenn aa ni aana buen tinaagbiir ni. Ni ga buen kitiŋ ki baa nan ma nimi ki ponn ni na la, le ni mɔmɔk ga ti kpo nima. 27Ni ga li neen ke ni ki kan kitiŋ kee, le ki mu aan ki gir ni ki pu.”
28Le m bui ke, “Ubɔr Jehoyachinn kpaln libuul li wii aan bi di li mee ubaa aa ki ban li na la aa? Kina pu le u ni waabim bi tinaagbiir ni, kitiŋ ki baa nyi kaabɔr na ni ii?
29Kitiŋ, kitiŋ, kitiŋ,
li pel Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.
30M siin ke uja wee lann waabim
ki li ye uja u kaan kan tinyoor na.
Waan li kpa yaabitiib bi ga nan li joo Juda aatiŋ
ke Ubɔr David aah nan ye pu na.
Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
A Message of Hope
The Lord said:
1 You leaders of my people are like shepherds that kill and scatter the sheep. 2You were supposed to take care of my people, but instead you chased them away. So now I'll punish you severely and make you pay for your crimes!
3I will bring the rest of my people home from the lands where I have scattered them, and they will grow into a mighty nation. 4I promise to choose leaders who will care for them like real shepherds. All of my people will be there, and they will never again be frightened.
5 Someday I will appoint
an honest king
from the family of David,
a king who will be wise
and rule with justice.
6As long as he is king,
Israel will have peace,
and Judah will be safe.
The name of this king will be
“The Lord Gives Justice.”
7A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living God who rescued Israel from Egypt. 8Instead, you will call me the Living God who rescued you from the land in the north and from all the other countries where I had forced you to go. And you will once again live in your own land.
Jeremiah Thinks about Unfaithful Prophets
9When I think of the prophets,
I am shocked, and I tremble
like someone drunk,
because of the Lord
and his sacred words.
10Those unfaithful prophets
misuse their power
all over the country.
So God turned the pasturelands
into scorching deserts.
The Lord Will Punish Unfaithful Prophets
11The Lord told me to say:
You prophets and priests
think so little of me, the Lord,
that you even sin
in my own temple!
12Now I will punish you
with disaster,
and you will slip and fall
in the darkness.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
13The prophets in Samaria
were repulsive to me,
because they preached
in the name of Baal
and led my people astray.
14 And you prophets in Jerusalem
are even worse.
You're unfaithful in marriage
and never tell the truth.
You even lead others to sin
instead of helping them
turn back to me.
You and the people of Jerusalem
are evil like Sodom
and Gomorrah.
15You prophets in Jerusalem
have spread evil everywhere.
That's why I, the Lord, promise
to give you bitter poison
to eat and drink.
The Lord Gives a Warning
The Lord said:
16Don't listen to the lies
of these false prophets,
you people of Judah!
The message they preach
is something they imagined;
it did not come from me,
the Lord All-Powerful.
17These prophets go to people
who refuse to respect me
and who are stubborn
and do whatever they please.
The prophets tell them,
“The Lord has promised
everything will be fine.”
18But I, the Lord, tell you
that these prophets
have never attended a meeting
of my council in heaven
or heard me speak.
19They are evil! So in my anger
I will strike them
like a violent storm.
20I won't calm down,
until I have finished
what I have decided to do.
Someday you will understand
exactly what I mean.
21I did not send these prophets
or speak to them,
but they ran to find you
and to preach their message.
22If they had been in a meeting
of my council in heaven,
they would have told
you people of Judah
to give up your sins
and come back to me.
23I am everywhere—
both near and far,
24 in heaven and on earth.
There are no secret places
where you can hide from me.
25These unfaithful prophets claim that I have given them a dream or a vision, and then they tell lies in my name. 26But everything they say comes from their own twisted minds. How long can this go on? 27They tell each other their dreams and try to get my people to reject me, just as their ancestors left me and worshiped Baal. 28Their dreams and my truth are as different as straw and wheat. But when prophets speak for me, they must say only what I have told them. 29My words are a powerful fire; they are a hammer that shatters rocks.
30-32These unfaithful prophets claim I give them their dreams, but it isn't true. I didn't choose them to be my prophets, and yet they babble on and on, speaking in my name, while stealing words from each other. And when my people hear these liars, they are led astray instead of being helped. So I warn you that I am now the enemy of these prophets. I, the Lord, have spoken.
News and Nuisance
The Lord said to me:
33Jeremiah, when a prophet or a priest or anyone else comes to you and asks, “Does the Lord have news for us?” tell them, “You people are a nuisance to the Lord, and he will get rid of you.”
34If any of you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” I will punish you and your families, even if you are a prophet or a priest. 35Instead, you must ask your friends and relatives, “What answer did the Lord give?” or “What has the Lord said?” 36It seems that you each have your own news! So if you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” you are twisting my words into a lie. Remember that I am your God, the Lord All-Powerful.
37If you go to a prophet, it's all right to ask, “What answer did the Lord give to my question?” or “What has the Lord said?” 38But if you disobey me and say, “Here is news from the Lord,” 39I will pick you up and throw you far away. And I will abandon this city of Jerusalem that I gave to your ancestors. 40You will never be free from your shame and disgrace.
translation_text:
N‑yoonn mu choo na aamakl
1Uwumbɔr yaa nan jin biyidam bi bii ki yaa waanib na tibɔr kan, naan li ŋan bi pu. 2Uwumbɔr, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na aah len biyidam bi aatuln ba ye bi li joo waanib mbamɔm na aabɔr pu na sɔ: “Naa joo maanib; ni yaa bi, le ki jenn bi buen. Tɔ, m ga daa nitafal naah tun titunwanbir ti na pu. 3M ga kuun ni maanib bi ŋmar na ki nya ni ntim mu m yaa bi aan bi bi mu ponn ni na, le ki giin ni bi bido aatiŋ pu. Bi ga li kpa mbim pam ki pɔr kpee. 4M ga ban biyidam bi ga li joo bi na. Maanib aan ki li san ijawaan, le maan ki daa bitafal. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
5Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “N‑yoonn choo le m ga nyan Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ponn ni ubɔr u aabimbin ŋan na. Ubɔr ngbaan ga di nlan le joo waanib ki li ŋani tiwan ni ŋan ki tok na kitiŋ ngbaan pu. 6U yaa nan ŋa ubɔr kan, Juda aanib ga kan lifuur, le Israel aanib kan nsuudoon. Bi ga li yin u ke ‘Uwumbɔr u gaal timi lir na’ la.”
7Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “N‑yoonn choo le binib aan ki li puur tipuur maayimbil pu ke, ‘Uwumbɔr u bi ki nyan ni Israel aanib Ijipt aatiŋ ni na.’ 8Bi ga li gur puur maayimbil pu ke, ‘Uwumbɔr u bi ki nyan ni Israel aanib ŋŋangan wɔb aatiŋ ni, ni ntim mu ponn ni m cha bi yaa ki bi mu ponn ni na la.’ Le bi ga li koo bima bibaa aatiŋ pu.”
Jeremia aah nan di Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib aabɔr ti len na sɔ
9Nsui mɔmɔk bii a, le m si jii.
Uwumbɔr pu, ni waabɔnyaan pu,
le m gur bi ke udagbiir,
ki bi ke unii u nyun ndaan sakpen na.
10Binib bi kaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na le gbii kitiŋ kee pu;
baabimbin aa ŋan,
le bi joo baapɔɔn tun ŋitun ŋi kaa ŋan na.
Uwumbɔr aah puun lii kitiŋ pu na, le ki wii ikpowiil,
le tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan kuur.
11Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“Maabɔnabtiib ni bitotoorb aa dii min Uwumbɔr;
m kan bi Maadichal ponn ni, bi bi tun titunwanbir.
12Baah dii isan i na ga li ŋar le ki bɔɔn;
m ga cha bi gbeer ki lir.
M ga cha tibɔbir dan bi pu.
Baatafadaan aayoonn choo.
Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.
13M kan bibɔnabr bi bi Samaria aatiŋ ni na aatunwanbir;
bi joo Baal aayimbil le nabr tibɔr, le ki di maanib yenn.
14M ki kan maabɔnabr bi bi
Jerusalem aatiŋ ni na aatunwanbir jer kina;
bi gɔr kidagook le ki geei inyamɔn;
bi ter binib le bi tun titunwanbir,
le ubaa aa ŋmaa di cha titunwanbir aatuln.
Mma chee kan, bi mɔmɔk bi ke
Sodom ni Gomora aanib na la.
15“Kina pu na, min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah len bibɔnabr bi bi Jerusalem ni na aabɔr pu na sɔ:
M ga di tisufar ti to na le tii bi, bi ji,
ki tii bi njinn bi nyu,
ba pu? bi cha titunwanbir gbiin kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk la.”
16Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui Jerusalem aanib ke, “Taa pel man bibɔnabr ngbaan aah len pu na; bi joo inyamɔn aamakl le gbiini nimi. Bi tuk nimi bima bibaa aah kal ki dakl pu na la, naa ye min mbaa aah len pu na. 17Bi tuk binib bi yii kaa pel maah len pu na ke nibaa aan ŋa bi, le ki tuk binib bimɔk kpa tafalaaŋun na ke tibɔbir aan dan bi pu.”
18Le m bui ke, “Bibɔnabr ngbaan ubaa aa nyi Uwumbɔr aalandak i bɔr na. Bi ponn ni ubaa aa bee waabɔr aatataa, kaa pel, kaa ŋun tii waah len pu na daalbaadaal. 19Waaŋuul ye kitaabuŋ la, li ye libupɔɔl li ga daa bibiindam aayil pu, 20kaan ŋmin see waah ban pu na mɔmɔk ti ŋa. N‑yoonn choo le waanib ga nan bee nimina mɔmɔk chain.”
21Le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Maa tun ni bibɔnabr ngbaan, le bi buen. Maa di maabɔr tibaa tuk bi, le bi len tibɔr maayimbil pu. 22Bi yaa nan ba nyi maalandak i bɔr na kan, bi ba ga di maabɔr tuk maanib, le bi ba di cha titunwanbir, ni mbiin aabimbin mu ponn ni bi bi na.
23“M ye Uwumbɔr u bi ni kookoo, kaa bi libuul libaa ni na la. 24Ubaa aan ŋmaa bɔr mi m taa kan u. Naa nyi ke m bi paacham, ni kitiŋ ni, ni ni kookoo la aa? 25M nyi bibɔnabr ngbaan aah len pu ki mɔln inyamɔn maayimbil pu, ke min le di maabɔr tuk bi tidaŋ ponn ni pu na aatataa. 26Bibɔnabr ngbaan ga li joo baah naan inyamɔn i na ŋmanni maanib ki ti saa bayoonn? 27Bi dak ke tidaŋ ti bi joo tuk maanib na ga cha maanib suln mbɔr, ke bitetiib aah nan suln mbɔr ki fenn toŋ liwaal Baal wɔb pu na la. 28Ubɔnabr u daŋ tidaŋ na, u bui ke ni ye tidaŋ la, tɔ, ubɔnabr u m di maabɔr tuk u na, u moon ti mbamɔm. Imuul ni timoor aa kpaa. 29Maabɔr naan mmii la, ki bi ke ligagaar li wiil ŋitakpal yuk yuk na la. 30M ni bibɔnabr bi joo biŋeen aatɔtiib aabɔr mooni ke ti ye maabɔr na ga kan tɔb. 31M ni bibɔnabr bi mu joo bibaa aabɔr mooni ke ti ye maabɔr na ga kan tɔb.” 32Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Li pel man maah len pu na. M ni bibɔnabr bi joo baadaŋ ti gbii inyamɔn na mooni na ga kan tɔb. Bi joo tidaŋ ngbaan le len, ki joo baanyamɔn ni kipupuk ŋmanni maanib. Maa tun bi, kaa bui bi ke bi li cha, le baa kpa nterm mubaa ki tii binib ngbaan. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Uwumbɔr aabɔr
33Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Jeremia, maanib ponn ni ubaa, bee maabɔnabr ubaa, bee utotoor ubaa yaa baa si ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aabɔr ye kinye kan,’ aa bui u ke, ‘Aa ye tibɔr le ki tii Uwumbɔr, le u ban u nyan si u chee.’ 34Maanii ubaa, bee ubɔnabr ubaa, bee utotoor le yaa bui ke ‘Uwumbɔr aabɔr’ kan, m ga daa u ni waadichal aatafal. 35Tɔ, bi mɔmɔk li baa bijɔtiib ni bido yaab ke, ‘Uwumbɔr gar kinye? Uwumbɔr len kinye?’ 36Kina pu na, bi taa ki len ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aabɔr;’ naa ye kina kan, m ga cha maabɔr li ye tibɔr ti bir na le ki tii udaan. Binib ngbaan fenn fenn Baawumbɔr u bi, ki ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na, aamɔboln la. 37Jeremia, baa bibɔnabr ngbaan ke, ‘Uwumbɔr gar nimi kinye? Uwumbɔr len kinye?’ 38Le bi yaa yii maah len pu na aan ki bui ke ‘Uwumbɔr aabɔr’ kan, le aa bui bi ke, 39m ga sil yoor bima ni kitiŋ ki m nan di tii bi ni biyaajatiib na di mee dandar dandar. 40M ga cha inimɔɔn ni kiyimbiyook ki kaa kpa ndoon na dan bi pu.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Has a Vision of Two Baskets of Figs
1 The Lord spoke to me in a vision after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had come to Judah and taken King Jehoiachin, his officials, and all the skilled workers back to Babylonia. In this vision I saw two baskets of figs in front of the Lord's temple. 2One basket was full of very good figs that ripened early, and the other was full of rotten figs that were not fit to eat.
3“Jeremiah,” the Lord asked, “what do you see?”
“Figs,” I said. “Some are very good, but the others are too rotten to eat.”
4Then the Lord told me to say:
5People of Judah, the good figs stand for those of you I sent away as exiles to Babylonia, 6where I am watching over them. Then someday I will bring them back to this land. I will plant them, instead of uprooting them, and I will build them up, rather than tearing them down. 7I will give them a desire to know me and to be my people. They will want me to be their God, and they will turn back to me with all their heart.
8The rotten figs stand for King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and all the others who were not taken away to Babylonia, whether they stayed here in Judah or went to live in Egypt. 9I will punish them with a terrible disaster, and everyone on earth will tremble when they hear about it. I will force the people of Judah to go to foreign countries, where they will be cursed and insulted. 10War and hunger and disease will strike them, until they finally disappear from the land that I gave them and their ancestors.
translation_text:
Tibɔɔkur tilee ti gbii ŋikakan na aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr nan di tibɔɔkur tilee ti gbii ŋikakan na mɔk mi, Waadichal aabisamɔb chee. Ni nan ye n‑yoonn mu Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan chuu Juda Aabɔr Jehoyachinn, u aate nan ye Jehoyakim na, ni Juda aayidam, ni baawanŋab, ni binib bi nyi tiwan sakpen na tinaagbiir nyan Jerusalem aatiŋ ni, ki di buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na aapuwɔb la. 2Njan aabɔɔkuuk na nan gbii ŋikakan ŋi puir mala ki ŋan na la; le kiken na gbii ŋikakan ŋi kaa ŋan, ki bur, baan ŋmaa ŋmɔ ŋi na. 3Le Uwumbɔr baa mi ke, “Jeremia, aa waa ba?”
Le m gar ke, “Ŋikakan. Ŋinyaan na nan ŋan sakpen, le ŋi kaa nan ŋan na, aa nan ŋan kpala unii ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ ŋi.”
4Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, 5“Min, Uwumbɔr, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, di baah nan chur binib bi buen Babiloŋ na ŋaŋ ŋikakan ŋi ŋan na la, m ga ŋa bi tiŋann. 6M ga li bi bi chee ki ki giin ni bi kitiŋ kee pu. M ga maa bi kaan, kaan ber bi; m ga di bi ŋum, kaan ki daa ŋɔb bi. 7M ga tii bi lineen li ga cha bi bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr na. Baah ga gir ni m chee ni bisui mɔmɔk pu na, le ga cha bi li ye maanib, le m mu ga li ye Baawumbɔr.
8“Juda Aabɔr Sedekia ma, ni bininkpiib bi ka gob u na, ni Jerusalem aanib bi gur ki ka kitiŋ kee pu, ni binib bi fii buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni na ma kan, min Uwumbɔr ga ŋa bi mɔmɔk ke ŋikakan ŋi si, kaa ŋan ke bi ŋmɔ ŋi na la. 9Maah ga cha tibɔbir ti aaboln dan bi pu na ga chuu dulnyaa aatimbol mɔmɔk ijawaan. Binib ga ŋa bi yaansara, ki ŋa bi mbɔnyun, ki li laa bi, ki li joo baayimbil puuni lir biken pu baah yaa ki bi ni kookoo na. 10M ga cha butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween dan bi pu ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu bi ponn ni ubaa aan gur kitiŋ ki m di tii bi ni biyaajatiib na pu na.”

english_text:
Seventy Years of Exile
1-2 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, which was the first year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia, the Lord told me to speak to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. So I told them:
3For 23 years now, ever since the thirteenth year that Josiah was king, I have been telling you what the Lord has told me. But you have not listened.
4The Lord has sent prophets to you time after time, but you refused to listen. 5They told you that the Lord had said:
Change your ways! If you stop doing evil, I will let you stay forever in this land that I gave your ancestors. 6I don't want to harm you. So don't make me angry by worshiping idols and other gods.
7But you refused to listen to my prophets. So I, the Lord, say that you have made me angry by worshiping idols, and you are the ones who were hurt by what you did. 8You refused to listen to me, 9and now I will let you be attacked by nations from the north, and especially by my servant, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. You and other nearby nations will be destroyed and left in ruins forever. Everyone who sees what has happened will be shocked, but they will still make fun of you. 10 I will put an end to your parties and wedding celebrations; no one will grind grain or be here to light the lamps at night. 11 This country will be as empty as a desert, because I will make all of you the slaves of the king of Babylonia for 70 years.
12When that time is up, I will punish the king of Babylonia and his people for everything they have done wrong, and I will turn that country into a wasteland forever. 13My servant Jeremiah has told you what I said I will do to Babylonia and to the other nations, and he wrote it all down in this book. I will do everything I threatened. 14I will pay back the Babylonians for every wrong they have done. Great kings from many other nations will conquer the Babylonians and force them to be slaves.
The Cup Full of God's Anger
15The Lord God of Israel showed me a vision in which he said, “Jeremiah, here is a cup filled with the wine of my anger. Take it and make every nation drink some. 16They will vomit and act crazy, because of the war this cup of anger will bring to them.”
17I took the cup from the Lord's hand, and I went to the kings of the nations and made each of them drink some. 18I started with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and the king and his officials were removed from power in disgrace. Everyone still makes insulting jokes about them and uses their names as curse words. 19The second place I went was Egypt, where everyone had to drink from the cup, including the king and his officials, the other government workers, the rest of the Egyptians, 20and all the foreigners who lived in the country.
Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod. 21Then I went to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, 22and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea. 23-24After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert, 25Zimri, Elam, Media, 26and the countries in the north, both near and far.
I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
27The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
28The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink. 29Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
30The Lord told me to say:
From my sacred temple
I will roar like thunder,
while I trample my people
and everyone else
as though they were grapes.
31My voice will be heard
everywhere on earth,
accusing nations of their crimes
and sentencing the guilty
to death.
Disaster Is Coming
32The Lord All-Powerful says:
You can see disaster spreading
from far across the earth,
from nation to nation
like a horrible storm.
33When it strikes, I will kill so many people that their bodies will cover the ground like manure. No one will be left to bury them or to mourn.
The Leaders of Judah Will Be Punished
34The Lord's people are his flock,
and you leaders
were the shepherds.
But now it's your turn
to be butchered like sheep.
You'll shatter like fine pottery
dropped on the floor.
So roll on the ground,
crying and mourning.
35You have nowhere to run,
nowhere to hide.
* 36-37Listen to the cries
of the shepherds,
as the Lord's burning anger
turns peaceful meadows
into barren deserts.
38Like a lion leaving its den,
the Lord has abandoned
his people
to the destruction of war.
translation_text:
Bidim bi nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb na aabɔr
1Juda aabɔr Jehoyakim, u aate nan ye Josia na, aanaan aabinanar ni, le Uwumbɔr nan di Juda aanib mɔmɔk aabɔr tee tuk mi. Babiloŋ aabɔr Nebukadnesar aanaan ni aajan aabiln ni le na. 2M nan bui Juda ni Jerusalem aanib mɔmɔk ke, 3“Ŋibin moninko ni ŋitaa ponn ni, ki nya Amonn aajapɔɔn Josia aah nan ye Juda aabɔr pu na aabin kipiik ni litatar ni ki nan saa din wee na, Uwumbɔr len m chee tibɔr, le m mu aa kee yii kaa di waah len pu na tuk nimi. Le ni yii, kaa pel waah len pu na. 4Naa pel, kaa kpa ŋuntii, le Uwumbɔr ma beenin tun ni waabɔnabr bi ye waatutum na ni chee. 5Bi nan bui nimi ke ni di cha nimi aabiin aabimbin mu ni bi na, ki di cha titunwanbir ti ni tun na, aan ki li beenin koo kitiŋ ki pu Uwumbɔr nan di tii nimi ni niyaajatiib, ke ki li ye nimi aawan n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na. 6Bi nan bui nimi ke ni taa li dooni ŋiwaa ki taa li dii ŋi, ki taa cha Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii naah dooni ŋiwaa ŋi ni naan nibaa na pu. Ni yaa ba nan kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb kan, waa ba ga nan daa nitafal. 7Tɔ, Uwumbɔr ubaa len ke ni yii, kaa pel u chee. Ni tee cha waaŋuul fii nimi aawaa pu, le ki joo ni ntafadaan mue nibaa pu.
8“Kina pu na, naah kaa ŋun tii u na, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke, 9‘M ban m tun yin ni ŋŋangan wɔb aanib mɔmɔk, ni Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar, u ye maatutunn na la. M ga cha bi dan ki nan tak Juda ni kaanib, ni ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk mu bi gbɔk ki na, ki cha mu li gur ye tilangbenn ti kpa ijawaan na, ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina. 10M ga cha baamɔɔn, ni mpopiin aafuuk, ni tibɔndinn aajim aapopiin aafuuk na ŋmin chii. Baan ki kan nkpan ki ŋa baakaryaa mam ni, kaan ki kan tijikaar mu. 11Kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk ga kpaln tilangbenn le ki li kpa ijawaan, le kaanib ni ŋitimbol ŋi bi gbɔk na ga li tun tii Babiloŋ aabɔr ki ti saa ŋibin imonko itaa ni kipiik. 12Nee aapuwɔb le m ga daa Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni kaabɔr aatafal baatunwanbir pu. M ga kuln kitiŋ ngbaan ki cha ki kpaln tilangbenn ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. 13M ga di tibɔbir ti m nan cha Jeremia di faan ŋitimbol na daa Babiloŋ aatiŋ aatafal, tibɔbir ti mɔmɔk bi kigbaŋ kee ni na. 14Babiloŋ yaab aah tun pu na, kina le m ga di teen bi, le ŋitimbol pam ni bibɔrkpaam di bi ŋa baanaagbiib.’”
Uwumbɔr aah ga daa ŋitimbol aatafal pu na
15Uwumbɔr, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na nan bui mi ke, “Ndaan aayikuuk ki gbii maaŋuul na sɔ. Di ki buen ŋitimbol ŋimɔk m tun si ŋi chee na, ki cha bi nyu ki ponn ni. 16Bi yaa nyun ki ponn ni kan, bi ga li chuun gbeer, kaan ki li kpa nlan, butɔb bu m ban m cha bu dan bi pu na pu.”
17Le m nan gaa kiyikuuk ngbaan Uwumbɔr aaŋaal ni, ki di tii ŋitimbol ŋimɔk Uwumbɔr tun mi ŋi chee na, ki cha ŋi nyun ki ponn ni. 18Jerusalem aatiŋ, ni Juda aatim mɔmɔk, ki kpee kaabɔrb ni biyidam mɔmɔk, m nan cha bi nyun ki ponn ni, ki cha bi kpaln nteersakpiin, ki kpa ijawaan, ki cha binib joo baayimbil puuni lir biken pu, ke baah beenin ŋani pu na.
19-26Binib bi mu nan ki nyun ki ponn ni na sɔ:
Ijipt aabɔr, ni waaninkpiib, ni biyidam,
Ijipt aanib mɔmɔk, ni biwɔwɔm bi mɔmɔk bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na,
Us aatiŋ aabɔrb mɔmɔk,
ni Filistia aatim mumina: Askelonn, ni Gasa, ni Ekronn, ni Asdod aatiŋ ki gur siib na aabɔrb mɔmɔk;
ni Edom, ni Moab, ni Amonn aatim aanib mɔmɔk;
ni Taya ni Saidonn aatim aabɔrb mɔmɔk;
ni Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem aatim aabɔrb mɔmɔk;
ni Dedann, ni Tema, ni Bus aatim mɔmɔk;
ni binib bi mɔmɔk chee biyigbeer pu aayikpir na,
ni Arabia aabɔrb mɔmɔk;
ni nteersakpiin ni aanibol aabɔrb mɔmɔk;
ni Simri, ni Elam, ni Media aatim aabɔrb mɔmɔk;
ni ŋŋangan wɔb, ni duun na, ni ni daa na, aabɔrb mɔmɔk ubaabaa.
Kitiŋ kee pu aatimbol mɔmɔk ga nyu ki ponn ni. Gbelngbeln yoo le nan ye Babiloŋ aabɔr u ga nyu ki ponn ni na.
27Le Uwumbɔr ki bui mi ke, “Tuk binib ngbaan ke min, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na le bui bi ke bi nyu ki ti gbii ki li wulni, ki ti lir ki taa ki ŋmaa fii sil, butɔb bu m ga cha bu dan bi pu na pu. 28Bi yaa yii kaa gaa kiyikuuk ngbaan aaŋaal ni ki nyu ki ponn ni kan, aa bui bi ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke see bi nyu ki ponn ni. 29M ga piin maabiil aatuln ngbaan mbaa aatiŋ ponn ni la. Bi dak ke maan daa bitafal la aa? Aayii, bi ga kan ntafadaan, ba pu? m ga cha butɔb dan kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aanib pu. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.
30“Sin Jeremia, di maah len pu na mɔmɔk moon.
Aa bui binib bee ke, ‘Uwumbɔr ga ŋuun ni paacham,
ki teen ke utaal na paachapaacham.
U ga ŋuun waanib pu;
u ga li tar ke uja u bi tai ŋisubil, aan nnyun nya pu na la.
Unii umɔk bi kitiŋ do na ga ŋun u pu,
31le kitiŋ aanaanmɔk mu ga ŋun.
Uwumbɔr kpa ŋitimbol ngbaan pu tibɔr.
U ga ji unii mɔmɔk tibɔr le ki ku bibiindam na.
Uwumbɔr le len kina.’”
32Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke tibɔbir ga dan litimbol libaa pu, le ki paan liken, kitaabuŋ ki pɔɔ sakpen na bi kitiŋ aanaanmɔk ki choo. 33Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, Uwumbɔr aah ku binib bi na aanikpol ga li dɔ kitiŋ kee pu, ni kookoo la. Ubaa aan wii baakpuul, le ubaa aan yoor ŋi di buen ti sub. Ŋi ga li dɔ ŋikpuk ŋikpuk ke tinaabin na la.
34Nimi biyidam, li wii man, nimi maanib aayidam, wii mpɔɔn pu man. Li wii ikpowiil ki bilni titan ni man. N‑yoonn mu bi ga ku nimi na fuu ni a, bi ga kɔr nimi ke ipihja na, le ŋinikpol ga yaa ni kookoo. 35Nibaa chee aa bi ni ga dii ki ŋmar. 36-37Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ponn ni le u kuln nimi aatimbol ki cha nimi aasuudoon aatiŋ nkuun, le ni wii ki ŋuuni ke inaa na. 38Uwumbɔr siir cha waanib ke uchinn aah siir cha waatakpaluŋ pu na la. Butɔb aajawaan, ni Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln cha kitiŋ ngbaan kpaln nteersakpiin a.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Message in the Temple
(Jeremiah 7.1-15)
1 Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
2Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you. 3Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins. 4Tell them that I have said:
You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings. 5Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once, 6 I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word.
Jeremiah on Trial
7The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said, 8-9and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
10The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial. 11While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
12-13Then I told the judges and everyone else:
The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
14You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right. 15But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
16The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
17Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that 18 years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said:
“I, the Lord All-Powerful, say
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple
now stands.”
19Then the leaders continued:
No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would.
People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
20-24After these leaders finished speaking, an important man named Ahikam son of Shaphan spoke up for me as well. And so, I wasn't handed over to the crowd to be killed.
Uriah the Prophet
While Jehoiakim was still king of Judah, a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah left his hometown of Kiriath-Jearim and came to Jerusalem. Uriah was one of the Lord's prophets, and he was saying the same things about Judah and Jerusalem that I had been saying. And when Jehoiakim and his officials and military officers heard what Uriah said, they tried to arrest him, but he escaped to Egypt. So Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men after Uriah, and they brought him back. Then Jehoiakim had Uriah killed and his body dumped in a common burial pit.
translation_text:
Baah jin Jeremia tibɔr pu na
1Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim aah jin Juda aanaan n‑yoonn mu na aapuwɔb, 2le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, “Sil Maadichal aachiln ni ki di maah bui si pu na moon tuk binib bi nyani Juda aatim ni ki nan dooni mi nima chee na. Taa nyan ti ponn ni tibaa lii. 3Nibaakan, binib ngbaan ga ŋun ki di cha baatunwanbir aabimbin. Bi yaa ŋun kan, m ga kpeln maalandak ki taa ki cha libiil li m ba ga joo ni bi pu, baabiin aatuln pu na, dan bi pu.”
4Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke m tuk binib ngbaan ke, “Min Uwumbɔr le len ke ni kii maamɔb ki li dii mmɔkm mu m di tii nimi na, 5ki li ŋun ŋimɔbon ŋi maatutum, bi ye bibɔnabr aan m tuni bi ni chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na. Naa kee kii tii baah len pu na daalbaadaal. 6Ni yaa beenin yiil kan, m ga bii Maadichal lee ke maah nan bii Silo aatiŋ pu na, le dulnyaa wee aatimbol mɔmɔk ga li joo Jerusalem aayimbil puuni lir biken pu.”
7Bitotoorb, ni bibɔnabr, ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk ŋun m bi len nimina mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, 8le maah len uma Uwumbɔr aah bui mi ke m len pu na doo na, le bi ber nan chuu mi ki teen ke, “Nimina ŋeer ke ti ku si. 9Ba ŋa aa di Uwumbɔr aayimbil len ke Waadichal lee ga bii ke Silo na, aan kitiŋ kimina mu ga kuln, ubaa taa ki li koo nima?” Binib ngbaan nan mann goln mi.
10Juda aatiŋ aayidam aah ŋun tiwan ni ŋa na pu, le bi san nyan ni nnaan aadichal ni, ki dan Uwumbɔr Aadichal chee, le ki ti kal baakakaa chee, mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Mbisamɔpɔɔn na chee. 11Le bitotoorb ni bibɔnabr nan bui biyidam ni binib ngbaan ke, “Uja wee ŋeer ke ti ku u, waah len tibɔr ti kitiŋ kee pu na pu. Nimi nibaa aatafal ŋun waah len pu na.”
12Le m bui ke, “Uwumbɔr le tun ni mi ke m nan di tibɔr ti mɔmɔk ni ŋun m joo mooni len Waadichal ni kitiŋ pu na len. 13Ni kpeln mbimbin mu ni bi mu ni na, ni tiwan ni ni ŋani na, ki kii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga kpeln waalandak ki taa ki cha libiil li u bui ke u ga joo ni ni pu na dan. 14M ma kan, m bi nimi aapɔɔn ni la. Naah gee pu na kan, ni ŋa mi. 15Tɔ, li nyi man kina: ni yaa ku mi kan, nimi ni kitiŋ kee aanib aabɔr ga bii ke ni ku unii u kaa tun taani ubaa na, ba pu? Uwumbɔr le tun ni mi ke m nan sak nimi.”
16Le biyidam ni binib ngbaan bui bitotoorb ni bibɔnabr ngbaan ke, “Uja wee len ti chee tibɔr Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu la; naa ŋan ke ni ku u.”
17Nee aapuwɔb, biyidam ngbaan bibaa nan fii sil le ki bui binib bi kuun ni na ke, 18“Hesekia aah nan ye Juda aabɔr na, Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Maika u nan bi Moresef aatiŋ ni na nan tuk binib mɔmɔk ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke,
‘Bi ga kpar Sionn ke lisikpel na,
le Jerusalem kpaln tilangbenn aakpuk,
le Uwumbɔr Aadichal
aagongoln ga kpaln kichook.’
19Ubɔr Hesekia ni Juda aanib aa nan ku Maika. Hesekia nan labr san Uwumbɔr le ki pɔɔn ubaa ke u kan lineen u chee. Le Uwumbɔr nan kpeln waalandak, kaa ki cha tibɔbir ti u nan bui ke ti ga dan bi pu na dan. Ti bi ban tibɔbir sakpenn le tii tibaa.”
20Tɔ, uja ubaa mu ki bi, ki len Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu tibɔbir kitiŋ kee, ni litimbol lee pu, ke Jeremiah aah len pu na. U nan ye Semaya u nyan ni Kiriaf Jearim na aajapɔɔn Uria. 21Ubɔr Jehoyakim ni waajab, ni waaninkpiib aah ŋun Uria aah len pu na, le ubɔr ngbaan nan pɔɔn ubaa ke bi ku u. Uria nan ŋun ti pu, le ki di ijawaan san buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni. 22Le ubɔr Jehoyakim nan tun Akbor aajapɔɔn Elnatann ni bijab bibaa Ijipt ni, ke bi ti li joo ni Uria. 23Bi nan ti joo ni u Ubɔr Jehoyakim chee, le u ku u ki di u mee kicheek ni.
24Tɔ, Safann aajapɔɔn Ahikam aah nan si nchaŋ ni na, le baa nan di mi tii binib ngbaan ke bi ku mi.

english_text:
Slaves of Nebuchadnezzar
1-2 Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me:
Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck. 3Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah. 4So have them tell their kings that I have said:
I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel, 5and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth, 6-7 and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
8This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease. 9You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar. 10If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed. 11But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
12After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said:
Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians. 13But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned. 14Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies. 15Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
16When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said:
Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying! 17If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
18If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem. 19-21After all, when Nebuchadnezzar took King Jehoiachin to Babylonia as a prisoner, he didn't take everything of value from Jerusalem. He left the bronze pillars, the huge bronze bowl called the Sea, and the movable bronze stands in the temple, and he left a lot of other valuable things in the palace and in the rest of Jerusalem.
But now I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, say that all these things 22will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeremia aah di inaaja i ko na aadɔ leen ubaa pu pu na
1Josia aajapɔɔn Sedekia aah nan jin Juda aanaan na, libuul ngbaan ni le Uwumbɔr bui mi 2ke m di ŋigbapapan ni idɔ, ki ŋa mbaa inaaja i ko na aadɔ i punn isil pu na ki di leen nsil. 3Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke m di inaŋ tii Edom, ni Moab, ni Amonn, ni Taya, ni Saidonn aaninkpiib bi dan Jerusalem ni ke bi nan kan Ubɔr Sedekia na, aan bi ti di i tii baabɔrb. 4Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, nan tuk mi ke m tuk bi ke bi ti bui baabɔrb ke uma Uwumbɔr len ke, 5“Maapɔɔnsakpiin pu le m naan dulnyaa wee, ni unibɔn, ni tiwakor ti mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ pu na; le ki joo ki tii unii umɔk m gee na. 6Min le di ŋitimbol ŋee mɔmɔk ŋa maatutunn Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar aapɔɔn ni, le ki cha ipeel mu tun tii u. 7Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ga tun tii u, ki ga tun tii ujapɔɔn, ni uyaabil ki ti saa buyoonn waatimbol ga lir na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le waatimbol ga li tun tii ŋitimbol ni bibɔrkpaam bi kpa ipɔɔn na.
8“Litimbol, bee nnaan mubaa yaa kaa kii tii u kan, m ga di butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween daa litafal ki ti saa buyoonn m ga cha Nebukadnesar kuln li pel pel na. 9Taa ŋun tii bibɔnabr man, bee unii umɔk bui ke u ga ŋmaa len tiwan ni ga fe ŋa fen na tidaŋ ni, bee bitekpiib aawiin, bee binib bi joo inyɔk tun na. Bi mɔmɔk tuk nimi le ke ni taa kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr. 10Bi ŋmanni nimi la, le kina ngbaan ga cha bi chur nimi buen dandar ki cha nimi aatiŋ. M ga jenn nyan nimi, le bi ku doo nimi. 11Tɔ, litimbol li kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr ki tun tii u na ma kan, m ga cha li li bi laatiŋ pu, ki li koo nima ki ko. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
12M nan bui Juda Aabɔr Sedekia tibɔchachaan ngbaan la, “Kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr. Li tun tii u ni waanib, ki li kpa limɔfal. 13Ba ŋa aa ban aa ni saanib kpo butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween aakun? Kina le Uwumbɔr len ke litimbol li kaa kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr na ga kan. 14Taa ŋun bibɔnabr bi tuk nimi ke ni taa di nibaa tii u na aabɔr. Bi ŋmanni nimi la. 15Uwumbɔr ubaa le len ke waa tun ni bi, ke bi joo inyamɔn le tuk nimi waayimbil pu. Kina pu na, u ga jenn nyan nimi, le bi ku nimi; nimi ni bibɔnabr bi joo inyamɔn yee tuk nimi na ga kpo.”
16Le m tuk bitotoorb ngbaan ni binib ngbaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ke, “Taa ŋun bibɔnabr bi len ke Maadichal ni aawangol ga ki nyan Babiloŋ ni ki gir ni dandana na aabɔr. Bi geei nimi inyamɔn la. 17Taa pel bi chee man. Kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr ki li kpa limɔfal man. Ba ŋa ni ban ke kitiŋ kee kpaln tilangbenn. 18Bi yaa sil ye maabɔnabr le ki kpa maabɔr kan, cha bi gaŋ min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ke m taa cha bi yoor liwangol li gur Maadichal ni, ni nnaan aadichal ni na buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.”
19-20Tɔ, Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aah nan yoor Jehoyakim aajapɔɔn Jehoyachinn u nan ye Juda aabɔr na, ni Juda, ni Jerusalem aasalolm buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na, waa nan yoor jaatɔlk mam, ni tikumann aakin, ni tɔroku mam, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aawangol ŋiken mu.
21“Li pel man, min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, aah kpa pu ki joo cha liwangol li gur ki bi Maadichal ni, ni nnaan aadichal ni, Jerusalem aatiŋ ni na: 22Bi ga yoor li buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu m ga fenn maalandak toŋ li wɔb na. Le m ga giin ni li ki nan di siin libuul lee ni. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Accuses Hananiah of Being a False Prophet
1 Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening, 2he told me that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I will smash the yoke that Nebuchadnezzar put on the necks of the nations to make them his slaves. 3And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia. 4King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
5The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
6Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home. 7But let me remind you and everyone else 8that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease. 9Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
10Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it. 11Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.”
I left the temple, 12and a little while later, the Lord told me 13-14to go back and say to Hananiah:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
15-16Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
17Two months later, Hananiah died.
translation_text:
Jeremia ni Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Hanania aabɔr
1Libinbaal ngbaan ponn ni, Sedekia aah nan ye ubɔr pu na aabinanar aaŋmaŋmu ni, le Asur aajapɔɔn Hanania u nan ye ubɔnabr Gibeonn aatiŋ ni na nan len m chee tibɔr Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. 2U nan bui mi bitotoorb ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aanimbil ni, ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na len ke, “M bii Babiloŋ aabɔr aapɔɔn. 3Joo cha ni ŋibin ŋilee na, m ga giin ni Maadichal ni aawangol li Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan yoor di buen na. 4M ga giin ni Juda aabɔr Jehoyachinn, u aate ye Jehoyakim na, ni Juda aanib bi mɔmɔk nan buen tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ ni na. Een, m ga bii Babiloŋ aabɔr aapɔɔn. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
5M nan bui Hanania ni bitotoorb, ni binib bi mɔmɔk nan si Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na aanimbil ni ke: 6“Mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr ba sil ŋa kina kan, ni ba ŋan. Saabɔkpiirkaan tee ba ga sil gbiin ke u nyan ni Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni, Waadichal ni aawangol ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi tinaagbiir ni nima na kan, m ba ga li gee kina sakpen. 7Tɔ, tee li pel maah kpa pu m tuk aa ni binib ngbaan na. 8Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr bi nan puen len tibɔr n‑yaajayoonn, waahr aan m ni sin nin fuu ni na, nan len ke butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween ga dan ŋitimbol ni bibɔrkpaam pam pu. 9Tɔ, ubɔnabr u len ke nsuudoon bi, aan waah len pu na nan gbiin kan, le bi ga bee u ke u sil ye ubɔnabr u Uwumbɔr tun ni u na.”
10Le Hanania chuu inaaja aadɔ i lee nsil na ki kool kool i yuk yuk, 11le ki len binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aanimbil ni ke: “Uwumbɔr bui ke kina le u ga bii Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aadɔ i u di leen ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aasil na; ki joo cha ŋibin ŋilee ponn ni le u ga ŋa kina.” Le m siir.
12Nee aapuwɔb, le Uwumbɔr bui mi 13ke m buen ti tuk Hanania ke: “Uwumbɔr bui ke aa ga ŋmaa koo idɔ i pui inaaja aasil pu na, le u ga ŋa tikur yaan teen idɔ yoo ngbaan aabuul ni. 14Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui ke u ga di tikur aadɔ kina le leen ŋitimbol ŋee aasil ki cha bi li tun tii Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar. Uwumbɔr ki len ke u ga cha ipeel mu tun tii Nebukadnesar.”
15Le m bui Hanania kina, le ki ki len ke, “Hanania, li pel. Uwumbɔr aa nan tun ni si, le aa cha binib ngbaan gaal saanyamɔn ngbaan. 16Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr ubaa len ke u ga ku si. Saah bui binib ngbaan ke bi yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na, aa ga kpo waahr aan libiln lee nin jer.”
17Le Hanania nan kpo libinbaal ngbaan aaŋmalole ponn ni.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Letter to the People of Judah in Babylonia
1-2 I had been left in Jerusalem when King Nebuchadnezzar took many of the people of Jerusalem and Judah to Babylonia as prisoners, including King Jehoiachin, his mother, his officials, and the metal workers and others in Jerusalem who were skilled in making things. So I wrote a letter to the priests, the prophets, the leaders, and the rest of our people in Babylonia. 3I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote 4that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you 5to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them. 6Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
7Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
8-9Some of your people there in Babylonia are fortunetellers, and you have asked them to tell you what will happen in the future. But they will only lead you astray with their dreams. And don't let the prophets fool you, either. They speak in my name, but they are liars. I have not spoken to them.
10 After Babylonia has been the strongest nation for 70 years, I will be kind and bring you back to Jerusalem, just as I have promised. 11I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering. 12You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers. 13 You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you 14and accept your worship. Then I will gather you from all the nations where I scattered you, and you will return to Jerusalem.
15You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
16-19But I have been sending prophets to the people of Judah for a long time, and the king from David's family and the people who are left in Jerusalem and Judah still don't obey me. So I, the Lord All-Powerful, will keep attacking them with war and hunger and disease, until they are as useless as rotten figs. I will force them to leave the land, and all nations will be disgusted and shocked at what happens to them. The nations will sneer and make fun of them and use the names “Judah” and “Jerusalem” as curse words.
And you have not obeyed me, even though 20I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now. 21-23You think Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah are prophets because they claim to speak for me. But they are lying! I haven't told them anything. They are also committing other horrible sins in your community, such as sleeping with the wives of their friends. So I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will put them to death while the rest of you watch. And in the future, when you want to put a curse on someone, you will say, “I pray that the Lord will kill you in the same way the king of Babylonia burned Zedekiah and Ahab to death!”
A Message for Shemaiah
24-25The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
26After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars. 27Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him? 28He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
29When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me. 30Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter 31to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said:
I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name. 32He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeremia aah ŋmee kigbaŋ ki tii Juu yaab bi bi Babiloŋ ni na aabɔr
1M nan ŋmee kigbaŋ tii bitotoorb, ni bibɔnabr, ni binib ngbaan aayidam, ni bi mɔmɔk gur aan Nebukadnesar nan nyan bi Jerusalem ki di bi buen tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na. 2Baah nan chuu Ubɔr Jehoyachinn, ni una, ni libɔrchiln ni aaninkpiib, ni Juda ni Jerusalem aayidam, ni bikpikpiib, ni biwanŋab mɔmɔk di buen tinaagbiir ni na aapuwɔb le m nan ŋmee kigbaŋ ngbaan. 3M nan di kigbaŋ ngbaan tii Safann aajapɔɔn Elasa, ni Hilkia aajapɔɔn Gemaria, bi Juda Aabɔr Sedekia nan tun bi Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni, Ubɔr Nebukadnesar chee na la. Kaabɔr sɔ:
4“Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, bui binib bi mɔmɔk u nan cha Nebukadnesar chur Jerusalem ni ki di buen tinaagbiir ni, Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na ke: 5‘Maa ŋidichal ki kal man. Naan tisar ki ji naah bun tijikaar ti ti ponn ni na. 6Yoor bipiib ki maa mbim man, ki cha nijapɔtiib mu yoor bipiib, nibisatiib mu mɔn tichar, aan ki mu kan mbim. Ni ŋan ke ni pɔr ki taa seen. 7Li tun man ki cha ntim mu m cha ni ti bi tinaagbiir ni mu ponn ni na kan tinyoor. Li mee limeel m chee bi pu, ba pu? bi yaa kan liwangol kan, ni mu ga kan. 8Min Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na sak nimi ke ni taa cha bibɔnabr bi bi ni ponn ni na li ŋmanni nimi, ki taa cha binib bi bui ke bi nyi fen aabɔr na ŋmann nimi. Taa pel man baadaŋ ti bi daŋni na. 9Bi joo maayimbil le geei inyamɔn. Maa tun ni bi. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.’
10“Uwumbɔr ki len ke, ‘Babiloŋ aabin imonko itaa ni kipiik na yaa jer kan, m ga mɔk nimi maah neen nimi pu ki joo tipuur ti m nan puu ke m ga giin ni nimi nido na. 11Min baanja le nyi maah dak ni pu pu na, ilandak i ye ke m joo ni nimi nkam kaa ye tibɔbir na, ilandak i ye ke m joo ni nimi fen u ni mak u pu na. N‑yoonn mu choo na kpa limakl; 12Le ni ga yin mi. Ni ga dan ki nan mee limeel, le m ga ŋun nimi aameel. 13Ni ga ban mi, le ki ga kan mi, ba pu? ni ga di nisui mɔmɔk le ban mi. 14Een, m bui ke, ni ga kan mi, le m ga giin ni nimi nido aatiŋ pu. M ga kuun ni nimi litimbol mɔk ni, ni nimɔk m cha ni yaa ki bi na, le m ga giin ni nimi kitiŋ ki pu m nan nyan nimi di buen tinaagbiir ni na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.’
15“Nimi le bui ke Uwumbɔr tii nimi bibɔnabr Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni. 16Li pel man Uwumbɔr aah len ubɔr u joo nnaan mu Ubɔrkpaan David nan joo na, ni kitiŋ kimina aanib, bima le ye nido yaab bi baa nan chur bi buen tinaagbiir ni, ni chee na, 17Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke, ‘M ban m cha butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween lir bi pu, m ga ŋa bi ke ŋikakan ŋi bur aan baan ŋmaa ŋmɔ ŋi na. 18M ga li joo ni butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween le san dii bi, le dulnyaa wee aatimbol mɔmɔk ga san ijawaan, baah kan pu na pu. Nimɔk m cha bi yaa ki bi na, binib aapobil ga yuk, ki san ijawaan, baah kan tiwan ni mɔmɔk na. Binib ga laa bi, ki li joo baayimbil puuni lir biken pu. 19Baah kaa kii tibɔr ti m nan joo tii ni maatutum, bi ye bibɔnabr na, le cha nimina ŋa. Tɔ, nimi bi bi tinaagbiir ni, Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na mu aa nan ŋun. 20Nimi bi mɔmɔk m cha ni buen tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na, li pel man, min Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.’
21“Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, len Kolaya aajapɔɔn Ahab ni Maaseya aajapɔɔn Sedekia, bi chuun joo waayimbil geei inyamɔn tuk nimi na aabɔr. U len ke u ga di bi ŋa Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar aaŋaal ni, le u ku bi ninimbil ni. 22Le baah chur binib bi tinaagbiir Jerusalem ni, ki di bi buen Babiloŋ ni na yaa ban bi puun lii unii pu kan, bi ga bui ke, ‘Uwumbɔr ŋa si ke waah nan cha Babiloŋ aabɔr pun Sedekia ni Ahab mmii ni, bi laa beenin fu pu na.’ 23Baah tun titunwanbir sakpen pu na, baadoon le ga li bi na; bi goor kidagook, ki di Uwumbɔr aayimbil geei inyamɔn. Uwumbɔr aa nan gee kina; u nyi baah tun pu na, le uma le ye useeraadaan. Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Semaya aah ŋmee kigbaŋ ki na aabɔr
24-25Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, nan tii mi tibɔr ke m di tii Semaya, u ye Nehelam aatiŋ aanii, ki nan di ubaa aayimbil pu ki ŋmee kigbaŋ tii Jerusalem aanib mɔmɔk, ni utotoor Sefania, u aate ye Maaseya na, ni bitotoorb biken na mɔmɔk. Semaya nan ŋmee tibɔr timina le waagbaŋ ngbaan ni tii Sefania:
26“Uwumbɔr nan yii Jehoyada le ki di si ŋa utotoor, sin le ye uma Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aayidaan. Ni ye sin le aatuln ke aa chur biwaarb bi mɔmɔk chuun ŋmanni ke bi ye bibɔnabr na, ki di tikur aabuen ŋmaan bisil, ki di tikululn baa bi kaan. 27Ba ŋa saa ŋa Anatof aanii u bi yin u ke Jeremia aan u chuun tuk binib tibɔr ke u ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr na kina? 28U tuk binib bi bi Babiloŋ ni, tinaagbiir ni na, ke bi ga li bi nima aan ni ti yunn, kina pu na, bi maa ŋidichal, ki kal nima, ki naan tisar, ki ji baah ko tijikaar ti na; kina pu na, cha bi chuu u.”
29Sefania nan karn kigbaŋ ngbaan tii mi. 30Le Uwumbɔr bui mi 31-32ke m di Semaya aabɔr tee naŋ tuk binib bi mɔmɔk bi tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ ponn ni na ke, “Min Uwumbɔr ga daa Semaya ni uyaabitiib aatafal. Maa tun ni u, le u len tibɔr ke waah ye maabɔnabr le na, ki cha ni gaa waah geei inyamɔn i na. Waan li kpa yaabil ni ponn ni. Waah bui maanib ke bi nya mpuwɔb na, waan li bi ki nan kan tiwanyaan ni m ban m nan ŋa tii maanib na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
1-2The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you. 3Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
4-5Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah:
Screams of terror are heard,
with no word of peace.
6Can men give birth?
Then why do I see them
looking so pale
and clutching their stomachs
like women in labor?
7My people, soon you will suffer
worse than ever before,
but I will save you.
8Now you are slaves
of other nations,
but I will break the chains
and smash the yokes
that keep you in slavery.
9Then you will be my servants,
and I will choose a king for you
from the family of David.
* 10 Israel, you belong to me,
so don't be afraid.
You deserved to be punished;
that's why I scattered you
in distant nations.
But I am with you,
and someday I will destroy
those nations.
11Then I will bring you
and your descendants
back to your land,
where I will protect you
and give you peace.
Then your fears will be gone.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
12The Lord said:
My people, you are wounded
and near death.
13You are accused of a crime
with no one to defend you,
and you are covered with sores
that no medicine can cure.
* 14Your friends have forgotten you;
they don't care anymore.
Even I have acted like an enemy.
And because your sins
are horrible and countless,
I will be cruel
as I punish you.
15So don't bother to cry out
for relief from your pain.
16But if your enemies try to rob
or destroy you,
I will rob and destroy them,
and they will be led as captives
