Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever.
Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
20 The Lord said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon 22and tell its people:
I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy. 23I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
24When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
A Blessing for Israel
25The Lord God said:
Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_text:
Taya Aabɔr aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke, 2“Unibɔn, tuk Taya aatiŋ aajojoor min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk u pu na ke: Aa di kigaak puun aabaa kin kin, ki yin aabaa ke liwaal. Aa bui ke aa ka libɔrjal pu ke liwaal na la, le nnyusakpem mann goln si. Aa ga ŋmaa ŋmann ke aa ye liwaal la, tɔ, aa po ye unibɔn le kaa kpa tiwan ni kaa ye unibɔn na aabimbin. 3Aa dak ke aa kpa nlan jer Danel, le tiwanbɔrkaan nibaa aan ŋmaa bɔr si. 4Saalan ni nwanyim le cha aa kpa liwangol li ye salmaa, ni tikunabr na. 5Aa nan di nlan ŋa kitiirk aatuln ki kani tinyoor. Aa sil mak saawankpal pu.
6“Tɔ, min, Aadindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: Saah dak ke aa kpa nlan ke liwaal na, 7m ga cha bidim bi kaa san kinimbaak na dan nan tak si. Bi ga nan kuln saah di nlan ni nwanyim kan tiwanyaan ni na mɔmɔk. 8Bi ga ku si. Nnyunsakpem ni, le aa ga kpo mpɔɔn aakun. 9Bi yaa nan dan ke bi ku si kan, aa ga li beenin len ke aa ye liwaal aa? Aa yaa nan sil binib bi ga ku si na aanimbiin ni kan, aa ga li ye unibɔn kaan li kpa liwaal aabimbin kpala. 10Aa ga kpo biwɔwɔm bi kaa san Uwumbɔr na aaŋaal ni ke ubɔ na la. Min Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina aabɔr.”
Taya aatiŋ aabɔr aah lir pu na
11Uwumbɔr nan ki len tibɔr m chee. U nan len ke, 12“Unibɔn, li wii ni mpombiin mbimbin mu dɔ kiir Taya aatiŋ aabɔr na pu. Bui u min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk u pu na ke: Aa nan ye n‑yaayoonn mubaa aanyaan sakpeŋ aamɔkl la. Saalan ni saanyaan nan nyaŋ a. 13Aa nan koo Uwumbɔr aasaak Edenn ni la, le ki kpa ŋitakpanyaan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ. Aa nan kpa ŋitakpanyaan ŋi bi yi ŋi ke rubi, ni diamonn, ni topas, ni beril, ni kaneliann, ni jaspa, ni safir, ni emeral, ni ganet na. Aa nan kpa salmaa aaleen. Nwiin mundaal bi naan si na, le bi nan ŋa tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk tii si. 14M nan di maatuun mu ga tii unii ijawaan na siin kiir si nima. Aa nan bi maajool li bi chain na pu, le ki chuun ŋitakpanyaan ŋi moor lak lak na ni. 15Saabimbin nan ŋan sakpen ki nyan nwiin mundaal bi naan si na ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu aa piin titunwanbir aatuln na. 16Aa nan di liwandaal ni liwankooh le muk aabaa, le kina aatuln di si koon mbimbin mu pɔɔ na, ni titunwanbir aatuln ni. Kina pu le maatuun mu nan kii si na jenn nyan si ŋitakpanyaan ŋi moor lak lak na ni. 17Aa nan mak saanyaan pu, le saayimbil nan cha aa bi ke ujɔr na. Nimina pu le m nan mee si lii kitiŋ, ki cha si nima, ke aa li ye nsurm ki tii bibɔrb biken. 18Aa nan di liwandaal ni liwankooh tun titunwanbir, le ki cha saameen aabuu ni kpaln njinjin aabuu ni. Kina pu le m see kitiŋ ngbaan mmii lii, ki cha ki wun ti kpaln nfatan. Unii umɔk yaar lik si na waa si ke aa gur ye nfatan la. 19Aa buen a, aa buen kookoo a, le ijawaan chuu ŋitimbol ŋi nan nyi si na sakpen, ŋi san ijawaan ke ŋi mu ga kan saah kan pu na.”
Saidonn aatiŋ aabɔr
20Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr ke, 21“Unibɔn, lik Saidonn aatiŋ wɔb ki len tibɔbir lii ki pu. 22Bui binib bi koo nima chee na, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah kpa baabɔr ti m tuk bi na ke: Saidonn aatiŋ, m ye saadin la; binib ga pak mi maah ŋa si pu na pu. M yaa mɔk maah bi chain pu na ki daa binib bi koo aa ponn ni na aatafal kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 23M ga cha iween dan aa pu, ki cha nsin puu saatiŋ ponn ni. Bi ga tak si ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu, ki ku saanib. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”
Uwumbɔr aah ga ŋa waanyoor ŋa Israel yaab pu pu na
24Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln Israel aatimbol ki nan lik li fam na libaa aan ki li bi ke ikokon na ki ŋa Israel nibaa. Le ŋi ga bee ke min le ye Dindaan Uwumbɔr.”
25Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “M ga ki nyan Israel yaab maah nan cha bi yaa ki bi ŋitimbol ŋi na ni, ki cha ŋitimbol mɔmɔk bee ke m ye chain la. Israel aanib ga li koo bibaa aatiŋ pu la, kima le ye kitiŋ ki m nan di tii maatutunn Jakob na. 26Bi ga li bi nima lifuur ni la. Bi ga maa ŋidichal ki ko ŋisubil aasar. M ga daa ŋitimbol ŋi nan lik bi fam na aatafal, le Israel aatiŋ ga kan nsuudoon. N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Egypt
1 Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people 3that I am saying:
King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy! 4I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body. 5I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh. 6 Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick. 7When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
8So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock, 9until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things.
You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it. 10Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia. 11No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for 40 years. 12It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those 40 years, and I will scatter your people throughout the nations of the world.
13Then after those 40 years have passed, I will bring your people back from the places where I scattered them. 14They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom 15and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past. 16My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
17Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
18King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city. 19So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops. 20Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
21Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Ijipt aatiŋ aabɔr
1Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni aaŋmapiik aawiin kipiik ni mulee daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke, 2“Unibɔn, lik Ijipt aatiŋ aabɔr Faro wɔb ki len tibɔbir lii u ni Ijipt aatiŋ mɔmɔk pu. Tuk u maah ga daa u ni Ijipt aatiŋ mɔmɔk aatafal pu na. 3Bui ke Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk Ijipt aabɔr pu na sɔ: sin unyiib, kiwanbiik ki dɔ nnyun ni na, m ye saadin la. Aa bui ke Nail Aamɔɔl ye sin yaan la, ki len ke sin le ŋa li. 4M ga di njapiin le saa chaar aalakpak aan ki cha saamɔɔl aajan dab baan si. Le m ga dar nyan si Nail Aamɔɔl ponn ni, aan ijan ngbaan mɔmɔk dab baa si. 5M ga di aa ni ijan ngbaan mɔmɔk mee lii nteersakpiin ni. Aa ga ti lir kitiŋ ki gaar nima, ubaa taa sub si. M ga di si tii inyoon ni ipeel i di ŋa tijikaar. 6N‑yoonn ngbaan le Ijipt aanib mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”
Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “Israel yaab nan mak nimi Ijipt yaab pu le ke ni ter bi, ni mu nan bi ke likal li kaa pɔɔ na la. 7Baah nan nyii ni pu na, le ni koo lir ki saa chaar biŋmɔŋ ni, le ki cha bi daa goob bichaŋ. 8Tɔ, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le bui si ke m ga ban bijab aan bi nan di kijaak aajum tak si, le bi ga ku saanib ni saawakor. 9Ijipt aatiŋ ga kpaln tilangbenkuun la. N‑yoonn ngbaan le ni ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.
“Saah bui ke Nail Aamɔɔl ye sin yaan na pu, ki len ke sin le ŋa li na, 10m ye saadin la, le ki ye saamɔɔl ngbaan mu aadin. M ga ŋa Ijipt aatiŋ mɔmɔk tilangbenkuun, ki nya Migdol aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ki ti saa Aswann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na, ki yoor kina ki ti saa Kus yaab aatinaanmɔk. 11Unibɔn, bee kiwakork aan ki chuun nima. Nibaa aan li bi ki pu ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee. 12M ga cha Ijipt aatiŋ li ye kitikuun ki jer dulnyaa wee ni aatim mɔmɔk. Ijipt aatim ga doon nkuun ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee, ni ga li ye tilangbenkuun ki jer kitiŋ mɔmɔk. M ga ŋa Ijipt yaab bikusam. Bi ga yaa buen litingbaln mɔmɔk ni ki ti li koo nima chee aanib chee.”
13Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “Ŋibin imonko ilee aapuwɔb, le m ga ki nyan ni Ijipt yaab maah nan cha bi yaa ki bi ŋitimbol ŋi ponn ni na, 14le ki ga cha bi ti li koo Ijipt aapepel li bi ŋŋangii wɔb ki ye biyaajatiib aalangbenn na; nima chee le bi ga li bi ki ye nnaan mu kaa kpa mpɔɔn na, 15mu ga li ye nnaan mu kaa po kpa mpɔɔn kpala na la, le baan ki li ye litimbol libaa aajojoob. M ga tii bi kiyimbibiik sakpeŋ le baan ki ŋmaa daa litimbol libaa dan bibaa chee. 16Israel aatimbol aan ki nyii bi pu daalbaadaal ki ban nterm. Ijipt aabimbin ngbaan le ga teer Israel yaab naah kaa ŋan pu ke bi nyii bi pu ki ban nterm na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Israel yaab ga bee ke min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.”
Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aah ga nyaŋ Ijipt aatiŋ pu na
17Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin moninko ni ŋilole aajan aaŋmal aajan aawiin daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke, 18“Unibɔn, Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar fii sil ki tak Taya aatiŋ. U cha waajab tun ŋitun ŋi nyuun sakpen na le biyikpir ti gui, le bibɔgbin mu puun puun, tɔ, ubɔr ngbaan ni waajab mɔmɔk aa kan nibaa nimina pu. 19Tɔ, Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: M joo Ijipt aatiŋ tii Ubɔr Nebukadnesar la. U ga koo ki yoor Ijipt aawangol mɔmɔk ke ni li ye waajab aapar. 20Waajab aah nan tun maatun na pu le m ga di Ijipt aatiŋ tii u. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.
21“Kina yaa nan ŋa kan, m ga cha Israel aanib pɔɔk, ki cha sin Esekiel sil unii mɔmɔk aah ga ŋun aa pu nin chee na ki len tibɔr, ki cha bi bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Egypt Will Be a Barren Desert
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying:
Cry out in despair,
3because you will soon
be punished!
That will be a time
of darkness and doom
for all nations.
4Your own nation of Egypt
will be attacked,
and Ethiopia will suffer.
You will be killed in battle,
and your land will be robbed
and left in ruins.
5Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle. 6All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
7Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin. 8I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
9On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
10Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army. 11He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
12I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins
The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
13All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land. 14The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed! 15The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
16I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear. 17The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner. 18You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity. 19When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord.
Egypt's King Is Powerless
20Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword. 22So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever, 23and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
24-25I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord. 26I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr ga daa Ijipt aatiŋ aatafal
1Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr ke, 2“Unibɔn, nabr ki moon min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na. Aa teen ŋimɔbon ŋimina mpɔɔn pu ke:
Ijawasakpiin aawiin mubaa choo,
3Nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga fii sil na duun ni a,
mu ga li ye ntaalangbam
ni tibɔbir aawiin le ki tii ŋitimbol.
4Butɔb ga li bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni
le mpombiin sakpiin ga li bi Kus aatiŋ ni.
Bi ga ku binib pam Ijipt aatiŋ ni;
bi ga yoor litingbaln ngbaan aawan ki cha ki nkuun.
5“Baah ti di ŋimombil pan bijab bi pu, aan bi nyan ni Kus, ni Libia, ni Lidia, ni Arabia, ni Kub aatim ni na ga bee butɔb ngbaan ni, hali ki kpee maanib mu ponn ni bibaa.”
6Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Ki nya Migdol aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ki ti saa Aswann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na, bi ga ku Ijipt yaab bi kii kitiŋ ngbaan na mɔmɔk. Bi ga kuln Ijipt aatɔb aajab bi kpa kigaak na. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. 7Kitiŋ ngbaan le ga doon nkuun ki jer dulnyaa aatim mɔmɔk, le kaatikpaan ga kpaln ŋilangben. 8M yaa moo mmii see Ijipt aatiŋ lii, aan bi ku kaakikiib mɔmɔk kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.
9“Nwiin ngbaan yaa fuu ni aan Ijipt aatiŋ kuln kan, m ga tun binib iŋɔi ni, le bi ti bui Kus yaab bi kaa nyi kina pu na, le ijawaan sakpiin ga chuu bi. Nwiin ngbaan choo.”
10Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M ga di Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar le kuln Ijipt aawangol. 11U ni waajab bi kaa san kinimbaak kpala na ga dan ki nan bii kitiŋ ngbaan. Bi ga di kijaak aajum le tak Ijipt aatiŋ, le kitiŋ ngbaan pu ga li ye ŋinikpol ŋmeen. 12M ga cha Nail Aamɔɔl foor ki kuur, aan ki di Ijipt aatiŋ ŋa bibiindam aaŋaal ni. Biwɔwɔm le ga bii kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk doo. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
13Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M ga kuln ŋiwaa ni inyɔk Memfis aatiŋ ni. Ubaa aan ki li bi ki ye Ijipt aatiŋ aajojoor, le m ga cha ijawaan sakpiin chuu kaanib mɔmɔk. 14M ga cha Ijipt aapepel li bi ŋŋangii wɔb na doon nkuun, ki see Soann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na mmii lii. M ga daa kaatiyil Tebes aatafal. 15M ga cha Ijipt aatikpaan Pelusium ki bi maa ŋigon kiir ki na, kan maaŋuul li pɔɔ na. M ga kuln Tebes aawangol. 16M ga see Ijipt aatiŋ mmii, le Pelusium aatiŋ ga li bi iween kpaan ni. Tebes aagon ga wɔi doon kitiŋ, le kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni kpaln nwam. 17Heliopolis ni Bubastis aatim aanachipɔm ga bee butɔb ni; le bi ga chur binib bi gur na tinaagbiir. 18M yaa nan bii Ijipt aapɔɔn mu bi nan mak mu pu sakpen na kan, mbɔmbɔɔn ga lir Tapanes aatiŋ pu. Ntaalangbam ga biin Ijipt aatiŋ pu, le bi ga chur kaatim mɔmɔk aanib tinaagbiir. 19M yaa daa Ijipt aatiŋ aanib aatafal kina kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”
Ijipt Aabɔr aapɔɔn aah doo pu na
20Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni libaa aajan aaŋmal aawinlole daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr. 21U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, m koo Ijipt aabɔr aaŋaal a. Ubaa aa di litaln poo mu, kaa di tiwan chuu mu ki di leen usil ke mu sɔŋ ki ki pɔɔk aan u ki di mu chuu kijaak aajuk. 22Tɔ, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: M ye Ijipt aabɔr aadin la. M ban m koo uŋaal ilee ngbaan mɔmɔk la, m ga koo mu pɔɔ na ni mu puun koo na, le kijaak aajuk nya uŋaal ni ki lir. 23M ga cha Ijipt yaab yaa koo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni. 24N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga cha Babiloŋ aabɔr aaŋaal pɔɔk, le m di kijaak aajuk ŋum u. Tɔ, m ga koo Ijipt aabɔr ma aaŋaal, le u ga li du iween pu ki ti kpo waadin aanimbiin ni. 25Mbamɔn, m ga diŋ u le ki moo pɔɔk Babiloŋ aabɔr ma. M yaa di maajaak aajuk tii u aan u di ki mɔk Ijipt aatiŋ kan, unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 26M ga cha Ijipt yaab yaa koo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Egypt's King Will Be Chopped Down like a Cedar Tree
1Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying:
You are more powerful
than anyone on earth.
Now listen to this.
3There was once a cedar tree
in Lebanon
with large, strong branches
reaching to the sky.
4This tree had plenty of water
to help it grow tall,
and nearby streams watered
the other trees
in the forest.
5But this tree towered over
those other trees,
and its branches
grew long and thick.
6Birds built nests
in its branches,
and animals were born
beneath it.
People from all nations
lived in the shade
of this strong tree.
7It had beautiful,
long branches,
and its roots found water
deep in the soil.
8 None of the cedar trees
in my garden of Eden
were as beautiful
as this tree;
no tree of any kind
had such long branches.
9I, the Lord, gave this tree
its beauty,
and I helped the branches
grow strong.
All other trees in Eden
wanted to be just like it.
10King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree:
The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant. 11So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness. 12Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else. 13Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
14Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
15On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither. 16This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble.
The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls. 17Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
18King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah di Ijipt aatiŋ ŋaŋ santina aasub pu na
1Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni libaa aaŋmataa aajan aawiin daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr. 2U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, tuk Ijipt aabɔr ni waanib mɔmɔk ke:
Nimi aapɔɔn nyaŋ a. M ga di nimi ŋaŋ ba?
3Ni bi ke Lebanonn aatiŋ aasantina na la,
ki kpa mboon aapanyaan,
ki ye busub bu fɔk ki ti tuu ntaalangbam na.
4Bu nan kpa nnyun ke bu di muun,
le ŋimɔɔ bi kitiŋ taab ki tii bu nnyun.
Bi nan kpir nnyun busub ngbaan aah si nin chee na
ki ŋa nkpen buen kichook ni aasui mɔmɔk chee.
5Bu aah nan kpa nnyun na, bu nan muun jer isui mɔmɔk.
Bu aapan nan filk ki fɔk.
6Inyoon mɔmɔk aabɔŋ nan ter yaadil bu aapan ni;
ipeel nan ma yaabim bu aaboon ni;
dulnyaa aatimbol nan kaa bu aaboon ni.
7Busub ngbaan aanyaan nan ti nyaŋ,
Bu nan fɔk, ki kpa ŋipan fɔfɔŋ.
Bu aanyaan nan koo taab taab
ki ti pii kitiŋ taab aamɔɔ na.
8Santina aa nan bi Uwumbɔr
aasaak na ni, aan aa ga di ŋaŋ bu.
Busub bubaa aaboln aa kpa kina aapan,
bu aasupuul aaboln aa nan bi.
Busub bubaa aa nan bi Uwumbɔr aasaak ni ki ŋan kina.
9M nan ŋa bu, bu ŋan ki kpa ŋipan ŋi fɔk na.
Busub bumɔk nan bi Uwumbɔr aasaak ni, Edenn aatiŋ ni na,
nan kpa bu pu lipiipoln la.
10“Tɔ, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr ga bui si tiwan ni ga ŋa busub bu muun ki ti tuu ntaalangbam na. Bu aah moo muun kpee na, le bu gur kpa kipupuk; 11kina pu na, m yii bu, ki ga di bu tii ujojoor u ye uwɔwɔnja na. U ga di tiwan ni ŋeer busub ngbaan aabiin na tii bu. 12Biwɔwɔm bi kaa san kinimbaak kpala na ga gaa bu lii ki siir cha bu. Bu aapan ni lisupuul ga lir lijool mɔmɔk, ni kifataŋ ki mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na pu. Ŋitimbol ŋi nan koo bu aaboon ni na ga yaa. 13Inyoon ga dan nan kal busub bu lir ki dɔ na pu, le ipeel ga taa bu aapan pu ki jer. 14Kina pu na, ki nya n‑yoonn mumina na, busub bubaa aan ki ŋmaa muun ke buma na, bee bu too ti chaar ntaalangbam ni ki ti pii kitaapaak. Hali bu yaa po kan nnyun sakpen pu na kan, bu aan fuu kina. I mɔmɔk ga kpo ke unibɔn na la, i ga buen ti kpee binib bi bi kitekpiitiŋ ni taab na pu.”
15Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ki len pu na sɔ: “Nwiin mundaal busub ngbaan ga buen kitekpiitiŋ ni na, m ga cha kitiŋ taab aanyun biin bu pu aan ni mɔk bu aakpowiil. M ga chuu ŋimɔɔ siin ki taa ki cha ikpen pam na puu nya. Busub ngbaan aah kpo na, m ga cha mbɔmbɔɔn biin Lebanonn Aajoo pu ki cha kichook ngbaan aasui mɔmɔk yɔl. 16M yaa tur bu lii kitekpiitiŋ ni kan, bu aah ga lir pu na ga dam ŋitimbol. Edenn aatiŋ aasui mɔmɔk, ni Lebanonn aachook aasunyaan i mɔmɔk sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni na aasui ga piir bu aalirm pu. 17I ga dii bu buen ti kpee isui i puun lir na pu. Le binib bi mɔmɔk ka bu aaboon ni na ga yaa koo ŋitimbol ŋiken ni.
18“Busub ngbaan le ye Ijipt aabɔr ni waanib mɔmɔk. Hali isui i nan bi Edenn aatiŋ ni na aa nan fɔk ki kpa kina aanyaan. Tɔ, n‑yoonn mue na, bu ga sunn kitekpiitiŋ ni ke Edenn aatiŋ aasui na, ki ti kpee binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na, ni baah ku binib bi butɔb ponn ni na pu. Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for the King of Egypt
1Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying:
You act like a lion
roaming the earth;
but you are nothing more than
a crocodile in a river,
churning up muddy water
with your feet.
3King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore. 4I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh. 5I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys, 6and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams. 7 I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining. 8The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
9Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you. 10They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
11The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt! 12Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed. 13I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water. 14The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
15Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
16This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
A Sad Ending for Egypt
17On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations. 19Say to them:
You may be more beautiful
than the people
of other nations,
but you will also die
and join the godless
in the world below.
20You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you. 21Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
22-23The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
24-25The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
26The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle. 27They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
28You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
29The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
30The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
31The Lord God says:
When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering. 32I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah di Ijipt aabɔr ŋaŋ unyiib pu na
1Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni lileler ponn ni aaŋmapiik ni ilee aajan aawiin daal, le Uwumbɔr len m chee tibɔr, 2ki bui ke, “Unibɔn, di nsakm kpaan tii Ijipt aabɔr. Di maanaŋ imina tii u: Aa ŋani ke saah ye uchinn na le ŋitimbol ŋiken chee, ki mu tee naahn unyiib u yuk lir limɔɔl ni na. Aa joo aataa gbir nnyun ki bii ŋimɔɔ aanyun. 3Ŋitimbol pam yaa kuun ni kan, m ga di maapɔɔk chuu si, ki cha ŋi dar si nyan ni nnyun aagbaan. 4M ga di si mee bil kitiŋ ki cha dulnyaa aanyoon, ni ipeel di si ŋa yaajikaar. 5M ga di saawon ti bur na gbiin ŋijoo ni tifatann mɔmɔk pu. 6M ga di saasin kpir le mu ti biin ŋijoo ni ikpen mɔmɔk pu. 7M yaa nan kuln si kan, m ga biin kitaapaak pu ki nyan iŋmabi. Nwiin ga bɔr ntaalangbam aapuwɔb, le uŋmal aan ki li wiin. 8M ga junn iwiihn i mɔmɔk bi paacham na, ki cha mbɔmbɔɔn gaa saatiŋ. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.
9“Ŋitimbol pam aasui ga bii buyoonn m di saalirm aabɔr moon ŋitingban ŋi mɔmɔk ponn ni saa kee ŋun ŋi pu na. 10Maah ga ŋa si pu na ga chuu ŋitimbol pam ijawaan. M yaa fiin maajaak aajuk kan, bibɔrb aawon ga li gbaa kpakpab ijawaan pu la. Nwiin mundaal aa lir na kan, bi mɔmɔk ga li si jii ni ijawaan, bibaa aamɔfal pu.”
11Tidindaan Uwumbɔr tuk Ijipt aabɔr ke, “Babiloŋ aabɔr aajaak aajuk ga pii si. 12M ga cha ŋitimbol ŋi kaa san kinimbaak na aatɔb aajab fuur baajaak aajum ki ku saanib mɔmɔk. Saanib mɔmɔk ni tiwan ni mɔmɔk aa mak ni pu na ga kuln. 13M ga kɔr kɔr saawakor nnyun aabuul mɔmɔk ni. Binib ni tiwakor aan ki li bi ki gbir nnyun. 14M ga cha saanyun mɔmɔk teŋ ki ŋa chain, ki cha saamɔɔ li puu suuna. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. 15M yaa cha Ijipt aatiŋ kpaln tilangbenn ki doon nkuun, ki kuln binib bi mɔmɔk koo nima chee na kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 16Nsakm kpaan mumina ga kpaln nkpolahn la. Ŋitimbol aapiib ga di mu wii Ijipt aatiŋ, ni kaanib mɔmɔk aakpuul. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Kitekpiitiŋ aabɔr
17Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni lileler ponn ni aajan aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni iŋmu daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr. 18U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, li wii Ijipt aanib mɔmɔk pu. Di bi ni ŋitimbol ŋi kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na buen kitekpiitiŋ ni.” 19Tuk bi ke,
“Ni dak ke ni ŋan jer unii mɔmɔk la aa?
Ni ga sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni
ki ti doon binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na chee.
20“Ijipt aatiŋ aanib, ni binib bi kpoi butɔb ni na ga kpaan lir. Kijaak aajuk gor ke ki ku bi mɔmɔk. 21Bijakaab kpaam na, ni bijab bi nan ter Ijipt yaab na ga gaa Ijipt yaab kitekpiitiŋ ni iŋaal ilee. Bi ga li tar ke, ‘Binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr aan ki nan kpoi butɔb ni na sunn ni do, le ki ga li dɔ do.’
22“Asiria aatiŋ, ni kaatɔb aajab aakaakul bi nima. Bi nan ku bi mɔmɔk butɔb ni la, 23le baakaakul bi kitekpiitiŋ aapepel li nyoo sakpen na ni. Asiria aatɔb aajab mɔmɔk nan lir butɔb ni, le baakaakul mann goln uyaal. Tɔ, bi mu nan tee faan binifuub aatiŋ sakpen.
24“Elam aatiŋ bi nima, le kaatɔb aajab aakaakul mann goln ki. Bi nan ku bi mɔmɔk butɔb ni la, le bi di ŋichakpamun sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni. Baamɔfal ponn ni, bi nan cha ijawaan bi ni kookoo, tɔ, dandana ma bi kpo dɔ inimɔɔn ŋmeen la. 25Elam aatiŋ dɔ ŋmal baah ku binib bi butɔb ni na la, le kaatɔb aajab aakaakul mann goln ki ni mɔmɔk. Bi mɔmɔk aa gii ŋichakpan, bi ku bi mɔmɔk butɔb ni la. Baamɔfal ponn ni, bi nan cha ijawaan bi ni kookoo, tɔ, dandana ma bi kpo dɔ inimɔɔn ŋmeen la, le bi ni binib bi kpoi butɔb ni na yakr ndoon baan.
26“Mesek ni Tubal aatim bi nima, mu aatɔb aajab aakaakul mann goln mu. Bi mɔmɔk aa gii ŋichakpan, le bi ku bi mɔmɔk butɔb ni. Tɔ, bi nan cha ijawaan chuu binifuub n‑yoonn mubaa. 27Baa nan sub bi liyimbil aasum ke baah nan sub n‑yaayoonn na aajakaab bi bi nan di baajawan sub bi chee aan bi di buen kitekpiitiŋ ni na. Baajaak aajum nan kul biyil, le baajaak aapen bii biwon pu. Bijakaab bimina nan kpa mpɔɔn n‑yoonn mubaa, ki nan cha ijawaan chuu binifuub.
28“Kina le Ijipt yaab ga wɔi ki doon ŋmal binib bi kaa gii ŋichakpan ki nan kpoi butɔb ni na ni.
29“Edom aatiŋ, ni kaabɔrb, ni bijojoob bi nima chee. Bi nan ye butɔb aajab bi kpa mpɔɔn na la, le ki gur dɔ kitekpiitiŋ ni, ki ŋmal binib bi kaa gii ŋichakpan ki nan kpoi butɔb ni na ni.
30“Ŋŋangan wɔb aayidam mɔmɔk bi nima, le Saidonn yaab mu bi nima. Baapɔɔn nan cha ijawaan bi ni kookoo n‑yoonn mubaa, tɔ, dandana ma bi di inimɔɔn koo likaakul ni, le bi ni binib bi nan kpoi butɔb ni na kpaan dii ti doon lifuur ni, kaa gii ŋichakpan. Bi ni binib bi sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni na yakr inimɔɔn baan la.
31“Ijipt aabɔr ni waatɔb aajab yaa yaar kan binib bi mɔmɔk kpoi butɔb ni na kan, bisui ga sɔŋ.” Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.
32“M cha Ijipt aabɔr ŋa binifuub mbiin sakpen, tɔ, bi ga ku u ni waatɔb aajab mɔmɔk, aan bi sub bi binib bi mɔmɔk aa geei ŋichakpan ki kpoi butɔb ni na chee.” Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

english_text:
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 3.16-21)
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying:
Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch 3and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming. 4-5If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
6But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
7Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 8When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death. 9If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
The Lord Is Always Fair
(Ezekiel 18.21-30)
10The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me. 11Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
12Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
13Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
14Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right. 15For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live. 16Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
17Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair. 18If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned. 19And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 20But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done.
The News of Jerusalem's Fall
21 Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
22The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak.
What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
23Then the Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
25So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying:
How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder 26and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
27As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases. 28I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them. 29I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The People Listen, but Don't Change
The Lord said:
30Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.” 31So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money. 32They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
33Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah di Esekiel ŋa ukikiir pu na
(Esekiel 3.16-21)
1Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke, 2“Unibɔn, bui saanib maah joo ni butɔb kitiŋ pu kan, tiwan ni ŋani na. Litingbaln ngbaan aanib nyan ni bi ponn ni ubaa le u ye ukikiir. 3U yaa kan ke bidim choo kan, le u faa nkuun ke unii mɔmɔk bee. 4Unii yaa ŋun nkuun ngbaan pu kaa gar, aan bidim ngbaan nan ku udaan kan, u yeh ubaa aakun aagalm. 5Uma le ku ubaa; ba pu? u ŋun nkuun pu le kaa gar. U yaa ba gar kan, u ba ga san ŋmar. 6Tɔ, ni yaa ye ke ukikiir na kan bidim aah choo pu na kaa faa nkuun kan, bidim ngbaan ga dan ki nan ku titunwanbirdam ngbaan, le m ga chuu ukikiir ngbaan taani baakun pu.
7“Tɔ, unibɔn, m di si ŋa Israel aatimbol aakikiir la. Aa di nsakm mu m di tii si na nabr bi. 8M yaa len ke utunwanbirdaan ga kpo, le saa sak u ke u kpeln waabimbin aan ki ŋmar kan, u ga kpo, ki beenin ye utunwanbirdaan, le m ga chuu si taani waakun pu. 9Aa yaa sak utunwanbirdaan, le u yii kaa kpeln waabimbin kan, u ga kpo ki beenin ye utunwanbirdaan, le aa ma ga ŋmar.”
Unii mɔk ni waatuln
10Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke, “Unibɔn, giin di Israel yaab aah bi len pu na tuk bi ke: ‘Timi aatunwanbir ni timi aataani le nyii baa ti pu. Ti door la. Ti ga ŋa kinye ki li kpa limɔfal?’ 11Tuk bi ke min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, maa neen ke m kan utunwanbirdaan aah kpo pu na. M tee ga li neen ke u di cha titunwanbir ki li kpa limɔfal. Israel yaab, di cha titunwanbir ti ni tun na. Ba ŋa ni ban ke ni kpo?
12“Tɔ, unibɔn, tuk Israel yaab ke uninyaan yaa tun titunwanbir kan, waatunyaan aan ŋmaa gaa u lii. Titunwanbirdaan yaa di cha titunwanbir aatuln kan, waan kan ntafadaan; le uninyaan yaa piin titunwanbir aatum kan, u ga lann waamɔfal. 13M ga ŋmaa puu limɔfal aapuur tii uninyaan, tɔ, u yaa piin ki dak ke waajan aatunyaan na ŋeer, ki piin ki tun titunwanbir kan, maan ki teer waajan aatunyaan ŋi u nan tun na bɔr. U ga kpo waatunwanbir pu. 14Nibaakan, m ga sak utunwanbirdaan ke u ga kpo, tɔ, u yaa di cha titunwanbir aatum, ki gur tun ni ŋan na kan, u ga ŋmar; 15nibaakan, u yaa giin waah nan gaa tiwan ni unii u pinn u chee ŋimombil na, bee u yaa giin tiwan ni u sun na, ki yaa di cha titunwanbir, ki dii ikaal i tii limɔfal na kan, waan kpo, u ga ŋmar. 16M ga di cha pinn u waatunwanbir ti u tun na, u ga li kpa limɔfal, ba pu? u ŋa tiwan ni tok ki ŋan na.
17“Nimi aanib le len ke maa ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na. Aayii, bima aasan le aa ŋan. 18Uninyaan yaa di cha litunyaan aatum ki piin titunwanbir aatum kan, u ga kpo kina pu. 19Utunwanbirdaan yaa di cha titunwanbir ki ŋa tiwan ni tok ki ŋan na kan, u kan waamɔfal a. 20Tɔ, Israel yaab, ni bui ke maah ŋani pu na aa ŋan. M ban m ji nimi tibɔr naah tun pu na pu la.”
Jerusalem aalirm aabɔr aah nyan pu na
21Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni lileler ponn ni aaŋmapiik aawinŋmu daal, le uja u nan san ŋmar Jerusalem aatiŋ ni na nan tuk mi ke kitiŋ ngbaan lir a. 22Kijook ki woln aan u nin fuu ni na, m nan kan ke Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn sakpiin dan m pu. Naah woln kichakpiik ni aan uja ngbaan fuu ni na, le Uwumbɔr nan ki lɔkr nlambil ke m len tibɔr.
Binib ngbaan aatunwanbir
23Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke, 24“Unibɔn, binib bi bi Israel aatiŋ aalangbenn ni na bi len ke: ‘Abraham nan ye unibaan la, le Uwumbɔr nan di kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk tii u. Timi le wiir, kina pu na, kitiŋ ngbaan ye timi yaak la.’
25“Tuk bi min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na: Ni ŋmɔ tinann ti nsin aa nyan ti ponn ni na. Ni dooni ŋiwaa. Ni ku binib. Ba cha ni dak ke kitiŋ ngbaan ye nimi yaak? 26Ni mak nimi aajaak aajum pu la. Nimi aabimbin sukr ponn ni la. Unii mɔmɔk gɔr kidagook la. Ba cha ni dak ke kitiŋ ngbaan ye nimi yaak?
27“Tuk bi ke min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr sak bi ke maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, bi ga ku binib bi koo tilangbenn aatim ngbaan ni na. Ipeel le ga ŋmɔ binib bi koo itingbaan ni na. Iween mu le ga ku binib bi bɔr ŋijoo ni titakpalunn ni na. 28M ga cha kitiŋ ngbaan kpaln kitikuun ki kaa kpa nibaa na, le mpɔɔn mu bi nan mak mu pu sakpen na ga doo. Israel aajoo pu ga li bir sakpen, le ubaa aan dii ŋi chee ki jer. 29M yaa daa binib ngbaan aatafal baatunwanbir pu ki cha kitiŋ ngbaan doon nkuun kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”
Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr aabɔr aah joo ni pu na
30Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “Unibɔn, saanib len saabɔr buyoonn bi kuun kitiŋ aagon chee na, ni baadichal aabisamɔi chee na. Bi len tɔb chee ke, ‘Cha ti buen ti pel ke ba aamɔboln nyan ni Uwumbɔr chee n‑yoonn mue.’ 31Kina pu na, maanib kuuni ke bi nan ŋun saah kpa pu aa len na, kaa tee ŋani saah tuk bi ke bi ŋa pu na. Ngeehm aabɔlen le bi bimɔi ni, le bi tee beenin dii baakumɔŋ aasan. 32Bima chee kan, aa po ye unii u gaa ngeehm aalahn, bee aa gbaa kibeek mmɔɔn pu na la. Bi pel saamɔbon mɔmɔk ki mu aa tee ŋani ŋi ponn ni libaa aah len pu na. 33Tɔ, saamɔbon mɔmɔk ngbaan sil ga gbiin. Ŋi mɔmɔk yaa nan gbiin kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr nan sil bi bikaasisik ni.”

english_text:
Israel's Leaders Are Worthless Shepherds
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them:
I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep. 3You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock! 4You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep. 5 They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals. 6So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
7-8Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep. 9-10So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
11The Lord God then said:
I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself, 12just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them 13and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields. 14They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills. 15I promise to take care of them and keep them safe, 16to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right.
Judgment on the Strong Sheep
17The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel:
I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak. 18Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy. 19That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
20So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak. 21You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak, 22but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
23 After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you. 24 He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep
The Lord God said:
25The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid. 26They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain 27to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord. 28Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear. 29I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners. 30Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise. 31They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_text:
Israel yaab aapihdam
1Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr. 2U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, len tibɔbir Israel aajojoob pu. Nabr maabɔr tuk bi, ki bui bi min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk bi pu na: Nimi Israel aapihdam, nimɔfal junn a. Ni kpiini nibaa la, kaa kpiini ipiih na. 3Ni nyu yaabiin, ki peeni yaakor aawanpeenkaan, ki kɔr ki ŋmɔ ipiih i ŋan sakpen na. Tɔ, naa tee kpiini ipiih ngbaan. 4Nitafal aa bi ipiih i kaa pɔɔ na ni; naa sɔŋ ipiih i bun na aaween, kaa poo i kan titotonn na aabuun, kaa ban kani i yenn na, kaa ban kani i wɔŋ na. Ni tee labr le ki ŋani i mbiin. 5Ipiih ngbaan aah kaa kpa upihdaan na, le i yaa, le ipeel chur i ki di i ŋman. 6Kina pu na, maapiih nan chuun kpak ŋigongon ŋi paa na, ni ŋijoo pu. I nan yaa ki bi kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu, le ubaa aa nyan ke u ban i, ubaa mu aa pɔɔn ubaa ke u ban kan i.
7“Tɔ, nimi bipihdam, li pel man, min Uwumbɔr aah bi tuk nimi pu na. 8Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, ni yaa ŋun tii mi kan, ni ŋan. Upihdaan aah kaa bi na, le ipeel ti lir maapiih pu ki ku i ki ŋman i. Maapihkpaab aa pɔɔni bibaa ke bi ban kan ipiih ngbaan. Bitafal nan bi bibaa ni la, bitafal aa nan bi ipiih ni. 9Kina pu na, nimi bipihkpaab, li pel m chee man. 10Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len ke m ye nimi aadin la. M ga gaa maapiih ni chee, kaan ki cha ni li ye yaapihkpaab daalbaadaal; maan ki cha nitafal li bi nibaa ni daalbaadaal. M ga gaa maapiih ni chee lii, kaan cha ni ŋmɔ i.
Upihdaanyaan na
11“Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bui nimi ke min mbaa le ga ban kan maapiih ki li joo i 12ke upihdaan aah joo waapiih i nan yaa aan u ki kuun ni i na pu na. M ga kuun i nya ni yaah nan yaa libiil aawinbɔbɔɔn ngbaan daal ki bi nin chee na. 13M ga nyan ni i nwɔwɔtim ni, ki kuun ni i nan kpaan, ki giin ni i yaatiŋ pu. M ga di i giin buen Israel aajoo, ni ikpen chee, ki ga cha i ŋmɔ timoor mmoŋmɔpaan mu ŋan na ni. 14M ga cha i ŋmɔ timoor lifuur ni, ŋijoo aamoŋmɔpaan, ni tifatann, ni Israel aatiŋ aamosɔnn mɔmɔk ni. 15Min mbaa le ga li ye maapiih aapihkpaal, le m ga ban nin chee i ga fuur na tii i. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.
16“M ga ban ipiih i wɔŋ na, ki giin ni i yenn na, ki poo i kan titotonn na aabuun, ki cha i bun na pɔɔk; le ipiih i filk ki pɔɔ na, m ga kuln ima, ba pu? m ye upihdaan u tun tiwan ni ŋan na la.
17“Tɔ, nimi maawakor, min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le tuk nimi ke m ga ji ni mɔmɔk tibɔr, ki gann i ŋan na, i kaa ŋan na chee, ki gann ipiih, iŋoob ni. 18Nimi nibaa aa faar yaah ŋman timonyaan ti na; hali ni taa kool ti naa ŋman na la. Ni nyu nnyun mu ŋan na, le ki taa gbir mu naa nyu na. 19Maapiih iken na ŋmɔ timoor ti ni taa kool na, le ki nyu nnyun mu ni taa gbir na.
20“Kina pu na, min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bui nimi ke m ga gann nimi ipiih i pɔɔ na, ni i kaa pɔɔ na. 21Ni tur ipiih i bun na nyan ngbaan ki saar nyani i ipiih iken ni. 22Tɔ, m ga gaa maapiih lii kaan ki cha ubaa ŋa i mbiin. M ga lik maapiih mɔk mbamɔm ki gann i ŋan na, i kaa ŋan na ponn ni. 23M ga tii i upihkpaal ke maatutunn David na, aan uma baanja li ye yaapihkpaal, le u ga li joo i mbamɔm. 24Min Uwumbɔr le ga li ye Yaawumbɔr, le ubɔr u ga li bi ke maatutunn David na li ye yaajojoor. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina. 25M ga puu tipuur ti ga mɔk ke i ga li bi ŋŋmarm ni na tii i. M ga jenn nyan tipeewanbir mɔmɔk kitiŋ ngbaan ni, aan maapiih ga ŋmaa li bi ikpaakon, ni ŋŋmarm ni, ki doo tichoor ni.
26“M ga ŋa maanyoor ŋa i pu ki cha i li bi maagongoln li bi chain na pu. Nima chee, le i yaa ban utaal kan, m ga tii i yaah ban pu na. 27Isui ga lu ŋisubil, tisar ga ŋa tijikaar, le unii mɔmɔk ga li bi waatiŋ pu, ŋŋmarm ni. M yaa kii maanib aakululn ki gaa bi binib bi nan di bi ŋa binaagbiib na chee lii kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 28Ŋitimbol ŋi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na aan ki yoor baawangol buen, le tipeewanbir mu aan ki ku bi ki ŋmɔ bi. Bi ga li bi ŋŋmarm ni, le ubaa aan ki cha ijawaan chuu bi. 29M ga tii bi ikpaakon i nyuun na, ki kuln nkon kitiŋ ngbaan pu. Ŋitimbol ŋiken na aan ki laa bi daalbaadaal. 30Unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le kii Israel aanib, le bi ye maanib. Min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
31Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Nimi maapiih, kipihpaak ki m kpiini na le ye maanib, le m ye nimi Aawumbɔr.”

english_text:
Edom Will Be a Wasteland
1 The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom 3and say to them:
I, the Lord God,
am now your enemy!
And I will turn your nation
into an empty wasteland,
4leaving your towns in ruins.
Your land will be a desert,
and then you will know
that I am the Lord.
5People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins. 6And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death. 7I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it. 8Dead bodies will cover your mountains and fill up your valleys, 9and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
10You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God, 11and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you! 12And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take. 13You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
14Everyone on earth will celebrate when I destroy you, 15just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah ga daa Edom aatiŋ aatafal pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr. 2U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, lik Edom aatiŋ wɔb ki len tibɔbir lii ki pu. 3Tuk kaanib min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi len pu na:
Edom aajoo, m ye nimi aadin la.
M ga ŋa si kitikuun ki bi fam na.
4M ga cha saatim kpaln tilangbenn,
ki cha saatiŋ doon nkuun;
le aa bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.
5“Aa nan ye Israel aatiŋ aadin n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la, le ki cha binib ku kaanib kaabɔbir aayoonn mu nan ye kaatunwanbir aakookoo aatafadaan na. 6Kina pu na, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu na, saadoon le ye nkun, le saan nya mu ni. Aa jin linikul aabɔkpol, le linikul ga li dii si. 7M ga ŋa sin Edom aatiŋ ki ye ligongoln aatiŋ na fam, ki ga ku unii umɔk dii ki ponn ni jer na. 8M ga di ŋinikpol gbiin ŋijoo pu, le baah ku binib bi butɔb ni na aanikpol ga gbiin ŋigongon, ni tifatann ni. 9M ga cha aa doon nkuun ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, le ubaa aan ki koo saatim ni daalbaadaal. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.
10“Aa bui ke ŋitimbol ŋilee, Juda ni Israel, ki kpee ŋaatim mɔmɔk ye sin yaan le aa ga li joo ŋi, ki nyi gbin gbin ke min Uwumbɔr le ye Baawumbɔr. 11Kina pu na, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, m ga teen si saaŋuul, ni lipiipoln, ni saananaŋ ki aa kpa maanib pu na. Bi ga li nyi ke saah ŋa bi pu na pu le m dar aatafal. 12N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr nan ŋun saah di lik‑seen bui ke Israel aajoo ŋa nkuun, ki ye sin yaan ke aa di nab na. 13M ŋun saah nan di kiwaatiik, ni kipupuk len m pu pu na.”
14Dindaan Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M ga cha aa doon nkuun ki ti nyaŋ, le dulnyaa mɔmɔk aasui piir saalirm pu, 15ke aasui aah nan piir Israel aatimbol li ye min yaan na aalirm pu pu na. Seir aajoo, mbamɔn, Edom aatiŋ mɔmɔk ga doon nkuun. N‑yoonn ngbaan le unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
A Message for Israel's Mountains
1The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel 2that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them. 3They ruined and crushed you from every side, and foreign nations captured and made fun of you. 4So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you. 5But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands. 6You have suffered long enough, and, I, the Lord God, am very angry! Nations have insulted you, 7so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
8Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home. 9I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes. 10The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them. 11Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
12I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve. 13It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve. 14-15But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Lord Will Be Honored
16The Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean. 18They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people 19and scattered them throughout the nations, just as they deserved. 20Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
21I care what those foreigners think of me, 22so tell the Israelites that I am saying:
You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name 23and to show foreign nations that I am holy. Then they will know that I am the Lord God. I have spoken.
24I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home. 25I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols. 26 I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts, 27because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings. 28You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
29I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve. 30Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food. 31You will remember your evil ways and hate yourselves for what you've done. 32People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
33After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them. 34Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren. 35Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people. 36Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
37I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep. 38The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah ŋa waanyoor ŋa Israel aatiŋ pu pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Unibɔn, len Israel aajoo chee tibɔr ki tuk ŋi ke ŋi li pel 2min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah kpa pu m tuk ŋi na: Israel aatiŋ aadim nan di kikumɔŋ lik ki, ki len ke, ‘Timi gur yeh n‑yaayoonn na aagongon ngbaan.’
3“Tɔ, nabr maabɔr ki moon min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi len pu na. Ŋitimbol ŋiken ŋi bi gbɔk Israel aatimbol na aah nan nyaŋ ki yoor Israel aajoo aawan na, ŋi mɔmɔk nan sii Israel la. 4Kina pu na, li pel min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk ŋijoo ni ŋigongon ngbaan, ni ikpen, ni tifatann, ni ŋipepel ŋi bii na, ni nimi ntim mu kpaln tilangbenn aan ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln nimi na nan yoor nimi aawan buen ki jinn nimi inimɔɔn na:
5“Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len tibɔbir ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln Israel na pu, ni Edom aatimbol mɔmɔk pu. Maaŋuul ponn ni le m len kina; ba pu? bi nan di mpopiin ni lik‑seen gaa maatiŋ Israel ni kaamoŋmɔpaan.
6“Kina pu na, nabr maabɔr tii Israel aatiŋ; bui ŋijoo, ni ŋigongon, ni ikpen, ni tifatann na min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu, lipiipoln ni liŋuul ni, ŋitimbol ngbaan aasiibil ni mbɔnyun mu ŋa na pu. 7Min, Dindaan Uwumbɔr puu tipuur kpaan ke ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln Israel na ga ji inimɔɔn. 8Tɔ, isui i bi Israel aajoo pu na ga toŋ tifar ki lu ŋisubil tii nimi maanib Israel yaab. Ni ga kun ni linampal dandana. 9M si nichaŋ ni, m ga kan ke bi kon nimi aatim ki bun njikaabim mu pu. 10M ga cha ni moo pɔr kpee. Ni ga li koo ntikpaam ni, ki gir maa tiwan ni mɔmɔk nan gur ye tilangbenn na. 11M ga cha binib ni tiwakor moo pɔr kpee. Ni ga wiir jer n‑yaayoonn na, le ki ga kan mbim pam. M ga cha ni li koo nima chee ke naah nan koo pu na, ki ga cha ni kan liwangol ki jer naah kaa kee kan pu na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le ni ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 12M ga giin ni nimi maanib Israel yaab, ni nan ki li koo kitiŋ ngbaan pu. Ki ga li ye nimi nibaa aatiŋ, le kaan ki cha nkon ku nimi aabim.
13“Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke: Ni ye mbamɔn ke binib yin kitiŋ ngbaan ke unikur, ki len ke ki ku litimbol ngbaan aabim. 14Tɔ, ki nya n‑yoonn mue ki joo cha, kaan ki li ye unikur u ku nimi aabim na. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. 15Kitiŋ ngbaan aan ki pel ŋitimbol aah ŋani ki mbɔnyun, bee ki kan binib aah laa kinanaŋ aalaar ti na. Kitiŋ ngbaan aan ki ku litimbol ngbaan aabim. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Israel yaab aabimbipɔm aabɔr
16Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr. 17U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, Israel yaab aah nan koo baatiŋ ni na, bi nan di baabimbin ni baah tun pu na le bii kaayimbil. Nsui nan gar baabimbin mu kaa nan bi chain ke upii u bi waaŋmal aapiir ni na aah kaa bi chain pu na pu. 18M nan cha bi kan maaŋuul aah bir pu na, baah nan ku binib bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na, ni baah nan di ŋiwaa ŋi bii ki na. 19M galn bi baabimbin ni baah nan tun pu na pu, le ki cha bi yaa koo biwɔwɔm aatingbaln ni. 20Baah nan buen nin chee mɔmɔk na, bi nan jinn maayimbil li bi chain na inimɔɔn la; ba pu? binib nan len le ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aanib sɔ, tɔ, ni nan ŋa ke bi nya waatiŋ ni.’ 21Nima le m cha ni muk mi maayimbil li ye chain na pu, ba pu? Israel yaab nan jinn li inimɔɔn nin chee bi buen na.
22“Tɔ, di inaŋ i min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr joo tii bi na tuk bi ke: Maah ban m ŋa pu na aa ye nimi Israel yaab pu, maayimbil li ye chain aan ni jinn li inimɔɔn nin chee mɔmɔk ni buen na pu le m ban m ŋa. 23M yaa mɔk ŋitimbol maayimbil li ni jinn li inimɔɔn ŋi ponn ni na aah ye chain pu na kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. Min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. 24M ga nyan ni nimi litimbol, ni kitiŋ mɔmɔk ni, ki giin nimi nibaa aatiŋ pu. 25M ga di nnyunyaan le yaa yaa ni pu ki nyan nimi, nimi aawaa mɔmɔk, ni tiwan ni mɔmɔk bii nimi na aajɔŋ ni. 26M ga tii nimi nsuupɔɔn ni nlandak pɔɔn. M ga chuu nyan nimi aatakpal aatafalaaŋun aasui na ki tii nimi nsui mu ye ŋuntii aasui na. 27M ga di Maafuur Nyaan ŋa ni ponn ni aan ki cha ni li joo maakaal, ni maah mɔk nimi ke ni li ŋani pu na mɔmɔk. 28N‑yoonn ngbaan le ni ga koo kitiŋ ki m nan di tii niyaajatiib na ni. Ni ga li ye maanib, le m ye nimi Aawumbɔr. 29M ga nyan nimi tiwan ni mɔmɔk bii nimi na ni. M ga bui njikaabim le mu ŋa mbamɔm, le naan ki kan nkon daalbaadaal. 30M ga cha nimi aasubil aasui moo lu, ki cha nimi aasar mu pɔr, aan nkon taa ki li bi ki jinn nimi inimɔɔn ŋitimbol ŋiken chee. 31Ni ga teer nimi aatunwanbir, ni taani u ni ŋa na, le niponn ni ga li sukr nibaa pu, naah tun titunwanbir, ni mbiin mu ni ŋa na pu. 32Israel aanib, m ban ke ni li nyi ke naa ye nimi pu le m ŋani nimina. M ban ke ni ji inimɔɔn naah ŋani tiwan ni pu na la. Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
33Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M yaa ŋa nimi chain nimi aatunwanbir pu kan, m ga cha ni ki koo nimi aatim ni, ki cha ni ki gir maa ntim mu ye tilangbenn na. 34Unii umɔk nan jer nimi aakpaakon chee na nan kan yaa ŋa timoor ki bii pu na, tɔ, m ga cha ni ki gir ko i. 35Unii mɔmɔk ga len kitiŋ ki nan ye kipɔɔk sakpeŋ na aah kpaln tisar ke Edenn aatiŋ aasaak na, ki len ntim mu binib nan ber, ki yoor mu aawan ki cha mu tilangbenn na aah gur ye binib ŋmeen ki pɔɔk na aabɔr. 36Le ŋitimbol ŋi bi gbɔk ki ŋmar na ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr le ki gir maa tilangbenn aatim, ki ki bun njikaabim ikpaakon i nan dɔ fam na ni. Min Uwumbɔr le puu ke m ga ŋa nimina, ki sil ga ŋa.”
37Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “M ga cha Israel yaab ki gir ban m chee nterm, m ga cha bi moo pɔr ke kipihpaak na. 38Ntim mu ye tilangbenn dandana na ga gbiin binib ke Jerusalem aatiŋ aah nan gbii ipiih i bi nan joo toor njim aatork na pu na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Dry Bones Live Again
1Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones. 2The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out. 3He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?”
I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
4He then told me to say:
Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you, 5“I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live. 6I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
7I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together! 8I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
9The Lord said:
Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
10 As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
11The Lord said:
Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future. 12So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel, 13and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord. 14My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.”
Judah and Israel Together Again
15The Lord said:
16Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.” 17Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick. 18And when your people ask you what this means, 19tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
20Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone 21and then say:
I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live. 22I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations. 23They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
24-25 Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did. 26I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time, 27 and I will live among my people and be their God. 28Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_text:
Ikpab aafataŋ aabɔr
1M nan bee ke Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn sakpiin koo m ni, le Waafuur Nyaan yoor mi ti siin kifataŋ ki ponn ni ye ikpab ŋmeen na. 2U nan di mi mann kifataŋ ngbaan ki ti ton, le m kan ke ikpab pam nan dɔ nima ki kuun wɔk wɔk. 3U nan baa mi ke, “Unibɔn, ikpab imina ga ki ŋmaa fikr aa?”
M nan gar u ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, sin baanja le ga ŋmaa tii ngarm ngbaan.”
4U nan len ke, “Nabr maabɔr tuk ikpab ngbaan. Bui ikpabkuun imina ke i pel Uwumbɔr aamɔboln. 5Tuk i ke min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le bui i ke m ban m di kifuurk ŋa ni ponn ni le ki ki tii nimi limɔfal. 6M ga tii nimi ŋigiinjal ni tigir, ki ban tiwon aagban biin ni pu. M ga di kifuurk ŋa ni ponn ni ki ki giin ni nimi limɔfal ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”
7Le m nan nabr tibɔr ngbaan waah tuk mi pu na. Maah bi len kina na, le m ŋun kifuuk ki weeni na, le ikpab ngbaan piin ki bi toŋni. 8Maah si lik na, ŋigiinjal, ni tigir nan baan baan ikpabkuun ngbaan pu, le tiwon aagban biin i pu. Tɔ, kifuurk mu aa nan bi tiwon ngbaan ni.
9Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke, “Unibɔn, nabr maabɔr tuk libuln. Tuk libuln ke Dindaan Uwumbɔr len ke li nya ŋipepel mɔmɔk, ki nan fuur lii ŋinikpol ŋimina pu, ki ki giin ni ŋi limɔfal ni.”
10Kina pu na, waah nan tuk mi pu na, m nan nabr kina. Kifuurk nan koo tiwon ngbaan ni, le ti fikr ki fii sil. Bi nan wiir pam, ki ga ŋeer butɔb aajab.
11Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke, “Unibɔn, Israel aanib bi ke ikpab imina na la. Bi len ke bi kuur la, ke baa ki kpa limakl libaa, kaa kpa fen u choo na. 12Kina pu na, nabr maabɔr tuk maanib Israel yaab, ki tuk bi ke min Dindaan Uwumbɔr ban m chuu biir baakaakul la. M ban m chuu nyan ni bi le ki di bi giin ni Israel aatiŋ pu. 13M yaa chuu biir ŋikaakul ŋi ponn ni bi di maanib sub na ki nyan ni bi kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 14M ga di Maafuurk ŋa bi ponn ni, ki ki giin ni bi limɔfal ni, ki cha bi li koo bima bibaa aatiŋ ni. Le bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. M puu ke m ga ŋa nimina, ki ga sil ŋa. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Juda ni Israel aah ga ŋa litimbol libaa pu na
15Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr. 16U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, ban lidabil ki ŋmee ŋibɔbil ŋimina li pu ke, ‘Juda aanaan,’ ki ki yoor liken ki ŋmee ŋibɔbil ŋimina li mu pu ke, ‘Israel aanaan.’ 17Di ŋidabil ŋilee ngbaan toŋ tɔb pu ki li joo ŋi ke lidabil libaa na. 18Saanib yaa bui si ke aa tuk bi nimina aatataa kan, 19tuk bi ke min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr ga yoor lidabil li si Israel aasisii na ki di kpaan Juda yaal chee. M ga di ŋidabil ŋilee ngbaan ŋa lidabil libaa, ki di li ŋum ŋŋaal ni.
20“Yoor ŋidabil ŋilee ngbaan aaŋaal ni aan binib ngbaan li waa ŋi, 21ki tuk bi ke min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr ban m nyan maanib mɔmɔk ŋitimbol ŋi ponn ni bi buen na, ki kuun ni bi, ki giin ni bi bibaa aatiŋ pu. 22M ga cha bi ŋa unibaan Israel aajoo pu, kitiŋ ngbaan ni. Ubɔrbaan le ga li joo bi, le baan ki yakr ki li ye ŋitimbol ŋilee, kaan ki yakr nnaan mulee pu. 23Baan ki di ŋiwaa ŋi sukr ponn ni na bii bibaa, kaan di titunwanbir bii baabimbin. M ga gaa bi mbimbin mu mɔmɔk ponn ni bi tun titunwanbir ki nya mpuwɔb na. M ga finn nyan bi tijɔŋ ni; bi ga li ye maanib, le m li ye Baawumbɔr. 24Ubɔr u bi ke maatutunn David na le ga li ye baabɔr. Bi mɔmɔk ga kpaan kimɔbaan ki li bi ujojoor baan aataab, ki ga li joo maakaal mbamɔm. 25Bi ga li bi kitiŋ ki m nan di tii maatutunn Jakob, nin chee biyaajatiib nan bi na. Bi ga li bi nima chee ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, le baabim ni biyaabitiib mɔmɔk mu ga li bi nima kina. Ubɔr u bi ke maatutunn David na le ga li joo bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. 26M ga puu tipuur ti ga tii bi lifuur ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na tii bi. M ga maa bi kaan, ki cha bi pɔr kpee, ki di Maadichal siin baatiŋ pu, nin chee li ga li bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. 27M ga li koo bi chee nima; m ga li ye Baawumbɔr, le bi li ye maanib. 28M yaa di Maadichal siin bikaasisik ni ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan le ŋitimbol ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr le lee Israel aanib ke bi li ye maanib.”

english_text:
Gog Invades Israel
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
3I, the Lord God, am your enemy, 4and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords. 5Your army includes soldiers from Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya, 6as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
7So keep your troops prepared to fight, 8because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land. 9But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
10When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan 11to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks. 12You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property. 13The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
14I, the Lord God, know that when you see my people Israel living in peace, 15you will lead your powerful cavalry from your kingdom in the north. 16You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy.
Judgment on Gog
17The Lord said to Gog:
Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming. 18When you invade Israel, I will become furious, 19and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel. 20Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse. 21I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other. 22I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur. 23I will do these things to show the world that I, the Lord, am holy.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah di Ubɔr Gog ŋa waajawan pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr. 2U nan len ke, “Unibɔn, lik Magog aatiŋ aanibol ŋi ye Mesek, ni Tubal aanibol na aajojookpaan Gog wɔb ki len tibɔbir lii u pu 3ki tuk u ke min Dindaan Uwumbɔr ye waadin la. 4M ga mur fenn u, ki di ijapiin saa chaar umɔkpaween, ki dar u ni waatɔb aajab buen. Waatɔb aajab, ni baataan, ni bitandam bi pee butɔb aawan na wiir sakpen, le uja mɔk joo kijaak aapeln, ni kijaak aajuk. 5Bijab nyan Pesia, ni Kus, ni Libia aatim ni ki bi u chee, ki joo kijaak aapen, ni tiyikpupur. 6Ŋŋangan wɔb aapepel aatim, Gomer, ni Bef Togama aajab bi u chee, bi mɔmɔk ye kijaak aajab la, le ŋitimbol ŋiken pam mu aajaak aajab bi u chee. 7Tuk u ke u di ubaa aamɔb gor waajab mɔmɔk. 8Ŋibin pam aapuwɔb le m ga bui u ke u ti di butɔb koo kitiŋ ki aanib nyan ni ŋitimbol pam ni ki gir ni, kaa nyi butɔb aajawan aan ni yunn na ni. U ga koo Israel aajoo ŋi bi nan san cha ŋi aan ŋi doon nkuun ki yunn, ki mu gur kpa binib bi bi lifuur ni na ni. 9U ni waajab, ni ŋitimbol pam ŋi bi u chee na ga ti tak ki ke kitaabuŋ na, ki biin kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu ke ntaalangbam na.”
10Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk ubɔr Gog pu na sɔ: “N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, aa ga piin ki bi dakl nlandak mu kaa ŋan na. 11Aa ga ŋa nlandak ke aa koo ti tak kitiŋ ki kaa kpa uteter ubaa aan kaanib bi nsuudoon, ni lifuur, ki koo ntim mu kaa kpa ŋigon ŋi ga ŋmaa kiir bidim na. 12Aa ga yoor ntim mu nan ye tilangbenn n‑yoonn mubaa na aanib aawan mpɔɔn buen. Bi kuun ki nyan ni ŋitimbol pam ni la, le ki kpa tiwakor, ni liwangol ki koo dulnyaa aasayakr aatiŋ ni. 13Seba aanib, ni Dedann aanib, ni Speenn aatim aawantiirb ga baa si ke, ‘Aa kuun saajab ki nan tak bi, ke ni yoor baawan mpɔɔn la aa? Aa ŋa nlandak ke aa kan tikunabr, ni salmaa, ni tiwakor, ni liwangol ki di nimina mɔmɔk buen la aa?’”
14Kina pu le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr tun mi ke m ti bui Ubɔr Gog waah bi tuk u pu na ke: “Maanib Israel yaab aah bi lifuur ni na, aa ga ŋmaa di 15saapepel li bi ŋŋangan wɔb dandar na aatɔb aajab bi wiir, ki kpa mpɔɔn, ki nyan ni ŋitimbol pam ni, ki dik itaan pu na nya sil. 16Aa ga tak maanib Israel yaab ke kitaabuŋ ki bɔ kitiŋ ponn ni ki jer na. N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, m ga cha aa ti koo maatiŋ ni ki di mɔk ŋitimbol maah ye Uwumbɔr u na, ki di maah joo si tun lituln li na mɔk maah ye chain pu na. 17Saabɔr le m nan len n‑yaayoonn na, ki cha maatutum, bi ye maabɔnabr ki nan bi Israel aatiŋ ni na moon, ke n‑yoonn choo le m ga nan cha unii ubaa tak Israel aatiŋ.” Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.
Uwumbɔr aah ga daa Ubɔr Gog aatafal pu na
18Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “Nwiin mundaal Ubɔr Gog ga koo Israel aatiŋ ni ki ti tak ki na, maaŋuul ga fii sakpen. 19Maaŋuul ngbaan ponn ni chob, le m ga cha kitiŋ dam ki puu Israel aatiŋ ni, ki li pɔɔ pam. 20Ujan mɔk, ni unyoon mɔk, ni kiwakork sakpeŋ ni kiwaatiir mɔmɔk, ni unibɔn u mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ pu na aawon ga li gbaa maatuln aajawaan pu. Ŋijoo ga lir, ŋijoomɔju ga wur lir, le ligoln mɔk ga lir. 21M ga di tibɔbir mɔmɔk aabɔŋ faan ubɔr Gog sakpen. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr len a. Waajab ga di baajaak aajum fenn lir tɔb pu. 22M ga di iween ni nkun le daa utafal. Utaal sakpiin ni ŋitaatakpabil, ki di kpee mmii, ni chirbil, ga lir ni u ni waajab, ni ŋitimbol ŋi wiir ki si uchaŋ ni na pu. 23Kina le m ga mɔk ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ke maapɔɔn nyaŋ, le m ye chain. N‑yoonn ngbaan le ŋi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

english_text:
Gog Is Defeated
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him:
You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy! 2I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel. 3I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand, 4 and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh 5of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
7My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel. 8The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
9When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years. 10They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees.
