21Maah nan beenin si lik na, le n‑yiin ngbaan to Uwumbɔr aanib butɔb ki nyaŋ bi. 22Le Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na dan ki nan di mbamɔn tii uma Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aanib. N‑yoonn nan fuu ni ke Uwumbɔr aanib ngbaan gaa nnaan aapɔɔn.
23Baah nan tuk mi naatataa pu na sɔ: “Upeel nanar ngbaan ye nnaan mu ga dan kitiŋ kee pu kaan li naahn nnaan muken na la. Mu ga wii kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk ki taa taa ki pu. 24Saah kan iyiin kipiik i na, i ŋaŋ bibɔrb kipiik bi ga ji nnaan ngbaan na la. Le ubɔr uken ga dan; u ni bibɔrb biken na aabimbin aan li kpaa, le ki ga nyaŋ bibɔrb bitaa. 25U ga sii Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na, ki muk uma Uwumbɔr waanib. U ga pɔɔn ubaa ke u kpeln baah dii isan i na, ni baajim aakuun mu, le Uwumbɔr aanib ga li bi waapɔɔn ni ki ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa ni ligeln. 26Le paacham aabɔjil ga kal ki ji tibɔr, ki gaa waapɔɔn, ki kuln u kookoo. 27Kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aanaan aapɔɔn mɔmɔk ga kpaln Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aanib aanaan la. Baanaan aapɔɔn aan li kpa ndoon, le dulnyaa wee ni aaninkpiib mɔmɔk ga tun baatuln ki kii baamɔi.”
28Maah nan ŋmee pu bil na le na. Ijawaan nan chuu mi sakpen, le nwon yɔl, le m nan di tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk ŋa nsui ni.

english_text:
Vision of a Ram and a Goat
1Daniel wrote:
In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision 2in which I was in Susa, the chief city of Babylonia's Elam Province. I was beside the Ulai River, 3when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first. 4The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
5I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn, 6and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river. 7The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help. 8After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
9A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land. 10 It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them. 11-12It humiliated heaven's army and dishonored its leader by keeping him from offering the daily sacrifices. In fact, it was so terrible that it even disgraced the temple and wiped out true worship. It also did everything else it wanted to do.
13Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
14The other answered, “It will be 2,300 evenings and mornings before the temple is dedicated and in use again.”
Gabriel Interprets the Vision
15Daniel wrote:
I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me. 16 And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
17Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
18While he was speaking, I fell facedown in a deep sleep. But he lifted me to my feet 19and said:
Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger. 20The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia, 21the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings. 22After this horn is broken, four other kingdoms will appear, but they won't be as strong.
23When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear. 24He will gain strength, but not on his own, and he will cause terrible destruction. He will wipe out powerful leaders and God's people as well. 25His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
26This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
27After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
translation_text:
Daniel aah daŋ tidaŋ ki kan upihja ni uŋoob pu na
1Ubɔr Belsasar aah nan ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa nnaan ni na, le m nan ki daŋ tidaŋ ki kan iwaan aawan lelee. 2Tidaŋ ngbaan ponn ni, m nan kan ke m si Susa, kitiŋ ki bi maa ligoln mann goln ki aan ki bi Elam aapepel ni na ni la. M nan si gbɔk Ulai Aamɔɔl la, 3le ki kan upihja u kpa iyiin ilee i fɔk na si gbɔk limɔɔl ngbaan. Waayiin ngbaan mubaa nan fɔk ki pɔɔ jer muken na. 4M nan si lik upihja ngbaan aah joo waayiin ngbaan ber toŋ liwilir, ni ŋŋangan, ni ŋŋangii pu na. Le kiwakork kibaa aa nan ŋmaa bui u ke u di cha, bee ki ŋmar waapɔɔn chee. U nan ŋani waah gee pu na ki moo kan mpɔɔn.
5Maah nan si dak lik tibɔr tee aatataa aah ye pu na, le uŋoja ubaa nyan ni liwilir wɔb, ki san mala mala le utaa aa ti ki piir kitiŋ. U nan kpa n‑yiin mu fɔk ki gbei na unimbil aakaasisik ni. 6U nan san tok upihja u m ba puen kan u si gbɔk limɔɔl na, ki di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk ber toŋ u. 7M nan kan u buen ti tak upihja ngbaan. Waaŋuul nan fii sakpen, le u ber ti saa upihja ngbaan ki kool waayiin ilee na. Upihja ngbaan aa nan kpa mpɔɔn u sil kiir u. U nan saa u lii kitiŋ ki taa u ŋmal titan ni, le ubaa aa ŋmaa gaa u lii.
8Le uŋoja ngbaan moo pɔɔk ki mak pam, le buyoonn waapɔɔn ti ban mu nyaŋ na, le waayiin ngbaan chuu koo. Mu aah koo na, le iyiin inaa i fɔk ki gbei na nyan mu aabuul ni. I mɔmɔk nan lik yaapepel ibaabaa la. 9Iyiin inaa ngbaan ponn ni mubaa pu le n‑yiin waatiir mubaa nan ki nyan ni, le mu aapɔɔn nan ti saa ŋŋangii, ni liwipuul, ni Kitiŋ ki Ŋan na ni. 10Mu nan kan mpɔɔn le ki ti kpaan tak iŋmabi i bi paacham na ibaa, ki ker ibaa lii ni kitiŋ ki taa taa i pu. 11Mu nan sii Uwumbɔr u ye paacham aajab aaninkpel na, kaa ki cha binib toor kitork tii u, ki bii Waadichal. 12Binib nan tun titunwanbir li ponn ni, kaa toor iwiin mɔmɔk aatork ki ba ye ke bi toor li ponn ni na, le ki di isan i ye ibamɔn ke bi dii i na lii. Tiwan nimɔk n‑yiin ngbaan nan ŋa na, nan kpa mu tinyoor la.
13Le m ŋun Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib ubaa baa uken ke, “Tiwan ni bi tidaŋ ngbaan ponn ni na ga yunn kinye? Titunwanbir ti gaa iwiin mɔmɔk aatork na ga yunn ki ti saa kinye? Baah taar paacham aaŋmabi ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal pu pu na ga yunn ki ti saa kinye?”
14Le m ŋun Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib uken gar njan yoo na ke, “Ni ga li ŋani kina ki ti saa iwiin lichur ni nkub ni piiŋmu. N‑yoonn mue le kijook ni kichakpiik ni aatork aan ki li bi. Nee aapuwɔb le bi ga toor Uwumbɔr Aadichal.”
Uwumbɔr aatuun Gabriel aah kpiir tidaŋ ngbaan aatataa tuk Daniel pu na
15Maah nan si pɔɔni mbaa ke m bee tidaŋ ngbaan aatataa na, libuul ngbaan ni le m kan unii ubaa si nnimbiin ni. 16Le m ŋun nneel nyan ni Ulai Aamɔɔl wɔb ki bui ke, “Gabriel, kpiir waah kan tiwan ni na aatataa mɔk u.” 17Le Gabriel dan nan sil gbaŋ mi, le ijawaan chuu mi le m lir kitiŋ.
Le u bui mi ke, “Unibɔn, bee tiwan ngbaan aatataa. Tidaŋ ngbaan ye dulnyaa wee aah ga nan doo pu na aabɔr la.” 18Waah nan bi len kina na, le nnimbil bɔln, le m lir kitiŋ kaa ki nyi mbaa chee. Le u chuu mi, ki fiin mi siin ntaa pu, 19le ki bui mi ke, “M bi mɔk si Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aah ga joo ni tiwan ni na la. Tidaŋ ngbaan mɔk kookoo aayoonn aabɔr la.
20“Saah kan upihja u kpa iyiin ilee na ye Media ni Pesia aanaan la. 21Uŋoja na mu ye Griis aanaan la, le n‑yiin mu fɔk ki gbei, ki baa unimbil aakaasisik ni na ye mu aabɔr. 22N‑yiin ngbaan aah nan koo aan iyiin inaa i nyan ni mu aabuul ni na ye nnaan ngbaan aah ga nan yakr nfum munaa pu pu na la, mu mu aan nan li pɔɔ ke njan aanaan na.
23“N‑yoonn mu nnaan munaa mue nan gur kpa mbiin sakpen ki yak mu kuln, ki ŋeer ntafadaan na, le ubɔr u bir ki kpa mbeebeelan na ga ji nnaan. 24U ga pɔɔk pam, ni mu aan li ye ubaa aapɔɔn pu. U ga bii tiwan pam, ki kan linyaŋ tiwan nimɔk u ŋa na ponn ni. U ga bii doo binib bi pɔɔ na, ki kpaan kpee Uwumbɔr aanib mu. 25Waah kpa beebee aalan pu na, u ga di kina aalan nyaŋ tiwan nimɔk u ŋani na. U ga li kpa kigaak, ki ga ku bii binib pam kaan cha bi li nyi. U ga kpaan fii sil Uwumbɔr u ye bibɔrb mɔmɔk Aayidaan na pu, le waah ga nan doo pu na aan nyan ni unibɔn aapɔɔn ni. 26Kijook ni kichakpiik ni aatork aadaŋ ti m kpiir taatataa tuk si na ga sil gbiin kina. Aa mu taa tee cha ti nya lipaal dandana wee, ba pu? ni ga yunn pam le ti nin ŋa kina.”
27Tidaŋ ngbaan pu, le min Daniel aataakpab nan yɔl, le m nan buŋ ni ti yunn pam. Le m nan pɔɔk ki ki piin ki tun lituln li ubɔr nan di ŋa ŋŋaal ni na. Tidaŋ ngbaan nan gar mi pam, le maa bee taatataa.

english_text:
Daniel Prays for the People
1-2 Daniel wrote:
Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for 70 years.” 3-4Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God:
Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you. 5But we have sinned terribly by rebelling against you and rejecting your laws and teachings. 6We have ignored the message your servants the prophets spoke to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and everyone else.
7 Everything you do is right, our Lord. But still we suffer public disgrace because we have been unfaithful and have sinned against you. This includes all of us, both far and near—the people of Judah, Jerusalem, and Israel, as well as those you dragged away to foreign lands, 8and even our kings, our officials, and our ancestors. 9Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you 10and rejected your teachings that came to us from your servants the prophets.
11 Everyone in Israel has stubbornly refused to obey your laws, and so those curses written by your servant Moses have fallen upon us. 12You warned us and our leaders that Jerusalem would suffer the worst disaster in human history, and you did exactly as you had threatened. 13We have not escaped any of the terrible curses written by Moses, and yet we have refused to beg you for mercy and to remind ourselves of how faithful you have always been. 14And when you finally punished us with this horrible disaster, that was also the right thing to do, because we deserved it so much.
15 Our Lord God, with your own mighty arm you rescued us from Egypt and made yourself famous to this very day, but we have sinned terribly. 16In the past, you treated us with such kindness, that we now beg you to stop being so terribly angry with Jerusalem. After all, it is your chosen city built on your holy mountain, even though it has suffered public disgrace because of our sins and those of our ancestors.
17 I am your servant, Lord God, and I beg you to answer my prayers and bring honor to yourself by having pity on your temple that lies in ruins. 18 Please show mercy to your chosen city, not because we deserve it, but because of your great kindness. 19Forgive us! Hurry and do something, not only for your city and your chosen people, but to bring honor to yourself.
The Seventy Weeks
Daniel wrote:
20I was still confessing my sins and those of all Israel to the Lord my God, and I was praying for the good of his holy mountain, 21 when Gabriel suddenly came flying in at the time of the evening sacrifice. This was the same Gabriel I had seen in my vision, 22and he explained:
Daniel, I am here to help you understand the vision. 23God thinks highly of you, and at the very moment you started praying, I was sent to give you the answer. 24God has decided that for 70 weeks, your people and your holy city must suffer as the price of their sins. Then evil will disappear, and justice will rule forever; the visions and words of the prophets will come true, and a most holy place will be dedicated.
25You need to realize that from the command to rebuild Jerusalem until the coming of the Chosen Leader, it will be 7 weeks and another 62 weeks. Streets will be built in Jerusalem, and a trench will be dug around the city for protection, but these will be difficult times. 26At the end of the 62 weeks, the Chosen Leader will be killed and left with nothing.
A foreign ruler and his army will sweep down like a mighty flood, leaving both the city and the temple in ruins, and war and destruction will continue until the end, just as God has decided. 27 For one week this foreigner will make a firm agreement with many people, and halfway through this week, he will end all sacrifices and offerings. Then the “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction will be put there. And it will stay there until the time God has decided to destroy this one who destroys.
translation_text:
Daniel aah mee Uwumbɔr tii waanib pu na
1Darius u ye Media aanii, aan ute nan ye Sekes na, nan jin Babiloŋ aanaan. 2Waah nan jin nnaan ngbaan na aajan aabiln ponn ni, le m nan bi bae Uwumbɔr aagbann ponn ni, ki dakl lik ŋibin imonko itaa ni kipiik ŋi ponn ni Jerusalem ga li bi libiil ni na. Uwumbɔr nan di libiil ngbaan aabɔr kpiir tuk waabɔnabr Jeremia la. 3Le m nan mee ki gaŋ Tidindaan Uwumbɔr linimaln, ki lulni bumɔb, ki peeni tiwan ni saak kuub na, ki kaa nfatan ni tibɔr ngbaan pu. 4M nan mee Ndindaan Uwumbɔr ki kpiir maatunwanbir ni maanib aatunwanbir tuk u.
M nan len ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, aa ye unikpaan la, le ti pak si. N‑yoonn mɔmɔk aa joo saah puu pu na, ki gee binib bi gee si ki ŋani saah len pu na.
5“Ti tun titunwanbir, ki ŋa tiwan ni kaa ŋan na. Ti yii saah len ke ti ŋa pu na, ki fenn tipuwɔb tii tiwan ni aa mɔk ke ni ŋan na. 6Taa nan pel saatutum ni saabɔnabtiib bi nan di saayimbil tuk timi aabɔrb, ni binib bi joo ntim na, ni tiyaajatiib, ni litimbol mɔln na aah nan len pu na. 7Ndindaan, aa ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le tima joo ni inimɔɔn nan tii tibaa n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Nimina ye mbamɔn ki tii timi bi bi Judea ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ni na, ni Israel yaab bi aa cha bi yaa ki bi ntim mu bi dandar na, ni mu duun na ni na, ke baa dii si mbamɔm. 8Ndindaan, timi aabɔrb, ni binib bi joo ntim na, ni tiyaajatiib nan tun titunwanbir ki jin inimɔɔn. 9Aa ye unimbaasaln la, ki joo cha pinni titunwanbir mu, le tima yii si. 10Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, ti nan yii kaa ŋun tii si, buyoonn aa nan bui timi ke ti li bi saah nan siin ikaal i ki di tii ni saatutum bi ye saabɔnabr na. 11Israel yaab mɔmɔk nan bii saakaal ki yii kaa pel saah len pu na. Ti nan tun si titunwanbir, le aa nan cha saah puun tibɔbir ti aan saatutunn Moses nan ŋmee ŋa saakaal ni na dan nan lir ti pu. 12Aa nan ŋa saah nan bui ke aa ga ŋa timi, ni binib bi joo timi na mɔmɔk pu na. Kitiŋ kibaa aa ki bi taab do ki kan ntafadaan mu aa nan di tii Jerusalem na. 13Aa nan tii timi ntafadaan mumɔk nan ŋmee dɔ Moses aakaal ponn ni na. Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, hali nima ngbaan aa cha ti mee si ki aa san timi kinimbaak, bee ti yii timi aatunwanbir ki fenn dii saasan mu ye ibamɔn na. 14Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, sin le nyan sil ke aa daa timi aatafal, ki mu sil ŋa kina; ba pu? aa ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le ti yii kaa ŋun tii si.
15“Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, aa nan mɔk saapɔɔn buyoonn aa nan di saanib nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, le bi beenin teer saapɔɔn bɔr. Ti tun titunwanbir, ki ŋa tiwan ni kaa ŋan na. 16Sin le nan kii timi n‑yoonn mu jer na, kina pu na, taa ki gee Jerusalem aatiŋ pu liŋuul. Ki ye saatiŋ ki bi chain na la. Binib bi mɔmɔk bi itingbaan mɔmɔk ni na lik seen Jerusalem aatiŋ, ni saanib, timi aatunwanbir, ni tiyaajatiib aatunwanbir pu. 17Uwumbɔr, ŋun maameel ni maah gaŋni si pu na. Gir maa Saadichal li bi nan ber na. Gir maa li, aan binib mɔmɔk bee ke sin le ye Uwumbɔr. 18Uwumbɔr, pel ti chee, lik timi, ki kan taah bi tibɔr ti ponn ni na, ki lik kitiŋ ki bi di saayimbil yin ki na aamukl. Saah san unibɔn kinimbaak pu na, le ti mee si, naa ye ke ti tun ni ŋan na la. 19Tidindaan, ŋun timi aameel. Tidindaan, di cha pinn timi. Tidindaan, ŋun timi aameel, ki ter timi. Taa cha ni yunn, aan binib mɔmɔk bee ke sin le ye Uwumbɔr. Kitiŋ kimina ni binib bee ye sin yaan la.”
Uwumbɔr aatuun Gabriel aah nabr tibɔr pu na
20M nan beenin mee Uwumbɔr, ki kpiir maatunwanbir ni maanib Israel yaab aatunwanbir, ki gaŋni Ndindaan Uwumbɔr ke u ki gir maa Waadichal li bi chain na. 21Maah nan beenin bi mee Uwumbɔr kina na, le waatuun Gabriel, u m ba puen kan u njan aadaŋ ponn ni na, fii dan maah si nin chee na. Ni nan ye buyoonn bi toor kijook aatork na la. 22Le u kpiir len ke, “Daniel, m dan ke m nan ter si aa bee tibɔr ngbaan aatataa la. 23Saah piin ki bi gaŋni Uwumbɔr na, le u kii saah ban pu na. U gee si, kina pu le m dan m nan tuk si saah ban pu na. Tɔ, li pel aan m kpiir tidaŋ ngbaan aatataa tuk si.
24“Ŋibin ŋi Uwumbɔr di siin ke u nyan saanib, ni kitiŋ ki bi chain na titunwanbir ni, ni tiwan ni kaa ŋan na ni na, ye ŋibin imonko itaa ni kipiik nfum mulole pu la. U ga di cha pinn titunwanbir, ki cha ibamɔn i ga li bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na dan, le tidaŋ ngbaan, ni Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ngbaan aamɔbon ga gbiin, le Uwumbɔr Aadichal li bi chain na ga ki gir sil. 25Chuu tibɔr timina ki bee taatataa: Ki nyan n‑yoonn mu bi ga lii bumɔb ke bi ki gir maa Jerusalem aatiŋ na, ki ti saa buyoonn Uwumbɔr aah lee usaloln u na fuu ni na, ga li ye ŋibin ŋilole nfum mulole pu la. Bi ga ki gir maa Jerusalem aatiŋ, le isan ga li bi ki ponn ni, le ki li kpa tiwan ni kiir ki aan ki pɔɔ na; le ki ga sil ki ti saa ŋibin imonko itaa ni ŋilee nfum mulole pu; n‑yoonn ngbaan tee ga li ye tibɔbir aayoonn la. 26N‑yoonn ngbaan aah ga ti doo pu na, le bi ga ku Uwumbɔr aah lee usaloln u kaa tun taani ubaa na. Le ubɔr pɔɔl ubaa aajab ga nan ber kitiŋ ngbaan ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal na. Ndoon ngbaan ga nan fuu ni ke nwam na la. Mu ga li joo ni butɔb ni libiil li Uwumbɔr nan gor siin na la. 27Ubɔr pɔɔl ngbaan ga cha u ni binib pam kpaan kimɔbaan ki pɔɔ na ki ti saa ŋibin ŋilole, le ŋibin ŋilole ngbaan ponn ni yaa nan saa ŋibin ŋitaa ni ligeln na, u ga kuln kitork ni ipiin, Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. U ga di tiwanbir ni bii tiwan nimɔk bi chain na ki di kaan Uwumbɔr Aadichal paab, nin chee paa na, le ni ga li ka nima ki ti saa buyoonn unii u di ni kaan nima na pii ndoon mu Uwumbɔr gor kiir u na.”

english_text:
Daniel's Vision beside the Tigris River
1In the third year of Cyrus the king of Persia, a message came to Daniel from God, and it was explained in a vision. The message was about a dreadful war, and it was true. 2Daniel wrote:
For three weeks I was in sorrow. 3I ate no fancy food or meat, I drank no wine, and I put no olive oil on my face or hair. 4Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River, 5 when I looked up and saw someone dressed in linen and wearing a solid gold belt. 6His body was like a precious stone, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming fires, his arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice like the roar of a crowd. 7 Although the people who were with me did not see the vision, they became so frightened that they scattered and hid. 8Only I saw this great vision. I became weak and pale, 9and at the sound of his voice, I fell facedown in a deep sleep.
10He raised me to my hands and knees 11and then said, “Daniel, your God thinks highly of you, and he has sent me. So stand up and pay close attention.” I stood trembling, while the angel said:
12Daniel, don't be afraid! God has listened to your prayers since the first day you humbly asked for understanding, and he has sent me here. 13 But the guardian angel of Persia opposed me for 21 days. Then Michael, who is one of the strongest guardian angels, came to rescue me from the kings of Persia. 14Now I have come here to give you another vision about what will happen to your people in the future.
15While this angel was speaking to me, I stared at the ground, speechless. 16Then he appeared in human form and touched my lips. I said, “Sir, this vision has brought me great pain and has drained my strength. 17I am merely your servant. How can I possibly speak with someone so powerful, when I am almost too weak to get my breath?”
18-19The angel touched me a second time and said, “Don't be frightened! God thinks highly of you, and he intends this for your good, so be brave and strong.”
At this, I regained my strength and replied, “Please speak! You have already made me feel much better.”
20Then the angel said:
Now do you understand why I have come? Soon I must leave to fight against the guardian angel of Persia. Then after I have defeated him, the guardian angel of Greece will attack me. 21I will tell you what is written in The Book of Truth. But first, you must realize that no one except Michael, the guardian angel of Israel, is on my side.
translation_text:
Daniel aadaŋ ti u nan daŋ Tigris aamɔɔl chee na
1Sairus aah nan ye Pesia aabɔrkpaan buyoonn na aabitatar ponn ni, le Uwumbɔr nan kpiir tibɔr tee tuk Daniel, u bi ki yin u ke Beltesasar na. Tibɔr ngbaan nan ye tibɔbamɔnn la, le ti mu aatataa nan pɔɔ pam ke unii bee ti. Tidaŋ ponn ni le Uwumbɔr nan kpiir taatataa tuk u.
2N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan bi mpombiin ni ki ti saa ŋikpaakoo ŋitaa. 3Maa nan jin tijikaanyaan tibaa, bee tinann, kaa nyun ndaan mu, kaa chaa maayikpir ki ti saa ŋikpaakoo ŋitaa.
4Libiln aajan aaŋmal aawiin moninko ni inaa daal, le m nan si gbɔk Tigris aamɔɔsakpeln, 5le ki yaar lik paacham ki kan unii ubaa si pee ŋitan ŋi ŋan na aawanpeenkaan, ki buu salmaa aagbapapaln. 6Uwon nan moor lak lak ke nleenyaan na. Le unimbil wɔb mu moor ke utaal aah moor pu na, le unimbil bi ke mmii mu gaal na. Uŋaal ni utaa nan moor ke tikumann ti bi pir ti mbamɔm na, le uneel naahn kinipaak aafuuk.
7Min baanja le nan kan lijinjiir aawan ngbaan. Bijab bi nan si m chee na aa nan kan nibaa; ijawaan mu nan tee chuu bi, le bi san ti bɔr. 8M nan gur si mbaa baanja le ki lik iwaan aawan ngbaan. Mpɔɔn mubaa aa nan ki bi m chee, le nnimbil wɔb kpeln, le nwon mɔmɔk yɔl. 9Maah nan ŋun waaneel na, le m fik ki lir kitiŋ mpuul pu ki dɔ chik. 10Le ŋŋaal mubaa chuu mi ki fiin mi gbaan ntaaŋaayil pu; le nwon beenin gbaa.
11Le Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan bui mi ke, “Daniel, Uwumbɔr gee si pam. Fii sil ki pel mbamɔm maah ban m len pu na. Uwumbɔr le tun ni mi aa chee.” Waah len kina na, le m fii sil, le nwon beenin gbaa.
12Le u ki bui mi ke, “Daniel, taa san ijawaan. Njan aawiin mundaal aa nan sunn aabaa taab ki piin ki bi mee u ke u tii si nlan na, le Uwumbɔr nan ŋun saameel. Saameel ngbaan pu le m dan. 13Paacham aatuun u joo Pesia aanaan na le kiir mi nsan ni ki ti saa iwiin moninko ni mubaa. Le Uwumbɔr aatuun Maikel, u ye Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib aayidaan ubaa na dan ki nan ter mi, ba pu? m nan gur bi Pesia aatiŋ ni mbaa baanja la. 14M dan ke m nan cha aa bee tiwan ni ga nan ŋa saanib n‑yoonn mu choo na la. Lijinjiir aawan ngbaan ye n‑yoonn mu choo na aabɔr la.”
15Waah len kina na, le m si lik kitiŋ, kaa ŋmaa waar mmɔb ki len tibaa. 16Le Uwumbɔr aatuun u nan naahn unibɔn na, taln uŋaal ki di mee mmɔgban. Le m bui ke, “Uninkpel, lijinjiir aawan ni m kan tidaŋ ponn ni na tii mi iween ki cha nwon yɔl sakpen. 17M gur naahn ke unaagbiija le aah si udindaan aanimbiin ni na. M ga ŋa kinye ki len aa chee tibɔr? Maa ki kpa mpɔɔn, bee kifuurk kibaa nwon ni.”
18Le u ki gir chuu mi le nwon moo pɔɔk. 19Le u bui mi ke, “Uwumbɔr gee si, kina pu na, taa cha nibaa li muk si, bee ni faan si.”
Waah ki len kina na, le nwon moo pɔɔk sakpen, le m bui ke, “Maaninkpel, tuk mi saah kpa pu aa len na. Aa cha nwon chuu a.”
20-21Le u baa mi ke, “Aa nyi budabu pu m dan aa chee na aa? M dan ke m nan kpiir baah ŋmee pu Ibamɔn Aagbaŋ ponn ni na le tuk si. Tɔ, m ga gir ti jan Paacham aatuun mu kii Pesia aatiŋ na kijaak. Nee aapuwɔb le Paacham aatuun mu kii Griis aatiŋ na mu ga dan. Ubaa aa bi ki ga ter mi see Maikel, Uwumbɔr aatuun mu kii Israel aatiŋ na baanja.

english_text:
1You also need to know that I protected and helped Darius the Mede in his first year as king.
The Angel's Message to Daniel
Part One: The Four Kings and Their Successors
2What I am going to tell you is certain to happen. Four kings will rule Persia, one after the other, but the fourth one will become much richer than the others. In fact, his wealth will make him so powerful that he will turn everyone against the kingdom of Greece. 3Then a mighty king will come to power and will be able to do whatever he pleases. 4But suddenly his kingdom will be crushed and scattered to the four corners of the earth, where four more kingdoms will rise. But these won't be ruled by his descendants or be as powerful as his kingdom.
5The king of the south will grow powerful. Then one of his generals will rebel and will rule an even larger kingdom. 6Years later the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom will make a treaty, and the daughter of the king of the south will marry the king of the north. But she will lose her power. Then she, her husband, their child, and the servants who came with her will all be killed.
After this, 7one of her relatives will become the ruler of the southern kingdom. He will attack the army of the northern kingdom and capture its fortresses. 8Then he will carry their idols to Egypt, together with their precious treasures of silver and gold, but it will be a long time before he attacks the northern kingdom again. Some years later 9the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom, but he will be forced back to his own country.
10The sons of the king of the north will gather a huge army that will sweep down like a roaring flood, reaching all the way to the fortress of the southern kingdom. 11 But this will make the king of the south angry, and he will defeat this large army from the north. 12The king of the south will feel proud because of the many thousands he has killed. But his victories won't last long, 13because the king of the north will gather a larger and more powerful army than ever before. Then in a few years, he will start invading other countries.
14At this time many of your own people will try to make this vision come true by rebelling against the king of the south, but their rebellion will fail. 15Then the army from the north will surround and capture a fortress in the south, and not even the most experienced troops of the southern kingdom will be able to make them retreat. 16The king who invaded from the north will do as he pleases, and he will even capture and destroy the holy land. 17In fact, he will decide to invade the south with his entire army. Then he will attempt to make peace by giving the king of the south a bride from the northern kingdom, but this won't be successful.
18Afterwards, this proud king of the north will invade and conquer many of the nations along the coast, but a military leader will defeat him and make him lose his pride. 19He will retreat to his fortresses in his own country, but on the way he will be defeated and never again be seen.
20The next king of the north will try to collect taxes for the glory of his kingdom. However, he will come to a sudden end in some mysterious way, instead of in battle or because of someone's anger.
Part Two: The Evil King from the North
21The successor of this king of the north will be a worthless nobody, who doesn't even come from a royal family. He will suddenly appear and gain control of the kingdom by treachery. 22Then he will destroy armies and remove God's chosen high priest. 23He will make a treaty, but he will be deceitful and break it, even though he has only a few followers. 24Without warning, he will successfully invade a wealthy province, which is something his ancestors never did. Then he will divide among his followers all of its treasures and property. But none of this will last very long.
25He will gather a large and powerful army, and with great courage he will attack the king of the south. The king of the south will meet him with a much stronger army, but he will lose the battle, because he will be betrayed 26by members of the royal court. He will be ruined, and most of his army will be slaughtered.
27The two kings will meet around a table and tell evil lies to each other. But their plans will fail, because God has already decided what will happen. 28Then the king of the north will return to his country with great treasures. But on the way, he will attack the religion of God's people and do whatever else he pleases.
29At the time God has decided, the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom again, but this time, things will be different. 30 Ships from the west will come to attack him, and he will be discouraged. Then he will start back to his own country and take out his anger on the religion of God's faithful people, while showing kindness to those who are unfaithful. 31 He will send troops to pollute the temple and the fortress, and he will stop the daily sacrifices. Then he will set up that “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction. 32The king will use deceit to win followers from those who are unfaithful to God, but those who remain faithful will do everything possible to oppose him.
33Wise leaders will instruct many of the people. But for a while, some of these leaders will either be killed with swords or burned alive, or else robbed of their possessions and thrown into prison. 34They will receive only a little help in their time of trouble, and many of their followers will be treacherous. 35Some of those who are wise will suffer, so that God will make them pure and acceptable until the end, which will still come at the time he has decided.
36 This king will do as he pleases. He will proudly claim to be greater than any god and will insult the only true God. Indeed, he will be successful until God is no longer angry with his people. 37This king will reject the gods his ancestors worshiped and the god preferred by women. In fact, he will put himself above all gods 38and worship only the so-called god of fortresses, who was unknown to his ancestors. And he will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and other costly gifts. 39With the help of this foreign god, he will capture the strongest fortresses. Everyone who worships this god will be put in a position of power and rewarded with wealth and land.
Part Three: The Time of the End
40At the time of the end, the king of the south will attack the kingdom of the north. But its king will rush out like a storm with war chariots, cavalry, and many ships. Indeed, his forces will flood one country after another, 41and when they reach the holy land, tens of thousands will be killed. But the countries of Edom and Moab and the ruler of Ammon will escape.
42The king of the north will invade many countries, including Egypt, 43and he will take its rich treasures of gold and silver. He will also conquer Libya and Ethiopia. 44But he will be alarmed by news from the east and the north, and he will become furious and cause great destruction. 45After this, he will set up camp between the Mediterranean Sea and Mount Zion. Then he will be destroyed, and no one will be able to save him.
translation_text:
1Min le nan ter u ki tii u mpɔɔn buyoonn Ubɔr Darius nan ye Media yaab aajojoor na aajan aabiln ponn ni na. 2Maah ban m bui si pu na ye ibamɔn la.”
Ijipt ni Siria aanaan aabɔr
Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan nan ki bui mi ke, “Bibɔrb bitaa ga ki ji nnaan Pesia aatiŋ ni, ki paan tɔb pu, le unanar mu ga paan ni bi pu, uma ga li kpa liwangol ki jer bitaa na. Buyoonn waapɔɔn ni waawangol ngbaan ga ti moo nyaŋ na, le u ga buen ti kpak Griis aanaan.
3“N‑yoonn ngbaan le ubɔr ubaa ga nyan ni ki ga li kaar ki kpa kipak sakpen. Waanaan ga li wiir pam, le u li ŋani waah gee pu na. 4Buyoonn waapɔɔn ti moo nyaŋ na, le waanaan ga bii ki yakr nfum munaa pu. Bibɔrb bi ga ji nnaan waanaan ni na aan li ye waamaal ni aanib, bi mu aan li kpa mpɔɔn mu u nan kpa na.
5“Ijipt aabɔr ga li pɔɔ pam. Le waatɔb aajab aaninkpel ubaa ga li pɔɔ jer u, ki ga li joo waanaan ni aapepel li wiir ki jer ubɔr ngbaan aapepel na. 6Ŋibin ŋibaa aapuwɔb le Ijipt aabɔr ngbaan ga buen ti ŋa kimɔbaan Siria aabɔr chee, ki ga di ubisal tii u. Kimɔbaan ngbaan mu aan yunn, le bi ga ku upii ngbaan ni uchal, ni ute, ni binaagbiib bi nan dii u nyan ni ute do na, ni unii u sil upuwɔb na. 7Nee aapuwɔb na, naan yunn le upii ngbaan aado yoo ubaa ga ji nnaan ngbaan. U ga tak Siria aabɔr aajab, ki koo baah maa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na kiir ntim mu na ni, ki nyaŋ bi. 8U ga yoor baawaa, ni salmaa, ni tikunabr aawan ni bi nan di tii baawaa ngbaan na mɔmɔk ki di gir buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Ŋibin siib ga jer ki li ye nsuudoon aabin la; 9ŋee aapuwɔb na Siria aabɔr ga buen ti loon tak Ijipt, le Ijipt yaab ga nyaŋ bi, le bi gir kun.
10“Siria aabɔr aajapɔtiib ga ban bijab pam ki gor kiir butɔb. Bi ponn ni ubaa ga san mala ke nwam na ki ti tak bidim bibaa aatim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na. 11Ijipt aabɔr aaŋuul ga fii pam le u ga ti to Siria aajab butɔb ki nyaŋ bi. 12Waah ga nyaŋ bi ki ku baajab sakpen pu na ga cha u kpaln umakdaan; tɔ, waanyaŋ ngbaan mu aan yunn.
13“Siria aabɔr ga gir ti ban bijab bi wiir jer njan yaab na. Le n‑yoonn yaa nan ŋeer kan, u ga di bijab bi wiir, ki kpa tijawan mbamɔm na gir buen. 14Le binib pam ga nya Ijipt aabɔr aapuwɔb. Le bijab bibaa ga nyan ni sin Daniel aatimbol ponn ni, ki ga li bir pam ki mu ga nya upuwɔb, ba pu? bi kan tiwan nibaa tidaŋ ponn ni. Bi mu ga lir. 15Kina pu na, Siria aabɔr ga ti loon kitiŋ ki bi maa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ gob ki na ki nyaŋ ki. Ijipt aatɔb aajab ga di cha kaan ki to butɔb; hali bi ponn ni bi kaar sakpen na aan ki li kpa mpɔɔn mubaa bi jan kijaak. 16Siria aabɔr ngbaan ga ŋa bi waah gee pu na, le ubaa aan ŋmaa sil kiir u. U ga sil Kitiŋ ki Ŋan na ni, ki ga li kpa mpɔɔn ki u kuln ki.
17“Siria aabɔr ga kpokl ke u di waajab mɔmɔk buen butɔb aaban. U ga li ban ke u bii waadin aanaan mɔmɔk, kina pu na, u ga cha u ni uma ŋa kimɔbaan ki di ubisal tii u; le ni mu aan kal kina. 18Nee aapuwɔb, le u ga ti tak ŋitimbol ŋi bi nnyusakpem chee na, ki nyaŋ mu ponn ni pam. Le biwɔwɔm aajab aaninkpel ga nan nyaŋ u ki kuln waamakl ngbaan; mbamɔn, u ga giin Siria aabɔr aamakl ngbaan di ŋa u. 19Ubɔr ngbaan ga gir buen waatim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na udo aatiŋ pu; tɔ, nima chee le bi ga ti nyaŋ u, le waamɔfal ga junn.
20“Ubɔr uken ga paan ni u pu, uma le ga tun waaninkpel u di mpɔɔn muk binib ki gaa lampoo ke waanaan kan ŋimombil sakpen. Naan yunn le bi ga ku ubɔr ngbaan, le ubaa aan li nyi waakun bɔr; ni mu aan li ye butɔb ponn ni.”
Siria yaab aabɔr aah nan ye utunwanbirdaan pu na
21Le Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan ki kpiir tuk mi ke: “Siria yaab aabɔr u ga paan ni na ga li bir pam, kaan li kpa nsan ke u ji nnaan, le ki mu tee ga di beebee nyan ni, ubaa aan li nyi u bɔr, le ki nan gaa nnaan ngbaan. 22U ga ku unii umɔk nyan sil u pu na, ki kpee Uwumbɔr Aatotoorninkpel mu. 23U ga ŋmann ŋitimbol ŋiken, ki cha bi ŋa kimɔbaan, le ki moo kani mpɔɔn kpae; u mu aah joo binib bi na aan li wiir. 24U ga loon ki tak lipepel li kpa liwangol na ki ŋa tiwan ni ubɔr ubaa aa kee ŋa na, le ki yakr waah gaa tiwan ni mpɔɔn butɔb ponn ni na tii bijab bi ye waadidiliib na. U ga kpokl ke u ti tak ntim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na, le waayoonn aan ki yunn kpala.
25“U ga di limakl ki ban bijab bi wiir na ke u ti tak Ijipt yaab aabɔr. Le Ijipt yaab aabɔr ngbaan mu ga gor ni bijab bi wiir ki kpa mpɔɔn jer waajab na ke bi to butɔb. Tɔ, bi ga ŋmann Ijipt yaab aabɔr ngbaan, le u lir. 26Waasusurb bi duun u sakpen na le ga ban bi kuln u. Bidim ga ku waajab mɔmɔk pel pel. 27Le bibɔrb bilee ngbaan ga kpaan kal ke bi ji tijikaar lisambil libaa ni, bi mu aalandak ga li ye titunwanbir aalandak la, le bi mɔnn tɔb inyamɔn. Baan kan baah ban pu na, ba pu? baah ban pu na aayoonn aa kee fuu ni. 28Siria yaab aabɔr ga di waah gaa tiwan ni mpɔɔn butɔb ni na gir kun, ki ga pɔɔn ubaa ke u bii Uwumbɔr aanib aah dii nsan mu na. U ga ŋa waah gee pu na, le ki gir kun udo aatiŋ pu.
29“Nee aapuwɔb na, u ga buen ti loon tak Ijipt aatiŋ lelee, le n‑yoonn mumina ma tibɔr ga labr lir u pu. 30Rom yaab ga di iŋɔi dan ki nan tak u, le ijawaan ga chuu u.
“U ga gee liŋuul ki fenn upuwɔb ki pɔɔn ubaa ke u bii doo Uwumbɔr aanib aasan. U ga ŋa binib bi yii nsan ngbaan na tiŋann. 31Waajab ngem ga bii Uwumbɔr Aadichal. Bi ga kuln iwiin mɔmɔk aatork, ki di tiwanbir ni bii tiwan nimɔk bi chain na siin nima. 32Ubɔr ngbaan ga di kimɔmɔɔn kan binib bi puen yii nsan ngbaan na aaterm, le binib bi dii Uwumbɔr na ga sil kiir bi. 33Binib ngbaan aaninkpiib bi kpa nlan na ga di baalan yakr tii binib pam. Le bi ponn ni bibaa ga kpo butɔb ni; bi ga see bibaa mu mmii ponn ni bi ti kpo, le ki su bibaa mu kinaayuk ki di bi ŋa kiyondiik ni; tɔ, falaa ngbaan mu aan yunn. 34Buyoonn linikul ngbaan beenin ku na, Uwumbɔr aanib ga kan nterm siib, binib pam le ga kpee bi pu, bi mu ga li ŋani kina ki ban bibaa aajim pu la. 35Bi ga ku bilandam ngbaan bibaa, le kina ngbaan ga nyan binib ngbaan baajɔŋ ni. Nimina ga li ŋani kina ki ti saa ndoon, n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr siin na.
36“Siria aabɔr ga li ŋani waah gee pu na la. U ga li kpa kipupuk ke liwaal libaa aa bi ki pii u, ke u kpaan jer Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na mu. U ga li ŋani kina ki ti saa buyoonn Uwumbɔr ga daa utafal na. Uwumbɔr aah kpokl ke u ŋa pu na, kina le ga ŋa. 37Ubɔr ngbaan aatafal aan li bi ŋiwaa ŋi uyaajatiib nan dii na, ni liwaal li bipiib gee na ni. Mbamɔn, utafal aan li bi liwaal libaa, bee Uwumbɔr ni; ba pu? u dak ke u jer ni mɔmɔk. 38Waah ga ŋa pu na le ye ke u nyuŋ liwaal li kiir ntim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na. U ga di salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni nleenyaan, ni liwangol aapiin tii liwaal li uyaajatiib aa kee dii li daalbaadaal na. 39U ga di binib bi dii liwaal yayan na le di kiir waatim mu bi maa ŋigon gob mu na. U ga nyuŋ binib bimɔk tii naadii ke u ye ubɔr na, ki siin bi lituln li kpa kipak na, ki tii bi kitiŋ, ke baapiin le na.
40“Buyoonn Siria aabɔr aayoonn nan ban mu fuu ni na, le Ijipt aabɔr ga ti tak u, le Siria aabɔr ga di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk sil kiir u, u ga di itaan aatɔroku tiib, ni itaan, ni iŋɔi pam jan kijaak ngbaan. U ga loon ntim pam, ke nwam na. 41U ga kpaan loon Kitiŋ ki Ŋan na mu, ki ku binib ŋichur ŋichur, le Edom, ni Moab, ni Amonn aatim aanib bi gur siib na ga san ŋmar. 42U ga loon ntim mumina mɔmɔk ki kpee Ijipt aatiŋ mu. 43U ga yoor Ijipt aatiŋ aawangol li bɔr ki ye salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni liwangol li kpa kidaak na mɔmɔk. U ga nyaŋ Libia ni Kus aatim mu. 44Le tibɔr ti ga nyan ni liwipuul wɔb, ni ŋŋangan wɔb na ga cha ijawaan chuu u, le u moo jan kijaak ke uwaar na, ki ku binib pam. 45U ga kpaan gaa waanaan aaboo sakpiin nnyusakpem ni lijool li Uwumbɔr Aadichal si li paab na aakaasisik ni. Tɔ, u mu ga kpo, le ubaa aan li bi nima ke u ter u.”

english_text:
Part Four: The Dead Will Rise to Life
1 Michael, the chief of the angels, is the protector of your people, and he will come at a time of terrible suffering, the worst in all of history. And your people who have their names written in The Book will be protected. 2 Many of those who lie dead in the ground will rise from death. Some of them will be given eternal life, and others will receive nothing but eternal shame and disgrace. 3 Everyone who has been wise will shine as bright as the sky above, and everyone who has led others to please God will shine forever like the stars.
4 Daniel, I now command you to keep the message of this book secret until the end of time, even though many people will go everywhere, searching for the knowledge to be found in it.
The End of Time
5Daniel wrote:
I looked around and saw two other people—one on this side of the river and one on the other side. 6The angel who had spoken to me was dressed in linen and was standing upstream from them. So one of the two beside the river asked him, “How long before these amazing things happen?”
7 The angel then raised both hands toward heaven and said, “In the name of the God who lives forever, I solemnly promise that it will be a time, two times, and half a time. Everything will be over, when the suffering of God's holy people comes to an end.”
8I heard what the angel said, but I didn't understand. So I asked, “Sir, how will it all end?”
The angel in my vision then replied:
9Daniel, go about your business, because the meaning of this message will remain secret until the end of time. 10 Many people will have their hearts and lives made pure and clean, but those who are evil will keep on being evil and never understand. Only the wise will understand. 11 There will be 1,290 days from the time that the daily sacrifices are stopped, until someone sets up the “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction. 12God will bless everyone who patiently waits until 1,335 days have gone by.
13So, Daniel, be faithful until the end! You will rest, and at the end of time, you will rise from death to receive your reward.
translation_text:
Kookoo aayoonn aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr aatuun mu pee ŋitanyaan aawanpeenkaan na len ke, “N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, Uwumbɔr aatuun Maikel u kpa mpɔɔn ki kii Israel aanib na ga dan. Le tibɔbir aayoonn ga fuu ni, tibɔbir ti kaa kee ŋa n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr naan ŋitimbol na ga fuu ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, saanib bimɔk aayimbil bi Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni na ga ŋmar. 2Bi puen kpo na pam le ga fikr nkun ni: bibaa ga kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na, le bibaa mu ji inimɔɔn i kaa kpa ndoon na. 3Bilandam bi mɔk biken ke bi li tun litulnyaan na ga li wiin chain ke kitaapaak aah wiin pu na, ki wiin ke iŋmabi i bi paacham na, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
4“Tɔ, Daniel, kpab kigbaŋ ngbaan ki ŋal biin ki pu ki ti saa dulnyaa aadoon; le binib pam ga bii baayoonn ke bi bee tiwan ni bi ŋani na aatataa.”
5Le m kan bijab bilee bibaa si gbɔk limɔɔl libaa, ubaa si lidapuul lee, le uken mu si lidapuul liken. 6Le ubaa baa Uwumbɔr aatuun mu si dandar limɔɔl aapaacham na ke, “Ni ga yunn kinye aan iwaan aawan nimina doo?”
7Le Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan yoor uŋaal ilee paacham; le m ŋun u puu tipuur Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na aayimbil pu ki len ke, “Ni ga li ye ŋibin ŋitaa ni ligeln la. Buyoonn Uwumbɔr aanib aapɔɔn ga kuln na, le tiwan nee mɔmɔk ga ŋa doo.”
8M ŋun waah len pu na, ki mu aa bee taatataa. Le m baa ke, “Tɔ, maaninkpel, ni mɔmɔk ga doo kinye?”
9Le u kii ke, “Daniel, li cha n‑yoonn mue; ba pu? tibɔr timina ye tibɔbɔrkaan la, ki ga li bɔr ki ti saa ndoon aayoonn. 10Uwumbɔr ga toor binib pam ki nya bi tijɔŋ ni aan bi ŋa chain. Binib bi kpa mbiin na aan bee taatataa le ki ga li moo ŋani mbiin; binib bi kpa nlan na baanja le ga bee taatataa.
11“Ki nya buyoonn bibiindam cha bi taa ki toor iwiin mɔmɔk aatork Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na, nima le ye buyoonn tiwanbir ni bii tiwan nimɔk bi chain na ga sil Uwumbɔr Aadichal ngbaan ni, iwiin lichur ni ikui ilee ni imonko inaa ni kipiik le ga jer. 12Binib bi ga li si chob aan iwiin lichur ni ikui itaa ni piitaa ni iŋmu ti jer na ga li kpa mpopiin.
13“Kina pu na, sin Daniel, li si chob ki ti saa ndoon ngbaan; le aa ga kpo, ki mu tee ga fikr ki ti gaa saapal, ndoon aayoonn ngbaan.”

english_text:
1 I am Hosea son of Beeri. When Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah, and when Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, the Lord spoke this message to me.
Hosea's Family
2The Lord said, “Hosea, Israel has betrayed me like an unfaithful wife. Marry such a woman and have children by her.” 3So I married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and we had a son.
4 Then the Lord said, “Hosea, name your son Jezreel, because I will soon punish the descendants of King Jehu of Israel for the murders he committed in Jezreel Valley. I will destroy his kingdom, 5and in Jezreel Valley I will break the power of Israel.”
6Later, Gomer had a daughter, and the Lord said, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah, because I will no longer have mercy and forgive Israel. 7But I am the Lord God of Judah, and I will have mercy and save Judah by my own power—not by wars and arrows or swords and cavalry.”
8After Gomer had stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she had another son. 9Then the Lord said, “Name him Lo-Ammi, because these people are not mine, and I am not their God.”
Hope for Israel
10 Someday it will be impossible to count the people of Israel, because there will be as many of them as there are grains of sand along the seashore. They are now called “Not My People,” but in the future they will be called “Children of the Living God.” 11Israel and Judah will unite and choose one leader. Then they will take back their land, and this will be a great day for Jezreel.
translation_text:
1Bibɔrb bimina aah nan jin jin nnaan ki paan paan tɔb pu n‑yoonn mu aan Jehoas aajapɔɔn Jeroboam mu nan ye Israel aabɔr na, le Uwumbɔr nan di tibɔr timina tuk Beeri aajapɔɔn Hosea: Juda aabɔrb ngbaan le nan ye Usia, uma le nan puen jin nnaan, le Jotam paan u pu, le Ahas mu nan paan Jotam pu, le Hesekia ti gbeln puwɔb.
Hosea aapuu ni waabim aabɔr
2Uwumbɔr aah nan puen di Israel yaab aabɔr ti tuk Hosea na, u nan bui Hosea ke, “Ti ban upii ki yoor, aapuu ngbaan aan li ye upii kpala, le waabim mu ga li bi ke uma na la. Kina le maanib mu yii mi, kaa ye binib bi dii mi na.”
3Le Hosea nan ti yoor upii ubaa, bi yin u ke Gomer. Ute aayimbil le nan ye Diblaim. Baah nan ma baajan aabo u na nan ye ubijabo la, 4le Uwumbɔr bui Hosea ke, “Yin u ke ‘Jesreel,’ ba pu? naan yunn le m ga daa Israel aabɔr aatafal, uyaaja Jehu aah nan ku binib bi bi Jesreel ni na pu. M ban m kuln Jehu aanaan aadichal la. 5Le n‑yoonn ngbaan m ga bii Israel aajab aapɔɔn, Jesreel aafataŋ ni.”
6Gomer nan ki ma ubo uken, n‑yoonn mumina ma kan, u nan ye upiibo la. Le Uwumbɔr bui Hosea ke, “Yin u ke ‘Maaneen,’ ba pu? maan ki li neen Israel aanib, kaan ki di cha pinn bi. 7Tɔ, m ga li gee Juda yaab ma. Min, Bidindaan Uwumbɔr ga gaa bi lii, m mu aan di kijaak aajum, bee itɔi ni ipiin, bee itaan ni bitandam tun li.”
8Gomer aah lii waapiibo ngbaan na, u nan ki dek, le ki ki ma ubijabo. 9Uwumbɔr nan bui Hosea ke, “Yin u ke ‘Baa‑ye‑maanib,’ ba pu? Israel aanib aan ki li ye maanib, le m mu aan ki li ye Baawumbɔr.”
Israel aanaan ga ki gir maa
10Israel aanib ga li wiir ke nnyusakpem aatambol na la. Bi ga li wiir jer baah ga kahn, bee bi ŋaŋ bi pu na. Le Uwumbɔr bui bi n‑yoonn mue ke, “Naa ye maanib,” tɔ, n‑yoonn choo le u ga nan bui bi ke, “Ni ye min Uwumbɔr u bi na aabim la.” 11Juda aanib ni Israel aanib ga ki gir kpaan kimɔbaan. Bi ga kpaan le ki ban usaloln ubaa, le bi ga ki pɔr ki kan nkam baatiŋ ni. Een, Jesreel aawiin daal ga li ye nwinkpaan la.

english_text:
1So let your brothers be called “My People” and your sisters be called “Shown Mercy.”
The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
2Accuse! Accuse your mother!
She is no longer my wife,
and now I, the Lord,
am not her husband.
Beg her to give up prostitution
and stop being unfaithful,
3or I will strip her naked
like the day she was born.
I will make her barren
like a desert,
and she will die of thirst.
4You children are the result
of her unfaithfulness,
and I'll show you no pity.
5Your mother was unfaithful.
She was disgraceful and said,
“I'll run after my lovers.
Everything comes from them—
my food and drink,
my linen and wool,
my olive oil and wine.”
6I, the Lord, will build
a fence of thorns
to block her path.
7She will run after her lovers,
but not catch them;
she will search,
but not find them.
Then she will say, “I'll return
to my first husband.
Life was better then.”
8She didn't know that her grain,
wine, and olive oil
were gifts from me,
as were the gold and silver
she used in worshiping Baal.
9So I'll hold back the harvest
of grain and grapes.
I'll take back
my wool and my linen
that cover her body.
10Then I'll strip her naked
in the sight of her lovers.
No one can rescue her.
11I'll stop Israel's celebrations—
no more New Moon Festivals,
Sabbaths, or other feasts.
12She said, “My lovers gave me
vineyards and fig trees
as payment for sex.”
Now I, the Lord, will ruin
her vineyards and fig trees;
they will become clumps of weeds
eaten by wild animals.
13I'll punish her for the days
she worshiped Baal
and burned incense to him.
I'll punish her for the times
she forgot about me
and wore jewelry and rings
to attract her lovers.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
The Lord Will Help Israel
14Israel, I, the Lord,
will lure you into the desert
and speak gently to you.
15 I will return your vineyards,
and then Trouble Valley
will become Hopeful Valley.
You will say “Yes” to me
as you did in your youth,
when leaving Egypt.
16I promise from that day on, you will call me your husband instead of your master. 17I will no longer even let you mention the names of those pagan gods that you called “Master.” 18And I will agree to let you live in peace—you will no longer be attacked by wild animals and birds or by weapons of war. 19I will accept you as my wife forever, and instead of a bride price I will give you justice, fairness, love, kindness, 20and faithfulness. Then you will truly know who I am.
21I will command the sky to send rain on the earth, 22and it will produce grain, grapes, and olives in Jezreel Valley. 23 I will scatter the seeds and show mercy to Lo-Ruhamah. I will say to Lo-Ammi, “You are my people,” and they will answer, “You are our God.”
translation_text:
1Kina pu na, ni li yin ninaabitiib Israel yaab ke, “Uwumbɔr Aanib,” ki ki yin bi ke, “Uwumbɔr aah gee bi na.”
Gomer ni Israel yaab aah kaa dii mbamɔm pu na
2Maabim, nina aa ki ye mpuu, le u mu aachal aa ki ye mi, tɔ, ni mu tee gaŋ u man. Gaŋ u ke u di cha kidagook. 3U yaa kaa di cha kan, m ga gbabr u ki cha u uŋmeen ke baah nan ma u nwiin mundaal na. M ga ŋa u nkuun ke kitiŋ ki kaa kpa tijikaar na, le ki cha nnyunyuu ku u. 4-5Maan san waabim kinimbaak; bi ye upiidagoor u kaa san inimɔɔn na aabim la. Uma ubaa le len ke, “M ga buen mbɔtiib chee la, bi tii mi tijikaar ni nnyun, ki tii mi ŋikeken, ni olif aakpan, ni ndaan.”
6Kina pu na, m ga di ikokon le gob u ki maa ligoln kiir waasan. 7U ga li san paa ubɔtiib pu, le kaan pii bi. U ga ban bi, kaan kan bi, le ki bui ke, “M ga gir nchakpok chee la, nima chee nan soor ni maah gur bi pu na.”
8Waan kii daalbaadaal ke ni ye mi le tii u tijikaar, ni ndaan, ni olif aakpan, ni tikunabr, ni salmaa u mɔmɔk u joo dooni liwaal Baal na. 9Kina pu na, lijikaacheel yoonn kan, m ga gaa maajikaar ni ndaan, ki gaa ŋikeken ŋi m tii u ke u li joo gbae na. 10M ga gbabr u ki cha u uŋmeen ubɔtiib aanimbil ni, le ubaa aan ŋmaa nyan u maapɔɔn ni. 11M ga kuln waajim mɔmɔk; m ga kuln libiln libiln, ni uŋmal uŋmal, ni likpaakool daal aajim, ni njim mu u siin na mɔmɔk. 12M ga bii ndaan aasubil aasui ni ŋisubil ŋiken aasui, i u bui ke waah tun tii ubɔtiib pu na le bi tii u na. M ga cha waadaan aasubil aasui ni ŋisubil ŋiken aasui na kpaln kichook, ipeel le ga bii ni mɔmɔk. 13N‑yoonn mu mɔmɔk u nan sulni mbɔr ki seer tulalee aayon tii liwaal Baal ki peeni nleenyaan ki san dii ubɔtiib na pu le m ga daa utafal. Uwumbɔr le len kina.
Uwumbɔr aah gee waanib pu na
14Kina pu na, m ga ki giin u buen nteersakpiin ni, nima chee le m ga ti ki di tibɔmbɔr gaa u. 15M ga ki di waah nan kpa ndaan aasubil aasar ti na tii u, ki cha kifataŋ ki bi yin ki ke Tibɔbir aafataŋ na kpaln limakl aabisamɔb. Waah nan laa ye usapɔɔn, ki nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki keei mi pu na, kina le u ga ki kii mi, 16le ki ga ki yin mi ke uchal, waan ki yin mi waaninkpel ke waah yin liwaal Baal pu na. 17Maan ki cha u yin liwaal Baal aayimbil kpala.
18N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ni ipeel, ni inyoon i bir na ga puu tipuukpaan tii tɔb, le ni taa ŋa maanib nibaa. M ga ki nyan butɔb aajawan mɔmɔk ni ye kijaak aajum na, ni itɔi na kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki cha maanib li bi nsuudoon, ni lifuur ni.
19Israel, m ga di si ŋa mpuu,
maan nya aapuwɔb, ki ga li bi mbamɔm aa chee;
m ga mɔk si ngeehm mu bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, ni kinimbaak,
ki cha aa li ye min yoo ki ti saa
n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
20M ga li joo maah puu tipuur ti na ki cha aa li ye min yoo,
ki cha aa bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.
21-22N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga kii maanib Israel yaab aameel.
M ga cha utaal nu kitiŋ pu,
le kitiŋ ga ŋa tijikaar, ni ŋisubil ni olif aasui.
23M ga maa maanib kaan kitiŋ ngbaan pu ki tii bi liwangol.
M ga mɔk baah nan yin bi ke “Maa‑neen” bi na ngeehm,
ki ga bui baah yin bi ke “Baa‑ye‑maanib” na ke “Bi‑ye‑maanib” la,
le bi ga kii ke, “Aa ye timi Aawumbɔr la.”

english_text:
God's Love Offers Hope
1Once again the Lord spoke to me. And this time he said, “Hosea, fall in love with an unfaithful woman who has a lover. Do this to show that I love the people of Israel, even though they worship idols and enjoy the offering cakes made with fruit.”
2So I paid 15 pieces of silver and about 150 kilograms of grain for such a woman. 3Then I said, “Now you are mine! You will have to remain faithful to me, though it will be a long time before we sleep together.”
4It will also be a long time before Israel has a king or before sacrifices are offered at the temple or before there is any way to get guidance from God. 5But later, Israel will turn back to the Lord their God and to David their king. At that time they will come to the Lord with fear and trembling, and he will be good to them.
translation_text:
Hosea ni upii u nyan upuwɔb na
1Le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Gir ki ti di ngeehm tii upii u bi ubɔɔn chee na. Aa li gee u ke maah gee Israel aanib pu na, aa mu tee lik kan, bi di bibaa tii ŋiwaa le ki gee ke bi li joo ŋisubil ŋi kuur na tii ŋiwaa ipiin.”
2Le m nan pan tikunabr aamombil kipiik ni ŋiŋmu, ni njikaabim kuruwaa nkub ni piiŋmu u pu. 3M nan bui u ke u ga kal ni yunn pam, ki taa tun kidagook aatuln, ki kiir mi, le n‑yoonn ngbaan na m ga li ka kii u. 4Kina le Israel yaab mu ga li gur bi, kaa kpa bibɔrb ni bisalolm, kaan ki li kpa kitork ki toor, kaan li kpa ŋitakpal ŋi bi toor na, kaan li kpa ŋiwaa, bee tiwanaankaan nibaa ke bi li joo buu tibɔɔr. 5Tɔ, n‑yoonn tee choo, le Israel aanib ga nan ki fenn dan Bidindaan Uwumbɔr chee, ki dan ubɔr David aayaabil chee. Le bi ga li san Uwumbɔr ki gaa waapiin i ŋan na.

english_text:
Israel Is Unfaithful
1Israel, listen
as the Lord accuses
everyone in the land!
No one is faithful or loyal
or truly cares about God.
2Cursing, dishonesty, murder,
robbery, unfaithfulness—
these happen all the time.
Violence is everywhere.
3And so your land is a desert.
Every living creature is dying—
people and wild animals,
birds and fish.
The Lord Warns the Priests
4Don't accuse just anyone!
Not everyone is at fault.
My case is against you,
the priests.
5You and the prophets
will stumble day and night;
I'll silence your mothers.
6You priests have rejected me,
and my people are destroyed
by refusing to obey.
Now I'll reject you and forget
your children, because you
have forgotten my Law.
7By adding more of you priests,
you multiply the number
of people who sin.
Now I'll change your pride
into shame.
8You encourage others to sin,
so you can stuff yourselves
on their sin offerings.
9That's why I will punish
the people for their deeds,
just as I will punish
you priests.
10Their food won't satisfy,
and having sex at pagan shrines
won't produce children.
My people have rebelled
11and have been unfaithful
to me, their Lord.
God Condemns Israel's Idolatry
My people, you are foolish
because of too much pleasure
and too much wine.
12You expect wooden idols
and other objects of wood
to give you advice.
Lusting for sex at pagan shrines
has made you unfaithful
to me, your God.
13You offer sacrifices
on mountaintops and hills,
under oak trees, and wherever
good shade is found.
Your own daughters
and daughters-in-law
sell themselves for sex.
14But I won't punish them.
You men are to blame,
because you go to prostitutes
and offer sacrifices with them
at pagan shrines.
Your own foolishness
will lead to your ruin.
15Israel, you are unfaithful,
but don't lead Judah to sin.
Stop worshiping at Gilgal
or at sinful Bethel.
And quit making promises
in my name—the name
of the living Lord.
16You are nothing more
than a stubborn cow—
so stubborn that I, the Lord,
cannot feed you like lambs
in an open pasture.
17You people of Israel
are charmed by idols.
Leave those people alone!
18You get drunk, then sleep
with prostitutes;
you would rather be vulgar
than lead a decent life.
19And so you will be swept away
in a whirlwind
for sacrificing to idols.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah nan galn Israel yaab pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan kpa ngalm u galn binib bi koo kitiŋ kee pu na. Israel yaab, li pel man waah len pu na; “Mbimbin mu bi chob na, ni ngeehm, aa bi kitiŋ kee pu, le binib ngbaan aa nyi ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. 2Bi puur tipuur le ki bii ti; bi geei inyamɔn, ki ku binib, ki su kinaayuk, ki ban tɔb aapuutiib. Libiil moo kpae la, le linikul libaa paa liken pu. 3Kina pu le kitiŋ ga kuur, le tiwan nimɔk bi ki pu na ga kpoi. Tiwakor, ni inyoon, ni ijan mu ga kpoi.”
Uwumbɔr aah galn bitotoorb pu na
4Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ubaa taa galn binib ngbaan ki taa sak bi; nimi bitotoorb chee le maagalm cha. 5Kinyeek ni nwiin pu mɔk ni moo bii cha, le bibɔnabr mu bi kina la. M ban m kuln nina Israel la. 6Maanib aah kaa bee mi na, le baamɔfal ga junn. Nimi bitotoorb yii ke naan bee mi, le ki yii maakaal, kina pu le m mu yii nimi, kaan kii ke nijapɔtiib li ye maatotoorb.
7“Nimi bitotoorb aah wiir pu na, kina le naah tun mi titunwanbir ti na mu wiir, le ki ga cha m kpeln nimi aanyuŋ ŋa inimɔɔn. 8Maanib aatunwanbir pu le ni moo kani titunwanbir aatork aawangol, le ki ban ke bi li moo tun titunwanbir. 9Nimi ni binib ngbaan aatafadaan ga li ye tiwanbaan la. M ga daa nitafal ki cha ni pa naah tun titunwanbir ti na pu. 10Bi yaa toor kitork kan, ni ga ji nimi yaan, ki mu aan bab. Ni ga li dii timar aawaa, ki mu aan li kpa mbim, ba pu? ni fenn nipuwɔb tii mi, le ki ti dii ŋiwaa.”
Uwumbɔr aah bui ke ŋiwaa aatoor aah kaa ŋan pu na
11Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ndakpok ni ndapɔm le gaa maanib aalan. 12Lidɔgeln chee le bi chaa ti baa tibɔkpiirkaan. Ndɔ le tuk bi baah ban ke bi li nyi tiwan ni na. Bi di mi Uwumbɔr di mee. Bi di bibaa tii ŋiwaa ke upii u di ubaa ŋa udagoor na la. 13Ŋijoo paab le bi toor ŋiwaa, le ki seer nnyɔknii isui sakpiin i aabon taln buen dandar na taab, ŋigongon pu, isui aaboon aah mɔ ni chee na, kina pu le nibisatiib joo bibaa kooh, le nibipuutiib mu kpaln bidagoob. 14Nimi ni bipiib bi bi nimi aawaadir ni na aah tun kidagook aatuln ki toor tijɔŋ aatork na pu, le maan daa nibisatiib ni nibipuutiib aatafal. Liyataŋakl libaa le len ke, ‘Binib yaa bi kaa kpa nlan kan, bi wɔŋ la.’
15“Tɔ, nimi Israel aanib aa kii maamɔb, Juda yaab ma taa ji kina aabɔkpol. Ni taa ki buen Gilgal, bee Bef Afenn ki ti doon mi, ki taa puu tipuur nima chee min Uwumbɔr u bi na aayimbil pu. 16Israel aanib aatafal pɔɔ ke uŋoob na la. Maan kpiin bi mmoŋmɔpaan ni ke ipihbi na. 17Ŋiwaa le chuu Israel aanib. Cha bi li dii baah gee nsan mu na. 18Bi yaa ti nyun ndaan bab kan, le bi fii lir kidagook pu, le ki neen inimɔɔn n‑yoonn ngbaan ki jer kipak. 19Uwumbɔr ga di bi buen ke kinaakpaajabuŋ le aah daar bi cha na, le inimɔɔn ga chuu bi ŋiwaa aatork pu.

english_text:
Israel and Judah Will Be Judged
The Lord said:
1Listen, you priests!
Pay attention, Israel!
Listen, you members
of the royal family.
Justice was your duty.
But at Mizpah and Mount Tabor
you trapped the people.
2At the place of worship
you were a treacherous pit,
and I will punish you.
3Israel, I know all about you,
and because of your unfaithfulness,
I find you unacceptable.
4Your evil deeds are the reason
you won't return to me,
your Lord God.
And your constant craving for sex
keeps you from knowing me.
5Israel, your pride
testifies to your guilt;
it makes you stumble,
and Judah stumbles too.
6You offer sheep and cattle
as sacrifices to me,
but I have turned away
and refuse to be found.
7You have been unfaithful
to me, your Lord;
you have had children
by prostitutes.
So at the New Moon Festival,
you and your crops
will be destroyed.
The Lord Warns Israel and Judah
8Give a warning on the trumpet!
Let it be heard in Gibeah,
Ramah, and sinful Bethel.
Benjamin, watch out!
9I, the Lord, will punish
and wipe out Israel.
This is my solemn promise
to every tribe of Israel.
10Judah's leaders are like crooks
who move boundary markers;
that's why I will flood them
with my anger.
11Israel was brutally crushed.
They got what they deserved
for worshiping useless idols.
12Now I, the Lord,
will fill Israel with maggots
and make Judah rot.
13When Israel and Judah saw
their sickness and wounds,
Israel asked help from Assyria
and its mighty king.
But the king cannot cure them
or heal their wounds.
14So I'll become a fierce lion
attacking Israel and Judah.
I'll snatch and carry off
what I want,
and no one can stop me.
15Then I'll return to my temple
until they confess their guilt
and worship me,
until they are desperate
and beg for my help.
translation_text:
1“Nimi bitotoorb, li pel nimina man. Israel yaab, pel man. Nimi bi ye nnaan ni yaab na, li pel man. Nimi aatuln le ye ke ni di ibamɔn ji binib tibɔr, kina pu na, m ga ji nimi tibɔr. Ni kpaln gaawɔb le ki dɔ Mispa, le ki ye kipɔɔk Tabor aajool pu, 2le ki ye libuusakpeln Sitim aatiŋ ponn ni, le m ga daa ni mɔmɔk aatafal. 3M nyi Israel aah bi pu na, waan ŋmaa bɔr mi. U nyan mpuwɔb, le waanib aa ŋeer ke bi li dooni mi.”
Hosea aah sak bi ŋiwaa aatork pu aabɔr pu na
4Binib ngbaan aah tun titunwanbir ti na le cha baa ŋmaa gir ni Baawumbɔr chee. Ŋiwaa kpa bi pu mpɔɔn, le baa ki nyi Uwumbɔr. 5Israel yaab aagaak mɔk ke bi kpa ngalm. Baatunwanbir cha bi gbeer le ki lir, le Juda aanib mu lir dii bi. 6Bi joo baapiih ni inaa ki ti kɔr toor ke bi tii Uwumbɔr la, le naa ter bi. Waah siir cha bi na, le baa kan u. 7Bi nyan Uwumbɔr aapuwɔb; kina pu le baabim aa ye waabim. Kina pu le naan yunn le baatim ga kuln.
Juda ni Israel yaab aatɔb aabɔr
8Pii butɔb aakpiin Gibea aatiŋ ni man. Faa nkuun Rama aatiŋ ni man. Faa butɔb aakuun Bef Afenn aatiŋ ni. Benjaminn aajab, fii buen butɔb ni man. 9Ntafadaan aawiin choo, le Israel aatiŋ ga ber. Israel aanib, nimina ga sil ŋa.
10Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Juda aanib aayidam aah koo Israel aatiŋ ni ki sun kaatiŋ ngem na, le maaŋuul fii. Kina pu na, m ga cha ntafadaan dan bi pu ke nwam na. 11Israel yaab bi ji limukl aafalaa la, ki lann kitiŋ ki nan ye bibaa aatiŋ na, ba pu? bi nan si chaa ti ban nterm binib bi kaan ŋmaa ter bi na chee la. 12M ga kuln Israel ni Juda yaab.
13“Israel aatiŋ nan kan kaah bun pu na, Juda mu kan kibaa aabuun na, le Israel buen Asiria aabɔrkpaan na chee ki ti ban nterm, le waa nan ŋmaa tii ki laafee, bee u yann kaabuun. 14M ga tak Israel ni Juda aanib ke uchinn na la. Min mbaa le ga daa par par bi, ki siir cha bi. M yaa nan dar bi cha kan, ubaa aan ŋmaa gaa bi lii.
15“M ga siir cha maanib, ki ti saa buyoonn bi ga ji falaa u ŋeer baatunwanbir ki gir ban ni mi na. Nibaakan bi ga fenn ban mi limukl ngbaan ni.”

english_text:
The Lord's People Speak
1Let's return to the Lord.
He has torn us to shreds,
but he will bandage our wounds
and make us well.
2In two or three days
he will heal us
and restore our strength
that we may live with him.
3Let's do our best
to know the Lord.
His coming is as certain
as the morning sun;
he will refresh us like rain
renewing the earth
in the springtime.
The Lord Speaks to Israel and Judah
4People of Israel and Judah,
what can I do with you?
Your love for me disappears
more quickly than mist
or dew at sunrise.
5That's why I slaughtered you
with the words
of my prophets.
That's why my judgments blazed
like the dawning sun.
6 I'd rather for you to be faithful
and to know me
than to offer sacrifices.
7At a place named Adam,
you betrayed me
by breaking our agreement.
8Everyone in Gilead is evil;
your hands are stained
with the blood of victims.
9You priests are like a gang
of robbers in ambush.
On the road to Shechem
you murder and commit
other horrible crimes.
10I have seen a terrible thing
in Israel—
you are unfaithful
and unfit to worship me.
11People of Judah,
your time is coming too.
The Lord Wants To Help Israel
I, the Lord, would like to make
my nation prosper again
translation_text:
Binib aah ŋmann ke bi yii titunwanbir pu na
1Binib ngbaan len ke, “Cha ti gir Uwumbɔr chee man. U tii timi titotonn, le ki ga sil tii timi laafee; u tii timi ibuun, le ki ga sil ban litaln poo biin i pu, u ga sil ŋa kina. 2U ga ki gaa timi iwiin ilee aakaasisik ni, le ti ga li bi unimbiin ni. 3Cha ti pɔɔn tibaa man ki li nyi Uwumbɔr, ki nyi waah ban pu na. U ga sil dan ti chee ke kitaak aah ga woln pu na, u ga dan ti chee ke unaalantaal u sɔŋni kitiŋ na.”
4Le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel ni Juda yaab, m ga ki ŋa nimi kinye? Naah kpa ngeehm mu m pu na fir mala ke kichakpiik ni aakpakpal na la, ki naahn limaln li fir nchakpawiin pu na. 5Kina pu le m di maah ga daa nitafal ki kuln nimi pu na tun ni maabɔnabr. Maah ban pu ni chee na aa duk kpala: 6M ban nimi aageehm le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, maa ban nimi aatork baanja la. M ga li gee ke maanib li nyi mi ki jer ke bi li joo kitork seer mmii ni tii mi.
7“Tɔ, baah ti kpaan koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, le bi bii tipuur ti m ni bima nan puu tii tɔb na, ke Adam aah nan bii pu na. 8Gilead ye kitiŋ ki gbii titunwanbirdam ni binikurb na la. 9Bitotoorb na bi ke kinaayupaak ki ti dɔ nsan ni kiir unii na la. Hali bi yaa cha Sekem aatiŋ ki bi chain na ni kan, bi ku binib nsan ni la. Bi po nyi le ki tun titunwanbir timina mɔmɔk. 10M kan tibɔbir tibaa Israel aatiŋ ni: tima le ye ke maanib Israel yaab bii bibaa le ki dooni ŋiwaa.
11“Le nimi Juda aanib ma, m siin n‑yoonn mu m ga di daa ni mu aatafal na.

english_text:
1and to heal its wounds.
But then I see the crimes
in Israel and Samaria.
Everyone is deceitful;
robbers roam the streets.
2No one realizes
that I have seen their sins
surround them like a flood.
3The king and his officials
take great pleasure
in their sin and deceit.
4Everyone burns with desire—
they are like coals in an oven,
ready to burst into flames.
5On the day their king
was crowned,
his officials got him drunk,
and he joined
in their foolishness.
6Their anger is a fire
that smolders all night,
then flares up at dawn.
7They are flames
destroying their leaders.
And their kings are powerless;
none of them trust me.
8The people of Israel
have mixed with foreigners;
they are a thin piece of bread
scorched on one side.
9They don't seem to realize
how weak and feeble they are;
their hair has turned gray,
while foreigners rule.
10I am the Lord, their God,
but in all of their troubles
their pride keeps them
from returning to me.
No Help from Foreign Nations
The Lord said:
11Israel is a senseless bird,
fluttering back and forth
between Egypt and Assyria.
12But I will catch them in a net
as hunters trap birds;
I threatened to punish them,
and indeed I will.
13Trouble and destruction
will be their reward
for rejecting me.
I would have rescued them,
but they told me lies.
14They don't really pray to me;
they just howl in their beds.
They have rejected me for Baal
and slashed themselves,
in the hope that Baal
will bless their crops.
15I taught them what they know,
and I made them strong.
Now they plot against me
16and refuse to obey.
They are more useless
than a crooked arrow.
Their leaders will die in war
for saying foolish things.
Egyptians will laugh at them.
translation_text:
1“M yaa ti ban ke m tii maanib Israel yaab laafee, ki ki tii bi nkam kan, m kani baatunwanbir ni mbiin mu bi tun na baanja la. Bi ji tɔb la; bi koo biken aadichal ni le ki su kinaayuk; ki su binib kinaayuk kitiŋ ponn ni. 2Naa kee koo biyil ni ke m ga teer titunwanbir timina mɔmɔk; le baatunwanbir mann goln bi, le maan ŋmaa yii ke maa waa ti.”
Libɔrchiln ni aabeebee aakpokl
3Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Binib joo baatunwanbir aakpokl le ŋmanni ubɔr ni waaninkpiib. 4Bi mɔmɔk ye nchakpokjum, le kaa si ubɔr aachaŋ ni. Baabiin nyakr ke baah pu boroboro nin chee na aamii mu unii u pu boroboro na aa tur mu ŋani ke boroboro ti nin ŋeer buyoonn u ga pu u na la. 5Ubɔr aajim daal, le bi cha ubɔr ni waaninkpiib nyu ndaan gbii le ki jɔr. 6Mbamɔn, baakpokl wu ke baah pu boroboro nin chee na aamii na la. Kinyeek ni kitaak aawoln pu, baaŋuul nyakr la, le kichakpiik ni kan, li gaa mmii.
7“Baaŋuul aakaasisik ni le bi ku baajojoob. Bi ku baabɔrb paani tɔb pu la. Le ubaa aa tee mee mi ki ban nterm.”
Israel ni ŋitimbol ŋiken aabɔr
8Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel aanib bi ke boroboro u bi pun u aan waa biir mbamɔm na la. Bi ka lik ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln bi na pu le ki ban nterm, 9kaa nyi ke biniyayam aaterm ngbaan gaal baapɔɔn la. Baawiin aa ki daa, le baa kpaan nyi. 10Israel aanib aagaak wii ban bi la. Hali tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋa na pu, baa fenn ki gir ni min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr chee. 11Israel chuun fii labr ke linanjel li kaa kpa nlan na la; njan, kaanib nan buen Ijipt yaab chee le ti ban nterm, le ki fenn san buen Asiria yaab chee. 12Bi yaa bi jer kan, m ga taln kipɔɔk ki chur bi ke inyoon na. Baah tun titunwanbir ti na pu le m ga daa bitafal.
13“Baamɔfal junn a. Bi di mi lii le ki nyan mpuwɔb. Bi ga kuln. M ba ban ke m ter bi la, le bi mu aa dii mi mbamɔm. 14Baa joo bisui mɔmɔk mee mi, le ki labr lir kitiŋ le ki kaani ke binib bi kaa dii maasan na aah ŋani pu na. Bi yaa bi mee ban njikaabim ni ndaan kan, bi joo njum le geei bibaa ke binib bi kaa dii maasan na aah ŋani pu na. Bi ye binib bi kaa keei min Uwumbɔr aamɔb na la. 15Min le nan kpiin bi ki tii bi mpɔɔn, le bi fenn ki kpokl m pu. 16Bi nya mpuwɔb n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le ki dii liwaal li kaa kpa mpɔɔn mubaa na. Saan ŋmaa li kpa bi pu limakl ke butɔm bu gɔr na la. Baasalolm aah len tibɔr kigaak ŋmeen na, le bi ga kpo mpɔɔkun, le Ijipt yaab ga laa bi.”

english_text:
Israel Rejects the Lord
The Lord said:
1Sound a warning!
Israel, you broke our agreement
and ignored my teaching.
Now an eagle is swooping down
to attack my land.
2Israel, you say, “We claim you,
the Lord, as our God.”
3But your enemies
will chase you for rejecting
our good agreement.
4You chose kings and leaders
without consulting me;
you made silver and gold idols
that led to your downfall.
5City of Samaria, I'm angry
because of your idol
in the shape of a calf.
When will you ever
be innocent again?
6Someone from Israel built
that idol for you,
but only I am God.
And so it will be smashed
to pieces.
7If you scatter wind
instead of wheat,
you will harvest a whirlwind
and have no wheat.
Even if you harvest grain,
enemies will steal it all.
8Israel, you are ruined,
and now the nations
consider you worthless.
9You are like a wild donkey
that goes its own way.
You've run off to Assyria
and hired them as allies.
10You can bargain with nations,
but I'll catch you anyway.
Soon you will suffer abuse
by kings and rulers.
11Israel, you have built
many altars where you offer
sacrifices for sin.
But these altars have become
places for sin.
12My instructions for sacrifices
were written in detail,
but you ignored them.
13You sacrifice your best animals
and eat the sacrificial meals,
but I, the Lord,
refuse your offerings.
I will remember your sins
and punish you.
Then you will return to Egypt.
14Israel, I created you,
but you forgot me.
You and Judah built palaces
and many strong cities.
Now I will send fire to destroy
your towns and fortresses.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah galn Israel yaab baah dooni ŋiwaa pu na aabɔr
1Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Faa nkuun man. Bidim boon nan lir maatiŋ pu ke ŋikaagii na la. Maanib bii tipuur ti m nan puu tii bi na, le ki yii maamɔkm. 2Bi yin mi ke Baawumbɔr la, le ki bui ke bi ye maanib le ki nyi mi, 3le ki tee yii lituln li ŋan na. Kina pu na, baadim ga li ban bi.
4“Maanib leer baabɔrb, le kaa ŋɔɔni m pu. Bi leer baasalolm, le kaa ŋɔɔni m pu. Bi di baakunabr ni salmaa le ki naan ŋiwaa; ŋima le ga kuln bi. 5Maa gee Samaria aanib aah di salmaa naan unaaja u ke u ye liwaal ki dooni u na. Maaŋuul fii bi pu sakpen a. Bayoonn aan bi ga di cha ŋiwaa aabɔr? 6Israel aawanaann ubaa le naan li, laa ye Uwumbɔr. Samaria yaab aah dooni salmaa aanaaja u na ga wii yuk yuk. 7Bi yaa bun libuln kan, kitaabuŋ le bi ga nan chee. Njikaabim mu bi nkpaakon ni kaa biir na aan ŋmaa ŋa tijikaar. Hali mu yaa biir kan, biwɔwɔm le ga di mu ŋmɔ. 8Israel gur bi ke ŋitimbol ŋiken aah bi pu na la, kaa bi tibaa ni ke libuul li wii na, 9ki kpa tafalaaŋun ke iŋoob na. Israel aanib bi bibaa pu la. Bi buen Asiria aatiŋ pu ti ban nterm, le ki pan ŋitimbol ŋiken ŋimombil ke ŋi ter bi. 10Le m ga kuun bi ki daa bitafal. Naan yunn le Asiria aabɔrkpaan ga di limukl pii bi, le bi ga lir ki biln kitiŋ iween pu.
11“Israel aanib aah moo maa kitork aabimbin ke bi kan titunwanbir aachapinn na, kina le bi moo kani nin chee bi ga tun titunwanbir na. 12M ŋmee ikaal i aa ti ki nyi imɔk na tii binib ngbaan, le bi yii i ke i ye tiwɔwɔwan, ni tiwachann le bi chee. 13Bi toor kitork tii mi, le ki ŋmɔ kaanann. Le min Uwumbɔr aasui aa piin bi pu, le m ga teer baatunwanbir n‑yoonn mumina ki daa bitafal ti pu; m ga giin bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni.
14“Israel aanib maa ŋibɔrdichal, le ki tee suln Uwumbɔr u naan bi na bɔr. Juda aanib maa ntim mu kpa tijawan aan bi maa ŋigon gob mu na. Le m ga cha mmii wu baabɔrdichal ni ntim ngbaan.”

english_text:
Israel Will Be Punished
1Israel, don't celebrate
or make noisy shouts
like other nations.
You have been unfaithful
to your God.
Wherever grain is threshed,
you behave like prostitutes
because you enjoy
the money you receive.
2But you will run short
of grain and wine,
3and you will have to leave
the land of the Lord.
Some of you will go to Egypt;
others will go to Assyria
and eat unclean food.
4You won't be able to offer
sacrifices of wine
to the Lord.
None of your sacrifices
will please him—
they will be unclean
like food offered to the dead.
Your food will only be used
to satisfy your hunger;
none of it will be brought
to the Lord's temple.
5You will no longer be able
to celebrate the festival
of the Lord.
6Even if you escape alive,
you will end up in Egypt
and be buried in Memphis.
Your silver treasures
will be lost among weeds;
thorns will sprout in your tents.
7 Israel, the time has come.
You will get what you deserve,
and you will know it.
“Prophets are fools,” you say.
“And God's messengers
are crazy.”
Your terrible guilt
has filled you with hatred.
8Israel, the Lord sent me
to look after you.
But you trap his prophets
and flood his temple
with your hatred.
9 You are brutal and corrupt,
as were the men of Gibeah.
But God remembers your sin,
and you will be punished.
Sin's Terrible Results
10 Israel, when I, the Lord,
found you long ago
it was like finding
grapes in a barren desert
or tender young figs.
Then you worshiped Baal Peor,
that disgusting idol,
and you became as disgusting
as the idol you loved.
11And so, Israel, your glory
will fly away like birds—
your women will no longer
be able to give birth.
12Even if you do have children,
I will take them all
and leave you to mourn.
I will turn away,
and you will sink down
in deep trouble.
13Israel, when I first met you,
I thought of you as palm trees
growing in fertile ground.
Now you lead your people out,
only to be slaughtered.
Hosea's Advice
14Our Lord, do just one thing
for your people—
make their women unable
to have children
or to nurse their babies.
The Lord's Judgment on Israel
15Israel, I first began
to hate you because
you did evil at Gilgal.
Now I will chase you
out of my house.
No longer will I love you;
your leaders betrayed me.
16Israel, you are a vine
with dried-up roots
and fruitless branches.
Even if you had more children
and loved them dearly,
I would slaughter them all.
Hosea Warns Israel
17Israel, you disobeyed my God.
Now he will force you to roam
from nation to nation.
translation_text:
Hosea aah moon Israel yaab aatafadaan aabɔr pu na
1Israel aanib, taa ki ji nimi aajim ke binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na aah ŋani pu na. Ni fenn nipuwɔb tii nimi Aawumbɔr le kaa keei waamɔb. Kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu, ni di nibaa kooh ke upiidagoor na le ki di tii liwaal Baal, le ki gee tijikaar ti ni dak ke u joo pa nimi na. 2Tɔ, naan yunn le nimi aajikaar, ni olif aakpan aan ki ŋeer nimi, le ndaan mu ga doo. 3Israel aanib aan ki li bi Uwumbɔr aatiŋ pu, bi ga gir buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki ga ti li ji tijikaar ti bi kɔ na Asiria aatiŋ ni. 4Baan ti ŋmaa tii Uwumbɔr ndaan aapiin, biwɔwɔm aatim ngbaan ni, kaan ŋmaa di baatork buen unimbiin ni. Biwɔwɔm ngbaan aajikaar ga bii umɔk jin ti na, ke baah jin likpuul ponn ni aajikaar pu na la. Bi ga li ji ti ke ti lee baakon la; ti ponn ni tibaa aan ŋmaa koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni ki ye ipiin tii u. 5Le n‑yoonn yaa nan fuu ni ke bi ji njim ki nyuŋ Uwumbɔr kan, baan li nyi baah ga ŋa pu na. 6Libiil yaa nan fuu ni ki yaa binib ngbaan kan, le Ijipt yaab ga kuun bi. Bi ga kuun bi ti sub Memfis aatiŋ ni la. Le timoor ni ikokon ga gaa baadichal ni baawangol aah nan si nin chee n‑yoonn mubaa na.
7Ntafadaan aayoonn fuu a, n‑yoonn ngbaan binib ga kan ni ŋeer bi na. Kina yaa nan ŋa kan, Israel yaab ga bee ni. Ni bui ke, “Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr umina ye ujɔr la. Unii u Nfuur Nyaan fir u pu ngbaan na aa ki kpa nlan la.” Nimi aatunwanbir aah nyaŋ na le kinanaŋ gbiin nimi. 8Uwumbɔr tun ni mi ke ubɔnabr na, ke m nan sak waanib Israel yaab. Le m yaa buen nimɔk na kan, ni pɔɔni nibaa ke ni chuu mi ke unyoon na. Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aanib aadin le ye uma Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr. 9Baatuln mɔmɔk ponn ni ye titunwanbir le kaa kpa ŋitataa, ke baah nan bi Gibea aatiŋ ni pu na. Uwumbɔr ga teer baatunwanbir le ki daa bitafal ti pu.
Israel aatunwanbir ni taapar
10Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Maah nan puen kan Israel na, ni nan bi ke unii aah kan ŋisubil nteersakpiin ni kan, ni bi pu na la. Maah nan puen kan niyaajatiib na, ni nan bi ke aa yaa kan ŋikakan ŋi puen puir na kan, ni bi pu na la. Baah nan fuu ni Peor Aajool chee na, le bi piin ki gur dooni liwaal Baal, le ki ŋa fam ke ŋiwaa ŋi bi gee ŋi na. 11Israel aayimbil ga fii buen ke unyoon na, le baan ki maa mbim, bipudam mu aan ki li bi, baan ki dek mbim aapuu. 12Tɔ, bi yaa ma mbim kan, m ga yoor bi mɔmɔk kaan gur ubaa. N‑yoonn mu m siir cha binib bee na kan, tibɔbir pam le ga kan bi.”
13M waa Efraim aanib bi lipepel li ŋan na ni, ke Taya aatiŋ na. Efraim mu ga nya baabim bi ti ku bi. 14Ba aan m ga bui ke aa ŋa binib bee? Cha baapiib kpaln biŋoob. Cha bi taa ki ŋmaa kpiin baabipɔm.
Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Israel yaab tibɔr pu na
15Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Baatunwanbir mɔmɔk nan piin Gilgal aatiŋ ni la. Maa ki gee bi nima chee. Le baah tun titunwanbir ti na pu, m ga jenn nyan bi maatiŋ pu. Maan ki li kpa bi pu ngeehm; baasalolm mɔmɔk fii sil m pu la. 16Israel aanib bi ke busub bu aanyaan kuur aan bu aa ki lu na la. Baan ki maa mbim, le bi ti ki ma bi kan, m ga ku baah gee baabim bi sakpen na.”
Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr aah len Israel yaab aabɔr pu na
17Maah dii Uwumbɔr u na ga yii waanib, baah kaa ŋun tii u pu na pu. Bi ga kpaln bichayiim le ŋitimbol ponn ni.

english_text:
1You were a healthy vine
covered with grapes.
But the more grapes you grew,
the more altars you built;
the better off you became,
the better shrines you set up
for pagan gods.
2You are deceitful and disloyal.
So you will pay
for your sins,
because the Lord will destroy
your altars and images.
3“We don't have a king,”
you will say.
“We don't fear the Lord.
And what good are kings?”
4Israel, you break treaties
and don't keep promises;
you turn justice
into poisonous weeds
where healthy plants should grow.
5All who live in Samaria tremble
with concern for the idols
at sinful Bethel.
The idol there was the pride
of the priests,
but it has been put to shame;
now everyone will cry.
6It will be taken to Assyria
and given to the great king.
Then Israel will be disgraced
for worshiping that idol.
7Like a twig in a stream,
the king of Samaria
will be swept away.
8 The altars at sinful Bethel
will be destroyed
for causing Israel to sin;
they will be grown over
with thorns and thistles.
Then everyone will beg
the mountains and hills
to cover and protect them.
