The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
9 Israel, you have never
stopped sinning
since that time at Gibeah.
That's why you
will be attacked at Gibeah.
10Your sins have doubled,
and you are rebellious.
Now I have decided
to send nations to attack
and put you in chains.
11Once you were obedient
like a calf
that loved to thresh grain.
But I will put a harness
on your beautiful neck;
you and Judah must plow
and cultivate the ground.
12 Plow your fields,
scatter seeds of justice,
and harvest faithfulness.
Worship me, the Lord,
and I will send my saving power
down like rain.
13You have planted evil,
harvested injustice, and eaten
the fruit of your lies.
You trusted your own strength
and your powerful forces.
14So war will break out,
and your fortresses
will be destroyed.
Your enemies will do to you
what Shalman did to the people
of Beth-Arbel—
mothers and their children
will be beaten to death
against rocks.
15Bethel, this will be your fate
because of your evil.
Israel, at dawn your king
will be killed.
translation_text:
1Israel aanib nan bi ke ŋisubil aasub bu lun ŋisubil sakpen na la. Buyoonn bi moo kan liwangol na, le bi too maa ŋiwaa aatork aabimbin kpae. Buyoonn baatiŋ moo ŋani tijikaar na, le bi too toor ŋiwaa ŋi bi dooni na ke ŋi li ŋan. 2Binib bi aasui ni ye ŋŋmann ŋmeen na ga ji baatunwanbir aafalaa. Uwumbɔr ga gbaa wii baawaa ni ŋaabimbin ngbaan ki tur ŋi lir.
3Binib ngbaan ga piin ki bi len ke, “Taah kaa san Uwumbɔr na le taa kpa ubɔr. Tɔ, ubɔr ba ga ŋmaa ŋa ba tii timi?” 4Bi len tibɔr ti kaa gbii na, ki puur tipuur kaa gbiini ti, ki ŋani inyamɔn aamɔbaan. Ibamɔn le kpaln inyamɔn, le ki moo kpae ke timoor ti kaa ŋan ki bi baah kon nkpaakon mu na ponn ni pu na.
5Binib bi koo Samaria aatiŋ ni na ga san ijawaan ki wii, baah ga lann salmaa aanaaja aawaal li bi naan siin Bef Afenn ni na pu. Bi ni bitotoorb bi dooni liwaal ngbaan na ga wii li pu. Buyoonn baadim chuu nyan laasalmaa aanyaan na le bi ga li kaani. 6Bi ga di liwaal ngbaan buen ti pa Asiria aabɔrkpaan. Israel yaab aah dii nsurm mu na pu le bi ga ji inimɔɔn ki kpaln binimɔɔnib. 7Bidim ga di baabɔr buen ke lidɔchɔl aah dee nnyun pu ki cha pu na la. 8Afenn aagongon pu aawaa ŋi Israel aanib dooni ŋi na ga ber. Ikokon ni timoor le ga gaa kitork aabimbin ngbaan. Binib ga bui ŋijoo ke, “Bɔr timi man,” le ki bui ŋigongon ke, “Biin ti pu man.”
Uwumbɔr aah bui ke u ga ji Israel yaab tibɔr ti na
9Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel yaab aah nan tun mi titunwanbir Gibea aatiŋ ni buyoonn na, baa kee di cha. Kina pu le butɔb ga pii bi Gibea aatiŋ ni. 10M ga pii titunwanbirdam bimina ki daa bitafal. Ŋitimbol ga kpaan ki tak bi, le m ga daa bitafal, baah tun titunwanbir sakpen pu na pu.
11“Israel nan bi n‑yoonn mubaa ke unaasal u bi bae tiwan mbamɔm na la, le ki gor kii ke u poi idi. Le m nan di ndɔ puin usil mu ŋan na pu, le ki di iŋmin pui u ke u tun lituln li pɔɔ jer kina na. M cha Juda dar ŋikujal, le ki cha Israel dar nkucham. 12Le m bui ke, ‘Ko nkpaakopɔɔn tii nibaa man, di mbimbinyaan bu, ki nan chee naah di nibaa tii mi pu na aanyoor. Ni ŋeer ke ni fenn gir ni min Uwumbɔr chee, le m ga dan ki nan di tinyoor gbiin nimi.’ 13Le ni yii ki di titunwanbir bun ki nan chee taanyoor. Ni jin nimi aanyamɔn aah joo ni pu na la.
“Naah mak nimi aataan aatɔroku tiib, ni nimi aajab aawiwiir pu na, 14le butɔb ga lir nimi aanib pu, le nimi aatim mu kpa tijawan ki pɔɔ na mɔmɔk ga kuln. Ni ga li bi ke ubɔr Salmann aah nan kuln Bef Arbel aatiŋ butɔb ni, ki ku natiib ni baabim pu na la. 15Betel aatiŋ aanib, kina ga ŋa nimi, naah tun titunwanbir sakpen ti na pu. Butɔb aah ga piin buyoonn na, le Israel yaab aabɔr ga kpo.”

english_text:
God's Love for His People
1 When Israel was a child,
I loved him, and I called
my son out of Egypt.
2But as the saying goes,
“The more they were called,
the more they rebelled.”
They never stopped offering
incense and sacrifices
to the idols of Baal.
3I took Israel by the arm
and taught them to walk.
But they would not admit
that I was the one
who had healed them.
4I led them with kindness
and with love,
not with ropes.
I held them close to me;
I bent down to feed them.
5But they rejected me,
and so must return to Egypt;
now Assyria will rule them.
6War will visit their cities,
and their plans will fail.
7My people are determined
to reject me for a god
they think is stronger,
but he can't help.
8 Israel, I can't let you go.
I can't give you up.
How could I possibly destroy you
as I did the towns of Admah
and Zeboiim?
I just can't do it.
My feelings for you
are much too strong.
9Israel, I won't lose my temper
and destroy you again.
I am the Holy God—
not merely some human,
and I won't stay angry.
10I, the Lord, will roar like a lion,
and my children will return,
trembling from the west.
11They will come back,
fluttering like birds from Egypt
or like doves from Assyria.
Then I will bring them
back to their homes.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Israel and Judah Compared
12Israel is deceitful to me,
their loyal and holy God;
they surround me with lies,
and Judah worships
other gods.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah gee waanib bi nyan upuwɔb na pu na
1Uwumbɔr len ke,
“Israel aah nan laa ye ubo pu na, m nan gee u,
le ki nan yin u nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni ke maabo na.
2Tɔ, buyoonn m moo yin u na, le u moo san m chee.
Maanib toor kitork tii liwaal Baal la,
le ki seer nnyɔknii tii ŋiwaa ŋiken.
3Tɔ, m mu le nan mɔk Israel lisachuln.
M yoor maanib ŋmam ŋŋaal ni,
le baa nyi ke min le joo bi.
4M di ngeehm ni lineen daa bi dan mbaa chee.
M nan yoor bi paacham ki di buŋ mbɔgbiln pu;
m nan sɔɔn taab ki kpiin bi.
5“Bi yii kaan gir ni m chee, kina pu le bi ga ki gir Ijipt aatiŋ ni, le Asiria aabɔr ti li joo bi. 6Butɔb ga ŋar baatim ŋŋaan ki gbaa wɔi mu aagon aabisamɔi. Maanib aah ŋani bibaa aageehn aatuln li na le ga cha butɔb bii bi. 7Bi nyan sil ke bi nya m chee la. Bi ga wii lituln li nyik bi pu na pu, le ubaa mu aan tuur bi.
8Israel, m ga ŋa kinye ki di si lii?
M ga ŋa kinye ki di si mee?
M ga ŋmaa kuln si ke maah nan bii Adma aatiŋ pu na aa?
M ga ŋmaa ŋa si ke maah nan ŋa Seboyim aatiŋ pu na aa?
Nsui aan cha m ŋa si kina, ba pu? m gee si sakpen a.
9Maan daa aatafal maaŋuul ponn ni;
maan ki kuln Israel yaab,
ba pu? M ye Uwumbɔr la, maa ye unibɔn.
Min u bi chain na bi ni chee.
Maan dan ni chee maaŋuul ponn ni.
10“M yaa nan ŋuun baadim pu ke uchinn na kan, maanib ga dii mi. Bi ga nya liwilir wɔb ki dan m chee mala. 11Bi ga nya ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni mala ke inyoon na, ki nya ni Asiria aatiŋ ni mala ke ŋinanjel na. M ga ki giin ni bi bido bido. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”
Israel ni Juda aanib aabɔr aah bii pu na
12Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel aanib di inyamɔn ni ŋŋmann le gob mi, le Juda aanib beenin yiil min Uwumbɔr u bi chain ki tun maah len pu na aamɔb.

english_text:
1All day long Israel chases
wind from the desert;
deceit and violence
are found everywhere.
Treaties are made with Assyria;
olive oil is taken to Egypt.
Israel and Judah Condemned
2The Lord also brings charges
against the people of Judah,
the descendants of Jacob.
He will punish them
for what they have done.
3 Even before Jacob was born,
he cheated his brother,
and when he grew up,
he fought against God.
4 At Bethel, Jacob wrestled
with an angel and won;
then with tears in his eyes,
he asked for a blessing,
and God spoke to us there.
5God's name is the Lord,
the Lord God All-Powerful.
6So return to your God.
Patiently trust him,
and show love and justice.
7Israel, you enjoy cheating
and taking advantage
of others.
8You say to yourself, “I'm rich!
I earned it all on my own,
without committing a sin.”
The Lord Is Still the God of Israel
9 Israel, I, the Lord,
am still your God,
just as I have been
since the time
you were in Egypt.
Now I will force you
to live in tents once again,
as you did in the desert.
10I spoke to the prophets—
often I spoke in visions.
And so, I will send my prophets
with messages of doom.
11Gilead is terribly sinful
and will end up ruined.
Bulls are sacrificed in Gilgal
on altars made of stones,
but those stones will be scattered
in every field.
12 Jacob escaped to Syria
where he tended sheep
to earn himself a wife.
13 I sent the prophet Moses
to lead Israel from Egypt
and to keep them safe.
14Israel, I will make you pay
for your violent crimes
and for insulting me.
translation_text:
1“Israel aanib aah tun pu kichakpiik ni ki ti saa kinyeek na aa kpa tinyoor, le ki ye libiil ŋmeen. Mbimbin mu pɔɔ na ni inyamɔn le moo kpae bi ponn ni. Bi ni Ijipt ni Asiria yaab kpaani kimɔbaan la.”
2Uwumbɔr kpa Juda aanib pu ngalm, le ki ga daa Israel aatiŋ aatafal, kaanib aatuln pu. U ga giin baah tun pu na le pa bi. 3Biyaaja Jakob ni ujaantɔ Esɔ nan mɔn, bi mɔmɔk bilee aah nan laa bi bina aaponn ni pu na; le Jakob aah nan chikr na, le u ni Uwumbɔr mɔn, 4u ni Uwumbɔr aatuun nan mɔn le u nyaŋ mu. U nan wii ki mee ban tinyoor. Le Uwumbɔr dan tiyaaja Jakob chee Betel aatiŋ ni, ki nan len u chee tibɔr. 5Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan nan ye. Liyimbil li bi ga li joo dooni u na le ye Uwumbɔr. 6Kina pu na, Jakob aayaabitiib, kii tii nimi Aawumbɔr, ki fenn gir ni u chee. Li si uchaŋ ni ki li bi mbamɔm, ki li kii nimi Aawumbɔr aah ga nan tun pu na.
Libɔjil aabɔr tiken
7Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel aanib ji biŋeen aatɔtiib ke Kanaann yaab na la; bi gee ke bi li joo tiwan ni kaa ye nibamɔnn na le ŋaŋni tiwan ki ji binib bi daa bi chee tiwan na. 8Bi len le ke, ‘Ti ye biwankpadam la. Ti kan liwangol sakpen. Le ubaa aan ŋmaa galn timi ke ti ji biken.’ 9Le min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, ga ki cha ni ki gir li koo igban aaboo ni, ke naah nan koo pu buyoonn m dan ni chee nteersakpiin ni na.
10“M nan len bibɔnabr chee tibɔr, le ki kpiir tibɔkpiirkaan pam tuk bi, le ki cha bi sak maanib. 11Tɔ, ŋiwaa le bi dooni ŋi Gilead aatiŋ ponn ni, le binib bi dooni ŋi na ga kpoi. Bi kɔr inaaja Gilgal aatiŋ ni toor kitork, le ŋiwaabimbin ŋi bi nima chee na ga kpaln ŋitakpakpuk le ikpaakon ni.”
12Tiyaaja Jakob nan san le ki buen Mesopotamia; nima chee, le u nan ti tun lituln tii uja uken ki kpaa waapiih, ke u tii u usapɔɔn. 13Uwumbɔr nan tun ubɔnabr ke u ti nyan Israel yaab tinaagbiir ni Ijipt ni, ki li joo bi. 14Israel aanib cha Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii ni ti nyaŋ, baatunwanbir ŋeer nkun la. Uwumbɔr ga daa bitafal titunwanbir ti bi di tii u na pu.

english_text:
Israel Is Doomed
The Lord said:
1When your leaders spoke,
everyone in Israel trembled
and showed great respect.
But you sinned by worshiping Baal,
and you were destroyed.
2Now you continue to sin
by designing and making
idols of silver
in the shape of calves.
You are told to sacrifice
to these idols—
yes, even to kiss them.
3And so, all of you will vanish
like the mist or the dew
of early morning,
or husks of grain in the wind
or smoke from a chimney.
4I, the Lord, have been your God
since the time
you were in Egypt.
I am the only God you know,
the only one who can save.
5 I took care of you
in a thirsty desert.
6I fed you till you were satisfied,
then you became proud
and forgot about me.
7Now I will attack like a lion,
ambush you like a leopard,
8and rip you apart like a bear
robbed of her cubs.
I will gnaw on your bones,
as though I were a lion
or some other wild animal.
9Israel, you are done for.
Don't expect help from me.
10 You wanted a king and rulers.
Where is your king now?
What cities have rulers?
11 In my anger, I gave you a king;
in my fury, I took him away.
Israel's Terrible Fate
The Lord said:
12Israel, your terrible sins
are written down
and stored away.
13You are like a senseless child
who refuses to be born
at the proper time.
14 Should I, the Lord, rescue you
from death and the grave?
No! I call death and the grave
to strike you like a plague.
I refuse to show mercy.
15No matter if you prosper
more than the other tribes,
I, the Lord, will wipe you out,
just as a scorching desert wind
dries up streams of water.
I will take away
your precious treasures.
16Samaria will be punished
for turning against me.
It will be destroyed in war—
children will be beaten
against rocks,
and pregnant women
will be ripped open.
translation_text:
Israel aakookoo aabɔjil
1N‑yoonn mu jer na, Efraim aanibol yaa nan len kan, ijawaan nan chur ŋinibol ŋi gur na la; ŋi mɔmɔk nan lik Efraim aanibol pu la. Le binib ngbaan dooni liwaal Baal, le ki ga kpo kina pu. 2Baah beenin naani tikur aawan ki dooni ni na, le bi beenin tun titunwanbir, bi dooni tikunabr aawaa ŋi unibɔn di waalan naan ŋi uyil ni, ki di uŋaal ŋa ŋi na. Le bi bui ke, “Toor kitork tii ŋi man.” Binib ga ŋa kinye ki moor ŋiwaa ŋi bi naan ŋi ke inaaja na? 3Kina pu le binib ngbaan ga wɔŋ ke kichakpiik ni aakpakpal na, ki wɔŋ ke limaln li wɔŋni kichakpiik ni na. Bi ga fii buen ke libuln aah daar kimook lipaal pu cha na la, ki naahn iŋmanyuu aah nya kidadiik aadipimoor ni pu na.
4Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u nan nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na. Naa ki kpa Uwumbɔr uken ki kpee m pu. Min baanja le ye u gaal nimi lir na. 5M nan kpiin nimi nteersakpiin mu aatiŋ kuun na ni. 6Le naah ti koo kitiŋ ki ŋan na ponn ni na, le ni nan jin bab, le ni ŋeer nimi, le ni kpaln bigaadam ki suln mbɔr. 7Kina pu le m ga tak nimi ke uchinn na. M ga doon nsan ni kiir nimi ke unaamuun na. 8M ga tak nimi ke kipeewanbiik ki aabim wɔŋ na, le ki daa par nimi. M ga di nimi ŋmɔ mala ke uchinn na libuul ngbaan ni, ki daa par par nimi ke kipeewanbiik na.
9“Israel aanib, m ga kuln nimi. Le ubaa aan ŋmaa ter nimi. 10Ni nan bui ke ni ban ubɔr ni bisalolm la; tɔ, bi ga ŋa kinye ki gaa litimbol ngbaan lii? 11Maaŋuul ponn ni le m nan tii nimi bibɔrb, le maaŋuusakpeln ni m nan ki gaa bi.
12“M ŋmee Israel aatunwanbir ni kaataani bil, le ki di tigbann ngbaan bil mbamɔm. 13Israel yaab kpa limɔfal aamakl, le ki tee jɔr sakpen ke bi kan limɔfal ngbaan, bi jɔr ke ubo u una ban u maa u aan u yii ke waan nya ni na la. 14Maan nyan binib ngbaan nkun ni, kaan nyan bi nkun aapɔɔn ni. Nkun, li joo ni saabiil. Kitekpiitiŋ, li joo ni saabiil. Maan ki san binib bimina kinimbaak. 15Israel pɔr ke timoor na la, le m tee ga cha libuln li ton ki nyan ni liwipuul wɔb nteersakpiin ni na dan ki nan foor baayayak aanyunbun, ni ŋibun. Li ga yoor tiwanbankaan mɔmɔk buen. 16Samaria aatiŋ aanib aah yii maamɔb na, bi ŋeer ntafadaan. Bi ga kpoi butɔb ni, le bidim di baabipɔm yur ku, ki saa gber bipudam aapuu.”

english_text:
Turn Back to the Lord
1Israel, return! Come back
to the Lord, your God.
Sin has made you fall.
2Return to the Lord and say,
“Please forgive our sins.
Accept our good sacrifices
of praise instead of bulls.
3Assyria can't save us,
and chariots can't help.
So we will no longer worship
the idols we have made.
Our Lord, you show mercy
to orphans.”
The Lord Promises To Forgive
4Israel, you have rejected me,
but my anger is gone;
I will heal you and love you
without limit.
5I will be like the dew—
then you will blossom like lilies
and have roots like a tree.
6Your branches will spread
with the beauty
of an olive tree
and with the aroma
of Lebanon Forest.
7You will rest in my shade,
and your grain will grow.
You will blossom
like a vineyard
and be famous as the wine
from Lebanon.
8Israel, give up your idols!
I will answer your prayers
and take care of you.
I am that glorious tree,
the source of your fruit.
9If you are wise, you will know
and understand what I mean.
I am the Lord, and I lead you
along the right path.
If you obey me,
we will walk together,
but if you are wicked,
you will stumble.
translation_text:
Hosea aah gaŋ Israel yaab pu pu na
1Nimi Israel aanib, gir ni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr chee. Nimi aatunwanbir le cha ni gbeer ki lir. 2Gir ni Uwumbɔr chee, ki cha limeel limina li ye ipiin i ni joo tii u na: “Di timi aatunwanbir mɔmɔk cha pinn timi, ki gaa timi aameel, le ti ga li pak si ke taah puu ke ti ga ŋa pu na. 3Asiria yaab aan ŋmaa gaa timi lii, le butɔb aataan mu aan ŋmaa ter timi. Taan ki bui timi aawaa ke ŋima le ye timi Aawumbɔr. Uwumbɔr, aa san binib bi kaa kpa nterm na kinimbaak.”
Uwumbɔr aah puu limɔfapɔln li tii Israel yaab na
4Uwumbɔr bui ke,
“M ga giin ni maanib mbaa chee.
M ga li gee bi ni nsui mɔmɔk;
maaŋuul aan ki fii bi pu.
5M ga li bi Israel aanib chee
ke utaal aah bi pu kitiŋ ki kuun na chee pu na la.
Bi ga pɔnn ke nsupuun na la;
bi ga chɔbaan ke Lebanonn aatiŋ aasui na la.
6Baanachipɔm ga li kpa limɔfal,
ki li ŋan ke olif aakpan aasui na.
Bi ga li kpa mbaan ke Lebanonn aasantina aasui na la.
7Bi ga ki li gur bi maajoom ni la.
Bi ga kpenn ke kisaak na, ki ga lu ŋisubil ke ndaan aasui na.
Bi ga li kpa liyimbil ke Lebanonn aasubil aadaan na.
8Israel aanib aatafal aan ki li bi ŋiwaa ni;
m ga kii baameel ki li joo bi.
M ga li kii bi ke busub bu aafar aa gbaar na la;
min le ye nin chee baanyoor mɔmɔk ga nya ni na.”
Kookoo aabɔr
9Cha binib bi kpa nlan na bee tibɔr ti ŋmee do na aatataa, ki di ti ŋa bisui ni. Uwumbɔr aasan le ŋan, le binib bi aabimbin ŋan na dii ima le ki kpa limɔfal, le titunwanbirdam ma aatafal aa bi i ni, le ki gbeer ki lir.

english_text:
1I am Joel the son of Pethuel.
And this is the message
the Lord gave to me.
Locusts Cover the Land
2Listen, you leaders
and everyone else
in the land.
Has anything like this
ever happened before?
3Tell our children!
Let it be told
to our grandchildren
and their children too.
4Swarm after swarm of locusts
has attacked our crops,
eating everything in sight.
5Sober up, you drunkards!
Cry long and loud;
your wine supply is gone.
6 A powerful nation
with countless troops
has invaded our land.
They have the teeth and jaws
of powerful lions.
7Our grapevines and fig trees
are stripped bare;
only naked branches remain.
8Grieve like a young woman
mourning for the man
she was to marry.
9Offerings of grain and wine
are no longer brought
to the Lord's temple.
His servants, the priests,
are deep in sorrow.
10Barren fields mourn;
grain, grapes, and olives
are scorched and shriveled.
11Mourn for our farms
and our vineyards!
There's no wheat or barley
growing in our fields.
12Grapevines have dried up
and so has every tree—
figs and pomegranates,
date palms and apples.
All happiness has faded away.
Return to God
13Mourn, you priests who serve
at the altar of my God.
Spend your days and nights
wearing sackcloth.
Offerings of grain and wine
are no longer brought
to the Lord's temple.
14Tell the leaders and people
to come together
at the temple.
Order them to go without eating
and to pray sincerely.
15 We are in for trouble!
Soon the Lord All-Powerful
will bring disaster.
16Our food is already gone;
there's no more celebrating
at the temple of our God.
17Seeds dry up in the ground;
no harvest is possible.
Our barns are in bad shape,
with no grain
to store in them.
18Our cattle wander aimlessly,
moaning for lack of pasture,
and sheep are suffering.
19I cry out to you, Lord.
Grasslands and forests are eaten
by the scorching heat.
20Wild animals have no water
because of you;
rivers and streams are dry,
and pastures are parched.
translation_text:
1Uwumbɔr aah di tibɔr ti tuk waabɔnabr Petuel aajapɔɔn Joel na sɔ:
Binib wii tijikaar aah bii pu na pu
2Li pel mbamɔm man, nimi bininkpiib,
ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi Juda aatiŋ ni na, ni li pel.
Naah fii ki pii nitetiib ni nimi aayoonn na,
tiwan nimina aaboln kee ŋa ni kan ni ii?
3Bui nimi aabilb tiwan ngbaan aabɔr man;
le bi mu ga nan bui baabilb,
le baabilb mu ga nan bui bi mu aabilb bi ga nan paan ni bi pu na.
4Itoon pam dan ki nan lir tijikaar pu.
Itoon ibaa aah ŋman gur ni na,
itoon iken nan di ŋman.
5Finn ki li wii man, nimi bidagbiib;
nimi bi ye bidanyurb na, li wii man;
ŋisubil ŋi bi joo ŋaa ndapɔm na mɔmɔk bii doo a.
6Itoon dan ki wiir pam ki nan gob timi aatiŋ a;
i kpa mpɔɔn ki wiir ke litambol na;
le yaanyin ka ke uchinn aanyin na.
7I ŋman bii timi aadaan aasui mɔmɔk,
ki ŋman bii timi aakakan doo a.
I ŋman lar tidapɔr mɔmɔk le ki cha ŋisubil ŋmeen.
8Nimi binib, li wii man, ke usapɔɔn aah ban
u mɔn uja u na aah kpo kan, u wii pu na.
9Njikaabim ni ndaan aa bi ti di tii ipiin Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni;
Uwumbɔr aatotoorb aa kan nibaa bi di toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr, le ki wii ikpowiil.
10Nibaa aa bi ikpaakon ponn ni;
le kitiŋ wii ikpowiil, ba pu? njikaabim mɔmɔk bii doo a,
ŋisubil mɔmɔk kuur ki bii, le olif aakpan aasui yak doo.
11Nimi bi ye bikpaab na, li wii man;
nimi bi lik nimi aakpaakon na, li wii man,
ba pu? idi, ni imuul, ni tijikaar mɔmɔk bii doo a.
12Ndaan aasubil aasui ni ŋikakan mɔmɔk bii doo a;
le ŋisubil aasui mɔmɔk yɔl ki kpoi doo.
Binib mɔmɔk aasuupiin doo a.
13Nimi bitotoorb bi dooni Uwumbɔr waatork aabimbiln taab na,
peen tiwan ni saak kuub na ki li wii man.
Li cha Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni ki ti li wii ikpowiil,
ki taa geen man.
Njikaabim ni ndaan aa bi ni di toor kitork tii nimi Aawumbɔr.
14Cha binib mɔmɔk lul bumɔb man;
yin binib mɔmɔk aan bi kuun ni.
Kuun binib bimɔk ye bisalolm na, ni Juda aatiŋ aanib mɔmɔk
aan bi mɔmɔk dan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni
ki nan wii yin u.
15Uwumbɔr aawiin peen ni a;
nwiin mundaal Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga bii tiwan mɔmɔk doo na peen ni a.
Ba aajawaan aaboln aan kina aawiin ga joo ni.
16Ti si lik kaa kpa nterm mubaa,
le timi aajikaar mɔmɔk bii doo.
Mpopiin mubaa aa bi timi Aawumbɔr Aadichal ni.
17Kitiŋ aah kuur pu na,
le njikaabim mɔmɔk kpoi doo ki ponn ni.
Njikaabim mubaa aa bi aan ti di siin,
kina pu na, timi aapikuun na mɔmɔk lir doo a.
18Inaa aah kaa kan timoor i ŋmɔ na,
le i wii ni mpombiin;
le ipiih mɔmɔk ji falaa.
19Uwumbɔr, m wii mpɔɔn pu ki yin si la,
ba pu? timoor ni isui mɔmɔk kuur,
ke mmii le aah wun ni mɔmɔk na.
20Hali timoor ni aawakor wii mpɔɔn pu ki yin si la,
ba pu? ibun mɔmɔk foor a.

english_text:
Locusts and an Enemy Army
1Sound the trumpet on Zion,
the Lord's sacred hill.
Warn everyone to tremble!
The judgment day of the Lord
is coming soon.
2It will be dark and gloomy
with storm clouds overhead.
Troops will cover the mountains
like thunderclouds.
No army this powerful
has ever been gathered before
or will be gathered again.
3Fiery flames surround them;
no one escapes.
Before they invaded,
the land was like Eden;
now only a desert remains.
4 They look like horses
and charge like cavalry.
5They roar over mountains
like noisy chariots,
or a mighty army
ready for battle.
They are a forest fire
that feasts on straw.
6The very sight of them
is frightening.
7They climb over walls
like warriors;
they march in columns
and never turn aside.
8They charge straight ahead,
without pushing each other;
even arrows and spears
cannot make them retreat.
9They swarm over city walls
and enter our homes;
they crawl in through windows,
just like thieves.
10 They make the earth tremble
and the heavens shake;
the sun and moon turn dark,
and stars stop shining.
11 The Lord God leads this army
of countless troops,
and they obey his commands.
The day of his judgment
is so terrible
that no one can stand it.
The Lord's Invitation
12The Lord said:
It isn't too late.
You can still return to me
with all your heart.
Start crying and mourning!
Go without eating.
13Don't rip your clothes
to show your sorrow.
Instead, turn back to me
with broken hearts.
I am merciful, kind, and caring.
I don't easily lose my temper,
and I don't like to punish.
14I am the Lord your God.
Perhaps I will change my mind
and treat you with mercy.
Then you will be blessed
with enough grain and wine
for offering sacrifices to me.
15Sound the trumpet on Zion!
Call the people together.
Show your sorrow
by going without food.
16 Make sure that everyone
is fit to worship me.
Bring adults, children, babies,
and even bring newlyweds
from their festivities.
17 Tell my servants, the priests,
to cry inside the temple
and to offer this prayer
near the altar:
“Save your people, Lord God!
Don't let foreign nations
make jokes about us.
Don't let them laugh and ask,
‘Where is your God?’ ”
The Lord Will Bless the Land
18The Lord was deeply concerned
about his land
and had pity on his people.
19In answer to their prayers
he said,
“I will give you enough grain,
wine, and olive oil
to satisfy your needs.
No longer will I let you
be insulted by the nations.
20An army attacked from the north,
but I will chase it
into a scorching desert.
There it will rot and stink
from the Dead Sea
to the Mediterranean.”
The Lord works wonders
21and does great things.
So tell the soil to celebrate
22and wild animals
to stop being afraid.
Grasslands are green again;
fruit trees and fig trees
are loaded with fruit.
Grapevines are covered
with grapes.
23People of Zion,
celebrate in honor
of the Lord your God!
He is generous and has sent
the autumn and spring rains
in the proper seasons.
24Grain will cover
your threshing places;
jars will overflow
with wine and olive oil.
The Lord Will Rescue His People
25I, the Lord your God,
will make up for the losses
caused by those swarms
and swarms of locusts
I sent to attack you.
26My people, you will eat
until you are satisfied.
Then you will praise me
for the wonderful things
I have done.
Never again will you
be put to shame.
27Israel, you will know
that I stand at your side.
I am the Lord your God—
there are no other gods.
Never again will you
be put to shame.
The Lord Will Work Wonders
The Lord said:
28 Later, I will give my Spirit
to everyone.
Your sons and daughters
will prophesy.
Your old men
will have dreams,
and your young men
will see visions.
29In those days I will even give
my Spirit to my servants,
both men and women.
30I will work wonders
in the sky above
and on the earth below.
There will be blood and fire
and clouds of smoke.
31 The sun will turn dark,
and the moon
will be as red as blood
before that great
and terrible day
when I appear.
32 Then I, the Lord will save everyone who faithfully worships me. I have promised there will be survivors on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and among them will be my chosen ones.
translation_text:
Itoon ye limɔkl le ki tii Uwumbɔr aawiin daal
1Pii kakaan man; faa nkuun Sionn aajool
li ye Uwumbɔr aajool ki bi chain na paab.
Juda aatiŋ aanib, cha niwon li gbaa man.
Uwumbɔr aawiin peen ni a.
2Nwiin ngbaan daal ga li bɔɔn ki bi timm,
mu ga li bɔɔn ki kpa ntaalangbam pam.
Kitoonpaak ngbaan choo ki naahn mbɔmbɔɔn sakpiin mubaa le aah biini ŋijoo paab na.
Tiwan nimina aaboln aa kee ŋa, kaan ki ŋa daalbaadaal.
3I ŋmɔ tijikaar mɔmɔk ke mmii le aah gaal na.
Aa yaa lik imɔi wɔb kan, ni naahn Edenn aasaak na la,
le aa yaa lik ipuwɔb kan, ni naahn nteersakpiin pu la.
Nibaa aan ŋmaa bɔr aan yaan kan ni.
4I naahn itaan la,
le ki san ke butɔb aajab aah joo itaan i chaa butɔb na.
5Yaah bi yuk ŋijoo paab pu na naahn itaan aatɔroku tiib la;
ki naahn timokuun aah gaal mmii ni pu na la.
I chol tɔb pu ke butɔb aajab aah gor bibaa
ki kii butɔb pu na la.
6Ijawaan chur unii umɔk waa yaah choo pu na.
7I tak ke bijab aah tak baadim pu na la;
ki joi ŋigon ke butɔb aajab na.
I mɔmɔk cha imɔi wɔb la,
ubaa aa yenn ki cha nibaa ki cha iken,
8ubaa mu aa punn uken aamɔb pu.
Yaah ga jer nin chee na,
tiwan nibaa aa bi ki ga leŋ yaasan ke i taa jer.
9I ga chii ki buen kitiŋ ponn ni;
ki fii labr ŋigon pu, ki joi ŋidichal pu,
ki diir takolu tiib koo tidir ponn ni ke binaayukb na.
10I yaa choo kan, kitiŋ deŋni la, le kitaapaak jii.
Nwiin ni uŋmal mɔmɔk bɔnn chirm, le iŋmabi aa ki wiin.
11Uwumbɔr tar ke utaal na
ki tuk waatɔb aajab baah ga ŋa pu na.
Waajab bi kii tii waamɔb na wiir ki kpa mpɔɔn.
Uwumbɔr aawiin ngbaan daal kan,
ubaa aan li wii aan uŋeen aatɔ ka laa.
Ubaa aan ŋmar nwiin ngbaan daal.
Kpeln nimi aabimbin mbamɔm man
12Uwumbɔr len ke, “Hali dandana,
kpeln nimi aabimbin mbamɔm man,
ki lul bumɔb, ki li wii ikpowiil, ki gir ni m chee.
13Cha nimi aasuugar mɔk nimi aapombiin,
naa ye ke ni daa kar nimi aawanpeenkaan baanja.”
Gir ni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr chee man.
U kpa tiŋann ki ye unimbaasaln daan la;
u kpa limɔr ki ŋmaa joo waah puu tipuur ti na;
n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan,
u gor ki kii ke u di cha pinn binib.
Waa ban ke u daa bitafal.
14Nibaakan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga kpeln waalandak,
ki ga ŋa waanyoor ŋa ni pu aan ni kan tijikaar sakpen.
Le ni ga ŋmaa tii u njikaabim ni ndaan aapiin.
15Pii kakaan Sionn aajool paab man;
cha binib mɔmɔk lul bumɔb ki kuun bi mɔmɔk kpaan.
16Kuun binib mɔmɔk kpaan tɔb chee;
cha bi mɔmɔk gor bibaa ki li kii nkuun mu bi chain na;
li joo ni binib bi por na; kuun bibilb ni mbipɔm mu.
Hali binib bi laa mɔn tichar na ga nyan ni baadir ni ki dan.
17Bitotoorb bi tun Uwumbɔr aatuln, waatork aabimbiln
ni Waadichal aabisamɔb aakaasisik ni na;
ni li mee Uwumbɔr ni tinyunyunn ke:
“Uwumbɔr, san saanib kinimbaak.
Taa cha ŋinibol ŋiken lik timi fam ki ŋa timi mbɔnyun
ki len ke, ‘Nimi Aawumbɔr ngbaan bi la?’”
Uwumbɔr aah cha kitiŋ ki gir pu na
18N‑yoonn ngbaan le Uwumbɔr ki san waatiŋ kinimbaak;
u san waanib kinimbaak.
19U kii baameel ki len ke:
“Dandana wee m ban m tii nimi tijikaar ni ndaan,
ni olif aakpan, aan ni mɔɔr nimi.
Ŋinibol ŋiken aan ki lik seen nimi.
20M ga chuu nyan itoon i nan nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb na
ki ga jenn ibaa buen litambol ŋmeen aatiŋ ni.
Itoon i loln i mɔmɔk pu nsan na ga buen ti koo
N‑yaan Aanyusakpem na ni,
le i paa puwɔb na ga buen ti koo
Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem na ni.
I ga kpo, le iwon ga bur ki nuŋ.
Yaa ŋa nimi pu na, nima le ga cha m ku i mɔmɔk.
21Ikpaakon, taa cha ijawaan li joo nimi man,
li kpa mpopiin man,
ki li mɔɔni man Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu tii nimi na mɔmɔk pu.
22Tiwakor, taa cha ijawaan li joo nimi man.
Nimi aamoŋmɔpaan ki boln timosɔnn
isui mɔmɔk lun ŋisubil,
le ŋikakan ni ŋisubil ŋiken moo kpee.
23Sionn aatiŋ aanib, cha nisui li piin man,
li mɔɔni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu tii nimi na pu.
U tii nimi kiseek ni aataal, ki ŋeer naah ban pu na;
ki cha utakuutaal ni unaalantaal mu nun mbamɔm
ke waah ti nu pu na.
24Ŋijikaapaa mɔmɔk ga gbiin tijikaar;
ndaan aasubil ni nkpan mu ga li wiir.
25M ga giin itoon aah di nimi aajikaar ti mɔmɔk ŋman
ŋibin ŋi jer na ki ki di tii nimi.
Min le nan tun ni itoon i wiir sakpen ngbaan na.
26Dandana wee ma kan, ni ga kan sakpen ki ji bab.
Ni ga pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr
u ŋa lijinjiir aawan ngbaan ki tii nimi na.
Ubaa aan ki lik seen min Uwumbɔr aanib.
27N‑yaayoonn ngbaan, le nimi Israel yaab ga bee
ke m bi nikaasisik ni,
ki bee ke min Uwumbɔr le ye Nidindaan,
ubaa aa ki bi ki kpee m pu.
Ubaa aan ki lik seen maanib.
Uwumbɔr aawiin daal
28“N‑yoonn mu choo na,
m ga di Maafuur Nyaan di ŋa maanib mɔmɔk pu:
nijapɔtiib ni nibisatiib ga nabr min Uwumbɔr aah len pu na;
nimi aaninkpiib ga daŋ tidaŋ,
le nimi aanachipɔm ga kan lijinjiir aawan.
29N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga nan di Maafuur Nyaan ŋa
maanaagbiijab ni maanaagbiipiib mu pu.
30M ga ŋa lijinjiir aawan kitaapaak ni, ni kitiŋ pu;
nsin, ni mmii, ni iŋmanyuu ga li bi.
31Nwiin ga bɔln, le uŋmal mann ke nsin na
waahr aan Uwumbɔr aawiin daal nin fuu ni.
Mu ga li ye nwiin sakpiin mu kpa ijawaan na la.
32Liyaadaal ngbaan unii umɔk mee Uwumbɔr na,
uma le ga ŋmar ke Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ke,
‘Bibaa bi Jerusalem aatiŋ ni ki ga ŋmar;
bima le ye binib bi m lee bi ke bi ga ŋmar na.’”

english_text:
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
1At that time I, the Lord, will make Judah and Jerusalem prosperous again. 2Then in Judgment Valley I will bring together the nations that scattered my people Israel everywhere in the world, and I will bring charges against those nations. They divided up my land 3and gambled to see who would get my people; they sold boys and girls to pay for prostitutes and wine.
4 You people of Tyre and Sidon and you Philistines, why are you doing this? Are you trying to get even with me? I'll strike back before you know what's happened. 5You've taken my prized possessions, including my silver and gold, and carried them off to your temples. 6You have dragged the people of Judah and Jerusalem from their land and sold them to the Greeks.
7But I'll make the people of Judah determined to come home, and what happened to them will happen to you. 8I'll hand over your sons and daughters to the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, who live far away. I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment in Judgment Valley
9Say to the nations:
“Get ready for war!
Be eager to fight.
Line up for battle
and prepare to attack.
10 Make swords out of plows
and spears out of garden tools.
Strengthen every weakling.”
11Hurry, all you nations!
Come quickly.
Ask the Lord to bring
his warriors along.
12You must come now
to Judgment Valley,
where the Lord will judge
the surrounding nations.
13 They are a field of ripe crops.
Bring in the harvest!
They are grapes piled high.
Start trampling them now!
If our enemy's sins were wine,
every jar would overflow.
14Crowds fill Decision Valley.
The judgment day of the Lord
will soon be here—
15no light from the sun or moon,
and stars no longer shine.
16 From the heart of Jerusalem
the Lord roars like a lion,
shaking the earth and sky.
But the Lord is a fortress,
a place of safety
for his people Israel.
God Will Bless His People
17I am the Lord your God.
And you will know I live on Zion,
my sacred hill,
because Jerusalem will be sacred,
untouched by foreign troops.
18On that day, fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
And your cattle and goats
that graze on the hills
will produce a lot of milk.
Streams in Judah
will never run dry;
a stream from my house
will flow in Acacia Valley.
19Egypt and Edom were cruel
and brutal to Judah,
without a reason.
Now their countries will become
a barren desert,
20but Judah and Jerusalem
will always have people.
21I, the Lord, live on Mount Zion.
I will punish the guilty
and defend the innocent.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr ga ji ŋitimbol tibɔr
1Uwumbɔr len ke, “N‑yoonn ngbaan kan,
m ga giin Juda ni Jerusalem aatim aawangol tii mu,
2le ki kuun ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ki nan ji ŋi tibɔr Libɔjil Aafataŋ ni.
Baah tun maanib pu na le m ga ji bi tibɔr.
Bi jenn yaa Israel yaab koon ntiyayam ponn ni,
le ki chuu yakr maatiŋ Israel ngbaan.
3Bi too inaan ke bi lik unii u ga li yeh binaagbiib bi bi chur na.
Bi kooh mbijabim ni mpiibim ki di bi ŋa tinaagbiir ponn ni
ke bi di ilik ngbaan pa pateer tiib ni ndaan pu.
4“Taya, ni Saidonn, ni ntim mumɔk bi Filistia aatingbaan na, ba le ni ban ke ni ŋa mi? Ni pɔɔni nibaa ke ni pa mi lipɔln la aa? Kina le yaa ye nimi aalandak kan, m ga giin pa nimi mala. 5Nimi le yoor maakunabr ni maasalmaa ki yoor maawangol ki di ti ŋa nimi aawaa aadir ni. 6Nimi le yoor Juda ni Jerusalem aanib ki di bi buen dandar, ki ti di bi kooh tii Griik yaab. 7Dandana wee ma kan, m ban m buen ti nyan ni bi nin chee ni ti di bi kooh tii na la. M ga ŋa nimi ke naah nan ŋa bi pu na, 8le ki cha binib di nijapɔtiib ni nibisatiib kooh tii Juda yaab; le bi mu di bi kooh tii Seba yaab bi bi dandar na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.
9Moon tibɔr tee ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ponn ni ke:
‘Gor ki kiir butɔb man;
yin nimi aajab bi ga ja kijaak na man;
kuun nimi aatɔb aajab mɔmɔk ki li chuun man.
10Di nimi aakuu mɔɔ kijaak aajum man,
ki di nimi aakpaacha tiib mɔɔ tikpaatunn.
Hali binib bi bun na mɔmɔk ga buen butɔb ni.
11Nimi ŋitimbol ŋimɔk mann goln na,
ŋa mala ki dan man, ki kuun tɔb kifataŋ ni.’”
Uwumbɔr, cha saajab sunn ni ki nan tak bi.
12“Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk, gor nibaa, ki dan Libɔjil Aafataŋ ni,
nin chee Uwumbɔr ga ji binib tibɔr na.
Le min Uwumbɔr ga kal ki ji ŋitimbol ŋimɔk mann goln na tibɔr.
13Bi ye bibiindam la;
gaa bi lii kitiŋ man ke baah bar ŋikalmaan pu na;
muen bi ke baah mueni ŋisubil pu
ki nyani ŋaanyun aan mu ti wiir na man.”
14Binib ŋichur ŋichur le gbii Libɔjil Aafataŋ ngbaan ni.
Nima chee le Uwumbɔr aawiin ngbaan ga gbeen fuu ni mala.
15Nwiin ni uŋmal ga bɔln, le iŋmabi aan ki li wiin.
Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa waanib pu
16Uwumbɔr tar ke uchinn na Sionn aajool pu;
uneel nyan ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ni, ke utaal aah tar pu na;
le kitiŋ ni kitaapaak jii.
U mu tee ga li kii waanib.
17“N‑yoonn ngbaan, le nimi Israel yaab ga bee
ke min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.
M bi Sionn, maajool li bi chain na pu la;
Jerusalem ga li ye kitiŋ ki bi chain na la;
le kaadim aan ki ŋmaa nyaŋ ki daalbaadaal.
18N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, ŋijoo mɔmɔk pu ga li ye ikpaakon la;
le inaa ga li bi ŋigongon mɔmɔk pu;
le Juda aakpen mɔmɔk ponn ni ga li kpa nnyun pam.
Nnyun ga li puu nyan ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni,
ki sɔŋ Sitim Aafataŋ.
19Ijipt ni Edom aatim ga kpaln nin chee nnyun aa bi na la.
Litambol ŋmeen le ga li gur bi nima,
ba pu? bima le buen ti tak ki ku Juda aanib bi kaa tun
taani ubaa na.
20-21M ga teen baah nan ku bi mɔmɔk na aapɔln;
m ga daa unii umɔk tun taani na aatafal.
Le binib ga li bi Juda ni Jerusalem aatim ni
ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na,
le min Uwumbɔr ga li bi Sionn aajool pu.”

english_text:
1 I am Amos. And I raised sheep near the town of Tekoa when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.
Two years before the earthquake, the Lord gave me several messages about Israel, 2 and I said:
When the Lord roars
from Jerusalem,
pasturelands and Mount Carmel
dry up and turn brown.
Judgment on Syria
3 The Lord said:
I will punish Syria
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They dragged logs with spikes
over the people of Gilead.
4Now I will burn down the palaces
and fortresses of King Hazael
and of King Benhadad.
5I will break through
the gates of Damascus.
I will destroy the people
of Wicked Valley
and the ruler of Beth-Eden.
Then the Syrians will be dragged
as prisoners to Kir.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Philistia
6 The Lord said:
I will punish Philistia
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They dragged off my people
from town after town
to sell them as slaves
to the Edomites.
7That's why I will burn down
the walls and fortresses
of the city of Gaza.
8I will destroy the king of Ashdod
and the ruler of Ashkelon.
I will strike down Ekron,
and that will be the end
of the Philistines.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Phoenicia
9 The Lord said:
I will punish Phoenicia
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They broke their treaty
and dragged off my people
from town after town
to sell them as slaves
to the Edomites.
10That's why I will send flames
to burn down the city of Tyre
along with its fortresses.
Judgment on Edom
11 The Lord said:
I will punish Edom
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They killed their own relatives
and were so terribly furious
that they showed no mercy.
12Now I will send fire to wipe out
the fortresses of Teman
and Bozrah.
Judgment on Ammon
13 The Lord said:
I will punish Ammon
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
In Gilead they ripped open
pregnant women,
just to take the land.
14Now I will send fire to destroy
the walls and fortresses
of Rabbah.
Enemies will shout and attack
like a whirlwind.
15Ammon's king and leaders
will be dragged away.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Tibɔr ti Amos u ye upihkpaal ki nyan ni Tekoa aatiŋ ni na nan len na sɔ. Ŋibin ŋilee waahr aan kitiŋ nin deŋ na, n‑yoonn ngbaan le Usia nan ye Juda aabɔrkpaan aan Jehoas aajapɔɔn Jeroboam mu nan ye Israel aabɔrkpaan na, le Uwumbɔr nan kpiir Israel aatiŋ aabɔr timina mɔmɔk tuk Amos.
2Le Amos len ke,
“Uwumbɔr ŋuun ni Sionn Aajool paab ke uchinn na;
uneel tar mpɔɔn pu ke utaal le aah gbeer na, ki nyan ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ni.
Inaa aah ŋmɔ timoor nin chee na mɔmɔk kuur a,
le Kamel Aajool paab kuur ki mann ke lipeel aamoor na.”
Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Israel aamaantɔtiib tibɔr pu na
Siria aatiŋ yaab
3Uwumbɔr len ke, “Damaskus yaab aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi ŋa Gilead yaab mbiin sakpen. 4Kina pu na, m ga cha mmii wu ubɔrkpaan Hasael aabɔrdichal, ki see ubɔrkpaan Ben‑Hadad aadichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na mɔmɔk mmii. 5M ga gbaa wii Damaskus aatiŋ aabisamɔi mɔmɔk, le ki jenn nyan Afenn Aafataŋ ni aanib ni Bef Edenn aayidaan. Le bi ga chur Siria aanib mɔmɔk tinaagbiir ki di bi buen Kir aatiŋ ni.”
Filistia aatiŋ yaab
6Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Filistia yaab Gasa aatiŋ aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi ŋa litimbol mɔln aanib mbiin ki di bi kooh tii Edom yaab. 7Kina pu na, m ga cha mmii wu Gasa aatiŋ aagon, ni kaadichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ aan bi maa kiir bibaa na mɔmɔk. 8M ga chuu nyan Filistia yaab aatim Asdod ni Askelonn aayidam. M ga daa baatiŋ Ekronn aanib aatafal, le Filistia yaab bi mɔmɔk gur na ga kpoi.”
Taya aatiŋ yaab
9Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Taya aatiŋ aanib aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi ŋa ntimɔln aanib mbiin ki di bi kooh tii Edom yaab, kaa joo limaantɔl aajɔtiik ki bi nan puu tii tɔb na. 10Kina pu na, m ga cha mmii wu Taya aatiŋ aagon, ni kaadichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ aan bi maa kiir bibaa na mɔmɔk.”
Edom aatiŋ yaab
11Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Edom yaab aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi tee mban ki ban bi ŋa binaabitiib Israel yaab mbiin ki ku bi, kaa san bi kinimbaak. Baaŋuul pɔɔ kaa sɔŋni kpala. 12Kina pu na, m ga cha mmii wu baatiŋ Temann aagon, ni baatiŋ Bosra aadichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ aan bi maa kiir bibaa na mɔmɔk.”
Amonn aatiŋ yaab
13Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Amonn yaab aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Baah nan jaa kijaak ki ban ntim bi kpee baatiŋ pu na, bi nan ŋa Gilead yaab mbiin pam ki saa gber baapudam aapuu ki nyan mbipɔm. 14Kina pu na, m ga cha mmii wu baatiyil Raba aagon, ni baah maa ŋidichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ kiir bibaa na mɔmɔk. Le bundaal butɔb ga fii na, iwiil ga li bi liyaadaal ngbaan, le kijaak ngbaan ga li pɔɔ ke kitaabuŋ na. 15Le baadim ga di baabɔrkpaan ni waaninkpiib buen tinaagbiir ni.”

english_text:
Judgment on Moab
1 The Lord said:
I will punish Moab
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They made lime from the bones
of the king of Edom.
2Now I will send fire to destroy
the fortresses of Kerioth.
Battle shouts and trumpet blasts
will be heard as I destroy Moab
3with its king and leaders.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Judah
4The Lord said:
I will punish Judah
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They have rejected my teachings
and refused to obey me.
They were led astray
by the same false gods
their ancestors worshiped.
5Now I will send fire on Judah
and destroy the fortresses
of Jerusalem.
Judgment on Israel
6The Lord said:
I will punish Israel
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They sell honest people for money,
and the needy are sold
for the price of sandals.
7They smear the poor in the dirt
and push aside
those who are helpless.
My holy name is dishonored,
because fathers and sons sleep
with the same young women.
8They lie down beside altars
on clothes taken
as security for loans.
And they drink wine in my temple,
wine bought with the money
they received from fines.
9 Israel, the Amorites were there
when you entered Canaan.
They were tall as cedars
and strong as oaks.
But I wiped them out—
I destroyed their branches
and their roots.
10I had rescued you from Egypt,
and for forty years I had led you
through the desert.
Then I gave you the land
of the Amorites.
11 I chose some of you
to be prophets
and others to be Nazirites.
People of Israel,
you know this is true.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
12But you commanded the prophets
not to speak their message,
and you pressured the Nazirites
into drinking wine.
13And so I will crush you,
just as a wagon full of grain
crushes the ground.
14No matter how fast you run,
you won't escape.
No matter how strong you are,
you will lose your strength
and your life.
15Even if you are an expert
with a bow and arrow,
you will retreat.
And you won't get away alive,
not even if you run fast
or ride a horse.
16You may be brave and strong,
but you will run away,
stripped naked.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Moab aatiŋ yaab
1Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Moab yaab aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi nan jinn Edom aabɔrkpaan aakpab inimɔɔn ki see i mmii ki cha i wun ki ti kpaln nfatan. 2M ga cha mmii wu Moab aatiŋ, ki see baatiŋ Keriof aadichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ aan bi maa kiir bibaa na mɔmɔk. Buyoonn butɔb aajab ga li tar aan kakaan tiib wii ki kpa kifuuk na, le Moab aanib ga kpoi. 3M ga ku Moab yaab aayidaan ni baaninkpiib mɔmɔk.”
Juda aatiŋ yaab
4Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Juda yaab aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi lik maamɔkm fam, kaa kii maamɔb. Biyaajatiib aah nan dii inyamɔn aawaa ŋi na le ŋmann bi koon timoor ni. 5Kina pu na, m ga cha mmii wu Juda ki wu Jerusalem yaab aah maa ŋidichal ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ kiir bibaa na mɔmɔk.”
Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Israel yaab tibɔr pu na
6Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Israel yaab aah tun titunwanbir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, kina le ga cha m sil daa bitafal. Bi joo bininyaam le kooh ke bi di teen baapɔln, hali bigiim bi kaan ŋmaa pa ŋinaatak aadaak na, bi kooh bi mu la. 7Bi jon ki taar binib bi kaa kpa mpɔɔn na pu, le ki tur bigiim lir isan ni. Le uja ni ute kpaani unaagbiipiibo baan, kina le bi bii maayimbil li bi chain na. 8Bijab doo kitork aabimbin mɔmɔk ponn ni, tiwanpeenkaan ni bi gaa bigiim chee ki joo teeni baah jin ŋipɔln ŋi pu na la. Maadichal ni, bi nyu ndaan mu bi gaa baapɔlndam chee na la.
9“Maanib, nimi pu le m nan ku doo Amonn yaab, bima le ye bijab bi nan fɔk ke santina aasui ki pɔɔ ke ŋikpan aasui na. 10Min le nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki di nimi dii nteersakpiin ni, ŋibin imonko ilee, le ki di Amor yaab aatiŋ tii nimi, le ki kpaln nimi aatiŋ. 11Min le nan lee nijapɔtiib bibaa bi li ye maabɔnabtiib, le ki lee biken mu bi li ye maatutum bi puu ke baan nyu ndaan kpala na. Israel yaab, m gii la aa? Min Uwumbɔr le len kina. 12Le ni cha maatutum ngbaan nyu ndaan, ki bui maabɔnabtiib na ke bi taa nabr maabɔr. 13Dandana, m ga ŋa nimi ke unii u tu lituln aan li nyaŋ u na la. 14Hali, binib bi ŋmaa san sakpen na aan ŋmar; bipɔɔndam aapɔɔn ga doo, le butɔb aajab aan ki ŋmaa gaa bibaa lii. 15Binib bi joo itɔi na aan ki ŋmaa sil ki too, le bitaasam aan ŋmaa san ŋmar, bijab bi dik itaan pu na mu aan ŋmaa ŋmar. 16Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, hali butɔb aajab bi kaar sakpen na ga di baajawan mae ki san.” Uwumbɔr le len kina.

english_text:
1People of Israel,
I rescued you from Egypt.
Now listen to my judgment
against you.
2Of all nations on earth,
you are the only one
I have chosen.
That's why I will punish you
because of your sins.
The Work of a Prophet
3Can two people walk together
without agreeing to meet?
4Does a lion roar in the forest
unless it has caught
a victim?
Does it growl in its den
unless it is eating?
5How can anyone catch a bird
without using a net?
Does a trap spring shut
unless something is caught?
6Isn't the whole city frightened
when the trumpet
signals an attack?
Isn't the Lord the one who brings
disaster on a city?
7Whatever the Lord God
plans to do,
he tells his servants,
the prophets.
8Everyone is terrified
when a lion roars—
and ordinary people
become prophets
when the Lord God speaks.
Samaria Is Doomed
9Here is a message
for the leaders
of Philistia and Egypt—
tell everyone to come together
on the hills of Samaria.
Let them see the injustice
and the lawlessness
in that city.
10The Lord has said
that they don't even know how
to do right.
They have become rich
from violence and robbery.
11And so the Lord God has sworn
that they will be surrounded.
Enemies will break through
their defenses
and steal their treasures.
12The Lord has promised
that only a few from Samaria
will escape with their lives
and with some broken pieces
of their beds and couches.
It will be like when a shepherd
rescues two leg bones
and part of a sheep's ear
from the jaws of a lion.
The Altars at Bethel
13The Lord God All-Powerful
told me to speak this message
against Jacob's descendants:
14 When I, the Lord, punish Israel
for their sins,
I will destroy the altars
at Bethel.
Even the corners of the altar
will be left in the dirt.
15I will tear down winter homes
and summer homes.
Houses decorated with ivory
and all other mansions
will be gone forever.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Israel yaab, linibomɔln li Uwumbɔr nyan li Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, li pel man nimi aabɔr ti u len na. 2“Dulnyaa aanibol mɔmɔk ponn ni, nimi baanja le m nyi nimi ki lik nimi, nibaa taa ŋa nimi. Nima le cha nimi aatunwanbir bir sakpen, ki cha m ga sil daa nitafal.”
Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr aatuln
3Bijab bilee aan ŋmaa kpaan piin lisachuln kaa puen kpokl waahr.
4Uchinn yaa kaa kee kan tinann kan, waan teen kipɔɔk ni.
Uchinn u laa diin na yaa kaa chuu nibaa waabuu ni kan, waa ŋuuni.
5Tijikaar yaa kaa bi gaawɔb ni kan, unyoon aan koo u ni aan u chuu u.
Nibaa yaa kaa taa gaawɔb pu kan, waan too.
6Ukpiin yaa wii kitiŋ ni kan, ijawaan chur binib mɔmɔk la.
Tibɔbir aan ŋmaa koo ni kitisakpeŋ ni kaa nyan ni Uwumbɔr chee.
7Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aa ŋani waawan nibaa kaa puen di ni kpiir mɔk waatutum bi ye waabɔnabtiib na.
8Uchinn yaa ŋuun kan, ijawaan chur binib mɔmɔk la.
Tidindaan Uwumbɔr yaa len tibɔr kan, ŋma bi kaan nabr ti tii biken?
Samaria aatiŋ aadoon
9Moon ki tuk binib bi mɔmɔk bi Ijipt ni Asdod aabɔrdichal ni na ke, “Kuun man ki buen ŋijoo ŋi mann goln Samaria aatiŋ na, ki ti lik tiwan yɔl yɔl ni titunwanbir ti bi ŋani nima chee na.”
10Uwumbɔr le len ke, “Binib bimina di baah gaa tiwan ni mpɔɔn na le di gbiin baadichal sakpiin ngbaan ponn ni. Baa nyi baah ga ŋa pu ki ŋa tiwan ni ŋan na. 11Kina pu na, baadim le ga mann goln baatiŋ, ki nyaŋ baajab bi to butɔb na, ki gbaa wii baadichal sakpiin ngbaan.”
12Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Samaria aanib bi ka ŋibɔrjal pu na ga nan gur siib ke Uchinn yaa chuu upiih ki ŋman kan, unaakpaal ga ti kan waah ŋman gur itaayakr bee litafal libaa pu na la. Kina le Samaria aanib siib ga ŋmar, le lijal ni tiwandookaan aageln baanja ga li gur baawangol ponn ni.” 13Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ki len ke, “Li pel man, ki sur Jakob aayaabitiib 14ke bundaal m ga daa Israel yaab aatafal baatunwanbir pu na kan, m ga gbaa wii ŋiwaabimbin ŋi bi Betel aatiŋ ni na mɔmɔk. Ŋibimbin ngbaan mɔmɔk aamɔju ga wii ki lir kitiŋ. 15M ga wii naah maa lipeel aadichal, ni kiseek aadichal ŋi na mɔmɔk. Naah di iluub aanyin di ŋa tidir ti pu ke ti li ŋan na mɔmɔk ga lir; lidichasakpeln libaa aan gur kaan bii.”

english_text:
The Women of Samaria
The Lord said:
1You women of Samaria
are fat cows!
You mistreat and abuse
the poor and needy,
then you say to your husbands,
“Bring us more drinks!”
2I, the Lord God, have sworn
by my own name
that your time is coming.
Not one of you will be left—
you will be taken away
by sharp hooks.
3You will be dragged through holes
in your city walls,
and you will be thrown
toward Harmon.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Israel Refuses To Obey
The Lord said:
4Come to Bethel and Gilgal.
Sin all you want!
Offer sacrifices the next morning
and bring a tenth of your crops
on the third day.
5Bring offerings to show me
how thankful you are.
Gladly bring more offerings
than I have demanded.
You really love to do this.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
How the Lord Warned Israel
6 I, the Lord, took away the food
from every town and village,
but still you rejected me.
7Three months before harvest,
I kept back the rain.
Sometimes I would let it fall
on one town or field
but not on another,
and pastures dried up.
8People from two or three towns
would go to a town
that still had water,
but it wasn't enough.
Even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9I dried up your grain fields;
your gardens and vineyards
turned brown.
Locusts ate your fig trees
and olive orchards,
but even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
10I did terrible things to you,
just as I did to Egypt—
I killed your young men in war;
I let your horses be stolen,
and I made your camp stink
with dead bodies.
Even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
11 I destroyed many of you,
just as I did the cities
of Sodom and Gomorrah.
You were a burning stick
I rescued from the fire.
But even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
12Now, Israel, I myself
will deal with you.
Get ready to face your God!
13I created the mountains
and the wind.
I let humans know
what I am thinking.
I bring darkness at dawn
and step over hills.
I am the Lord God All-Powerful!
translation_text:
1Samaria aapiib, li pel man tibɔr timina, nimi bi filk ke Basann aanaa i jin ki bab na, nimi bi muk binib bi kaa kpa mpɔɔn, ni bigiim na, nimi bi muk nichatiib ke bi li tii nimi ndaan n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, li pel man. 2Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi chain kaa kpa tijɔŋ tibaa na, u puu ke, “Iwiin ibaa choo, le bi ga nan di ijapiin dar nimi buen; ni mɔmɔk ga li bi ke ijan i ijapiin chur i na la. 3Bi ga dar fuul nimi ki di baan mae ligoln aah wii nin chee na, Harmonn wɔb.”
Israel yaab aah kaan bae pu na aabɔr
4Tidindaan Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel yaab, ni yaa gee kan, ni li cha man Betel aabuul li bi chain na ni ki ti tun titunwanbir man. Di man nimi aapɔɔn mɔmɔk ki buen Gilgal aatiŋ ni ki ti tun titunwanbir. Li joo ni man nimi aawakor iwiin mɔmɔk ki nan toor kitork, ki joo ni nimi aajikaar aapar iwiin itata daal. 5Di nimi aaboroboro tii Uwumbɔr ki doon u waah ter nimi pu na, ki li kpa kipupuk naah ki tii ipiin i kpee na pu. Naah gee ke ni li ŋani tiwan ni na le na.
6“Min le nan lii nimi nkon, nimi aatikpaan ponn ni, le naa kee gir ni m chee. 7Min le nan chuu utaal buyoonn nimi aajikaar nan ban utaal sakpen na. M nan cha utaal nu kitiŋ kibaa ni, kaa nu kiken ni. Utaal nan nun bukpaab bubaa ni, le buken ma kuur. 8Binib nan di nnyunyuu ki nyan kitiŋ kibaa ponn ni, ki buen kitiŋ kiken ponn ni, ki dak ke nnyun bi nima, le bi mɔmɔk aa ti ŋmaa kan bi nyu. Nimina mɔmɔk mu aa cha ni gir ni m chee.
9“M nan tun ni libuln li ton sakpen na ke li nan kuur nimi aajikaar. Le itoon dan nan di nimi aasar mɔmɔk ŋman, ki ŋman nimi aawanyukaan aasui, ni ŋisubil, ni nkpan aasui mu. Nee mu aapuwɔb na, naa ki gir ni m chee.
10“Le m tun ni iween nan lii ni pu ke maah nan di lii Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na. M nan ku nimi aanachipɔm butɔb ni, ki di nimi aataan mu buen. Le ŋinikpol aanunun gbiin nimɔfataabun ni, ni nimi aakookoo yaan chee. Nee aapuwɔb na, naa di cha nimi aatunwanbir ki gir ni m chee ke m di cha pinn nimi.
11“M nan doo nimi bibaa ke maah nan doo Sodom ni Gomora yaab pu na. Nimi bi nan ŋmar na nan naahn limiidɔtɔgeln la. Nee mu aa cha ni gir ni m chee.” Min Uwumbɔr le len kina. 12“Kina pu na, Israel yaab, m ga daa nitafal. Maah ga ŋa kina na, gor nibaa man ke ni sil min u ye nimi Aawumbɔr na aanimbiin ni, le m ga ji nimi tibɔr.”
13Uma Uwumbɔr le naan ŋijoo sakpiin, ki naan libuln mu.
U joo waakaal kpiir tuk unibɔn;
u kpeln nwiin pu ŋani kinyeek.
U chuun dulnyaa wee ni, nin chee fɔk sakpen na.
Waayimbil sɔ: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan.

english_text:
Turn Back to the Lord
1Listen, nation of Israel,
to my mournful message:
2You, dearest Israel, have fallen,
never to rise again—
you lie deserted in your own land,
with no one to help you up.
3The Lord God has warned,
“From every ten soldiers
only one will be left;
from a thousand troops,
only a hundred will survive.”
4The Lord keeps saying,
“Israel, turn back to me
and you will live!
5Don't go to Gilgal or Bethel
or even to Beersheba.
Gilgal will be dragged away,
and Bethel will end up
as nothing.”
6Turn back to the Lord,
you descendants of Joseph,
and you will live.
If you don't, the Lord
will attack like fire.
Bethel will burn to the ground,
and no one can save it.
7You people are doomed!
You twist the truth
and trample on justice.
8 But the Lord created the stars
and put them in place.
He turns darkness to dawn
and daylight to darkness;
he scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
9God destroys mighty soldiers
and strong fortresses.
Choose Good Instead of Evil!
The Lord said:
10You people hate judges
and honest witnesses;
11you abuse the poor and demand
heavy taxes from them.
You have built expensive homes,
but you won't enjoy them;
you have planted vineyards,
but you will get no wine.
12I am the Lord, and I know
your terrible sins.
You cheat honest people
and take bribes;
you rob the poor of justice.
13Times are so evil
that anyone with good sense
will keep quiet.
14If you really want to live,
you must stop doing wrong
and start doing right.
I, the Lord God All-Powerful,
will then be on your side,
just as you claim I am.
15Choose good instead of evil!
See that justice is done.
Maybe I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will be kind to what's left
of your people.
Judgment Is Coming
16This is what the Lord has sworn:
Noisy crying will be heard
in every town and street.
Even farmers will be told
to mourn for the dead,
together with those
who are paid to mourn.
17Your vineyards will be filled
with crying and weeping,
because I will punish you.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
When the Lord Judges
18You look forward to the day
when the Lord comes to judge.
But you are in for trouble!
It won't be a time of sunshine;
all will be darkness.
19You will run from a lion,
only to meet a bear.
You will escape to your house,
rest your hand on the wall,
and be bitten by a snake.
20The day when the Lord judges
will be dark, very dark,
without a ray of light.
What the Lord Demands
21 I, the Lord, hate and despise
your religious celebrations
and your times of worship.
22I won't accept your offerings
or animal sacrifices—
not even your very best.
23No more of your noisy songs!
I won't listen
when you play your harps.
24But let justice and fairness
flow like a river
that never runs dry.
25 Israel, for forty years
you wandered in the desert,
without bringing offerings
or sacrifices to me.
26Now you will have to carry
the two idols you made—
Sakkuth, the one you call king,
and Kaiwan, the one you built
in the shape of a star.
27I will force you to march
as captives beyond Damascus.
I, the Lord God All-Powerful,
have spoken!
translation_text:
Mbimbin aakpeln aayim
1Israel aanib, li pel man nkpolahn mu m gaa ni pu na:
2Israel aatiŋ lir a, kaan ki fii sil kpala.
Ki kpo bee kitiŋ, le ubaa aan ter ki, ki fii sil.
3Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le len ke, “Israel aatiŋ kibaa ponn ni ga nyan butɔb aajab lichur ke bi ti to butɔb, le nkub baanja le ga ŋmar ki gir ni; le kiken mu ga nyan nkub, le kipiik baanja le ga ŋmar ki gir ni.”
4Le Uwumbɔr bui Israel yaab ke, “Dan m chee man, aan ki kan limɔfal. 5Taa ki buen Beerseba ke ni ti mee limeel. Taa buen Betel, ke ni ban mi. Betel aatiŋ ga nan doo fam la. Taa buen man Gilgal aatiŋ ni mu, bi ga di nima yaab buen tinaagbiir ni.”
6Li cha man Uwumbɔr chee ki ti kan limɔfal. Ni yaa kaa ŋa kina kan, u ga dan Israel yaab pu ke kimosakpeŋ aamii na la. Mmii ngbaan ga wu Betel yaab, le ubaa aan ŋmaa junn mu. 7Nimi bi len ibamɔngangal ki ji binib biken baabamɔn pu na, ni kpoi doo a.
8Uwumbɔr le naan iŋmabi, ni paacham aawan mɔmɔk.
U kpeln mbɔmbɔɔn ki di ŋa nwiihn,
ki di nwiin pu mu kpeln ŋa kinyeek.
Uma le yin nnyusakpem aanyun, ki joo kpir kitiŋ pu.
Waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr.
9U bii mpɔɔndam ni baapɔɔn mu.
10Nimi le nan binib bi len ibamɔn kaa gee inyamɔn aabɔr na. 11Ni muk bigiim le ki gaal baah kpa tijikaar ni tiwan siib ni na. Kina pu na, naan koo ŋitakpal aadichanyaan ŋi ni maa siin na ni, kaan nyu naah ŋum ŋisubil aasui i na aadaan mu. 12M nyi nimi aatunwanbir sakpenn ti ni ŋani na aakahm. Ni ŋani binibamɔm mbiin, le ki gaal igaŋgaŋlik, le ki cha bigiim aa ŋmaa kani ibamɔn libɔjil ni. 13Kina pu na, kinimbɔŋ aayoonn ngbaan kan, unii u kpa nlan na ga li ŋmin suuna la.
14Cha tiwan ni ŋan na li ye tiwan ni ni ban na, ki taa li ban kinimbɔŋ aabɔr, ki li kpa limɔfal; le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga sil li bi ni chee, ke naah len ke u bi ni chee pu na. 15Li nan kinimbɔŋ man, ki li gee tiwan ni ye ibamɔn na, aan ki cha ibamɔn li bi libɔjil ponn ni. Nibaakan, Uwumbɔr ga san binib bi gur linibol limina ni kaa kpoi na kinimbaak.
16Kina pu na, Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na le len ke, “Kinimbaak aawiil le bi ga li kaani kitisakpeŋ aasan pu. Hali bikpaab ga nyan ni baasar ni ke bi nan wii binib bi kpoi na aakpowiil ki ter baah pan binib bi ke bi wii ikpowiil na. 17Ndaan aasubil aasar mɔmɔk ponn ni ye ikpowiil ŋmeen la. Nimina mɔmɔk ga ŋa, ba pu? m choo m nan daa nitafal la.” Uwumbɔr le len kina.
18Naan nan li ŋan tii nimi bi kii Uwumbɔr aawiin ngbaan na. Nwiin ngbaan daal aan nan joo ni tiwan nibaa ni ŋan. Ba pu? mu ga nan li ye libɔmbɔln ŋmeen kaan li kpa nwiihn. 19Ni ga nan li naahn ke unii aah san uchinn chee ki ti tooh upeenaamuun nsan ni pu na la, ki li bi ke unii u kun ni linampal ki nan di uŋaal paan ligoln pu aan uwaa kpaan juu u pu na la. 20Uwumbɔr aawiin ngbaan daal ga joo ni libɔmbɔln ŋmeen la, naan li ye nwiihn; mu ga li ye nwiin mu bɔɔn timm kaan li wiin kpala na la.
21Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Maa gee naah kuuni ki ji njim ki dooni mi pu na; naa ŋan m chee kpala. 22Ni yaa toor kitork ki di see mmii ni, ni nimi aajikaabim aapiin tii mi kan, maan gaa ni; maan gaa naah lii tiwakor ti filk ke ni nan di tii mi ipiin na. 23Di cha naah gaa ilahn mpɔɔn pu ki gbaa tibar ki tii mi na man. Maan pel. 24Naah ga ŋa pu ki piir nsui na sɔ: Cha ibamɔn ni mbimbinyaan li wiir ke limɔɔl aanyun aah wiir kaa door pu na.
25“Israel aanib, maa nan ban kitork ni ipiin ibaa ŋibin imonko ilee ŋi ponn ni m nan di nimi dii ni litambol ŋmeen aatiŋ ni na ni chee. 26Tɔ, dandana wee, naah dii ki toor liwaal Sakuf li ye nimi aawaabɔr na, ni liwaal Kaiwann li ye liŋmabil aanaŋ na, nima pu na, ni ga li joo tiwanaankaan ngbaan 27le m ga di nimi buen tinaagbiir ni, kitiŋ ki bi Damaskus aatiŋ aapuwɔb na ni,” Tidindaan u aayimbil ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na le len kina.

english_text:
Israel Will Be Punished
1Do you rulers in Jerusalem
and in the city of Samaria
feel safe and at ease?
Everyone bows down to you,
and you think you are better
than any other nation.
But you are in for trouble!
2Look what happened
to the cities of Calneh,
powerful Hamath,
and Gath in Philistia.
Are you greater than any
of those kingdoms?
3You are cruel, and you forget
the coming day of judgment.
4You rich people lounge around
on beds with ivory posts,
while dining on the meat
of your lambs and calves.
5You sing foolish songs
to the music of harps,
and you make up new tunes,
just as David used to do.
6You drink all the wine you want
and wear expensive perfume,
but you don't care about
the ruin of your nation.
7So you will be the first
to be dragged off as captives;
your good times will end.
8The Lord God All-Powerful
has sworn by his own name:
“You descendants of Jacob
make me angry by your pride,
and I hate your fortresses.
And so I will surrender your city
and possessions
to your enemies.”
9If only ten of you survive
by hiding in a house
you will still die.
10As you carry out a corpse
to prepare it for burial,
your relative in the house
will ask, “Are there others?”
You will answer, “No!”
Then your relative will reply,
“Be quiet! Don't dare mention
the name of the Lord.”
11At the Lord's command,
houses great and small
will be smashed to pieces.
12Horses can't gallop on rocks;
oceans can't be plowed.
But you have turned justice
and fairness
into bitter poison.
13You celebrate the defeat
of Lo-Debar and Karnaim,
and you boast by saying,
“We did it on our own.”
14But the Lord God All-Powerful
will send a nation to attack
you people of Israel.
They will capture Lebo-Hamath
in the north,
Arabah Creek in the south,
and everything in between.
translation_text:
Israel aatiŋ aah ga bii pu na
1Nimi bi bi dafir Sionn aatiŋ ni, ni nimi bi dak ke ni kan limɔfal Samaria aatiŋ ni na, naan nan li ŋan ni pu, nimi bi ye linibokpaan Israel na aaninkpiib, nimi bi binib biken chaa ni chee ki ti ban nterm na, 2li cha ti lik man Kalne aatisakpeŋ na, ki buen man Hamaf aatisakpeŋ ki kpa mpɔɔn na, ki sunn buen Filistia yaab aatisakpeŋ Gaf chee. Mu aa ŋan ki jer Juda ni Israel aanaan. Le mu aatingbaan mu aa wiir jer nimi yoo. 3Nimi, ni yii kaa kii ke nwiin mundaal tiwan mɔmɔk ga bii na choo, le naah tee ŋani pu na le moo joo nwiin ngbaan duuni nimi. 4Nimi bi dɔ nimi aawandookaan ni diin ki ŋan na pu, ki ji n‑yaan ni nkpan na, naa ga nan li ŋan tii nimi kpala. 5Ni gee ke ni li naani ilahn ke David aah nan naani pu na, ki joo gbaa tibar. 6Ni nyu ndaan tiyikur ti wiir na ponn ni, ki ŋani tulalee tiib bi nu mɔ sakpen na, kaa tee wii Israel aah ga bii pu na aakpowiil. 7Kina pu na, nimi le ga puen buen tinaagbiir ni. Le nimi aajim mɔmɔk ga doo.
8Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le tii nsurm mumina: “M nan Israel yaab aagaak, kaa neen baadichasakpiin ŋi kpa kinyaan ni tiwan mɔmɔk na. M ga di baatiyil ni tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi ki ponn ni na di tii baadim.”
9Binib kipiik le yaa gur lidichal ni kan, bi ga kpo. 10Utekpel aado yoo, u yeh waakpuul na, le ga yoor linikpol ngbaan nyan lidichal ngbaan ni. Udo yoo ngbaan ga yin unii umɔk gur lidichal ngbaan ni na ki baa ke, “Unii ubaa ki gur ki bi aa chee ee?”
Le nneel ga kii ke, “Aayii.”
Le udo yoo ngbaan ga bui ke, “Li ŋmin suuna. Ti ga chuu tibaa le ki taa ki yin Uwumbɔr aayimbil.”
11Uwumbɔr yaa tii waamɔboln kan, ŋidichasakpiin ni ŋiwaatiir mɔmɔk ga wii yuk yuk. 12Itaan san ŋitakpasakpiin pu uu? Bijab joo inaaja ko nima aa? Le nimi tee di ibamɔn kpaln njinn, ki di mbamɔn kpaln inyamɔn.
13Ni puk kipupuk ke ni nyaŋ Lo Debar aatiŋ. Ni puk kipupuk ke, “Ti nan pɔɔ ki nyaŋ Karnayim aatiŋ.”
14Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ubaa le len ke, “Israel aanib, m cha ke m ti joo ni bijab bi kaa ye Israel yaab na, le bi nan gaa nimi aatiŋ. Bi ga muk nimi, nimi aatim mɔmɔk ni, ki nya Hamaf aasan mu bi liwipuul aaŋangan wɔb na ki ti saa Araba aakpen mu bi liwipuul aaŋangii wɔb na.”

english_text:
A Vision of Locusts
1The Lord God showed me that he is going to send locusts to attack your crops. It will happen after the king has already been given his share of the grain and before the rest of the grain has been harvested. 2In my vision the locusts ate every crop in the land, and I said to the Lord, “Please forgive your nation. It's so weak. How can it survive?”
3Then the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of Fire
4The Lord showed me that he is going to send a ball of fire to burn up everything on earth, including the ocean. 5Then I said, “Won't you please stop? How can our weak nation survive?”
6Again the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of a Measuring Line
7The Lord showed me a vision of himself standing beside a wall and holding a string with a weight tied to the end of it. The string and weight had been used to measure the straightness of the wall. 8Then he asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A measuring line,” I answered.
The Lord said, “I'm using this measuring line to show that my people Israel don't measure up, and I won't forgive them any more. 9Their sacred places will be destroyed, and I will send war against the nation of King Jeroboam.”
Amos and Amaziah
10Amaziah the priest at Bethel sent this message to King Jeroboam of Israel, “Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. Our nation cannot put up with his message for very long. 11Here is what he is saying:
‘Jeroboam will be put to death,
and the people will be taken
to a foreign country.’ ”
12Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet. 13Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
14I answered:
I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees. 15But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel. 16And here you are, telling me not to preach! 17Now, listen to what the Lord says about you:
Your wife will become
a prostitute in the city,
your sons and daughters
will be killed in war,
and your land will be divided
among others.
You will die in a country
of foreigners,
and the people of Israel
will be dragged
from their homeland.
translation_text:
Itoon aadaŋ
1Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le kpiir tiwan nimina mɔk mi tidaŋ ponn ni. Tidaŋ ngbaan ponn ni m nan kan u naan itoon buyoonn bi chee ubɔrkpaan aamoor ki doo aan timopɔln ki bi tukni na. 2Maadaŋ ngbaan ponn ni m nan kan itoon ngbaan ŋman tiwan nimɔk soon na kitiŋ ngbaan pu doo, le m bui ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, di cha pinn saanib. Bi ga ŋa kinye ki ŋmar? Bi par le kaa kpa mpɔɔn.”
3Le Uwumbɔr kpeln waalandak ki bui ke, “Saah kan tiwan ni na aan ŋa kina.”
Mmii aadaŋ
4Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le nan ki kpiir tiwan nimina mu mɔk mi tidaŋ ponn ni. Tidaŋ timina ponn ni m nan kan ke u gor ubaa ke u di mmii daa waanib aatafal. Mmii ngbaan nan cha nnyusakpem mu dɔ kitiŋ kee aataab na foor, ki piin ki bi wu kitiŋ mu. 5Le m bui ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, di cha. Saanib ga ŋa kinye ki ŋmar? Bi par pam kaa kpa mpɔɔn mubaa.”
6Le Uwumbɔr ki kpeln waalandak ki bui ke, “Nimina mu aan ki ŋa kina.”
Likpaln li bi joo ŋaŋni tiwan na aadaŋ
7Uwumbɔr nan ki kpiir tiwan nimina mɔk mi tidaŋ ponn ni. M nan kan u, le u si gbɔk ligoln li bi di likpaln li bi joo tukni tiwan ni tuk na maa li na, le ki joo likpaln uŋaal ni, 8le u baa mi ke, “Amos, aa waa ba?”
Le m bui u ke, “Likpaln li bi joo ŋaŋni tiwan na.”
Le u bui mi ke, “M joo li ke m di mɔk si ke maanib naahn ligoln li bi maa li aan laa tuk na la. Maan ki kpeln maalandak maah ga daa bitafal pu na. 9Nin chee Aisak aayaabitiib nan mee min Uwumbɔr na mɔmɔk ga bii doo. Israel yaab aameen aadir mɔmɔk ga kpaln ŋilangben ŋi ber doo na la. M ga kuln ubɔr Jeroboam aanaan.”
Amos ni Amasia
10Amasia, u nan ye utotoor ki bi Betel aatiŋ ni na, le nan tun ti tuk Israel aabɔrkpaan Jeroboam ke: “Amos chuun ban isan binib chee ke u nyan si nnaan ni la. Waabɔlen ga bii litimbol lee doo. 11Waah len pu na sɔ: ‘Jeroboam ga kpo butɔb ni, le Israel aanib aadim ga chuu bi ki di buen kitiyayaŋ ni.’”
12Amasia aah nan tuk Amos pu na sɔ: “Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr, nima ngbaan ŋeer kina. Gir li cha Juda ki ti li mooni Uwumbɔr aabɔr nima, ki cha bi pa si tibɔr ngbaan pu. 13Taa ki nabr Uwumbɔr aabɔr Betel aatiŋ pu do kpala. Ubɔrkpaan aah dooni Uwumbɔr nin chee na sɔ, linibol lee Aameen Aadichal le na.”
14Le Amos bui u ke, “Maa ye ubɔnabr. Unii ubaa mu aa mɔk mi Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr aatuln. M ye upihkpaal la, le ki lik ŋisubil aasui mu. 15Le Uwumbɔr chuu nyan mi maapihkpaal ponn ni ki bui mi ke m ti nabr waabɔr tuk waanib Israel yaab. 16Kina pu na, li pel Uwumbɔr aah len pu dandana wee na. Aa bui ke m di cha libɔnabr ki taa ki mooni tibɔbir Israel aanib pu. 17Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr le len sin Amasia chee na, ‘Aapuu ga kpaln upiidagoor le kitiŋ kimina ponn ni, le bi ga ku saabim mu butɔb ni. Bi ga yakr saatiŋ tii biniyayam, le sin aabaa ga ti kpo kitiyayaŋ ni la. Le bidim ga sil chuu Israel yaab ki di bi buen kitiyayaŋ ni.’”

english_text:
A Basket of Fruit
1The Lord God showed me a basket of ripe fruit 2and asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied.
Then he said,
“This is the end
for my people Israel.
I won't forgive them again.
3Instead of singing
in the temple,
they will cry and weep.
Dead bodies will be everywhere.
So keep silent!
I, the Lord, have spoken!”
Israel Is Doomed
The Lord said:
4You people crush those in need
and wipe out the poor.
5You say to yourselves,
“How much longer before the end
of the New Moon Festival?
When will the Sabbath be over?
Our wheat is ready,
and we want to sell it now.
We can't wait to cheat
and charge high prices
for the grain we sell.
We will use dishonest scales
6and mix dust in the grain.
Those who are needy and poor
don't have any money.
We will make them our slaves
for the price
of a pair of sandals.”
7I, the Lord, won't forget
any of this,
though you take great pride
in your ancestor Jacob.
8Your country will tremble,
and you will mourn.
It will be like the Nile River
that rises and overflows,
then sinks back down.
9On that day, I, the Lord God,
will make the sun
go down at noon,
and I will turn daylight
into darkness.
10Your festivals and joyful singing
will turn into sorrow.
You will wear sackcloth
and shave your heads,
as you would at the death
of your only son.
It will be a horrible day.
11I, the Lord, also promise you
a terrible shortage,
but not of food and water.
You will hunger and thirst
to hear my message.
12You will search everywhere—
from north to south,
from east to west.
You will go all over the earth,
seeking a message
from me, the Lord.
But you won't find one.
13Your beautiful young women
and your young men
will faint from thirst.
14You made promises
to the goddess Ashimah
at Samaria;
you made vows to other gods
at the shrines
of Dan and Beersheba.
So now you will fall
and never get up.
translation_text:
Ŋisubil aadaŋ
1Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le nan ki di tiwan nimina mɔk mi tidaŋ ponn ni. Tidaŋ ngbaan ponn ni m nan kan ŋisubil ŋi ŋeer limool na kibɔɔkuuk ponn ni. Le Uwumbɔr baa mi ke, “Amos, aa waa ba?”
Le m bui u ke, “M waa ŋisubil ŋi ŋeer limool na kibɔɔkuuk ponn ni la.”
2Le Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, “Buyoonn maanib Israel yaab ga doo na ŋeer le na; maan ki kpeln maalandak ke maan daa bitafal. 3Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, baah gaa ilahn i libɔrdichal ni na ga kpaln ikpowiil la. Ŋinikpol ga po li dɔ ni kookoo la. Le bi ga di bi mae liŋmiŋmiln.”
Israel aatiŋ aah ga doo pu na
4Li pel nimina man, nimi bi muk bifalaadam, ki ban ke ni ku doo bigiim kitiŋ kee ni na. 5Ni bui nibaa ke, “Taan ŋmaa kiir ke iwinyaan daal ti jer waahr aan ti nin kooh timi aajikaar. Bayoonn aan likpaakool aawiin ga doo, aan ti ki piin ki kooh timi aawan, ki cha ti tii kidaak ki pɔɔ na, ki di tiwaŋaŋkaan ni kaa ye nibamɔnn na di ŋaŋ ki ji biwandaab? 6Ti ga ŋmaa di tigbengbir kooh kidaak ki pɔɔ na. Ti ga kan ugiin u kaan ŋmaa pa waapɔln na, hali kaan ŋmaa pa ŋinaatak pu na ki daa u, ki di u ŋa unaagbiija.”
7Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aadindaan na le puu ke, “Maan suln baatunwanbir pu kpala. 8Kina pu na, kitiŋ ga deŋ, le unii umɔk bi kitiŋ kee pu na aasui ga bii. Kitiŋ mɔmɔk ga nyɔŋ, ki ga fii ki gir lir ke Nail Aamɔɔsakpeln na. 9N‑yoonn choo le nwiin ga lir liwinjakal pu, le dulnyaa bɔnn liwiyil pu. Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. 10M ga kpeln nimi aajim aayoonn ŋa ŋikpuu, ki kpeln nimi aamɔɔn aalahn ŋa inimbaalahn. M ga cha ni kuu nimi aayikpir ki peen tiwan ni saak kuub na, aan ki cha ni li naahn libibaal li kpo na aate ni una aah wii waakpuul pu na. Nwiin ngbaan daal ga li cho kina le ki ti saa mu aadoon.
11“N‑yoonn choo, buyoonn m ga tun ni nkon kitiŋ kee pu na. Nkon ga li joo binib, ni mu aan li ye tijikaar aakon; nnyunyuu ga li joo bi, ki mu aan li ye nnyun aanyunyuu. Uwumbɔr aabɔr aakon ni taanyunyuu le ga li joo bi. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔndaan le len kina. 12Binib ga chuun liwipuul ni liwilir, ki nya ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa ŋŋangii wɔb. Bi ga lik ni kookoo ki ban Uwumbɔr aabɔr kaan kan ti. 13Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, binachipɔm ni bisapɔm bi pɔɔ na ga lir ki fik nnyunyuu pu. 14Binib bi puuni Samaria aawaa ki len ke ‘Dann aawaal pu’, bee ‘Beerseba aawaal pu’ na, kina aanib ga lir, kaan ki fii sil daalbaadaal.”

english_text:
Judgment on Israel
1I saw a vision of the Lord
standing by the temple altar,
and he said,
“Shake the columns
until the tops fall loose,
and the doorposts crumble.
Then make the pieces fall
on the people below.
I will take a sword and kill
anyone who escapes.
2“If they dig deep into the earth
or climb to the sky,
I'll reach out and get them.
3If they escape to the peaks
of Mount Carmel,
I'll search and find them.
And if they hide from me
at the bottom of the ocean,
I'll command a sea monster
to bite them.
4I'll send a sword to kill them,
wherever their enemies
drag them off as captives.
I'm determined to hurt them,
not to help them.”
His Name Is the Lord
5When the Lord God All-Powerful
touches the earth, it melts,
and its people mourn.
God makes the earth rise
and then fall,
just like the Nile River.
6He built his palace in the heavens
and let its foundations
rest on the earth.
He scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
His name is the Lord.
The Lord Is God
7Israel, I am the Lord God,
and the Ethiopians
are no less important to me
than you are.
I brought you out of Egypt,
but I also brought
the Philistines from Crete
and the Arameans from Kir.
8My eyes have seen
what a sinful nation you are,
and I'll wipe you out.
But I will leave a few
of Jacob's descendants.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9At my command, all of you
will be sifted like grain.
Israelites who remain faithful
will be scattered
among the nations.
And the others will be trapped
like trash in a sifter.
10Some of you are evil,
and you deny
that you will ever get caught.
But you will be killed.
The Lord's Promise to Israel
11 In the future, I will rebuild
David's fallen kingdom.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again,
just as it used to be.
12Then you will capture Edom
and the other nations
that are mine.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and my words will come true.
13You will have such a harvest
that you won't be able
to bring in all of your wheat
before plowing time.
You will have grapes left over
from season to season;
your fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
14I'll make Israel prosper again.
You will rebuild your towns
and live in them.
You will drink wine
from your own vineyards
and eat the fruit you grow.
15I'll plant your roots deep
in the land I have given you,
and you won't ever
be uprooted again.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aabɔjil
1M nan kan Uwumbɔr si gbɔk kitork aabimbiln, le ki tii waamɔboln ke: “Faa man Maadichal aagon mpɔɔn pu aan kaadipimoor deŋ. Gbaa wii ŋi aan ŋi lir binib ngbaan aayil pu man. M ga ku binib bi gur na butɔb ni la. Ubaa aan san ŋmar; ubaa kina aan ŋmar. Hali bi yaa gbii ibuu ki koo kitekpiitiŋ ni kan, m ga chuu bi. 2Hali bi yaa jon buen paacham kan, m ga sunn ni bi kitiŋ. 3Bi yaa jon ti kal Kamel aajool paab kan, m ga ban kan bi ki chuu bi. Bi yaa koo nnyusakpem aataab ki ti bɔr mi kan, m ga cha nnyusakpem ponn ni aapeewanbiik juu bi. 4Baadim yaa chuu bi kunn bido kan, m ga cha bi ku bi. M ban m kuln bi la, maa ban m ter bi.”
5Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan yaa meeh kitiŋ kan,
ki deŋni la,
le binib bimɔk bi nima na wii ikpowiil.
Dulnyaa mɔmɔk fii ki lir ke Nail Aamɔɔsakpeln aah fii ki lir pu na la.
6Uwumbɔr maa waadichal paacham la,
le ki cha kitaapaak bi kitiŋ aapaacham,
le ki joo nnyusakpem aanyun kpir kitiŋ pu.
Waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr.
7Uwumbɔr len ke, “Israel aanib, m gee Kus aanib ke maah gee nimi pu na la. Maah nan nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na, kina le m nan di Filistia yaab nyan ni Krete aatiŋ ni, ki nyan Siria yaab mu Kir aatiŋ ni. 8Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔndaan ka ki lik titunwanbir sakpenn ti Israel aanaan mue tun na, ki ga doo mu dulnyaa wee ni. Maan tee ku biyaabitiib doo.
9“M ga tii maamɔboln ki cha Israel aanib deŋ ke baah bi yak n‑yon le kiyayak ponn ni na. Ŋinibol mɔmɔk ponn ni, m ga yak bi, ki nyan binib bi kaa bi tibaa ni na. 10Titunwanbirdam bi ŋmal maanib ni na ga kpoi butɔb ni, binib bi mɔmɔk len ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aan cha kinimbɔŋ duun ni timi’ na ga kpoi.”
Baah ga ki gir maa Israel aatiŋ pu na
11Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Nwiin mubaa choo, buyoonn m ga ki gir maa Ubɔrkpaan David aanaan mu bi ke lidichal li ber doo na. M ga ki gir fiin mu. M ga ki fiin mu siin ke mu aah nan bi pu n‑yaayoonn na. 12Le Israel yaab ga jan ki gaa Edom aatiŋ ki gur na, ni ntim mumɔk nan puun ye maatim na.” Uwumbɔr u ga cha nimina ŋa na le len kina.
13Uwumbɔr le ki len ke,
“N‑yoonn choo, buyoonn tijikaar ga ŋa mala mala
ki jer baah ga ŋmaa chee pu na,
le ndaan aasubil ga lu mala mala
ki jer baah ga ŋmaa ŋaa ndaan pu na.
Ŋijoo ni ŋigongon paab ga kpaln ikpaakon ŋmeen la.
14Le m ga giin ni maanib baatiŋ ni,
le bi ga ki gir maa baatim mu nan ber doo na ki koo mu ni.
Bi ga ŋum ndaan aasubil aasui ki nyu ŋaadaan,
ki ga ko ikpaakon ki ji yaajikaar.
15M ga giin bi kaan, maah tii bi kitiŋ ki na pu,
le ubaa aan ki ŋmaa daa nyan bi ki ni daalbaadaal.”
Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

english_text:
Edom's Pride and Punishment
1 The Lord God gave Obadiah
a message about Edom,
and this is what we heard:
“I, the Lord, have sent
a messenger
with orders for the nations
to attack Edom.”
2The Lord said to Edom:
I will make you the weakest
and most despised nation.
3You live in a mountain fortress,
because your pride
makes you feel safe from attack,
but you are mistaken.
4I will still bring you down,
even if you fly higher
than an eagle
or nest among the stars.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
5If thieves break in at night,
they steal
only what they want.
And people who harvest grapes
always leave some unpicked.
But, Edom, you are doomed!
6Everything you treasure most
will be taken from you.
7Your allies can't be trusted.
They will force you out
of your own country.
And your best friends
will trick and trap you,
even before you know it.
8Edom, when this happens,
I, the Lord, will destroy
all your marvelous wisdom.
9Warriors from the city of Teman
will be terrified,
and you descendants of Esau
will be wiped out.
The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
