10You were cruel to your relatives,
the descendants of Jacob.
Now you will be destroyed,
disgraced forever.
11You stood there and watched
as foreigners entered Jerusalem
and took what they wanted.
In fact, you were no better
than those foreigners.
12Why did you celebrate
when such a dreadful disaster
struck your relatives?
Why were you so pleased
when everyone in Judah
was suffering?
13They are my people,
and you were cruel to them.
You went through their towns,
sneering and stealing
whatever was left.
14In their time of torment,
you ambushed refugees
and handed them over
to their attackers.
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
15The day is coming
when I, the Lord,
will judge the nations.
And, Edom, you will pay in full
for what you have done.
16I forced the people of Judah
to drink the wine of my anger
on my sacred mountain.
Soon the neighboring nations
must drink their fill—
then vanish without a trace.
Victory for Israel
17The Lord's people who escape
will go to Mount Zion,
and it will be holy.
Then Jacob's descendants
will capture the land of those
who took their land.
18Israel will be a fire,
and Edom will be straw
going up in flames.
The Lord has spoken!
19The people of Israel
who live in the Southern Desert
will take the land of Edom.
Those who live in the hills
will capture Philistia,
Ephraim, and Samaria.
And the tribe of Benjamin
will conquer Gilead.
20Those who return from captivity
will control Phoenicia
as far as Zarephath.
Captives from Jerusalem
who were taken to Sepharad
will capture the towns
of the Southern Desert.
21Those the Lord has saved
will live on Mount Zion
and rule over Edom.
Then the kingdom will belong
to the Lord.
translation_text:
1Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah di tibɔr ti tuk waabɔnabr Obadia, ki joo cha Edom aatiŋ wɔb na sɔ.
Uwumbɔr ga daa Edom yaab aatafal
Uwumbɔr tun waabɔnabr ŋitimbol mɔmɔk chee,
le ti ŋun waabɔr ti u tuk u na ke,
“Gor nibaa man.
Cha ti buen ti to Edom yaab butɔb man.”
2Uwumbɔr bui Edom yaab ke, “M ga ŋa nimi bigiim,
unibɔn mɔmɔk ga lik nimi fam.
3Nimi aagaak le ŋmann nimi.
Nimi aatiyil pɔɔ ke litakpal na la,
le nido bi ŋijoo ŋi fɔk na pu,
le ni bui nibaa ke,
‘Ŋma ga ŋmaa daa ker timi lii ni taab?’
4Hali ni yaa di nimi aadichal ti maa paachapaacham
ke likaagiil aadir na,
aan ŋi daa ke iŋmabi na kan,
m ga ŋmaa daa ker nimi lii ni taab.
5Binaayukb yaa dan kinyeek bi nan su tiwan kan,
bi yoor tiwan ni bi ban na baanja la.
Bipiib mu yaa peei ikpa kan,
bi peei le ki gur ngem.
Le nimi aadim ma ku doo nimi kookoo.
6Esɔ aayaabitiib, binib sun nimi aawangol mɔmɔk a.
7Nimi aamaantɔtiib ŋmann nimi la;
le bi jenn nyan nimi,
nimi aatiŋ ponn ni.
Binib bi nan ye nijɔtiib na le nyaŋ nimi butɔb ni
dandana wee na.
Nijɔtiib bi nan ji ni chee tijikaar na
le ŋmann nimi koon gaawɔb ni;
bi baa le ke, ‘Baalan mu bi kpa na bi la?’
8Nwiin mundaal m ga daa Edom yaab aatafal na,
m ga ku bilandam mɔmɔk aan baalan mɔmɔk doo.
9Temann aajab bi jaa kijaak na ga san ijawaan pam,
le baatiŋ Edom aatɔb aajab mɔmɔk ga kpoi.
Budabu pu Uwumbɔr ga daa Edom yaab aatafal na
10“Naah ŋa pu ki sun ninaabitiib,
bi ye Jakob aayaabitiib na aawan, ki ku bi na,
kina le binib ga lik nimi fam ki kuln nimi.
11Nwiin mundaal aan baadim nan koo ni baatiŋ ni ki bii baawan na,
ni nan si nima kaa gar tibaa.
Ni bir ke biwɔwɔm bi nan yoor Jerusalem aatiŋ aawangol di buen ki ti yakr na la.
12Naa ŋan ke ni ba li mɔɔni
buyoonn ninaabitiib Juda yaab kan mpombiin na.
Nwiin mundaal bi nan kuln baatiŋ na,
naa ba ga nan li kpa mpopiin liyaadaal ngbaan.
Naa ŋan ke buyoonn bi nan bi tibɔbir ni na, nimi li bi laa.
13Naa ba ga nan koo maanib aatiŋ ni ki ti lik bi fam,
ki su baawangol nwiin mundaal bi bi tibɔbir ni na.
14Naa ba ga nan li si isayakr
ki chur binib bi nan san ke bi ŋmar na,
kaa ba ga di bi tii baadim,
nwiin mundaal bi nan bi tibɔr ni na.
Uwumbɔr ga ji ŋitimbol tibɔr
15“Nwiin ngbaan peen ni, bundaal aan min Uwumbɔr
ga ji ŋitimbol mɔmɔk tibɔr na peen ni.
Edom yaab, naah ŋa pu na,
kina le ni ga kan.
Naah tii pu na,
kina le bi ga giin tii nimi.
16Maanib nan kan ntafadaan mu bir na
maajool li bi chain na pu.
Binib bimɔk bi ki mann goln na
ga kan ntafadaan mu jer kina na.
Bi ga kan ntafadaan, le ki lil, kaan ki gir ni.
Israel yaab aah nyaŋ kijaak pu na
17“Sionn aajool na pu le binib bibaa ga ŋmar,
le lijool ngbaan pu ga kpaln miyaan.
Jakob aayaabitiib ga gaa baatiŋ ki ye baatiŋ ibamɔn ni na.
18Jakob ni Josef aanib ga li naahn mmii la;
bi ga doo Esɔ aanib ke mmii aah wu kinaakook pu na la.
Esɔ aanib ponn ni ubaa aan ŋmar.
Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.
19Binib ga nyan ni Juda aawilir aaŋangii wɔb
le ki nan gaa Edom aatiŋ;
le binib bi bi liwilir wɔb aagongon ni na ga gaa Filistia yaab aatiŋ,
Israel yaab mu ga gaa Efraim ni Samaria aatim,
le Benjaminn aanib ga gaa Gilead aatiŋ.
20Israel yaab bi binib nan chur bi buen kitiyayaŋ ni
ki cha baatiŋ liwipuul aaŋangan wɔb na
ga ki gir nan gaa Fonisia aatiŋ
ki ti saa Sarefaf aatiŋ ni ŋŋangan wɔb.
Jerusalem yaab bi binib nan chur bi tinaagbiir
ki di bi buen Sadis aatiŋ ni na
le ga gaa ntim mu bi Juda aaŋangii wɔb na.
21Jerusalem yaab bi ga nyaŋ baadim mɔmɔk na
ga tak Edom yaab ki nyaŋ bi.
Le Uwumbɔr uma ubaa ga li ye Ubɔrkpaan.”

english_text:
Jonah Runs from the Lord
1 One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai, 2to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
3Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
4But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces. 5The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter.
All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep. 6The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
7Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
8They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
9Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
10When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
11The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
12Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
13The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute. 14So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.” 15Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down. 16The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
17 The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_text:
Jona aah yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb pu na
1Daalbaadaal, le Uwumbɔr nan len Amitai aajapɔɔn Jona chee tibɔr timina. 2U nan bui u ke, “Li cha kitisakpeŋ Ninefa ponn ni ki ti galn ki; m nyi kaanib aah kpa mbiin pu na.” 3Le Jona nan tee fii ki di toŋ nibaa wɔb ke u bɔr Uwumbɔr. U nan di buen Jopa aatiŋ ni la, nima chee le u ti kan buŋɔb bu cha Speenn aatiŋ ni na. U nan pan le ki koo bu ponn ni, biŋɔŋaab chee, ke bi buen Speenn aatiŋ ni, nin chee Uwumbɔr aan ki kan u na. 4Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan cha libupɔɔl libaa dan nan lir nnyusakpem ngbaan pu, libuln ngbaan nan bir pam, le buŋɔb ngbaan nan ban bu wii ki muin. 5Ijawaan nan chuu biŋɔŋaab ngbaan, le bi mɔmɔk wii ki yin baawaa ki ban nterm. Bi nan nyan ŋitun ŋi bi bu ponn ni na mae ŋa nnyun ni ke bu taa ki li nyuun. N‑yoonn mue na, Jona nan dɔ bu ponn ni ki dɔ geen.
6Le biŋɔŋaab ngbaan aaninkpel nan ti kan u nima chee, le ki baa u ke, “Aa dɔ ŋani ba, aa dɔ geen la aa? Fii sil ki mee saawaal aan li ter timi. Nibaakan, li ga san timi kinimbaak ki gaa timi lii.”
7Biŋɔŋaab ngbaan nan bui tɔb ke, “Cha ti pul kipulk timi aakaal aah mɔk pu na man, ki lik ke ŋma ye unimbɔŋdaan u joo ni timi linimaln limina na.” Bi nan ŋa kina, le ki kan ke Jona le ye unimbɔŋdaan. 8Le bi bui u ke, “Tɔ, bui timi, ŋma aan ti ga galn tibɔr timina pu? Aa bi ŋani ba do chee na? Aa nyan ni lilatingbaln ni? Aado ye la chee? Aa ye lilanibol aanii?”
9Le Jona gar bi ke, “M ye Hiibru aanii la. M dooni Uwumbɔr u ye paacham Aadindaan, ki naan kitiŋ, ni nnyusakpem na la.” 10Jona nan ki tuk bi ke u bi san bɔrni Uwumbɔr la.
Ijawaan nan chuu biŋɔŋaab ngbaan, le bi bui u ke, “Saah ŋa pu na aa ŋan kpala.” 11Kitaabuŋ ngbaan nan moo pɔɔk kpae la, le biŋɔŋaab ngbaan baa u ke, “Ti ga ŋa kinye aan kitaabuŋ ngbaan di cha?”
12Jona nan gar bi ke, “Di mi ŋa nnyusakpem ngbaan ni man, le mu ga doon suuna. M nyi ke ni ye maataani pu le ni nan koo kitaabuŋbiik kee ni.”
13Tɔ, biŋɔŋaab ngbaan nan tee pɔɔn bibaa ke bi di buŋɔb ngbaan buen ligbaal, le ki moo ŋaal bu mpɔɔn pu. Tɔ, kitaabuŋ nan moo kpae la, le baa ŋmaa buen nibaa chee. 14Kina pu le bi wii ki yin Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, ti mee si, taa daa titafal ki ku timi uja wee aamɔfal pu. Uwumbɔr, sin le tun nimina mɔmɔk; ni ye saatuln la,” 15le ki yoor Jona di mee ŋa nnyusakpem ngbaan ni. Libuul ngbaan ni le mu doon suuna. 16Nima le nan cha biŋɔŋaab ngbaan san Uwumbɔr ijawaan ki toor kitork tii u, ki puu tipuur tii u.
17Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan cha ujan sakpiin ubaa chuu Jona di nab, le u nan bi ujan ngbaan aaponn ni, iwiin itaa ni tinyer titaa.

english_text:
Jonah's Prayer
1From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
2When I was in trouble, Lord,
I prayed to you,
and you listened to me.
From deep in the world
of the dead,
I begged for your help,
and you answered my prayer.
3You threw me down
to the bottom of the sea.
The water was churning
all around;
I was completely covered
by your mighty waves.
4I thought I was swept away
from your sight,
never again to see
your holy temple.
5I was almost drowned
by the swirling waters
that surrounded me.
Seaweed had wrapped
around my head.
6I had sunk down deep
below the mountains
beneath the sea.
I knew that forever,
I would be a prisoner there.
But, you, Lord God,
rescued me from that pit.
7When my life was slipping away,
I remembered you—
and in your holy temple
you heard my prayer.
8All who worship worthless idols
turn from the God
who offers them mercy.
9But with shouts of praise,
I will offer a sacrifice
to you, my Lord.
I will keep my promise,
because you are the one
with power to save.
10 The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_text:
Jona aah mee limeel li na
1Jona nan bi ujan ngbaan aaponn ni taab le ki mee Udindaan Uwumbɔr ke:
2“Uwumbɔr, buyoonn nsui bii na le m yin si,
le aa kii maayim ngbaan.
M nan bi kitekpiitiŋ ni taab taab ki wii yin si ki ban nterm,
le aa ŋun maah yin pu na.
3Aa di mi mee lii taab taab, nnyusakpem aataab,
nin chee nnyun nan mann goln mi na,
le saanyunkpenn ti kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na fii labr m pu.
4M nan nyi ke aa nyan mi aanimbiin ni la,
le maan ki kan Saadichal li bi chain na.
5Nnyun nan biin m pu ki kpar mi,
nnyusakpem nan biin m pu kookoo a,
le nnyusakpem ponn ni aamoor biin n‑yil pu.
6M nan buen taab taab ŋijoo aataab,
ki ti fuu kitiŋ ki aabisamɔi lak n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na ni.
Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, sin le giin nyan ni mi taab taab ngbaan,
le m beenin kpa limɔfal.
7Uwumbɔr, buyoonn m dak ke
maamɔfal doo na, le m mee si,
le aa bi Saadichal li bi chain na ponn ni
ki ŋun maameel ngbaan.
8Binib bi dooni ŋiwaa ŋi kaa po kpa tinyoor tibaa na
yii saanimbaasaln.
9Le mma ga gaa ilahn pak si, m ga toor kitork tii si,
ki ŋa maah puu ke m ga ŋa pu na.
Limɔfal nyan ni Uwumbɔr chee la.”
10Le Uwumbɔr bui ujan ngbaan ke u ti wuln Jona lii limɔɔtambol pu, le u ŋa kina.

english_text:
Jonah Goes to Nineveh
1Once again the Lord told Jonah 2to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
3Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it. 4 After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
5They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
6When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust. 7-9Then he and his officials sent out an order for everyone in the city to obey. It said:
None of you or your animals may eat or drink a thing. Each of you must wear sackcloth, and you must even put sackcloth on your animals.
You must also pray to the Lord God with all your heart and stop being sinful and cruel. Maybe God will change his mind and have mercy on us, so we won't be destroyed.
10When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_text:
Jona ŋa Uwumbɔr aah bui u pu na
1Uwumbɔr nan ki gir len Jona chee tibɔr, 2ki bui ke, “Li cha kitisakpeŋ Ninefa ni, ki ti di tibɔr ti m di tii si na tuk bi.” 3Jona nan kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki buen Ninefa, kitisakpeŋ ki u nan di iwiin itaa bɔ dii ki ponn ni ki ti saa kimɔk na. 4Jona nan piin ki bɔ dii kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni, le waah chuun nwimɔn aasachuln na, le u mooni tuk binib ngbaan ke, “Joo cha ni iwiin imonko ilee na, Ninefa aatiŋ ga kuln.”
5Ninefa aanib nan tii naadii Uwumbɔr aah di tibɔr ti tuk bi na pu, le ki cha unii mɔk lul bumɔb; le binib mɔmɔk, bi ye biwankpadam ni bigiim na mɔmɔk nan peen tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na ki mɔk ke bi kpeln baabimbin la.
6Ninefa aabɔr aah ŋun tibɔr ngbaan na, le u fii libɔrjal pu, ki chuu peer waanaan aawanpeenkaan, le ki di tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na peen, le ki kal nfatan ponn ni. 7U nan moon tuk Ninefa aatiŋ aanib ke: “Tibɔr timina nyan ni ubɔr ni waaninkpiib chee la: Ubaa taa ji nibaa, binib mɔmɔk, ni inaa, ni ipiih taa ji nibaa ki taa nyu nibaa mu. 8Binib mɔmɔk peen tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na ki di kina aawanpeenkaan paan tiwakor mu pu. Unii mɔk mee Uwumbɔr ni linimaln, ki di cha mbiin ni titunwanbir aabimbin. 9Nibaakan, Uwumbɔr ga kpeln waalandak aan waaŋuul ga sɔŋ, le ti taa kpo.”
10Uwumbɔr nan kan baah ŋa pu na; u nan kan ke bi di cha baabiin aabimbin, kina pu le u kpeln waalandak kaa ki daa bitafal ke waah ba ga daa pu na.

english_text:
Jonah Gets Angry with the Lord
1Jonah was really upset and angry. 2 So he prayed:
Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
3 Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
4The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
5Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
6The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine, 7but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up. 8During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
9But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?”
“Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
10But the Lord said:
You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next. 11In that city of Nineveh there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
translation_text:
Jona aah gee liŋuul pu na, ni Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln
1Jona aasui nan bii kina ngbaan pu, le liŋuul chuu u sakpen. 2Le u mee Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, maah nan laa bi linampal na, m nan len ke kina le aa ga ŋa. Kina pu le m nan pɔɔn mbaa ke m san mala ki buen Speenn aatiŋ ni. M nyi ke aa ye Uwumbɔr u gee binib ki san bi kinimbaak na la, aa kpa limɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki kpa tiŋann n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki ŋmaa kpelni saalandak kaa dar binib aatafal. 3Uwumbɔr, cha m kpo. M yaa ba tee kpo kan, ni ba soor ni ke m li kpa limɔfal.”
4Le Uwumbɔr nan gar u ke, “Saah gee liŋuul pu na, ni ŋan aa?”
5Jona nan nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ni, le ki di toŋ liwipuul wɔb ki ti kal nibaa chee. Nima chee le u nan gaa kinambuŋ ki kal kaaboon ni, ki ka kii tiwan ni ga ŋa Ninefa aatiŋ na. 6Le Uwumbɔr cha lipulaajil punn ki jon kinambuŋ ngbaan, ki biin ki pu, ki tii Jona mboon, aan ki sɔŋ uwon. Jona aasui nan piir lipulaajil ngbaan pu sakpen. 7Tɔ, kitaak ki ga woln na aachakpinaanyeek ni, le Uwumbɔr cha likpaambil libaa di lipulaajil ngbaan aafar ŋman, le li kpo. 8Nwiin aah puu na, le Uwumbɔr cha liwipuul wɔb aabuln li ton na dan, le ki nan see Jona aayil, le u ti ban u fik. Le u mee Uwumbɔr ke u ba kpo. U nan bui ke, “M yaa ba tee kpo kan, ni ba soor ni ke m li kpa limɔfal.”
9Le Uwumbɔr nan ki bui u ke, “Saah gee liŋuul lipulaajil ngbaan aakun pu na, ni ŋan aa?”
Le Jona gar ke, “Ni ŋan ke m gee liŋuul. M kpa liŋuul li ga ŋmaa ku mi na.”
10Uwumbɔr nan ki bui u ke, “Kinyeek kibaa ponn ni le lipulaajil ngbaan punn ki muun, le ki ki kpo kinyeek ki paa na; saa ŋa nibaa tii li, naa ti ki ye sin le cha li punn ki muun, le laah kpo na, aasui bii li pu. 11Tɔ, aa dak ke kinye aan m ga san kitisakpeŋ Ninefa aanib kinimbaak? Binib bi ki ponn ni, ki jer ŋichur nkub ni moninko, kaa ŋmaa yakr ni ŋan na ni ni kaa ŋan na, le tiwakor pam mu bi.”

english_text:
1 I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah.
Judgment on Samaria
2Listen, all of you!
Earth and everything on it,
pay close attention.
The Lord God accuses you
from his holy temple.
3And he will come down
to crush underfoot
every pagan altar.
4Mountains will melt
beneath his feet
like wax beside a fire.
Valleys will vanish like water
rushing down a ravine.
5This will happen because of
the terrible sins of Israel,
the descendants of Jacob.
Samaria has led Israel to sin,
and pagan altars at Jerusalem
have made Judah sin.
6So the Lord will leave Samaria
in ruins—
merely an empty field
where vineyards are planted.
He will scatter its stones
and destroy its foundations.
7Samaria's idols will be smashed,
and the wages
of temple prostitutes
will be destroyed by fire.
Silver and gold from those idols
will then be used by foreigners
as payment for prostitutes.
Judah Is Doomed
8Because of this tragedy,
I go barefoot and naked.
My crying and weeping
sound like howling wolves
or ostriches.
9The nation is fatally wounded.
Judah is doomed.
Jerusalem will fall.
10Don't tell it in Gath!
Don't even cry.
Instead, roll in the dust
at Beth-Leaphrah.
11Depart naked and ashamed,
you people of Shaphir.
The town of Bethezel mourns
because no one from Zaanan
went out to help.
12Everyone in Maroth
hoped for the best,
but the Lord sent disaster
down on Jerusalem.
13Get the war chariots ready,
you people of Lachish.
You led Jerusalem into sin,
just as Israel did.
14Now you will have to give
a going-away gift
to Moresheth.
Israel's kings will discover
that they cannot trust
the town of Achzib.
15People of Mareshah,
the Lord will send someone
to capture your town.
Then Israel's glorious king
will be forced to hide
in Adullam Cave.
16Judah, shave your head
as bald as a vulture
and start mourning.
Your precious children
will be dragged off
to a foreign country.
translation_text:
1N‑yoonn mu bibɔrb bitaa bimina nan jin nnaan Juda aatiŋ pu ki paan paan tɔb pu na, le Uwumbɔr nan di tibɔr timina tuk waabɔnabr Maika, u ye Moresef aatiŋ ni aanii na. Bibɔrb ngbaan sɔ: Jotam le nan puen jin nnaan, le Ahas paan u pu, le Hesekia nan gbeln puwɔb. Uwumbɔr nan kpiir Samaria ni Jerusalem aatim aabɔr tee mɔmɔk le tuk Maika.
Samaria ni Jerusalem aatim aakpolahn
2Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk, ŋun tibɔr tee man,
binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ kee pu na, li pel man tibɔr tee.
Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔndaan ga len ibamɔn, le ki galn nimi.
Li pel man. U bi waapaacham aadichal ni le ki len ni.
3Uwumbɔr ga nya ni waabuul li bi chain na ni le ki dan;
u ga sunn ni ki nan chuun ŋijoo paab.
4Le ŋijoo ngbaan ga donn u taab
ke tisikakpiin aah donni mmii ni pu na;
ŋi ga puu ti lir tifatann ponn ni
ke nnyun aah puu sunni ligongoln pu pu na.
5Israel aanib aah tun titunwanbir ki yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na le ga cha nimina mɔmɔk ŋa kina. Ŋma aan bi ga galn Israel yaab aah yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb pu na pu? Ni ye Israel aatiyil Samaria la. Ŋma bi Juda aatiŋ ni ki dii ŋiwaa? Ni ye Jerusalem aatiŋ la. 6Kina pu le Uwumbɔr len ke, “M ga cha Samaria kpaln litakpakpokl le kipɔɔk ni, nin chee bi ga ko ndaan aasubil aasui aasar na. M ga ber kaagon lii, ki faa kaabir ti mee kifataŋ ni. 7Kaawaa ŋi bi gee sakpen na ga wii yɔk yɔk, le baawaadir ni aapiidagoob aawangol wu mmii ni, le kaawaa mɔmɔk ga kpaln litapuln li bi fii cha li na. Samaria yaab nan ban nimina mɔmɔk ke bi pɔr la, le baadim ga yoor ŋi mɔmɔk buen nibaa wɔb ki ti li pa bipiidagoob biken.”
8Le Maika bui ke, “Nimina pu le m ga wii, ki gaa ikpolahn. M ga chuun ŋŋmeen kaan taŋ ŋinaatak, ki mɔk maapombiin aah bi pu na. M ga gbei ke ikakal na, ki wii ke taataa na. 9Samaria yaab aabuun aan yann, le Juda yaab mu ga kan kina aaween dandana; libiil fuu ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ni nin chee maanib koo na aabisamɔi ibaa ni.”
Bidim aah duun ni Jerusalem aatiŋ pu na
10Taa bui man timi aadim bi bi Gaf aatiŋ ni na baah nyaŋ timi pu na; taa cha bi kan naah wii pu na man. Bef Leafra aanib, biln titan ni man ki mɔk nimi aapombiin. 11Safir aatiŋ aanib, di inimɔɔn ki chuun niŋmeen man, nimi aadim aah di nimi buen kitiyayaŋ ni man. Binib bi koo Saanann aatiŋ ni na aa kaa ke bi nya ni baatiŋ ponn ni. Ni yaa nan ŋun Bef Esel aatiŋ aanib bi wii kan, ni bee ke lifuur aa bi nima. 12Marof aatiŋ aanib ka jek ki kii lifuur; ba pu? Uwumbɔr di tibɔbir ŋɔŋ ni Jerusalem aatiŋ pu a. 13Lakis aatiŋ aanib, di itaan aatɔroku tiib tul itaan pu man. Ni mu tun Israel yaab aatunwanbir, le ki cha Jerusalem yaab tun titunwanbir. 14Tɔ, Juda aanib, chɔi Moresef Gaf aatiŋ aanib man. Israel aabɔrb aan kan nterm Aksib aatiŋ ni.
15Uwumbɔr ga di Maresa aatiŋ aanib tii udin u ga gaa baatiŋ na. Israel aayidam bi kpa kipak na ga buen ti bɔr Adulam aatakpaluŋ ni. 16Juda aanib, kuu nimi aayikpir man ki li wii naah gee nimi aabim bi na pu. Kuu ŋiyikun ke nangba tiib na man, ba pu? bi ga di nimi aabim buen kitiyayaŋ ni ki cha nimi.

english_text:
Punishment for Those Who Abuse Their Power
1Doomed! You're doomed!
At night you lie in bed,
making evil plans.
And when morning comes,
you do what you've planned
because you have the power.
2You grab any field or house
that you want;
you cheat families
out of homes and land.
3But here is what the Lord says:
“I am planning trouble for you.
Your necks will be caught
in a noose,
and you will be disgraced
in this time of disaster.”
4When that happens,
this sorrowful song
will be sung about you:
“Ruined! Completely ruined!
The Lord has taken our land
and given it to traitors.”
5And so you will never again
own property
among the Lord's people.
6“Enough of your preaching!”
That's what you tell me.
“We won't be disgraced,
so stop preaching!”
7Descendants of Jacob,
is it right for you to claim
that the Lord did what he did
because he was angry?
Doesn't he always bless
those who do right?
8My people, you have turned against
one another!
You have even stolen
clothes right off the backs
of innocent neighbors
who pass by in peace.
9You take over lovely homes
that belong to the women
of my nation.
Then you cheat their children
out of the inheritance
that comes from the Lord.
10Get out of here, you crooks!
You'll find no rest here.
You're not fit to belong
to the Lord's people,
and you will be destroyed.
11The only prophet you want
is a liar who will say,
“Drink and get drunk!”
A Promise of Hope
12I, the Lord, promise
to bring together
the people of Israel
who have survived.
I will gather them,
just as a shepherd
brings sheep together,
and there will be many.
13I will break down the gate
and lead them out—
then I will be their king.
translation_text:
Binib bi muk bigiim na aatafadaan
1Tibɔbir bi binib bi dɔ dak titunwanbir pu kinyeek na pu. Kitaak yaa woln, aan bi kan nsan siib na, le bi ŋa titunwanbir ti bi kpokl na. 2Bi yaa ban ikpaakon kan, bi gaal i mpɔɔn la; bi yaa ban ŋidichal kan, bi gaal ŋi mpɔɔn la. Ubaa aadichal bee waawangol aa nyan tibɔr ni.
3Kina pu le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M bi dakl ke m joo ni tibɔbir nan lii ni pu la, le naan ŋmaa nya ti ponn ni. Ni ga kan ke ni bi tibɔr ni la, le naan ki chuun kigaak aasachuln. 4N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, binib ga di nimi aabɔr le di ŋa tibɔbir aaseeraa, le ki ga gaa nnandalahn mue, naah kan pu na pu:
Ti doo a. Uwumbɔr chuu gaa timi aatiŋ ti chee,
ki di tii binib bi chur timi tinaagbiir na.”
5Kina pu na, n‑yoonn yaa nan fuu ni ke bi di kitiŋ ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr aanib kan, ni ponn ni ubaa aan ti li kpa nibaa ki ponn ni.
6Binib mooni m pu ki len ke, “Taa mooni ti chee. Taa mooni tima ngbaan mɔmɔk man. Uwumbɔr aan jinn timi inimɔɔn. 7Nimi Israel yaab len ke Uwumbɔr aa ki kpa limɔr la aa? U ga sil ŋa tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk aa? Waa len binib bi ŋani ni ŋan na chee ki san bi kinimbaak aa?”
8Le Uwumbɔr ga gar ke, “Ni tak maanib ke bidim na la. Bijab nyan ni butɔb ni, ki dak ke baah fuu ni linampal na bi ŋmar la, le ni bi nima chee ke ni nan su baabɔkur. 9Ni jenn nyani maanib aapuutiib ŋidichal ŋi ponn ni bi gee na, le ki gaa baabim chee maanyoor. 10Fii ki li cha man; lifuur libaa aa ki bi do. Nimi aatunwanbir kuln do doo a.
11“Binib bee ban bibɔnabr bi chuun ŋmanni ki geei inyamɔn, ki len ke, ‘M nabr ke ni ga gur ndaan la.’
12“Le m ga kuun ni nimi Israel aanib bi gur na nan kpaan. M ga kuun ni nimi ke ipiih aah kpaan chaa koo yaabool ponn ni pu na la. Nimi aatiŋ ga ki gbiin binib ke kipihkpaamook ki ponn ni gbii ipiih na la.”
13Uwumbɔr le ga ki piir nsan tii bi aan ki di bi nya ni tinaagbiir kitiyayaŋ ni. Bi ga gaa bibaa lii ki dii ibisamɔi nya. Baabɔr, Uwumbɔr ubaa, le ga cheen bi nya ni.

english_text:
Evil Rulers and Lying Prophets
1Listen to me,
you rulers of Israel!
You know right from wrong,
2but you prefer to do evil
instead of what is right.
You skin my people alive.
You strip off their flesh,
3break their bones,
cook it all in a pot,
and gulp it down.
4Someday you will beg the Lord
to help you,
but he will turn away
because of your sins.
5You lying prophets promise
security for anyone
who gives you food,
but disaster for anyone
who refuses to feed you.
Here is what the Lord says
to you prophets:
6“You will live in the dark,
far from the sight of the sun,
with no message from me.
7You prophets and fortunetellers
will all be disgraced,
with no message from me.”
8But the Lord has filled me
with power and his Spirit.
I have been given the courage
to speak about justice
and to tell you people of Israel
that you have sinned.
9So listen to my message,
you rulers of Israel!
You hate justice
and twist the truth.
10You make cruelty and murder
a way of life in Jerusalem.
11You leaders accept bribes
for dishonest decisions.
You priests and prophets
teach and preach,
but only for money.
Then you say,
“The Lord is on our side.
No harm will come to us.”
12 And so, because of you,
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple now stands.
translation_text:
Maika aah len tibɔbir lii Israel aayidam pu pu na
1Nimi bi ye Israel yaab aajojoob na, li pel man. Nimi aatuln le ba ye ke ni li dii ibamɔn, 2le ni nan tiwan ni ŋan na, ki tee gee titunwanbir. Maanib aa kee kpoi le ni sun baagban ki dar lui baanann baakpab pu. 3Ni ŋmɔ maanib la. Ni lui nyani baagban, le ki kool baakpab, ki chɔi chɔi bi ke baah ban bi di tinann ti ŋaa na. 4N‑yoonn choo le ni ga nan wii ban Uwumbɔr chee nterm, le waan gar nimi. Waan ŋun nimi aameel; ba pu? ni tun titunwanbir la.
5Baabɔnabr bi gaal tipar na le ŋmann maanib ke nsuudoon bi bi chee, le ki faani binib bi kaa pa bi na ke butɔb choo. Uwumbɔr bui bibɔnabr ngbaan ke, 6“Bibɔnabr, nimi aawiin bi door la; nwiin ga lir buyoonn naa kee gor na. Naah di maanib yenn pu na, le ni ga ŋa kina, naan ki kan tibɔkpiirkaan ti ni ga di nabr na, kaan ki ŋmaa bui ke tiwan nibaa ga ŋa, aan tiwan ngbaan sil ŋa kina.” 7Binib bi nyi n‑yoonn mu choo na aabɔr ki nabr na ga ji inimɔɔn, baah kaan ki li nyi nibaa pu na pu. Uwumbɔr aah kaan gar bi pu na pu le bi ga kpaln binimɔɔnib.
8Tɔ, mma kan, Uwumbɔr le joo Waafuur Nyaan ni waapɔɔn gbiini mi, le ki tii mi ibamɔn aalan, ni ntaakpapɔɔn mu m ga ŋmaa di bui Israel yaab baatunwanbir aah ye pu na. 9Nimi Israel aanib aajojoob, li pel man, nimi bi kaa gee ibamɔn ki kpelni tiwan ni ŋan na ŋani taani na. 10Ni bi maa Uwumbɔr aatiŋ Jerusalem nnikum ni mbiin pu la. 11Igaŋgaŋlik pu le kitiŋ ngbaan aajojoob joo ki, le bitotoorb tuk binib Uwumbɔr Aakaal ki gaal tipar, le bibɔnabr mu kpiir Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ŋimombil pu, le bi mɔmɔk len ke Uwumbɔr bi ti chee. Bi len le ke, “Tibɔbir tibaa aan dan ti chee. Uwumbɔr bi ti chee.”
12Kina pu na, nimi pu le bidim ga kpar Sionn ke lisikpel na, le Jerusalem kpaln tibir aatapuln, le Uwumbɔr Aadichal aagongoln kpaln kichook.

english_text:
Peace and Prosperity
1In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills,
and every nation
will rush to it.
2People of many nations
will come and say,
“Let's go up to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
3 He will settle arguments
between distant
and powerful nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never again make war
or attack one another.
4 Everyone will find rest
beneath their own fig trees
or grape vines,
and they will live in peace.
This is a solemn promise
of the Lord All-Powerful.
5Others may follow their gods,
but we will always follow
the Lord our God.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
6The Lord said:
At that time
I will gather my people—
the lame and the outcasts,
and all others into whose lives
I have brought sorrow.
7Then the lame and the outcasts
will belong to my people
and become a strong nation.
I, the Lord, will rule them
from Mount Zion forever.
8Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
guardian of my people,
you will rule again.
9Jerusalem, why are you crying?
Don't you have a king?
Have your advisors gone?
Are you suffering
like a woman in childbirth?
10Keep on groaning with pain,
you people of Jerusalem!
If you escape from your city
to the countryside,
you will still be taken
as prisoners to Babylonia.
But later I will rescue you
from your enemies.
11Zion, because of your sins
you are surrounded
by many nations who say,
“We can hardly wait
to see you disgraced.”
12But they don't know
that I, the Lord,
have gathered them here
to grind them like grain.
13Smash them to pieces, Zion!
I'll let you be like a bull
with iron horns
and bronze hoofs.
Crush those nations
and bring their wealth to me,
the Lord of the earth.
translation_text:
Nsuudoon mu kaa kpa ndoon na
(Aisaya 2.2-4)
1N‑yoonn choo, le lijool li pu Uwumbɔr Aadichal si na
ga li ye lijool li paa jer ŋijoo mɔmɔk na,
li ga chaar ŋigongon mɔmɔk pu.
Le ŋitimbol pam ga dan li chee;
2le ŋaanib ga bui ke,
“Cha ti jon Uwumbɔr aajool
ki buen Israel yaab Aawumbɔr Aadichal ni;
ba pu? u ga mɔk timi waah ban ti ŋa pu na,
le ti ga chuun waah lee isan i na pu.
Uwumbɔr aamɔkm nyan ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ni la;
Sionn pu le u len ni waanib chee tibɔr.”
3U ga toor ŋitimbol pam aabɔr;
ki toor ŋitimbokpaan ŋi bi duun u na, ni ŋi bi ni daa na aabɔr.
Bi ga di baajaak aajum mɔɔ ŋikuu
ki di baakpaatunn mɔɔ gɔrk tiib.
Ŋitimbol aan ki to tɔb butɔb,
kaan ki gor bibaa kiir butɔb daalbaadaal.
4Unii mɔmɔk ga li bi nsuudoon ni
ubaa aadaan aasubil, ni ŋisubil ŋiken aasui aasar ni,
le ubaa aan faan u nima.
Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le puu kina.
5Litimbol mɔk dooni ki keei laawaal aamɔb la, le ti mɔmɔk ga nan doon ki kii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.
Israel yaab ga nya tinaagbiir kitiyayaŋ ni ki gir ni
6Uwumbɔr bui ke, “N‑yoonn choo, le m ga kuun ni binib bi m daa bitafal, aan bi jin falaa tinaagbiir ni kitiyayaŋ ni na nan kpaan. 7Binib bi gur na wɔb le ki daa bido, le m ga tii bi mpɔɔn, le bi ga kpaln litimbol kpaan. M ga li bi Sionn Aajool paab le ki joo bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”
8Le sin, Jerusalem aatiŋ ni, nin chee Uwumbɔr lik waanib pu ke upihdaan na, ga ki gir kpaln nnaan mu aa nan yeh na aatiyil. 9Ba ŋa aa wii mpɔɔn pu sakpen kina? Ba ŋa aa ji falaa ke upii u imalween joo u na? Saah kaa kpa ubɔr, aan saasusurb mu kpoi na pu le aa wii ii? 10Jerusalem aatiŋ aanib, li mur fenni ki ker idun ke upii u imalween joo u na, ba pu? ni ga nya kitiŋ ponn ni ki ti li koo timoor ni. Ni ga buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni; le Uwumbɔr ga ti tee gaa nimi, nimi aadim chee lii nima. 11Ŋitimbol pam le kuun ni ke ŋi nan tak nimi. Bi bui ke, “Ti ga bii Jerusalem aatiŋ doo. Ti ga kan ke kitiŋ ngbaan bii doo.” 12Tɔ, ŋitimbol ngbaan mu aa tee nyi Uwumbɔr aalandak. Baa nyi ke bi kuun ni tɔb ke Uwumbɔr nan daa bitafal, ke baah kuuni ŋikalmaan bilni pu ke bi poi ŋi na la.
13Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Jerusalem aanib, li cha ti daa nimi aadim aatafal man. M ga cha ni li pɔɔ ke unaaja u kpa tikur aayiin ni tikumann aataabuseen na. Ni ga ber ŋitimbol pam, le baah di mpɔɔn kan liwangol li na, ni ga joo ni li nan tii min, u ye dulnyaa mɔmɔk Aawumbɔr na.”

english_text:
A Promised Ruler
1Jerusalem, enemy troops
have surrounded you;
they have struck Israel's ruler
in the face with a stick.
2 Bethlehem Ephrath,
you are one of the smallest towns
in the nation of Judah.
But the Lord will choose
one of your people
to rule the nation—
someone whose family
goes back to ancient times.
3The Lord will abandon Israel
only until this ruler is born,
and the rest of his family
returns to Israel.
4Like a shepherd
taking care of his sheep,
this ruler will lead
and care for his people
by the power and glorious name
of the Lord his God.
His people will live securely,
and the whole earth will know
his true greatness,
5because he will bring peace.
Assyria Will Be Defeated
Let Assyria attack our country
and our palaces.
We will counterattack,
led by a number of rulers
6 whose strong army will defeat
the nation of Assyria.
Yes, our leaders will rescue us,
if those Assyrians
dare to invade our land.
The Survivors Will Be Safe
7A few of Jacob's descendants
survived and are scattered
among the nations.
But the Lord will let them
cover the earth like dew and rain
that refreshes the soil.
8At present they are scattered,
but later they will attack,
as though they were fierce lions
pouncing on sheep.
Their enemies will be torn
to shreds,
with no one to save them;
9they will be helpless,
completely destroyed.
Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
10The Lord said:
At that time I will wipe out
your cavalry and chariots,
11as well as your cities
and your fortresses.
12I will stop you
from telling fortunes
and practicing witchcraft.
13You will no longer worship
the idols or stone images
you have made—
I will destroy them,
14together with the sacred poles
and even your towns.
15I will become furious
and take revenge on the nations
that refuse to obey me.
translation_text:
1Jerusalem aanib, kuun nimi aajab man. Bi loon timi a. Bi bi tak Israel aayidaan la.
Uwumbɔr puu ke ujojoor ga nya ni Betlehem aatiŋ ni
2Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Betlehem Efrata, aa ye kitiwaatiir kibaa le Juda aatiŋ pu, le sin ponn ni le m ga nyan ni ujojoor u ga li joo Israel aanib na, u ga nya ni mmaal mu ye n‑yaayoonn na aamaal ponn ni la.”
3Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr ga di waanib tii baadim, kaan ki gar bi ki ti saa buyoonn upii u ban u maa na maa waabijabo. Le Israel yaab bi bi biwɔwɔm aatiŋ ni na, ni bi bi Israel aatiŋ ni na ga ki kpaan tɔb chee. 4Ujojoor ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, u ga di mpɔɔn sakpiin mu nyan ni Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ubaa chee na le di joo waanib. Waanib ga li bi lifuur ni la; ba pu? kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aanib ga li nyi waapɔɔn bɔr, 5le u ga joo ni nsuudoon.
Gaalii ni ntafadaan
Asiria yaab yaa nan koo ni timi aatiŋ ni ki nyaŋ binib bi kii timi na kan, le ti ga di timi aayidam bi pɔɔ sakpen na tun aan bi ni bima ti jan. 6Buyoonn bi koo ni timi aapepel ni na, le bi ga di tijawan ki nyaŋ Nimrod aatiŋ Asiria, le ki gaa timi Asiria yaab chee lii.
7Israel aanib bi ŋmar na ga li naahn limaln li Uwumbɔr tun ni li na le ŋitimbol pam chee, ki naahn utaal u pui tijikaar pu na. Bi ga li bi Uwumbɔr pu la, naan li ye unibɔn pu. 8Binib bi gur ki ŋmal ŋitimbol ŋiken ni na ga li bi ke uchinn u bi ban tijikaar kichook ni, bee kipihkpaamook ni na la: u ga koo ipiih ni, le ki chur i, le ki daa par par i, le yaan kan nterm nibaa chee. 9Israel yaab ga nyaŋ baadim le ki ku doo bi mɔmɔk.
10Uwumbɔr bui ke, “N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, m ga gaa nimi aataan ni chee, le ki bii nimi aataan aatɔroku tiib. 11M ga bii nimi aatim mɔmɔk, le ki ber naah maa tiwan ni mɔmɔk kiir nibaa na. 12M ga bii nimi aanyɔk i ni joo tun nimi aatun na, ki cha ni taa ki li kpa bibɔɔb. 13M ga bii nimi aawaa, ni nimi aatakpal ŋi ni dooni na; naan ki doon tiwan ni, ni di nibaa aaŋaal naan ni na. 14M ga ber liwaapii Asera aanann ti ni maa ti nimi aatiŋ pu na, ki bii nimi aatim. 15Le maaŋuul ponn ni m ga teen ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk yii maamɔb na.”

english_text:
The Lord's Challenge to His People
1The Lord said to his people:
Come and present your case
to the hills and mountains.
2Israel, I am bringing charges
against you—
I call upon the mountains
and the earth's firm foundation
to be my witnesses.
3My people, have I wronged you
in any way at all?
Please tell me.
4 I rescued you from Egypt,
where you were slaves.
I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
to be your leaders.
5 Don't forget the evil plans
of King Balak of Moab
or what Balaam son of Beor
said to him.
Remember how I, the Lord,
saved you many times
on your way from Acacia
to Gilgal.
True Obedience
6What offering should I bring
when I bow down to worship
the Lord God Most High?
Should I try to please him
by sacrificing
calves a year old?
7Will thousands of sheep
or rivers of olive oil
make God satisfied with me?
Should I sacrifice to the Lord
my first-born child as payment
for my terrible sins?
8The Lord God has told us
what is right
and what he demands:
“See that justice is done,
let mercy be your first concern,
and humbly obey your God.”
Cheating and Violence
9I am the Lord,
and you are wise to respect
my power to punish.
So listen to my message
for the city of Jerusalem:
10You store up stolen treasures
and use dishonest scales.
11But I, the Lord, will punish you
for cheating with weights
and with measures.
12You rich people are violent,
and everyone tells lies.
13Because of your sins,
I will wound you and leave you
ruined and defenseless.
14You will eat,
but still be hungry;
you will store up goods,
but lose everything—
I, the Lord, will let it all
be captured in war.
15You won't harvest what you plant
or use the oil
from your olive trees
or drink the wine
from grapes you grow.
16 Jerusalem, this will happen
because you followed
the sinful example
of kings Omri and Ahab.
Now I will destroy you
and your property.
Then the people of every nation
will make fun and insult you.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah joo tibɔr ti Israel aanib pu na
1Li pel man Uwumbɔr aah joo tibɔr ti Israel aanib pu na. Uwumbɔr, fii sil ki cha bi ŋun saah joo tibɔr ti Israel aanib pu na; cha ŋijoo ni ŋigongon ŋun saah joo pu aa len na.
2Nimi ŋijoo, nimi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na aatinyik, li pel Uwumbɔr aabɔr man. Uwumbɔr ni waanib le kpa tibɔr. U ban ke u joo ni ngalm Israel aanib pu la.
3Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Maanib, m ŋa nimi ba? Kinye pu aan m ye lituln ki tii nimi? Gar mi man. 4M nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni; m nyan ni nimi tinaagbiir ni; m nan tun Moses, ni Aaronn, ni Miriam ke bi nan loln ni pu nsan. 5Maanib, teer man Moab aabɔr Balak aah nan kpokl ke u ŋa nimi pu na, ki teer Beor aajapɔɔn Balaam aah nan gar u pu na. Teer man maah nan cha ni puur Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl na, buyoonn ni nan nyan ni Sitim aakakaa chee ki cha Gilgal aatiŋ ni na. Teer man tiwan nimina mɔmɔk ki bee maah nan ŋa pu ke m gaa nimi lii na.”
Uwumbɔr aah ban pu na
6Buyoonn m dan ke m nan doon Uwumbɔr u ye paacham Aadindaan na kan, m ga joo ba nan tii u? M ga joo ni inaabi i ŋan sakpen na le nan see mmii ni tii u uu? 7M yaa joo ni ipiih ŋichur ŋichur, bee olif aakpan mu kaan doo na kan, ni ga piir Uwumbɔr aasui ii? M ga di maajan aabijabo le toor kitork tii u maatunwanbir pu uu? 8Aayii. Uwumbɔr bui timi tiwan ni ŋan na. Waah ban tiwan ni ti chee na sɔ: ke ti ŋa tiwan ni tok ki ŋan na, ki li kpa ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki li bi suuna timi Aawumbɔr chee.
9Ni ye nlan aawan le ke ti li san Uwumbɔr. U yin kitiŋ ngbaan ni aanib ke, “Li pel man, nimi bi kuun kitiŋ ngbaan ni na. 10Titunwanbirdam aadichal ni gbii liwangol li bi di titunwanbir kan na la. Baah joo tiwan ni ŋaŋni baawan na aa ye nibamɔnn. Maa gee kina kpala. 11M ga ŋa kinye aan ki di cha pinn binib bi joo inyamɔn aawan ŋaŋni tiwan na? 12Nimi aawankpadam ji bigiim pem pem la, le ni mɔmɔk ye binyamɔndam. 13Kina pu na, m puun gor ke m bii doo nimi, nimi aatunwanbir pu. 14Ni ga ji, le ki mu aan bab; mbamɔn, nkon ga li joo nimi. Ni ga kuun liwangol di bil, le ki mu aan ŋmaa li joo li; naah ga li kpa tiwan nimɔk na, m ga bii kina aawan butɔb ponn ni. 15Ni ga bu njikaabim, ki mu aan chee tijikaar. Ni ga nyan nkpan olif aasubil ni, ki mu aan ŋmaa di mu ŋa nibaa. Ni ga ŋaa ndaan, ki mu aan nyu mu. 16Naah dii Ubɔr Omri aajapɔɔn Ubɔr Ahab aatunwanbir aasan na pu, le kina ga ŋa. Ni beenin joo baakaal la, kina pu le m ga bii doo nimi, le unii mɔk ga lik nimi fam. Binib bi bi dulnyaa wee ni na ga lik seen nimi.”

english_text:
Israel Is Corrupt
1I feel so empty inside—
like someone starving
for grapes or figs,
after the vines and trees
have all been picked clean.
2No one is loyal to God;
no one does right.
Everyone is brutal
and eager to deceive
everyone else.
3People cooperate to commit crime.
Judges and leaders demand bribes,
and rulers cheat in court.
4The most honest of them
is worse than a thorn patch.
Your doom has come!
Lookouts sound the warning,
and everyone panics.
5Don't trust anyone,
not even your best friend,
and be careful what you say
to the one you love.
6 Sons refuse to respect
their own fathers,
daughters rebel against
their own mothers,
and daughters-in-law despise
their mothers-in-law.
Your family is now your enemy.
7But I trust the Lord God
to save me,
and I will wait for him
to answer my prayer.
The Nation Turns to God
8My enemies, don't be glad
because of my troubles!
I may have fallen,
but I will get up;
I may be sitting in the dark,
but the Lord is my light.
9I have sinned against the Lord.
And so I must endure his anger,
until he comes to my defense.
But I know that I will see him
making things right for me
and leading me to the light.
10You, my enemies, said,
“The Lord God is helpless.”
Now each of you
will be disgraced
and put to shame.
I will see you trampled
like mud in the street.
A Bright Future
11Towns of Judah, the day is coming
when your walls will be rebuilt,
and your boundaries enlarged.
12People will flock to you
from Assyria and Egypt,
from Babylonia
and everywhere else.
13Those nations will suffer disaster
because of what they did.
Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
14Lead your people, Lord!
Come and be our shepherd.
Grasslands surround us,
but we live in a forest.
So lead us to Bashan and Gilead,
and let us find pasture
as we did long ago.
15I, the Lord, will work miracles
just as I did when I led you
out of Egypt.
16Nations will see this
and be ashamed because
of their helpless armies.
They will be in shock,
unable to speak or hear,
17because of their fear of me,
your Lord and God.
Then they will come trembling,
crawling out of their fortresses
like insects or snakes,
lapping up the dust.
No One Is Like God
The people said:
18Our God, no one is like you.
We are all that is left
of your chosen people,
and you freely forgive
our sin and guilt.
You don't stay angry forever;
you're glad to have pity
19and pleased to be merciful.
You will trample on our sins
and throw them in the sea.
20You will keep your word
and be faithful to Jacob
and to Abraham,
as you promised our ancestors
many years ago.
translation_text:
Israel yaab aaninsuŋ aabimbin
1Maa kpa nsuupiin. M naahn uja u nkon joo u aan lisubil mu aa gur waasui pu, aan ndaan aasubil mu aa bi ŋaasui pu na la. Bi ker ŋisubil mɔmɔɔn ngbaan mɔmɔk a. 2Unii ubaa aa gur kitiŋ ngbaan pu ki bi chob, ubaa mu aa bi ki kii tii Uwumbɔr. Binib mɔmɔk ka kii ke bi ku binib biken la. Unii mɔmɔk dɔ ban udo yoo le u ku. 3Bi mɔmɔk ye binib bi nyi titunwanbir aatuln na la. Ŋitun aaninkpiib, ni bibɔlem ban igaŋgaŋlik la. Binib bi kpa mpɔɔn na len baah ban pu na la, le bi kpaani ki kpokl. 4Hali binib bi ŋan ki bi chob na aa kpa tinyoor tibaa ke timoor aah bi pu na la.
N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ga di daa binib ngbaan aatafal, ke waah nan cha waabɔnabtiib sak bi pu na fuu ni a. Dandana wee, baalan ŋmal a. 5Taa tii aajɔ, bee aa ni unii u koo gbɔk tɔb na naadii. Li nyi saah len pu na, hali aapuu mu chee kan, li nyi. 6N‑yoonn mumina ponn ni le mbijabim yin bitetiib bijɔrb, le mpiibim aa keei binatiib aamɔi; le bipiisapɔm ni bichapiitiib jaa; le unii aadim ye udo lichiln ni aanib.
7Le mma ga li lik Uwumbɔr pu; m ga ji limɔr ki li kii Uwumbɔr u ga gaa mi lii na. Maawumbɔr ga ŋun maayim.
Uwumbɔr ga gaa timi lii
8Timi aadim aa kpa nsan ke bi li kpa mpopiin timi aafalaa pu. Ti lir la, le ki mu tee ga ki fii. Ti bi mbɔmbɔɔn ni le dandana, le Uwumbɔr ga tii timi nwiihn. 9Ti tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir, kina pu na, ni ŋan ke ti ji falaa waaŋuul pu. Nee aapuwɔb na u ga sil tipuwɔb ki toor taani u bi ŋa timi na. U ga nyan ni timi dan nwiihn ni; ti ga li bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu u ga gaa timi lii na. 10Timi aadim ga kan nimina, le ki ji inimɔɔn, bidimbaam bi nan ŋani timi yaansara ki bui ke, “Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi la?” na. Ti ga kan binib aah nyaŋ bi pu na, ki taa bi bil kitiŋ ke tikpakpar na.
11Jerusalem aanib, n‑yoonn mu ni ga ki gir maa kitiŋ kee aagon na choo. N‑yoonn ngbaan le nimi aapepel ga moo kpee. 12Nimi aanib ga nya ni ni kookoo ki gir ni, ni chee; bi ga nya ni Asiria aatiŋ, ki bi liwipuul wɔb na ni, ki nya ni Ijipt aatiŋ ki bi liwipuul aaŋangii wɔb na, ki nya ni Yufrates aapepel wɔb, ki nya ni nnyusakpem, ni ŋijoo ŋi bi dandar na ni. 13Tɔ, kitiŋ kee tee ga kpaln nteer ŋmeen, binib bi bi ki pu na aatunwanbir pu.
Uwumbɔr aah san Israel yaab kinimbaak pu na
14Uwumbɔr, li bi saanib bi aa lee na chee ke upihdaan na. Bi yaa, ki bi kipɔɔk ni la, le kitiŋ ki nyuun na bi bi chee. Cha bi buen Basann, ni Gilead aapihkpaamoor ti nyuun na ni, ke baah nan bi n‑yaayoonn na pu na.
15Uwumbɔr, tun lijinjiir aatun tii timi saanib, ke saah nan ŋa pu n‑yoonn mu aa nan nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na. 16Ŋitimbol ga kan nimina le bitaakpab yɔl, le baan ki li kpa mpɔɔn. Bitaakpab aah ga yɔl pu na, le bi ga muib bimɔi ki ŋeeb bitafal mu. 17Bi ga baar kitiŋ titan ni, ke iwaa na la; bi ga nyan ni baadichal ŋi kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk na ni, ki jii ijawaan pu. Ijawaan pu, bi ga fenn ban Tidindaan Uwumbɔr.
18Uwumbɔr, ubaa aa ki bi ke sin na; aa di cha pinn saanib bi ŋmar na aatunwanbir. Saa joo saaŋuul ni yunni, le ki tee gee ke aa mɔk timi ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. 19Aa ga ki san timi kinimbaak lelee. Aa ga taa taa timi aatunwanbir ŋmal titan ni, ki di ti buen nnyusakpem aataab. 20Aa ga mɔk saanib, Abraham ni Jakob aayaabitiib, ke saah bi mbamɔm ki kpa ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, ke saah nan puu tii tiyaajatiib n‑yaayoonn na pu na.

english_text:
1 I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh.
The Fierce Anger of the Lord
2The Lord God demands loyalty.
In his anger, he takes revenge
on his enemies.
3The Lord is powerful,
yet patient;
he makes sure that the guilty
are always punished.
He can be seen in storms
and in whirlwinds;
clouds are the dust from his feet.
4At the Lord's command,
oceans and rivers dry up.
Bashan, Mount Carmel,
and Lebanon wither,
and their flowers fade.
5At the sight of the Lord,
mountains and hills
tremble and melt;
the earth and its people
shudder and shake.
6Who can stand the heat
of his furious anger?
It flashes out like fire
and shatters stones.
The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
7The Lord is good.
He protects those who trust him
in times of trouble.
8But like a roaring flood,
the Lord chases his enemies
into dark places
and destroys them.
9So don't plot against the Lord!
He wipes out his enemies,
and they never revive.
10They are like drunkards
overcome by wine,
or like twisted thornbushes
burning in a fire.
11Assyria, one of your rulers
has made evil plans
against the Lord.
12But the Lord says, “Assyria,
no matter how strong you are,
you will be cut down!
My people Judah,
I have troubled you before,
but I won't do it again.
13I'll snap your chains
and set you free
from the Assyrians.”
14Assyria, this is what else
the Lord says to you:
“Your name will be forgotten.
I will destroy every idol
in your temple,
and I will send you to the grave,
because you are worthless.”
15 Look toward the mountains,
people of Judah!
Here comes a messenger
with good news of peace.
Celebrate your festivals.
Keep your promises to God.
Your evil enemies are destroyed
and will never again
invade your country.
translation_text:
1Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Nahum u nyan ni Elkos aatiŋ ni na aah nan kan Ninefa aatiŋ aabɔr ti na sɔ. Uwumbɔr le nan kpiir ti mɔk u.
Uwumbɔr aah gee Ninefa aatiŋ pu liŋuul pu na
2Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aa kii ke unii doon liwaal libaa;
u dar binib bi kpak u na aatafal.
Waaŋuul ponn ni le u teeni bi baah tun pu na.
3Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aa fiir mala mala,
le u tee kpa mpɔɔn sakpen,
le ki dar binib bi aabɔr aa ŋan na aatafal,
kaa joo cha pinni bi.
Kitaabuŋ fii nin chee Uwumbɔr chuun na la;
utaa aatangbaak le ye ntaalangbam.
4Uma le len nnyusakpem chee, le mu foor.
U cha ŋimɔɔ foor.
Basann aatiŋ aakpaakon kuur la,
Kamel Aajool mann ke titan na la,
le Lebanonn aatiŋ aasupuun gbar lir.
5Ŋijoo jii Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni la;
le ŋigongon donn unimbiin ni.
Kitiŋ yaa kan Uwumbɔr kan, ki deŋni la;
dulnyaa, ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi u pu na aawon gbaa la.
6Uwumbɔr aaŋuul yaa fii kan, ŋma ga ŋmar?
Ŋma ga ŋmar waaŋuusakpeln ni?
U cha waaŋuul puu nyan ni ke mmiigaal na la;
ŋitakpal wur unimbiin ni ki kpaln titan la.
7Uwumbɔr ŋan; waanib yaa bi tibɔr ni kan, u kii bi;
le ki lik binib bi fenn buen u chee ki ban nterm na pu.
8U kuln waadim ke nwam mu san mala mala na la;
u ku binib bi kpak u na la.
9Ba aan ni bi kpokl Uwumbɔr pu? U ga kuln nimi.
Ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak u ki jer nfum mubaa.
10Nimi bidanyurb ga wu mmii ke ikokon i lɔk tɔb ni na,
ni timokuun aah wu pu na la.
11Uja u aasui nan gbii mbiin aalandak na nan nyan ni sin Ninefa aatiŋ ni la, uma le nan kpokl Uwumbɔr pu. 12Uwumbɔr aah bui waanib Israel yaab pu na sɔ: “Hali Asiria yaab aah wiir ki kpa mpɔɔn pu na, bi mɔmɔk ga kuln ki wɔŋ. Maanib, min le nan cha ni jin falaa, tɔ, maan ki ŋa kina. 13Dandana wee ma m ga kuln Asiria yaab aapɔɔn mu bi nan kpa ni pu na, ki kii tikululn ti nan buu nimi na.”
14Uwumbɔr aah siin pu Asiria aatiŋ pu na sɔ: “Baan li kpa yaabitiib bi ga cha baayimbil li beenin bi na. M ga kuln ŋiwaa ŋi bi baawaadir ni na. M bi gbii likaakul bilni Asiria yaab la, naa ŋan ke bi li kpa limɔfal.”
15Lik man, ntuun nyan ni ŋijoo pu ki joo ni tibɔnyaan. U choo u nan moon linyaŋ aabɔr la. Juda aanib, ji nimi aajim man, ki tii Uwumbɔr naah di nisui mɔmɔk puu ke ni ga tii u ni na. Bibiindam aan ki dan nan jenn gaa nimi aatiŋ daalbaadaal. Bi kuln doo kookoo a.

english_text:
Nineveh Will Fall
1Nineveh, someone is coming
to attack and scatter you.
Guard your fortresses!
Watch the road! Be brave!
Prepare for battle!
2Judah and Israel are like trees
with branches broken
by their enemies.
But the Lord is going to restore
their power and glory.
* 3Nineveh, on this day of attack,
your enemies' shields are red;
their uniforms are crimson.
4Their horses prance,
and their armored chariots
dart around like lightning
or flaming torches.
5An officer gives a command.
But his soldiers stumble,
as they hasten to build
a shelter to protect themselves
against rocks thrown down
from the city wall.
6The river gates fly open,
and panic floods the palace.
7Nineveh is disgraced.
The queen is dragged off.
Her servant women mourn;
they moan like doves,
and they beat their breasts
in sorrow.
8Nineveh is like a pond
with leaking water.
Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!”
can be heard everywhere.
But everyone is leaving.
9Enemy soldiers shout,
“The city is full of treasure
and all kinds of wealth.
Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
10Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed!
Her people tremble with fear;
their faces turn pale.
11What happened to this city?
They were safer there
than powerful lions in a den,
with no one to disturb them.
12These are the same lions
that ferociously attacked
their victims,
then dragged away the flesh
to feed their young.
13The Lord All-Powerful
is against you, Nineveh.
God will burn your chariots
and send an army to kill
those young lions of yours.
You will never again
make victims of others
or send messengers to threaten
everyone on this earth.
translation_text:
Ninefa aatiŋ aah kuln pu na
1Ninefa aatiŋ, bi gob si a.
Mpɔɔn mu ga wii si yuk yuk na fuu ni a.
Ban bijab sil saatiŋ aagon paab.
Cha bi kiir nsan ngbaan. Gor ki kiir butɔb.
2Uwumbɔr ban u ki giin Israel aatiŋ aapak ki ki nan kpa, aan kaadim nan gaa kaawangol butɔb ni na tii ki la.
3Bidim aajab joo kijaak aapeln ti man na la,
le ki pee tiwanpeenkaan mamann mu.
Bi bi gor ke bi nan tak la.
Baataan aatɔroku tiib moor ke mmii na la, baataan bi yuk la.
4Itaan aatɔroku tiib san kitiŋ ponn ni ke baah waar le na,
ki san ti nya do ki di nan nya do kitiŋ ngbaan aapaan ni.
Bi moor ke limotaafil aamii na la,
ki moor ni mɔmɔk ke utaal na.
5Bi kuun bijab aayidam;
le baah tur cha mɔb pu na, bi gbeer.
Bidim chii ki buen kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln chee
ki gor baajaak aapeln ke baah ga li joo yur tɔb le na.
6Ibisamɔi i bi limɔɔl wɔb na chuu piir a;
le ijawaan gbiin libɔrdichal ni.
7Bi chuu ubɔrpii a; le waatutum wii ke ŋinanjel na
ki joo biŋaal gbaa bibiŋ mpombiin pu.
8Binib san nyan Ninefa aatiŋ ni ke limɔɔl aah kar kan,
laanyun puu nya pu na la.
Iwiil nya ni ke, “Sil man. Sil man.”
Le ubaa aa fenni upuwɔb ke u lik.
9Gaa tikunabr ngbaan mpɔɔn man.
Gaa salmaa ngbaan mpɔɔn man.
Kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni gbii liwangol la.
10Ninefa aatiŋ bii a, ki ber a, le ki gur dɔ nkuun.
Ijawaan cha binib aapobil donn a;
mpɔɔn doo a, le ŋitaaŋaayil gbaa tɔtɔk,
le ŋinimbil wɔb ŋa yɔl yɔl.
11Tɔ, kitiŋ ki nan bi ke ichinn aabuu na ki bi la chee?
nin chee ichinn aabim ji, aan uchinnja ni uchinnpii nan chaa, aan yaabim bi lifuur ni na, bi la chee?
12Uchinn nan chuu tinann le ki daa par par ti
ki tii upuu ni waabim;
u nan di tinankaab le gbiin waabuu ni.
13Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke, “Saadin ye min la. M ga see saataan aatɔroku tiib mmii. Bi ga ku saajab butɔb ni la, le m ga yoor saah nan gaa tiwan ni biken chee na ki di buen. Ubaa aan ki ŋun saah nan kpa mpɔɔn mu dulnyaa wee ni na pu.”

english_text:
Punishment for Nineveh
The Lord said:
1Doom to the crime capital!
Nineveh, city of murder
and treachery,
2here is your fate—
cracking whips,
churning wheels;
galloping horses,
roaring chariots;
3cavalry attacking,
swords and spears flashing;
soldiers stumbling
over piles of dead bodies.
4You were nothing more
than a prostitute
using your magical charms
and witchcraft
to attract and trap nations.
5But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am now your enemy.
I will pull up your skirt
and let nations and kingdoms
stare at your nakedness.
6I will cover you with garbage,
treat you like trash,
and rub you in the dirt.
7Everyone who sees you
will turn away and shout,
“Nineveh is done for!
Is anyone willing to mourn
or to give her comfort?”
Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
8Nineveh, do you feel safer
than the city of Thebes?
The Nile River
was its wall of defense.
9Thebes trusted the mighty power
of Ethiopia and Egypt;
the nations of Put and Libya
were her allies.
10But she was captured and taken
to a foreign country.
Her children were murdered
at every street corner.
The members of her royal family
were auctioned off,
and her high officials
were bound in chains.
11Nineveh, now it's your turn!
You will get drunk and try to hide
from your enemy.
12Your fortresses are fig trees
with ripe figs.
Merely shake the trees,
and fruit will fall
into every open mouth.
13Your army is weak.
Fire has destroyed the crossbars
on your city gates;
now they stand wide open
to your enemy.
14Your city is under attack.
Haul in extra water!
Strengthen your defenses!
Start making bricks!
Stir the mortar!
15You will still go up in flames
and be cut down by swords
that will wipe you out like a field
attacked by grasshoppers.
So, go ahead and increase
like a swarm of locusts!
16More merchants are in your city
than there are stars
in the sky—
but they are like locusts
that eat everything,
then fly away.
17Your guards and your officials
are swarms of locusts.
On a chilly day
they settle on a fence,
but when the sun comes out,
they take off
to who-knows-where.
18King of Assyria,
your officials and leaders
are sound asleep,
while your people are scattered
in the mountains.
Yes, your people are sheep
without a shepherd.
19You're fatally wounded.
There's no hope for you.
But everyone claps
when they hear this news,
because your constant cruelty
has caused them pain.
translation_text:
1Kitiŋ ki gbii inyamɔn, ni linikul,
ni liwangol li bidim ga gaa li mpɔɔn na aadoon le na.
2Li pel ŋinaalab aah wii pu na man,
ni itaan aatɔroku tiib aah san pu na.
3Baataan berni la,
le kijaak aajum moor lak lak, le tikpaatunn mu moor.
Bi kuun ŋinikpol paan tɔb pu paacham,
ŋinikpol ŋi baa nyi ŋaakahm na,
bijab gbeer ŋi le ki lir.
4Uwumbɔr daa pateer Ninefa aatiŋ aatafal la.
Ki nan ŋan sakpen, le ki kpa ibɔnyɔk i bir na,
ki nan ŋmal ŋitimbol ŋiken ibɔnyɔk,
ki di mu ŋa tinaagbiir ni.
5Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke,
“M ga daa sin Ninefa aatiŋ aanib aatafal.
M ga gbabr si ki cha si aaŋmeen
ki cha ŋitimbol ŋiken kan si,
ŋi ga kan si saanimɔɔn ngbaan ni.
6M ga lik si fam, ki di tijɔŋ biin aa pu.
Binib ga lik si ki san ijawaan la.
7Binib bimɔk kan si na ga sur bipuwɔb.
Bi ga len ke, ‘Ninefa aatiŋ kpaln tilangbenn le ki dɔ.
Ubaa aan san ki kinimbaak.
Ubaa mu aan li ban ke u sɔŋ kisui.’”
8Ninefa aatiŋ, aa jer Ijipt aatiyil Tebes aa? Ki mu nan kpa limɔɔl li kii ki ke ligoln na. Nail aamɔɔl le nan ye kaakikiir. 9Kima le nan joo Kus ni Ijipt aanib, le ubaa aa nan nyi kaapɔɔn mɔk. Kimaantɔ le nan ye Libia aatiŋ. 10Le bi nan yoor Tebes aanib buen tinaagbiir ni. Bi nan gbaa ku baabim bil kitiŋ ngbaan aalɔlɔnn mɔmɔk ni. Bi nan di tikululn le gbin binib bi ye baasalolm na, le ki yakr bi tii binib bi nan nyaŋ bi ki chur bi na.
11Sin Ninefa aatiŋ mu ga ŋa ke saah gbii ndaan le na. Aa mu ga pɔɔn aabaa ke aa san ŋmar saadim chee. 12Saah maa tidir ti fɔk ki pɔɔ kiir aabaa na ga li gur naahn ŋikakan aasui i aasubil puir na la: dam isui ngbaan le ŋikakan ga gbar lir ni aamɔb ni. 13Saajab naahn bipiib la, le ubaa aa kii saatiŋ ke saadim taa nyaŋ ki. Mmii le ga wu idɔ i aa di laŋ saabisamɔi na. 14Lu nnyun ki gor kiir baah ban bi gob si pu na, ki moo pɔɔk saadir ti fɔk na. Taa titan ti ni ga di ŋa ŋitambil na man, ki gor tiwan ni ni joo ŋani ŋitambil na man. 15Ni po gee ni ŋa pu na kan, mmii le ga wu nimi, bee ni bee butɔb ponn ni. Bi ga ŋar nimi ŋŋaan ke itoon aah ŋmɔ tijikaar pu na la.
Ni pɔr ke itoon na la. 16Nimi aanib bi tiir kitiirk na wiir jer iŋmabi aah wiir kitaapaak pu na. Le dandana ma kan, bi mɔmɔk buen ke itoon i taln ifeen ki fii buen na la. 17Saaninkpiib naahn itoon i koo ŋigon ni nwiin mundaal soon na la, le nwiin yaa nyan ni kan, i fii buen, le ubaa aa ki nyi yaa buen nin chee na.
18Asiria aabɔrkpaan, saayidam kpoi a, le saanib bi kpa ŋiyimbil na mu geen kaan ki finn kpala. Saanib yaa, ki bi ŋijoo paab, le ubaa aa bi ki ga giin bi kunn ni linampal. 19Nnyɔk aa bi ki ga sɔŋ saatotonn ti aa kan na, le saabuun ngbaan aan yann. Binib bi mɔmɔk ŋun saah bii doo pu na gbaa tinyɔpur mpopiin pu la. Unii ubaa nan ŋmaa ŋmar saabiin mu kaa nan kpa ndoon na ni ii?

english_text:
1I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me.
Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
2Our Lord, how long must I beg
for your help
before you listen?
How long before you save us
from all this violence?
3Why do you make me watch
such terrible injustice?
Why do you allow violence,
lawlessness, crime, and cruelty
to spread everywhere?
4Laws cannot be enforced;
justice is always the loser;
criminals crowd out honest people
and twist the laws around.
The Lord Answers Habakkuk
5 Look and be amazed
at what's happening
among the nations!
Even if you were told,
you would never believe
what's taking place now.
6 I am sending the Babylonians.
They are fierce and cruel—
marching across the land,
conquering cities and towns.
7How fearsome and frightening.
Their only laws and rules
are the ones they make up.
8Their cavalry troops are faster
than leopards,
more ferocious than wolves
hunting at sunset,
and swifter than hungry eagles
suddenly swooping down.
9They are eager to destroy,
and they gather captives
like handfuls of sand.
10They make fun of rulers
and laugh at fortresses,
while building dirt mounds
so they can capture cities.
11Then suddenly they disappear
like a gust of wind—
those sinful people who worship
their own strength.
Habakkuk Complains Again
12Holy Lord God, mighty rock,
you are eternal,
and we are safe from death.
You are using those Babylonians
to judge and punish others.
13But you can't stand sin or wrong.
So don't sit by in silence
while they gobble up people
who are better than they are.
14The people you put on this earth
are like fish or reptiles
without a leader.
15Then an enemy comes along
and takes them captive
with hooks and nets.
It makes him so happy
16that he offers sacrifices
to his fishing nets,
because they make him rich
and provide choice foods.
17Will he keep hauling in his nets
and destroying nations
without showing mercy?
translation_text:
1Uwumbɔr aah nan kpiir tibɔr ti tuk waabɔnabr Habakuk na sɔ.
Habakuk aah len waanib aatunwanbir aabɔr pu na
2Uwumbɔr, ni ga yunn kinye aan aa ŋun maah yin si ki ban nterm pu na, aan ki nyan mi linimaln ni? 3Ba ŋa aa cha m kani tibɔbir timina aaboln? Ni ga ŋa kinye aan aa li ka lik titunwanbir ki ŋmin? Mbiin ni mbimbin mu pɔɔ na le mann goln mi na, le kijaak ni kinikpakpak bi ni kookoo. 4Nkaal aa kpa mpɔɔn, le ki bee fam, kina pu na, ibamɔn aa bi. Titunwanbirdam nyaŋ binib bi aabimbin ŋan na, le ki laŋ ibamɔn pu.
Uwumbɔr aah gar pu na
5Uwumbɔr nan bui waanib ke, “Li lik man ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln nimi na, aan ki lik ke naah ga kan tiwan ni na ga chuu nimi ijawaan aan naan chuu nimi ijawaan. M ban ke m ŋa tiwan ni binib yaa tuk nimi ni pu na kan, naan tii naadii na la. 6M ban ke m di mpɔɔn ŋa Babiloŋ aanib bi kpa mbiin kaa san nibaa na aaŋaal ni la. Bi chuun dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni ki ban ntim ke bi nyaŋ ki gaa mu la. 7Bi ye binib bi biken san bi ijawaan sakpen na la, le ki kpa kigaak ki ŋani baah gee pu na.
8“Baataan ŋmaa san mala mala ki jer ipeenaamuun, le ki bir jer nkon aah joo takɔtiib bi na. Baatandam nyan ni dandar aatim ni le ki jak ni baataan, baataan aataagbendun pɔɔ sakpen. I booni ke ŋikaagii le aah booni ke ŋi ti chuu tinann na.
9“Baajab choo bi ti nyaŋ ntim mɔmɔk. Bi wiir pam, ki nya ni liwipuul wɔb ke kitaabuŋ na. Le baah chur binib bi tinaagbiir na wiir ke litambol na. 10Bi lik seeni bibɔrb le ki laa baaninkpiib. Baah maa ŋigon kiir ntim mu aan mu pɔɔ na kibaa aa ŋmaa sil kiir bi, bi kuun titan le ti din kaagon, le ki nyaŋ ki, 11le ki chuun mala ke libuln na ki jer, titunwanbirdam bi aapɔɔn ye baawaal na le na.”
Habakuk aah ki gir bui Uwumbɔr binib aah tun titunwanbir pu na
12Uwumbɔr, ki nyan mpiin na, sin le ye Uwumbɔr. Sin le ye Maawumbɔr u bi chain kaa kpa ndoon na. Uwumbɔr, Ndindaan ni maakikiir, sin le lee Babiloŋ yaab ki cha bi kpa mpɔɔn ke bi ŋmaa daa timi aatafal. 13Tɔ, ba ŋa saa daa bibiindam ngbaan aatafal? Aanimbil bi chain pam kaan ŋmaa lik titunwanbir, kaan ŋmaa li si lik aan binib ŋani tiwan ni kaa ŋan na. Kina pu na, ba ŋa aa ka ŋmin aan bi bi kuln binib bi aabimbin ŋan jer baabimbin na?
14Binib ye ijan i bi nnyun ni kaa kpa ujojoor na aa? 15Babiloŋ yaab ngbaan joo ijapiin le chur binib ke baah ye ijan le na. Bi joo baapɔr le dar bi cha, le ki tar mpopiin pu. 16Bi kpaan dooni baapɔr ngbaan le ki toor kitork tii ti; ba pu? tima le tii bi baah ban tiwanyaan ni mɔmɔk na.
17Bi ga li joo baajaak aajum kuln ŋitimbol, kaa san ŋi kinimbaak kina le ki cha aa?

english_text:
The Lord Answers Habakkuk Again
1While standing guard
on the watchtower,
I waited for the Lord's answer,
before explaining the reason
for my complaint.
2Then the Lord told me:
“I will give you my message
in the form of a vision.
Write it clearly enough
to be read at a glance.
3 At the time I have decided,
my words will come true.
You can trust what I say
about the future.
It may take a long time,
but keep on waiting—
it will happen!
4 “I, the Lord, refuse to accept
anyone who is proud.
Only those who live by faith
are acceptable to me.”
Trouble for Evil People
5Wine is treacherous,
and arrogant people
are never satisfied.
They are no less greedy
than death itself—
they open their mouths as wide
as the world of the dead
and swallow everyone.
6But they will be mocked
with these words:
You're doomed!
You stored up stolen goods
and cheated others
of what belonged to them.
7But without warning,
those you owe
will demand payment.
Then you will become
a frightened victim.
8You robbed cities and nations
everywhere on earth
and murdered their people.
Now those who survived
will be as cruel to you.
9You're doomed!
You made your family rich
at the expense of others.
You even said to yourself,
“I'm above the law.”
10But you will bring shame
on your family
and ruin to yourself
for what you did to others.
11The very stones and wood
in your home
will testify against you.
12You're doomed! You built a city
on crime and violence.
13 But the Lord All-Powerful
sends up in flames
what nations and people
work so hard to gain.
14 Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
15You're doomed!
You get your friends drunk,
just to see them naked.
16Now you will be disgraced
instead of praised.
The Lord will make you drunk,
and when others see you naked,
you will lose their respect.
17You destroyed trees and animals
on Mount Lebanon;
you were ruthless to towns
and people everywhere.
Now you will be terrorized.
Idolatry Is Foolish
18What is an idol worth?
It's merely a false god.
Why trust a speechless image
made from wood or metal
by human hands?
19What can you learn from idols
covered with silver or gold?
They can't even breathe.
Pity anyone who says to an idol
of wood or stone,
“Get up and do something!”
20Let all the world be silent—
the Lord is present
in his holy temple.
translation_text:
Uwumbɔr aah ki gar Habakuk pu na
1M ga jon maakikiib aadifɔfɔk pu, ki ti li ka nima, ki lik Uwumbɔr aah ga bui mi pu ke m len na, ni ngarm mu u ga tii mi maabɔr ti m len na pu.
2Le Uwumbɔr gar mi ke, “Ŋmee tibɔbɔrkaan ti m ga kpiir tuk si na tiyakr aapen pu, aan unii umɔk yaar tuur ti pu na ga ŋmaa karn ti; 3ba pu? tibɔkpiirkaan ngbaan aayoonn aa kee ŋeer ke ti gbiin, ti ye ndoon aabɔr la, le ki ga dan mala ki nan gbiin kina. Nibaakan, ti ga yunn siib, aa mu tee li kii ti, ti ga sil dan kaan yunn. 4Tibɔr ngbaan sɔ: ‘Utunwanbirdaan aan ŋmar, le uninyaan aah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na, u ga li kpa limɔfal.’”
Titunwanbirdam aah kuln pu na
5Mbamɔn, liwangol ŋmanni unii la, u kpa kigaak le kaa tee kpa lifuur ma. Waah kpa kikumɔŋ ke likaakul ki bi ke nkun na, waa babr tiwan nibaa, le ki nyaŋni ŋitimbol ki chur binib mɔmɔk tinaagbiir. 6Bi mɔmɔk ga ŋa u mbɔnyun ni yaansara ki len ke, “Unii u kuun kinaayuk aawangol ki gaal binib aawan mpɔɔn pu bilni na aamɔfal ga kuln. Kina aatuln ga yunn kinye?”
7Libuul ngbaan ni le binib bi ye saapɔndam na ga fii sil. Bi ga finn ngeen pu, le ki cha ijawaan chuu si, le sin aabaa ga kpaln baapɔndaan. 8Saah gaa ŋitimbol pam aawangol mpɔɔn pu pu na, kina le binib bi ŋmar na mu ga nan gaa saawangol; ba pu? aa ku binib pam ki kuln baatim ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi mu ni na.
9Saamɔfal junn a. Aa di mpɔɔn ni beebee le ki di gaa binib aawangol le ki kpaln uwankpadaan, le ki pɔɔn aabaa ke aa maa saadichal paacham ki nya mbiin ni tibɔr ni. 10Aa ban isan ki kuln binib pam aamɔfal, le ki joo ni inimɔɔn nan lii saadichal pu, ki lann aabaa aamɔfal. 11Tidir aagon aatakpal wii saabiin pu la, le ilɔkdɔ ti keei.
12Saamɔfal junn a. Aa di titunwanbir naan kitiŋ, le ki di linikul maa kitiŋ ngbaan siin. 13Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le nan siin ke binib ngbaan aatotoŋ li ye idɔ i ga tuur mmii na, ki mɔk ke ŋitimbol nan tun nimina mɔmɔk fam. 14Nnyun aah bi ni kookoo nnyusakpem ponn ni pu na, kina le binib ga li nyi Uwumbɔr aah kpa mpɔɔn sakpen pu na dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni.
15Tibɔbir bi aa pu la. Sin le bar ŋisubil aadaan lidabuul ni tii biken le bi ti gbii ki dɔ bi ŋmeen ki jinn bibaa inimɔɔn aanimbil ni. 16Sin le ga kan inimɔɔn, naan li ye kipak. Sin aabaa ga nyu ndaan ki gbii. Uwumbɔr le ga daa aatafal ki cha inimɔɔn biin saapak pu. 17Mbiin mu aa nan di ŋa Lebanonn aachook na ga gir ni aa pu, le saah nan ku tiwakor ti na ga cha ijawaan chuu si, ba pu? aa ku binib pam ki kuln baatim ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi mu ponn ni na.
18Liwaal kpa ba aanyoor? Unibɔn le naan li, le li joo inyamɔn baanja tuk si. Unii u naan li na tii li naadii, le li mu aa tee ŋmaa len tibɔr. 19Saamɔfal junn a; ba pu? aa bui lidɔgeln ke, “Finn ngeen pu,” le ki ki bui litakpal li kaa kpa kifuurk na ke, “Finn ngeen pu.” Liwaal ga ŋmaa kpiir tiwan nibaa tuk si ii? Bi ga di salmaa ni tikunabr le boon li, le li mu aa tee kpa kifuurk.
20Uwumbɔr bi Waadichal li bi chain na ni, cha kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk ŋmin chii unimbiin ni.

english_text:
Habakkuk's Prayer
1This is my prayer:
2I know your reputation, Lord,
and I am amazed
at what you have done.
Please turn from your anger
and be merciful;
do for us what you did
for our ancestors.
3You are the same Holy God
who came from Teman
and Paran to help us.
The brightness of your glory
covered the heavens,
and your praises were heard
everywhere on earth.
4Your glory shone like the sun,
and light flashed from your hands,
hiding your mighty power.
5Dreadful diseases and plagues
marched in front
and followed behind.
6When you stopped,
the earth shook;
when you stared,
nations trembled;
when you walked
along your ancient paths,
eternal mountains and hills
crumbled and collapsed.
7The tents of desert tribes
in Cushan and Midian
were ripped apart.
8Our Lord, were you angry
with the monsters
of the deep?
You attacked in your chariot
and wiped them out.
9Your arrows were ready
and obeyed your commands.
You split the earth apart
with rivers and streams;
10mountains trembled
at the sight of you;
rain poured from the clouds;
ocean waves roared and rose.
11The sun and moon stood still,
while your arrows and spears
flashed like lightning.
12In your furious anger,
you trampled on nations
13to rescue your people
and save your chosen one.
You crushed a nation's ruler
and stripped his evil kingdom
of its power.
14His troops had come like a storm,
hoping to scatter us
and glad to gobble us up.
To them we were refugees
in hiding—
but you smashed their heads
with their own weapons.
15Then your chariots churned
the waters of the sea.
Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
16When I heard this message,
I felt weak from fear,
and my lips quivered.
My bones seemed to melt,
and I stumbled around.
But I will patiently wait.
Someday those vicious enemies
will be struck by disaster.
Trust in a Time of Trouble
17Fig trees may no longer bloom,
or vineyards produce grapes;
olive trees may be fruitless,
and harvest time a failure;
sheep pens may be empty,
and cattle stalls vacant—
18but I will still celebrate
because the Lord God
is my Savior.
19 The Lord gives me strength.
He makes my feet as sure
as those of a deer,
and he helps me stand
on the mountains.
To the music director:
Use stringed instruments.
translation_text:
Habakuk aah mee limeel pu na
1Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Habakuk aameel sɔ:
2Uwumbɔr, m ŋun saah tun lituln li na pu,
le ijawaan chuu mi sakpen.
Tɔ, ŋa timi aayoonn mumina ŋitukpaan ŋi aa nan ŋani na.
Hali saaŋuul ponn ni kan, san timi kinimbaak.
3Uwumbɔr ki nyan ni Edom aatiŋ ni ki choo;
Uwumbɔr u ye chain na nyan ni Parann aagongon pu ki choo.
Waanyuun gbiin paacham,
le waapak mu gbiin kitiŋ kee pu.
4Waah wiin pu na naahn nwiin aah wiin pu na la;
uŋaal moor lak lak ke mmii na la,
le waapɔɔn ma tee bɔr.
5U cha iween le lolni u pu nsan,
le nkun paa upuwɔb.
6U yaa sil kan, kitiŋ deŋni la;
le u yaa yaar lik kan, ŋitimbol jii.
Ŋijoo ŋi bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na wur la;
le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk aagongon na mu ber lir kitiŋ.
Ŋima pu le u nan chuun n‑yaayoonn na.
7M nan kan ke ijawaan nan chuu Kusann aanib,
le Midiann aatiŋ aanib aawon gbaa.
8Uwumbɔr, ŋimɔɔ pu le saaŋuul nan fii ii?
nnyusakpem pu le saaŋuul nan fii ii?
Aa nan jak saataan ni yaatɔroku tiib bi ye linyaŋ yaab na.
9Aa nan gor saatɔm kiir, ki ban ipiin pam;
Aa cha ŋimɔɔ puu ki bɔkl kitiŋ.
10Le ŋijoo kan si ki mur fenni.
Nnyusakpem nyan ni paacham ki lir ni;
le nnyun mu bi kitiŋ na puu mpɔɔn pu,
le mu aanyunkpenn fii jon paacham.
11Nwiin ni uŋmal aah kan saapiin
ni saakpaatuŋ aah san mala mala pu na,
le ni sil paacham chii.
12Aa nan di liŋuul bɔ dii kitiŋ kee pu;
le saaŋuul ponn ni aa taa taa ŋitimbol pu.
13Aa nan dan ke aa ti gaa saanib ni saah nyan ubɔr u na lii la.
Aa nan kuln titunwanbir aatiŋ aayidaan,
aa nan doo u kookoo la.
14Aa di ubaa aakpaatuŋ le too chaar uyil
buyoonn waajab chii ni ke bi nan jenn timi,
ki mɔɔni ke baah ban bi ti loon
le ki ku doo bigiim bi bi limukl ni na.
15Aa di saataan taa taa nnyusakpem,
ki taa taa nnyun mu ti kpaln tipupur.
16M ŋun timina mɔmɔk pu le mpobil gbaa,
le mmɔgban jii ijawaan pu,
le nwon mɔmɔk kpo, le ntaa jii.
Le m tee ga mɔr ki li kii nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga daa
binib bi tak timi na aatafal na.
17Ŋikakan yaa kaa ŋeen,
le ndaan aasubil mu yaa kaa baa isui pu,
olif aakpan aasui mu yaa yii kaa lun,
le tijikaar mu yaa kaa ŋa ikpaakon ni,
ipiih mu yaa kaa bi kibɔkpuk ni,
le inaa mu yaa kaa bi tinaabar ni kan,
18m tee ga li mɔɔni Uwumbɔr pu,
m ga li kpa mpopiin Uwumbɔr u gaal mi lir na pu.
19Ndindaan Uwumbɔr le ye maapɔɔn;
u ŋa maataafar ke upeeman aataabuseen na la,
le ki kii mi ŋijoo paab.

english_text:
1 I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah.
When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message.
Judgment on Judah
2I, the Lord, now promise
to destroy everything
on this earth—
3people and animals,
birds and fish.
Everyone who is evil
will crash to the ground,
and I will wipe out
the entire human race.
4I will reach out to punish
Judah and Jerusalem—
nothing will remain
of the god Baal;
nothing will be remembered
of his pagan priests.
5Not a trace will be found
of those who worship stars
from their rooftops,
or bow down to the god Milcom,
while claiming loyalty
to me, the Lord.
6Nothing will remain of anyone
who has turned away
and rejected me.
7Be silent! I am the Lord God,
and the time is near.
I am preparing
to sacrifice my people
and to invite my guests.
8On that day I will punish
national leaders
and sons of the king,
along with all who follow
foreign customs.
9I will punish worshipers
of pagan gods
and cruel palace officials
who abuse their power.
10I, the Lord, promise
that on that day
noisy crying will be heard
from Fish Gate, New Town,
and Upper Hills.
11Everyone in Lower Hollow
will mourn loudly,
because merchants
and money changers
will be wiped out.
12I'll search Jerusalem with lamps
and punish those people
who sit there unworried
while thinking,
“The Lord won't do anything,
good or bad.”
13Their possessions will be taken,
their homes left in ruins.
They won't get to live
in the houses they build,
or drink wine from the grapes
in their own vineyards.
A Terrible Day
14The great day of the Lord
is coming soon, very soon.
On that terrible day,
fearsome shouts of warriors
will be heard everywhere.
15It will be a time of anger—
of trouble and torment,
of disaster and destruction,
of darkness and despair,
of storm clouds and shadows,
16of trumpet calls
and battle cries
against fortified cities
and mighty fortresses.
17The Lord warns everyone
who has sinned against him,
“I'll strike you blind!
Then your blood and your insides
will gush out like vomit.
18Not even your silver or gold
can save you on that day
when I, the Lord, am angry.
My anger will flare up
like a furious fire
scorching the earth
and everyone on it.”
translation_text:
1Uwumbɔr aah nan di waabɔr ti tuk Sefania, buyoonn Amonn aajapɔɔn Josia nan ye Juda aabɔr na sɔ. Sefania nan ye Kusi aajapɔɔn la. Le Kusi mu aate nan ye Gedalia, u mu aate nan ye Amaria na, le Amaria mu aate nan ye ubɔr Hesekia.
Uwumbɔr aabɔjil aawiin daal
2Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M ga kuln tiwan mɔmɔk kitiŋ kee pu, 3m ga kuln binib, ni tiwakor, ni inyoon, ni ijan mɔmɔk. M ga cha bibiindam lir baatun mɔmɔk ni. M ga kuln unibɔn, ubaa aan ŋmar. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.
4“M ga daa Jerusalem aatiŋ, ni Juda aapepel aanib mɔmɔk aatafal. M ga kuln kookoo aanib bi gur ki dooni liwaal li bi yin li ke Baal na, ki kuln baawaadam bi toor li na. 5M ga kuln unii umɔk joi ŋidichal aapaacham ki ti dooni nwiin, ni uŋmal, ni iŋmabi na. M ga kuln binib bi mɔmɔk dooni mi ki bui ke bi ga kii maamɔb, ki tee puur liwaal li bi yin li ke Milkom na. 6M ga kuln binib bi mɔmɔk fenn bipuwɔb tii mi, kaa ki dii mi na, bima le aa ki choo m chee ke m nan li mɔk bi nsan na.”
7Uwumbɔr aawiin peen ni a, nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga ji binib tibɔr na peen ni a, kina pu na, li ŋmin suuna man. Uwumbɔr gor ke u kɔr waanib ke kitork aawakor na la, le ki yin baadim ke bi nan yoor baawan. 8Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Linikul ngbaan daal kan, m ga daa bininkpiib, ni mbɔrbim, ni bi mɔmɔk kaa dii maasan na aatafal. 9M ga daa binib bi mɔmɔk aa taar mbisamɔb na aatafal. Bi su kinaayuk mu, ki ku binib, ki joo baawan ti bilni baawaadir ni na.”
10Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, ni ga ŋun iwiil pu Ujan Aabisamɔb chee, Jerusalem aatiŋ ni. Ni ga ŋun ikpowiil pu baah laa maa tidipɔnn kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni nin chee na, ki ŋun ŋidichal aah lir pu na aafuuk ŋigongon paab. 11Nimi bi bi kitiŋ ngbaan aanyaŋ ni wɔb na, ni li wii ikpowiil, ba pu? binib bi mɔmɔk chuun daa ki tiir na ga kpo.
12“N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga yoor karyaa ki biln Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni. M ga daa binib bi lik bibaa ke bi ye bininyuum ki lik pak bibaa na aatafal. Bi len ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aa ŋani nibaa ni ŋan, kaa ŋani ni kaa ŋan na mu.’ 13Bidim ga yoor baawangol buen, le baadichal ber. Baan koo ŋidichal ŋi bi bi maa na ponn ni, kaan nyu baah bi ŋumni ndaan aasubil aasui i na aadaan kpala.”
14Uwumbɔr aawinkpaan ngbaan peen ni, mu peen ni ki choo mala mala. Mu ga li ye mpombiin daal la, hali bijab bi kaar na ga wii itaakpayɔl pu. 15Mu ga li ye liŋuusakpeln daal la, mu ga li ye libiil ni liwonyɔl daal la, mu ga li ye libiil ni likuln daal la, mu ga li bɔɔn ki kpa ntaalangbam pam, 16mu ga li ye nwiin mundaal bijab ga pii butɔb aakpiin, ki faa butɔb aakuun, ki tak ntim mu bi maa tidifɔfɔŋ ni ŋigon kiir mu na la.
17Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “M ga cha tibɔbir ngbaan aaboln dan unibɔn pu aan unii mɔmɔk li chuun baani ke ujoon na. Bi tun mi taani, le m ga cha baasin puu ke nnyun na, le baanikpol ga li dɔ kitiŋ ki ti bur.”
