3Biminmanib a yudaau wan biɛn wee bi gann biɛn ye u li tenn ipiin le ki sin ji li mann kumanug, ni bu che ni kpaa le ke uminmann yudaan nmɔn li jɔɔ nan wee u li ta mann. 4Ni ye u nan bi be dulinya nan yaan ke, waa nan bi li ye biminmanib a yudaau wi, nan bu-n bininfob pii nan be ki mann nsiim nmɔn kaah wɔɔn man nin le. 5Wonjiɛn bol kan yaan wee bi tun ibamɔn a toon yin ki nann le ke paab a naamin a jinjiimin. Ni niɛ bu le bi nan kpaan Moziz n-yonn man wee u na yin tii kuwonjiɛn nanboŋin ke: “Che niwann biɛn n ŋa ke maah nan wɔɔniŋ kuwonjiɛn nanboŋ kan lijɔɔl a paabin.” 6Amaa itoon yan wee Yisa gaa-n yab jon bi yaa toon ke, tipoopɔnn tan wee Yisa si bininfob nin Uwonbɔr a sisiigin nin kaah jon tipookpegirin man nin, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinl ŋanl nmɔn tɔɔ lifiɛŋanlin bu le.
7Ni ma bu ni ye chinchinn a poor nmɔn kaa nan bi jɔɔ kuŋmaruŋ ke, baah ji nan bi li ban tipoor tiba jigin ni. 8Amaa Uwonbɔr nan kan bininfob a galin le ki len ke:
“Uyudaan le len ke, n-yonn chaan,
le N na li poo tipoopɔnn
ki sei Iziral Yaab nin Juda yaab.
9Uyudaan len ke tipoor nmɔn kaa na yin nann,
tan wee N nan poo sei bi yaajam
n-yonn man wee N nan da bi
nyan Ijibir a tingbɔŋin nni,
nan bu-n baa nan ŋmag tipoor nmɔn nbamɔmi,
le N nan labir ki jiɛn bi,
Uyudaan le len.
10N-yonn nmɔn nan jon ke,
maah li poo tipoor tan sei Iziral yaab sɔ, Uyudaan le len.
N li ta n siim ki ŋa bi potiɛrin
le ki sɔb nsiim nmɔn ŋa bi sufu ni.
Le n na li ye bi Wonbɔru,
le bi mu na li ye n ninfob.
11Uba kaa ji na li wɔɔn u kunkɔɔn tau
bee u nabig ki ke, ‘Li nyi Uyudaan ni,’
nan bu-n bi biɛn na yin nyim le,
naah nyan nbuwaabin ki tan kpaa bininkpeebin.
12Nan bu-n N na li jiɛn bi pootomin ki per bi
le kaa ji li tiɛr bi bir bu jigin ni.”
13Uwonbɔr kaah nan yin tipoor nan ke, “Tipoopɔnn nin” le U ŋa tipoor tan chinn nin tipookpegir tan kaa ji tun ni; le niwann nan mu ŋa niwann kpegin ki por li bor kaa li yuuri.

english_text:
The Tent in Heaven
1The first promise included rules for worship and a tent for worship here on earth. 2 The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
3 Behind the curtain was the most holy place. 4 The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them. 5 On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy.
Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things. 6 But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties. 7 However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
8All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship. 9This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices. 10These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
11 Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world. 12Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
13 According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf. 14But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
15Christ died to rescue those who had sinned and broken the old agreement. Now he brings his chosen ones a new agreement with its guarantee of God's eternal blessings! 16In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use. 17In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
18Blood was also used to put the first agreement into effect. 19 Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water. 20He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.” 21 Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship. 22 The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered.
Christ's Great Sacrifice
23These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better. 24This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
25Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal. 26If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
27We die only once, and then we are judged. 28 So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
translation_text:
Dulinya nan nin paab a wonjiɛnl
1Chinchinn a poorin nan jɔɔ liwonjiɛnl a siim le nin dulinya nan a wonjiɛn bol. 2Bi nan tii kunanboŋ le. Ki yi ki poolin niba yaan ke kasi a bol nan yaan wee fila a titɔɔnbol nin teebul nin kasi a boroboro kan wee bi jɔɔ tenn liwonseil a mann bolin nan be. 3Kunanboŋ kiba mu ji nan be kunanboŋ nmɔn a poolin le likinkenl takpenl nan deg ku bu, le bi yi ki ke kasi mu a kasi a bol, 4kunanboŋ nmɔn a poolin nan jɔɔ salima a binbinl nan yaan wee bi nan nyɔɔr nnyɔgkusim ki tenn Uwonbɔr, le Uwonbɔr a poor adaka kan wee salima nan tab ki bu-n mu be niin. Adaka nmɔn a poolin nan jɔɔ salima a binbog kan gbee nin tijiir tan wee bi yi maana nan, nin Arɔnn a jaangbiɛg kan nan bunn tifarin, nin itangbag ilee yan wee bi nan sɔb nsiim ki paan i bu-n nan kpee niin. 5Le tiwann naan wann tan jɔɔ jilima ki nann bininfob nin tikpinkpann nan tɔɔ adaka nmɔn bu, le bi kpinkpann nmɔn deg nan yaan ye tibir a jiɛnper a bolin. Amaa taa li fir pag tibɔr nmɔn biɛn daandaan nan ni.
6Ni ye niwann biɛn a sili nan ti ŋa ke, biminmanib nan ti kɔɔ le iyoo biɛn chinchinn a nanboŋ n-yaan ki tan tun bi wonjiɛnl a toon. 7Amaa biminmanib a yudaau a binba le nan ti kɔɔ kunanboŋ kan be poolin nin taaliba libinl a poolin, u nan ti ŋmag ncham le ki kɔɔ, nan wee u li ta mann ubaantɔɔl a bir bu, nin bininfob kaah tun tibir tan wee kaa nyi. 8Kasi a Naaŋ nan wɔɔn ni niɛ le ke, nsan man chaa kasi mu a kasi a bolin kaa la loori, chinchinn a wonjiɛn nanboŋin kaah la si n bu. 9Ni niɛ le ye nan mag ki wɔɔn n-yonn man wee ti be daandaan nan, ni wɔɔn ke ipiin nin kumanug kan wee bi nan mann nin kaa nan fir ŋunn uwonjiɛn a potiɛli. 10Ni nan ye tijiir, nin tiwann nyuwann, nin kuchiig daal a kaal nin dulinya nan a siim kaah wɔɔn man hali ki nan kpaa tipoopɔnn nin a yoo.
11Masiya kaah nan dan wee ki ye biminmanib a yudaau wan ye tiwann ŋan tan pii nan be-n, u nan kɔɔ kuwonjiɛn nanboŋ kan yab ki ŋan jon kan be dulinya nan yaan, wee naa ye bininfob le tii ki-n yaan le. 12Waa nan ŋmag iŋɔɔb nin nnaabum a cham le ki kɔɔ nin yaan ni; amaa nba bu le u nan kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bolin ki ta u tɔɔl a cham ki mann kumanug kan ye nkpenim a manug kan kaa jɔɔ diɛm Uwonbɔr ban ki sei ti. 13Bi minmanib nan ti taar iŋɔɔb nin inaaja a cham le nin kinaasiɛg kan bi nyɔɔ ki a fatam le ki jɔgin bininfob bu ban jɔɔ tijaginn bi kaal bu-n wee nin ŋa bi kasi bi gbanann nin. 14Mambu ke, Masiya ma a chamin tun nan jon man na, uma wan kaa jɔɔ igalin wee kinaaŋ kan be u ni kaa jɔɔ diɛmin nan che u ta uba ki mann kumanug ki sei Uwonbɔr, ki ŋunn ti potiɛri a toon yan yin liin ti kɔɔn nkumin nin, wee nin che ti fir jiɛn Uwonbɔr wan foo-n!
15Ni ma bu le Masiya ye ti sandanfaaru tipoopɔnn n-yaan, ke nin che ban wee Uwonbɔr yin bin kan Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinl lan ye lifaal lan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi. Nan bu-n Masiya pii nan kpo ke un da ban nan tun tibir n-yonn man wee tipookpegirin la nan si-n le, ki nyan bi tibir nmɔn a tudarilin.
16Ni ye uninfo por u faal waah nan kpo ke u faalin ji man ke, naa tun itoon ni, see ke u nan kpo, 17Nan bu-n uba kaa li fir ji uninfo a faal wee udaan la fo; amaa see ke udaan nan kpo. 18Ni nan bu le che hali chinchinn a poorin kaa nan bi li fir tun itoon wee ncham kaa be. 19Moziz kaah nan ta Uwonbɔr a siimin biɛn ki wɔɔn bininfobin biɛn n-yonn man nin, le u ta nnaabum a cham nin nnyum, nin tipeekormann nin iduufala ki lol tabin tab ki ta bɔ ncham nin nnyumin yaan ki jɔg jɔg Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ kpabkaagin nin bininfobin biɛn bu. 20Le ki len ke, “Ni niɛ le ye tipoorin a cham, tan wee Uwonbɔr ke ni li ŋmagin.” 21Man mu jigin le u nan ta ncham nmɔn ki jɔg jɔg kuwonjiɛn nanboŋin bu nin niwann nan biɛn nan be kunanboŋin nmɔn a poolin wee bi jɔɔ mann bi kaal a manugin. 22Ibamɔn buu nsiimin wɔɔn ke ncham le ye min ŋunn niwann biɛn, ni bu ncham kaa nyan ke tibir a jiɛnper kaa be.
Masiya a manug le nyann tibir
23Ni nan kpaa talar le, nin bi li mann kumanug ki ŋunn tiwann tan nann paab a wan yɔɔrin, amaa paab a wan yɔɔrin tɔɔl jɔɔ kumanug kan ŋan jon ti niɛ nan. 24Nan bu-n Masiya kaa nan kɔɔ bininfob kaah maa wonjiɛn bol lan nan nann wonjiɛn bol bamɔnlin yaan ni; paab baantɔɔl le u nan don, le ki si ti taalin Uwonbɔr a nintogil. 25Waa nan don paab nmɔn ke u ta li gbaa jɔɔ uba ki mann kumanug ke biminmanib a yudaau kaah ti kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bol ibin biɛn ki ŋmag ncham man kaa ye u tɔɔl a cham ki tan mann man nin ni. 26Ni bi ye man ke Masiya nan bi li ji fala n-yonn takpem naah nyan dulinya a piinimin. Amaa daandaan nan u degirin ti bu nba bu le, iyoo nan a diɛmin ki ta uba ki mann kumanug ki nyan tibir. 27A li ke uninfo kaah ye un kpo nba bu man nin, wee ni bɔɔn ke bin ji u tibɔr man nin, 28man mu le Masiya a manugin nan mann nba bu ki nyan bininfob takpem a bir; le u ji li jirin, kaa ye u nan ji tibir a fala, amaa u li ŋmag feegab ki nan sei ban guu win.

english_text:
1The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year. 2If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices. 3-4But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
5 When Christ came into the world, he said to God,
“Sacrifices and offerings
are not what you want,
but you have given me
my body.
6No, you are not pleased
with animal sacrifices
and offerings for sin.”
7Then Christ said,
“And so, my God,
I have come to do
what you want,
as the Scriptures say.”
8The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them? 9Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.” 10So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
11 The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins. 12 But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side, 13and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power. 14By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
15The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
16 “When the time comes,
I will make an agreement
with them.
I will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
17 Then I will forget
about their sins
and no longer remember
their evil deeds.”
18When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices.
Encouragement and Warning
19My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place 20by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
21We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house. 22 So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water. 23We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us. 24We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things. 25Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
26No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth. 27 They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire. 28 If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death. 29 But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy. 30 We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people. 31It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
32Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light. 33Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others. 34You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
35Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards. 36Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised. 37 As the Scriptures say,
“God is coming soon!
It won't be very long.
38The people God accepts
will live because
of their faith.
But he isn't pleased
with anyone
who turns back.”
39We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
translation_text:
1Nsiimin ye tiwann ŋann tan chaan nin a jinjiim le, amaa naa ye tiwann ŋann bamɔn nmɔn tɔɔl le ye ni. Ni ma bu kumanug kan gbaa mann ibin biɛn kaa diɛrin, kaa yin fir ŋa ban fɔɔr mal bin jiɛn Uwonbɔrin kasi. 2Ni ye biminmanib nmɔn nan bi li fir ke, baa nan bi li ta kumanug ki jiɛn naa? Ni ma bu na biwonjiɛmin bi kan nŋunnim nba buu le nin diɛ, le bi sufu kaa ji bi li bii bi toonbir bu. 3Amaa kumanug nmɔn a manim libinl biɛn nmɔn nan ye nan tiɛr bininfob le bi bir, 4nan bu-n inaaja nin iŋɔɔb a cham kaa li fir nyan tibiri.
5Mambu Masiya kaah dan dulinya nan yaan nin, u nan bei Uwonbɔr ke:
“Ŋaa ban kumanug nin ipiin nin,
amaa tigbanann le a ŋa ti sili ki seim;
6A num kaa nan gbee
kumanug kan wee bi nan mann ki nyɔɔr ti nŋmi ni nin tibir a manugin ni.
7Le n nan len ke, ‘Min sɔ, ni sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ kpabkaagin ki jiin n paam ke,
“N dan n nan tun a bam le, Uwonbɔr aa.’ ”
8Chinchinn u nan len ke, “Ŋaa ban kumanug nin ipiin nin tiwankor tan wee bi nyɔɔ nŋmi, nin tibir a manug kan wee bi ti mann tibir bu-n nni” (hali nin nsiimin kaah le sei nsan ke bi li ŋaan man nin gbaa). 9Le u len ke, “Min sɔ, N dan n nan tun ŋaah ban man le.” Le Uwonbɔr ta chinchinn a manugin ki gab, le ki siin kumanug kan kpiɛ milee nan. 10Uwonbɔr a bam nmɔn bu le U ŋa ti kasidam Yisa Masiya kaah nan ta u gbanann ki mann kumanug nba bu ki sei ti-n bu.
11Biminmanib biɛn si le lidaal biɛn ki tun bi wonjiɛn toon; ki le gbaa sagir ki mann kumanug kuba nmɔn, kan kaa li fir nyan tibiri. 12Amaa uminmann u niɛ man nan mann kumanugin nba bu le kpeŋileŋ tibir bu, le ki kal Uwonbɔr a nɔɔjiim paam. 13Ki guu iyoo yan wee Uwonbɔr na li che u dataam n kpann u taai a tɔɔn bol, 14nan bu-n kumanug kiba nmɔn le u che ban wee u nyan bi tibirin ki ŋaan bi kasi hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.
15Kasi a Naaŋin mu jin kumanug nmɔn a siɛra ki sei ta. Chinchinn u len ke:
16Uyudaan len ke,
“Tipoor tan wee N yin poo sei bi sɔ
n-yonn man chaan nan a bɔɔn bu,
N li ta N siimin ki ŋa bi sufu ni,
le ki sɔb nsiim nmɔn ki ŋa bi potiɛrin.”
17Le u ji len kpiɛ ke:
“Bi bir nin bi tukangbir a toon yin,
maa ji li tiɛr i bu.”
18Nan yaan wee tibir a jiɛn per be-n, naa kpaa talar nin tibir a manug ji li be.
Ni che ti fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr
19Mambu, n nabum, taah jɔɔ tidindann ke ti na li kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bolin Yisa a chamin bu-n, 20nsanpɔɔn man fo wee ti kan likinkenlin loor ki sei ti-n, n ma ye, Yisa a gbanann, 21nin taah jɔɔ uminmann wan yab ki ŋmag Uwonbɔr a niin nin, 22ni che ti fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr nin sufu ŋaŋ nin yada kan gbee nin ibamɔn na, waah jɔgin ki ŋunn ti sufu nyan kasi, wee ti nyan igalin ti potiɛlin ni, wee ki fun tigbanann mu nnyum ŋami. 23Ni che ti li ŋmag taah jɔɔ tama kan ki pag ki bɔrin wee ki laa yeŋi, nan bu-n wan siin limɔsiinlin nmɔn ye yada daan le. 24Ni che ti baga li be taah li ŋa man ki li pɔɔgir ti kpiɛtiib a sufu, wee nin che ti fir wɔɔn ti jiɛm nin tab kaah ye man ki li tun itoon ŋan. 25Ni laa che ti ta tab ban a lagim ki jiɛn ni, a li ke bibam kaah ŋaan man nin ni, amaa ni che ti li mann pɔɔg tab a gbanann, a li ke naah kan Uyudaan a dan daalin kaah fɔɔr maligin man nin.
26Taah biɛ ibamɔn yan wee bi wɔɔn ti nan a bɔɔn bu, ni ye ti ji be ki tun titoonbir ke, kumanug kuba kaa ji gur ki li ŋunn tibir nmɔn ni, 27amaa taah guu tibɔr a jim nin nŋmi takpen man na yin gaa Uwonbɔr a dataamin a jawaam le be. 28Ni ye uninfo nan ti yii Moziz a siimin ke, wee bininfob bilee bee bita jin u siɛra ke, bi nan ti ku udaan le kaa san u kunyunyunbaagi. 29Mambu, ni tiɛr ke baa a tudaril kpaan nin uninfo wan taah Uwonbɔr a bija a taal bu nan n kan naa, wan ŋa ncham man ye Uwonbɔr a poorin tijaginn a ŋaar, wee ncham nmɔn ŋunn udaan, wee udaan ji sug Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl a Naaŋin naa? 30Nan bu-n ti nyi wan nan len ke, “Ni ye min le nkɔn jiin; n li yɔ,” ki ji len ke, “Uyudaan li ji u ninfob tibɔr.” 31Ni jɔɔ bijawaam le nin uninfo n lu Uwonbɔr wan ye limiɛfoldaan nan a nɔɔn.
32Ni tiɛr iyoo yan nan chinn nin, wee ni nan gaa nwonween nin a bɔɔn bu, wee ni nan ye fala a jim nin linunmanlin, amaa naa nan nyaŋ ni. 33Iyonn iba bi nan ti sugir ni le ki mugir ni npaan ni; le iyonn iba mu ke ni ti kpiɛg ban wee bi mugir nbu le ki ji fala. 34Ni nan jogir biloondiikɔɔbin le, le ki chee sei ban yug ni wan yɔɔrin nin nmɔn, nan bu-n ni tɔɔl nyi naah jɔɔ nan nin kaah ŋan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi.
35Mambu ni laa ta ni dindanin ki gabi; nan bu-n ni nyɔɔr na li yab. 36Ni ŋan nin ni li jɔɔ limɔril wee ni nan fir tun Uwonbɔr a bam ke, ni li kan nan wee U nan siin limɔsiinl ke U li sei nin. 37Ni ma bu n-yonn wama nan yaan,
“Wan chaan nin li dan kaa li yuuri.”
38Amaa N yaa ninfo buchin win li be u yada ni.
Ni ye u jir bɔɔn ke,
N num kaa li gbee wi.”
39Amaa tim kaa ye ban sul jir bɔɔn wee ki gab yɔli nni, amaa ti ye ban ŋa yada nin ban kan feegabin le.

english_text:
The Great Faith of God's People
1Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see. 2 It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
3 Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
4 Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
5 Enoch had faith and did not die. He pleased God, and God took him up to heaven. This is why his body was never found. 6But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
7 Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
8 Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen. 9 Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise. 10Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
11 Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son. 12 Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
13 Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth. 14When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own. 15If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time. 16But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
17-18 Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac, 19because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
20 Isaac had faith, and he promised blessings to Jacob and Esau. 21 Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons. 22 And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
23 Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders. 24 Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson. 25 He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while. 26Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
27Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger. 28 His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
29 Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
30 God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
31 Rahab had been a prostitute, but she had faith and welcomed the spies. So she wasn't killed with the people who disobeyed.
32 What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets. 33 Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions 34 and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
35 Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life. 36 Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail. 37 Still others were stoned to death or sawed in two or killed with swords. Some had nothing but sheep skins or goat skins to wear. They were poor, mistreated, and tortured. 38The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
39All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised. 40This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
translation_text:
Yada
1Yada a ŋaam ye taah kaa jɔɔ nbiɛnim nin nan wee ti jɔɔ tama ni bu-n, wee ti num kaa ga nin. 2Ni niɛ nan bu le yaaja yonn a ninfob nan jɔɔ kupag.
3Yada bu le ti biɛ ke Imɔleen le Uwonbɔr nan ta naan dulinya, ni bu naa ye nan wee ti ga nan le Uwonbɔr nan ta naan dulinya.
4Yada bu le Ebiɛl nan mann kumanug ŋaŋ ki sei Uwonbɔr ki jon Kenn a manug. Yada bu le Uwonbɔr nan pag u ke u ye ubuchin le, Uwonbɔr kaah nan pag nan ŋan ki jiin u manugin paamin. Yada bu le u le la pag, hali nin waah le kpo nan.
5Yada bu le Uwonbɔr nan taah Enog dulinya nan yaan; le waa kan nkumi; le uba kaa ji nan kan wi, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr le nan ta u don paab. Nin Uwonbɔr kaah nan nan ta u don paabin, U nan pag u ke uma ye wan gbee Uma Uwonbɔr a num. 6Naa ye yada ke uba kaa li fir tun wee nin gbee Uwonbɔr a numi, nan bu-n wan biɛn dan Uwonbɔr ban ke ni ŋan udaan li jɔɔ yada ke Uwonbɔr be, ki ye wan tenn ban ban u nin inunman tinyɔɔr.
7Yada bu le Nowa, Uwonbɔr kaah nan kpaan u ikpaan ki ta jiin tiwann tan paam wee u num kaa la nan kan nin, le kasi a jawaam nan che u kpee kuŋaluŋ kan fee uma nin u niin yaab gabin. U yada bu le Uwonbɔr nan bii dulinya le Nowa kpann ufaajir u buchin tan nyan u yada nin.
8Yada bu, Abiraham nan chee Uwonbɔr a yim ki jon kitiŋ kan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinl ke U li ta kitiŋ kan ki sei win, u nan chee Uwonbɔr a mɔb le ki jon, hali nin waah kaa le nan nyi kitiŋ nmɔn yaan ni, ni biɛn yɔli u nan jon na. 9Yada bu le u nan ŋa u kukɔɔbol limɔsiinl a tiŋin n-yaan ki be ke uchaan kaah ŋaan man kitinchaŋin nin, u nan be Tinanbonn nin le uma nin Azig nin Jekɔb ban mu nan ye limɔsiinl nmɔn a faajibin. 10Nan bu-n u nan lig nintogil le ki guu kitiŋ kan a fiɛl wee Uwonbɔr nan loon wee ki maa ki-n.
11Yada bu le Abiraham nin u poo Sɛra wan nan ye upiiŋɔɔb ki ji porin nan kan npɔɔn ki ma ki big, nan bu-n bi nan ŋa Uwonbɔr wan nan siin limɔsiinlin le yada. 12Hali nin Abiraham kaah kaa ji nan fɔg nin nkumin gbaa, uma uja uba nmɔn a yaabili le nan yabig ke iŋmabil yan be titalangbann nin ni, ki ji yab ke limɔgil a gbaam a tanbiidil yan kaa jɔɔ kanlin.
13Bininfob nan biɛn la nan be nin bi yada le ki kpo. Baa nan gaa tiwann tan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinlin ni; amaa bi nan kan tiwann nmɔn dindanl le ki jɔɔ npopeen. Bi nan chee ke bi ye kitiŋ kiba a ninfob le ki ye bicham dulinya nan yaan. 14Bininfob ban pag man nin nmɔn wɔɔn ke bi ban kitiŋ kan ye bi tɔɔl yaag le. 15Ni ye bi nan bi tiɛr kitiŋ kan yaan wee bi nan fiin nbu ke, na bi nan bi kan nsan ki jira. 16Amaa bi nan ban kitiŋ kan ŋan le, ki be papaab. Mambu naa jɔɔ Uwonbɔr ifa nin bin yin U ke bi Wonbɔr wi, ni ma bu U mann kitiŋ le ki guu bi.
17Yada bu Abiraham, Uwonbɔr kaah nan mag u ligin, u nan ta u bija Azig ke un mann kumanug ki sei Uwonbɔr. Uma wan nan gaa limɔsiinlin ji nan yin ta u bijagaŋ nmɔn le ki mann kumanug, 18hali nin Uwonbɔr kaah le nan bei u ke, “Azig bu le bi na li tiɛr a yaabili bu-n.” 19Abiraham nan tiɛr ke Uwonbɔr li fir fiin utakpiir nkumin, pag wonn a poolin, u sin nan gaa Azig ki nyan nkumin.
20Yada bu le Azig nan kaab tikaar jaa Jekɔb nin Isɔɔ bu ki jiin iyoo yan la chaan nin paam.
21Yada bu Jekɔb, kaah nan yin kpe-n, u nan kaab tikaar ki jaa Josef a naachim bu ubaba, le ki nyii u jaangbiɛg bu ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr.
22Yada bu Josef a kum kaah nan malin, u nan pag Iziral yaab a nyam Ijibir a tiŋin, ki ji wɔɔn bi waah kpo ke bin ŋa u kpabi man.
23Yada bu le Moziz a baa nin u na nan ta u ki woon iŋmal itaa, baah nan maa u a bɔɔn. Bi nan kan ke Moziz ye kibiŋiŋaŋ kan kaa jɔɔ kpiɛg le, mambu baa nan san ubɔr a siimin ni.
24Yada bu Moziz kaah nan yabig, u nan yii le kaa ban bin ke u ye ubɔr Faro a bisa a bigi. 25U nan chee nin un ji fala nin Uwonbɔr a ninfobin, ki jon nin un ji tibir a mɔm man kaa yuurin na. 26U nan tiɛr ke u jin ifa Masiya bu ke ni jɔɔ tinyɔɔr jon Ijibir a jɔɔma, nan bu-n u num nan tɔɔ u nyɔɔr tan be nintogilin bu le.
27Yada bu Moziz nan nyan Ijibir, kaa san bijawaam ubɔr a ŋuul bu; u nan jɔɔ limɔril le, nan bu-n u nan kan Uwonbɔr wan wee baa ga-n le. 28Yada bu le u nan ŋmag Yuglagir a chiigin, ki nan che bi ta ncham ki jɔg jɔg inaangan bu ke nkum a malaka wan ku nbininkpeemin nan foon ke, un laa ku Iziral yaab a bininkpeemin ni.
29Yada bu le Iziral yaab nan don limɔgmanlin ke kitinkooŋin; amaa Ijibir yaab ma kaah nan bigin ke bin do-n, nnyum nan jin ba.
30Yada bu Iziral yaab kaah nan choon jin Jeriko a goi a lapoob iweehn ilile-n, ni bɔɔn bu i nan lur le. 31Yada bu baah nan ku ban ye limɔyiildamin, baa nan ku Rahab wan nan ye lipiijagɔɔrilin ki kpiɛ bi bu, nan bu-n waah gaa Iziral a ninfob ban jon bin pigir kitiŋin ki ligin ki woon u niin nin bu.
32Ke n ji yin len ke baa? Maa jɔɔ isaŋ nin n pag ni Gidion, nin Barag, nin Samisin, nin Jafita, nin Defid, nin Samɔɔl nin bilinlemin biɛn a bɔri, 33ban a yada bu wee bi nan kɔn ki nyaŋ ntim a bɔrtiib, ki tun ibamɔn a itoon, ki kan nan nan ye Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinlin; ki ye ban nan loon igbegin a mɔɔŋi, 34le ki junn nŋmipeen a tuntom, le ki guun ŋmar takoobi a kumin; ban a daburigi nan kpann npɔɔn, le ki nan to bitɔb nin npɔɔn ki nyaŋ itindoo a tɔtob. 35Bipiib biba a takpiib le Uwonbɔr nan fiin bi nkumin, le bi ji be nin bi miɛfol. Biba nan kan limugil, amaa le baa chee bin guun nin, naah li ŋa man wee bin kan nkum a fiim man ŋan.
36Bi nan daar bibam nyɔɔrug le ki boo bi, le ki lol bibam tikulor ki kɔɔn bibam mu tiloondirin. 37Bi nan gabir bi itangbag, ki jiil bibam por milee lee, ki ta takoobi ki ku bibam. Bibam nan yee tipeegbann le nin tiŋɔɔgbann, ki ye faladam, le bininfob mugir bi ki ŋaan bi nan kaa ŋan. 38Dulinya kaa nan kpaan bi. Bi nan choon yelin le kukunkɔɔg nin ijɔɔ a paab, ki dɔɔ titangbafiɛrin nin ifalin.
39Bi niɛ nan biɛn bi yada bu le Uwonbɔr nan pag bi, amaa le bi ni uba kaa gaa nan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinl ke U li sei bin ni. 40Uwonbɔr nan bon ibonn yan ŋan le ki sei ti ke tim nin bi ma nan lagin ki be ke u li ŋa bi kasi.

english_text:
A Large Crowd of Witnesses
1 Such a large crowd of witnesses is all around us! So we must get rid of everything that slows us down, especially the sin that just won't let go. And we must be determined to run the race that is ahead of us. 2 We must keep our eyes on Jesus, who leads us and makes our faith complete. He endured the shame of being nailed to a cross, because he knew later on he would be glad he did. Now he is seated at the right side of God's throne! 3So keep your mind on Jesus, who put up with many insults from sinners. Then you won't get discouraged and give up.
4None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin. 5 But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children,
“When the Lord punishes you,
don't make light of it,
and when he corrects you,
don't be discouraged.
6The Lord corrects the people
he loves
and disciplines those
he calls his own.”
7Be patient when you are being corrected! This is how God treats his children. Don't all parents correct their children? 8God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him. 9Our earthly fathers correct us, and we still respect them. Isn't it even better to be given true life by letting our spiritual Father correct us?
10Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is. 11It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
12 Now stand up straight! Stop your knees from shaking 13 and walk a straight path. Then lame people will be healed, instead of getting worse.
Warning against Turning from God
14Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord. 15 Make sure no one misses out on God's wonderful kindness. Don't let anyone become bitter and cause trouble for the rest of you. 16 Watch out for immoral and ungodly people like Esau, who sold his future blessing for only one meal. 17 You know how he later wanted it back. But there was nothing he could do to change things, even though he begged his father and cried.
18 You have not come to a place like Mount Sinai that can be seen and touched. There is no flaming fire or dark cloud or storm 19or trumpet sound. The people of Israel heard a voice speak. But they begged it to stop, 20 because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain. 21The sight was so frightening that Moses said he shook with fear.
22You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate. 23Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect. 24 And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
25 Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven? 26 When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
27The words “once again” mean that these created things will someday be shaken and removed. Then what cannot be shaken will last. 28We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect. 29 Our God is like a destructive fire!
translation_text:
Ti Baa Uwonbɔr
1Mambu taah jɔɔ siɛradam takpem ban gɔɔn jin ti nan, ni che ti ta nan biɛn li legin ti samin ki gab nin tibir tan fir chor ti-n, ni che ti nyigin ki guun ti taguunl lan dɔ guu ti nan. 2Ni che ti ta ti num ki tɔɔn Yisa bu, wan ye ti yada a piinim nin njoorimin. U nan jin fala lidapunpunl bu nin limɔril kaa san ifa, nmɔn man nan dɔ guu nbu, ki kal Uwonbɔr a naangbɔŋ bu u nɔɔjiim paam.
3Ni li tiɛr waah kan limugil tibirdam ban kaa nan chee win a nɔɔn nin bu, wee nin laa che ni gbanann ngbarig wee ni ta ni yada gabi. 4Naah kɔn nin tibirin, naa la kɔn tan foo nan yaan ye ni nyan ni chami. 5Ni tam imɔleen yan wee Uwonbɔr ta pɔɔg ni gbanann ki yin ni u buwaab ki ke:
“N big, Uyudaan dar a tul ke, laa yin li yɔli,
ni ye U fuun a bu ke, laa che a gbanann ngbɔɔ,
6nan bu-n Uyudaan kpaan ban wee U jiɛ-n le,
le ki dar wan biɛn wee U chee sei u ke u ye a bigin a tul.”
7Chee sei limugil a tuntomin na ke ni ye ikpaan le; Uwonbɔr ŋmag ni le ke u buwaabin. Bibolinba wee ki baa kaa kpaan kaa? 8Ni ye baa kpaan ni (wee ni biɛn kan ikpaan ke), man ke naa ye u baantɔɔl a bimarimi. 9Nan kpiɛ, ti biɛn nan jɔɔ ti baam ban ma ti tininforin nin, ki kpaan ti le ti tenn bi jilima ni bu. Mambu ni ŋan ti chee sei wan ye ti naaŋ a Baa-n ke nin jo man wee ki fo! 10Ti baam nan ti kpaan ti le wama baah tiɛr ke ni ŋan man; amaa Uwonbɔr ma kpaan ti le naah ŋan sei ti bu, naah li ŋa man wee ti por u kasi a binbemin. 11Ikpaan a yoo kaa jɔɔ nmɔni, amaa ni ye nton le. Ni bɔɔn bu ke, le nim ban mu tinn nmɔn nkan nbuchin binben nin nposɔɔn.
Nwɔɔm nin ikpaan
12Mambu, ni tann ni nɔɔi yan bagin nin ni dun yan kaa pɔɔ nna. 13“Ni mann nsan man tel ki sei ni taai,” wee ni laa nyaŋ kuwɔbigi, amaa wee un kan kutebug.
14Ni pɔɔn niba ki li jɔɔ nposɔɔn nin bininfob biɛn wee ki li be kasi; naa jɔɔ kasi a binbem ke uba kaa li fir kan Uyudaan ni. 15Ni laa che uba n nan lann Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanli, wee nin laa che nton a sibonl npa ki yabig ni sufu-n ni wee nin ta kuŋmaruŋ ki dan ki bii bininfob takpemi. 16Ni laa che ni ni uba n tun iwanchɔgin toon upiibanlin bee ujabanlin ni, bee kaa jɔɔ nwonjiɛn binben ke Esɔɔ, wan nan kɔɔr u ninkper a faal kisaayiig kiba bu nni. 17Ni bɔɔn bu, a li ke naah nyi man nin, waah nan nan ban un gaa lifaal nmɔn a kaarin u baa nan yiiu, waa nan fir kpenn u baa a potiɛli, nin waah le nan ban tikaar nmɔn ki mɔr nin tinyinyinin biɛn yɔli.
18Nim kaa foo lijɔɔl lan wee ni li fir ma li wee li gaan nŋmi nni; nan yaan wee nibɔɔngem ki ŋmin sulim wee ntafapɔɔrim daar; 19kunaatuŋ kaah mɔr nan yaan bee likukɔlin kaah pag ileen yan, wee ban nan gbirin nan balin ke u laa ji pag ileen nmɔn sei bi, 20nan bu-n baa nan li fir ŋmag nsiimin kaah wɔɔn man nin ke: “Hali ni ye kuwankobug le maa lijɔɔl nmɔn ke, bin gabir ki itangbag ki kuu.” 21Baah nan kan nan nin nan jɔɔ bijawaam le, le Moziz len ke “Bijawaam le jɔɔm le n gbanann jegil.”
22Amaa nim foon Zayɔnn a Jɔɔlin ban na, papaab a Jerusalam n-yaan, Uwonbɔr wan fo-n a tiŋin, ni foon malakam turil mu a tuturil a mɔmin a laguŋ n-yaan na, 23ni foon biwonjiɛm ban ye nbininkpeemin ban na, ban a yin sɔb dɔ papaabin. Ni foon Uwonbɔr, wan ye bininfob biɛn a bɔjiru win ban na, bininfob buchim ban a naaŋ ŋa kasi, 24ni foon Yisa wan ye usandanfaar tipoopɔnn n bu ban na, nin ncham jɔg kaam man pag ibamɔn ki jon Ebiɛl a chamin ban na.
25Ni laa nyi yii Uwonbɔr wan pag nan ni. Ni ye baa nan ŋmar baah nan yii wan a kpaan yin dulinya nan yaan nin ban ke, ŋma nin nan chaa baan timaa, ni ye ti labir ti bɔɔn kpaa wan be papaab ki kpaan ti nan ke naa? 26Iyaayoo nmɔn, Uwonbɔr a kukɔl nan che dulinya dam le, amaa daandaan nan u siin limɔsiinl ki ke, “Maa ji yin che dulinya a binba n dami, amaa n li che paab mu n dam.” 27Imɔbon yan len ke, “N ji li chee-n,” wɔɔn ke tiwann tan dam ki ye tiwann naan kaarin na li choo nyan ki jiɛn tan kaa yin damin paar.
28Mambu taah gaan nnaam a yerin man kaa li fir dam nan, ni che ti pag Uwonbɔr, ki li jiɛn u nin jilima nin bijawaam, 29ni ma bu “Ti Wonbɔru nmɔn ye nŋmi man gaan le.”

english_text:
Service That Pleases God
1Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
2 Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
3Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
4 Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
5 Don't fall in love with money. Be satisfied with what you have. The Lord has promised that he will not leave us or desert us. 6 This should make you feel like saying,
“The Lord helps me!
Why should I be afraid
of what people
can do to me?”
7Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
8Jesus Christ never changes! He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. 9Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them. 10But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
11 After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp. 12Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy. 13This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace. 14On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
15Our sacrifice is to keep offering praise to God in the name of Jesus. 16But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
17Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
18Pray for us. Our consciences are clear, and we always try to live right. 19I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon.
Final Prayers and Greetings
20God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock. 21 I pray God will make you ready to obey him and that you will always be eager to do right. May Jesus help you do what pleases God. To Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever! Amen.
22My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
23By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
24Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people.
His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
25I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
translation_text:
Taah li ŋa man wee nin gbee Uwonbɔr a num
1Ni li jiɛ ni kpiɛtiib ke ni nabuma. 2Ni laa tami wee ki li gaan bichama, nan bu-n ni ŋaan man ke, bibam gaan malakam le kaa nyi. 3Ni li tiɛr ban be tiloondirin nin bu, a li ke ni gbaa tɔɔl be tiloondirin le-n, nin ban wee bi mugir bin a li ke ni mu ji bi fala nmɔn le-n.
4Lipiikɔɔnl nin lijakunl ye ti biɛn li tenn li jilima le, lipiikɔɔnl nin lijakunl a didɔɔbol ye ni li be kasi le, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr na li ji ban tun iwanchɔgin toon nin tibɔr bipiib banlin nin bija banlin.
5Ni choo niba nin ilig a jiɛma, wee ki che ni num ngbee nan wee ni jɔɔ-n, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr len ke,
“Maa li nyi ki jiɛn ni;
maa li nyi ki yii ni.”
6Ni ma bu le ti pag nin tidindann ke,
“Uyudaan le ye wan terim; ni bu jawaam kaa jɔɔmi.
Uninfosaal li fir ŋaam baa?”
7Ni li tiɛr ni sanliib ban nan pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr ki sei nin. Ni li tiɛr bi binbem kaah nan nan joor man na, wee ki li toog bi yada kaah nan ye man nin. 8Yisa Masiya kaah won be man won nin yaan nin, u le be man le dinan, u le yin gbaa be man le nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi. 9Ni laa che nwɔɔncham nan a booli biɛn nboon ni. Ni ŋan nin ti sufu n kan npɔɔn Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanlin bu, naa ye ikaal a jiir tan kaa ter ban ji ti nni.
10Ti jɔɔ kumanug a binbinl lan wee ban tun itoon tiwonjiɛn nanbonn nin kaa jɔɔ nsan nin bin ji li bu a jiiri. 11Ni ma bu biminmanib a yudaau nan ti ŋmag tiwankor a cham le ki kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bolin le ti ye tibir a manug, amaa le ki nyɔɔ tiwankor nmɔn bi laguŋ nmɔn a gbaam. 12Mambu le Yisa mu nan jin fala ntingbaan kitiŋ nmɔn a timansanmɔnn, ki ta u tɔɔl a cham ke un nyan bininfob tibirin. 13Ni che ti jo u ban kulaguŋ nmɔn a gbaam, ki tan ji ifa yan wee u jin nin. 14Nan bu-n dulinya nan yaan taa jɔɔ kitiŋ kan li gbaa be, amaa ti lig kitiŋ kan la yin danin le. 15Mambu, Yisa a yinlin bu, ni che ti li pagir Uwonbɔr kumanug a pag kan nya timɔgban yin ki wɔɔn U yinlin. 16Ni laa tam itoon ŋan a tumi, ki li por tab naah jɔɔ nan na, man a manug le Uwonbɔr a num gbee.
17Ni li jɔɔ limɔcheel nin ni sanliib wee ki chee sei bi ninkper a pɔɔma. Bi baga be nin ni, ki ye bininfob ban na li wɔɔn baah tun nan. Ni chee sei ba wee bi toon li ye nmɔn, ki laa ye litugili, naa ye man ke naa na yin ŋan sei ni.
18Ni li miɛ Uwonbɔr ki tenn ta. Ti nyi ke ti jɔɔ potiɛri yan ween le ti ban ti li be jilima a binbemin niwann biɛn nin. 19N tɔɔl le balin ni le ke, ni li miɛ Uwonbɔr a wee Un che n jirin ni ban daandaan nan.
Ndiɛm a miɛm
20Uwonbɔr wan ye nposɔɔndaan wan nan ta tipoor tan kaa jɔɔ diɛmin a cham ki fiin ti yudaau Yisa wan ye upeekpaaŋanin nkumin nin, 21un sei ni nan ŋan biɛn wee ni ta tun u bam, ki che ni tinn nan li gbee u num, Yisa Masiya, wan ŋan nin npagim iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛm bu. Ibamɔn.
Imɔbon yan joor
22N nabum, n balin ni le ke, ni li jɔɔ limɔril wee ki gaa n kpaan nan a bɔra, nan bu-n tibɔr wama le n ta sɔb kugbɔŋ nan ki sei ni. 23N ban ni li nyi ke bi loor ti nabig Timoti kuloondiigin ki jaau. Ni ye u foon weem ke, n li ta u ki dan wee ti nan kan ni.
24Ni poor ni sanliib nin Uwonbɔr a ninfobin nan. Itali yaab poor ni.
25Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl be ni biɛn bu.

english_text:
1 From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world.
Faith and Wisdom
2 My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble. 3You know you learn to endure by having your faith tested. 4But you must learn to endure everything, so you will be completely mature and not lacking in anything.
5 If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking. 6But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm. 7-8If you are that kind of person, you can't make up your mind, and you surely can't be trusted. So don't expect the Lord to give you anything at all.
Poor People and Rich People
9Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them. 10 But any who are rich should be glad when God makes them humble. Rich people will disappear like wild flowers 11scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business.
Trials and Temptations
12 God will bless you, if you don't give up when your faith is being tested. He will reward you with a glorious life, just as he rewards everyone who loves him.
13 Don't blame God when you are tempted! God cannot be tempted by evil, and he doesn't use evil to tempt others. 14We are tempted by our own desires that drag us off and trap us. 15Our desires make us sin, and when sin is finished with us, it leaves us dead.
16Don't be fooled, my dear friends. 17Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father who created all the lights in the heavens. He is always the same and never makes dark shadows by changing. 18He wanted us to be his own special people, and so he sent the true message to give us new birth.
Hearing and Obeying
19 My dear friends, you should be quick to listen and slow to speak or to get angry. 20If you are angry, you cannot do any of the good things God wants done. 21You must stop doing anything immoral or evil. Instead be humble and accept the message planted in you to save you.
22Obey God's message! Don't fool yourselves by just listening to it. 23If you hear the message and don't obey it, you are like people who stare at themselves in a mirror 24and forget what they look like as soon as they leave. 25But you must never stop looking at the perfect law that sets you free. God will bless you in everything you do, if you listen and obey, and don't just hear and forget.
26If you think you are being religious, but can't control your tongue, you are fooling yourself, and your religion is useless. 27Religion that pleases God the Father must be pure and spotless. You must help needy orphans and widows and not let this world make you evil.
translation_text:
1Min Jemisi wan ye Uwonbɔr nin Uyudaan Yisa Masiya a yomu-n:
N poor Uwonbɔr a ninfob ibol piig nin ilee yan yal be dulinya nan a logi ina nan biɛn nin.
Yada nin nlam
2N nabum, ni ye nbigim man biɛn dan ni bu ke, ni che ni li ye nmɔn takpen ki sei na, 3nan bu-n ni nyi ke ni yada a magim mann kpiɛg ni limɔril le. 4Ni kpaa le nin limɔril n diɛ mi toonl wee nin che ni gbee bininfob nbamɔm, wee niba n laa par ni.
5Ni ye ni ni uba par nlam ke, u yaadaan n miɛm Uwonbɔr wan tenn bininfob nin tibuchinn wee kaa galin uba-n li ta sei u. 6Amaa u miɛ ke, ni kpaa le nin un ŋa Uwonbɔr yada ki laa biɛn ni, nan bu-n wan jɔɔ nbiɛnim nann limɔgil a nyungbɔŋ le, man wee nfaam daar mi ki yeŋin. 7U yaadaan n laa tiɛr ke u li kan niba Uyudaan ban ni; 8u ye ipotiɛ ilee daan le, kaa si bogiliba nan biɛn wee u tun ni.
Fala nin njɔɔm
9Kinabig kan jɔɔ jiininba iyoo biɛn n nan kan ndom ke, ki na li fa ligbingbanl. 10Amaa wan ye uwandaan dulinya nan yaan wee Uwonbɔr nan jiin u tum ke, u daan li far ligbingbanla, nan bu-n u na yin kpo le ke nsipuumin. 11Babu nween pɔɔ wee ntuton nin fa kisiigin ke, npuumin koor le ki lu le mi ŋamin bii. Man mu le ni ye ki sei uwandaan, n-yonn man wee u tiɛr ke u toon li jo nintogilin, iyaayoo le u kpeg.
Nmagim nin nbiginim
12Tikaar be wan jɔɔ limɔril limagil a poolin nin bu, nan bu-n ni ye u nyaŋ limagil ki diɛ ke u li kan u naan yuchigirig kan ye limiɛfol wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinl ke u li ta sei ban ban win.
13Ni ye nbigim kan wan ke, un laa len ke “Uwonbɔr li bigin mi.” Nan bu-n libiginl liba kaa be ki li fir bigin Uwonbɔr i, le U mu kaa bigin uba; 14amaa uninfo biɛn ga nbiginim, n-yonn man wee u potiɛ bir a bam dar u ki chor u nle. 15Tɔ, ni bɔɔn bu a bam nmɔn choo lipool ke, mi yin ma tibir le, le tibir nmɔn nan yabig ke, mi mu nmaa nkum.
16N nabubankaam, ni laa che bin lar ni. 17Nan ŋan nin nan be kasi biɛn ye ipiin yan nyan paab le, ki nyan ti Baa wan jɔɔ papaab a weemin, wan kaa kpenn ke nbɔɔm kaah kpenn man nin. 18U yaa wiib bu le U ma ti, ibamɔn a mɔleen yin bu, ke nin che ti kpann u bininkpeem waah naan nan biɛn ni.
Ngbirim nin ntum
19N nabum ni li nyi ni niɛ nan bu: Ni ŋan nin uninfo li gbir weenweem, ki li pag soonsoon, wee u ŋuul mu n laa fii weenweemi. 20Uninfosaal a ŋuufiiŋ kaa che Uwonbɔr a buchinn forin ni. 21Mambu, ni nyam niwann nan biɛn ye tijaginn nin nbinben biin nin, wee ki jiin niba tum ki gaa imɔleen yan wee bi ta sei nin, imɔleen nmɔn le li fee ni ki jaa.
22Ni laa pelig imɔleen nin a binba, wee ki lar niba. Ni tum yaah len man nin. 23Wan pel imɔleen nan amaa wee kaa ŋa yaah len man nin ke, u nann uninfo kaah lig u nundaag niɛnu ni le, 24le u lig uba ki diɛ ke, ni bɔɔn bu u fɔr ke libol nmɔn yaan le un tam u nunaŋ kaah ye man. 25Amaa uninfo lig Uwonbɔr a siim man be kasi wee ki tenn wiibin, wee ki le gbaa ŋaan man kaa tamir nan wee u gbirin, amaa wee ki ŋaan imɔleen nin kaah len man nin ke, tikaar li be ubu waah yin tun nan biɛn nin.
26Ni ye uba tiɛr ke u ye uwonjiɛn wee kaa chor u lanbil ke, u lar uba le, u wonjiɛnl nmɔn ye yɔli le. 27Liwonjiɛnl lan wee ti Baa a num gbeeg ke li ye kasi kaa jɔɔ tibir ye nan le: Nkpeebim nin ipukɔɔ a terim bi bɔmugkaarin nin choonba ki jiin dulinya nan a ŋmaruŋ paam.

english_text:
Warning against Having Favorites
1My friends, if you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you won't treat some people better than others. 2Suppose a rich person wearing fancy clothes and a gold ring comes to one of your meetings. And suppose a poor person dressed in worn-out clothes also comes. 3You must not give the best seat to the one in fancy clothes and tell the one who is poor to stand at the side or sit on the floor. 4This is the same as saying that some people are better than others, and you would be acting like a crooked judge.
5My dear friends, pay attention. God has given a lot of faith to the poor people in this world. God has also promised them a share in his kingdom that he will give to everyone who loves him. 6You mistreat the poor. But isn't it the rich who boss you around and drag you off to court? 7Aren't they the ones who make fun of your Lord?
8 You will do all right, if you obey the most important law in the Scriptures. It is the law that commands us to love others as much as we love ourselves. 9But if you treat some people better than others, you have done wrong, and the Scriptures teach that you have sinned.
10 If you obey every law except one, you are still guilty of breaking them all. 11 The same God who told us to be faithful in marriage also told us not to murder. So even if you are faithful in marriage, but murder someone, you still have broken God's Law.
12Speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that sets us free. 13Do this, because on the day of judgment there will be no pity for those who have not had pity on others. But even in judgment, God is merciful!
Faith and Works
14My friends, what good is it to say you have faith, when you don't do anything to show you really do have faith? Can this kind of faith save you? 15If you know someone who doesn't have any clothes or food, 16you shouldn't just say, “I hope all goes well for you. I hope you will be warm and have plenty to eat.” What good is it to say this, unless you do something to help? 17Faith that doesn't lead us to do good deeds is all alone and dead!
18Suppose someone disagrees and says, “It is possible to have faith without doing kind deeds.”
I would answer, “Prove that you have faith without doing kind deeds, and I will prove that I have faith by doing them.” 19You surely believe there is only one God. That's fine. Even demons believe this, and it makes them shake with fear.
20Does some stupid person want proof that faith without deeds is useless? 21 Well, our ancestor Abraham pleased God by putting his son Isaac on the altar to sacrifice him. 22Now you see how Abraham's faith and deeds worked together. He proved his faith was real by what he did. 23 This is what the Scriptures mean by saying, “Abraham had faith in God, and God accepted him.” That's how Abraham became God's friend.
24You can now see that we please God by what we do and not only by what we believe. 25 For example, Rahab had been a prostitute. But she pleased God when she welcomed the spies and sent them home by another way.
26Anyone who doesn't breathe is dead, and faith that doesn't do anything is just as dead!
translation_text:
Ikpaan ki jiin nganim paam
1N nabum naah ŋa ti yudaau Yisa Masiya wan ye kupag daan nin yada man ni, ni laa gann tabi. 2Ni ye uba dan ni laguŋin ki yee tiwanŋann nin salima a gbiɛŋ, wee faladaan mu nan kɔɔn ki yee tiwanchar ke, 3ni ye ni sei wan yee tiwanŋann nin jilima ki bei u ke, “Kikaabol ŋaŋ sɔ kalim” amaa wee ki bei faladaan nin ke, “Fin li si doo,” bee “Kalim tum,” ke, 4naa ye nganim le ni ŋa ni sisiigin nmɔn naa? Ki labir bibɔjib ni potiɛbir buu?
5N nabum; ni pela man: Naa ye Uwonbɔr le gann ban ye faladam kutingbɔŋ nan a poolin, ke bi li ye biwandam yada a ŋaam bu, wee ki nan ji paab a naam a faal lan wee Uwonbɔr siin limɔsiinl ke u li sei ban ban win naa? 6Amaa le nim sug faladam. Naa ye biwandamin le jɔɔ ni ki mugir ki chor ni chaa tibɔr a jim a dirin ni naa? 7Naa ye bi ma pag ki bii Masiya a yin ŋanl lan wee Uwonbɔr ta sei ni nnaa?
8Ni ye a ŋmag nnaam a siim man be Uwonbɔr a mɔleen yin nin ki ke, “Li jiɛ a kunkɔɔn taba ke ŋaah ban a ba man nin,” ke a ŋa man ke a ŋa choba. 9Ni ye a gann bininfob ke a ŋa tibira ki ye wan bii nsiim. 10Wan ŋmag nsiimin biɛn, amaa wee ni ŋa le u bii nsiim nmɔn miba ke, u bii nsiim man gurin biɛn na. 11Amaa wan len ke, “Laa tun iwanchɔgin toon ni,” uma le ji len ke, “Laa ku.” Ni ye ŋaa tun iwanchɔgin toon amaa wee ki ku ke, a ye wan bii nsiim le.
12Ni li paga, wee ki sin li tun ke bininfob ban wee bi na li ji bi tibɔr nsiim man tenn feeja-n, 13nan bu-n, ban kaa san bikpiɛtiib kunyunyunbaagin, Uwonbɔr mu na li ji bi tibɔr kaa yin san bi kunyunyunbaagi. Linyunyunbasanl jon tibɔr a jima.
Yada a ŋaam nin itoon a tum
14N nabum, ni ŋam ye baa, ni ye uninfo ke u jɔɔ yada wee u yada nmɔn kaa tun itoon ke, yada nmɔn a bosu li fir fee u jaa? 15Che ti ke a nabig wan ye kibijag bee kibisiɛg be wee kaa jɔɔ tiwanyeer bee tijiir tan li ji. 16Le ni ni uba bei u ke, “Li chaa nin nposɔɔn na,” ki ji bei u ke, “Uwonbɔr li seiŋ wee a ji gbee,” wee kaa ŋa nan wee u ban ki sei u ke, ni ŋam ye baa? 17Ni ye man le, yada a ŋaam a binba wee yada nin itoon kaa nɔɔ tab ke, yada kpiiŋ le yen.
18Amaa uba li len ke, “Fin le jɔɔ yada, le n mu tun itoon.” Wɔɔm a yada kan kaa tun itoon nin ni, wee n wɔɔniŋ n yada nin n toon yan wee n tun. 19Ni ŋa yada ke Uwonbɔr ye u ba le kpeŋileŋ. Ni ŋan! Nnaanbiim gbaa tɔɔl ŋa yada man le ki san bijawaam.
20Fin kujɔrug nan, a ban a biɛ ke yada wan kaa tun itoon ye yɔlii? 21Naa ye itoon ŋan a tum bu le Uwonbɔr nan ŋa ti yaaja Abiraham ubuchin, waah nan ta u big a Azig paan kumanug a binbinl bu ke un mann kumanug ki sei Uwonbɔr nnaa? 22Ni kan ke u yada nin u toon nan lagin tab le ki tun, le u yada nan ŋa nbamɔm u toon a tum bu. 23Le ni nan gbeen Uwonbɔr a mɔleen yan len ke, “Abiraham nan ŋa Uwonbɔr yada, le U ŋa u tibuchinn,” le ki nan yin u ke Uwonbɔr a jɔ. 24Ni kan ke uninfo a toon ŋan bu le bi ke u ye uninfoŋan amaa naa ye u yada a binba bu.
25Naa ye man mu jigin le Rahab wan nan ye lipiijagɔɔril nmu bi nan yin u ubuchin, waah nan ta kudiig ki sei ban nan dan bin nan pigir lig kitiŋ nmɔn ki ji nyan bi wee baa ku bin nnaa? 26A li ke tigbanann tan kaa jɔɔ kinaaŋ kaah ye tigbanann kpiinn man nin, man le yada a ŋaam kan kaa tun itoon mu ye yada kpiiŋ.

english_text:
The Tongue
1My friends, we should not all try to become teachers. In fact, teachers will be judged more strictly than others. 2 All of us do many wrong things. But if you can control your tongue, you are mature and able to control your whole body.
3By putting a bit into the mouth of a horse, we can turn the horse in different directions. 4It takes strong winds to move a large sailing ship, but the captain uses only a small rudder to make it go in any direction. 5Our tongues are small too, and yet they brag about big things.
It takes only a spark to start a forest fire! 6 The tongue is like a spark. It is an evil power that dirties the rest of the body and sets a person's entire life on fire with flames that come from hell itself. 7All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures can be tamed and have been tamed. 8But our tongues get out of control. They are restless and evil, and always spreading deadly poison.
9-10 My dear friends, with our tongues we speak both praises and curses. We praise our Lord and Father, and we curse people who were created to be like God, and this isn't right. 11Can clean water and dirty water both flow from the same spring? 12Can a fig tree produce olives or a grapevine produce figs? Does fresh water come from a well full of salt water?
Wisdom from Above
13 Are any of you wise or sensible? Then show it by living right and by being humble and wise in everything you do. 14But if your heart is full of bitter jealousy and selfishness, don't brag or lie to cover up the truth. 15This kind of wisdom doesn't come from above. It is earthly and selfish and comes from the devil himself. 16Whenever people are jealous or selfish, they cause trouble and do all sorts of cruel things. 17But the wisdom that comes from above leads us to be pure, friendly, gentle, sensible, kind, helpful, genuine, and sincere. 18When peacemakers plant seeds of peace, they will harvest justice.
translation_text:
Lilanbil a bɔr
1N nabum, ni takpem nlaa ban ni ŋa ban wɔɔnn ni, nan bu-n, ni pii nyi ke tim ban wɔɔnn nin, a bɔr a jim na li pɔɔ ki jo bininfob biɛn yaal. 2Tiwann takpemin, ti biɛn tun ki bura. Ni ye uba kaa nyi ki pag burin u pipagirin ke, u yaadaan ye kasi daan le, ki li fir ŋmag u gbanann nbamɔm.
3Ni ye ti lee itaan a mɔɔŋi itangalig ke yin ŋa taah ban man ke, ti li fir labir bi gbanann ki kpaa taah ban nan paam. 4Bee ni taam tiŋalin ki ŋa siɛra. Hali tiŋalin kaah le yab man wee ntafaam daar ti chaan, ni biɛn yɔli, amaa kisalaabig le wan donn n jɔɔ donn tiŋalin, le ki jɔɔ chaa waah ban nan paam. 5Lilanbil mu ye kiwanbig man le tigbanann nin, amaa le ki far ligbingbanl takpem. Lig! Nŋmi wama kaah lu timɔɔrin ke min nyɔɔ kutingbɔŋ man. 6Lilanbil mu tɔɔl ye nŋmi le, ki ji ye dulinya nan a bɔbir ki be tigbanann a yagi biɛn, ki tenn tigbanann nmɔn biɛn tijaginn, ki jɔɔ nŋmi nyɔɔr tigbanann nmɔn a binbemin biɛn, le Sintani a ŋmiim man kaa junn nin mu nnyɔɔ lilanbil nmɔn. 7Tiwankor a booli nin nnɔɔm a booli nin iwaalab a booli nin iwanfol yan be limɔgilin biɛn nan, uninfo le jɔɔ ni biɛn a pɔɔm, 8amaa uba kaa jɔɔ lilanbil a pɔɔmi. Lilanbil jɔɔ tibir, ki gbee nin tilabir tan ku.
9Lilanbil le ti jɔɔ pagir ti yudaau nin ti Baa, le ki biɛ jɔɔ li ki sugir bininfob, ban wee Uwonbɔr naan bi wee bi nann win. 10Bimɔb biba nmɔn le tibɔŋann nin tibɔbir nya. N nabum, naa kpaan ke ni li ye man ni. 11Kinyunbuŋ kiba li fir bun nnyum man mɔ ki ji bun nnyum man ye n-yaam maa? 12N nabum, bikinkam a sub li fir lo tisaan naa? Bee kigansiig li fir lo ikinkan naa? Man mu le ni ye kinyunbuŋ kan bun n-yaam a nyum kaa li fir bun nnyum man mɔ.
Nlam man nyan paab
13Ŋma ye ulandaan nin ubiɛndaan ni sisiigin naa? Ni che un wɔɔn ni u binben ŋam a lam a toon yan ye jiininba a toon nmɔn. 14Amaa ni ye ni jɔɔ lipiiponl nin npooton ni sufu ni ke, ni laa far igbingban Mambu bee ki yii ibamɔn ni. 15“Nlam nmɔn a bosu kaa nyan paab a naamin ni amaa mi ye dulinya nan a lam man kaa gbee nin Kinaaŋ ki ye ulinlaril yaamin le. 16Nan yaan wee linunchɔril nin kujaŋuuŋ a don nba a potiɛl be-n nin yaan le kuŋmaruŋ nin titoonbir be. 17Amaa nlam man nyan paab a naamin nin, chinchinn mi ma ye kasi ki ye man jɔɔ limɔril nin jiininba, ki gbee nin linyunyunbasanl nin nbinben ŋan, nin ibamɔn a pagim. 18Ban jɔɔ limɔril ki bu tibur nin nposɔɔn nin, bi na li chiɛ nin tibuchinn.

english_text:
Friendship with the World
1Why do you fight and argue with each other? Isn't it because you are full of selfish desires that fight to control your body? 2You want something you don't have, and you will do anything to get it. You will even kill! But you still cannot get what you want, and you won't get it by fighting and arguing. You should pray for it. 3Yet even when you do pray, your prayers are not answered, because you pray just for selfish reasons.
4You people aren't faithful to God! Don't you know if you love the world, you are God's enemies? And if you decide to be a friend of the world, you make yourself an enemy of God. 5Do you doubt the Scriptures that say, “God truly cares about the Spirit he has put in us”? 6 In fact, God treats us with even greater kindness, just as the Scriptures say,
“God opposes everyone
who is proud,
but he blesses all who are humble
with undeserved grace.”
7Surrender to God! Resist the devil, and he will run from you. 8Come near to God, and he will come near to you. Clean up your lives, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you people who can't make up your mind. 9Be sad and sorry and weep. Stop laughing and start crying. Be gloomy instead of glad. 10Be humble in the Lord's presence, and he will honor you.
Saying Cruel Things about Others
11My friends, don't say cruel things about others! If you do, or if you condemn others, you are condemning God's Law. And if you condemn the Law, you put yourself above the Law and refuse to obey either it 12or God who gave it. God is our judge, and he can save or destroy us. What right do you have to condemn anyone?
Warning against Bragging
13 You should know better than to say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to the city. We will do business there for a year and make a lot of money!” 14What do you know about tomorrow? How can you be so sure about your life? It is nothing more than mist that appears for only a little while before it disappears. 15You should say, “If the Lord lets us live, we will do these things.” 16Yet you are stupid enough to brag, and it is wrong to be so proud. 17If you don't do what you know is right, you have sinned.
translation_text:
Dulinya a jɔtiig
1Ba che ikɔn nin imɔkpel be ni sisiigin naa? Naa ye ni nyan ni gbanann a bam man be nin ni ki kɔn nin ni n lee? 2Ni ban niba amaa le kaa ga ni. Ni bu le ni jɔɔ linunchɔril ki ku bininfob, amaa naa li fir kan nan wee ni ban nmɔn ni. Ni jɔɔ imɔkpel ki kɔn nin tab. Naa jɔɔ naah ban nan nni, nan bu-n naa miɛ Uwonbɔr i. 3Ni ye ni miɛ ke, naa ga, nan bu-n ni miɛ nin tipotiɛbir le, ni miɛ ke ni ta ŋa ni baantɔɔl a gbanann a bam le.
4Nim ban kaa si bogiliba nan, naa nyi ke nim ban jɔɔr dulinya nan kujɔtiigin ŋa Uwonbɔr ni dataag lee? Wan jɔɔr dulinya nan kujɔtiig ke, udaan ŋa Uwonbɔr u dataaga. 5Bee ni tiɛr ke Uwonbɔr a bɔr kaah len man ni kaa jɔɔ bu lee? Ke Kinaaŋ kan wee Uwonbɔr ta ŋa ti ban nin ki jɔɔ linunchɔril takpem maa? 6Amaa le u san ti kunyunyunbaag takpem. Mambu le Uwonbɔr a bɔr len ke, “Uwonbɔr yiin kalanbaanidam le, amaa le ki sin san ban jɔɔ jiininba kunyunyunbaag.
7Mambu ni taam niba ki sei Uwonbɔr a. Ni tom Sintani, wee un guun ki jiɛn ni. 8Ni fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr a, wee Uwonbɔr mu nfɔɔr ki mal ni. Nir ni nɔɔi ya, nim tibirdam nan, ki ŋa ni sufu kasiu, nim ipotiɛ ilelee dam nan. 9Ni li jɔɔ npoobiin na, ki li mɔr ki kuun na. Kpenn ni laar ŋa timɔra ki che ni mɔm nlabir lisufubiila. 10Jiin ni ba ki sei Uyudaan na, wee Un yuur ni paab.
Ikpaan ki jiin tab a bɔr a jim paam
11N nabum, ni laa jɔɔ kutingbiig nin tabi. Wan pag tibɔbir ki sei u nabig bee ki jin u tibɔr ke, u pag galin nsiimin le, ki jin nsiim nmɔn tibɔra. Ni ye a jin nsiim tibɔr ke, ŋaa ŋmag mi le nmɔn, a ye wan jin nsiim nmɔn le tibɔr. 12Uwonbɔr a binba le siig nsiim, ki ji li fir ji bininfob tibɔr, ki biɛ li fir fee bininfob gab, bee ki bii bininfob. Amaa fin, a ye ŋma ki li fir ji a kunkɔɔn tau tibɔraa?
Ikpaan ki jiin ligbingbanfaal paam
13Ni pela man, nim ban ti ŋa ke ni len ke, “Dinan bee won ti wo li jo kitiŋ poolin ki tan ji libinl niin ki kpeŋ kpoŋkpoŋ ki kan ilig.” 14Ba ŋaa? Naa nyi nan wo li ŋa won ni. A miɛfol ye baa? Ni nann le ke liŋunl kaa lu ke naa yuur wee ki fɔr man ni. 15Amaa naah ye ni pag man ye nan le, “Ni ye Uyudaan a bam ke, ti li be ki tun ni niɛ bee ni niɛ.” 16Ke naah ye man nin, ni far igbingban le ki jɔɔ kalanbaani, ni gbingbanfaal nmɔn ye yɔli le.
17Mambu wan nyi itoon ŋan yan bi ye un tun, wee kaa tun ke, u ŋa tibira.

english_text:
Warning to the Rich
1You rich people should cry and weep! Terrible things are going to happen to you. 2 Your treasures have already rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes. 3 Your money has rusted, and the rust will be evidence against you, as it burns your body like fire. Yet you keep on storing up wealth in these last days. 4 You refused to pay the people who worked in your fields, and now their unpaid wages are shouting out against you. The Lord All-Powerful has surely heard the cries of the workers who harvested your crops.
5While here on earth, you have thought only of filling your own stomachs and having a good time. But now you are like fat cattle on their way to be butchered. 6 You have condemned and murdered innocent people, who couldn't even fight back.
Be Patient and Kind
7My friends, be patient until the Lord returns. Think of farmers who wait patiently for the autumn and spring rains to make their valuable crops grow. 8Be patient like those farmers and don't give up. The Lord will soon be here! 9Don't grumble about each other or you will be judged, and the judge is right outside the door.
10My friends, follow the example of the prophets who spoke for the Lord. They were patient, even when they had to suffer. 11 In fact, we praise the ones who endured the most. You remember how patient Job was and how the Lord finally helped him. The Lord did this because he is so merciful and kind.
12 My friends, above all else, don't take an oath. You must not swear by heaven or by earth or by anything else. “Yes” or “No” is all you need to say. If you say anything more, you will be condemned.
13If you are having trouble, you should pray. And if you are feeling good, you should sing praises. 14 If you are sick, ask the church leaders to come and pray for you. Ask them to put olive oil on you in the name of the Lord. 15If you have faith when you pray for sick people, they will get well. The Lord will heal them, and if they have sinned, he will forgive them.
16 If you have sinned, you should tell each other what you have done. Then you can pray for one another and be healed. The prayer of an innocent person is powerful, and it can help a lot. 17 Elijah was just as human as we are, and for three and a half years his prayers kept the rain from falling. 18 But when he did pray for rain, it fell from the skies and made the crops grow.
19My friends, if any followers have wandered away from the truth, you should try to lead them back. 20 If you turn sinners from the wrong way, you will save them from death, and many of their sins will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Bijɔɔndam a kpaani
1Nim bijɔɔndam, ni pela man, ni li mɔra ki li kuun na, nan bu-n fala kan yin dan ni bu-n bu. 2Ni jɔɔmin biɛn bura, le ipɔgliɛn liɛ ni wann yɔɔr biɛn ki bii u. 3Ni salima nin ni kurninann nin kɔɔ likurila. Likuril nmɔn le li ye siɛra ki li gaa ni gbanann ke nŋmi-n. Ni taah ifaa le ki woon idaajoorikaan. 4Lig! Ni jin bitoontum ban tun ni kpaan nin dulima, kaa yɔn bi. Le bi mɔr, bidichiɛb nmɔn a mɔr kɔɔ Liwonbɔr Gbingbemil a tuli yin na. 5Ni be naah ban man le dulinya nan yaan, ki nɔɔ ni gbanann a bam, ki don ni ba. Ni ŋaam nmɔn polig ni gbanann le lidaal lan wee bi na yin kɔr ni. 6Ni nan pag ki bii bipopendam ma, ki ku ban kaa nan kɔnn nin ni-n.
Limɔril nin liwonmiɛl
7Mambu n nabum, ni mɔra, hali ki nan kpaa ti Yudaau a jirim. Ni lig ukpaar kaah jɔɔ limɔril man ki guu u kpaab kaah na li ŋa tijiir, naah yuur unalantaal a yonn ki nan kpaa utakotaal a yoo. 8Ni mu li jɔɔ limɔrila, ki li si nbamɔma, nan bu-n Uyudaan a damin mala. 9Ni laa ŋulin nin tabi, n nabum, ni ye man ke bi na li ji ni tibɔr. Ubɔjirin si ntimɔsan!
10N nabum, nim le ye limagil ki jɔɔ limɔril fala a poolin, ki si bilinlem ban mɔɔn Uyudaan a yinlin a taai-n. 11Ke naah nyi man ni, ni ye tinyɔɔr le ki sei ban jin fala. Ni gbir Job kaah nan jɔɔ limɔril man u fala a jimin, ki ji kan ni joorim Uwonbɔr kaah tun nan ki sei wa. Uyudaan ye Unyunyunbasann le.
12N nabum, nan jon ni biɛn ye le ke, laa poo paab a naamin bee dulinya bee niba a wan ni. Che a “Nn” li ye nn, le a “Aai” mu li ye aai, wee bi laa galiŋi.
13Ni ni uba be tibɔmugkaarin naa? Un miɛm Uwonbɔr. Ni ni uba jɔɔ lipoopenl laa? Ni che un gaah ilan ki pag Uwonbɔr. 14Ni ni uba buu? Un yim biwonjiɛm a ninkpeeb wee bin miɛ Uwonbɔr sei u ki sin war nkpam ki jaa ubu Uyudaan a yinlin. 15Bi miɛ nin yada ke, ubaar nmɔn li pɔɔg, Uyudaan li fiin u paab. Ni ye u ŋa tibir le ke, u li kan jiɛn per. 16Mambu, ni kpiir ni bir ki wɔɔn taba, ki li miɛ Uwonbɔr ki tenn taba wee ni kan kutebug. Ubuchinn a wonmiɛl jɔɔ npɔɔn le mitoon yin.
17Elaja nan ye uninfosaal le ke taah ye man nan, u nan miɛ nin linunmanl ke utaal nlaa nu, le utaal kaa sin nan nun kitiŋ nmɔn yaan ki tan kpaa ibin itaa nin iŋmal iloob. 18Le u ji nan nan miɛ Uwonbɔr, le utaal nun, le tijiir naan.
19N nabum, ni ye ni ni uba bor kaa nɔɔ ibamɔn a samin, wee uba ta u jiin nin ibamɔn a sam nmɔn yaan ke, 20ni li tiɛr ni niɛ: Wan biɛn fir labir tibirdaan wan borin ki jiin siin ibamɔn a samin yaan ke, udaan fee tibirdaan nmɔn nkum a nɔɔn na, ki li che tibirdaan nmɔn n kan feegab u bir takpemin bu.

english_text:
1From Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ.
To God's people who are scattered like foreigners in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
2God the Father decided to choose you as his people, and his Spirit has made you holy. You have obeyed Jesus Christ and are sprinkled with his blood.
I pray that God will be kind to you and will keep on giving you peace!
A Real Reason for Hope
3Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is so good, and by raising Jesus from death, he has given us new life and a hope that lives on. 4 God has something stored up for you in heaven, where it will never decay or be ruined or disappear.
5You have faith in God, whose power will protect you until the last day. Then he will save you, just as he has always planned to do. 6On that day you will be glad, even if you have to go through many hard trials for a while. 7 Your faith will be like gold that has been tested in a fire. And these trials will prove that your faith is worth much more than gold that can be destroyed. They will show that you will be given praise and honor and glory when Jesus Christ returns.
8You have never seen Jesus, and you don't see him now. But still you love him and have faith in him, and no words can tell how glad and happy 9you are to be saved. This is why you have faith.
10Some prophets told how God would treat you with undeserved grace, and they searched hard to find out more about the way you would be saved. 11The Spirit of Christ was in them and was telling them how Christ would suffer and would then be given great honor. So they searched to find out exactly who Christ would be and when this would happen. 12But they were told that they were serving you and not themselves. They preached to you by the power of the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven. And their message was only for you, even though angels would like to know more about it.
Chosen To Live a Holy Life
13Be alert and think straight. Put all your hope in how God will treat you with undeserved grace when Jesus Christ appears. 14Behave like obedient children. Don't let your lives be controlled by your desires, as they used to be. 15Always live as God's holy people should, because God is the one who chose you, and he is holy. 16 That's why the Scriptures say, “I am the holy God, and you must be holy too.”
17You say that God is your Father, but God doesn't have favorites! He judges all people by what they do. So you must honor God while you live as strangers here on earth. 18You were rescued from the useless way of life you learned from your ancestors. But you know you were not rescued by such things as silver or gold that don't last forever. 19 You were rescued by the precious blood of Christ, that spotless and innocent lamb. 20Christ was chosen even before the world was created, but because of you, he did not come until these last days. 21And when he did come, it was to lead you to have faith in God, who raised him from death and honored him in a glorious way. This is why you have put your faith and hope in God.
22You obeyed the truth, and your souls were made pure. Now you sincerely love each other. But you must keep on loving with all your heart. 23Do this because God has given you new birth by his message that lives on forever. 24 The Scriptures say,
“Humans wither like grass,
and their glory fades
like wild flowers.
Grass dries up,
and flowers fall
to the ground.
25But what the Lord has said
will stand forever.”
Our good news to you is what the Lord has said.
translation_text:
1Min Piita wan ye Yisa Masiya a toomin,
Le sɔb kugbɔŋ nan ki tenn Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab ban ye bicham ki be dulinya ni, ki yal kɔɔ ntimin ki be Pɔntusi nin Galantiya nin Kapadosiya nin Asiya nin Batiniya, 2ban wee bi nan gann, wee ti Baa Uwonbɔr pii nan nyi ke bi li gann bin, ŋa bi kasi, Kasi a Naaŋ a toon bu-n, ki che bi chee Yisa a mɔb le u cham n ŋunn bi:
Linyunyunbasanl nin nposɔɔn li be ni bu takpem.
Tama kan fo a bɔr
3Ipoor ye Uwonbɔr wan ye ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya a Baa-n yaal le! U nyunyunbasanl takpenlin bu ti kan nmaal pɔɔn man be tama kan fo-n, waah nan fiin Yisa Masiya nkumin, 4ki sei ti lifaal lan kaa li nyi buri, bee ki bii bee ki wiiri. Le li be paab ki guu nim, 5ban wee Uwonbɔr a pɔɔm guu ni-n, ni yada bu-n, hali nin feegab a nyɔɔr kaah na li foon, tan ŋa sili ki na li kpiir iyoo yan na yin joorin.
6Ni niɛ nan bu ni mɔ ni le takpem, hali naah le jin fala kan daandaan nan wee kaa li yuurin a booli biɛn nin yɔli. 7I niɛ nan dan le, ke ni yada kan ŋan jon salima kan burin, hali nŋmi kaah le mann salima kan li fir bii-n gbaa, yada nmɔn li wɔɔn ke ni ye ibamɔn le, ki ta kupag nin jilima dan ni joorimin, ni ye Yisa Masiya nan kpiirin ke. 8Hali naah kaa le kan u nni, amaa ni jiɛ u; nin hali naah kaa le la kan u daandaan nan gbaa, ni ŋaa u yadau, mambu le ni gbee nin nmɔn man kaa jɔɔ magimi, 9nan bu-n ni gaan ni yada a nyɔɔr le, nin ni naam a feeja.
10Ki ta jiin feegab nan paam, bilinlem ban nan pag ke linyunyunbasanl li foon ni ban nin, bi nan feen le nin linunmanl le bi baga be niin takpem, 11ke bin kan iyoo yan nin naah li ŋa man wee Masiya a Naaŋ kan be bi ni nan chinn kan le ki wɔɔn bi Masiya a fala a jim nin kupag kan li ŋɔɔrin. 12Ni nan kpiir ki wɔɔn bi ke baa nan tun tenn biba le, amaa nim. Bilinlemin kaah nan pag tiwann tan wee ni gbirin wee ban mɔɔn tibɔŋann nin mɔɔn ti sei ni Kasi a Naaŋ kan nyan paabin a pɔɔm bu-n. Hali malakam ban bin biɛ tiwann nmɔn le.
Nbinben ŋan a yim
13Mambu, ni ŋaam ni potiɛl sili ki tun itoon; ni choom niba; ki ta ni tama biɛn ki ŋa linyunyunbasanl lan wee bi na li sei nin, n-yonn man wee Yisa Masiya na yin kpiirin nin. 14Naah ye nbuwaab ban jɔɔ limɔcheelin, ni laa ji nɔɔ kɔlisabirug, kan wee naa la nan nyi wee ki nɔɔ nni. 15Amaa Uwonbɔr wan yin ni kaah be kasi man nin, ni mu li be kasi nin ni toon biɛn nin na; 16ni ma bu ni sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin ke: “Ni li be kasiu, nan bu-n min Uwonbɔr be le kasi.”
17Nan bu-n naah yin ti Baa wan ji bininfob biɛn a bɔr nin bi toon kaah ye man wee kaa gann nin, ni bu ni che ni binbem li be ke ni ye bicham le dulinya nan yaan ki li san Uwonbɔr bijawaam nin jilimau. 18Nan bu-n ni nyi ke naa ye tiwann tan boon ke tikurninann bee salima le Uwonbɔr nan ta mann nkpenim a manug ki fee ni ki nyan nbinben man kaa jɔɔ bu wee ni yaajam nan ta sei ni-n ni, 19amaa ni nan ye Masiya wan a cham ŋan nin le, Masiya wan ye kipeebig kan kaa jɔɔ igalin bee kidaŋi. 20Uwonbɔr nan gann u le ki nin naan dulinya, amaa le ki nan kpiir u wɔɔn idajoorikaa nan yaan nim bu. 21Uma bu le ni ŋa Uwonbɔr yada, wan nan fiin Yisa nkumin ki sei u kupag, mambu ni yada a ŋaam nin ni tama be Uwonbɔr ban le.
22Naah mann niba kasi wee ki jɔɔ ibamɔn a mɔcheelin wee ki jiɛ ni nabum ibamɔn ni, ni li jiɛ tab nin ni sufu biɛn na. 23Ni ma bu, ni ji kan nmaam jigin na, naa ye biwanboolib ban buri, amaa biwanboolib ban kaa bur, Uwonbɔr a mɔleen yan jɔɔ limiɛfol, ki be iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛmin bu. 24Ni ma bu
“Bininfob biɛn nann timɔɔr le,
le bi pag biɛn nann nmɔɔpuum man be kulɔŋ;
timɔɔr koor le, le nmɔɔpuum mu lur,
25amaa Uyudaan a mɔleen ma le gbaa be le.”
I ma ye imɔleen yan wee bi nan ta mɔɔn sei ni.

english_text:
A Living Stone and a Holy Nation
1Stop being hateful! Quit trying to fool people, and start being sincere. Don't be jealous or say cruel things about others. 2Be like newborn babies who are thirsty for the pure spiritual milk that will help you grow and be saved. 3 You have already found out how good the Lord really is.
4Come to Jesus Christ. He is the living stone people have rejected, but which God has chosen and highly honored. 5And now you are living stones being used to build a spiritual house. You are also a group of holy priests, and with the help of Jesus Christ you will offer sacrifices that please God. 6 It is just as God says in the Scriptures,
“Look! I am placing in Zion
a choice and precious
cornerstone.
No one who has faith
in this one
will be disappointed.”
7 You are followers of the Lord, and this stone is precious to you. But it isn't precious to those who refuse to follow him. They are the builders who tossed aside the stone that turned out to be the most important one of all. 8 They disobeyed the message and stumbled and fell over this stone, because they were doomed.
