24Uwonbɔr wan li fir ŋmag ni wee ni laa lu-n, U li ta ni ki siin U nintogil U pag kan kaa jɔɔ igalin ki jɔɔ nmɔn takpen nin bu. 25Ti sei Uwonbɔr wan be U binba wan ye ti feeru ki jɔɔ kupag, nin jilima, nin npɔɔn, nin tininkper a pɔɔm, ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya a yinlin, iyoo yan nan jon nin, nin daandaan nan nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm! Ibamɔn.

english_text:
1This is what God showed to Jesus Christ, so that he could tell his servants what must happen soon. Christ then sent his angel with the message to his servant John. 2And John told everything he had seen about God's message and about what Jesus Christ had said and done.
3God will bless everyone who reads this prophecy to others, and he will bless everyone who hears and obeys it. The time is almost here.
4 From John to the seven churches in Asia.
I pray that you
will be blessed
with kindness and peace
from God, who is and was
and is coming.
May you receive
kindness and peace
from the seven spirits
before the throne of God.
5 May kindness and peace
be yours
from Jesus Christ,
the faithful witness.
Jesus was the first
to conquer death,
and he is the ruler
of all earthly kings.
Christ loves us,
and by his blood
he set us free
from our sins.
6 He lets us rule as kings
and serve God his Father
as priests.
To him be glory and power
forever and ever! Amen.
7 Look! He is coming
with the clouds.
Everyone will see him,
even the ones who stuck
a sword through him.
All people on earth
will weep because of him.
Yes, it will happen! Amen.
8 The Lord God says, “I am Alpha and Omega, the one who is and was and is coming. I am God All-Powerful!”
A Vision of the Risen Lord
9I am John, a follower together with all of you. We suffer because Jesus is our king, but he gives us the strength to endure. I was sent to Patmos Island, because I had preached God's message and had told about Jesus. 10On the Lord's day the Spirit took control of me, and behind me I heard a loud voice that sounded like a trumpet. 11The voice said, “Write in a book what you see. Then send it to the seven churches in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”
12When I turned to see who was speaking to me, I saw seven gold lampstands. 13 There with the lampstands was someone who seemed to be the Son of Man. He was wearing a robe that reached down to his feet, and a gold cloth was wrapped around his chest. 14 His head and his hair were white as wool or snow, and his eyes looked like flames of fire. 15 His feet were glowing like bronze being heated in a furnace, and his voice sounded like the roar of a waterfall. 16He held seven stars in his right hand, and a sharp double-edged sword was coming from his mouth. His face was shining as bright as the sun at noon.
17 When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead person. But he put his right hand on me and said:
Don't be afraid! I am the first, the last, 18and the living one. I died, but now I am alive forever, and I have the keys to death and the world of the dead. 19Write what you have seen and what is and what will happen after these things. 20I will explain the mystery of the seven stars you saw at my right side and the seven gold lampstands. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the lampstands are the seven churches.
translation_text:
1Tibɔkpiirikaar tan wee Uwonbɔr nan ta sei Yisa Masiya ke, un ta wɔɔn u toontum nan yin tun daandaan nan. U nan che U malaka le wɔɔn U toontunnu Jɔnn, 2le Jɔnn nan jin siɛra waah kan nan biɛn nin bu, ti ma ye, Uwonbɔr a mɔleen nin Yisa Masiya a siɛra. 3Wan karin ilinlen leen yan be kugbɔŋ nan a poolin ke tikaar be udaan bu, le ban mu gbir tibɔr nmɔn ki ta ŋa bi sufu ni ke tikaar be bi bu, nan bu-n iyoo mala.
Ipoor yan tenn biwonjiɛm a laginn tilile
4Min Jɔnn,
le sɔb kugbɔŋ nan ki tenn biwonjiɛm a laginn tilile tan be Asiya a yerin ni:
Linyunyunbasanl nin nposɔɔn lan nyan Uwonbɔr ban li be nin ni, Uma wan be, nin wan nan be, nin wan yin dan, ki ji nyan ntinaam milile man be u naangbɔŋin u nintogilin li be ni ban. 5Linyunyunbasanl nin nposɔɔn lan ji nyan Yisa Masiya, wan ye ibamɔn a siɛradaau win, kibininkpeeg kan chinn fii nkumin, nin wan ye dulinya nan a bɔrtiib biɛn a bɔru win li be ni ban.
Wan jiɛ ti wee ki ta u cham ki nyan ti tibirin nin, 6le ki che ti ŋa u naam a ninfob nin biminmanib ke ti li jiɛn Uwonbɔr wan ye u Baa-n, u binba le kpaan nin kupag nin npɔɔn iyoo nin iyoo! Ibamɔn.
7Lig, u be titalangbann nin ki chaan,
le nnumbim biɛn na li kan u;
hali nin ban nan ŋu win li kan u;
le dulinya yaab biɛn na li mɔɔ u bu.
Ni sin li ŋa man! Ibamɔn.
8“Min le ye Npiinim nin Njoorim,” Uyudaan Uwonbɔr le len man, “Min wan be, nin wan nan be, nin wan yin dan, npɔɔn biɛn daan.”
Masiya a zii
9Min, Jɔnn wan ye ni nabig, wee ki ye ni kpiɛg ti fala-n nin ti naamin nin ti mɔril a nyiginimin nan ye ti yaan Yisa bu-n, wee ki nan be ligungonl lan be nnyum a sisiigin Patmosi-n Uwonbɔr a mɔleen bu nin maah ye Yisa a siɛra bu-n. 10Uyudaan a kpakɔɔl daal, n nan be nin Kinaaŋ le, le ki gbir likukɔl kaah tiɛn paab n bɔɔn ki nann kunaatuŋ, 11ki len ke, “Sɔb nan wee a kan nan ki ŋa kugbɔŋ kpabkaagin ki ta tan sei biwonjiɛm a laginn a kerim milile-n na: Ti ma ye Efesusi, nin Simarina, nin Pagamum, nin Tayatira, nin Sadusi, nin Filadelifiya nin Laodisiya.”
12Le n gbiɛ lig n bɔɔn ke n kan likukɔl lan pag ki tenn nim nmɔn. N-yonn man wee n labir n bɔɔn paamin, le n kan salima a filaam a tutɔɔnbol ilile kaah si, 13le filaam a tutɔɔnbol nmɔn uba nan be niin “ki nann uninfosaal a big”, ki yee daala kan fɔg ki tan piin u taabili bu le salima a changbam lol paan u gbingbanl bu. 14Le u yul nin u yukper peen ke tigunn nin, bee liŋunlin, le u num paam be ke nŋmipeen nin. 15U taai nan nann tukur tan wee bi ta pul nŋmi-n ke ti nyagin man nin le, le u kukɔl a fur nann nnyum puukaam. 16U nan ŋmag iŋmabil ilile le u nɔɔjiim, le takoobi kaaŋ kan jɔɔ imɔɔŋ ilee nyan u mɔnn. Le u num paam nyagin ke nwosisiigin nin.
17Maah nan kan u n-yonn man nin le n lu u ta tum ke utakpiirin. Le u ta u nɔɔjiim ki paan nbu ki len ke, “Laa san bijawaami. Min le ye Npiinim nin Njoorim. 18N ye Wan Fo-n le; N nan kpou, liga n fii nkumin na ki ye wan fo-n le hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm! Le ki ŋmag Nkum nin Kitakpiin tiŋ a naanganl a piin.
19“Mambu, sɔbim ŋaah kan nan na, nan be daandaan nan nin nan na yin ŋa ni bɔɔn. 20Ŋaah kan iŋmabil ilile yan n nɔɔjiim paamin nin salima a filaam a tutɔɔnbol ilile liwoolin nin a taai ye nan le: Iŋmabil ilile-n ye biwonjiɛm a laginn tilile-n a malakam le, le salima a filaam a tutɔɔnbol ilile-n mu ye biwonjiɛm a laginn tilile-n.

english_text:
The Letter to Ephesus
1This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Ephesus:
I am the one who holds the seven stars in my right hand, and I walk among the seven gold lampstands. Listen to what I say.
2I know everything you have done, including your hard work and how you have endured. I know you won't put up with anyone who is evil. When some people pretended to be apostles, you tested them and found out they were liars. 3You have endured and gone through hard times because of me, yet you have not given up.
4But I do have something against you! And it is this: You don't have as much love as you used to. 5Think about where you have fallen from, and then turn back and do as you did at first. If you don't turn back, I will come and take away your lampstand. 6But there is one thing you are doing right. You hate what the Nicolaitans are doing, and so do I.
7 If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. I will let everyone who wins the victory eat from the life-giving tree in God's wonderful garden.
The Letter to Smyrna
8 This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Smyrna:
I am the first and the last. I died, but now I am alive! Listen to what I say.
9I know how much you suffer and how poor you are, but you are rich. I also know the cruel things being said about you by people who claim to be God's people. But they are not really God's people. They are a group that belongs to Satan.
10Don't worry about what you will suffer. The devil will throw some of you into jail, and you will be tested and made to suffer for ten days. But if you are faithful until you die, I will reward you with a glorious life.
11 If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. Whoever wins the victory will not be hurt by the second death.
The Letter to Pergamum
12This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Pergamum:
I am the one who has the sharp double-edged sword! Listen to what I say.
13I know you live where Satan has his throne. But you have kept true to my name. Right there where Satan lives, my faithful witness Antipas was taken from you and put to death. Even then you did not give up your faith in me.
14 I do have a few things against you. Some of you are following the teaching of Balaam. Long ago he told Balak to teach the people of Israel to eat food that had been offered to idols and to be immoral. 15Now some of you are following the teaching of the Nicolaitans. 16Turn back! If you don't, I will come quickly and fight against these people. And my words will cut like a sword.
17 If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. To everyone who wins the victory, I will give some of the hidden food. I will also give each one a white stone with a new name written on it. No one will know that name except the one who is given the stone.
The Letter to Thyatira
18This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Thyatira:
I am the Son of God! My eyes are like flames of fire, and my feet are like bronze. Listen to what I say.
19I know everything about you, including your love, your faith, your service, and how you have endured. I know you are doing more now than you have ever done before. 20 But I still have something against you because of that woman Jezebel. She calls herself a prophet, and you let her teach and mislead my servants to do immoral things and to eat food offered to idols. 21I gave her a chance to turn from her sins, but she did not want to stop doing these immoral things.
22I am going to strike down Jezebel. Everyone who does these immoral things with her will also be punished, if they don't stop. 23 I will even kill her followers. Then all the churches will see that I know everyone's thoughts and feelings. I will treat each of you as you deserve.
24Some of you in Thyatira don't follow Jezebel's teaching. You don't know anything about what her followers call the “deep secrets of Satan.” So I won't burden you down with any other commands. 25But until I come, you must hold firmly to the teaching you have.
26 I will give power over the nations to everyone who wins the victory and keeps on obeying me until the end. 27-28I will give each of them the same power my Father has given me. They will rule the nations with an iron rod and smash those nations to pieces like clay pots. I will also give them the morning star.
29If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
translation_text:
Ntoon man chaa Efesusi yaab ban
1Le u beim ke, “Sɔb sei Efesusi a wonjiɛm a malaka ke:
Wan ŋmag iŋmabil ilile u nɔɔjiimin wee ki choon salima a filaam a tɔɔnbol ilile-n a mɔleen sɔ: 2N nyi ni ŋaar, ni nunman nin ni mɔril man. Ki ji nyi naah kaa ban bininfob ban a pooi to, mambu le ni nan mag ban nan ke bi ye itoon wee kaa sin ye-n ki biɛ baah ye tibɔkardam man. 3Ni jɔɔ limɔril le ki jin fala n yinl bu, amaa le naa bagi.
4Amaa nan bu wee n galin ni sɔ: Ni jiɛ-n ni chinchinn a jiɛmin nna. 5Ni tiɛrim naah nan nyan nan fɔg man wee ki nan lunn! Ni kpenn ni binbema wee ki li tun ke naah nan tun man chinchinn nin na. Ni ye naa kpenn ke, n li dan ki nan yuur ni salima a filaam a tutɔɔnbolin kisisibol. 6Amaa naah ŋaan nan wee ni ŋan sɔ: Ni nan titoonbir tan wee Nikolatan yaab tun ni, ke n baantɔɔl kaah kaa nan ti man nin le.
7Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man. Wan fir nyaŋ ke, n li sei u npaan wee un ji limiɛfol a siig a looi, yan be Uwonbɔr a kpaabin.”
Ntoon man chaa Simarina yaab ban
8Le u ji ke “Sɔb sei Simarina a wonjiɛm a malaka ke:
Wan ye Npiinim nin Njoorim, wan nan kpo wee ki ji fii nkumin nin a mɔleen sɔ. 9N nyi ni fala a jim bu nin naah ye faladam, amaa ni ye bijɔɔndam le! Ki nyi biba kaah jɔɔ kutingbiig ki bei ni ke bi ye Juu yaab le amaa kaa sin ye; amaa bi ye Sintani a wonjiɛndiig a ninfob le. 10Ni laa che bijawaam jɔɔ ni fala kan wee ni yin ji nbu. N bei ni le, Sintani li loon nim bibam tiloondirin ki mag ni, le nin che ni ji fala iweehn piig. Ni le li ŋmag ni yadau, hali ni le ye nkum ke ni, wee n nan sei ni limiɛfol a yuchigirig.
11Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man. Wan fir nyaŋ ke, waa li kan nkum man yin kpiɛ milee-n a daŋ kolibi.”
Ntoon man chaa Pagamum yaab ban
12Ki ji ke “Sɔb ki sei Pagamum a wonjiɛm a malaka ke:
Wan jɔɔ takoobi kaaŋ imɔɔŋ ilee-n a mɔleen sɔ. 13N nyi naah be nan yaan, nan yaan wee Sintani a naam a gbɔŋ be-n. Amaa le ni sin ŋmag n yinl nbamɔm. Naa ta naah ŋaam yada-n ki jaa, hali nin Antipasi a yonn nin wan nan ye n yada a siɛradaau ibamɔn nin, wee bi nan ku u ni tiŋin ni, Sintani a binbebolin.
14Ni biɛn yɔli, n jɔɔ tiwann wama nan che n galin ni: Ni jɔɔ bininfob biba be ni ban ki ŋmag Balaam a wɔɔmin, wan nan tinn Balag waah li ŋa man wee Iziral yaab n tun tibir ki ŋman tibawonann, ki li tun iwanchɔgin toon. 15Man le ni mu jɔɔ ban ŋmag Nikolatan yaab a wɔɔnim. 16Mambu ni kpenn ni binbem ma! Naa ye man ke, n li dan daandaan nan ki nan ta takoobi kan nyan n mɔbin nin ki kɔnn bi.
17Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man. Wan fir nyaŋ ke, n li sei u kulɔŋ a boroboro kan woo-n, wee bi yi ke maana-n. N mu ji li sei u litangbag penl lan wee liyinl pɔnl sɔb paan li bu, le wan gaa litangbagil nmɔn a binba le li nyi liyinl nmɔn a taai.”
Ntoon man chaa Tayatira yaab ban
18Ki ji ke “Sɔb sei Tayatira yaab a wonjiɛm a malaka ke:
Uwonbɔr a bija wan a numbili nann nŋmipeen wee u taafar nyagin ke kukurug kan nyagin nin a mɔleen sɔ. 19N nyi ni ŋaar, ni jiɛm ni yada, ni toon nin ni nnyiginim, le ni nin tun ki jon naah nan chinn ki tun man nin na.
20Ni biɛn yɔli, Nan wee n jɔɔ ki galin ni sɔ: Ni cheel tenn upii wan wee bi yi u ke Jezebiɛl, wee u yi uba ke ulinlenn nin. Upii nmɔn a wɔɔm che n toontum kɔɔ iwanchɔgin toon nin lipiibanlin nin lijabanlin nin tibawojiir a jimin. 21N sei u isaŋ ke un kpenn u wanchɔgin toon nmɔn na, amaa le waa ban man ni. 22Mambu n li che un dɔɔn nin iwiɛn, ki che ban dɔɔn nin win n ji fala takpem, man ke bi kpenn ki nyan upii nmɔn a binbemin. 23N li ku u buwaab. Le biwonjiɛm a laginn biɛn n biɛ ke min le ye wan dibir bininfob a sufu nin bi potiɛl, le n li yɔ ni biɛn ni ŋaar bu. 24Daandaan nan n bei nim ban gur be Tayatira, wee kaa nɔɔ upii nmɔn a wɔɔm wee kaa ji tinn Sintani kaah yi nan ke tibɔwoonkaarin (Maa yin ta litugil liba tun ni): 25Ni le li ŋmag nan wee ni jɔɔ-n hali nin maah na li dan.
26Wan fir nyaŋ ki tun maah ban man hali ki nan kpaa ndiɛm ke, n li sei u tininkper a pɔɔm wee un ŋmag ibol biɛn.
27‘U na li ta kukurug a jaangbiɛg le ki ŋmag dulinya yaab;
u li burbur bi ke tiyɔgirin’
a li ke maah gaa tininkper a pɔɔm n Baa ban man nin. 28N ji li sei u njakpanyiɛn a ŋmabil. 29Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man.”

english_text:
The Letter to Sardis
1This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Sardis:
I have the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. Listen to what I say.
I know what you are doing. Everyone may think you are alive, but you are dead. 2Wake up! You have only a little strength left, and it is almost gone. So try to become stronger. I have found that you are not completely obeying God. 3 Remember the teaching you were given and heard. Hold firmly to it and turn from your sins. If you don't wake up, I will come when you least expect it, just as a thief does.
4A few of you in Sardis have not dirtied your clothes with sin. You will walk with me in white clothes, because you are worthy. 5 Everyone who wins the victory will wear white clothes. Their names will not be erased from the book of life, and I will tell my Father and his angels that they are my followers.
6If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
The Letter to Philadelphia
7 This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Philadelphia:
I am the one who is holy and true, and I have the keys that belonged to David. When I open a door, no one can close it. And when I close a door, no one can open it. Listen to what I say.
8I know everything you have done. And I have placed before you an open door no one can close. You were not very strong, but you obeyed my message and did not deny you are my followers. 9 Now you will see what I will do with those people who belong to Satan's group. They claim to be God's people, but they are liars. I will make them come and kneel down at your feet. Then they will know that I love you.
10You obeyed my message and endured. So I will protect you from the time of testing everyone in all the world must go through. 11I am coming soon. So hold firmly to what you have, and no one will take away the crown you will be given as your reward.
12 Everyone who wins the victory will be made into a pillar in the temple of my God, and they will stay there forever. I will write on each of them the name of my God and the name of his city. It is the new Jerusalem my God will send down from heaven. I will also write on them my own new name.
13If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
The Letter to Laodicea
14 This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Laodicea:
I am the one called Amen! I am the faithful and true witness and the source of God's creation. Listen to what I say.
15I know everything you have done, and you are not cold or hot. I wish you were either one or the other. 16But since you are lukewarm and neither cold nor hot, I will spit you out of my mouth. 17You claim to be rich and successful and to have everything you need. But you don't know how bad off you really are. You are pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.
18Buy your gold from me. It has been refined in a fire, and it will make you rich. Buy white clothes from me. Wear them and you can cover up your shameful nakedness. Buy medicine for your eyes, so you will be able to see.
19 I correct and punish everyone I love. So make up your minds to turn away from your sins. 20Listen! I am standing and knocking at your door. If you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in and we will eat together. 21Everyone who wins the victory will sit with me on my throne, just as I won the victory and sat with my Father on his throne.
22If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
translation_text:
Ntoon man chaa Sadisi yaab ban
1Ki ji ke, “Sɔb sei Sadisi yaab a wonjiɛm a lagim a malaka ke:
Wan ŋmag Uwonbɔr a naam milile nin iŋmabil ilile-n a mɔleen sɔ. N nyi ni ŋaar kaah ye man; bininfob nyi ke ni fo le amaa ni kpou. 2Ni fii paaba! Wee ki pɔɔg nan gur ki ban nin kpe-n, nan bu-n maa kan ni ŋaar tan ŋan ki gbee Uwonbɔr a numi. 3Mambu, ni li tiɛr, nan wee ni gaa ki gbirin; ni chee sei tibɔr nmɔn na, wee ki kpenn ni binbema. Amaa ni ye naa fii paab ke, n li dan ke unaayig a dann nin, le naa yin nyi n-yonn man wee n yin dan ni.
4Amaa ni jɔɔ bininfob wama Sadisi ban kaa che bi wan yɔɔr gbarin niba. Min nin bi ma na yin lagin chonn ki yee tiwanpenn, nan bu-n bi kpaan nin man le. 5Wan fir nyaŋ ke u li yee tiwanpenn ke baah yee man nin. Maa li nyan udaan a yinl limiɛfol a gbɔŋin yaan ni, amaa le ki na li tiɛr u yinl n Baa nin U malakam a nintogil. 6Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man.”
Ntoon man chaa Filadelifiya yaab ban
7Ki ji ke, “Sɔb sei Filadelifiya a wonjiɛm a laguŋ a malaka:
Wan be kasi ki ye ubamɔndaan ki ŋmag Defid a naanganl a piimin a mɔleen sɔ. U loor nan ke uba kaa li fir loon ni, le nan mu wee u loon ke uba kaa be ki li fir loor ni. 8N nyi ni ŋaar kaah ye man. Ni lig, n loor ntisamɔn le ki sei ni le uba kaa li fir loon ntisamɔn nmɔn ni. N nyi naah jɔɔ npɔɔn wama, amaa ni biɛn yɔli ni ŋmag n mɔleen le kaa yii n yinli. 9N li ŋa ban be Sintani a jiɛndiigin, wee ki ke bi ye Juu yaab amaa wee kaa sin ye Juu yaabin, ki ye bilinlaribin, n li che bin dan ki nan gbaan ni taatum ki tiɛr ke n jiɛ ni. 10Naah nyigin wee ki jɔɔ limɔril ki ŋmag n siimin bu, n na li nyan ni limugil lan yin foon ki nan mag ban be dulinya nan yaan biɛn nin.
11N chaan le daandaan nan. Ni li ŋmag nan wee ni jɔɔ nna, wee uba laa nan fee ni naam a yuchigirigi. 12Wan nyaŋ ke, n li ŋa udaan Uwonbɔr a diig a jaantelig. Le waa ji li nya niin ni. N li sɔb n Wonbɔru a yinl nin n Wonbɔru a tiŋ kan ye Jerusalam pɔŋin ki paan u bu, kan yin nyan paab n Wonbɔru ban wee ki jiirin nin; le ki ji sɔb n mu a yin pɔnl ki paan u bu. 13Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man.”
Ntoon man chaa Laodisiya
14Le ki ji ke, “Sɔb ki sei Laodisiya a wonjiɛm a malaka ke:
Wan a yinl ye Ibamɔn nin, nin ibamɔn a yada a siɛradaan wee ki ŋmag nan biɛn wee Uwonbɔr naan nin a mɔleen sɔ. 15N nyi ni ŋaar kaah ye man, naa ton ni kaa ji sɔɔn ni. N bi ban ke ni li ye ban ton le bee ban sɔɔn! 16Ni bu, naah ton mala mala wee kaa ton kaa ji sɔɔn nin, n yin sii ni le n mɔn ki gab. 17Nim len le ke, ‘N ye uwandaan le; N ye wan jɔɔ le kaa ji ban niba.’ Amaa le kaa biɛ ke ni ye tikpachar le, ki jɔɔ kunyunyunbaag nin faladam ki ye bijɔɔm ban gaan nin ijakpalon. 18Mambu n kpaan ni le ke ni daam salima kan pul nŋmi-n wee ki mann nin n ban, wee ni ŋa biwandam; ki ji daa tiwann yɔɔr penn tan wee ni li yee, ki fir degin ni fai naah gaan nin bu; wee ki daa nnunkpam n ban ki li balig wee ki ga.
19Ban wee n jiɛ-n, bi ma le n fu bi bu ki dar bi tuli. Mambu ni ŋaam kinunmaŋ ki kpenn ni binbema. 20Min sɔ! N si ntisamɔn ki kpaar linaanganl. Ni ye wan gbir n kukɔl wee ki loor linaanganl ke, n li kɔɔ wee ki nan ji nin u, wee u mu nji nim.
21Wan fir ki nyaŋ ke, n li sei udaan nsan wee min nin uma n nan lagin ki kal n naangbɔŋin bu. A li ke maah nan nyaŋ wee min nin n Baa lagin ki kal U naangbɔŋ bu man nin. 22Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir, Kinaaŋ kaah bei biwonjiɛm a laginn man.”

english_text:
Worship in Heaven
1After this, I looked and saw a door that opened into heaven. Then the voice that had spoken to me at first and that sounded like a trumpet said, “Come up here! I will show you what must happen next.” 2 Right then the Spirit took control of me, and there in heaven I saw a throne and someone sitting on it. 3The one who was sitting there sparkled like precious stones of jasper and carnelian. A rainbow that looked like an emerald surrounded the throne.
4Twenty-four other thrones were in a circle around that throne. And on each of these thrones there was an elder dressed in white clothes and wearing a gold crown. 5 Flashes of lightning and roars of thunder came out from the throne in the center of the circle. Seven torches, which are the seven spirits of God, were burning in front of the throne. 6 Also in front of the throne was something that looked like a glass sea, clear as crystal.
Around the throne in the center were four living creatures covered front and back with eyes. 7The first creature was like a lion, the second one was like a bull, the third one had the face of a human, and the fourth was like a flying eagle. 8 Each of the four living creatures had six wings, and their bodies were covered with eyes. Day and night they never stopped singing,
“Holy, holy, holy is the Lord,
the all-powerful God,
who was and is
and is coming!”
9The living creatures kept praising, honoring, and thanking the one who sits on the throne and who lives forever and ever. 10At the same time the 24 elders knelt down before the one sitting on the throne. And as they worshiped the one who lives forever, they placed their crowns in front of the throne and said,
11 “Our Lord and God,
you are worthy
to receive glory,
honor, and power.
You created all things,
and by your decision they are
and were created.”
translation_text:
Paab a wonjiɛnl
1Ni bɔɔn bu le n nan lig, ki kan paab a naam a naanganl kaah loor ki yaa. Le likukɔl lan wee n pii nan chinn gbir wee li nann kunaatuŋin beim ke, “Donn do, wee n wɔɔniŋ nan kpaa talar ki na yin tun ni niɛ nan biɛn a bɔɔn.” 2Libol nmɔn n nan be nin Kinaaŋ le, ki kan kunaangbɔŋ kaah be paab le uba ka ki bu. 3Le wan nan ka ki bu nmɔn nan nyagin le ke sataŋ nin lichabilin. Le uwaakpajatooŋ nan jin kunaangbɔŋ nmɔn ki tan to litangbagil lan nann kisikpinnsiig. 4Le tinaangbann pilee nin tina nan gɔɔn kunaangbɔŋ nmɔn, le bininkpeeb pilee nin bina nan ka ti bu. Bi nan yee tiwann penn le ki chig salima a naam a yuchigirim bi yuli bu. 5Le kitajug nyagin ki nyan kunaangbɔŋ nmɔn yaan, nin utaal a dundunl nin titintann. Le filaam bilile si niin ki gaan. Ni niɛ nan le ye Uwonbɔr a naam milile. 6Le niwann niba mu nan be kunaangbɔŋ nmɔn a nintogil ki nann niɛnu a maar tan yaalin ke limɔgilin.
Niɛnu a maarin a sisiigin, kunaangbɔŋ nan be, le tiwann naan wann tan fo tina nan be ki gɔɔn ki. Le bi bɔɔn nin bi nintogil biɛn nan ye inunbil. 7Chinchinn a wanfolin nan nann ugbegin le, le wan kpiɛ milee mu nann unaaja, wan kpiɛ mitaa n mu a num nann uninfosaal, le wan kpiɛ bina-n mu nann libaanweenl lan yugiri paab. 8Tiwann naan wan tan fo tina nmɔn biɛn nan jɔɔ tikpinkpann tiloloob, le bi gbanann biɛn ye inunbil, hali nin bi ŋmiɛn nin na. Le nween nin kunyiɛg biɛn baa jiɛn ni le ki ke,
“Kasi, kasi, kasi,
le ye Uyudaan Uwonbɔr Npɔɔn biɛn daan,
wan nan be, ki la be, ki la yin dan.”
9Ni ye tiwann naan wan tan fo tina-n nan sei wan ka kunaangbɔŋ bu ki gbaa be kaa jɔɔ diɛmin kupag, jilima nin ipoor ke, 10bininkpeeb pilee nin bina-n lur wan ka kunaangbɔŋin bu n yaa taatum le, ki jiɛn uma wan be wee kaa jɔɔ diɛmin. Bi chigir bi naam a yuchigirim le bil kunaangbɔŋin yaan ki len ke:
11“Ti Yudaau Uwonbɔr, a sin kpaan,
a gaa kupag nin jilima nin npɔɔn na
nan bu-n fin le nan naan niwann biɛn,
a bam bu le bi nan naan niwann biɛn,
le ki fo be.”

english_text:
The Scroll and the Lamb
1 In the right hand of the one sitting on the throne I saw a scroll that had writing on the inside and on the outside. And it was sealed in seven places. 2I saw a mighty angel ask with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?” 3No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it.
4I cried hard because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it. 5 Then one of the elders said to me, “Stop crying and look! The one who is called both the ‘Lion from the Tribe of Judah’ and ‘King David's Great Descendant’ has won the victory. He will open the scroll and its seven seals.”
6 Then I looked and saw a Lamb standing in the center of the throne surrounded by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb looked as if it had once been killed. It had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God, sent out to all the earth.
7The Lamb went over and took the scroll from the right hand of the one who sat on the throne. 8 After he had taken it, the four living creatures and the 24 elders knelt down before him. Each of them had a harp and a gold bowl full of incense, which are the prayers of God's people. 9 Then they sang a new song,
“You are worthy
to receive the scroll
and open its seals,
because you were killed.
And with your own blood
you bought for God
people from every tribe,
language, nation, and race.
10 You let them become kings
and serve God as priests,
and they will rule on earth.”
11 As I looked, I heard the voices of a large number of angels around the throne and the voices of the living creatures and of the elders. There were millions and millions of them, 12and they were saying in a loud voice,
“The Lamb who was killed
is worthy to receive power,
riches, wisdom, strength,
honor, glory, and praise.”
13Then I heard all beings in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and in the sea offer praise. Together, all of them were saying,
“Praise, honor, glory,
and strength
forever and ever
to the one who sits
on the throne
and to the Lamb!”
14The four living creatures said “Amen,” while the elders knelt down and worshiped.
translation_text:
Kugbɔŋ kpabkaag nin Kipeebig a bɔr
1Le n kan wan ka kunaangbɔŋin bu kaah ŋmag kugbɔŋ kpabkaag u nɔɔjiim, le kugbɔŋ nmɔn jɔɔ nsɔbim ku bɔɔn nin ku nintogil, le bi ta tiwann tan tabin tilile ki tabin piin ku bu. 2Le n kan malaka wan jɔɔ npɔɔn takpem kaah tann papaab takpem ki len ke, “Ŋma kpaan ki li fir tabir tiwann tabin wan nan wee ki loor kugbɔŋ kpabkaag nmɔn naa?” 3Amaa uba kaa nan be paab a naamin bee dulinya nan yaan bee kitakpiin tiŋ ki na li fir loor kugbɔŋ kpabkaag nmɔn bee ki lig ku poolin ni. 4Le n mɔɔ ki mɔɔ nan bu-n uba kaa nan be ki kpaan un loor kugbɔŋ kpabkaag nmɔn bee ki lig ku poolin ni. 5Le bininkpeebin a ni uba beim ke, “Laa mɔri! Lig, wan ye ligbeginl wee ki nyan Juda a maalimin nin, ki ye Defid a yaabilin, u nyaŋ niwann biɛn na. U li fir tabir ndaagim mulile-n ki loor kugbɔŋ kpabkaag nmɔn.”
6Le n kan Kipeebig, le ki nann ke bi kɔr ki le-n, le ki si Kunaangbɔŋin a sisiigin, le tiwann naan wann tan fo tina-n nin bininkpeebin gɔɔn u. Kipeebig nmɔn nan jɔɔ iyinh ilile le nin inunbil ilile, ni ma nan ye Uwonbɔr a naam milile ban wee u nan tun bi dulinya nan a logi ina-n yaan biɛn ni. 7Le u dan ki nan gaa kugbɔŋ kpabkaag nmɔn wan ka kunaangbɔŋin bu a nɔɔjiimin ban. 8Waah nan gaa kugbɔŋ nmɔn ki diɛ-n, le tiwann naan wann tan fo tina-n nin bininkpeeb pilee nin bina-n sɔɔn tum Kipeebig nmɔn a nintogil. Bi biɛn nan jɔɔ tibiɛr le nin salima a yir, le nnyɔgkusim gbee bi sam nmɔn yaan, ki ye Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaabin a wonmiɛl. 9Le bi gaah ilan pɔɔn ki ke,
“Fin le kpaan nin a yuur kugbɔŋ nmɔn
ki loor ndaagimin,
nan bu-n fin le bi nan kɔr,
le a ta a cham ki da bininfob ki sei Uwonbɔr
ki nyan imaal biɛn nin ileen biɛn, nin bininfob biɛn nin ibol biɛn ni.
10Le a jin bi nnaam, ki ta bi ŋa biminmanib ke bi li jiɛn ti Wonbɔru,
le bi na li kal kunaangbɔŋin bu.”
11Le n lig ki gbir malakam takpem a kukɔli, le bi kanl ye turil turil, nin turpiig a turpiig. Le malakam nmɔn nan gɔɔn kunaangbɔŋin nin tiwann naan wann tan fo tina-n nin bininkpeebin. 12Ki gaah ilan nin ikukɔl yan pɔɔ ki ke,
“Kipeebig kan wee bi nan kɔrin le kpaan,
nin un gaa npɔɔn nin lifaal, nin nlamgɔrikaam, nin ngbananpɔɔn,
nin jilima nin kupag nin ndom!”
13Le n gbir nan biɛn wee Uwonbɔr nan naan, wee ni be paab, nin kutingbɔŋ nan yaan, nin kitakpiin tiŋ nin nan be nnyumin, nin nan biɛn be i yaan, kaah gaah ilan ki ke,
“Ndom nin jilima nin kupag nin npɔɔn li be wan ka
kunaangbɔŋin bu nin Kipeebigin bu,
hali nin isaŋ yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.”
14Le tiwann naan wann tan fo tina-n len ke, “Ibamɔn” le bininkpeebin sɔɔn tum ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr.

english_text:
Opening the Seven Seals
1At the same time I saw the Lamb open the first of the seven seals, I heard one of the four living creatures shout with a voice like thunder. It said, “Come out!” 2 Then I saw a white horse. Its rider carried a bow and was given a crown. He had already won some victories, and he went out to win more.
3When the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come out!” 4 Then another horse came out. It was fiery red. And its rider was given the power to take away all peace from the earth, so people would slaughter one another. He was also given a big sword.
5 When the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come out!” Then I saw a black horse, and its rider had a balance scale in one hand. 6I heard what sounded like a voice from somewhere among the four living creatures. It said, “A liter of wheat will cost you a whole day's wages! Three liters of barley will cost you a day's wages too. But don't ruin the olive oil or the wine.”
7When the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come out!” 8 Then I saw a pale green horse. Its rider was named Death, and Death's Kingdom followed close behind. They were given power over one fourth of the earth, and they could kill its people with swords, famines, diseases, and wild animals.
9When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of everyone who had been killed for speaking God's message and telling about their faith. 10They shouted, “Master, you are holy and faithful! How long will it be before you judge and punish the people of this earth who killed us?”
11 Then each of those who had been killed was given a white robe and told to rest for a little while. They had to wait until the complete number of the Lord's other servants and followers would be killed.
12 When I saw the Lamb open the sixth seal, I looked and saw a great earthquake. The sun turned as dark as sackcloth, and the moon became red as blood. 13 The stars in the sky fell to earth, just like figs shaken loose by a windstorm. 14 Then the sky was rolled up like a scroll, and all mountains and islands were moved from their places.
15 The kings of the earth, its famous people, and its military leaders hid in caves or behind rocks on the mountains. They hid there together with the rich and the powerful and with all the slaves and free people. 16 Then they shouted to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us! Hide us from the one who sits on the throne and from the anger of the Lamb. 17 That terrible day has come! God and the Lamb will show their anger, and who can face it?”
translation_text:
Tiwann tabin wann a bɔr
1Le n kan Kipeebigin kaah tabir chinchinn a wan tabin waŋ mulile-n a poolin. Le n gbir tiwann naan wann tan fo tina-n a ni uba a kukɔl kaah tann papaab ke utaalin ki ke, “Dan!” 2Le n nan lig ki kan utanpeen n nintogil! Le wan jig utaan nmɔn ŋmag butɔm, le bi sei u nnaam a yuchigirig, le u nyan ke unyaŋirin ki sin bon un nyaŋ.
3N-yonn man wee Kipeebigin tabir kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ milee-n, le n gbir tiwann naan wann tan fo wan kpiɛ milee-n kaah len ke, “Dan!” 4Le utaan uba ji nyan ki ye utanman. Le wan jig utaan nmɔn nan gaa npɔɔn ke un choo nposɔɔn nyan dulinya nan yaan, ki che bininfob n kɔr tab. Bi nan ta takoobi takpeŋ le ki sei u.
5N-yonn man wee Kipeebigin tabir kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ mitaa-n, le n gbir kuwan naan waŋ kan fo ki kpiɛ mitaa-n kaah len ke, “Dan!” Le n lig, ki kan utanbɔn n nintogil! Wan nan jig utaan nmɔn nan ŋmag nan wee bi jɔɔ magir tiwann yɔɔrin tilee le u nɔɔn. 6Le n gbir tifur tiba le ti nann likukɔl ki nyan tiwann naan wann tan fo tina nmɔn a sisiigin ki len ke, “Iyoo a kuliba kuba ye utoontunn a ween nba a yɔr le, ikɔɔn mu a kuliba itaa mu ye utoontunn a ween nba a yɔr, amaa laa bii nkpam nin ndaami!”
7N-yonn man wee Kipeebigin tabir kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ mina-n, le n gbir kuwan naan waŋ kan fo ki kpiɛ mina-n a kukɔl kaah len ke, “Dan!” 8Le n lig ki kan utanpeen lalag! Le wan jig utaan nmɔn a yinl ye Nkum, le Kitakpiin tiŋ yaab nɔɔ u bɔɔn ki mal u. Le Uwonbɔr sei bi npɔɔn ke bin ku dulinya nan a ninfob nbɔgirim mina a poolin nkerim nbau, ke bin ta takoobi, nin nkom, nin iwiɛn, nin dulinya nan a wan bir ki ku bi.
9Waah nan tabir kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ miŋmu-n, le n kan ban wee bi nan kɔrin a tinnaam kumanug a binbinlin a nyagilin, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr a mɔleen nin siɛra kan wee bi nan ŋmagin. 10Le bi nan yin nin nkukɔpɔɔn ki ke, “Uyudaan wan jɔɔ npɔɔn biɛn, fin wan ye kasi nin ubamɔndaan, ni yin yuur ki tan kpaan niin a tarig wee a ji dulinya nan yaab tibɔr ki jiin ti cham a pɔnlaa?” 11Le bi nan sei bi biɛn daalapeen fufɔbir, ki bei bi ke bin guur wamau hali nin bitoontum tab nin bi nabum ban wee bi na yin ku ke baah nan ku bi miɛnin man nin a kanlin nan foo.
12Le n lig ki kan waah tabir kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ miloobin. Le kutingbɔŋ dam takpem. Nween labir libunbɔnl ki nann botu a kinkenl lan wee bi ta tiŋɔɔkor ki naan nin, le uŋmal mu mann ke nchamin, 13le iŋmabil nyan titilangbann nin ki nan lu tum, a li ke ntafapɔɔrim kaah ti ŋa ke mi daar bikinkam a sub wee iloonkal ker lur man nin. 14Le kitilangbɔŋ kpab kpab ke kugbɔŋ kpabkaagin, le ijɔɔ nin igungon yan be nnyum a sisiigin fɔɔr i sisibol.
15Le dulinya a bɔrtiib, nin nbɔrbum, nin bitɔtogib a sanliib, nin biwandam, nin ininfojal, nin biyom biɛn nin ban kaa ye biyom woo titangbafiɛrin nin titanpirin. 16Le bi yin ijɔɔ nin titanpirin ki len ke, “Ni lu ti bu ki woon ti ni wee wan ka kunaangbɔŋin bu-n laa ji kan ti, wee Kipeebigin mu a ŋuufiiŋin laa pii ti! 17Nan bu-n, bi ŋuul a fiim a daal takpenl nmɔn foon na, ke ŋma li fir siraa?”

english_text:
The 144,000 Are Marked for God
1-2 After this I saw four angels. Each one was standing on one of the earth's four corners. The angels held back the four winds, so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree. These angels had also been given the power to harm the earth and the sea. Then I saw another angel come up from where the sun rises in the east, and he was ready to put the mark of the living God on people. He shouted to the four angels, 3 “Don't harm the earth or the sea or any tree! Wait until I have marked the foreheads of the servants of our God.”
4Then I heard how many people had been marked on the forehead. There were 144,000, and they came from every tribe of Israel:
512,000 from Judah,
12,000 from Reuben,
12,000 from Gad,
612,000 from Asher,
12,000 from Naphtali,
12,000 from Manasseh,
712,000 from Simeon,
12,000 from Levi,
12,000 from Issachar,
812,000 from Zebulun,
12,000 from Joseph, and
12,000 from Benjamin.
People from Every Nation
9 After this, I saw a large crowd with more people than could be counted. They were from every race, tribe, nation, and language, and they stood before the throne and before the Lamb. They wore white robes and held palm branches in their hands, 10as they shouted,
“Our God, who sits
upon the throne,
has the power
to save his people,
and so does the Lamb.”
11The angels who stood around the throne knelt in front of it with their faces to the ground. The elders and the four living creatures knelt there with them. Then they all worshiped God 12and said,
“Amen! Praise, glory, wisdom,
thanks, honor, power,
and strength belong to our God
forever and ever! Amen!”
13One of the elders asked me, “Do you know who these people are that are dressed in white robes? Do you know where they come from?”
14 “Sir,” I answered, “you must know.”
Then he told me:
“These are the ones
who have gone through
the great suffering.
They have washed their robes
in the blood of the Lamb
and have made them white.
15And so they stand
before the throne of God
and worship him in his temple
day and night.
The one who sits on the throne
will spread his tent
over them.
16 They will never hunger
or thirst again,
and they won't be troubled
by the sun
or any scorching heat.
17 “The Lamb in the center
of the throne
will be their shepherd.
He will lead them to streams
of life-giving water,
and God will wipe all tears
from their eyes.”
translation_text:
Iziral yaab turikobig nin turpina nin turina (144,000) a bɔr
1Ni bɔɔn bu le n kan malakam bina kaah si dulinya nan a logi ina-n yaan ki choo nfaam man nyan ilog ina-n nin ŋmag ke mi laa daar kɔɔ kutingbɔŋin ni bee limɔgilin ni bee ki daar busub bu. 2Le n ji kan malaka uba le u nyan liwonpɔɔnl paam ki ŋmag Uwonbɔr wan fo-n a wann tabin wann. Le u yin nin nkukɔpɔɔn ki bei malakam bina ban wee bi sei bi npɔɔn ke bin sei kutingbɔŋ nin limɔgilin kidaŋin ke: 3“Ni laa sei kutingbɔŋ bee limɔgil bee isiig kidaŋi, hali nin taah na li ta tiwann tabin wann ki tabin ti Wonbɔru a toontum a yutun bu.” 4Le n nan gbir baah tabin ibol yan biɛn nyan Iziral a kanlin: Le bi kanl nmɔn nan ye turikobig nin turpina nin turina, ibol yan biɛn nyan Iziral.
5Juda a mɔfiigin bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin bi,
le Rubenn a mɔfiigin bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Gad a mɔfiigin bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
6Aser a mɔfiigin bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Nafitali a mɔfiigin bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Manaasa a mɔfiigin bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
7le Simiɛn a mɔfiigin, bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Liifai a mɔfiigin, bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Isakar a mɔfiigin, bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
8le Zebulun a mɔfiigin, bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Josef a mɔfiigin, bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
le Bɛnjamɛnn a mɔfiigin, bininfob turpiig nin turilee le bi nan tabin,
Kuninfogbaluŋ a bɔr
9Ni bɔɔn bu le n lig ki kan kuninfogbaluŋ n nintogil ban wee uba kaa li fir kan bi kanli, bi nan nyan ininfobool, nin imaal, nin bininfob, nin ileen biɛn nin le, ki si kunaangbɔŋin ban Kipeebigin a nintogil. Bi nan yee tiwanpenn le ki ŋmag tikpikpagbann bi nɔɔn. 10Le bi mɔɔ nin nkukɔpɔɔn ki ke:
“Feegab ye Uwonbɔr yaan le,
wan ka kunaangbɔŋ bu-n,
ki ji ye Kipeebigin yaan le.”
11Malakam biɛn nan si le ki gɔɔn kunaangbɔŋin, nin bininkpeebin nin tiwann naan wann tan fo tina-n. Le bi nan lu ki ta bi num chigin tum kunaangbɔŋin a nintogil ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr 12ki ke:
“Ibamɔn!
Ndom nin kupag,
nin nlamgɔrikaam nin kunɔɔpoog nin jilima
nin npɔɔn nin ngbananpɔɔn
ye ti Wonbɔru yaan le hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi.
Ibamɔn!”
13Le bininkpeebin a ni uba baanim ke, “Ban yee tiwanpenn nan ye ŋmam maa, bee bi nyan laa?”
14Le n jiin ke, “N yudaau, fin le nyi.”
Le u len ke, “Bi ma ye ban nyann limug takpenl a poolin; ki ye ban wee bi ta Kipeebigin a cham ki ŋunn biwan yɔɔr le ti nin peen. 15Mambu,
“Bi be Uwonbɔr a naangbɔŋin a nintogil le
ki tun tenn Uwonbɔr nween nin kunyiɛg u wonjiɛndiigin;
le wan ka kunaangbɔŋ bu-n li nyann u nanboŋin ki piin bi bu.
16Nkom kaa ji li choo bi;
nnyunyum kaa ji li choo bi,
nween mu kaa li faa bi,
bee nan ton biɛn nin.
17Nan bu-n Kipeebig kan ka kunaangbɔŋ bu ki be bi sisiigin nin, le yin ye bi peekpaaru;
u li ta bi ki jo limiɛfol a nyunbuŋin.
Le Uwonbɔr li pir bi num a nyinyinn biɛn.”

english_text:
The Seventh Seal Is Opened
1When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. 2I noticed that the seven angels who stood before God were each given a trumpet.
3 Another angel, who had a gold container for incense, came and stood at the altar. This one was given a lot of incense to offer with the prayers of God's people on the gold altar in front of the throne. 4Then the smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of God's people, went up to God from the hand of the angel.
5 After this, the angel filled the incense container with fire from the altar and threw it on the earth. Thunder roared, lightning flashed, and the earth shook.
The Trumpets
6 The seven angels now got ready to blow their trumpets.
7 When the first angel blew his trumpet, hail and fire mixed with blood were thrown down on the earth. A third of the earth, a third of the trees, and a third of all green plants were burned.
8When the second angel blew his trumpet, something like a great fiery mountain was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned to blood, 9a third of the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
10 When the third angel blew his trumpet, a great star fell from heaven. It was burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on a third of the springs of water. 11 The name of the star was Bitter, and a third of the water turned bitter. Many people died because the water was so bitter.
12 When the fourth angel blew his trumpet, a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck. They each lost a third of their light. So during a third of the day there was no light, and a third of the night was also without light.
13Then I looked and saw a lone eagle flying across the sky. It was shouting, “Trouble, trouble, trouble to everyone who lives on earth! The other three angels are now going to blow their trumpets.”
translation_text:
Kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ milile
1N-yonn man wee u nan tabir kuwan tabin waŋ kan kpiɛ milile-n, le paab nan ŋmin chii ki tan kpaa minti pita. 2Le n nan kan malakam bilile-n kaah si Uwonbɔr a nintogil, le Uwonbɔr sei bi tinaatunn tilile.
3Le malaka uba nan ŋmag nnyɔgkusim a salima a saŋ ki tan sir kumanug a binbinl ban. Le bi sei u nnyɔgkusim takpem ke un kpiɛ Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaabin bu bi wonmiɛlin, le u ta paan salima a binbinlin bu kunaangbɔŋin a nintogil. 4Le nnyɔgkusimin a kpinnyir, nin Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab a miɛm nyan malaka nan a nɔɔn ki don paab. 5Le malaka nmɔn yuur kisaŋin, ki mɔɔn nŋmi kumanug a binbinlin ki gbeen kisaŋin, ki kpaar yaal kutingbɔŋ bu; le utaal dun ki tann ki nyagin le kutingbɔŋ dam.
Tinaatunn a bɔr
6Le malaka bilile ban ŋmag tinaatunn tilile-n ŋa sili ke bin pee bi naatunn nmɔn.
7Le chinchinn a malaka pee u naatuŋ, le itanyunbɔl nin nŋmi ŋmarin nin ncham ki lunn kutingbɔŋ nan bu. Le kutingbɔŋ bɔgir nkerim mitaa le nkerim nba gaa nŋmi, le isiig bɔgir nkerim mitaa le nkerim nba gaa nŋmi, le timɔsɔɔn biɛn gaa nŋmi.
8Le malaka wan kpiɛ milee mu pee u naatuŋ, le niwann niba nann lijɔɔl takpenl le nŋmi gaan li bu, le bi ta li ki gab limɔgilin. Limɔgil nmɔn a bɔgirim mitaa le nkerim nba nan kpann ncham, 9le limɔgil nmɔn a wanfoli a bɔgirim mitaa, le nkerim nba kpo, le tiŋalin a bɔgirim mitaa, le nkerim nba bii.
10Le malaka wan kpiɛ mitaa-n mu pee u naatuŋ, le liŋmabijal lan yab ki ween ke limumɔl a ŋmiimin nyan kitilangbɔŋ bu ki nan lu ikpen nin nnyunbum a bɔgirim mitaa-n a kerim nba ni, 11liŋmabil nmɔn a yinl le nan ye Kpajarig. Le nnyum nmɔn a bɔgirim mitaa-n a kerim nba kpann kunyuntuntoŋ, le kunyuntuntoŋ nmɔn nan ku bininfob takpem.
12Le malaka wan kpiɛ mina-n mu pee u naatuŋ, le bi faa nween nin uŋmal nin iŋmabil biɛn le bi wonweem a bɔgirim nkerim mitataa a kerim nbaba bɔŋ. Lidaal a bɔgirim a kerim mitaa, nkerim nba kaa nan jɔɔ nwonween ni, kunyiɛg mu a bɔgirim a kerim mitaa-n, nkerim nba mu nan ye man le.
13Iyaayoo le n lig, ki gbir libaanweenl kaah be paab ki laan ki mɔr nkukɔpɔɔn ki ke: “Ni li bir! Ni li bir! Ni li bir ki sei dulinya, nan bu-n malakam bita ban gur wee ki la yin pee bi naatunn nbu!”

english_text:
1When the fifth angel blew his trumpet, I saw a star fall from the sky to earth. It was given the key to the tunnel that leads down to the deep pit. 2 As it opened the tunnel, smoke poured out like the smoke of a great furnace. The sun and the air turned dark because of the smoke. 3 Locusts came out of the smoke and covered the earth. They were given the same power that scorpions have.
4 The locusts were told not to harm the grass on the earth or any plant or any tree. They were to punish only those people who did not have God's mark on their foreheads. 5The locusts were allowed to make them suffer for five months, but not to kill them. The suffering they caused was like the sting of a scorpion. 6 In those days people will want to die, but they will not be able to. They will hope for death, but it will escape from them.
7 These locusts looked like horses ready for battle. On their heads they wore something like gold crowns, and they had human faces. 8 Their hair was like a woman's long hair, and their teeth were like those of a lion. 9 On their chests they wore armor made of iron. Their wings roared like an army of horse-drawn chariots rushing into battle. 10Their tails were like a scorpion's tail with a stinger that had the power to hurt someone for five months. 11Their king was the angel in charge of the deep pit. In Hebrew his name was Abaddon, and in Greek it was Apollyon.
12The first horrible thing has now happened! But wait. Two more horrible things will happen soon.
13 Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet. I heard a voice speak from the four corners of the gold altar that stands in the presence of God. 14The voice spoke to this angel and said, “Release the four angels who are tied up beside the great Euphrates River.” 15The four angels had been prepared for this very hour and day and month and year. Now they were set free to kill a third of all people.
16By listening, I could tell there were more than 200,000,000 war horses. 17 In my vision their riders wore fiery-red, dark-blue, and yellow armor on their chests. The heads of the horses looked like lions, with fire and smoke and sulfur coming out of their mouths. 18One third of all people were killed by the three terrible troubles caused by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur. 19The horses had powerful mouths, and their tails were like poisonous snakes that bite and hurt.
20 The people who lived through these terrible troubles did not turn away from the idols they had made, and they did not stop worshiping demons. They kept on worshiping idols that were made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood. Not one of these idols could see, hear, or walk. 21No one stopped murdering or practicing witchcraft or being immoral or stealing.
translation_text:
1Le malaka wan kpiɛ miŋmu mu pee u naatuŋ, le n kan liŋmabil kaah nyan kitilangbɔŋ bu ki nan lu tum. Le bi sei liŋmabilin libogil lan nyɔɔ kaa jɔɔ tarig nmɔn a piim. 2N-yonn man wee u loor libogil lan nyɔɔ kaa jɔɔ tarigin, le tikpinnyir nyan niin ki nann nŋmi takpen a kpinnyir, le tikpinnyir nmɔn nan bɔŋ nween nin titilangbann. 3Le itɔɔn nan nyan tikpinnyir nmɔn yaan ki lunn tum, le Uwonbɔr sei bi npɔɔn ke inɔɔn kaah jɔɔ npɔɔn man dulinya nan yaan nin. 4Uwonbɔr nan bei bi ke bi laa sei dulinya nan a mɔɔr bee tiwann bu wan bee isiigi kidaŋi, amaa bin sei bininfob ban kaa jɔɔ Uwonbɔr a daagim bi yutun bu-n a binba. 5Uwonbɔr kaa nan sei bi npɔɔn ke bin ku bininfobi, amaa ke bin mugir bi ki tan kpaa iŋmal iŋmu. Ntiton man wu ke unɔɔn kaah jun uninfo ke ni wu man nin. 6Iyaayoo bininfob na li ban nkum, amaa le kaa li kan ni; bi na li ban bin kpo amaa le nkum na li guun ki jiɛn bi.
7Itɔɔn nmɔn nan nann itaan yan wee bi ŋai bitɔb a sili-n le. Bi nan chig niba bi yuli bu le ni nann salima a naam a yuchigirig, le bi num paam nann bininfosaalib a num paam. 8Bi kor nan nann bipiib a yukper le, le bi nyin mu nann igbegin a nyin. 9Bi nan jɔɔ ngbingban tegirim man nann tikur a gbingban tegirim le, le bi kpinkpann fu ke itaan takpem kaah dar torokom ki chaa bitɔb a tom ke ni fu man nin le. 10Bi jɔɔ ijoo le ki junn ke inɔɔn nin, bi jɔɔ npɔɔn bi jo-i nmɔn yaan ki li fir mugir bininfob iŋmal iŋmu. 11Bi nan jɔɔ wan ye ubɔr le u ye libogil nmɔn yaan a malaka, ki ye ubiir.
12Chinchinn a nan bir ma jon na; nan bir milee la chaan.
13Le malaka wan kpiɛ miloob mu pee u naatuŋ, le n gbir likukɔl liba nyan salima a binbinlin lan be Uwonbɔr a nintogilin. 14Le likukɔl nmɔn bei malaka wan kpiɛ miloob ki jɔɔ kunaatuŋin ke, “Lor malakam bina ban wee bi lol bi nkpen takpen man wee bi yi ke Yufiratiisi n yaan ki jaau.” 15Le u nan lor malakam ban pii nan ŋa sili ki guu isaŋ, nin lidaal, nin li ŋmalu, nin libinl nmɔn ke bin ku bininfob a bɔgirim nkerim mitaa a kerim nba-n. 16Le n gbir bitɔtogib ban jig itaan nin a kanl, le bi kanl nan ye tur a tur a kobilee. N gbir bi kanl la.
17Maah nan kan itaan nin bitanjigib nmɔn nin, n zii ni, ni nan nann nan le: Bitanjigibin nan jɔɔ bigbingban tegirim man man ke nŋmi-n, ki be ke buginu, ki ye nduuyom a li ke lichibilin. Le itaan nin a yuli nann igbegin a yuli, le nŋmi nin tikpinnyir nin lichibil nyan bi mɔɔŋin ni. 18Le imag itaa yan ye nŋmi nin tikpinnyir nin lichibil yan nyan itaan a mɔɔŋi ni nan ku bininfob a bɔgirim nkerim mitaa a kerim nba. 19Itaan nin a pɔɔm nan be bi mɔɔŋin nin bi joi ni le, nan bu-n bi joi nan nann iwaa le, ki jɔɔ iyul, le bi jɔɔ junn bininfob.
20Le bininfob ban gur wee imag nan kaa ku bi nan, kaa nan chee ke bin kpenn ki ta bitɔɔl kaah maa nan nin ki gabi, baa nan ta npɔniim a jiɛnim ki jiɛn ni, nin ibawol yan wee bi ta salima ki maa i, nin salima nin tikur ninann nin tikurdiin nin itangbag nin tidaar, kaa chee bin ta bi bawoli yan kaa gaa bee kaa gbiri bee kaa choon nin gabi. 21Le kaa chee kpenn bi binben ki jiɛn lininfokuli, nin inyɔg a toon, nin iwanchɔgin toon, nin nnaayigimin.

english_text:
The Angel and the Little Scroll
1I saw another powerful angel come down from heaven. This one was covered with a cloud, and a rainbow was over his head. His face was like the sun, his legs were like columns of fire, 2and with his hand he held a little scroll that had been unrolled. He stood there with his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land. 3Then he shouted with a voice that sounded like a growling lion. Thunder roared seven times.
4After the thunder stopped, I was about to write what it had said. But a voice from heaven shouted, “Keep it secret! Don't write these things.”
5 The angel I had seen standing on the sea and the land then held his right hand up toward heaven. 6He made a promise in the name of God who lives forever and who created heaven, earth, the sea, and every living creature. The angel said, “You won't have to wait any longer. 7God told his secret plans to his servants the prophets, and it will all happen by the time the seventh angel sounds his trumpet.”
8 Once again the voice from heaven spoke to me. It said, “Go and take the open scroll from the hand of the angel standing on the sea and the land.”
9When I went over to ask the angel for the little scroll, the angel said, “Take the scroll and eat it! Your stomach will turn sour, but the taste in your mouth will be sweet as honey.” 10I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it. The taste was sweet as honey, but my stomach turned sour.
11Then some voices said, “Keep on telling what will happen to the people of many nations, races, and languages, and also to kings.”
translation_text:
Malaka nin kigbanbig kpabkaag a bɔr
1Le n ji kan malaka takpeŋ uba kaah nyan paab ki chaa jiirin. U nan yee kitilangbɔŋ le ke likinkenlin, le uwaakpajatooŋ be u yul a paab; le u num paam nann nween, le u taai mu nann nŋmipeen. 2U nan ŋmag kigbanbig kpabkaag le, le ki kpar ki be u nɔɔn, le u ta u nɔɔjiim a taal ki siin limɔgilin, le u nɔɔgam a taal mu si limɔgil nmɔn a dool. 3Le u tiɛn paab takpem ke ugbegin nin. Waah tiɛn man ki diɛ, le utaal a tintann a kukɔli nkerim milile-n pag. 4Utaal a tiɛm kerim milile nmɔn kaah pag ki diɛ, le n ŋa sili ke n sɔb; amaa le n ji gbir likukɔl liba nyan paab ki len ke, “Li ŋmag utaal kaah tiɛn nkerim milile man nin a sufu-n na, wee ki laa sɔb ti ki bili.”
5Le n kan malaka wan a taaliba tɔɔ limɔgil a nyum bu wee litɔ mu tɔɔ limɔgil a doolin kaah don u nɔɔjiim paab. 6Le u poo Uwonbɔr wan be ki le gbaa be-n ke, wan nan naan paab nin nan biɛn be bi ni, nin dulinya nin nan biɛn be dulinya ni, nin limɔgil nin nan biɛn be limɔgilin ki len ke, “Nguurim kaa ji be! 7Amaa idaa yan wee malaka wan kpiɛ bilile-n na yin pee u naatuŋ ke, Uwonbɔr a wool a bɔr li gbee, a li ke waah nan bei u toontum bilinlemin man nin.”
8Le likukɔl lan wee n bi gbir wee li nyan paabin ji beim ke, “Li chaa, ki tan gaa kugbɔŋ kpabkaag kan kpar ki be malaka a nɔɔn wee u tɔɔ nyum nin limɔgil a dool bu-n.”
9Le n jon malaka nban ki tan bei u ke un ta kigbanbig kpabkaag nmɔn ki seim ni. Le u beim ke, “Gaa ki ki ŋman na. Ni yin mɔ a mɔnn le ke tiseerin, amaa le ki mɔŋ a poolin.” 10Le n gaa kigbanbig kpabkaag nmɔn u nɔɔn ki ŋman. Le ki sin mɔ n mɔnn ke tiseerin, amaa maah nan ŋman diɛ le ki mɔŋ n poolin. 11Le bi nan beim ke, “Ni kpaa le nin a pag ilinlen leen ki jiin bininfob, nin ibol, nin ileen balbal, nin bibɔrtiib paam takpem.”

english_text:
The Two Witnesses
1 An angel gave me a measuring stick and said:
Measure around God's temple. Be sure to include the altar and everyone worshiping there. 2 But don't measure the courtyard outside the temple building. Leave it out. It has been given to those people who don't know God, and they will trample all over the holy city for 42 months. 3My two witnesses will wear sackcloth, while I let them preach for 1,260 days.
4 These two witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand in the presence of the Lord who rules the earth. 5Any enemy who tries to harm them will be destroyed by the fire that comes out of their mouths. 6 They have the power to lock up the sky and to keep rain from falling while they are prophesying. And whenever they want to, they can turn water to blood and cause all kinds of terrible troubles on earth.
7 After the two witnesses have finished preaching God's message, the beast that lives in the deep pit will come up and fight against them. It will win the battle and kill them. 8 Their bodies will be left lying in the streets of the same great city where their Lord was nailed to a cross. And this city is spiritually like the city of Sodom or the country of Egypt.
9For three and a half days the people of every nation, tribe, language, and race will stare at the bodies of these two witnesses and refuse to let them be buried. 10Everyone on earth will celebrate and be happy. They will give gifts to each other, because of what happened to the two prophets who caused them so much trouble. 11 But three and a half days later, God will breathe life into their bodies. They will stand up, and everyone who sees them will be terrified.
12 The witnesses then heard a loud voice from heaven, saying, “Come up here.” And while their enemies were watching, they were taken up to heaven in a cloud. 13 At that same moment there was a terrible earthquake that destroyed a tenth of the city. Seven thousand people were killed, and the rest were frightened and praised the God who rules in heaven.
14The second horrible thing has now happened! And the third one will be here soon.
The Seventh Trumpet
15 At the sound of the seventh trumpet, loud voices were heard in heaven. They said,
“Now the kingdom
of this world
belongs to our Lord
and to his Chosen One!
And he will rule
forever and ever!”
16Then the 24 elders, who were seated on thrones in God's presence, knelt down and worshiped him. 17They said,
“Lord God All-Powerful,
you are and you were,
and we thank you.
You used your great power
and started ruling.
18 When the nations got angry,
you became angry too!
Now the time has come
for the dead
to be judged.
It is time for you to reward
your servants the prophets
and all your people
who honor your name,
no matter who they are.
It is time to destroy everyone
who has destroyed
the earth.”
19 The door to God's temple in heaven was then opened, and the sacred chest could be seen inside the temple. I saw lightning and heard roars of thunder. The earth trembled and huge hailstones fell to the ground.
translation_text:
Siɛradam Bilee a bɔr
1Le bi ta ligbingbaanl lan nann kijaangbiɛg wee bi jɔɔ magir tiwann nin ki seim, ki beim ke, “Li chaa ki tan mag Uwonbɔr a wonjiɛn niin nin i binbinlin na, wee ki kan biwonjiɛn ban be niin nin. 2Amaa laa mag iwonjiɛn niin a loobin ni, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr ta nloob nmɔn ki sei ban kaa ye biwonjiɛmin na. Bi na li chonn ki taan kasi a tiŋ nmɔn bu ki tan kpaan iŋmal pina nin ilee. 3Le n na li sei n siɛradam bilee nmɔn npɔɔn wee bin pag ilinlen leen ki tan kpaa iweehn turil nin kobilee nin piloob ki yee botu a kinkenl.”
4Siɛradam bilee nmɔn le ye Olif a siigi ilee-n nin fila a tutɔɔnbol a kerim milee-n, yan si kutingbɔŋ a Yudaau a nintogilin. 5Ni ye uba nan ban un sei bi kidaŋ ke, nŋmi li nya bi mɔnn ki nan nyɔɔ bi dataam nmɔn ki ku bi. Wan biɛn nan ban un sei bi kidaŋ ke, ni kpaa le nin udaan nkpo man. 6Siɛradam nmɔn jɔɔ npɔɔn man li fir choo utaal ke waa li nu n-yonn man wee bi be ki pag ilinlen leen nin; ki ji jɔɔ npɔɔn man li fir che nnyum nkpann ncham, ki ji li fir che imag a booli biɛn dan dulinya bu baah ban man nin.
7N-yonn man wee bi nan diɛ bi siɛra a toon nmɔn ke, kuwanbiigin na li nyann libogil lan nyɔɔ wee kaa jɔɔ tarigin yaan ki to bi bitɔb ki nyaŋ ki ku bi. 8Bi gbanann na li dɔɔn kitintakpeŋ a sanjal bu, ntim man wee pag woon a poolin bi yi mi ke Sodom nin Ijibir, nan yaan mu jigin wee bi nan kpaa bi Yudaau lidapunpunl bu-n. 9Le bininfob na li nyan imaal biɛn, nin ileen balbal biɛn, nin ibol biɛn nin, ki nan lig bi gbanann nmɔn iweehn mun itaa nin ligenl amaa kaa yin chee bin pii tigbanann nmɔn ni. 10Kutingbɔŋ nan a ninfob a pooi na li penn bi bilee nmɔn a kum bu, ki gel igel ki sei bi kpiɛtiib ipiin, nan bu-n bilinlem bilee nmɔn che ban be dulinya nan yaan jin fala pam.
11Iweehn itaa nin ligenl nmɔn kaah nan jon a bɔɔn, le kufoorug kan ye limiɛfolin nyan Uwonbɔr ban ki nan kɔɔ bi, le bi fii sir paab, le bijawaam choo ban kan bin takpem. 12Le siɛradam bilee nmɔn gbir nkukɔpɔɔn kaah nyan paab ki bei bi ke, “Ni donn paab do.” Le bi don kitilangbɔŋin ki jon paab, le bi dataam nan si ki lig bi.
13Iyaayoo nmɔn le kutingbɔŋ dam takpem, le kitiŋ nmɔn a niin piig a poolin nkerim nbaba lu, le bininfob turilile nan kpo kutingbɔŋ nmɔn a damim ni, le bijawaam nan choo ban gurin, le bi sei Uwonbɔr wan be paabin kupag.
14Ni lig! Niwanbirin nan kpiɛ milee-n jon na; niwanbirin nan kpiɛ mitaa-n li foon ke naa yuuri.
Kunaatuŋ kan kpiɛ milile
15Le malaka wan kpiɛ milile mu pee u naatuŋ, le ikukɔpɔɔr be paab ki tann ki len ke:
“Dulinya a naam kpann ti Yudaau nin U Masiya yaala,
le u li ŋmag u naam hali nin isaŋ yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.”
16Le bininkpeeb pilee nin bina ban nan ka bi naangbann bu Uwonbɔr a nintogilin lu ki ta binum chigin tum ki poor Uwonbɔr, 17ki len ke:
“Ti tenniŋ kunɔɔpoog, Uyudaan Uwonbɔr wan jɔɔ npɔɔn biɛn,
Wan pii nan be ki le la biɛ nin be,
nan bu-n a gaa a pɔɔm man yaba
le ki piin a naam a ŋmagim.
18Le ibol a ŋuui fii; le A ŋuufiiŋ foon.
Isaŋ foou nin bitakpiib a bɔr a jima
nin A yɔ A toontum ban ye bilinlemin,
nin A ninfogannkaab nin ban tenn A yinl jilima-n,
ban gbee bininfob, nin ban kaa gbee bininfobi,
ki bii ban bii dulinya.”
19Le Uwonbɔr a wonjiɛn niin yan be paabin loor, le n kan Uwonbɔr a kaal adaka iwonjiɛn niin a poolin. Le utaal a jugin nyagin ki dun ki tann, le kutingbɔŋ dam, le itanyunbɔl gbingbem nan lunn.

english_text:
The Woman and the Dragon
1Something important appeared in the sky. It was a woman whose clothes were the sun. The moon was under her feet, and a crown made of twelve stars was on her head. 2She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
3 Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads. 4 With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
5 The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne. 6The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for 1,260 days.
Michael Fights the Dragon
7 A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels. 8But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven 9 and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan. 10 Then I heard a voice from heaven shout,
“Our God has shown
his saving power,
and his kingdom has come!
God's own Chosen One
has shown his authority.
Satan accused our people
in the presence of God
day and night.
Now he has been thrown out!
11“Our people defeated Satan
because of the blood
of the Lamb
and the message of God.
They were willing
to give up their lives.
12“The heavens should rejoice,
together with everyone
who lives there.
But pity the earth
and the sea,
because the devil
was thrown down
to the earth.
He knows his time is short,
and he is very angry.”
13When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son. 14 But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
15The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away. 16But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth. 17This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught. 18The dragon stood on the beach beside the sea.
translation_text:
Upii nin kutunwiɛŋ
1Le lijinjeel nin ligaril a siɛra takpenl nan degirin paabin: Le upii uba nan yee nween a li ke likinkenlin, le uŋmal be u taatum, le u chig nnaam a yuchigirig kan jɔɔ iŋmabil piig nin ilee u yul bu. 2U nan jɔɔ lipool le ki kuun imariwiɛn kaah choo u nbu.
3Le siɛra liba mu ji degirin paab a naamin ni: Ki ye kutunwiɛŋ kan man ki jɔɔ iyul ilile nin iyinh piig, le nnaam a yuchigirig milile chig iyul nmɔn bu. 4Le kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn ta u jool ki tigin iŋmabil a bɔgirim a poolin mitaa nkerim nba ki jaa kutingbɔŋin, le kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn jon tan si upii wan yin maa nmɔn a nintogil ki guu, ke upii nan maa ke un ŋman kibiliɛgin. 5Le upii nmɔn nan maa kibijag, kibijag kan na yin ta kukurug a jaangbiɛg ki ŋmag dulinya yaab biɛn ni. Le Uwonbɔr ta u don paab u naangbɔŋin bu. 6Le upii nmɔn guun ki jon kukunkɔɔg a paab, nan yaan wee Uwonbɔr nan mann npaan ki bil guur upii nmɔn ke bi li lig u ki tan kpaa iweehn turil nin iweehn kobilee nin iweehn piloob.
7Bitɔb le nan be paab. Le Maakil nin u malakam nan ton kutunwiɛŋ, le kutunwiɛŋ nin u mu a malakam ton jiin. 8Amaa kutunwiɛŋ a pɔɔm kaa nan yabi, le bi nyaŋ bi, le bi lann binbebol paab. 9Le bi nyan kutunwiɛŋ takpeŋ nmɔn gab, u pii ye uwaa wan nan be le yaayoo-n, wee bi yi u ke ulinlaril bee Sintani, wan liir dulinya yaab a sam ki che bi borin, le bi nyan uma nin u malakam ki gabin dulinya nan yaan.
10Iyaayoo le n gbir nkukɔpɔɔn miba nyan paab ki ke:
“Daandaan nan feegab nin npɔɔn nin ti Wonbɔru a naam dan na,
nin U Masiya a naam a ninkper a pɔɔm foona.
Nan bu-n wan nan galin ti nabumin,
wan nan galin bi ti Wonbɔru a numin nween nin kunyiɛgin,
bi nyan u gabin tuma.
11Bi nyaŋ wa
kipeebig a cham bu
nin bi siɛram bu
baa nan jiɛ bi miɛfolin ki tan kaagi
ki sul jir bɔɔn ki nyan nkumin ni.
12Mambu, ni che ni li mɔn na!
Paab nin nan biɛn be niin ni!
Amaa tibɔbir be dulinya nin limɔgil bu,
nan bu-n ulinlaril kaah jiirin ni ban nin!
U gbee nin kiŋuufiiŋ le,
nan bu-n u nyi u saŋi kaah kaa yabi.”
13Kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn kaah nan kan baah nyan u jaa dulinya nan yaan nin, le u nin nɔɔ ke un choo upii wan maa kibijagin. 14Le Uwonbɔr nan ta libaanweenl takpenl a kpinkpann tilee ki sei upii nmɔn ke un yug ki jo kukunkɔɔg a paab nan yaan wee Uwonbɔr mann npaan ki guun win ke bi li jin u ki tan kpaan ibin itaa nin ligenl ki jiɛn uwaa-n wee u laa pii wi. 15Le uwaa nmɔn nan sii nnyum u mɔnn a li ke nkpenn a nyumin, ke nnyum nmɔn npuu ki tan ta upii nmɔn. 16Amaa le kutingbɔŋ nan ter upii nmɔn ki yaar u mɔb ki ta nnyum man wee kutunwiɛŋ sii u mɔn nin ki nyun. 17Iyaayoo le kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn a ŋuul nan fii upii nmɔn bu, le u lol bitɔb ki jon ke un tan tob upii nmɔn a buwaab ban gurin, ban chee Uwonbɔr a siim wee ki jɔɔ Yisa a siɛra-n.

english_text:
The Two Beasts
1 I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God. 2 The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast. 3One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast, 4and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
5 The beast was allowed to brag and claim to be God, and for 42 months it was allowed to rule. 6The beast cursed God, and it cursed the name of God. It even cursed the place where God lives, as well as everyone who lives in heaven with God. 7 It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race. 8 The beast was worshiped by everyone whose name wasn't written before the time of creation in the book of the Lamb who was killed.
9If you have ears,
then listen!
10 If you are doomed
to be captured,
you will be captured.
If you are doomed
to be killed by a sword,
you will be killed
by a sword.
This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
11I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon. 12It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast. 13It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
14This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword. 15It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death. 16 All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves, 17they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
18You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is 666, and it stands for a person.
translation_text:
Tiwankobir tilee a bɔr
1Le kutunwiɛŋ nan sir limɔgil a dool. Le n kan kuwanbiig kaah chaa nyan limɔgilin. Ku nan jɔɔ iyinh piig le nin iyul ilile, ki chig nnaam a yuchigirim piig u yin bu, le iyin yan sugir Uwonbɔr nan sɔb paa u yuli nmɔn biɛn bu. 2Maah nan kan kuwanbiig kan nmɔn nan nann unamuun le, amaa le u taai nann ke ubakar a taai, le u mɔb nann ligbeginl a mɔb. Le kutunwiɛŋ ta u pɔɔm, nin u naangbɔŋ nin tininkper a pɔɔm ki sei kuwanbiigin. 3Kuwanbiig nmɔn a yul liba bu nan nann le ke li kan kidaŋ takpem le-n, amaa kidaŋ takpeŋ nmɔn a biɛl nan bugira. Ni nan gar dulinya yaab le bi nɔɔ kuwanbiig nmɔn. 4Le bininfob nan jiɛn kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn waah ta tininkper a pɔɔm ki sei kuwanbiigin nbu, le bi ji nan jiɛn kuwanbiigin mu ki len ke, “Ŋma nann kuwanbiig nan naa? Ŋma be ki li fir to kuwanbiig nan bitɔbaa?”
5Le kuwanbiig nmɔn nan kan bimɔb ki pag kalanbaani a leen nin tisugir ki ta u ninkper a pɔɔm ki tun ki tan kpaa iŋmal pina nin ilee. 6Le u nan yaar u mɔb ki sugir Uwonbɔr, ki gbii kutingbiig U yinl nin nan yaan wee U be, nin ban be paab. 7Bi nan sei u npɔɔn ke un kɔnn Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab wee ki nyaŋ bi. Le bi ji sei u tininkper a pɔɔm ke u li ye imaal, nin bininfob, nin ileen, nin ibol biɛn. 8Bininfob ban biɛn be dulinya nan yaan wee bi yin kaa sɔb ŋa Kipeebig kan wee bi nan ku-n a miɛfol a gbɔŋin yaan dulinya nan a piimin nin, bi biɛn nan yin jiɛn kuwanbiig nmɔn le.
9Wan jɔɔ litul ke, ni che un gbir.
10Wan ye bin nan choo u tiyomir ke,
see ki bi nan choo u tiyomir
wan ye bi nan ta takoobi ki ku u ke,
takoobi nmɔn le bi yin ta ki ku u.
Mambu ni ŋan nin Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab li jɔɔ limɔril nin nyiginim ki ŋa Uwonbɔr yada nin ibamɔn.
11Le n ji kan kuwanbiig kuba kaah nyan dulinya nan yaan. U nan jɔɔ iyin ilee le a li ke kipeebig, amaa le ki pag a li ke kutunwiɛŋin. 12Le ki sir chinchinn a wanbiig a ninkper a pɔɔm ki che dulinya a ninfob biɛn jiɛn chinchinn a wanbiigin, kan nan kan kidaŋ wee ni bugir. 13Le kuwanbiig nmɔn ŋa ligaril a siɛra takpenl, hali ki che nŋmi nyan paab ki lunn nin le bininfob kan mi npaan nin. 14Chinchinn a wanbiigin kaah sei u npɔɔn man wee u si u taalin ki fir ŋa siɛra a toon yin, ni bu che u fir lar dulinya yaaba. Le ki bei bi ke bin maa litingbanl nin jilima lan nann chinchinn a wanbiigin kan nan kan takoobi a daŋ amaa wee kaa kpe-n. 15Le Uwonbɔr nan sei kuwanbiig kan kpiɛ milee nmɔn npɔɔn ke kin foor jaa litingbanl lan jɔɔ chinchinn a wanbiigin a nunaŋ, wee lin fir pag wee ban yii kaah jiɛn li ke lin ku bi. 16Le u mu ji mug bininfob biɛn, ban kaa gbee bininfob nin ban gbee bininfob, ban jɔɔ nin ban kaa jɔɔ, ban ye biba nin ban ye biyom, ke un daag bi nɔɔjiim bee bi yutun bu ndaagim, 17wee nin che uba laa ji fir da niba bee ki kɔɔr niba wee naa ye udaan jɔɔ kuwanbiig nmɔn a daagim le, ndaagim man ye u yinl nin u kanl.
18Ni niɛ nan ban nlamgɔrikaam le. Ni ye uba jɔɔ nlam ke, ni che un kanh tiwanbir a kanl, nan bu-n ni ye uninfo a kanl le. U kanl le ye kobiloob nin piloob nin iloob (666) le.

english_text:
The Lamb and His 144,000 Followers
1 I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion! With him were 144,000, who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads. 2 Then I heard a sound from heaven that was like a roaring flood or loud thunder or even like the music of harps. 3And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the 144,000 who had been rescued from the earth. 4All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth. 5 They never tell lies, and they are innocent.
The Messages of the Three Angels
6I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth. 7The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
8 A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
9Finally, a third angel came and shouted:
Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead. 10 You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
11 If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
12God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
13Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.”
The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.”
The Earth Is Harvested
14 I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand. 15 An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.” 16The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
17Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven. 18After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.” 19The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger. 20 The pit was outside the city, and when the grapes were mashed, blood flowed out. The blood turned into a river that was about 300 kilometers long and almost deep enough to cover a horse.
translation_text:
Kipeebig nin ki ninfob
1Le n lig ki kan Kipeebig n nintogil le ki si Zayɔnn a jɔɔl bu, le bininfob turikobig nin turpina nin turina (144,000) kaah si u ban, ban wee bi nan sɔb u yinl nin u Baa a yinl ki tabin bi yutun bu-n. 2Le n nan gbir likukɔl kaah nyan paab, le li fur nann nnyum man puu a fur bee utaal kaah ti tann man ni. Maah nan gbir likukɔl lan nmɔn a fur nan nann ke bibiɛfaab kaah far bi biɛr le-n. 3Le bi nan gaah ilan pɔɔn kunaangbɔŋin nin tiwann naan wan tan fo tina-n nin bininkpeebin a nintogil. Uba kaa nan li fir ki tinn ilan nmɔn ni, see bi ma bininfob turikobigin nin turpina nin turina ban nan kan nŋmarim dulinya nan yaan nin a binba. 4Bi ma ye ban kaa bii biba lipiibanlin ni, nan bu-n bi ŋmag biba le chasi. Bi nɔɔ Kipeebigin kaah chaa nan yaan biɛn le. Bi ma ye ban wee Uwonbɔr nan da bininfob a sisiigin, ke bin ŋa chinchinn a ninfob ki sei Uwonbɔr nin Kipeebigin. 5Bi mɔɔŋi kaa nan nyi por tibɔkari; baa nan jɔɔ igalin ni.
Malakam bita a bɔr
6Le n kan malaka uba kaah be paab ki yugir, ki ŋmag tibɔŋann tan kaa diɛrin ke un pag sei bininfob ban be kutingbɔŋ nan yaan, ibol, nin imaal, nin ileen nin bininfob biɛn. 7Le u pag nin nkukɔpɔɔn ke, “Ni li san Uwonbɔr wee ki li tenn U kupaga, nan bu-n U bɔjil a yoon foou. Ni li jiɛn wan nan naan paab, nin kutingbɔŋ, nin limɔgil nin nnyunbuma.”
8Le malaka wan kpiɛ milee nɔɔ u bɔɔn ki len ke, “Ki lu! Babilɔnn kan ye kitiŋ takpeŋ wee ki nan mug bininfob a booli biɛn wee bi nyun ndapɔɔrim ke u wanchɔgin toon yin luu.”
9Le malaka wan kpiɛ mitaa mu nɔɔ bi bɔɔn ki len ke, “Ni ye uba jiɛn kuwanbiigin nin kuwanbiig nmɔn a nunaŋ wee ki gaa ki daagim u yutunl bu bee u nɔɔ bu ke, 10udaan mu li nyu Uwonbɔr a ŋuufiiŋ a daam man wee U minn ŋa U ŋuufiiŋ a dapɔɔrim a yiigin. Bi na li ta lichibil a ŋmiim ki mugir udaan malakam ban be kasi nin Kipeebigin a nintogil. 11Le bi fala a jim a ŋmiim a kpinnyir na li dug ki do paab hali nin isaŋ yan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛm. Lifooril kaa na li be nween bee kunyiɛgin ki sei ban jiɛn kuwanbiigin nin kuwanbiig nmɔn a nunaŋin, bee ban ga kuwanbiig nmɔn a yinl a daagimi. 12Ni niɛ nan bu ni kpaan nin Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab ban chee Uwonbɔr a siim wee ki ŋa Yisa yada-n li ye ban li jɔɔ limɔril nin nnyiginim.
13Le n gbir likukɔl nyan paab ki len ke, “Sɔba: Tikaar be bitakpiib ban kpo nin Uyudaan nin, naah nyan daandaan nan ki jɔɔ chaa.”
Le Kinaaŋ len ke, “Nn, bi li foor bi baginn nin, bi ŋaar nmɔn li nɔɔ bi.”
Kutingbɔŋ a chiɛm
14Le n nan lig ki kan kitalangbɔŋ peŋ, le uba ka niin ki “nann Uninfosaal a bija” ki chig salima a naan yuchigirig, le ki ŋmag gɔrug kaaŋ u nɔɔn. 15Le malaka uba mu ji nyan iwonjiɛn niin ki tiɛn paab ki yin wan ka kitalangbɔŋin yaan nin ke, “Taam a gɔrug ki chiɛ, nan bu-n nchiɛm a saŋa foo, nan bu-n kutingbɔŋ a dii beer foo nchiɛma.” 16Le wan nan ka kitilangbɔŋ bun ta u gɔrug ki fiɛn fiɛn kutingbɔŋ bu, le ki chiɛ kutingbɔŋ.
17Le malaka uba mu ji nyann paab a wonjiɛn niin yin, le ki mu ŋmag gɔrug kaaŋ. 18Le malaka wan guu nŋmi mu ji nyann libinbinl n-yaan, ki yin nkukɔpɔɔn ki bei malaka wan ŋmag gɔrug kaaŋin ke, “Taam a gɔrug kaaŋin ki lagin igbiin bon yan be kutingbɔŋ nan a gbiinsiig bu-n na, nan bu-n ki gbiin mann na.” 19Le malaka nmɔn ta u gɔrug ki fiɛn fiɛn kutingbɔŋ bu, le ki lagin kutingbɔŋ a gbiin ki gab baah ŋmaŋ Uwonbɔr a ŋuufiiŋ a silooi a daam nan ban nin. 20Le bi nan nyan kitiŋ nmɔn a gbaam ki kɔɔ baah taan isiloon ki toog ndaam nan yaan nin, le ncham nyan ndaam a toon bolin ki puu, ki do paab ki tan yegin itangalig a tarig maal kobig nin piniin nin (180).

english_text:
The Last of the Terrible Troubles
1After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
2Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps, 3 and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing,
“Lord God All-Powerful,
you have done great
and marvelous things.
You are the ruler
of all nations,
and you do what is
right and fair.
4 Lord, who doesn't honor
and praise your name?
